process.title: Say which guide, and ask us the same question back
process.description: The first useful message confirms that your child is sitting Digital Society rather than ITGS, names the level, says whether the Higher Level extension applies, and states where the inquiry project has reached. Then ask the prospective tutor whether they have taken a cohort through to examination on the current guide. That one question sorts the market faster than any other.

process.title: A free diagnostic built on a source question
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing, is one per student, and needs no card details. It is spent on a source-based question answered to time and then marked against the published descriptors, plus a look at whatever examples the student can produce from memory. You leave knowing whether the gap is examples, concepts, technical accuracy or timing.

process.title: Build the examples file from session one
process.description: Every session adds two or three dated, sourced, located examples to a file the student owns, tagged to concepts and contexts. Doing this from the start costs nothing extra and produces the only revision asset in the subject that cannot be bought. Doing it in the final term produces a thin list assembled under pressure.

process.title: Put the inquiry project on a dated chain
process.description: Before any content planning, the inquiry gets dates: question tested, methods and ethics cleared, documentation checked while it accumulates, one feedback round, internal deadline. Families who leave this until the school raises it are usually working backwards from a question that was never investigable.

process.title: Drill the papers on source material, to time
process.description: In the final two terms, sessions move to full components under exam conditions, with minutes allocated by mark tariff and the student's own examples deployed from memory in every answer. Marked against descriptors rather than impressions, and the marks are shown to the student rather than summarised to the parent.

process.title: Reassess at the mocks, and stop if it is done
process.description: After the mock session the plan is rebuilt from the marked papers. If the evidence says the candidate is reliably in the top bands with the inquiry submitted, the right recommendation is to stop, and it gets made. Continuing to bill a student who has finished is the easiest kind of waste there is.

whyPoints.title: Taught from the current guide, not from ITGS leftovers
whyPoints.description: Most material a Dubai family finds for this subject describes the course it replaced. Sessions here work from the current guide and the school's own assessment outline, and old papers are used only where they genuinely practise a skill the current components still test. That alone removes a large share of wasted revision.

whyPoints.title: An examples file as a deliverable, not an afterthought
whyPoints.description: A dozen dated, sourced, located examples tagged to concepts and contexts is the asset that separates a top-band candidate from a fluent one. It gets built from the first session and reviewed each term, because this is the fastest-moving subject in Group 3 and last year's example is often no longer the best one.

whyPoints.title: The inquiry project supervised as a project
whyPoints.description: Question tested for investigability, methods and ethics cleared through the school, documentation checked while it is being produced, and one round of criterion-referenced comments on the student's own draft. Spread across months, scheduled from DP1, and quoted as supervision rather than absorbed into weekly teaching.

whyPoints.title: Technical accuracy without drifting into Computer Science
whyPoints.description: Answers have to describe systems correctly and still be social analysis. A tutor from a pure computing background tends to over-technicalise and a tutor from a pure humanities background tends to hand-wave. Matching here is explicitly on having taught this course, which is why the pool is searched online rather than locally.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before you book
whyPoints.description: Where no tutor who has taught the current guide to examination is free in your slot, you are told that, along with the real alternatives and their trade-offs. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, and a near-miss match in a scarce subject costs more than a short wait.

whyPoints.title: Honesty rules stated, including about AI tools
whyPoints.description: Submitted work must be the student's own, tool use must be acknowledged as the school requires, and a tutor comments once on a student-written draft without supplying text. In a subject that studies generative systems, this is worth saying explicitly rather than leaving to inference.

faqs.question: What is IB Digital Society and how does it differ from ITGS?
faqs.answer: Digital Society is a Group 3 course that replaced Information Technology in a Global Society. ITGS organised its content by application area and IT system and assessed a project with a defined product. Digital Society reorganises the same territory into concepts such as change, power and values, content strands covering data, algorithms, artificial intelligence, networks and media, and contexts from cultural to environmental, then assesses source-based papers plus a student-designed inquiry. The practical consequence for a Dubai family is that most revision material found online, including past papers, belongs to the old course and is not practice for the new components.

faqs.question: Why is it so hard to find a Digital Society tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the course is young and almost nobody trained in it. The teachers running it came from Computer Science, Business Management, Geography or ITGS, and the number of people anywhere who have taken a cohort through to examination on the current guide is small. In a single city the number is smaller still. That is the honest explanation for why availability is limited, and it is also the strongest argument for looking online rather than locally: the match should be to someone who has taught this guide, not to someone who can reach your district.

faqs.question: What is the inquiry project in IB Digital Society?
faqs.answer: The internally assessed component, in which a student designs and carries out their own investigation of a real digital-society question and reports it. It is usually what decides whether a candidate reaches the top bands, and it receives the least class supervision because no single teacher can oversee twenty individual investigations across two year groups. The common failure is scope: a question like whether artificial intelligence helps education cannot be investigated, so the project becomes a summary. Narrow, located questions about a specific system and a specific group of people work.

faqs.question: How long should the Digital Society inquiry project be?
faqs.answer: Confirm the current word limit, permitted formats and number of supporting items with your child's coordinator rather than from any search result. This is one of the specifics that has been revised since the course launched, and because so much ITGS material is still circulating, limits quoted online are frequently for the wrong course entirely. The more useful planning point is the allocation: draft the analytical sections first and let the description of what was done occupy whatever space remains, because trimming description is painless and trimming analysis costs marks.

faqs.question: Does my child need coding skills to take Digital Society?
faqs.answer: No. This is a social science, not a programming course, and no component requires a student to write code. What is required is enough technical accuracy to describe a system correctly: what a training data set is, how a recommendation feed is assembled, where a data asymmetry arises. Students arriving from Computer Science have an advantage on that accuracy and a specific risk, which is answering social questions with technical detail that earns nothing. Students arriving from a humanities background have the opposite profile and need the technical vocabulary built deliberately.

faqs.question: What counts as a real-world example in this subject?
faqs.answer: A located, dated case with identifiable actors and at least one specific detail, recorded with the source it came from. Saying that platforms collect user data names a category, not an example, and categories cannot be analysed. The working target is around a dozen examples spread across the content strands and contexts, each tagged with the concepts it illustrates. Build the file from DP1 and review it every term, because this is the fastest-moving subject in Group 3 and an example that was current eighteen months ago is often no longer the best available one.

faqs.question: What does the Higher Level extension add for a Dubai Digital Society candidate?
faqs.answer: An additional element on contemporary challenges arising from digital systems and the interventions proposed to address them, assessed in its own component. Students prepare it as a research exercise and it is assessed as an evaluative one, which is why a list of eight interventions scores below three that are each traced to the mechanism causing the problem and judged against it. The teachable routine is: name the mechanism, ask whether the intervention touches it, ask who bears the cost, ask what it might cause instead. Confirm the component format with the coordinator, since arrangements have been revised.

faqs.question: Do universities accept Digital Society for computing degrees?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a social science rather than as a technical prerequisite. Programmes that require Mathematics or Computer Science at Higher Level will still require them, and Digital Society does not substitute. Where it helps is in demonstrating analytical writing about technology and society, which is well regarded for information systems, digital policy, media, law and business pathways. Check the published prerequisites of the specific programmes your child is considering, including UAE universities, and do not let anyone imply that a subject choice or tutoring changes a stated entry requirement.

faqs.question: Can my child use an AI chatbot while working on the inquiry project?
faqs.answer: Submitted work must be the student's own, and any tool that contributes to it has to be acknowledged in the manner the school requires, so start by asking the coordinator for the school's written policy. The practical distinction is between research and substitution. Using a model to surface candidate sources, then reading, verifying and citing those sources, is research. Pasting generated text into the report is not, and in this subject a marker is unusually likely to spot it, because generated passages tend to be exactly the undated, unlocated generality the descriptors penalise.

faqs.question: My child's Dubai school switched from ITGS. What actually changes?
faqs.answer: The framework, the assessment and the usable practice material. Content is now analysed through named concepts in named contexts rather than organised by application area, ethics is woven through as values and power rather than treated as a separate strand, and the old project is replaced by a student-designed inquiry. Past papers from the previous course do not practise the current components. Ask the department which current-guide practice material they use, how many internal feedback rounds the inquiry receives, and whether the teacher has taken a cohort through to examination yet.

faqs.question: Which concepts does Digital Society assess, and how?
faqs.answer: The framework uses concepts such as change, identity, power, values, space, systems and expression as analytical lenses, and the papers expect at least one of them to frame any answer. They are not assessed as definitions. A candidate who opens by identifying which concept a source is really about has done the hardest part of the question; one who describes the technology and then mentions a concept in passing has not. Drilling this early in DP1 as a deliberate vocabulary exercise is one of the cheapest improvements available in the subject.

faqs.question: Is Digital Society a Group 3 or a Group 4 subject?
faqs.answer: Group 3, Individuals and Societies, alongside History, Economics, Geography and Psychology. That matters for Diploma planning: it satisfies the social science requirement rather than the experimental science one, so a student taking it still needs a Group 4 subject. In Dubai it is frequently timetabled against Computer Science or Business Management, which forces a choice rather than allowing both. Ask the school in Year 11 which blocks it sits in and whether Higher Level will run, because several Dubai schools introduced the course at Standard Level only.

faqs.question: How many Digital Society sessions does a Dubai student usually need?
faqs.answer: A realistic shape is weekly sessions through DP1 to build the examples file and the conceptual vocabulary, four to six supervision sessions on the inquiry project spread across months, six to eight on source-paper drilling in the final two terms, and for Higher Level candidates three to five on the extension. That is roughly twenty-five to thirty-five hours across the two years. The examples file is why front-loading matters: it accumulates, and it cannot be assembled retrospectively in the final term with anything like the same quality.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to take Arabic alongside the Diploma in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA's published requirements. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. For these subjects, additional or different content requires prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: What happens if no Digital Society specialist is available in our slot?
faqs.answer: You are told, with the alternatives set out. The options are a tutor in a time zone whose working day overlaps a Dubai evening, a different weekly slot, or a short wait for a specific person. For inquiry project supervision the wait is often the right choice, because supervision done well in DP1 is worth considerably more than supervision done immediately in DP2. What is not offered is a Geography or Computer Science specialist presented as an equivalent, because in a subject this young the difference between having taught the guide and having read it is large.

faqs.question: Is Digital Society easier than Computer Science for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Different rather than easier, and the students who find it easy are usually the ones who write well. There is no code and no formal problem-solving, but there is a research obligation that Computer Science does not have: a maintained set of sourced examples, and a self-designed inquiry that has to be investigable. Students who dislike open-ended work often find Computer Science more comfortable because the tasks are bounded. Students who can argue from evidence usually do better here. Choose on a term of marked work in both where the school allows it.

dubai/ib-dp-digital-society-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Digital Society at both levels, along with the Group 3 subjects Dubai students most often pair it with. Each one has taught the current subject guide rather than the legacy ITGS course, and each works from the student's own marked answers rather than a fixed worksheet pack.

intro.heading: Why this subject trips up good students in their first Diploma year
paragraphs: Digital Society is the newest subject on the Diploma timetable. It replaced Information Technology in a Global Society, moved into classrooms in September 2024, and reached its first examination session in 2026. That timeline matters more than it sounds. It means your child's teacher is almost certainly teaching the course for the first or second time, that the archive of past papers every other subject leans on barely exists, and that the exemplar answers circulating between Dubai staff rooms are still few enough to count. Families searching for an IB DP Digital Society tutor in Dubai are usually reacting to a first report that says something vague: strong ideas, insufficient evidence, needs to develop analysis.

The subject looks approachable on the option sheet, which is part of the problem. Students who read widely and argue well in English or Global Politics assume the same approach transfers. It does not. A Digital Society answer is marked on whether a claim is anchored to named, real, current digital systems and then evaluated from more than one perspective. A paragraph that says social media harms teenagers earns almost nothing. A paragraph that names a specific platform, the recommendation algorithm behind it, who holds the data, which concept that illustrates, and what the counter-case is, earns the marks. The gap between those two paragraphs is not intelligence; it is method, and method is teachable in a handful of sessions.

The second pressure is the inquiry project, which is the largest single piece of internally assessed work in the course and the one students begin too late. It is not a research essay in the school-report sense. It demands a researchable question about a real digital system, a defensible choice of sources, and an argument that survives examination. Dubai students often choose a topic that is genuinely interesting but impossible to evidence, then lose six weeks discovering that. A tutor who has read several of these through to submission can usually tell inside one session whether a question will hold.

Online delivery suits the subject better than most. Everything the course studies is on a screen already: platforms, interfaces, datasets, policy documents, news coverage. A session over live video can open the actual artefact the student is writing about, annotate the student's draft in the same window, and leave the marked version behind. IB Gram's UAE tuition is delivered this way as standard. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and the trade-off is explained in plain terms further down this page.

What follows is the working detail rather than a sales pitch: how answers are actually marked, which UAE examples hold up as evidence, how to pick an inquiry question that can be researched from Dubai, what the two years look like counted backwards from the May session, what the Dubai market charges for this kind of help, and where the honesty line sits in a subject that spends half its time discussing artificial intelligence.

dubai/ib-dp-digital-society-tutor.programmesIntro: Digital Society sits in the Diploma, but the students who cope with it best usually arrive with habits built earlier. These are the three IB programmes a Dubai family is most likely to be choosing between or moving through, and what each one contributes to this particular subject.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma, where Digital Society sits in Group 3 alongside Economics, Geography, Global Politics, History, Psychology and Business Management. Students take it at Standard or Higher Level, with Higher Level adding an extension on challenges and interventions. Assessment combines externally marked papers with the internally assessed inquiry project, so coursework deadlines inside the school term carry real weight long before the examination session.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is the densest Diploma market in the UAE, with KHDA counting 227 private schools in 2024-25 and International Baccalaureate students making up roughly seven in every hundred across the emirate's private sector. Digital Society availability varies school by school, because it depends on which teacher the school has been able to redeploy from the old ITGS course or recruit new, and that is often why a Dubai family looks outside school for subject help.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five-year programme that feeds the Diploma in continuum schools. Its Design and Individuals and Societies courses are where the habits Digital Society rewards are first built: investigating a real context, citing sources properly, and evaluating a solution rather than describing it. Students arriving into the Diploma from MYP usually handle the inquiry project more comfortably than those arriving from a purely examination-led system.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the full continuum, which means a student can reach Digital Society having already written structured investigations with a bibliography. Students transferring in from IGCSE or a CBSE background in Dubai are often strong on content recall and unpractised at evaluation, and the first few online sessions usually go on closing that specific gap rather than teaching new material.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The IB's career-linked route, where students combine DP courses with a career-related study and a personal and professional skills element. Digital Society is a natural DP course inside a CP built around technology, media or business, and the reflective project asks for the same evidence discipline the inquiry project does.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is offered by a small number of UAE schools rather than being widely available, so most Dubai families reading this page are looking at the full Diploma. Where a student is on the CP route, the tutoring work is usually heavier on the reflective project and lighter on examination technique, and sessions are planned against the school's own internal deadlines.

dubai/ib-dp-digital-society-tutor.subjectsIntro: Digital Society is rarely the only subject a family wants help with. These are the courses Dubai students most often take alongside it, with the specific place marks tend to disappear in each, so a parent can judge whether one tutor or two is the sensible plan.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Marked on claim, evidence and evaluation across data, algorithms, computers, networks, media and artificial intelligence. Marks are lost on unsupported generalisation, examples that are vague or out of date, and single-perspective answers. The Higher Level extension on challenges and interventions needs a separate answer structure from the papers.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Often confused with Digital Society by option-sheet readers. This one is programming, data structures, computational thinking and a developed solution. Students who want to build software should be here; students who want to argue about the consequences of software belong in Digital Society. A few Dubai students take both and need help keeping the two answer styles separate.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Shares the case-study discipline. Marks disappear where students describe a business tool rather than applying it to the stimulus, and where evaluation is a final sentence rather than a thread. Students pairing it with Digital Society can reuse one bank of real companies across both subjects if the examples are kept current.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and definition precision decide a large share of the marks, and the internal assessment commentaries are a recurring pressure point in the first Diploma year. Students who find Digital Society's open-ended questions comfortable often find the technical discipline here much harder, and that is usually what tutoring targets.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: The closest neighbour to Digital Society in argument style, built on key concepts, case studies and perspectives. The overlap on governance, power and regulation is real and useful. The risk is a student recycling a political argument into a Digital Society answer without anchoring it to a specific digital system, which marks poorly.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies, ethics and research methods are the marked content, and students lose ground by narrating a study instead of evaluating its method. The research-methods teaching transfers directly to the inquiry project, so a student taking both usually needs less support on project design and more on examination timing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The route most Digital Society students take, because its statistics and modelling content matches how they think. Marks go missing in the technology-assisted questions and in interpreting output rather than generating it. The data-handling confidence it builds is directly useful when an inquiry project involves a dataset.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The non-literary texts half of this course — advertising, news, digital media — overlaps with Digital Society's media content. Marks are lost on paper one where students summarise the text rather than analysing how it works. Students strong here often write Digital Society answers that read well and evidence badly.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: The making counterpart to Digital Society's analysis. Both carry a major internally assessed project and both reward evidence of iteration rather than a polished final artefact. Dubai students taking both tend to need help scheduling two coursework cycles that peak in the same term.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Compulsory, assessed by essay and exhibition, and the place Digital Society students can gain quickly. The course's questions about evidence, technology and knowledge map onto Digital Society content, and a student who can handle one usually transfers to the other with a few targeted sessions on essay structure.

sections.heading: What the first month of Digital Society tutoring actually fixes
paragraphs: An IB DP Digital Society tutor in Dubai working with a new student spends the first session diagnosing, not teaching. The tutor asks for two things: the most recent marked piece of work, and the student's own list of real-world examples. Those two documents tell you almost everything. A marked answer shows whether the student is losing marks on knowledge, on structure, or on evidence. The example list shows whether there is anything to build an answer from, and in roughly nine cases out of ten the list is either empty or made up of stories the student half-remembers from the news.

The fix for the first failure is mechanical. Students write what they think about a digital system and assume the thinking is the answer. The marker is looking for a claim, the specific system that supports it, the concept it illustrates, and a counter-perspective. Rehearsing that shape on short questions, out loud, with the tutor interrupting at the point the evidence should appear, changes scores faster than any amount of content revision. Most students need three or four sessions of this before the shape becomes automatic.

The fix for the second failure is slower and more useful. The student builds a personal example bank, kept in one document, with each entry carrying the system, who owns it, what data it uses, the concepts it illustrates and the contexts it sits in. Twelve good entries, properly annotated, will cover almost any question the papers can ask. Building that bank is homework the tutor checks weekly, and it is the single most transferable thing a Digital Society student can own.

By the end of a first month, a family should be able to see three concrete changes: answers that name systems instead of gesturing at them, a written example bank that did not exist before, and a marked timed question with a score the student can explain. If none of those three has moved, the tutoring is not working and the match should change.

sections.heading: How a Digital Society answer is actually marked
paragraphs: Command terms do more work in this subject than students expect. The verb at the front of the question sets the depth of response and, with it, the mark ceiling. An answer that describes where the question says evaluate cannot reach the top band regardless of how much the student knows. Dubai students who have come through IGCSE are particularly prone to this, because the reward structure there is weighted towards accurate recall and they arrive expecting the same deal.

The second marking reality is that evidence has to be specific and current. Naming a company is not evidence. Naming a company, the system it runs, the data that system collects and the stakeholders affected is evidence. Examiners in a new subject are also seeing the same half-dozen famous examples in thousands of scripts, which is an argument for a student holding two or three examples nobody else will use, and a Dubai student has those available locally.

The third is perspective. A top-band answer carries more than one point of view and resolves between them rather than listing both. Students write the counter-argument as a paragraph beginning with a concessive clause and then abandon it. The repair is to make the counter-case do work: who benefits, who carries the cost, what the evidence says about which effect dominates. A tutor can model this in ten minutes and then make the student do it in writing for the next six weeks.

sections.heading: The UAE as an evidence base: examples a Dubai student can use that nobody else will
paragraphs: Digital Society rewards specificity, and specificity is where a student in Dubai has a genuine advantage over a student in a country with a thinner public digital infrastructure. The UAE has built, at national scale, exactly the kinds of systems the course asks students to analyse: a federal digital identity, a national artificial intelligence strategy with a minister attached to it since 2017, smart-city data programmes, platform-mediated gig work across food delivery and ride-hailing, and a personal data protection law passed as Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021. Each of these is researchable in English, locally relevant, and almost entirely absent from the scripts examiners read.

Using a local example well means doing more than naming it. The student has to be able to say what the system does technically, who operates it, what data it depends on, which stakeholders gain and lose, and what the regulatory position is. That is a research task a tutor can set and check, and it is where online delivery pays off: the session can open the regulator's own page, read the relevant clause together, and the student leaves with a sourced note rather than an impression.

There is a caution attached. A local example is only an advantage if it is accurate. Writing confidently about a UAE system and getting the operator or the legal basis wrong is worse than using a generic international example, because an examiner who notices the error discounts the whole paragraph. Sessions on this material spend as much time checking the claim as building it, and anything the student cannot source from an official page gets struck out of the example bank.

sections.heading: Writing about algorithms without turning the answer into Computer Science
paragraphs: The most common structural error in Digital Society answers written by able students is drift into technical explanation. A question asks about the consequences of algorithmic recommendation and the student writes four hundred words on how collaborative filtering works. The technical knowledge is real and the marks are not there. Digital Society asks what a system does to people, institutions and values. The mechanism matters only to the depth required to make the consequence intelligible.

The discipline is easier to teach as a ratio. One or two sentences of mechanism, then the consequence, then the stakeholders, then the evaluation. Students who have come from a strong computing background in a Dubai school resist this, because the mechanism is the part they are confident about and the evaluation is the part that feels like guessing. Making the evaluation concrete fixes the resistance: a judgement supported by a named outcome is not guessing, and once a student has written three of them properly the preference flips.

The reverse error exists too and is less often diagnosed. Students with no technical confidence avoid mechanism altogether and write entirely in abstractions, which reads fluently and cannot be credited because nothing is anchored to a real system. These students usually need a short, bounded technical vocabulary rather than a computing course: enough to say what training data is, what a recommendation system optimises for, what personal data means in law, and what a network dependency implies when it fails.

A tutor working on this will often set the same question twice, a fortnight apart, and show the student the two answers side by side. That comparison does more than a mark scheme, because the student can see their own drift and name it. It is also the point at which most students stop asking whether Digital Society is an easy subject.

sections.heading: The inquiry project: choosing a question that can be answered from Dubai
paragraphs: The inquiry project is the largest internally assessed piece of work in the course, and the stage that decides its mark happens before any writing: choosing the question. A question has to be about a real digital system, narrow enough to evidence, and open enough to argue. Students in Dubai frequently pick something global and enormous, because the big topics are the ones in the news, and then discover in week five that every source is a press release.

A workable question usually has three properties. There is a specific system or intervention at its centre rather than a technology in general. There is a stakeholder group whose experience can be documented. And there is published material from more than one kind of source: an operator or regulator, a news or industry account, and something academic or statistical. A tutor who has read several projects through to submission can test a question against those three properties in one session, which is the single highest-value hour in the whole project.

The research itself is the student's work, and the line is not negotiable. A tutor asks questions about the draft, points out where a claim is unsupported, flags a source that will not hold, and teaches the student how to evaluate reliability. A tutor does not research the project, does not supply the sources, and does not write or rewrite any part of it. IB academic honesty rules make that a malpractice exposure for the student, and a page that offered otherwise would be selling your child a risk.

Scheduling matters as much as method. Dubai school calendars put internal project deadlines inside the same weeks as mock examinations for other subjects, and a student who leaves the project until that collision loses marks in both. Review blocks are planned backwards from the school's own submission date, with the question settled early in the first year and the bulk of the writing done before the mock window opens.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the May session: a two-year Digital Society plan
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session, and the calendar that actually governs a Diploma student is not the examination window but the sequence of internal deadlines before it. Entries are made by the school, usually in the autumn term of the second year, and the dates that matter to a family are the ones the school sets for drafts, mocks and submissions. We publish no specific IB examination or results date on this page: the IB's own site is the only source worth trusting for those, and your child's Diploma coordinator will have the school's version in writing.

What can be planned is the shape of the two years. The first year is content and method: building the example bank, learning the command terms, and settling the inquiry question. The second is consolidation and technique: finishing the project early, surviving mocks, and spending the final term on timed questions rather than new material. Students who invert this, leaving the project to the second year, end up revising and writing coursework in the same fortnight.

Higher Level students carry an additional load in the extension material on challenges and interventions, which has its own answer shape and cannot be absorbed in a revision week. Spreading it across the second year, a few hours a month, is far cheaper in both effort and money than a crash block in the final term. The table below sets out the sequence as it usually runs in a Dubai school year, without inventing dates that belong to the IB.

One practical note for families planning around the UAE calendar: Ramadan falls inside the Diploma teaching year, school hours shift, and energy levels change. Sessions can move later in the evening for the month, and most families find the week after is a better slot for a mock-style timed paper than the week before.

sections.heading: What Digital Society support costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: Dubai tutoring rates are public if you look, and the band for Diploma-level subject help runs roughly from AED 150 to AED 450 an hour depending on the tutor's experience and the format. At the lower end, EdFlik published rates from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour for budget online tutoring and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, both for general online support rather than Diploma subject specialists. In the middle, Unitors published IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Higher up, TutorChase published AED 270 an hour and Bestimate's 2026 rate survey put specialist IB and A-Level tutoring at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with examiner-level provision at AED 650 reported for BartyED. Those are the providers' own published figures as they stood in October 2026, not our prices.

A new subject prices differently from an established one, and families should understand why before they negotiate. The pool of people who have actually taught the current Digital Society guide through to a submitted inquiry project is small, so scarcity sits at the top of the band rather than the bottom. A cheaper generalist can help with essay structure and will not be able to tell you whether a research question will survive, which is the part of the course where money is best spent.

In-home tutoring in Dubai carries a travel premium, with Bestimate putting home visits at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors between AED 200 and AED 500. Some of that is the tutor's time in traffic rather than teaching. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so this is background for your decision rather than a service comparison: our UAE delivery is online, one-to-one, and the saving sits in access to a subject specialist rather than whoever lives a short drive away.

For context on the household budget, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package the Dubai Media Office valued at AED 1.5 billion within a larger AED 2.5 billion programme. A family planning tuition against a flat fee year has more room to think in terms of a focused block of hours around the project and the mocks than an open-ended weekly commitment.

sections.heading: Honesty in a course about artificial intelligence, and who may legally tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: Digital Society students spend part of the course studying generative artificial intelligence, which makes the academic-honesty question unusually live. The IB's position is about authenticity and acknowledgement rather than prohibition: the work submitted has to be the student's own, and any assistance or source has to be acknowledged. In practice the safe pattern is to treat an AI tool the way you would treat a conversation with a knowledgeable stranger. Use it to understand something, never to produce text that goes into an assessed piece, and record what you used and how. Your child's school will have its own written policy, and that policy governs.

What a tutor may do sits inside the same rule. A tutor teaches content, models technique, sets and marks practice questions, reads a draft and asks hard questions about it, and explains why a source will not hold. A tutor does not produce any part of assessed work, does not edit a draft to completion, and does not supply research the student should be doing. We say this on every page because two providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments, and buying one risks the student's Diploma, not just the mark.

There is also a licensing question Dubai parents ask less often than they should. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

Two further points worth knowing. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct runs along the same lines, so a request for your child's own class teacher is the wrong request to make. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different thing from an individual's permit. IB Gram runs no premises in the UAE and holds no regulator approval of any kind; what we do is match students to online tutors.

sections.heading: Where the subject leads: universities, equivalency and the Group 3 question
paragraphs: Parents ask whether a new subject will be read as a soft option, and the honest answer has two halves. Universities assess the Diploma as a whole and then look at the specific subjects a course requires. Digital Society is a Group 3 individuals and societies subject, so it satisfies that part of the Diploma's structure, and for a degree in media, law, business, politics or information management it is relevant content. For engineering or computer science degrees that specify a computing or mathematics prerequisite, it does not substitute for the subject the admissions page names.

The practical move is to read the entry requirements for the actual programmes on the student's list, including the UAE universities, and to do that in the first Diploma year rather than the second. Subject requirements are published by each institution and they change. A tutor can help a student read a requirements page properly, but no tutor should tell a family that a particular subject combination secures admission anywhere, and any provider who does is guessing with your child's options.

There is a separate UAE process families confuse with university admission: Ministry of Education equivalency, the recognition of a foreign school certificate for use inside the country. For the British track the requirements are published and specific, including five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the IB there is no figure we will publish here, because no points threshold has been read on an official Ministry source; check it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before you plan around it.

Equivalency is also not something a tutoring service performs, and nobody should imply it is. It is a government process with its own channel, it is not a reason to buy tutoring, and tutoring is not required for it. What a tutor can reasonably do is make sure a student is not caught out by a subject-count rule in the final year, which happens more often in Dubai than it should because the rule is widely misquoted. One ranking competitor currently publishes the wrong subject count for UAE candidates.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the deadline
process.description: A short message with the level, the school's next internal deadline and what the last report said is usually enough. If you have a marked piece of work, send it; a diagnostic that starts from real marking is worth more than a conversation about aims.

process.title: A free trial lesson, used as a diagnostic
process.description: Sixty minutes, one-to-one, online. The tutor works through one question and one piece of the student's own writing, then says plainly where the marks are going. No payment details are taken to book it, and there is no obligation after it.

process.title: A written plan with the first three targets
process.description: After the trial you get the tutor's read in writing: what is wrong, in what order it should be fixed, and roughly how many sessions each target needs. If the honest answer is that school support plus better practice would fix it, the plan says that.

process.title: Weekly sessions, with marking between them
process.description: Sessions run at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time. Work set in one session is marked before the next, and a short note after each session tells you what was covered and what the next target is. Slots move for Ramadan, travel and examination weeks.

process.title: Review the evidence, change the match if it is not working
process.description: Every four to six weeks, look at the marked work rather than the feeling. If scores and written answers have not moved, ask for a different tutor; a match that is not working is a scheduling problem, not a verdict on the student.

whyPoints.title: Tutors who have taught the current guide, not the legacy course
whyPoints.description: Digital Society is not ITGS with a new name. The concepts, content strands and assessment shape are different, and a tutor who has only taught the old course will coach the wrong answer structure. Ask directly, and ask whether they have taken a student through a submitted inquiry project.

whyPoints.title: Access rather than proximity
whyPoints.description: A Dubai family looking locally is choosing from the specialists who live within a reasonable drive. Online delivery removes that constraint, which matters most in a subject this new, where the number of people who have taught it through to submission is small anywhere in the world.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can check
whyPoints.description: Marked work, a written note after each session, and a visible error log. You should never have to take progress on trust, and after six weeks you should be able to read two answers side by side and see the difference without anyone explaining it to you.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and mark. They do not produce any part of an inquiry project, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. In a market where completed coursework is openly sold, that line is the thing protecting your child's Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that fits a Dubai week
whyPoints.description: Sessions sit after the school run and shift for Ramadan, travel and mock weeks without losing the slot. Families on a single-car school run in the villa communities tend to end up on weekend mornings, which works better for timed papers anyway.

whyPoints.title: Honesty about availability
whyPoints.description: If no Digital Society specialist is free at the hour you want, we say so and offer the nearest real option rather than putting a generalist in front of your child. A thin week is better than a wrong match in a subject where the subject-specific judgement is what you are buying.

faqs.question: Which UAE examples can my child actually use in a Digital Society answer?
faqs.answer: The useful ones are systems your child can research from official sources: the federal digital identity used for government services, the national artificial intelligence strategy and the ministerial portfolio created for it in 2017, the Personal Data Protection Law passed as Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, the delivery and ride-hailing platforms operating in Dubai, and household smart metering. Each one needs the operator, the data involved and the stakeholders verified from the organisation's own page before it goes into the example bank. Local examples are an advantage precisely because examiners rarely see them, but only if the detail is right.

faqs.question: What does a Digital Society marker mean by evidence?
faqs.answer: Something specific, real and current. Naming a company is not evidence. Naming the system that company runs, the data it depends on, who operates it and which stakeholders gain or lose is evidence. The test a tutor applies is whether the claim could be checked by someone reading the answer. A sentence beginning 'studies show' or 'many people believe' has no evidential weight in this subject, however confidently it is written. Students who move from general assertion to named systems usually see the clearest single jump in their marks, often within a month.

faqs.question: My son writes long, fluent answers and still scores in the middle. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answer is an essay rather than a response to the command term. Fluent writers describe at length where the question asked them to analyse or evaluate, and length cannot buy a band the command term has already capped. The second common cause is a single perspective argued well. A top-band answer carries the opposing case and resolves between the two. Both faults are structural rather than a knowledge gap, which is why they respond quickly to practice on short questions with immediate marking rather than to more content revision.

faqs.question: How many real-world examples does a Diploma student need by the final term?
faqs.answer: Around a dozen, properly annotated, will cover almost anything the papers can ask. Quality beats quantity: each entry should carry the system, who operates it, the data it uses, the concepts it illustrates, the contexts it sits in and one line on the counter-perspective. Thirty half-remembered news stories are worth less than twelve sourced entries the student can deploy under time pressure. Building that document is weekly homework a tutor checks, and it is the one revision asset that transfers across both papers and the Higher Level extension material.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child choose the inquiry project research question?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where tutoring earns its money. A tutor can test a proposed question against three things: whether there is a specific system at its centre, whether a stakeholder group's experience can be documented, and whether published material exists from more than one kind of source. That assessment takes one session and can save six weeks. What a tutor will not do is choose the topic for your child, supply the sources or write any part of the project. The research and the writing have to be the student's own work.

faqs.question: Does Digital Society count as a Group 3 subject for university applications?
faqs.answer: It is a Group 3 individuals and societies subject, so it satisfies that part of the Diploma's structure. Whether it satisfies a specific degree is a different question, and the answer lives on the admissions page of the actual programme. For media, law, business, politics or information management it is relevant content. For engineering or computer science degrees that name a computing or mathematics prerequisite, it does not replace the subject specified. Read the requirements for the programmes on your child's list during the first Diploma year, not the second.

faqs.question: Is Digital Society accepted for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: We publish no IB points threshold for equivalency, because no figure has been read on an official Ministry source and an unverified number would be worse than none. The published British-track rules are specific: five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels. For the IB route, check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a government process, it is not something a tutoring service performs, and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: How do online sessions work for a subject with this much reading?
faqs.answer: Better than for most subjects, because everything the course studies lives on a screen already. A session opens the platform, dataset, policy document or news coverage being discussed, annotates the student's draft in the same window, and leaves the marked version behind afterwards. Reading is set between sessions with a specific output attached, usually one new example-bank entry or one timed question. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai, and the trade-off is access to a specialist rather than proximity.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes, one-to-one, online, used as a diagnostic rather than a sample lesson. The tutor works through one question with the student and reads one piece of their recent writing, then says plainly where the marks are going: knowledge, structure or evidence. You get that read in writing afterwards with the first three targets in order. No payment details are taken to book the trial and there is no obligation after it. If the honest conclusion is that school support plus better practice would fix the problem, the write-up says so.

faqs.question: How often should sessions run during the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: One session a week is the usual pattern, following whatever the school is teaching, with a timed question marked between sessions. Weekly works because the bottleneck in year one is method rather than content, and method needs repetition on fresh material. Twice-weekly is rarely the right answer that early; it tends to replace the student's own practice. The pattern that changes is around the inquiry project and the mock window, where families typically switch to a fixed block of four to six sessions planned backwards from the school's own deadline.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor help with the Theory of Knowledge essay as well?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and the overlap is genuine: the Theory of Knowledge questions about evidence, technology and knowledge map closely onto Digital Society content, and the essay rewards the same discipline of claim, support and counter-claim. Where one tutor covers both, sessions usually alternate by deadline rather than splitting each hour. The same limit applies to both pieces of work: the tutor discusses, questions and gives feedback on the student's own drafting, and never produces text that goes into an assessed submission.

faqs.question: How can I check that a Dubai tutor is permitted to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and ask to see it. The permit is issued free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring privately without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted at you as unverified.

faqs.question: How does the Ramadan timetable change a weekly Digital Society session?
faqs.answer: School hours shift during Ramadan and most families move the session later in the evening for the month, often after iftar. The slot is held rather than cancelled, because a month's gap in the first Diploma year costs more than a month of shorter sessions. What usually changes is the content: less new material, more consolidation and example-bank work, which carries a lighter cognitive load. Families planning a mock-style timed paper tend to find the week after Ramadan a better fit than the week before it.

faqs.question: What happens if no Digital Society specialist is free at the time we want?
faqs.answer: We say so. The honest options are a different slot with the right tutor, a short wait, or a tutor whose subject background is adjacent with that stated openly before you decide. What we will not do is put a generalist in front of a Digital Society student and let you discover the gap in week four, because the subject-specific judgement is the thing you are paying for. This subject is newer than most, so the pool of people who have taught the current guide through to a submitted inquiry project is genuinely small.

faqs.question: Should my child take Digital Society at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: The decision usually turns on two things: whether the student can sustain the extension material on challenges and interventions across the second year, and what the rest of their Higher Level combination looks like. The extension needs its own answer shape and cannot be absorbed in a revision week, so it suits a student who is already comfortable with evaluation rather than one still fighting the command terms. Talk to the subject teacher before the entry deadline in the autumn term of year two, because late level changes are harder than families expect.

dubai/ib-dp-digital-society-tutor.closingHeading: Start with a diagnostic, not a commitment
dubai/ib-dp-digital-society-tutor.closingBody: If your child is losing marks in Digital Society, the useful first step is finding out which kind of mark is going missing. Send the most recent marked piece of work, the level, and the date of the next deadline the school has set. The trial lesson is free, no payment details are taken to book it, and what you get afterwards is a written read on where the marks are and what order to fix things in. Sessions are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to your Dubai school week. If the answer is that your child does not need a tutor, we will say that too.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-hl-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are Economics specialists who teach the Diploma Programme course at Higher Level, including the Paper 3 policy paper and the three-commentary portfolio. Each one works from your child's own school scheme of work, and each sends a written record of what was marked after every lesson.

intro.heading: Why Dubai Economics HL families ask for evidence before they ask for a tutor
paragraphs: A Dubai parent looking for an IB DP Economics HL home tutor is usually reacting to a specific document: a DP1 report with a 4 in Economics, a mock paper that came back with an unexplained 11 out of 25, or a first commentary that the teacher described as "descriptive". The question behind the search is not really about tutoring. It is about whether anyone can show, in writing, why the marks are where they are and what would change them.

That is a reasonable thing to ask, and Economics HL happens to be a subject where it is answerable. The course is assessed through four separate instruments with published weightings, and each one fails in a different, diagnosable way. A student can know every definition in Unit 2 and still lose six marks in Paper 1 part (b) because no evaluation appears in the final paragraph. A student can draw a flawless externality diagram and lose a criterion A mark because the axes are unlabelled. These are not vague problems, and they do not need a motivational conversation. They need a marked script and a second attempt.

So this page is built around evidence rather than around a sales argument. Below you will find the HL assessment structure with the weighting on each component, the five places where HL students most often lose marks, the IA criteria set out by letter with the marks attached to each, the market rate for Economics tutoring in Dubai in AED with its source named, and a sixteen-week schedule counted backwards from the May session showing what a parent should be able to see at each stage. If a tutoring arrangement is working, each of those stages produces a document you can read.

The practical point about delivery: tutoring for families in Dubai is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE — sending a tutor to a residence is a service we run only in India. For Economics HL that constraint turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise. Economics HL is a comparatively thin market. The number of people in Dubai who can teach the Paper 3 policy recommendation properly and mark a commentary against the 2022 criteria is small, and most of them are already employed full time at a school in Emirates Hills or Deira. Online delivery means the match is made on subject depth rather than on who can reach Jumeirah by 16:30 on a Tuesday.

It also means the record is kept automatically. A lesson over live video can be recorded with the family's consent, the annotated script is a file rather than a sheet of paper left on a kitchen table, and the mark history sits in one place from DP1 term one to the final session before study leave. Parents who have tried an in-home arrangement in Dubai often say the same thing about it: the lessons may well have been good, but there was nothing to look at afterwards.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-hl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Economics HL sits at the end of a route that usually starts in MYP Individuals and Societies. Where a student joined that route changes what the first weeks of support have to cover, so the four programme entries below describe the handover rather than the brochure.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Economics is a group 3 subject taken at Higher or Standard Level across two years. At HL the course covers the same four units as SL — introduction, microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy — plus HL extension content including market power, asymmetric information, the Keynesian multiplier and the Marshall-Lerner condition. Assessment is three written papers plus a portfolio of three internally assessed commentaries.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma is the minority route by enrolment: KHDA's 2024-25 figures put International Baccalaureate students at 7% of the private-school population against 37% UK curriculum. That ratio matters for Economics HL because a DP2 cohort at a Dubai school is often small enough that the subject is taught by one teacher with no second specialist to ask.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies in MYP 4 and 5 is where most future Economics HL students meet supply, demand and market structures for the first time. MYP assessment runs on four criteria marked 1-8 against task-specific descriptors, which is a different instrument from a DP mark scheme. Students arriving in DP1 from MYP are usually fluent in investigation and weak in the short, precise definitional answers Paper 2 rewards.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai IB schools run MYP through to Year 11 without IGCSE, so a DP1 Economics class in Al Barsha or Nad Al Sheba can contain students with no external examination experience at all. The first marked Paper 2 of DP1 is often their first timed external-style paper, and the gap shows in timing rather than in understanding.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines DP courses with a career-related study and four compulsory components. A CP student may take Economics SL or HL as one of their DP courses, in which case the subject is assessed exactly as it is for a full Diploma candidate. The difference is workload shape: CP students carry a reflective project alongside the commentaries, and the two deadlines often land in the same fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: CP is offered by a small number of Dubai schools and the Economics cohort within it can be two or three students. Where a school runs CP Economics alongside DP Economics in one timetabled class, the commentary deadlines are set once for everybody, which is worth knowing before DP1 term two.

programmes.name: IGCSE and Year 11 into DP1
programmes.description: Most Dubai students reaching Economics HL arrive from IGCSE rather than MYP, often from Cambridge Economics 0455 or Business Studies 0450. The transition has a specific shape: IGCSE rewards accurate recall and clear explanation, while Paper 1 part (b) at HL awards marks for weighing one effect against another. Students who scored a 9 at IGCSE by writing complete explanations frequently stall at 9-11 out of 15 on the HL evaluation band.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's British-curriculum schools dominate by enrolment, so the IGCSE-to-DP1 handover is the common case here rather than the exception. A student who finished 0455 in June and starts Economics HL in late August has roughly nine weeks of overlap content before the course moves past anything IGCSE covered.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-hl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Economics HL is the subject in the URL, and the list below starts there. The other entries are the subjects Dubai DP students most often pair with it, with the specific assessment pressure each one adds to the same two years.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.levels: HL (the subject of this page) and SL
subjects.description: Four units plus HL extensions. Assessed by Paper 1 extended response, Paper 2 data response, Paper 3 policy paper and a portfolio of three commentaries. HL-only content includes market power, asymmetric information, the inability of markets to achieve equity, the Keynesian multiplier, terms of trade and the Marshall-Lerner condition with the J-curve effect.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Shares Economics HL's diagram discipline but assesses differently: a business research project at HL, a pre-released case study for Paper 1, and tools such as Ansoff, BCG and break-even that have to be applied rather than described. Students taking both subjects often transplant Economics evaluation language into Business answers, where the command terms want something more operational.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The common pairing for Economics HL students heading towards a quantitative degree. The overlap is real but narrow: differentiation supports marginal analysis, and the statistics content helps with Paper 3 calculation questions. AA HL's proof and complex-number work has no Economics application, which surprises students who expected the two subjects to carry each other.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is the more frequent partner for Economics HL at Dubai schools, and the better fit for Paper 3. Regression, correlation and the use of a graphic display calculator map directly onto data-response work. Some UAE and UK university economics programmes specify AA rather than AI, so the route choice should be checked against the named course before DP1 subject selection closes.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: The closest group 3 neighbour to Economics in content, through the global interactions and resource topics. Geography's internal assessment is a fieldwork report, which means a student taking both subjects faces a field report and three commentaries in the same academic year. Mapping both deadline sets onto one calendar in DP1 term two prevents the usual February collision.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Shares the global economy unit's territory from the other direction, and the HL extension work involves an oral presentation on a political issue. Economics students often find the engagement activity easier than their commentaries because the source material is self-selected; the transferable skill is the discipline of linking a claim to a named piece of evidence.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The most common group 3 second choice at Dubai IB schools after Business Management. Its Paper 2 and Paper 3 essays reward sustained argument, which supports Economics Paper 1 part (b) directly. The risk runs the other way: History students write long, and Economics Paper 1 gives roughly 45 minutes for the second part of one question.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Behavioural content in the Economics course gives these two subjects an unexpected overlap, particularly around rationality assumptions. Psychology's experimental internal assessment teaches a method of evidence handling that transfers well to commentary writing, where the weakest drafts assert an effect without showing the mechanism.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: ESS covers common pool resources and sustainability from an ecological standpoint, which is the same ground as the Economics market-failure unit. Students taking both can reuse one body of reading across two subjects, provided the written work is independent — reusing a passage across two subjects is a malpractice question, not an efficiency.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Not an obvious Economics partner, but the HL essay and the paper 1 analysis both train the skill Economics commentaries most often lack: reading a text closely enough to quote the precise clause that supports the point. Commentary criterion C marks are lost more often to loose paraphrase of the article than to weak theory.

sections.heading: What a parent searching for an Economics HL home tutor in Dubai is really asking for
paragraphs: The literal answer first. An IB DP Economics HL home tutor in Dubai, as the market uses the phrase, means a specialist who works with one student on the Higher Level Diploma Economics course at a time and place the family chooses. In practice in this city that has come to mean two different products: a tutor who travels to a residence in Mirdif or Arabian Ranches, charging a rate that includes the travel; or a tutor who teaches the same course one-to-one over live video at the same hour of the evening. IB Gram sells the second. Home visits are an India-only service and no page on this site offers them in the UAE.

Underneath the search term, though, the request is usually narrower than "a tutor". A parent who types this phrase has generally already seen something concrete: a predicted grade of 4 against a university offer that wants 6, a commentary returned with the comment that it lacks evaluation, or a Paper 3 mock where the student lost most of the calculation marks. What they want is somebody who can look at that specific document and say what is wrong with it.

Economics HL rewards that approach because the course is unusually transparent about where its marks sit. Four assessed components, each with a published weighting. Paper 1 part (a) wants explanation with a diagram; part (b) wants a judgement supported by the explanation. Paper 2 wants short definitional accuracy early and a 15-mark evaluation at the end that uses the provided text. Paper 3 wants arithmetic that is right, and then a policy choice that is defended. The IA wants five criteria met across three separate commentaries. None of that is mysterious, and none of it improves by being talked about in general terms.

So the structure of this page follows the evidence rather than the pitch. The next section sets out the HL components with weightings; after that comes the mark-loss analysis, the IA criteria by letter, the market rate in AED with its source, and a schedule counted backwards from the May session. Read them as a checklist you can hold any Economics tutor to, including ours.
bullets: The phrase describes a delivery format; the underlying request is diagnostic

Every component fails in a different and nameable way

sections.heading: The HL assessment structure, component by component
paragraphs: Economics at Higher Level is assessed through three external papers and one internal portfolio. Paper 1 is an extended-response paper of 1 hour 15 minutes in which the student answers one question from a choice, in two parts: an explanation worth 10 marks and a judgement worth 15. Paper 2 is a data-response paper of 1 hour 45 minutes, again one question from a choice, worth 40 marks in total and structured as a series of short parts building to a final 15-mark evaluation that must draw on the provided text and data.

Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level and is where the HL grade is most often decided. It is a 1 hour 45 minute policy paper with two compulsory questions, each carrying quantitative work and a part that asks the student to recommend and justify a policy response using the material supplied. The arithmetic is not hard in isolation — elasticity coefficients, tax incidence, multiplier values, terms of trade — but it is unforgiving, and a wrong figure early in a question can carry through several parts.

The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries, each on an article the student selects, each addressing a different unit of the syllabus, each limited to 800 words and each marked out of 15. The portfolio is marked internally by the school and moderated externally. At HL it carries 20% of the final grade; at SL the same portfolio carries 30%, which is the single biggest structural difference between the two levels and the reason an HL student cannot afford to treat Paper 3 as an afterthought.

Put together, the external papers carry 80% of an HL Economics grade and the portfolio carries 20%. The weightings matter for planning: a student with a strong portfolio and a weak Paper 3 is in a worse position than the reverse, because Paper 3 is worth 30% on its own and the portfolio closes in DP2 term two while Paper 3 is sat in the examination session. Always confirm current weightings, timings and rubric wording against the published subject guide on ibo.org or with your school's DP coordinator before planning around them.

sections.heading: Where Economics HL marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Five failure modes account for most of the gap between a 4 and a 6 in HL Economics, and each is visible on a marked script. The first is the evaluation band in the 15-mark parts. A student explains an effect clearly, then concludes by restating it. The command term asked them to discuss, evaluate or assess, which requires weighing the effect against a counter-effect, a time horizon, a magnitude or an assumption. A paragraph that begins "however, in the short run" and ends with a reasoned preference is the difference between 9 and 13 out of 15.

The second is diagram integrity. Economics diagrams carry marks for axes, labels, correct shifts and an indicated equilibrium, and they carry further marks for being referred to in the prose. A correct diagram that the text never mentions is decorative. The third is data neglect in Paper 2: the paper supplies a text and figures precisely so the final answer can quote them, and answers that could have been written without ever reading the extract cap themselves in the middle band.

The fourth is Paper 3 arithmetic. Elasticity signs, percentage-change bases, the split of an indirect tax between producer and consumer, the value of the multiplier from a marginal propensity — these are routine calculations under no time pressure and they are repeatedly lost through rounding, unit confusion or a dropped negative. They are also the easiest marks on the HL paper to secure, because they are drillable to near-certainty in six or seven sessions.

The fifth is the commentary that reads as a summary of the article. Criterion C rewards application and analysis of theory to the specific situation in the source; a paragraph that paraphrases the journalist earns little. The fix is mechanical: every paragraph of a commentary should contain a piece of economic theory, a piece of the article, and a sentence connecting them. A tutor marking a draft against the criteria will tell you which paragraphs fail that test, and the student rewrites those paragraphs themselves.

sections.heading: The internal assessment, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The Economics internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries. Each responds to a published article, each addresses a different syllabus unit, each is capped at 800 words and each is marked out of 15 across five criteria. The total is 45 raw marks, scaled to 20% of the Higher Level grade. Because the criteria are published, a draft can be scored before the school ever sees it, and the student can be told precisely which criterion is costing them.

In practice the marks cluster. Criterion A, on diagrams, is usually either full or near-full once a student has been shown that an unlabelled axis costs a mark. Criterion B, on terminology, is similar: use the term, use it correctly, use it where it belongs. Criterion C, application and analysis, is where competent students sit in the middle band, because they explain theory accurately in the abstract and connect it loosely to the article. Criterion D requires the chosen key concept to be genuinely woven through rather than named in the introduction. Criterion E, evaluation, is the one most often simply absent from a first draft.

The honest boundary matters here more than anywhere else on this page. A tutor may teach the theory, explain the criteria, question a draft, point at a paragraph that does not connect to the article and ask what the student thinks is missing. A tutor may not write any part of the commentary, rewrite a paragraph, supply sentences to paste in, or edit a draft to completion. Under IB academic-honesty rules that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student: a withheld Diploma, not a refunded invoice. Any service offering to supply a finished Internal Assessment is selling your child's candidacy.

A workable cycle runs to three or four passes per commentary. Pass one checks the article: is it inside the permitted publication window, is it from a different source than the other two, does it actually contain enough economics for the chosen unit. Pass two scores the structure. Pass three scores the draft against all five criteria in writing. Pass four checks compliance — word count, cover sheet, diagram labels, citation. Always verify the current rubric, word limit and article-window rules against the live subject guide on ibo.org or with the school's teacher before submitting.
