sections.heading: What a marked script tells you that a school report does not
paragraphs: A Dubai school report gives you a predicted grade, an attainment grade and a sentence or two of comment. It is a summary produced for a cohort, and it is accurate at the level it operates. What it cannot tell you is why the number is what it is. A 4 in Economics HL can come from weak macroeconomics, from strong understanding ruined by timing, from a Paper 3 calculation problem, or from writing that never evaluates. Those four students need four different interventions, and the report looks the same for all of them.

A marked script tells you which one you have. When a tutor returns a Paper 2 attempt with the marks itemised part by part, the shape of the loss is visible: full marks on parts (a) to (d), half marks on the calculation, three out of fifteen on the final evaluation. That is not a grade, it is a diagnosis, and it points at one fixable behaviour. Three such scripts across a month tell you whether the behaviour is changing.

This is why a working arrangement should produce documents, and why IB Gram's Economics HL sessions end with something written. A marked timed question. A commentary draft scored A to E. A diagram set with the deductions circled. A short note of what the next session will cover and why. The parent does not need to understand price elasticity to read any of that; they need to see that this week's loss is not the same as last week's.

Set a plain test for any tutoring arrangement in Dubai, ours included. After four weeks, ask to see the marked work. If the answer is that lessons are going well and the student seems more confident, the arrangement may still be worth keeping, but you have no evidence either way. If the answer is a folder of annotated scripts with the mark on each, you can judge for yourself whether the trend goes up.

sections.heading: Sixteen weeks to the May session, counted backwards
paragraphs: Dubai IB schools sit the May examination session, and the useful way to plan Economics HL support is backwards from it rather than forwards from today. The table below counts in weeks before the session opens rather than in dates, for one reason: IB session and results dates in this project are not independently verified, because ibo.org blocks automated retrieval. Confirm every date with your school's DP coordinator or on ibo.org directly before you build a plan on it.

What the backwards count exposes is how early the portfolio stops being available as a lever. The three commentaries are internally deadlined and moderated; by the time a DP2 student is sixteen weeks from the session, the portfolio is usually finished and the 20% it carries is fixed. Everything still in play from that point is examination technique across three papers — which is good news, because examination technique moves faster under focused work than understanding does.

The count also catches two Dubai-specific collisions. Ramadan falls inside the UAE academic year and shortens school days, which changes when revision can realistically happen; the practical answer is usually a shift to post-Iftar sessions rather than a pause. And the Dubai school calendar's spring break lands close enough to the session that families routinely travel during the period they had mentally reserved for revision. Both are manageif planned in January, and neither is manageable in April.

Use the row that matches where your child is now. A student at twelve weeks out with a Paper 3 problem has time for a full calculation block and six timed papers. A student at four weeks out has time for timed practice on the two components with the heaviest weighting and nothing else; attempting to rebuild macroeconomics understanding in that window costs marks elsewhere.

sections.heading: What Economics HL tutoring costs in Dubai, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Dubai has a wide and poorly documented tutoring market. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The figures below are market bands in AED, attributed to the source that published them, and they are not IB Gram's price list. Our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and the rate for a specific subject and level is quoted after that conversation.

Four things move the number in this emirate specifically. Level is the first: Higher Level commands more than Standard Level because the HL extension content and Paper 3 narrow the pool of people who can teach it. Format is the second, and it is the largest single factor — an in-home visit in Dubai prices in the tutor's travel time across a city where a cross-town trip at 17:00 can take 50 minutes, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 against lower online bands.

The third factor is proximity to the session. Rates quoted in February for an April start are generally higher than the same arrangement booked in September, because supply of specialists who can teach Paper 3 is fixed and demand is not. The fourth is the coursework question: commentary review is a different kind of work from teaching a unit, it is slower per hour, and it is priced accordingly by most providers.

Context worth holding alongside the rate: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. School fees being flat does not make tutoring cheaper, but it does mean a tutoring budget set last year is not being squeezed from the other direction. The sensible comparison is not the hourly rate but the total cost of the plan — two sessions a week for twelve weeks is a number a family can actually assess.

sections.heading: Online versus an in-home Economics tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: This comparison deserves a straight answer rather than a defence, because the two formats genuinely differ and the honest case for online in Economics HL rests on one specific fact: scarcity. Dubai is a large market for tutoring and a small market for this particular subject at this particular level. The people who can mark a commentary against criterion E and drill terms-of-trade calculations are few, and a family restricted to tutors who can physically reach Mirdif by 17:30 is choosing from a fraction of that already small group.

An in-home arrangement has real advantages and it is worth naming them. A tutor in the room can see a student's working as it happens without any technology in between, can pick up a pen, and can read the mood of a 17-year-old who says they are fine. For younger students and for subjects where the work is physical, those advantages are substantial. IB Gram does not sell that format in the UAE: it is available from us only in India, and a Dubai family that wants a tutor in the room should hire locally and will pay the market's in-home band for it.

What online gives an Economics HL student is specific rather than general. The tutor is chosen for the subject rather than for the postcode. Screen-sharing suits diagram work, because a shifted curve can be drawn, undone and redrawn in seconds and the final version saved. Annotated scripts arrive as files that accumulate rather than as paper that is lost. Sessions can be recorded with consent, which matters most in the fortnight before a session when a student wants the Paper 3 explanation again. And no part of the hour is spent on travel, by anybody.

The scheduling point is not trivial in this city. A 90-minute in-home session in Dubai Marina booked for 17:00 commonly occupies a tutor from 16:10 to 19:05, and that cost sits inside the rate whether or not it appears as a line item. Online, the hour is the hour. Families who switch usually report the same two changes: more consistent attendance, and a visible pile of marked work.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what an Economics tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Economics HL carries 20% of its grade in work that must be the student's own, and this SERP contains services that sell completed Internal Assessments outright. One of them was found during research advertising finished IAs at a fixed price. Buying one is not a shortcut with a financial downside; it is malpractice under IB rules, and the sanction falls on the candidate. A Diploma can be withheld. That risk is carried entirely by the 17-year-old, not by the vendor.

The permitted boundary is wide enough to be genuinely useful, which is what makes the breach unnecessary. A tutor may teach any theory in the syllabus. A tutor may explain each criterion and what the descriptors mean. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and score it against the published criteria. A tutor may say that paragraph four asserts an effect without a mechanism, and ask the student what the mechanism is. A tutor may check that an article falls inside the permitted window and suits the chosen unit. A tutor may teach how to label a diagram so criterion A is secure.

A tutor may not write any part of the commentary, supply sentences for insertion, rewrite a paragraph, choose the article on the student's behalf and hand over a plan, or edit a draft until it is finished. The practical test we use is simple: feedback is given as questions and scores, and the keyboard stays with the student. If a tutoring conversation ever produces text that the student did not compose, the line has been crossed regardless of intention.

The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay and to TOK, and it applies to past-paper material too. Published mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge or Pearson; they are referenced and linked, not reproduced or distributed as downloads. Any provider offering a library of mark schemes to take away is answering a different question from the one about your child's grade.
bullets: Permitted: teaching theory, explaining criteria, scoring drafts, asking questions
Not permitted: writing, rewriting, supplying text, or editing to completion
The sanction for malpractice falls on the student, not the provider

sections.heading: KHDA, your school's reporting, and what to ask at the next meeting
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a rating on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Dubai's private sector carried 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, with International Baccalaureate students at 7% of enrolment.

What an inspection rating tells an Economics HL parent is limited and worth understanding precisely. The judgement covers the school, across all phases and subjects. It does not tell you how the Diploma Economics class is staffed this year, whether the HL extension content is taught separately from the SL cohort, or whether the teacher marking your child's commentaries has taught the subject before. In a minority subject at a school where IB is 7% of the city's enrolment, those are the facts that affect the grade.

IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and no page on this site should be read as claiming otherwise. KHDA's Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes operating premises in Dubai; we operate none. Separately, individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. A parent can ask any tutor whether they hold one.

Three questions are worth taking to the next parents' meeting, and all three are answerable. Who teaches HL extension content, and is it timetabled separately from the SL group? When are the internal commentary deadlines for each of the three pieces, in writing? And by which component was the mock grade reached — Paper 1, Paper 2, Paper 3 or the portfolio? The third question is the one that tells you what to do next, and it is the one least often asked.

sections.heading: Equivalency, universities and why the Economics HL grade is being chased
paragraphs: Behind most Economics HL enquiries from Dubai sits a university condition. A UK offer that specifies 6 in Economics HL, a Dutch or Canadian programme with a points requirement, or a UAE institution that needs the Diploma attested. The grade is being chased for a reason, and the reason determines how much of the plan should be about marks versus about paperwork.

For families planning to use the Diploma inside the UAE, there is a separate process: the Ministry of Education's equivalency and attestation route for secondary certificates. IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency, and no tutoring is required for it. For British-curriculum students the published requirements are specific — five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes six subjects rather than five.

For the IB route specifically, no points threshold is published here, because none has been read on the Ministry's own pages during research for this project. That is a deliberate omission rather than an oversight: an unsourced equivalency figure repeated across a large set of pages is a large number of wrong answers. Check the requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, and treat any site that states an IB figure without citing the Ministry with caution.

The route choice that does interact with Economics HL is mathematics. Several economics degrees specify Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation, while Paper 3's statistical work sits closer to AI. A student intending to read economics at a quantitative department should check the named programme's stated requirement before DP1 subject selection closes, and the Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City enquiries we see suggest this check is often made a year too late.

process.title: Send the evidence, not a description
process.description: The useful opening message contains a marked paper, a returned commentary or a report with component grades, plus the school and the DP year. From those documents the first conversation can be about the specific loss rather than about general study habits. Nothing is needed beyond what the school has already given you.

process.title: Free trial lesson with an Economics HL specialist
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video, at no cost and with no card details taken. The tutor works through a real question with your child and returns a short written note: what was understood, what was not, and which component the marks are coming from. If the match is wrong, say so and a different tutor is proposed.

process.title: A written plan against the weightings
process.description: A short plan naming which component the work targets, the number of sessions, and the order of topics. For a DP2 student in January this usually means Paper 3 calculations before anything else, because it carries 30% and improves fastest. The plan says what evidence will exist at four weeks.

process.title: Weekly sessions that end in marked work
process.description: A fixed slot on Gulf Standard Time, with a timed question marked between lessons. Each marked script shows the mark, the band and the specific lost marks. Commentary drafts come back scored against criteria A to E with written reasons, and the revision is done by the student.

process.title: Review at four weeks against the mark record
process.description: Four weeks in, the marked work is read together: has the component trend moved, and is the same error recurring. If the trend is flat, the plan changes or the tutor changes. This review is the point of keeping records, and it is a conversation about documents rather than impressions.

whyPoints.title: The work is visible
whyPoints.description: Every session produces something readable: a marked script with the mark on it, a commentary scored by criterion, a diagram set with deductions circled. A parent who cannot explain price elasticity can still see whether this month's Paper 2 evaluation mark is higher than last month's.

whyPoints.title: Matched on Economics HL, not on location
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run online, the tutor is chosen for the ability to teach Paper 3 and mark against criterion E rather than for proximity to your community. In a subject this thin in Dubai, that is the difference between a specialist and a generalist who is nearby.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Commentary support is feedback on the student's own drafts, given as scores and questions. We do not write, rewrite or complete assessed work, and we say so on the page rather than in the small print. The risk of malpractice falls on the candidate, which makes the boundary non-negotiable.

whyPoints.title: Sessions built around the Dubai calendar
whyPoints.description: Slots start after school-run and sport commitments, shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan rather than pausing, and are planned around the spring break that sits close to the May session. Scheduling is the most common reason tutoring stops working in this city.

whyPoints.title: Figures carry a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, and marked as market rate rather than ours. Regulatory statements cite u.ae, KHDA or MoHRE. Where a fact could not be sourced — IB session dates, an IB equivalency threshold — it is left out.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer about availability
whyPoints.description: Economics HL specialists are a limited pool and sometimes none is free in the slot a family wants. We say so and offer the next realistic start, rather than booking a generalist into an HL Paper 3 brief and leaving the family to discover the gap in March.

faqs.question: How is IB Economics HL assessed, and what is each component worth?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Economics is assessed through three external papers and one internal portfolio. Paper 1 is an extended-response paper of 1 hour 15 minutes carrying 20%. Paper 2 is a data-response paper of 1 hour 45 minutes carrying 30%. Paper 3, which exists only at Higher Level, is a 1 hour 45 minute policy paper also carrying 30%. The internal assessment portfolio of three commentaries carries the remaining 20%. The external papers therefore account for 80% of the grade. Confirm current weightings and timings against the published subject guide on ibo.org or with your school's DP coordinator before planning around them.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 actually ask an Economics HL student to do?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is the Higher Level policy paper: two compulsory questions, each combining quantitative work with a requirement to recommend and justify a policy response using the material supplied. The calculations are routine in isolation — elasticity coefficients, the split of an indirect tax, a multiplier value, terms of trade — but they are unforgiving, and one wrong figure early can carry through later parts. The recommendation part is where most marks are lost, because students name a policy without defending it against an alternative or stating its limitations. It is the most drillable component on the HL course.

faqs.question: How many Economics commentaries does my child write, and how long is each one?
faqs.answer: The portfolio is three commentaries. Each responds to a published article the student selects, each addresses a different unit of the syllabus, and each is capped at 800 words. Each is marked out of 15 across five criteria, giving 45 raw marks in total, scaled to 20% of the Higher Level grade. The articles must come from different sources and fall within the publication window the subject guide specifies. Compliance failures — an article outside the window, a commentary over the word limit, a missing cover sheet — cost marks before any economics is assessed. Verify current rules in the live subject guide.

faqs.question: Which Economics IA criterion loses the most marks in a first draft?
faqs.answer: Criterion E, evaluation, carries four marks and is usually the weakest part of a first draft — often one or two out of four, because the commentary explains an effect and then stops rather than weighing it against a counter-effect, a time horizon or an assumption. Criterion D, the key concept, is the second most common loss: the concept is named in the opening paragraph and never carried into the analysis. Criteria A and B, diagrams and terminology, are usually recoverable in a single conversation once a student knows that an unlabelled axis costs a mark.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's Economics HL past papers the way an examiner would?
faqs.answer: A tutor can mark a timed attempt against the published assessment criteria and band descriptors, itemise where the marks were lost, and show which band the answer sits in and why. That is useful and it is what our sessions produce. What nobody outside the examination process can do is replicate an actual examiner's judgement or know unreleased grade boundaries. We also do not describe tutors as current IB examiners unless that status can be evidenced, and examiner status gives no access to marking, boundaries or paper content in any case.

faqs.question: How will I know the Economics HL grade is genuinely moving?
faqs.answer: By reading the marked work rather than asking for an impression. Each session returns a timed question with the mark on it, so after four weeks there is a short series of scores for the same component. If Paper 2 final-part marks have gone from 3 to 7 to 9 out of 15, the trend is visible without any economics knowledge. If every script shows the same recurring error, the plan needs changing. We review that record with you at four weeks and change the plan or the tutor if the trend is flat.

faqs.question: Is Economics HL harder than Economics SL in a way that matters for a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two concrete ways. Higher Level adds extension content — market power, asymmetric information, the Keynesian multiplier, terms of trade, the Marshall-Lerner condition — and it adds Paper 3, worth 30% on its own. The portfolio stays the same three commentaries but carries 20% at HL against 30% at SL, so a strong portfolio covers less of the grade. In Dubai schools where HL and SL sit in one timetabled class, the extension content is often taught in separate sessions, and those are the first to be compressed when a term runs short.

faqs.question: What does an Economics HL tutor charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates for IB specialist tutoring in Dubai run roughly AED 200-450 per hour online according to Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Unitors starting IB tuition at AED 200. In-home one-to-one sits higher, around AED 180-350 in that same table and up to AED 500 from independent home tutors, because the rate absorbs cross-city travel. Those are market figures, not ours. IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and quotes for the specific subject, level and session length after it.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our villa in Dubai for Economics HL lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a residence is a service we run only in India. Economics HL tuition for Dubai families is delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-sharing for diagram work and annotated scripts returned as files. The URL you arrived from uses the phrase parents search, and we would rather answer it honestly than sell a format we do not run. If you want a tutor physically in the room, hire locally and expect the in-home market band.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 at a KHDA-inspected school. Is it too early to start Economics HL support?
faqs.answer: DP1 is the point at which support changes the most, because the portfolio is still open. By the time a DP2 student is sixteen weeks from the May session the three commentaries are usually submitted and the 20% they carry is fixed. Starting in DP1 means article selection can be checked before writing, drafts can be scored against the criteria with time to revise, and the HL extension content can be met before the class reaches it. It also spreads the work, which matters when the commentary deadlines collide with another subject's internal assessment.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help with the Economics IA without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is specific. A tutor may teach the theory, explain each criterion, check that a chosen article falls inside the permitted window and suits the unit, read a draft the student has written, score it against criteria A to E, and ask what is missing from a paragraph. A tutor may not write any part of the commentary, supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph or edit a draft to completion. Our test is that feedback is given as scores and questions and the keyboard stays with the student. Malpractice sanctions fall on the candidate.

faqs.question: How do you fit Economics HL sessions around Dubai school hours and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Slots usually start between 16:30 and 19:00 Gulf Standard Time, set by the area: communities with schools inside them can take 16:30, while Marina and JLT families with long northbound commutes generally want 18:00 or later. During Ramadan the UAE school day shortens and the practical answer is to move sessions to post-Iftar timing rather than pause, since pausing in a DP2 spring costs weeks that cannot be recovered. The Dubai spring break sits close to the May session, so travel plans are worth mapping onto the revision schedule in January.

faqs.question: Does Economics HL count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process and tutoring is no part of it. For British-curriculum students the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the IB route no points threshold is stated on this page, because none was read on the Ministry's own pages during research. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly, and be wary of sites quoting an unsourced IB figure.

faqs.question: What happens if no Economics HL specialist is free when we enquire?
faqs.answer: We say so and give you the next realistic start date, rather than placing a generalist into a Higher Level brief. Economics HL at the level that includes Paper 3 calculation work and criterion-level commentary feedback is a limited pool, and demand concentrates in the months before the May session. If the gap matters, the usual options are a different weekly slot, a shorter focused block on a single component, or a start date with a specific tutor named. Availability is disclosed before any payment, not discovered in March.

faqs.question: How many weeks of Economics HL support does a DP2 student usually need before the May session?
faqs.answer: It depends which component is weak, and that is why the first conversation asks for marked work. A Paper 3 calculation problem is typically six to eight focused sessions, because the question types are finite and drillable. A missing evaluation habit in the 15-mark parts takes longer, around ten to twelve weeks of weekly timed practice with marking, because it is a writing behaviour rather than a knowledge gap. Rebuilding macroeconomics understanding from a low base needs a term. A student four weeks out should work only on the heaviest-weighted component.

No card details are taken for the trial. If the match is wrong, tell us and we will propose a different tutor. If it is right, you will have a folder of marked work to read inside a month.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-hl-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Economics at Higher Level: the four units, the Higher Level extensions including the theory of the firm, the Keynesian multiplier and the Phillips curve, and the quantitative work Paper 3 demands. intro.heading: Economics is marked on three things students cannot see in their own work
paragraphs: Parents describe this subject the same way across Dubai. The child enjoys it, talks about it at dinner, writes two pages on demand-side policy, and comes back with a 4. There is no mystery in it. Diploma Economics awards marks against band descriptors, and a fluent essay that contains no diagram, no named example and no genuine weighing of alternatives sits in the middle of those bands however well it reads. The student cannot see this, because from the inside the essay feels complete.

At Higher Level the structure makes the problem sharper. Paper 1 is an extended response worth 20% of the grade, with a ten-mark explanatory part and a fifteen-mark evaluative part. Paper 2 is data response at 30%. Paper 3, which Standard Level candidates do not sit, is 30% on its own and is quantitative and policy-focused. The portfolio of three commentaries is the remaining 20%, marked out of 45. More than half the grade therefore sits in components with a heavy technical element, and essay fluency carries you through none of them.

So the sessions on this page are built around marked work. The student writes a fifteen-mark part (b) under time. The tutor marks it against the band descriptors, writes beside each paragraph which descriptor it satisfies and which it does not, and the two of them rebuild it. The output is an essay with the band movement annotated on it. Three of those and the pattern is unmistakable, usually the same two descriptors missing every time.

Alongside that run two record-keeping jobs that sound administrative and are worth several marks each. The first is a diagram checklist: every diagram the course needs, with what must be labelled on each, ticked off as the student proves they can draw it from memory with axes titled correctly. The second is an example bank the student builds themselves: concept, country, date, what happened, where it was read. Both are documents you can look at, and neither exists in most Economics students' folders.

Lessons are delivered online, over live video, one student at a time, in Gulf Standard Time slots arranged around the school week. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. Economics suits a shared screen better than most subjects, because a diagram can be drawn, corrected and redrawn in front of the student, and an essay can be marked with both people reading the same page.

This page is written for DP1 and DP2 students in Dubai's KHDA-inspected private schools. Every AED figure below is a market rate with the source and the month it was read. The first lesson is free, runs for 45 minutes, covers one subject and asks for no card details at that stage.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-hl-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Higher Level Economics reaches Dubai students through three International Baccalaureate routes, and the pressure around the subject differs sharply between them even though the examination does not. Knowing which route your child is on changes the number of hours that make sense.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Economics is a Group 3 subject and at Higher Level it carries four assessed components rather than three. The course is organised in four units, introduction to economics, microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, and threaded through nine key concepts that the portfolio and the papers both reference. Higher Level adds the theory of the firm, several macroeconomic models and a significant amount of calculation.
programmes.countryNote: Economics is one of the more popular Group 3 choices in Dubai, where many families have a business or finance degree in view. Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate candidates at 7% of enrolment, and Economics sets are usually large, which means a student's fifteen-mark essays may be marked quickly and returned without the band reasoning attached.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years individuals and societies builds argument and source-handling skills, but it does not require diagrams, calculations or the kind of named, dated evidence Economics marks reward. Students arriving in Higher Level Economics from the Middle Years Programme are usually strong writers who have never been asked to support a claim with a specific country and a specific year, which is precisely where the band descriptors bite.
programmes.countryNote: The transition is easiest to manage in the first term of DP1, when the diagram checklist can be built as the content is taught rather than reconstructed in DP2. Dubai schools running both programmes on one campus often assume the continuity is smooth; the discontinuity is technical rather than academic, and it is cheap to fix early.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Career-related Programme students take Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, the reflective project and the personal and professional skills course. Economics at Higher Level is a demanding choice in that context because of Paper 3, which is a full component with its own skill set. It is examined identically to the full Diploma version, including the portfolio and its 45 marks.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Career-related cohort is small and easy to overlook. A Career-related Economics candidate may be the only student sitting Paper 3 in their timetable band, which removes the study-group effect that carries most Higher Level students through the quantitative work. One-to-one hours do more here than they would for a student inside a large set.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-hl-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Higher Level Economics is usually taken with two other Higher Levels, and the combination decides how much time it can have. The grid lists the subjects Dubai families most often ask about alongside it, with the thing each pairing actually needs.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The four units plus the Higher Level extensions: the theory of the firm, the Keynesian multiplier, the Phillips curve, and calculation across all four units. Sessions divide between marked essays, Paper 3 quantitative drill, the diagram checklist and the portfolio commentaries.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The commonest pairing in Dubai. Students conflate the two subjects' command terms, answering an Economics evaluation question with a business recommendation. Separating the two mark schemes explicitly is usually the first useful hour where both subjects are being supported.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The standard maths route for an Economics student and the one that pays into Paper 3. Percentage change, index numbers, elasticity arithmetic and interpreting a rate of change are shared ground, and a session on either subject tends to move both.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Taken by Economics students whose degree target specifies it, which many quantitative economics programmes do. The calculus content helps with marginal reasoning, and the mathematical exploration competes with the Economics portfolio for the same DP2 autumn weeks.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Shares development and trade content with the global economy unit, and rewards the same skill of using a named place and a date as evidence. Students strong in one and weak in the other are usually applying the technique in only one of the two.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Pairs naturally with the global economy unit. The difficulty students report is that Global Politics rewards contested interpretation while Economics rewards a model applied precisely, so the two subjects need their written registers kept apart.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside Economics by Dubai students heading for social science degrees. The transferable skill is argument structure; the thing that does not transfer is the diagram, which History students consistently under-use in their Economics answers.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Chosen as a third Group 3 subject or alongside one. Its research-methods content supports the evaluation habit Economics rewards, since both subjects ask how far evidence supports a claim rather than whether a claim sounds reasonable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Requested where an Economics grade is being limited by structure rather than content. A student who writes long undifferentiated paragraphs loses marks in both subjects, and one block of work on paragraph function improves both scripts.

sections.heading: The four Higher Level components, and why fluency carries none of them
paragraphs: Higher Level Economics is assessed in four parts, and Standard Level students sit only three of them. Paper 1 is an extended response worth 20% of the grade, offering a choice of questions each with a ten-mark explanatory part and a fifteen-mark evaluative part. Paper 2 is data response at 30%, built around unseen text and figures. Paper 3 is Higher Level only and worth 30% on its own, quantitative and policy-focused. The portfolio of three commentaries completes the grade at 20%, marked out of 45.

Set out like that, the shape of the problem is obvious. The two components where a confident writer scores well on fluency alone are worth half the grade between them, and even there the band descriptors require a diagram and a named example before the upper bands open. Paper 3 rewards fluency not at all. The portfolio rewards it only once the diagrams, terminology, key concept and evaluation criteria have been satisfied.

This is the first conversation to have with a Dubai family whose child is enjoying the subject and scoring a 4 or a 5. The content is usually fine. What is missing is technical, component-specific and entirely teachable, and the hours should be allocated by component rather than by unit. A student weak in Paper 3 and strong in Paper 1 should not be spending sessions on microeconomics theory.

The table puts each component against what it actually rewards and the failure mode seen most often in marked Dubai scripts. Read it against your child's last school report, component by component if the school breaks it down that way. If it does not, that is a reasonable thing to ask the teacher for, and most will provide it.

sections.heading: Paper 3: the component Standard Level students never see and Higher Level students rarely practise
paragraphs: Paper 3 is thirty per cent of the grade and the component Dubai students are least prepared for. It is quantitative, it is compulsory rather than a choice of questions, and it closes by asking for a policy recommendation that has to be justified from the figures just produced. Students who are comfortable writing about monetary policy find themselves calculating and then arguing from their own numbers, which is an unfamiliar sequence.

The calculations themselves are not advanced mathematics. Percentage change, index numbers and real values, price and income elasticity, the effect of an indirect tax or subsidy on consumer and producer surplus, unemployment and inflation rates, the Keynesian multiplier, measures of inequality including the Gini coefficient, terms of trade, and the balance of payments arithmetic. What makes them cost marks is presentation: a student who writes only the final number loses everything when the arithmetic slips, where one who sets out the method keeps most of it.

The policy part has its own discipline. A recommendation that lists three possible policies scores less than one that chooses, says why, and names what the choice gives up. Dubai students are generally good at the breadth and weak at the commitment, which is the same habit that caps their fifteen-mark essays. Practising it inside Paper 3 is efficient because it improves two components at once.

The table lists the calculation families with where each comes from and the error that recurs. A block of four to six sessions covers all of them with timed practice attached, which is the most contained and most reliably productive block on this page.

sections.heading: Diagrams are marks: the checklist most Economics folders do not contain
paragraphs: In Diploma Economics a diagram is not an illustration. Band descriptors and portfolio criteria award marks for diagrams that are correctly labelled, correctly titled on both axes, relevant to the question, and referred to in the written answer rather than parked beside it. A student who draws a competent supply and demand diagram and never mentions it in the text has done most of the work and collected part of the mark.

The list of diagrams the course needs is finite, which is why a checklist works. Supply and demand with shifts and with a change in quantity supplied distinguished from a shift. Price ceilings and floors with the resulting shortage or surplus shown. Indirect tax and subsidy with incidence split. Negative production and positive consumption externalities. The cost curves and profit maximisation at the Higher Level theory of the firm, with the market structure diagrams that follow. Aggregate demand and aggregate supply in both the Keynesian and the new classical presentations. The Phillips curve in the short and long run. Tariffs, quotas and subsidies in trade. An exchange rate diagram. The Lorenz curve.

The checklist is used in one way only: the student draws each diagram from memory, with axes titled, before the item is ticked. Recognising a diagram in a textbook is not the same as producing it under time with the axes right, and the gap between those two states is where a large number of marks sit. Most students discover they can draw perhaps half the list cold.

Once the checklist is complete it changes how essays get written. A fifteen-mark question becomes a decision about which diagram carries the argument, drawn first and then written around. Students who adopt that order stop producing diagram-free essays entirely, which is the single most common cap on an Economics grade in this market.
bullets: Axes titled, curves labelled, equilibria marked, and referred to in the text
A shift distinguished from a movement along the curve, every time
Drawn from memory before the checklist item is ticked
Diagram chosen first, essay written around it afterwards
Most students can draw about half the list cold at the first test

sections.heading: The example bank: nine key concepts, and evidence with a date on it
paragraphs: Diploma Economics is organised around nine key concepts: scarcity, choice, efficiency, equity, economic well-being, sustainability, change, interdependence and intervention. They are not decoration. The portfolio requires a commentary to engage with a named key concept, and the papers' upper bands expect real-world evidence rather than hypothetical illustration. A student who writes that governments sometimes subsidise agriculture has produced no evidence at all.

The remedy is a bank the student builds and owns. Each entry records the key concept, the country or market, the year, what actually happened, and where it was read. Fifteen to twenty entries spread across the four units is enough to answer almost any question with something specific, and building them is work the student does between sessions rather than inside them.

The discipline that makes the bank useful is the date and the source. An example with no year attached reads as something half-remembered, and examiners treat it that way. An example with a year and a named policy or figure reads as evidence. Dubai students have an advantage here that most of them do not use: the UAE economy supplies clean, current illustrations of intervention, diversification, subsidy, indirect taxation and interdependence through trade, and those examples are as valid as any other.

Tested cold in a later session, the bank reveals the same thing as the diagram checklist: students know fewer specifics than they believe. The repair is cheap and it is the student's own work, which is also why it holds. Nothing in the bank is supplied by a tutor; the tutor's role is to ask for the date, the source and the concept each entry is filed under, and to reject entries that cannot supply all three.
bullets: Entries carry concept, country or market, year, event and source
Fifteen to twenty entries across the four units is a working minimum
An undated example reads to an examiner as a half-memory
UAE policy examples are legitimate and under-used by local candidates

sections.heading: Where the fifteen-mark answer stops being a six and becomes a four
paragraphs: The fifteen-mark part (b) is the question Dubai Economics students most reliably underperform on, and the reason is consistent. Asked to discuss or evaluate, students explain thoroughly and then add a short paragraph beginning with a concession. That structure satisfies the explanatory descriptors and barely touches the evaluative ones, which is why hard-working students plateau in the middle bands for a whole year.

Evaluation in this subject has a specific content. It weighs the magnitude of an effect, not just its direction. It names the assumptions the model requires and asks whether they hold in the case being discussed. It distinguishes short run from long run and says which matters here. It considers who bears the cost and who receives the benefit. And it reaches a position, with the strongest objection to that position acknowledged rather than ignored.

Taught as a list of moves, this is learnable in a term. A student who has written six fifteen-mark answers, each marked against the descriptors with the missing move named, starts producing the moves unprompted. The marking is the mechanism: a grade on its own teaches nothing, while a descriptor written beside a paragraph saying this is where the band changes teaches something immediately usable.

Command terms matter alongside this. Explain asks for a mechanism. Analyse asks for the mechanism plus its consequences. Discuss asks for a balanced treatment with a judgement. Evaluate asks for the judgement to be supported by weighing. Examine asks for the assumptions to be interrogated. Students who treat these as synonyms write one kind of answer for all of them, and get one kind of mark.
bullets: Weigh magnitude, not just direction of an effect
Name the model's assumptions and test whether they hold here
Separate short run from long run and say which is decisive
Identify who bears the cost and who gets the benefit
Reach a position and acknowledge the strongest objection to it

sections.heading: The portfolio: three commentaries, and the boundary a tutor keeps
paragraphs: The portfolio is 20% of the Higher Level grade and marked out of 45. It is three commentaries, each on a different unit of the course and engaging a different key concept, each capped at 800 words, built from a published news article the student selects. The marks inside each commentary reward diagrams, accurate terminology, application and analysis, engagement with the key concept and evaluation, with a further allocation for meeting the portfolio's overall requirements.

The decision that governs the mark is the article, and it is made before any writing happens. An article has to be recent, has to contain enough economic substance to support diagrams and analysis, and has to genuinely carry the key concept it is being filed under. Students routinely choose a piece that mentions inflation, then discover at 600 words that there is nothing in it to analyse. Re-selecting at that point is cheaper than continuing, and a tutor's most useful contribution here is to say so early.

What a tutor may do is explain how a criterion is satisfied, show what a commentary with strong evaluation looks like in general terms, ask whether the diagram selected supports the argument, and comment against each criterion so the student can see which marks are unearned. What no tutor may do is author any part of a commentary, supply text for it, or return a version with sentences inserted. The student revises their own words. Each checkpoint leaves a written record the school may inspect.

This matters more in Economics than in most subjects, because finished commentaries are openly sold in this market. A purchased commentary is an academic honesty breach that lands on the candidate's Diploma, not on the seller, and it is detectable. Saying that plainly is part of the service rather than a disclaimer attached to it.
bullets: Three commentaries, different units, different key concepts, 800 words each

sections.heading: What progress looks like in a subject with no right answers
paragraphs: Economics parents ask a fair question: if the essay has no correct answer, how is improvement measured? The answer is that the band descriptors are specific enough to track, and the technical elements are countable. Whether a diagram appeared, whether it was labelled, whether it was referred to in the text, whether an example carried a date, how many evaluative moves the answer contained, and which descriptor the marker identified as the ceiling. Those are all recordable, and together they are a better progress measure than a grade.

Measured that way, different things move at different rates. Diagram production moves within two or three sessions, because it is a drawing skill with a finite list. The example bank moves as fast as the student is willing to build it. Evaluation structure takes a term, because it is a thinking habit rather than a technique. Paper 3 calculation moves inside its block, provided the method-writing discipline is included rather than assumed.

A reported grade lags all of them, which families should know in advance. A school grade aggregates components sat at different times, so a student whose essays have visibly changed may see no movement on the next report and a clear change after the mocks. Anyone offering a grade improvement by a given date is selling a promise over something they do not control, and in this market that promise is made often.

The table sets out the measures, where each one comes from, and what counts as movement in it. It is deliberately plain. You should be able to open the folder at any point and see the marked essays, the diagram checklist, the example bank and the descriptor notes, and form your own view without asking anyone how things are going.

sections.heading: Economics in Dubai: KHDA schools, the UAE as evidence, and what Higher Level is for
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and inspection outcomes are published on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Elsewhere the regulator changes: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods rather than only inspecting.

For an Economics student the local setting is also material. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a government intervention in a market, with a stated objective and a cost, and it is exactly the kind of dated, sourced example the upper bands reward. Dubai's 2026-27 intake also adds seven private schools and 16,846 places, with enrolment having risen 6% in 2025-26, which is a supply response a student can analyse properly.

Higher Level Economics is a common choice for Dubai students heading to business, finance, international relations or economics degrees. Whether Higher Level is required depends on the programme: quantitative economics courses often specify a particular mathematics route rather than Economics itself, and several business programmes require neither. That makes the subject choice conversation worth having with the admissions pages open, because the assumption that Economics is the prerequisite for a business degree is frequently wrong.

Separately, the Ministry of Education runs certificate equivalency, which is a regulatory process and not something a tutoring provider performs, influences or guarantees. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No verified International Baccalaureate points figure has been read on the ministry's own pages, so none is published here.

sections.heading: Cost in AED, scheduling, and what happens if the slot cannot be filled
paragraphs: Published market rates in Dubai put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and an International Baccalaureate or A Level specialist at roughly AED 200-450 and above, from agency rate pages and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table as read in October 2026. Platform rates for university-student tutors advertise from around AED 33-150, in-home visiting rates including travel are quoted at AED 180-500, and a premium named tutor is advertised at up to AED 650 an hour. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Higher Level Economics tends to sit in the upper half of the specialist band for one specific reason: marking. A fifteen-mark essay marked properly against the descriptors takes time outside the session, and providers differ on whether that time is charged, included or simply not done. That single difference matters more than twenty dirhams on the hourly rate, and it is the first question to ask. IB Gram publishes no rate card here; the first lesson is free and the rate is agreed in writing before the second.

Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time against the school week. Ninety minutes suits this subject better than sixty, because a timed fifteen-mark answer plus its marking does not fit in an hour. During Ramadan school hours shorten and many families move to a post-Iftar slot, which works well for diagram and example-bank work even if full essays are better left to weekends. Eid is normally a clean pause. Agreeing any change before Ramadan begins is what keeps the plan intact.

Coverage is stated before booking. Higher Level Economics with Paper 3 depth in a narrow evening window is a specific request and in some weeks it cannot be met. The alternatives are a different time with the right specialist, a dated waiting period, or a tutor whose Higher Level experience is adjacent, described plainly so you can decide. On the legal side, individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts and therefore none quoted here.

process.title: Send one essay, unedited
process.description: A single fifteen-mark answer in your child's own handwriting or typing, with the teacher's mark on it if there is one. That one document shows whether a diagram appeared, whether an example had a date, and how many evaluative moves the answer contained, which is most of the diagnosis.

process.title: Free 45-minute first lesson
process.description: One subject, 45 minutes, no card details. The essay is marked against the band descriptors with the student watching, and the ceiling descriptor is named. You receive a written note saying which of the three usual gaps applies and whether Paper 3 needs its own block.

process.title: Build the two documents first
process.description: Before any content teaching, the diagram checklist and the example bank get started, because they change every subsequent essay. The student builds both; sessions test them cold. Two or three sessions covers the setup, and the documents stay with your child afterwards.

process.title: Rotate marked essays weekly
process.description: One timed fifteen-mark answer per session, across different units, each marked against the descriptors in front of the student with the missing move named. The pattern across three essays is what tells you whether the problem is structural or content-based.

process.title: Add the Paper 3 block when it is needed
process.description: Paper 3 is thirty per cent of the grade and a separate skill, so it is booked as its own block of four to six sessions rather than folded into weekly essay work. Students doing well on Papers 1 and 2 often need only this, which is a short and finite commitment.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 actually ask Higher Level Economics students to do?
faqs.answer: It is a compulsory quantitative and policy paper worth 30% of the Higher Level grade, and Standard Level candidates do not sit it. Questions require calculation across all four units, percentage change and index numbers, elasticities, tax and subsidy incidence, unemployment and inflation rates, the Keynesian multiplier, inequality measures, terms of trade, then a policy recommendation justified from the figures just produced. The arithmetic is not advanced. What costs marks is writing only the final number, because an arithmetic slip then removes the whole mark instead of one part of it.

faqs.question: How many diagrams does a Higher Level Economics student need to be able to draw?
faqs.answer: The list is finite, which is why a checklist works: supply and demand with shifts distinguished from movements, price ceilings and floors, indirect tax and subsidy with incidence split, negative production and positive consumption externalities, the cost curves and profit maximisation, the market structure diagrams, aggregate demand and supply in both presentations, the short and long run Phillips curve, tariffs, quotas and trade subsidies, an exchange rate diagram and the Lorenz curve. Most students can draw about half of them cold at a first test, with axes correctly titled.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter write a full essay and still score in the middle band?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because she is explaining thoroughly and evaluating thinly. The usual structure is several strong paragraphs of mechanism followed by one short concession, which satisfies the explanatory descriptors and barely touches the evaluative ones. Evaluation in this subject means weighing magnitude rather than direction, naming the assumptions the model needs and testing them, separating short run from long run, identifying who bears the cost, and reaching a position with the strongest objection acknowledged. Taught as a set of moves and practised on six marked essays, it is learnable within a term.

faqs.question: What counts as a real-world example, and how many does a student need?
faqs.answer: An example needs a country or market, a year, a specific policy or figure, and a source where it was read. Writing that governments sometimes subsidise agriculture is not evidence; naming the country, the year and the measure is. Fifteen to twenty entries spread across the four units is enough to answer almost any question with something specific. Dubai students have an advantage they rarely use, since UAE policy supplies current, documented illustrations of intervention, diversification, subsidy and trade interdependence that are as valid as any other country's.

faqs.question: Is Economics at Higher Level harder than Standard Level, or simply longer?
faqs.answer: Structurally harder, because of Paper 3. Higher Level sits four components rather than three, and Paper 3 is 30% of the grade on its own, quantitative and compulsory. The content additions are also specific: the theory of the firm with cost curves, revenues, profit maximisation and market structures, the Keynesian multiplier, the Phillips curve, and calculations across all four units, plus the Marshall-Lerner condition and terms of trade in the global economy. The portfolio is identical at both levels in form, with the share of the grade differing.

faqs.question: How much does a Higher Level Economics online tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified online subject tutor in Dubai run roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with International Baccalaureate and A Level specialists at roughly AED 200-450 and above, from published agency rate pages and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table as read in October 2026. Economics tends to sit in the upper half of that band because marking a fifteen-mark essay properly takes time outside the session. Ask directly whether that marking is charged, included, or not done, because it affects real cost more than the headline rate does.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark a fifteen-mark essay and show where the band changes?
faqs.answer: That is the core of these sessions. The student writes the answer under time, then the tutor marks it against the band descriptors with the student watching, writing beside each paragraph which descriptor it satisfies and which it does not, and naming the descriptor that is currently the ceiling. The student then rewrites part of the answer rather than redrafting the whole thing. Across three marked essays the same one or two missing descriptors usually recur, which turns a vague sense of underperformance into a specific target.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Economics require strong mathematics?
faqs.answer: It requires confident arithmetic rather than advanced mathematics. Percentage change, index numbers and real values, elasticity formulae, rates calculated from the right denominator, areas read off a diagram and then quantified, and the multiplier. Students taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation find the overlap substantial and should plan the two subjects together. Students who struggle with Paper 3 usually struggle with presentation and with knowing which base or denominator applies, not with the operations themselves, and both respond quickly to drilling.

faqs.question: My son takes Higher Level Economics but no business subject. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Not at all, and in one respect it helps. Students taking both frequently conflate the two mark schemes, answering an Economics evaluation question with a business-style recommendation, which costs marks in the Economics paper. A student with no business subject has no such habit to unlearn. What he does need is the technical set this page is built around: the diagrams drawn from memory, examples with dates and sources, and evaluation written as weighing rather than as a concession paragraph.

faqs.question: How do you show progress in a subject where essays have no right answer?
faqs.answer: By tracking the countable parts. Whether a diagram appeared, whether it was labelled and referred to in the text, whether each example carried a year and a source, how many evaluative moves the answer contained, and which descriptor the marker identified as the ceiling. All of those are recorded on the marked scripts and in the two documents the student builds. Diagram production moves in two or three sessions, evaluation structure takes a term, and a reported school grade lags everything because it aggregates components sat at different times.

faqs.question: Can UAE economic policy be used as evidence in the examination papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and local candidates under-use it. Examiners want specific, dated, sourced evidence and have no preference for any particular country. The UAE supplies clean illustrations of government intervention, diversification away from a single sector, subsidy and indirect taxation, and interdependence through trade and logistics. A Dubai example with the year and the measure named scores exactly as well as a European one and is often easier for the student to remember accurately, which matters under time pressure.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with a portfolio commentary draft?
faqs.answer: Explain how each criterion is satisfied, describe in general terms what strong evaluation looks like, ask whether the diagram chosen actually supports the argument being made, point out that the article cannot carry the key concept it has been filed under, and comment against each criterion so the student can see which marks are unearned. A tutor may not author any part of a commentary or return a version with sentences inserted. The student revises their own words, and each checkpoint leaves a written record the school may inspect.

faqs.question: When should a Higher Level Economics student start outside support?
faqs.answer: The most efficient point is the first term of DP1, because that is when the diagram checklist can be built as the content is taught rather than reconstructed eighteen months later. The second-best point is immediately after the first set of internal examinations, when the gap between content knowledge and band performance becomes visible. Starting after the February mocks still works for Paper 3 and for evaluation structure, both of which are technique, but it is too late to build an example bank at a comfortable pace.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Economics needed for a business or finance degree?
faqs.answer: Often not, which surprises families. Many business and management programmes require no Economics at all, while quantitative economics and finance courses more frequently specify a particular mathematics route than the Economics subject itself. Requirements differ by country and by institution and are revised between cycles, so the subject-choice conversation should happen with the admissions pages open. Tutoring does not change a published prerequisite, and no tutoring is required for any application or for a certificate equivalency process.

faqs.question: Can Economics sessions shift during Ramadan and the examination run?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the change agreed before Ramadan rather than during its first week. School hours shorten and evenings run late, and post-Iftar slots work well for diagram practice and example-bank building, which do not need long sustained concentration. Full timed essays are usually better moved to a weekend morning during that period. Eid is normally a clean pause. In the run to the session itself, families commonly keep the weekly essay slot and add a short second slot for Paper 3 practice.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level Economics specialist is available for our slot?
faqs.answer: You are told before booking rather than afterwards. Higher Level Economics with Paper 3 depth in a narrow weekday evening window is a specific request, and in some weeks it cannot be filled. The options are a different time with the right specialist, a waiting period with an actual date attached, or a tutor whose Higher Level experience sits in an adjacent part of the course, described plainly so the judgement is yours. No competitor page reviewed in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Economics at Higher Level for Dubai students. Each begins by marking a piece of the student's own written work against the published descriptors, because in this subject the gap between fluent writing and a high mark is the thing a report card is least able to explain.

intro.heading: Economics is the subject where confident writing hides a capped mark
paragraphs: Economics attracts articulate students, and that is the trap. A Higher Level student who writes clearly, uses the vocabulary correctly and structures a paragraph properly will be described by a school as doing well, and will frequently score in the middle bands. The reason is that economics answers are credited against four assessment objectives, and fluent writing satisfies the first two comfortably while leaving the third and fourth largely untouched. Knowledge and understanding are present. Application and analysis are usually present. Synthesis and evaluation are often absent, and the use of appropriate skills, which includes diagrams and calculation, is uneven.

That diagnosis is invisible in a term grade and obvious on a marked script. A student answers a fifteen-mark question with eight paragraphs of accurate explanation and reaches the middle band because no judgement is ever stated. Another student produces a diagram that is drawn correctly and never referred to in the prose, so it decorates the answer rather than earning anything. A third defines a term in their own words, accurately, and does not score the definition mark because the examination wanted the economic definition. None of those students lacks economics. All three are losing marks that a marker can name in a sentence.

The structure of the assessment makes this worse at Higher Level than at Standard Level. A Higher Level candidate sits three papers rather than two, and the third is heavily quantitative: it asks for calculation, manipulation of data and policy reasoning in a format a student who prefers essays has usually practised least. Add a portfolio of three commentaries, each capped at 800 words, each marked on diagrams, terminology, application and analysis, a key concept and evaluation, and the subject turns out to require five distinct competences rather than one.

The remedy is marking rather than teaching, at least to begin with. A student who has written twenty answers and had none of them marked against the descriptors has twenty pieces of practice and no information. A student who has had four answers marked properly knows which objective is missing, and that is a smaller and more actionable problem than being told to revise macroeconomics. We start there and keep a record of the four objectives separately in every session note, because the whole argument of this page is that the aggregate grade hides the fault.

Dubai supplies the context. KHDA oversees 227 private schools in the emirate, enrolling 387,441 pupils across 17 curricula in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment. Economics is a popular Higher Level choice among students heading for business, finance and policy degrees, and the UAE itself provides unusually rich material for a subject that rewards real examples: an oil-linked economy diversifying deliberately, a currency pegged to the dollar, free zones, a value added tax introduced in 2018, and government intervention visible enough to be discussed with dates attached.

sections.heading: Every Economics HL mark belongs to one of four assessment objectives
paragraphs: Economics answers are credited against four assessment objectives, and knowing which is which turns a vague instruction to improve into a specific task. The first is knowledge and understanding: defining, listing, outlining, stating. The second is application and analysis: explaining, applying a model to a context, analysing a chain of effects. The third is synthesis and evaluation: discussing, evaluating, comparing, justifying, reaching a position. The fourth is the use of appropriate skills, which covers diagrams, calculation and the handling of data.

Most Dubai students we see are secure on the first two and thin on the third and fourth, and the aggregate mark hides the shape. A fluent answer that explains four causes of inflation accurately will satisfy knowledge and application and stop there, scoring in the middle band of a fifteen-mark question no matter how long it is. The marks the student did not reach are not for more explanation. They are for weighing the causes against one another, for a judgement about which matters most in the context given, and for a diagram that the prose actually uses.

The fourth objective is the one families least expect to be a problem. Diagrams in economics are not illustrations. A correctly drawn diagram that the answer never refers to earns little, because the credit is for using it: naming the axes and the curves, identifying the shift, and pointing at the new equilibrium in the prose. Similarly a calculation without units or without a sentence saying what the figure means is half an answer. Students who are strong writers are frequently weakest here, and students who are strong at mathematics often have the reverse profile.

We record the four objectives separately in every session note, with marks available against marks gained for each. After three or four answers the profile is clear, and the plan becomes practising the weakest objective on content the student already knows well. Holding the content constant is deliberate: it makes the skill the only variable, so an improvement is attributable rather than guessed at.

sections.heading: Definitions: the two marks nobody practises
paragraphs: Economics awards marks for defining terms, and they are the cheapest marks in the subject and among the most frequently dropped. The reason is that students define in their own words. A description that a competent economist would accept as meaning the right thing often does not score, because the mark is awarded for a definition with the specific elements the examination expects: the entity, the condition, and frequently a qualifier such as ceteris paribus or per unit of time.

Take price elasticity of demand. A student who writes that it measures how much demand changes when price changes has described it and will usually not score fully. The definition wants responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price, expressed as a proportionate or percentage relationship. The elements that score are quantity demanded rather than demand, the proportionate relationship, and the direction. That level of precision looks pedantic until a student sees the same two marks appear in question after question.

The list is finite and it is short enough to master. Across the three units of the course there are perhaps eighty terms a Higher Level candidate should be able to state precisely, and the work is twenty definitions written out, tested cold, and rewritten where wrong. Students resist this because it feels like memorisation rather than economics, and it delivers a higher return per hour than any other revision activity available in the subject.

There is a second benefit in the portfolio. Terminology is a criterion in each commentary, and a student with precise definitions available uses them naturally in 800 words rather than padding with explanation. A commentary that defines its key terms accurately in its opening lines is also easier to keep inside the word limit, because precision is shorter than description.

sections.heading: The evaluation ladder: why a fifteen-mark answer is a different kind of answer
paragraphs: A ten-mark question and a fifteen-mark question are not the same task at different lengths. The shorter one asks for explanation: a model applied to a context with a chain of effects, supported by a diagram the prose uses. The longer one asks for explanation plus judgement, and the judgement is where the top band sits. A student who writes a longer version of the ten-mark answer will reach the middle of the fifteen-mark band and no further, which is the single commonest pattern on Dubai economics scripts.

Evaluation has levels, and treating it as one thing is why students plateau. The lowest rung is acknowledgement: noting that a policy has drawbacks. Above that is magnitude: saying how large an effect is likely to be and on what it depends. Above that is conditionality: identifying the circumstances under which the conclusion would change, such as the elasticity of demand, the state of the output gap, or the time horizon. Above that is prioritisation: saying which consideration matters most here and why. And at the top is a stated position that follows from the reasoning rather than being asserted at the end.

The practical technique is a margin plan before writing. Two or three lines listing the considerations, one line for the condition that would change the answer, and one line stating the conclusion. Writing the conclusion first, in note form, is counterintuitive and effective, because the essay then argues towards something instead of surveying a topic and stopping. Students who do this gain marks in the first fortnight, because the economics was already there.

Short-run and long-run is the most reliable evaluation lever in the subject, and the most frequently forgotten. Almost every policy question has a different answer over three months and over three years, and a student who routinely asks which horizon the question implies has an evaluation point available in nearly every answer. Stakeholder impact, assumption-testing and the quality of the data are the other three levers worth having permanently to hand.
