dubai/ib-dp-economics-sl-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Economics does not begin in Year 12. A Dubai student usually meets it through MYP Individuals and Societies, or through IGCSE Economics 0455 at a British-curriculum school, before choosing SL or HL in the Diploma. The route taken changes which parts of the SL course feel new.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Individuals and Societies is the usual first contact with economic reasoning. It is marked on four criteria, A Knowing and understanding through D Thinking critically, and it is assessed on investigation and argument rather than on diagrams. A student who scored well in MYP on written analysis can still arrive at DP Economics unable to draw a correctly labelled market diagram, because nothing in MYP demanded one.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running the full IB continuum, including Uptown International School in Mirdif and Swiss International Scientific School in Al Jaddaf, take students straight from MYP 5 into DP1. The gap that shows up in October of DP1 is almost always diagram technique and command-term discipline, not reading or writing ability.

programmes.name: IGCSE Economics as a pre-Diploma route
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 covers basic economic problem, allocation of resources, microeconomic decision makers, government and the macroeconomy, and international trade. It is a good foundation for DP Economics SL and a slightly misleading one: the IGCSE rewards accurate recall, the Diploma rewards evaluation against stated criteria. Students who got an A* on recall often plateau at a 4 or 5 in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools account for the largest share of Dubai's private enrolment, so a large number of DP1 Economics students in the emirate arrive from IGCSE rather than MYP. The first six weeks of tuition for that group is usually spent unlearning the IGCSE habit of listing points instead of weighing them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Economics
programmes.description: The current Economics course is built on four units, introduction to economics, microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, and on nine key concepts including scarcity, efficiency, equity, interdependence and intervention. SL students sit Paper 1 and Paper 2 and submit a portfolio of three commentaries. HL students add a third paper on policy and quantitative work and carry a lower portfolio weighting.
programmes.countryNote: Economics is one of the most heavily chosen group three subjects across Dubai's IB schools, which means large SL classes and limited one-to-one marking time for the teacher. That is the specific gap a weekly session fills: not new content, but a second set of eyes on scripts the class teacher does not have hours to annotate.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs two or more DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and a language development strand. Economics SL is a frequent DP choice inside a CP built around business or hospitality. The assessment burden for that single SL course is identical to the full Diploma version.
programmes.countryNote: CP is offered by a smaller number of Dubai schools than the full Diploma, so a CP student taking Economics SL is often the only person in their cohort sitting that paper. Online one-to-one is the practical answer when there is no class to revise with and no peer group to compare a commentary against.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-sl-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Economics rarely travels alone. The same Dubai student who needs help with a data-response paper is often carrying a Maths AA commitment and a science HL. Each subject below is listed with what it actually assesses, because that is what determines whether one tutor can hold two of them.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: SL sits Paper 1 extended response and Paper 2 data response, with a portfolio of three 800-word commentaries. HL adds a policy paper with quantitative content. Marks are lost on unlabelled diagrams, undefined terms in part (a) and evaluation that lists two sides without applying a criterion.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Shares the pre-released case study at HL and SL, with tools such as the business management toolkit replacing rote theory recall. Students who mix up the Economics command-term ladder with the Business one lose marks in both; the two subjects reward different styles of answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI SL carries the statistics and modelling that Economics students meet in Paper 2: correlation, regression lines, index numbers and percentage change. A student weak on AI SL statistics will usually also be weak on quantitative data response in Economics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: AA is the route most UAE and international economics degrees prefer at entry. Calculus and algebraic manipulation dominate, and the Paper 3 at HL rewards extended problem solving. Choosing AA SL over AI HL is a decision worth checking against target university pages before DP1 ends.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Overlaps Economics in the global economy unit: trade, development indicators and resource allocation appear in both. Geography is assessed with a fieldwork-based internal assessment, which demands a different writing discipline from a 800-word economic commentary.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Builds on the same intervention and interdependence concepts, assessed through an engagement activity and oral components. Students taking both Economics and Global Politics often need help keeping the two evaluation styles separate, since Politics rewards contested-concept analysis.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Shares nothing in content and everything in essay discipline. A student who can structure an argument for a History Paper 2 essay transfers that skill directly into Economics Paper 1 part (b), which is why the two subjects are often improved by the same intervention.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Assessed on research methods and empirical evidence, with an experimental internal assessment. The statistics vocabulary overlaps with Economics data response, and the two subjects both punish students who describe a study without evaluating its limitations.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Carries Paper 1 guided analysis and Paper 2 comparative essay plus oral components. For an Economics student, the relevant transfer is paragraph construction under timed conditions, which is where most Paper 1 part (b) answers in Economics come apart.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A frequent fourth or fifth subject alongside Economics in Dubai, built on a written paper pair plus a solution-development internal assessment. The scheduling note matters: both subjects carry internal deadlines in DP2, usually in the same term.

sections.heading: What a Dubai parent is actually asking when they search for an Economics SL tutor
paragraphs: The search is almost never about content. A student sitting Economics SL in a Dubai school has a textbook, a scheme of work and a teacher. What they usually do not have is anyone with the time to read their own script line by line and say which mark was available and why it was not awarded. That is the gap, and it is why this page is built around artefacts rather than aspiration.

Economics SL is assessed through two external papers and one internal portfolio. Paper 1 asks for an extended response: the student chooses one question from a set, answers a part (a) worth 10 marks that requires explanation supported by a diagram, and a part (b) worth 15 marks that requires evaluation. Paper 2 is data response, built around a set of extracts with figures, and it rewards a student who quotes and manipulates the data over one who recalls a textbook chapter. The portfolio is three commentaries, each capped at 800 words, each based on a published news article, each marked out of 15.

A parent weighing tutors should therefore ask three questions and ignore everything else. First: can you mark a Paper 2 script against the published criteria and show me the annotation? Second: how do you spread three commentaries across four units and nine key concepts without duplication? Third: what will I have in my hands after six weeks that tells me whether this is working? A tutor who answers those three fluently is a specialist. A tutor who answers with reassurance is not.

Delivery for every UAE family is live video, one student at a time. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE and does not operate a centre in Dubai; the home-visit service exists only in India. The practical consequence for a Dubai household is that the tutor is selected on subject depth rather than on postcode, and the comparison table further down sets the two models side by side on cost, travel and tutor pool.

sections.heading: Economics SL assessment: three components and what each is worth
paragraphs: The weighting is the first thing to get straight, because it determines where tuition hours should go. At Standard Level the portfolio carries 30 per cent of the final grade and is submitted long before the examination series. Paper 2 carries 40 per cent and Paper 1 carries 30 per cent. A student who treats the portfolio as a chore and the papers as the real assessment has already given away the most controllable third of the grade, since the portfolio is written at home with feedback available under academic-honesty rules.

Higher Level sits a third paper on policy and quantitative work, which changes the arithmetic considerably: the portfolio weight drops and the examination load rises. The table below includes the HL paper as a contrast row rather than as something an SL student sits, because a surprising number of SL students in Dubai revise from HL resources borrowed from a sibling or a classmate and waste hours on content they will never be examined on.

Guided teaching hours matter too. A DP Standard Level course is designed around roughly 150 hours of teaching across two years, against 240 at Higher Level. That number is a useful reality check on a request for help six weeks before the examination series: a weekly hour added at that point is a technique intervention, not a content rescue, and the honest version of a tuition plan says so in the first conversation.

Read the deduction column as the thing to practise, not as a list of complaints. Each entry there is a repeated, diagnosable habit rather than a knowledge gap, and habits respond to marked practice faster than content gaps respond to re-teaching.

sections.heading: The portfolio read criterion by letter, with the deduction we see most against each
paragraphs: Nobody in the competitor set names a single assessment criterion by letter. That absence is odd, because the criteria are published, the mark allocations are fixed, and a student who knows them can self-check a draft in twenty minutes. Each commentary is marked out of 15 across five criteria, and the three commentaries together give a portfolio mark out of 45 that is then scaled to the published percentage weight.

Criterion A rewards diagrams: correctly selected, correctly drawn, correctly labelled, and referred to in the text rather than parked beside it. This is where the largest number of easy marks in the whole course sit, and where most of them are lost. An unlabelled vertical axis, a missing new equilibrium point, or a diagram that appears but is never discussed will each cost marks that cost nothing to secure. Criterion B is terminology, which rewards accurate and consistent use of economic vocabulary rather than a glossary paragraph at the start.

Criterion C is application and analysis: the student has to link the article to economic theory with a chain of reasoning, not an assertion. Criterion D is the key concept, and it is the criterion most often treated as decoration. The concept has to do work in the argument; naming scarcity in the introduction and then never returning to it scores low. Criterion E is evaluation, carrying the largest single allocation, and it rewards judgement supported by the article: stakeholders named, short run separated from long run, assumptions questioned, magnitude considered.

Three further procedural rules sink more portfolios in Dubai than any analytical weakness. The three commentaries must each draw on a different unit of the syllabus. Each must use a different key concept. Each article must come from a different source and must be recent relative to when the commentary is written. A student who writes three brilliant pieces from the same macroeconomics unit has not written a portfolio, and no amount of late editing fixes that.

sections.heading: Where Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Mark loss in Economics SL is patterned enough to be predictable. On Paper 1 part (a), the instruction is to explain, and the mark band separates explanation from description. A student who writes what a price ceiling is, draws it, and stops has described. A student who writes what a price ceiling does to quantity supplied and quantity demanded, shows the shortage on the diagram, and names the consequence has explained. The difference is often two sentences and four marks.

On Paper 1 part (b), the command term almost always asks for evaluation or discussion. Evaluation that scores is evaluation against something: the magnitude of the effect, the time frame, the assumptions the model rests on, the stakeholders who gain and lose, the quality of the evidence available. Evaluation that does not score is a paragraph beginning with a concessive clause and ending without judgement. Students who have been told to write a balanced answer frequently produce exactly this, and they are not being careless; they have followed advice that was too vague to act on.

Paper 2 fails in a different way. The extracts carry figures, and the examiner expects them used: quoted, converted into percentage change, compared across years, read off a table. Students who revise content thoroughly and then answer a data-response question from memory produce fluent answers that sit in the middle bands because the data never appears. Timing is the second Paper 2 problem: the paper runs an hour and three quarters, students who spend thirty minutes on the first short part have no time left for the extended part carrying the most marks.

The fix in both cases is marked practice, not more reading. A script annotated with where each mark was available, returned within the week, read through with the student over screen share, produces a measurable change over a half-term. That is the work, and it is the reason the next section is about what the file of marked work should look like rather than about teaching philosophy.

sections.heading: The evidence file: what six weeks of Economics tuition should leave behind
paragraphs: This is the part of the page the brief for it is built around, and it is the part most tuition providers do not commit to in writing. If one-to-one teaching is worth AED 250 an hour of a family's money, there should be a file at the end of six weeks that a parent who does not know any economics can still interrogate. Not a dashboard with a percentage on it, which is a number invented by the provider, but the student's own work with someone else's marking on it.

The table below is the shape of that file for a typical half-term with an SL student in DP1 or early DP2. The columns are deliberately split between what the student produces, what comes back marked, and what a parent can check without reading the syllabus. The third column is the accountability one: a parent who can see that week four returned a commentary draft with criterion letters attached, and week five returned a revised draft with the mark band moved, has evidence. A parent who has only a tutor's verbal assurance has none.

Two honest caveats belong here. First, grade movement over six weeks is not reliably measurable in Economics, because internal school assessments are not calibrated against each other and a predicted grade can move for reasons unrelated to tuition. What is measurable is mark movement on comparable tasks marked by the same person against the same criteria. Second, no tutor can commit to a grade outcome, and anyone who does should be treated with real scepticism; the published criteria and the examiner, not the tutor, decide the mark.

What the file does support is a decision. After six weeks a family can look at the annotated scripts and the draft history and decide whether to continue, change tutor, change frequency or stop. That decision is the actual deliverable of a trial period, and it is more useful than any promise made before the first session.

sections.heading: What Economics tuition costs in Dubai, and what the invoice should show
paragraphs: Dubai's tutoring market is wide and almost entirely unpublished. Of the pages ranking for this type of search, three publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The table below gathers the AED bands that are actually on the record, each with the provider or survey the figure came from, so a parent can see where a quote sits rather than guessing.

These are market rates, not a price list for this platform. Where a figure is attributed to a named provider, that provider published it; where it is attributed to a rate survey, the survey is Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. Monthly packages circulate too: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions at the budget end, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions at the mid-market end. Rates close to an examination series tend to firm up rather than soften.

Three cost questions are worth asking any provider before booking. Does the hourly figure include marking time, or is a returned script billed separately? Is the price per hour or per session, and what happens to a 90-minute booking? What is the position on a session cancelled by the family with 24 hours' notice? None of those answers is in any competitor page we examined, and all three change the real cost per term by a material amount.

One piece of Dubai context makes the tutoring line item easier to read. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. For a family budgeting a two-year Diploma, that means the tuition decision is being made against a flat school fee rather than a rising one, which is unusual and worth noticing.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not touch on a portfolio commentary
paragraphs: This matters more in Economics than in most subjects, because the portfolio is written at home over months and the temptation to blur the line is structural. The IB position is not ambiguous. Assessed work submitted under a student's name must be that student's own work. A teacher or tutor may teach, explain, question, point to a weakness, and comment on a draft. A tutor may not author any part of an assessed piece, supply paragraphs for insertion, or edit a draft to the point where the sentences are no longer the student's.

In practice the boundary is easy to hold if feedback is written as questions and observations rather than as replacement text. Useful: this diagram does not show the new equilibrium, and your criterion A mark will reflect that. Useful: criterion D asks the key concept to do work, and yours appears only in the opening paragraph. Not acceptable: a rewritten paragraph pasted into a comment for the student to adopt. The first two teach, the third substitutes.

One Dubai-specific rule belongs beside this. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also restricts serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK directly if it affects a decision, but the principle it reflects is sound anywhere in the UAE: a paid arrangement with the person who marks your child's internal work is a conflict worth avoiding on its own merits.

There is also a commercial dimension. One operator in this search results page sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the seller. A page that states plainly what a tutor will not do is doing a family a favour, because it tells them what to refuse when it is offered.
bullets: A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and comments; the student is the author
Feedback belongs in criterion order, as observations rather than replacement text
No syllabus document, mark scheme or past paper is supplied as a download here
Any provider offering to supply finished assessed work should be declined outright

sections.heading: Fitting an Economics session into a Dubai Year 12 timetable
paragraphs: A Dubai Diploma student's week is fuller than the subject list suggests. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and those requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Instructional time for those subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met.

KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For a timetable planner, that means more discrete blocks rather than fewer, and for a family it means the free evening for an Economics session is genuinely scarce. Booking one fixed weekly slot and defending it works better than a flexible arrangement that quietly erodes.

The academic calendar supplies two more constraints. Ramadan shortens school days and shifts the household rhythm, and sessions in that period usually move later in the evening; a post-Iftar slot is a normal request and easy to accommodate over video. Internal assessment deadlines across subjects cluster, so a student taking Economics, a science and a language will meet three internal deadlines inside a few weeks of DP2. Mapping those out at the start of DP1 is dull work and it prevents the single most common scheduling failure in the Diploma.

On examination dates, this page deliberately publishes none for the IB. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date here has been confirmed from the IB directly. UAE schools sit the May session and some candidates sit November; confirm the exact windows with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. For families also sitting Cambridge or Pearson papers, those boards publish their own timetables, and the pattern there is instructive: Cambridge's March 2027 series has final entries due on 27 November 2026, months before the February exam period, which is why entry administration should never be left to the student.

process.description: Before any block is booked, the plan states which syllabus units will be covered in what order, how often timed work will be set, and in what form marked scripts come back. Anything not written down at this stage tends not to happen in week five.

process.description: At the half-term point you get a one-page summary and the accumulated marked work. Continue, change frequency, change tutor or stop. If no Economics specialist is free at your preferred time, we say so and offer the nearest available slot rather than substituting a general humanities tutor.

whyPoints.title: Marking is the product, not an add-on
whyPoints.description: The thing a Dubai school cannot give a large SL Economics class is individual script annotation at volume. Timed work returned with mark allocations written beside each paragraph is what changes a part (b) answer, and it is the main thing a weekly hour buys.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-order feedback on portfolio drafts
whyPoints.description: Commentary feedback is written criterion by criterion, A through E, with the band named for each. A student can then act on criterion D without re-reading everything. General encouragement on a draft is pleasant and does not move a mark.

whyPoints.description: Because delivery is live video across the UAE, the tutor is selected for depth in Diploma Economics rather than for living within a short drive of your community. That is the substantive argument for the online format, and it holds regardless of which emirate you are in.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP Economics SL online tutor in Dubai charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market figures in Dubai put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IB rates from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate survey puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those are market rates from the providers and survey named, not a price list for this platform. Ask any provider whether marking of timed scripts is inside the hourly figure, because that single answer changes the real cost per term more than the headline rate does.

faqs.question: What exactly does Paper 1 ask an Economics SL student to do?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 is the extended-response paper, sat in an hour and fifteen minutes, and it carries 30 per cent of the Standard Level grade. The student chooses one question from a set and answers it in two parts. Part (a), worth 10 marks, asks for explanation supported by an accurately labelled diagram that is discussed in the prose rather than parked beside it. Part (b), worth 15 marks, asks for evaluation or discussion. The mark bands separate explanation from description in part (a), and separate judgement from a list of two sides in part (b). Most recoverable marks sit in those two distinctions.

faqs.question: How is the Economics portfolio weighted differently at SL and HL?
faqs.answer: Standard Level students sit two external papers, so the portfolio of three commentaries carries a larger share of the final grade, published at 30 per cent. Higher Level students sit a third paper on policy and quantitative work, which pushes the examination load up and the portfolio share down. The practical consequence for an SL student in Dubai is that the portfolio is the most controllable third of the grade, because it is written at home across DP1 and DP2 with legitimate feedback available under academic-honesty rules. Treating it as a side task while revising for papers is the commonest strategic error we see at SL.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's Economics commentary draft before the school deadline?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is squarely inside the rules. A tutor may read a draft, comment on it, ask questions about the reasoning, point out that a diagram is missing its new equilibrium, and name the criterion each comment belongs to. What a tutor may not do is author any part of the piece, supply paragraphs for the student to insert, or edit sentences until the voice is no longer the student's. The useful form of feedback is criterion-ordered observation: criterion A has a labelling problem, criterion D names a key concept that then disappears. The student does every revision themselves, and a record of what changed between drafts is kept.

faqs.question: My son draws the diagram but never labels the axes. Is that really costing marks?
faqs.answer: It is, and it is one of the cheapest losses in the subject. Criterion A of the portfolio awards marks for diagrams that are relevant, accurately drawn, fully labelled and explained in the text, out of three marks per commentary. On Paper 1 part (a), a diagram with unlabelled axes or no marked new equilibrium undercuts the explanation it was supposed to support. The fix is mechanical rather than conceptual: a rebuilt diagram bank, drawn live on a shared whiteboard, with both axes labelled, the original equilibrium marked, the shift shown and the new equilibrium identified every single time until the habit is automatic.

faqs.question: How many weeks of Economics tuition does a Dubai Year 12 student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the problem is content or technique, and the diagnostic in the first session is designed to tell you which. A technique problem, such as part (b) answers that balance without judging, often responds within a half-term of weekly marked practice. A content gap across a whole unit takes longer, because a Standard Level course is built around roughly 150 guided teaching hours across two years and a weekly hour cannot replace missing teaching at that scale. Families commonly book six weeks, review the accumulated marked work, then decide whether to continue, change frequency or stop.

faqs.question: What evidence will I actually get that the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: The student's own work with someone else's marking on it, accumulated weekly. That means timed scripts annotated with the marks available beside each paragraph, commentary drafts with feedback written in criterion order and the band named for each criterion, a revision history showing what the student changed between drafts, and a coverage log of which syllabus units have been taught. At six weeks you also receive a one-page summary. Deliberately absent is any invented percentage or satisfaction score, because a number a provider generates about itself is not evidence and nobody should be asked to act on one.

faqs.question: Does taking Economics at Standard Level rather than Higher Level limit university options?
faqs.answer: It can, and it depends entirely on the course and country rather than on any general rule. Some economics and business degrees specify Higher Level Economics or a particular mathematics route at Higher Level; many specify neither and care more about the mathematics course taken. The reliable method is to read the entry requirements on the admissions pages of three or four target universities before subject choices are locked at the end of DP1, and to check whether Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation is named. Nobody should rely on a tutoring page, including this one, for an admissions requirement.

faqs.question: Which news articles are acceptable for an Economics portfolio commentary?
faqs.answer: The article has to be a published news piece, recent relative to when the commentary is written, and each of the three commentaries must come from a different source. Beyond that, the choice is strategic. Each commentary has to draw on a different unit of the syllabus and use a different key concept, so the three articles should be selected together rather than one at a time. An article that cannot be linked to a diagram is a poor choice whatever its subject, because criterion A rewards diagram work. Checking article suitability before drafting saves more marks than any later editing.

faqs.question: Is Economics SL easier than Business Management SL for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: They are hard in different places, so the comparison rarely helps. Economics rewards diagram technique, theoretical chains of reasoning and evaluation against stated criteria, and it punishes students who write fluently without using the data supplied. Business Management rewards application to a given organisation and to a pre-released case study, with its own toolkit of analytical frameworks. A student strong on abstraction usually finds Economics the better fit; a student who prefers concrete organisational detail often does better in Business Management. Choose on the student's habits of mind, not on a reputation for difficulty.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to a later evening slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Dubai families ask for exactly that. School days shorten, the household rhythm changes, and a 17:00 session that worked in January is unworkable in Ramadan. A post-Iftar slot is a standard arrangement, and because delivery is live video there is no travel to reschedule around on either side. The practical advice is to agree the Ramadan timetable a fortnight in advance rather than week by week, so the slot is protected. The same approach applies to school examination weeks and family travel, where a paused block is better than a run of cancelled sessions.

faqs.question: Does an Economics grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency rules are set by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority, not by any tutoring provider, and they differ by curriculum. For the British track the published requirements include five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the IB track no points threshold is published here, because none could be verified on the Ministry's own site. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate authority directly, and treat any unsourced IB figure with suspicion.

faqs.question: What happens if no Economics specialist is free at the time we want?
faqs.answer: You are told at the point of enquiry, not after a payment. The honest options are a different slot with the specialist you want, a different specialist at the slot you want, or a short wait. What does not happen is a general humanities tutor being presented as an Economics specialist, which is the failure mode that wastes a term. Because delivery is live video across the UAE rather than tied to a drive radius, the pool for a Diploma subject is wider than a local search would suggest, but it is not unlimited and a narrow window plus a niche component can genuinely mean no match this week.

faqs.question: Does a teacher at my child's Dubai school need a permit to tutor privately?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. Separately, a paid arrangement with the person who marks your child's internal work is a conflict of interest worth avoiding regardless of permit status.

faqs.question: How do you teach Paper 2 data response over video?
faqs.answer: Screen sharing suits this component better than a kitchen table does. The extract sits on a shared screen, the student annotates it live while a stopwatch runs, and the tutor can see the order in which the data is used rather than only the finished answer. That order is usually the problem: students read the question, answer from memory, then look for figures to decorate the answer. Working live surfaces that habit in one session. Scripts are then marked offline with a count of how many times the supplied data was actually used, and returned before the next lesson.

intro.heading: What the number depends on, before anyone quotes you an hour
paragraphs: A Dubai parent who asks three providers what Economics tuition costs will get three answers that do not compare with each other. One quotes AED 180 for a 45-minute session. One quotes AED 350 an hour and includes marking. One sells a monthly block of eight sessions at around AED 799 and never says how long a session runs. None of them is being dishonest. They are pricing different things, and the only way to compare them is to fix what you are buying first: session length in minutes, whether written feedback is included, whether a timed paper gets marked between sessions, and which of the three assessed components the hour is actually pointed at. Do that arithmetic and the three quotes resolve into one comparable figure, which is usually within a hundred dirhams of each other once marking and session length are equalised. Skip it and you are choosing on confidence rather than on price.

Standard Level Economics is a smaller course than Higher Level, and that changes the arithmetic. There is no quantitative third paper to prepare for, the portfolio carries proportionally more of the final grade, and the content stops where the Higher Level extension starts. A plan built for a Higher Level candidate therefore wastes money on a Standard Level student, and a tutor who has only ever taught Higher Level will spend the first month teaching material your child will never be examined on. Ask in the first message which level the tutor usually teaches and how many Standard Level portfolios they have supervised through to submission.

The second variable is timing. Support bought in DP1, while the course is still being taught, costs less per mark recovered than the same support bought six weeks before the May session, because in DP1 a tutor closes gaps as they appear instead of rebuilding four units at once. Families who start in the final term usually need two sessions a week rather than one, and they are buying exam technique under pressure rather than understanding. Nobody in the Dubai market raises their headline rate in March. The number of hours required simply doubles, and so does the invoice.

The third is what the tutor is permitted to do with the portfolio. A commentary is the student's own work. Any provider offering to hand over a finished one is selling an academic-honesty problem that lands on your child rather than on them. Legitimate portfolio support looks dull by comparison: the student brings an article they found themselves, the tutor asks which key concept it illustrates and whether the diagram carries the argument, the student rewrites it, and the tutor reads it again. That is slower than the alternative, which is exactly why the honest version costs what it costs.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: Economics appears only in the final two Diploma years, but the habits it rewards are built earlier: reading a diagram as an argument, writing a definition that earns its mark, treating evidence as something to be cited rather than remembered. These are the IB programmes Dubai schools run and what each contributes to a Standard Level Economics grade.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Economics is not a named MYP subject. It arrives through Individuals and Societies, where students are assessed against four criteria on knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. The useful inheritance is criterion D: evaluating sources and recognising that a claim needs support. The gap is technical. MYP marking rewards a well-argued position, while Diploma Economics also demands an accurate diagram and a defined term.
programmes.countryNote: A large share of Dubai Diploma candidates arrive from an MYP cohort in the same building, which makes the handover smoother on skills and rougher on numeracy. Departments here often report the same pattern in DP1: students who write fluently about inflation but cannot shift a curve correctly or read a percentage change off a data table without prompting.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Economics sits in Group 3, Individuals and Societies, and runs across both Diploma years at Standard or Higher Level. Standard Level candidates sit two written papers and submit a portfolio of three commentaries, each built on a published news article and capped at 800 words. The course is organised around nine key concepts and four units, and the concepts are assessed, not decorative.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has the densest Diploma provision in the UAE, and Economics is one of the most commonly offered Group 3 subjects in the emirate alongside Business Management and Geography. KHDA inspects these schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the published report names subject strengths, which is worth reading before you decide whether the problem is teaching or workload.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. A CP student taking Economics sits the same examination papers and submits the same portfolio as a Diploma student in that subject, so the subject-level support needed is identical.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of Dubai schools run the Career-related Programme, so a CP student is often the only one in the building taking Economics on that route. It matters for scheduling rather than for content: the career-related study and the reflective project compete for the same evenings as portfolio work, and the clash usually lands in the first term of the second year.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Standard Level Economics is four units and a portfolio, and the marks are not spread evenly across them. Below are the parts of the course a tutor works through with a Dubai candidate, what each one assesses, and where marks most often go missing in a script.

subjects.name: Unit 1: Introduction to Economics
subjects.description: Scarcity, choice, opportunity cost, the factors of production and the nine key concepts that frame the whole course. It looks like the easy unit and is quietly the most expensive to skip, because a Paper 1 answer that never names a concept loses the marks for conceptual understanding no matter how good the economics is.

subjects.name: Unit 2: Microeconomics
subjects.description: Demand, supply, elasticity, market equilibrium, government intervention and market failure. The diagrams live here, and so do most of the avoidable deductions: unlabelled axes, a movement drawn where a shift was asked for, and welfare-loss triangles shaded in the wrong place on a tax diagram.

subjects.name: Unit 3: Macroeconomics
subjects.description: Measuring economic activity, aggregate demand and supply, the business cycle, unemployment, inflation and the four macroeconomic objectives. Marks go on precision of language rather than on breadth: students who describe a deflationary gap without putting it on an AD-AS diagram score in the lower bands of a 15-mark question.

subjects.name: Unit 4: The Global Economy
subjects.description: Trade, protectionism, exchange rates, the balance of payments, economic integration and development economics. Dubai students usually have the strongest intuition here and the weakest technique, because the unit rewards named, dated, sourced examples and most candidates arrive with general impressions instead.

subjects.name: Paper 1: extended response
subjects.description: A choice of extended-response questions in two parts, each requiring definitions, a diagram and a real-world example. The common failure is structural: candidates write a long part (a) and run out of clock for the evaluative part (b), which carries the larger share of the marks for that question.

subjects.name: Paper 2: data response
subjects.description: A choice of data-response questions built on text extracts, tables and charts, finishing with an extended evaluative part. The data has to be used, not summarised. A script that quotes a figure without saying what it implies for the market being discussed is the single commonest pattern in mid-band work.

subjects.name: The portfolio of three commentaries
subjects.levels: Standard and Higher Level internal assessment
subjects.description: Three commentaries, each on a different unit and a different source, each capped at 800 words, each built on an article published within a defined window before it is written. The marks sit in the lettered criteria rather than in the prose quality, which is why a well-written commentary can still score in the middle.

subjects.name: Diagram technique
subjects.description: Nine or ten diagrams cover almost everything a Standard Level candidate is asked to draw. Each needs labelled axes, a title, correctly directed shifts and annotation that connects the figure to the argument in the text. It is the fastest-moving mark on the page and the one least often practised under a clock.

subjects.name: Command terms and definitions
subjects.description: Define, explain, discuss, evaluate and examine do different jobs, and the mark allocation follows the term rather than the topic. A good drill is to answer the same stem under two different command terms in one session and compare what the band descriptors reward in each case.

subjects.name: Real-world examples
subjects.description: Every extended answer needs at least one named, located, reasonably recent example. Standard Level candidates in Dubai have good material close to hand and rarely use it, defaulting to textbook cases from twenty years ago that an examiner has read several hundred times already.

dubai/ib-dp-economics-sl-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Dubai changes one practical thing for an Economics student: the earliest hour a weekday session can realistically start once the school run is done. Below are the parts of the emirate the question comes from most often, with what each one does to the shape of a weekly slot.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: The densest band of Diploma provision in the emirate, and the band where a Standard Level Economics cohort is usually large enough that the school runs separate SL and HL classes. Sessions here typically start at five, after a school run that rarely runs past twenty minutes.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Quoz
regions.note: Mostly new-build family housing with short runs to several Diploma schools. Families here tend to buy ninety-minute sessions rather than hourly ones, because a timed data-response paper and the read-back afterwards do not fit inside sixty minutes.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Older villa communities with several long-established Diploma schools within a short drive. A frequent request here is a late-evening Economics slot for a student who also sits Arabic as a first language, because that subject carries its own after-school commitments.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Larger households, more siblings on the same school bus, and arrival times that push a realistic session start to half past six. Smaller Diploma cohorts here mean Economics is sometimes taught as a combined SL and HL class, which is the exact situation that produces mid-band Paper 1 scripts.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown Dubai and DIFC
regions.note: Apartment living with short commutes and a high proportion of parents who work in finance, which tends to produce confident students with excellent macroeconomic general knowledge and under-practised diagram technique. The ask here is usually marking rather than teaching.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Two schools inside the district and several more one interchange away on Sheikh Zayed Road, so a 4.30pm start is feasible on most days. Portfolio deadlines drive the enquiries from this area more often than examination technique does.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, The Springs and Motor City
regions.note: Inland communities where the school run can take forty minutes each way at the wrong hour, which is why families here were already buying online tuition before it became common. Weekend morning slots are more popular here than anywhere else in the emirate.

schoolClusters.note: Where Standard Level Economics is most reliably offered as its own class rather than taught alongside Higher Level. Families in this band most often ask for Paper 2 marking and portfolio supervision rather than content teaching, because the departments here generally cover the four units on schedule.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and the Al Sufouh corridor
schoolClusters.note: A long-established band of Diploma schools where Economics cohorts are mixed in prior attainment and the commentary deadlines tend to be set early in DP2. The common request from this corridor is help sequencing three commentaries so they do not all land in the same fortnight.

sections.heading: What an Economics Standard Level hour costs in Dubai, and what sits inside it
paragraphs: A Standard Level Economics tutor in Dubai costs between roughly AED 45 and AED 650 an hour depending on who you buy from, and the spread is not about quality alone. It reflects five different products being sold under one word. At the bottom sit university students and general subject tutors working online from outside the UAE; at the top sit named practitioners charging premium rates for technique work on a single component. Most families settle in the middle, paying between AED 200 and AED 450 for someone who has taught the Diploma syllabus and can mark against the band descriptors.

The figures below come from what providers publish. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. None of these is an IB Gram price list; they are the market you are shopping in, which is the thing no competitor page in this search will show you.

Convert every quote to a cost per sixty minutes before you compare anything, because the Dubai market sells 45, 60, 90 and 120-minute sessions interchangeably and quotes them all as a session fee. Then ask what the fee includes. Marking a timed paper takes a tutor between twenty-five and forty minutes for a Paper 2, and whether that work is inside the rate or billed on top is the single largest hidden variable in a Dubai tutoring invoice.

sections.heading: Cost per mark: where an Economics hour actually pays back
paragraphs: Hourly rate is the wrong number to optimise. The useful question is which component gives the most marks back per hour paid, and for a Standard Level Economics candidate the answer is almost always the portfolio. It is internally assessed, it has no clock on it, it is worth a substantial share of the grade, and a commentary scoring in the middle band can usually be moved by two or three sessions of criterion-by-criterion work before the school deadline. Nothing else in the course responds that reliably to a small number of hours.

The written papers behave differently. Paper 2 is technique-heavy, which means the content is usually already known and the marks are going on command terms, on using the data rather than restating it, and on finishing the evaluative part. That work takes eight to twelve hours spread over a term, and roughly half of it is marking rather than teaching. Paper 1 needs diagram accuracy and real-world examples, both of which are built by repetition. Neither responds to a single intensive weekend.

Unit content is the one purchase with a fixed cost. Two to four hours closes a missed topic, and it does not come back if it is closed when it appears. This is why a DP1 plan costs less across two years than a DP2 rescue: the same gaps are being fixed, but in DP1 they are being fixed one at a time at the single-topic price, and in the final term they are being fixed simultaneously at the specialist rate with a mock grade already on the file.

sections.heading: Standard Level without the Higher Level content: what your child is examined on
paragraphs: A Standard Level Economics candidate sits two written papers and submits a portfolio. A Higher Level candidate sits three papers, the third being a quantitative paper built on calculation and policy-response questions, and covers additional content in each unit. That difference has two financial consequences. Hours spent on quantitative drilling are wasted on a Standard Level student, and the Standard Level portfolio matters proportionally more, because it is carrying its weight against two papers rather than three.

This matters when you hire. A tutor who normally teaches Higher Level will often default to Higher Level depth, partly from habit and partly because it feels more rigorous. The result is a student who can discuss the Keynesian multiplier but cannot write a tight 15-mark evaluation of a price ceiling. Ask directly how many Standard Level candidates the tutor has taken through to the May session, and ask what they would cut from a Higher Level scheme of work to build a Standard Level one. A specialist answers that question in a sentence.

It also matters for the level decision itself, which some Dubai families are still making in the first weeks of DP1. Standard Level Economics is accepted for a wide range of degrees, including most economics and business programmes that ask for mathematics at Higher Level instead. The deciding factor is usually not the Economics level at all but which mathematics course the student is taking, because that is the prerequisite universities tend to specify. Check the published entry requirements for the actual universities on the list before paying for a level change.

sections.heading: Diagrams are where Standard Level marks go missing
paragraphs: Ask a Dubai Economics teacher where the easiest marks on a script are lost and the answer is rarely a topic. It is the diagrams. Ten or so figures cover almost everything a Standard Level candidate is asked to draw, and each one has a fixed set of requirements: labelled axes with units where they apply, a title, correctly directed shifts, the new equilibrium marked, and annotation that ties the figure to the sentence it supports. Most mid-band scripts contain diagrams that are recognisable but incomplete, and each incomplete diagram costs between one and three marks.

The errors are predictable enough to drill. Students draw a movement along a curve when the question asked for a shift. They shade the welfare loss on a tax diagram in the wrong triangle. They label an AD-AS diagram with price rather than average price level. They draw the externality diagram with marginal social cost below marginal private cost. None of these is a conceptual failure; all of them are habits, and habits respond to five minutes of repetition at the start of every session far better than to an explanation.

This is also the part of the subject most often used to test a tutor before you commit. In a free first lesson, ask for a timed fifteen-mark question that requires a diagram, and look at what comes back. A specialist marks the diagram separately, names the missing label, and says what the figure needed to show for the argument to work. A generalist writes that the diagram was good and moves on to the prose, which tells you where the next six months will go.

sections.heading: Using the UAE economy as evidence in an Economics answer
paragraphs: Every extended Economics answer needs a real-world example, and Dubai candidates routinely reach for textbook cases from other decades and other continents. They are sitting inside one of the more interesting economies available to a seventeen-year-old. A student who can explain why a currency peg constrains monetary policy, using the dirham rather than a hypothetical, is writing the kind of answer examiners remember, and the research involved is a single afternoon's work rather than a term's.

The discipline is accuracy. An example earns marks when it is named, located, dated and used, and loses them when it is vague or wrong. So each of the examples below comes with the place to check it. Federal Tax Authority material covers the VAT position, the Central Bank covers the exchange-rate arrangement, and KHDA's own newsroom covers the schools decision. Teach the student to cite where they read it, which is also the habit the portfolio requires.

One caution worth passing on directly. Economics answers about the UAE should stay on economics: mechanisms, incentives, trade-offs and evidence. There is no need for political commentary in a Paper 1 answer, and an examiner is not marking opinions. A student who explains the efficiency and equity trade-off in a subsidy decision is doing exactly what the mark scheme asks for, which is also the safest and strongest way to write about any government's policy choices. The examples below are chosen because each maps onto a specific unit of the Standard Level course and each can be checked against a published official source in under five minutes.

sections.heading: The Standard Level Economics year counted backwards
paragraphs: Nobody in this search publishes a calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what determines whether tutoring is worth buying at all. The decisions that matter are made months before the examinations: which articles the commentaries are built on, when the school wants the portfolio finished, when the mock papers are sat, and when the school submits its entries. A family who knows those dates can buy three sessions at the right moment instead of twenty at the wrong one.

Work backwards rather than forwards. The portfolio is finished well before the papers are sat, so portfolio hours belong in DP1 and the first term of DP2, and paper hours belong after the mocks. Dubai schools set their own internal deadlines for the portfolio and they vary by several weeks between schools in the same district, which is why the first useful question to a Diploma coordinator is not about the IB calendar but about the department's own one.

On the IB dates themselves, be careful what you accept from a tutoring website. UAE schools sit the May session, and results reach candidates during the following summer, but the exact windows change between years and are published by the IB rather than by anyone selling tuition. Confirm every date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org before you plan around it. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own timetables with zone-specific versions for international centres, and those are the pages to use for an IGCSE sibling in the same house.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed to deliver, and KHDA's own guidelines require those requirements to be in place from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Diploma student that is additional timetabled instruction sitting on top of six Diploma subjects, the core, and whatever else the school requires. It is the main reason a Year 12 week has less room in it than parents expect.

The detail matters for scheduling. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Schools must also organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited. That constraint shapes timetables, and timetables decide which evenings are actually free.

Do the arithmetic before buying a weekly slot. Add up the mandatory lessons, the Diploma contact time, any after-school commitment, and the travel. What is left is the real budget of hours, and it is usually one weekday evening and part of a weekend. A plan that assumes two weekday sessions in a house with an Arabic first-language student and a Thursday commitment will be abandoned inside a month, and the money spent on the sessions that were missed is gone.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the portfolio, and the new problem of AI summaries
paragraphs: A commentary must be the student's own work, built on a source the student located, with the analysis and the evaluation theirs. A tutor may teach the unit, explain what a criterion rewards, ask whether a diagram supports the claim being made, and point out that a paragraph does not answer the question it opens with. A tutor may not supply the sentences, choose the article, or hand over a draft. The line is not a style preference. It is the difference between support and malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate.

Generative AI has made this harder to police and easier to get wrong. A student who asks a language model to summarise an article and then writes about the summary has not read the source, and it shows: the commentary discusses an economy in general terms with no figures from the piece. More seriously, if the model invented a detail, the candidate has published a fabricated fact under their own name. Schools in Dubai increasingly ask for the article to be submitted alongside the commentary for exactly this reason.

There is a practical test any parent can run. Ask your child to explain, without notes, why the chosen article is a good source for this unit and what the diagram is meant to show. A student who did the work answers in thirty seconds. A student who did not will talk about the topic instead of the source. Any tutor worth their rate will have run that test already, and will tell you honestly what the answer was.

sections.heading: What a Dubai parent can verify before paying
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. Individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fee schedule is published, so treat any figure you see quoted as unverified.

That gives you a concrete question to ask, and the answer tells you a lot. A legitimate tutor knows what the permit is, knows it costs nothing, and will say plainly whether they hold one. A provider that waves the question away, or implies that tutoring sits outside regulation, has told you how it handles every other rule as well. The official application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Be equally careful with claims of approval. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and no tutoring platform should describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson unless it holds the specific permit and can show the number. IB Gram holds none of them, and says so. Nor is there an IB Gram office in the UAE: delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, and the comparison with an in-home arrangement is set out below rather than hidden.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home Economics tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: In-home tuition is a real and widely sold product in this emirate, and it is worth understanding before dismissing it. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with some home tutors charging AED 200 to 500, and monthly in-home blocks advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. The premium over online covers travel, and the travel is paid for in two currencies: dirhams on the invoice, and the size of the pool of tutors willing to make the trip.

That second cost is the one that decides an Economics grade. A Standard Level Economics candidate in Mirdif who hires locally is choosing among the Diploma Economics specialists prepared to drive to Mirdif for a 6.30pm start. Online, the same family is choosing among everyone who teaches Standard Level Economics at that hour. For a subject taught in most Dubai Diploma schools but specialised at this level, that difference is the difference between a tutor who has supervised thirty commentaries and one who has read about them.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Lessons are delivered live and one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, recorded so revision does not depend on notes taken during the session, with a shared whiteboard for the diagrams and screen sharing for data extracts. We say this plainly rather than burying it, because two of the pages competing for this search route UAE parents to a phone number in another country without mentioning where the tutor sits.
