sections.heading: Eight weeks of evidence: what movement actually looks like
paragraphs: Families ask how long it takes. The honest answer is that criterion-level movement on Paper 1 is usually visible within six to eight weeks of fortnightly marked work, that Paper 2 recall improves as fast as the student is willing to memorise, and that criterion D language problems take a year. Anybody promising a grade is selling something nobody can deliver, and we publish no outcome statistics because we cannot produce the data behind them.

What we can show you is a record. Every marked piece carries per-criterion scores, so the plan has a visible shape rather than a feeling. The table below is the rhythm a typical eight-week block follows for a student whose diagnosis was feature-listing on criterion B. A student with a different diagnosis gets a different table, which is the point: the sequence comes from the evidence rather than from a template.

The review at week eight is a real decision point, not a sales conversation. Three outcomes are normal. The diagnosis was right and the scores moved, in which case the rhythm continues with the next component. The diagnosis was right and the scores did not move, which usually means the work is being produced but not under timed conditions, and the fix is procedural. Or the diagnosis was wrong, in which case we say so and start again from the newer evidence.

One Dubai-specific note on this cycle. Mock weeks, school productions, Islamic Education and Arabic assessments for the KHDA mandatory subjects, and Ramadan all interrupt a fortnightly rhythm. A plan that pretends otherwise is missed and then abandoned. We build the pauses in at the start and add the sessions back afterwards, and during Ramadan post-Iftar slots are straightforward precisely because nobody is travelling.

sections.heading: What English A tuition costs in Dubai, and why ours is delivered online
paragraphs: Dubai families usually begin by looking for somebody who can come to the house. It is worth being clear about both halves of that: what the in-home market actually costs here, and what we sell. IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and nothing on this site should be read as an offer of one in Dubai.

For English A specifically, the online format has an unusually concrete advantage. The work being handled is a script. A marked Paper 1 on a shared screen, with the tutor's cursor on the sentence that failed criterion B and the student rewriting it live in a shared document, is a better teaching instrument than two people leaning over the same piece of paper. Annotated work is saved and searchable afterwards, which is what makes the eight-week record possible at all.

The second advantage is supply. The constraint on English A tutoring is not the number of people who can teach English; it is the number who have marked against the Diploma's four criteria and can tell you which one a script failed. Restricting that search to people who can drive to your community by five o'clock means choosing from whoever is nearby, which usually means a general English tutor. Removing the travel constraint means choosing on the one qualification that matters.

On price, the figures below are published Dubai market rates gathered in October 2026, attributed to the providers who publish them. They are not an IB Gram price list, and we do not publish one on these pages because the rate depends on level, component and availability; the route in is a free trial lesson and a consultation. One piece of context worth knowing: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, which makes tutoring the variable line in most Dubai education budgets this year.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and the practical rules a Dubai parent should know
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the detail is worth having. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences follow for a parent. Anyone offering private lessons in the UAE without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule has been published, no amount should be quoted to you by anyone. And a permit is a permit, not a quality mark: it says the person may lawfully tutor, not that they have ever marked an English A script. Ask about both separately.

On academic honesty the position is simple enough to state in one paragraph. The individual oral, the HL essay and the Extended Essay must be the student's own work. A tutor teaches the component, explains the criteria, questions a line of inquiry, and gives written feedback on drafts the student has produced. Nobody supplies prose, nobody rewrites a draft into their own voice, and nobody hands over a thesis. Any service offering finished coursework for an IB subject is creating a malpractice risk that falls on your child.

A last practical point specific to Dubai. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed by KHDA to teach, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Those lessons occupy real timetable space, and a realistic English A plan is built around the week your child actually has rather than the one a template assumes.

process.title: Send four pieces of evidence
process.description: The most recent marked Paper 1, a marked Paper 2 if one exists, the school's criterion breakdowns, and the learner portfolio as it stands. These four documents produce a diagnosis in twenty minutes. A description of the problem, however detailed, does not.

process.title: See two named English A tutors
process.description: You get names, the components each has taught, and Gulf Standard Time availability. If the component you need is not covered by anyone free in your window, we say so and give a realistic wait rather than substituting a general English tutor without telling you.

process.title: Use the free trial as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial lesson reads the evidence and ends with a written finding: the criterion that is capping the grade, what it was inferred from, and the first piece of work that will test it. You see that finding before deciding whether to carry on.

process.title: Set the marking rhythm
process.description: We agree what gets submitted, how often, and under what conditions. For most Dubai families this is a weekly live session with a timed piece marked every fortnight, with pauses written in around mock weeks, school assessments and Ramadan.

process.title: Review the scores at week eight
process.description: Per-criterion scores across four or five marked pieces either show movement or do not. We go through the record with you and decide to continue, change the rhythm, change the tutor, or stop. Three honest outcomes, including the one where the first diagnosis was wrong.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from marked work, not from a conversation
whyPoints.description: The first session reads four pieces of your child's existing marked work and names the criterion capping the grade. That is a different starting point from a lesson built on a parent's description of the problem, and it is the reason the first six weeks are not spent on the wrong thing.

whyPoints.title: Marking in writing, with criterion letters
whyPoints.description: Every submitted piece comes back annotated with the criterion named and a score against it. A student who knows that a paragraph failed criterion B can act. A student told to add more analysis cannot, and that comment is the single commonest thing in a Dubai mock script's margin.

whyPoints.title: Timed conditions, because that is what is assessed
whyPoints.description: Paper 1 is seventy-five minutes at Standard Level and two hours fifteen at Higher. Work produced over two comfortable evenings measures something that is never assessed. We set and mark timed pieces so the practice matches the thing it is preparing for.

whyPoints.title: A record you own
whyPoints.description: Annotated scripts, per-criterion scores and the written diagnosis belong to you. If a tutor becomes unavailable or the match is wrong, the next person starts from the record. Over a two-year Diploma that continuity is worth more than any single tutor.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on what a tutor does
whyPoints.description: The oral, the HL essay and the Extended Essay are the student's own work. We state before the first session what feedback looks like and what nobody will do, because an academic-honesty finding costs a student their diploma and no amount of convenience is worth that risk.

faqs.question: What is the difference between English A Language and Literature and English A Literature?
faqs.answer: Literature is built entirely from literary works - nine at Standard Level, thirteen at Higher - and its Paper 1 hands the student an unseen literary passage. Language and Literature splits the course between literary works and non-literary bodies of work such as advertising, speeches, journalism and photography, requires four literary works at SL and six at HL, and its Paper 1 is an unseen non-literary text. Dubai schools normally decide which course a student sits. The practical difference for tutoring is large: Language and Literature students need a working method for text types they have never been taught.

faqs.question: How is Paper 1 different at Higher Level and Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Standard Level gives one unseen non-literary text with a guiding question and 1 hour 15 minutes. Higher Level gives two texts and asks for a separate analysis of each in 2 hours 15 minutes, which is less time per text once planning is counted. The weighting is 35% at both levels, which makes Paper 1 the largest single component at Higher Level and the only entirely unseen one. That is why, when a family has a limited number of sessions, Paper 1 is usually where they buy the most unprepared marks back.

faqs.question: What counts as a non-literary body of work in this course?
faqs.answer: A coherent set of texts by one producer or from one source, studied together rather than as isolated examples: a photographer's body of work, one columnist's writing across a period, a political campaign's material, a brand's advertising, a cartoonist's output. The individual oral requires one non-literary body of work alongside one literary work. Schools vary in how systematically they teach this half of the course, and a thin treatment of it is the commonest cause of weak Paper 1 scripts among Dubai students arriving from a literature-heavy IGCSE.

faqs.question: How long is the HL essay and how much does it count for?
faqs.answer: Between 1,200 and 1,500 words, and it carries 20% of the Higher Level grade. It takes one work or body of work studied in the course and pursues a narrow line of inquiry developed out of the learner portfolio. Most weak drafts fail at the line of inquiry rather than in the writing: a question broad enough to need 5,000 words produces 1,400 words of summary. Students with a properly kept portfolio from Year 12 have material to mine for a question; students without one spend weeks looking for a subject instead of writing.

faqs.question: What is a global issue, and how narrow should my child's be?
faqs.answer: A global issue is a significant concern that operates across cultures and is visible in the texts chosen - not a theme in the classroom sense, and not a topic as broad as climate or identity. It should be narrow enough to argue in ten minutes and present enough in both texts to sustain comparison. The test we use is whether the student can state it in one sentence that names an angle rather than a subject. Orals that describe the issue score modestly; orals that analyse how each text constructs it score well.

faqs.question: Why does my child get good class marks but a 4 in the English A mock?
faqs.answer: Usually because classroom work is discussed and untimed while the mock is neither. A student can understand a text thoroughly and still produce a thin script in seventy-five minutes if they have no planning routine, because they discover their argument while writing rather than before. Read the mock's criterion breakdown: if the marks are low on criterion C, focus and organisation, the problem is procedure rather than understanding, and a four-minute planning routine practised under timed conditions usually moves it within a few weeks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's Paper 2 essays properly?
faqs.answer: Marking against the published criteria with a score per criterion is exactly what the work on this page consists of, and it is the thing that distinguishes a subject specialist from a general English tutor. What a tutor cannot do is replicate the school's own moderation or predict a final grade, and anyone offering that is overselling. What marking does give you is a visible pattern: four essays with per-criterion scores show whether the gap is knowledge, analysis, structure or language, and that decides what the next six weeks address.

faqs.question: How many literary works does Language and Literature require?
faqs.answer: Four at Standard Level and six at Higher Level, chosen by the school from the prescribed reading list alongside non-literary bodies of work. That is substantially fewer works than English A: Literature, which requires nine at SL and thirteen at HL, and the difference is made up by the non-literary half of the course. For Paper 2 the number matters less than the depth of recall, since no text is available in the examination room and a student needs precisely remembered moments from two of the works to support a comparison.

faqs.question: Does the individual oral have to be recorded?
faqs.answer: The school records and submits the oral as part of its internal assessment process, and your child's coordinator will explain the school's own procedure. For preparation, we record rehearsals deliberately, because pacing is the second-commonest reason an oral underperforms: a student with four points and ten minutes typically spends six minutes on the first one. Hearing the recording fixes this faster than any amount of advice. The five minutes of teacher questions are also worth rehearsing, since they are marked and students frequently treat them as an afterthought.

faqs.question: What does IB English A tuition cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates in October 2026 run roughly AED 45-150 for budget online tutors, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 for in-home visits with travel included, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB specialist, with one premium provider publishing AED 650. Those are other providers' own figures, attributed to them, not an IB Gram price list. We start with a free trial lesson and a consultation, because the rate for a specialist depends on level, component and availability rather than on a single published number.

faqs.question: Is Language and Literature easier than Literature for a student whose first language is not English?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. The non-literary half involves less dense reading but demands precise handling of register, audience and cultural reference, which can be harder for a student still building idiomatic range. The real question is whether the student should be in English A at all or in English B, which is a placement decision the school makes from evidence rather than from fluency in conversation. The honest test is whether the student can sustain written analysis of an unseen text, and a marked Paper 1 answers it quickly.

faqs.question: My child is in the first term of Year 13. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan changes. With two terms left the priority is Paper 1, because it is the largest component at Higher Level and the one where method produces fast movement, followed by Paper 2 recall, which improves as quickly as a student is willing to memorise. The HL essay and the oral are usually already in motion with internal deadlines close, so the work there is feedback on existing drafts rather than a fresh start. What we will not tell you is that a grade is assured, because nobody can know that.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an English tutor to our apartment in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Dubai families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise: the thing being worked on is a marked script, and a shared screen with the tutor's cursor on the sentence that failed a criterion beats two people reading the same sheet of paper. The annotations are also saved, which is what makes a progress record possible.

faqs.question: How will I actually see whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Through per-criterion scores across marked work, reviewed with you at week eight. Each submitted piece carries a score against criteria A to D, so the record shows movement or its absence rather than a feeling. Three outcomes are normal at that review: the diagnosis was right and scores moved, the diagnosis was right and the work was not being done under timed conditions, or the diagnosis was wrong and we start again from newer evidence. We publish no outcome statistics, because we cannot produce the underlying data.

faqs.question: Do tutors teaching Dubai students from outside the UAE need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, governs individuals providing private tuition in the UAE. It is free of charge, valid for two years, and open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen, with a two-working-day processing time on MoHRE's own service page. Ask any tutor directly about their permit position, and ask separately about their experience marking English A scripts - the two questions are unrelated and both matter.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-liter.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB DP English A Language and Literature online tutor in Dubai, the fastest route to a useful first session is a marked script rather than a description. Send the most recent Paper 1 or Paper 2 with the school's criterion breakdown, and the learner portfolio as it stands. The trial lesson reads them and gives you a written finding: which of criteria A to D is capping the grade, the evidence behind that, and the first piece of work that will test it. The trial is free, the tutor is named before you book, and lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The cost question, answered before anything else
paragraphs: Published rates for English tuition in Dubai run from roughly AED 45 an hour to AED 650, and the two ends of that range are selling different things. At the bottom sit platforms advertising university-student tutors: EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. In the middle sit qualified subject tutors working online, broadly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. At the top sit IB specialists, around AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table showing AED 200 to AED 450 or more, while BartyED publishes AED 650 for named premium tutoring. Those are other providers' own figures, read in October 2026. None of them is our price list.

What almost nobody in this market explains is why the same subject costs four times as much from one provider as another, and the answer is simple enough to state in a sentence: the expensive hour includes marking and the cheap hour does not. In English A Language and Literature the thing that is hard to buy is a person who will read a 900-word response to an unseen text, score it against each descriptor, and explain in writing which sentence lost the mark. Conversation about themes is cheap because almost anyone can supply it. Accurate marking against published criteria is scarce, and it is what the grade actually responds to.

That reframes the budgeting question usefully. A family deciding between two providers at AED 150 and AED 300 is not choosing between value and luxury; they are choosing between an hour of discussion and an hour of assessment. Six discussion hours and two marked scripts cost about the same as four marked scripts, and in this subject the four marked scripts will do more. The arithmetic is unglamorous and it is the single most useful thing a Dubai parent can know before the first phone call.

This page is therefore organised by what a paid hour does rather than by what it is called. The tables set out the market bands with their sources, the cost of support component by component across the four assessed pieces, and a two-year sequence showing where the hours are worth most in DP1 and where they are wasted. Where the honest answer is to buy nothing, that is written down too, because in English A there are two stretches of the course where a tutor adds very little and a reading list adds a great deal.

Everything here is delivered one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own essay on screen while it is annotated. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For a marking-led subject that removes a real cost rather than a convenience: nobody is paying for forty minutes of Sheikh Zayed Road in an hourly rate, and the family selects from people who have marked Group 1 scripts rather than from whoever lives nearby.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-liter.programmesIntro: English A Language and Literature is a Diploma Programme Group 1 course, but families are usually budgeting across a longer arc than two years. The programmes below are the ones that set a student's starting position in it, with a note on what each one leaves unpaid for when DP1 begins.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Language and Literature is offered at Higher and Standard Level and assesses four components: Paper 1 on unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 as a comparative essay, an individual oral, and at Higher Level an additional essay on a studied work or body of work. Two of the four are sat under examination conditions with no texts in the room, which is why timed marked practice is the expensive part of the course rather than the reading.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools commonly run Language and Literature as the default Group 1 course because it suits a student body studying in English without English always being a first language at home. That makes the cohort wide in ability, and it is the main reason paid support in this subject is bought at very different price points inside the same classroom.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language and Literature assesses analysing, organising, producing text and using language, and it introduces unseen extract work early. A student arriving in DP1 from a continuum school has usually met the demand before. The budget consequence is direct: that student needs marked timed practice rather than teaching, which is the cheaper of the two to buy in volume.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a large number of IB continuum schools, so a significant share of DP1 students here come through MYP rather than IGCSE. Families moving between the two systems mid-school should budget for one diagnostic marked script early rather than a term of weekly sessions bought blind.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE English
programmes.description: IGCSE English rewards accuracy, structure and a clear response to a seen question. The transition into Language and Literature costs most students one grade in the first term, because the Diploma asks for the effect of a specific choice on a specific audience rather than a competent general answer. That gap is a teaching problem, which is the one part of this course where paying for instruction rather than marking is correct.
programmes.countryNote: UK curriculum accounts for 37 per cent of enrolment across Dubai's private schools, so the IGCSE-to-Diploma transition is the single commonest route into English A here. Budgeting two or three teaching hours in the first term of DP1 is cheaper than six marking hours in DP2 trying to unpick habits that were never corrected.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: Group 1 students frequently register the Extended Essay in English, and the Theory of Knowledge essay draws on the same analytical writing. Both compete for the same budget and the same evenings. Families who plan the core alongside the subject usually buy fewer hours overall, because one tutor covering the analytical craft across all three is cheaper than three separate arrangements.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai schools the Extended Essay internal deadlines and the English A individual oral window often fall within the same half-term, which is the predictable spending spike in DP2. Mapping it in October rather than discovering it in February is the difference between a planned block and an emergency rate.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-liter.subjectsIntro: Families rarely buy support in one subject alone, and the cost of a package depends on which combination is being covered. The subjects below are the ones most often bought alongside English A Language and Literature in Dubai, with a note on whether a shared tutor is realistic or whether a specialist is unavoidable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Four components, two of them unseen and timed. Paid hours earn most on marked Paper 1 practice and on narrowing the individual oral global issue; they earn least on reading the set works, which the school already does and a student can do unpaid.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: The sibling Group 1 course, built on nine or thirteen prescribed works. Cost behaves differently: the volume of reading drives the budget rather than the marking load, so a student behind on set works needs a reading plan before they need a tutor.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language acquisition course, not a Group 1 literature course. Parents sometimes buy English B support for a child in English A, which is cheap and ineffective. The criteria are different and so is the marking, so the saving disappears at the first assessed piece.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK essay rewards the same discipline as a Language and Literature Paper 2: a controlled claim, evidence, and an acknowledged limitation. A Group 1 specialist can usually cover both inside one booked hour, which is the clearest package saving available in the Diploma core.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Essay-heavy and often bought in the same term. Source evaluation in History and the handling of non-literary text types in Language and Literature train the same habit of asking who produced a text and for whom, so marked essays in one frequently improve the other.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Chosen widely in Dubai schools and heavy on precise written explanation under time pressure. Students who write loosely in English A usually write loosely here too, which means one marking-led arrangement can address both and a second tutor is often an avoidable cost.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Paper answers demand definition, diagram and evaluation in a fixed order. Group 1 students who struggle with structure rather than ideas often improve in both subjects from the same intervention, so check for overlap before funding two separate weekly hours.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study writing rewards relevance and selection, the exact skill a Paper 2 comparative essay tests. A student losing marks for including everything they know will be losing them in both subjects, and the fix is one habit rather than two syllabuses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: No overlap at all, and listed here for budgeting honesty. Maths support cannot share an hour with English A; it is a separate specialist and a separate line in the budget, usually at the upper end of the published Dubai bands in an exam year.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-liter.regionsIntro: What a Dubai family pays is partly a function of where they live, because in-home arrangements price travel into the hour and the local supply of Group 1 specialists varies. The notes below record the practical cost effect in each area rather than describing the neighbourhood.

regions.name: Jumeirah
regions.note: Short commutes and a dense school cluster, so in-home rates here sit at the lower end of the travel premium. The local tutor pool is mostly primary and IGCSE; Diploma Group 1 specialists are scarce enough that families end up paying a scarcity premium for proximity.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: High apartment density and easy access, which keeps visiting rates competitive, but parking and building access routinely cost ten minutes a visit. Families here are among the most likely to switch to online once they have compared two quotes for the same component.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Villa communities a long way from the central school belt. Travel is the dominant variable in any in-home quote, and published in-home bands of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 sit near the top of that range by the time a tutor has driven out and back.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer schools, high demand and families often buying two subjects at once. The useful saving here is a shared hour across English A and Theory of Knowledge rather than a discount on the rate itself, which providers in this area rarely offer.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Large catchments and long school runs, so evening slots are compressed into a narrow window and in-demand tutors charge accordingly for it. An online slot after dinner is both cheaper and more reliable than anything booked between four and six.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Apartment living with heavy parking constraints and a working-parent profile. Later evening sessions are the norm, and the premium charged for a 8pm in-home visit is the clearest example in the city of paying for logistics rather than for teaching.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Several large IB schools within a few kilometres, which makes it one of the few areas where a local Diploma specialist is genuinely findable. Even here the pool is small, and a family needing Higher Level marking usually widens the search beyond the area.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Growing family communities further from the established school cluster. Visiting rates reflect the drive, and the saving from online delivery is larger here than in almost any other part of Dubai for the same quality of tutor.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Al Sufouh
schoolClusters.note: The established selective cluster, where Group 1 cohorts are large and school feedback is usually detailed. Families here most often buy a single marked read as a second opinion rather than a weekly block, which is the cheapest useful purchase in this subject.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Dubai Hills and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Large IB continuum schools with mixed-ability Group 1 classes. Spending here tends to start earlier, in the first term of DP1, which is also where it is most effective: teaching hours bought at the transition cost less than marking hours bought in DP2.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Academic City
schoolClusters.note: Long-established schools with big year groups and later session windows. The commonest purchase pattern here is a compressed block before the individual oral, and the commonest avoidable cost is paying for the same block twice because the first provider returned no written marks.

sections.heading: What an hour of English A support actually costs in Dubai, by provider model
paragraphs: An IB DP English A Language and Literature tutor in Dubai charges somewhere between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour depending on the model, and the model matters more than the badge. The table below compares the shapes of provider rather than named brands, with the AED bands taken from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, all read in October 2026. The column that decides value is not the rate; it is whether marked written work comes back.

Three of the six providers researched for this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency Dubai families do not transact in. That opacity is itself a cost: a parent cannot compare what they cannot see, and the first quote they receive becomes the anchor for every judgement afterwards. Publishing the bands here is not generosity. It is the only way the rest of this page's arithmetic makes sense.

Read the table as a shopping list rather than a league table. A student who writes fluently and needs timed practice should buy from the row with marking included and ignore the rest. A student who has not understood what Paper 1 asks needs teaching first, which the lowest band can sometimes supply adequately. A student eight weeks from the May session with three unmarked mocks in a drawer should buy marking only, and quickly.

Monthly packages are also visible in this market, and they are worth reading carefully. Figures seen include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Divide any package by the number of hours before comparing it with an hourly rate; the per-hour figure is often higher than it looks.

sections.heading: The five variables that move an English A quote up or down
paragraphs: Two families in the same Dubai building, with children in the same class, are routinely quoted rates that differ by a factor of three. The variation is not arbitrary and it is not mostly about the tutor's charisma. Five things move the number, and four of them are inside the family's control, which makes them worth knowing before the first conversation rather than after the third invoice.

The first is whether marking is included. An hour that contains a marked 900-word response consumes close to two hours of the tutor's time, and any honest rate reflects that. The second is level: Higher Level adds a fourth assessed component and a longer essay, so the same weekly arrangement covers more ground and is priced accordingly. The third is urgency. A block booked eight weeks before a school deadline is priced differently from one booked in October, because the tutor is displacing other work and the hours have to be compressed.

The fourth is delivery format, which is the largest single lever in this city. Published in-home bands of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 overlap with online specialist bands of AED 200 to AED 450, but the in-home figure buys a smaller pool of tutors and a fraction of the hour spent in traffic. The fifth is the one families almost never ask about: whether the tutor has marked IB Group 1 work before. A tutor who has not cannot score a script against the descriptors, and a session without a score is a conversation, whatever it costs.

There is a sixth variable that behaves differently, and it belongs in a warning rather than a list. Providers in this market do sell finished coursework, and the price looks competitive against a term of honest sessions. A family comparing quotes should establish early that what is being sold is teaching, marking and feedback on the student's own writing. Anything else is an academic malpractice risk that falls on the student under IB rules, and no saving justifies it.

sections.heading: Cost by component: which paid hours earn their fee
paragraphs: English A Language and Literature is four separate assessments with four separate cost profiles, and treating it as a single weekly habit is how families overspend. The table below sets out what a paid hour actually does on each component, roughly how many hours it usually takes, and the market band that applies. The final column is the one that saves money, because it names the point in the course at which the purchase is worth making rather than merely possible.

Paper 1 is the component where paid marking is close to irreplaceable. The text is unseen, the skill is transferable and the only way to build it is to write under time pressure and have the result scored accurately. A student can read about unseen analysis for a term and improve very little; four marked responses with descriptor-level feedback will usually move something. This is the line of the budget to protect first.

At the other end, the set works are the cheapest part of the course to cover and the most commonly bought. A student who has not read a prescribed text does not need a tutor; they need the text and three weeks. Paying for summaries of works the school is already teaching is the single clearest waste in this subject, and any provider who encourages it should be treated with caution. The same is true of generic essay-writing lessons untied to a scored piece of the student's own work.

Two components sit in between and reward narrow, specific purchases. The individual oral stands or falls on whether the global issue is narrow enough to be evidenced by two extracts, which is one hour of hard questioning rather than a term of coaching. The Higher Level essay turns on the line of inquiry, which is likewise a single decision taken early and expensively reversed late. Buy one hour at the decision point in each and you will not need six later.

sections.heading: Why marking is the expensive part, and the unseen text is the reason
paragraphs: Paper 1 gives a student a text nobody has prepared them for and asks what the writer is doing and how. Nothing on the paper can be revised in advance. That single design decision determines the economics of the whole course, because it means the only thing worth paying for is the repeated cycle of attempt, accurate score, named correction, next attempt. A tutor who discusses a text with a student is doing something pleasant and almost unmeasurable. A tutor who scores the student's own writing is doing the thing the grade responds to.

Accurate scoring is also genuinely hard, which is why it costs what it costs. The descriptors reward the analysis of specific choices and their effect on a particular audience, and they are unforgiving about general appreciation however well written. Marking against them requires somebody who has internalised the standard, usually by teaching the course or by marking for a board. An intelligent graduate reader without that calibration will give a response a generous mark and a useless commentary, and the family will not discover the problem until a mock.

This is why the cheapest effective purchase in English A is a package of marked scripts with no teaching attached. Four timed responses, scored descriptor by descriptor, with the specific sentence-level fault named each time, is a smaller invoice than a term of weekly hours and a larger movement for most students. It also produces a record: scores on dated scripts that a parent can compare without being able to mark English themselves.

The limit is worth stating. Marking works for students who can already produce a response of roughly the right shape. A student who does not yet know what the question is asking will get little from a score, because they cannot act on it, and for them two or three genuine teaching hours must come first. That diagnosis takes one marked script to make, which is the honest reason the free trial hour exists and why its output is a written statement rather than a sales conversation.

sections.heading: A two-year English A budget, sequenced rather than spread
paragraphs: Most Dubai families spend on English A reactively: nothing for a year, then an expensive scramble in the second term of DP2. The sequence below spends roughly the same money in a different order and buys more with it. The principle is simple. Buy teaching early, when habits are cheap to change. Buy decisions at the point they are taken. Buy marking throughout DP2. Buy nothing at all during the two stretches where a tutor adds little.

The AED figures in the table are indicative totals at mid-market specialist rates of roughly AED 200 to AED 300 an hour, which is where a tutor who returns descriptor-level scores generally sits in this market. They are arithmetic on published market bands, not a quotation from us. A family working to a smaller total should cut rows from the bottom of the list rather than reduce the quality of the marking rows, because a cheap mark is worse than no mark; it tells a student something confident and wrong.

The two zero-spend stretches deserve naming, because no provider has any incentive to mention them. The first is the opening months of DP1 once the transition habits are corrected, when the course is reading and the student needs the books rather than a tutor. The second is the fortnight immediately before the written papers, when new teaching cannot land and the useful activity is timed practice the student can do alone with a mark scheme the school already has.

One more piece of context Dubai parents find useful when setting a figure. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are largely fixed and outside a family's control; tutoring is not. That makes it the education cost most worth planning deliberately, in blocks tied to named components, rather than as an open-ended monthly subscription.

sections.heading: What you should not be paying for in this market
paragraphs: Some of the clearest savings in Dubai come from refusing things that are commonly sold. The first is past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables. These belong to the IB, Cambridge or Pearson and should not be reproduced or supplied as downloads by a tutoring provider; a legitimate tutor references them and points to the official source. Paying for a bundle of copied material is paying for somebody else's copyright risk.

The second is anything resembling an accreditation claim. No tutoring provider should attach the name of a regulator — KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education — or of an examination board to words such as approval, accreditation or authorisation unless it holds that specific permit and can show you the number. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises, which is a different legal animal from an individual tutor; a provider using that language loosely is either confused or hoping you are. We hold no such approval and do not imply one.

The third is a statistic. Rates in this market are frequently justified with figures that have no sample, no date and no method: satisfaction percentages, average score claims, self-published star ratings. Two researched competitors show different review totals on the same page. A number without an n and a date is a marketing device, and paying a premium because of one is paying for the device.

The fourth is a guarantee. Nobody can promise a grade, a point total or a specific improvement in a subject with two unseen components marked externally, and a refund promise tied to an outcome is a reason for more scepticism rather than less. What a provider can honestly commit to is the process: marking returned in writing, descriptor-level scores, dated artefacts, and a stated fallback when no specialist is free. Those are checkable before you pay and worth more than any promise about results.

sections.heading: Online delivery, the in-home premium, and who is permitted to teach
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is what many Dubai families picture when they start looking, and the published bands are roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel priced in. The question worth asking is what the extra money buys in a subject whose assessed work is written. A visiting tutor and an online tutor both read an essay on a screen or a page; one of them has also spent forty minutes on Al Khail Road, and somebody is paying for that. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE at all. Tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we offer only in India, and the Dubai arrangement is one-to-one over live video with the student's own writing shared on screen.

The practical gain is not price alone. The pool of people who have marked IB Group 1 scripts is small, and restricting it to a twenty-minute drive from Mirdif or Al Furjan shrinks it to almost nothing. Families who insist on proximity usually end up paying a specialist rate for a generalist, which is the worst available trade. Online delivery also survives travel, which matters in a city where families are routinely out of the country for several weeks a year and a weekly slot otherwise collapses in July.

There is a legal dimension families should know before paying anyone. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any figure quoted to you as unverified.

One related rule saves money and trouble. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. The idea of hiring your child's own English teacher privately is therefore not a bargain to negotiate; it is an arrangement to decline. An external marker is also more useful, because they read the essay as an unknown examiner will rather than as the person who taught the lesson it came from.

process.title: Say what you are trying to buy
process.description: Send the student's level, the components causing trouble, the next school deadline and any budget ceiling. A stated ceiling produces a better plan than a vague one, because the sequencing changes completely between a four-hour total and a two-year arrangement. Nothing beyond the student's existing school work is needed.

process.title: Take the free trial hour
process.description: One hour, online, one-to-one, with no card required. One existing piece of writing is marked against the published descriptors and returned, and you receive a written statement of what the student needs and what it would cost in hours. If the answer is that no paid support is required, that is what the document says.

process.title: Agree hours against named components
process.description: Work is booked as hours attached to components rather than as an open monthly habit: four marked Paper 1 scripts, one hour on the oral global issue, one read of the Higher Level draft. The rate is stated per hour before anything is confirmed, with no package that hides the per-hour figure.

process.title: Marking returned in writing, every time
process.description: Each piece comes back with a score against every descriptor, the sentence that cost the mark identified, and a dated record added to the running file. The work stays in the student's own words; a tutor marks, questions and models, and never supplies text that will be submitted.

process.title: Review the record, then cut or continue
process.description: At the end of the block the scores are read in sequence. If descriptor marks have moved, the next hours go to the components still at risk. If they have not, the arrangement changes or stops. Continuing to buy weekly hours that the record does not support is the commonest way families overspend in this market.

whyPoints.title: Published bands, with the source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider and the month it was read, so a family can judge any quote they receive. Three of the six competitors researched for this market publish no price at all; two of the rest quote in dollars. A parent cannot compare what nobody will show them.

whyPoints.title: Costed by component, not by calendar
whyPoints.description: Hours are attached to Paper 1 scripts, the oral global issue and the Higher Level line of inquiry, so you can see what you are buying marks for. It also makes the two zero-spend stretches of the course visible, which no provider paid by the month has any reason to mention.

whyPoints.title: Marking is the product
whyPoints.description: An hour here includes a response scored against each published descriptor with the sentence that lost the mark named. That is the component of tutoring a Group 1 grade responds to, and it is the one most commonly left out of a cheap rate and charged as an extra in a mid-market one.

whyPoints.title: No accreditation language we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: We hold no KHDA, ADEK, MoE, IB or Cambridge approval and never imply one. A KHDA Educational Services Permit belongs to training institutes with premises. Providers in this market use that language loosely, and it is the single most misleading phrase available to a page like this one.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is priced in
whyPoints.description: A tutor reads, marks, questions, models and records. Finished coursework is sold in this market at prices that look competitive against honest sessions; under IB rules the consequence falls on the student. Anything we will not do is written here rather than discovered during a call.

whyPoints.title: A stated fallback instead of a placement
whyPoints.description: When no Group 1 specialist is free for the slot a family needs, we say so and offer a different time, a marked-script package without live teaching, or a wait. Placing a generalist at a specialist rate is how the published upper bands in this market get justified, and it is not something we will do.

faqs.question: What does an English A Language and Literature tutor charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market run from roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour. Budget platforms advertise from AED 45 to AED 65, qualified online subject tutors broadly AED 150 to AED 300, IB specialists around AED 200 to AED 450 and above, in-home visits AED 180 to AED 500 with travel priced in, and premium named tutoring up to AED 650. Those are other providers' own published figures read in October 2026, including Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. What separates the bands is whether marked written work comes back, not the badge on the website.

faqs.question: Why do two quotes for the same English A support differ by three times?
faqs.answer: Five things move the number. Whether marking is included, because scoring a 900-word response consumes close to two hours of a tutor's time. Whether the student is at Higher Level, which adds a fourth component. How urgent the booking is, since compressed blocks displace other work. Whether delivery is in-home, which prices travel into the hour. And whether the tutor has ever marked IB Group 1 work, which determines if a score means anything. Four of those five are inside a family's control, which is why asking about them before the first quote changes the price.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to buy a block of hours or pay one session at a time?
faqs.answer: Per hour, a block is usually quoted slightly lower, and that is not the main reason to prefer one. A block tied to a named component forces both sides to state what the hours are for, which prevents the open-ended weekly habit that is the commonest overspend in this subject. Paying session by session suits a student who needs occasional marking and already works well with their school. Avoid monthly packages whose per-hour figure is not shown: divide the total by the hours before comparing, because the real rate is often above the headline.

faqs.question: Does marking a Paper 1 response cost more than an hour of teaching?
faqs.answer: It costs more of the tutor's time, so an honest rate reflects it. A timed response of around 900 words takes real time to score against every descriptor and to annotate at sentence level, and that work happens before the session rather than during it. The trade is still favourable for most students, because a marked script produces a specific, dated, actionable finding while an hour of discussion usually produces a pleasant conversation. For a student who does not yet understand what the paper asks, teaching has to come first; one marked script reveals which case you are in.

faqs.question: Which part of the English A course is worth paying for first?
faqs.answer: Marked practice on the unseen Paper 1, because nothing about that paper can be revised in advance and the only route to the skill is write, score accurately, correct, repeat. Protect that line of the budget before anything else. The next best purchases are single hours at two decision points: narrowing the individual oral global issue before extracts are chosen, and pressure-testing the Higher Level essay line of inquiry when the question is set. Both are cheap early and expensive to reverse late, which is the opposite of how most families sequence their spending.

faqs.question: Our school teaches English A well. What are we actually paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Volume and calibration of marking. A Dubai Group 1 teacher with a full timetable and a large cohort cannot score every timed response at descriptor level for every student, however good they are. A paid hour buys that attention on your child's own writing, plus a second reader who has no investment in the lesson the essay came from. If the school is already returning detailed descriptor-level marks and the student is acting on them, the honest answer is that you do not need a tutor, and a trial hour will say so in writing.

faqs.question: Does the Higher Level essay need its own budget line?
faqs.answer: Two hours, placed carefully, usually covers it. The first goes on the line of inquiry at the point the question is set, because a question that is too broad caps the mark before any writing happens and is painful to change later. The second goes on one marked read of the near-final draft. A third read rarely repays itself. At mid-market Dubai specialist rates of roughly AED 200 to AED 300 an hour, that is a small, defined cost against a component that carries real weight at Higher Level and is frequently left to the last fortnight.

faqs.question: How many hours does a student usually need before the individual oral?
faqs.answer: One to two at the decision stage, plus one rehearsal, is the common pattern. The oral stands or falls on whether the global issue is narrow enough that two extracts can genuinely evidence it, and that is a questioning exercise rather than a teaching one: an hour of someone asking what the issue excludes until it survives. Rehearsal coaching bought before the issue is settled is money spent polishing something that will have to be rebuilt. Families who get the order right usually spend less in total and arrive calmer.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor who has never marked IB work a saving?
faqs.answer: Not in this subject. The descriptors reward analysis of specific choices and their effect on a particular audience, and they are unforgiving about general appreciation however fluently written. A reader without that calibration gives a generous mark and a vague commentary, and the student acts on both. The error surfaces at a mock, usually in the second term of DP2, when there is no time left to rebuild. A cheap mark is worse than no mark, because it tells a student something confident and wrong.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai rise closer to the May session?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than list prices changing, and the effect on a family is the same. Specialists fill their slots by January, so a block booked in March is competing for compressed hours and is priced accordingly, if it can be found at all. Bestimate's monthly estimates put specialist exam-year support at roughly AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for weekly sessions, against AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. Booking the marking line of the budget in the first term of DP2 is both cheaper and more likely to exist when you need it.

faqs.question: Should we ask a Dubai provider whether their rate includes VAT?
faqs.answer: Yes, and ask it in writing. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees here, because doing so responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and this page does not have one. What a family can reasonably require of any provider is clarity about their own quoted figure: whether the number is final, what it covers, and whether a tax registration number exists. A provider who cannot answer plainly about their own invoice is telling you something useful about how the rest of the arrangement will run.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful second opinion on an English A essay?
faqs.answer: A single marked read. One hour in which an existing essay is scored against each published descriptor and returned annotated, with a short conversation about the three changes that matter most. It costs one hour at the specialist band rather than a term at it, and it answers the question most families actually have, which is whether the school's feedback is right and whether paid support is needed at all. Several families use it once, act on it, and never book anything else. That is a good outcome.

faqs.question: Is small-group English A tuition worth the saving in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For teaching a shared skill, sometimes. For marking, no. A group of two to four students is cheaper per student and works adequately when everybody needs the same explanation of what Paper 1 asks for. It stops working the moment the need becomes individual, which in this subject is almost immediately, because the sentence that costs your child a mark is not the sentence costing the student beside them. Group marking produces a common commentary rather than descriptor scores on an individual script, and the grade responds to the latter.

faqs.question: We have a fixed total of about AED 3,000 for the year. Where should it go?
faqs.answer: At mid-market specialist rates of roughly AED 200 to AED 300 an hour that is ten to fifteen hours, and the sequence matters more than the total. Spend two or three hours early on the transition habits, one or two at the individual oral decision point, then put the bulk into marked Paper 1 scripts across DP2 at about one a fortnight, keeping two hours in reserve for the Higher Level draft. Buy no set-work summaries and no new teaching in the final fortnight. That order consistently produces more movement than the same money spread evenly.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an English A tutor to our address in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not arrange home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. English A support for Dubai families is delivered one-to-one over live video, with the student's own essay shared on screen while it is annotated. For a marking-led subject that removes a cost rather than a benefit: no part of the hour is spent in traffic, and the family chooses from people who have scored IB Group 1 scripts rather than from whoever is within driving distance.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-liter.closingHeading: Price the marking first, then the rest
dubai/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-liter.closingBody: If you are weighing quotes for English A Language and Literature in Dubai, the useful first step costs nothing and takes an hour. Send one piece of your child's recent writing and take the free trial: it comes back scored against each published descriptor, with the sentence that cost the mark identified and a written note of how many hours the real work needs and what it would cost at a stated rate. You will also be told plainly if the answer is no paid support at all, which happens more often than this market admits. Decide after you have the document, not before.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-literature-home-tu.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach DP Literature as a markable subject: unseen extract analysis returned with criterion marks, comparative essays tracked across attempts, and oral rehearsals scored rather than praised. Each card shows levels, Gulf Standard Time availability and current capacity for marking work.

intro.heading: A predicted grade is not evidence, and most Dubai families are working from one
paragraphs: The call that starts most DP Literature enquiries in Dubai goes roughly like this. The student is predicted a 5. The school report says they write thoughtfully and need to develop their analysis. Nobody at home can tell whether that means the readings are shallow, the structure is loose, the quotations are decorative or the essays simply run out of time. The family has a grade, a sentence of feedback and no mechanism for finding out which of those four things is true.

That is a measurement problem rather than a teaching problem, and it has a measurable solution. Every component of DP Literature is marked against four criteria with published mark allocations, and every practice response can be given a mark on each of them. Do that eight or ten times across a term and a pattern appears: a student who sits consistently at the top band for understanding and the bottom band for organisation has a completely different problem from one whose marks are even across all four and simply low. Those two students need opposite teaching, and without marked evidence nobody can tell them apart.

Dubai's school context makes this worse rather than better, and not because the teaching is poor. KHDA records 227 private schools in the emirate teaching 387,441 students across 17 curricula, and the IB accounts for 7% of enrolment. DP Literature classes are frequently small, which is good, but the teacher marking them is also running Language and Literature, the Extended Essay supervision and often a Group 1 cohort across two year groups. Detailed criterion-level marking of practice work is the first thing that gets squeezed, and it is exactly the thing a family cannot replace at home.

There is a second thing schools squeeze, and it costs marks silently. The course requires works studied in translation, and those works are the ones a stretched department covers fastest. A student who has read a translated work in three weeks, discussed it once, and will be asked about it in an individual oral or a Paper 2 comparison carries a weak point into two components. Nobody flags it because nothing went wrong in class; it only shows up in the exam, where a comparison is only as strong as its weaker half.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai. Home visiting is a service we offer only in India, as every page in our UAE set states. Dubai Literature students work with us one to one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the marked paper on a shared screen. The format matters less than the discipline attached to it: a mark per criterion on every response, a written record of the pattern, and a six-week cycle at the end of which you can read what changed rather than being told that progress is being made.
bullets: Four criteria with published mark allocations run across every component of the course
A mark pattern across eight to ten responses distinguishes four different problems that look identical in a report
Works studied in translation are the commonest silent weak point in a Dubai cohort
SL studies a minimum of nine works; HL a minimum of thirteen
Progress is reported as a tracked mark pattern, never as a predicted grade we invented

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-literature-home-tu.programmesIntro: Dubai students arrive at DP Literature from distinct starting points, and each produces a recognisable mark signature in the first term. These are the stages we support.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme English A: Literature
programmes.description: Two years of literary study organised around three areas of exploration — readers, writers and texts; time and space; intertextuality — with seven central concepts running through them. Assessed by Paper 1 guided literary analysis of unseen extracts, Paper 2 comparative essay, an individual oral on two extracts, and at Higher Level an essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words on one studied work.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is usually the smaller of the two Group 1 courses, taken by students who want literary study for its own sake or who need it for a humanities application. Smaller classes mean better discussion and, paradoxically, less marked practice, because one teacher is covering both English A courses.

programmes.name: MYP Language and Literature
programmes.description: Marked on analysing, organising, producing text and using language on eight-point scales. Students from a full MYP route arrive in DP1 already used to criterion-referenced marking, which means a mark per criterion is a familiar language to them rather than a novelty.
programmes.countryNote: Students who join a Dubai IB sixth form at 16 from a non-IB system frequently have never seen a criterion-referenced mark before, and their first reaction to one is to read it as a percentage. Teaching them to read their own marks is the first week's work.

programmes.name: IGCSE English Literature
programmes.description: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE English Literature examine set texts and unseen poetry or prose. The mark signature these students arrive with is distinctive: strong on quotation recall, weak on sustained argument, because IGCSE rewards coverage of points and DP rewards one argument held across an essay.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools make up 37% of Dubai private-school enrolment (KHDA, 2024-25), so this is the commonest feeder route. The point-by-point habit is diagnosable from a single marked Paper 1 and takes about four cycles to unlearn.

programmes.name: English A: Language and Literature, for students comparing courses
programmes.description: The parallel Group 1 course, where Paper 1 presents unseen non-literary texts and the individual oral pairs a literary work with a non-literary body of work. Students occasionally switch between the courses in DP1, and the mark evidence from the first term is the only sensible basis for that decision.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai IB schools run both, with Language and Literature carrying the larger cohort. Where a switch is being considered, the school's DP coordinator decides; what we can contribute is a marked record rather than an impression.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-literature-home-tu.subjectsIntro: Literature students in Dubai usually need support in one or two other subjects in the same term. These are the ones we most often run alongside it.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis of unseen literary extracts, Paper 2 comparative essay, individual oral on two extracts including one work in translation, and at HL an essay on one studied work. Translated works are the commonest weak half of a comparison.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The parallel course, with unseen non-literary texts in Paper 1 and a non-literary body of work in the oral. Students comparing the two courses need the mark evidence from DP1, not a preference.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source evaluation papers, a world-history topic and a historical investigation. The subject whose marking most resembles Literature's: an argument sustained across an essay beats a list of accurate points.

subjects.name: Philosophy
subjects.description: A core theme, optional themes, a prescribed text and an internal assessment on a non-philosophical stimulus. Offered by few Dubai schools and a natural pairing for strong Literature students.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word prescribed-title essay and an exhibition of three objects with commentaries. Literature students are usually comfortable with the essay and underestimate how specific the exhibition commentaries must be.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches with an experimental study report. Command terms decide marks, and students who write associatively in Literature carry the habit across.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro, the global economy and a portfolio of commentaries on published articles. The commentaries reward precise reading of a source, which is a transferable Literature skill.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof-oriented route with a mathematical exploration due in the same term as the HL essay. The clash is the problem more often than the content is.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Comparative study, process portfolio and exhibition. The comparative study asks for the same move as a Paper 2 answer: a comparison that reveals something neither object shows alone.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay. Studies in Language and Literature is a common category in Dubai and the commonest failure is a question that can be answered by describing the novel.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-literature-home-tu.regionsTitle: Dubai communities our Literature students come from
dubai/ib-dp-english-a-literature-home-tu.regionsIntro: Literature runs at fewer Dubai schools than its sister course, so our students travel further to school and are spread across the emirate rather than clustered. These are the communities we work with most, and what the local day does to a session slot.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Dubai Science Park
regions.note: Apartment and townhouse communities within reach of several IB schools. Students here can usually commit to a timed 75-minute block on a weekday evening, which makes the six-week cycle easier to run to schedule.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Spread-out villa districts with few schools inside them, so students travel in several directions. Session times here are set after confirming the actual bus arrival rather than the published one.

regions.name: Town Square and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Newer, value-oriented family housing with long commutes to the older IB schools. These students lose the most time to travel, and an online timed paper at home recovers an hour of it each week.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour and Ras Al Khor
regions.note: Recently occupied towers with young families and a growing secondary cohort. School options are still limited nearby, so students commonly attend schools across the creek and arrive home late.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and The Gardens
regions.note: Dense, affordable apartment living with students at a wide range of schools and prior curricula. The mark signatures here vary more than in any other community we work with, which is exactly why a diagnosis comes before a plan.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej and Mushrif
regions.note: Low-density villa areas on the eastern edge, with long drives to the western IB cluster. Weekend morning sessions work better here than weekday ones, and timed papers are scheduled accordingly.

regions.name: Jebel Ali Village and The Gardens
regions.note: Older established housing near the southern school cluster. Students frequently take Literature alongside two sciences, so the HL essay deadline competes with internal assessment deadlines elsewhere.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB schools running Literature as a separate Group 1 class
schoolClusters.note: In this group Literature is timetabled as its own course rather than merged into Language and Literature. Classes are small and discussion is strong; marked practice is usually what thins, because one teacher covers both English A courses and Extended Essay supervision.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools where Literature runs as a minority option
schoolClusters.note: Here Group 1 is effectively one class and Literature candidates may be taught alongside Language and Literature students, sharing lessons and splitting for the components that differ. Those candidates carry the largest gaps on works in translation and on unseen literary extract practice.

schoolClusters.city: British-track schools feeding DP Literature at 16
schoolClusters.note: Students arriving from IGCSE English Literature bring quotation recall and a point-by-point essay habit. The DP demand for one argument sustained across an essay is the specific thing to unlearn, and it is visible in a single marked Paper 1.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-literature-home-tu.modesIntro: Every pattern below produces the same artefact: a marked record. The difference is what gets marked and how often. All sessions run one to one over live video.

modes.title: The six-week evidence cycle
modes.description: The default pattern. Six weeks, one timed response written each week and returned with a mark against each criterion, one session a week spent on the gap between the mark awarded and the mark available. At the end of six weeks the mark pattern is readable and the plan for the next cycle is set by the evidence rather than by a guess.
bullets: A mark per criterion on every response, dated and kept
The pattern reviewed at week six, in writing, with the family
The next cycle's focus chosen from the pattern, not from a syllabus checklist

modes.title: Works in translation repair
modes.description: A short block aimed at the half of the course that schools cover fastest. Translated works are read properly, the questions an examiner can ask about translation and context are rehearsed, and the student builds comparative notes that will hold in Paper 2 and in the oral. Usually four to six sessions, best placed in the spring of DP1.
bullets: One translated work read in full, not in summary
Comparative notes built so Paper 2 has two strong halves rather than one
Translation and context questions rehearsed, since both appear in orals

modes.title: HL essay supervision with a draft trail
modes.description: Four to six sessions from line of inquiry to submitted essay, with every draft dated and kept. The trail matters for two reasons: it shows the family what changed between drafts, and it is the student's own record of their process if any question about authorship is ever raised. Drafting happens between sessions, by the student.

Every draft dated and retained, so the development is visible
Feedback written against criteria; the rewriting is the student's own

sections.heading: What counts as evidence of progress, and what only looks like it
paragraphs: Families hiring an IB DP english A literature home tutor in Dubai are usually hoping to buy improvement, and improvement in this subject is slow enough that something has to stand in for it week to week. What stands in matters. A session that ends with the student feeling more confident has produced a feeling. A session that ends with a marked response, a mark against each of four criteria and a named difference from last week's mark has produced a data point. Six of those make a pattern, and a pattern is the only honest basis for saying anything about progress at all.

The distinction is worth being blunt about because the market trades heavily on the wrong side of it. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this sector publish no price and no method; several publish satisfaction percentages with no sample size, date or method behind them. We publish no such figure on this page for the straightforward reason that we cannot produce the underlying data, and any provider quoting one to you should be asked for its n, its date and how it was collected.

What we can do is be specific about the artefact a family receives. At the end of a six-week cycle you get the dated responses, the criterion marks on each, a short written note on which criterion moved and which did not, and a statement of what the next cycle will target. That is checkable. If nothing moved, the note says so, which is uncomfortable and occasionally the most useful sentence in the document. No tutor can promise a grade, and the evidence pack exists precisely so that nobody has to.
