sections.heading: Reading a marked Paper 1 response: what the annotations actually mean
paragraphs: Most Dubai parents have a marked Literature paper in a file somewhere and cannot read it. Teacher annotations are written for the student and in the compressed idiom of someone marking thirty scripts, and they map onto the criteria in ways that are not obvious. Learning to decode them is a twenty-minute skill that permanently changes a family's ability to tell whether a tutor is earning their fee.

Paper 1 in Literature presents unseen literary extracts with a guiding question — one extract at Standard Level in 75 minutes, two at Higher Level in 135 minutes — and carries 35% of the grade at both levels. The response is marked against four criteria covering understanding and interpretation, analysis and evaluation, focus and organisation, and language. Almost every annotation a teacher writes is a comment on one of those four, and the trick is knowing which.

"Develop this" usually means the analysis criterion: a point was made and its effect was not argued. "Relevance?" is almost always the organisation criterion: the paragraph has drifted from the guiding question. "Expression" and any underlined phrase without comment is the language criterion. "Explain" or a question mark beside a quotation is the understanding criterion: the interpretation is asserted rather than shown. Once a family can sort a page of annotations into four piles, the shape of the problem becomes visible without anyone having to be an examiner. The blank final third of a script is its own annotation, and the loudest one on the page: it says the student planned more paragraphs than the time allowed, and that the examiner read an argument that stopped rather than finished. That is an organisation loss, not a writing-speed problem, and it is fixed by planning four paragraphs instead of six.

"Relevance?" — organisation: the paragraph has left the guiding question
Underlined phrases, "expression", "awkward" — language control
"Explain", or a question mark by a quotation — interpretation asserted rather than demonstrated

sections.heading: A six-week cycle, week by week
paragraphs: Six weeks is the shortest period over which a mark pattern becomes readable rather than noisy. A single response can be a bad day; three can be a run of unfamiliar extracts; six across varied material, written to time, show something real. The cycle below is what we run with most Dubai Literature students, and the sequence is deliberate rather than arbitrary — diagnosis first, then one criterion at a time, then an unsupported attempt at the end to see what has actually stuck.

The important structural point is that the student writes between sessions and the session is spent on the marked output. Families sometimes expect the opposite: an hour of teaching followed by homework. That order produces a pleasant hour and no evidence. Writing first means every session has a document in front of it, and every comment attaches to something the student did rather than to something they might do.

Week six is the one that matters to a family. It produces a written note: which criterion moved, by how much, which stayed flat, and what the next cycle targets. Sometimes the honest content of that note is that the organisation mark moved two bands and the language mark did not budge, which tells you the next six weeks should look nothing like the last six. Occasionally the note says nothing moved. That happens, it is said plainly, and it is the point at which a family should ask hard questions rather than renew out of habit.

sections.heading: Works in translation: the half of the course Dubai schools cover fastest
paragraphs: Literature requires works studied in translation, and in a stretched department those are the works covered in the least time. The reason is practical rather than negligent: a teacher running both English A courses prioritises the texts that most students will write about, and translated works are frequently read late, discussed once and never revisited. The student does not experience this as a gap. Nothing went wrong in class.

It shows up in two places and both are expensive. In Paper 2, a comparative essay is only as strong as its weaker half, so a student with a thoroughly known novel and a half-read translated work writes a lopsided comparison and loses marks on both the knowledge and analysis criteria. In the individual oral, one of the two extracts comes from a work in translation, and a student who cannot discuss the work's context or the fact of its being translated has thin material for ten minutes of presentation plus five of questions.

The repair is unglamorous: read the work properly, build comparative notes that connect it to at least two other studied texts, and rehearse the specific questions translation invites. What does it mean that this phrasing is a translator's choice? What in the work is culturally specific and what travels? Those are not trick questions and they are routinely asked. In Dubai there is a small advantage available here that few students use: in a city where most students speak at least two languages, the question of what survives translation is not abstract to them, and the ones who draw on that write noticeably better answers.

sections.heading: Grade movement that is realistic, and the arithmetic behind it
paragraphs: Nobody can promise a grade and we will not. What can be described honestly is the arithmetic: which criterion movements produce which band movements, and roughly how much work each tends to need. That is useful to a family deciding whether to spend, because the answer differs enormously depending on where the student currently sits and why.

The cheapest movement in this subject is usually organisation. A student whose readings are genuinely strong and whose essays wander is losing marks on a criterion that responds to structural discipline rather than to insight, and structural discipline can be taught in a handful of cycles. The most expensive is interpretation: a student who consistently asserts readings the text does not support needs to read more and read differently, which is months rather than weeks. Language control sits in between and depends heavily on the student's starting point.

The arithmetic also explains why some students should not buy tutoring at all. A student already scoring in the top band on three criteria and the second band on one has very little headroom, and the honest advice is a short targeted block rather than a year of sessions. We would rather say that and lose the booking than take a standing weekly hour from a family whose child needs four sessions. The flip side is also true: a student whose marks are uniformly low across all four criteria is not going to move much in six weeks, and pretending otherwise is how families end up disappointed in May.

sections.heading: The individual oral and the HL essay: what a family can check before the exam
paragraphs: Two components in this course are effectively invisible to parents until it is too late, and both can be checked. The individual oral is delivered live to the teacher and recorded, and it is marked out of forty across the four criteria, at 30% of the grade at Standard Level and 20% at Higher Level. The HL essay is submitted written work of 1,200 to 1,500 words on one studied work, worth 20% of the Higher Level grade.

For the oral, the checkable artefact before the exam is the student's own extract annotations and their ability to speak for ten minutes without reading. A student whose annotations have become a script will deliver something that sounds exactly like a script, and that costs marks on organisation and language. In a session we time a rehearsal, mark it, and tell the student plainly when the annotations have crossed from prompts into prose. That is an unwelcome message a week before the oral and a useful one a month before.

For the HL essay the checkable artefact is the draft trail. Every draft dated and kept shows a family what changed and when, and it shows the student's own development if any question about authorship is ever raised. The test we apply to the line of inquiry stays the same across both English A courses: if a well-read person could answer it in two sentences from a summary of the work, it is not a line of inquiry. Getting to one that is usually means discarding three or four, which feels like going backwards and is the most valuable part of the process.
bullets: Individual oral: 40 marks across the four criteria; 30% at SL and 20% at HL
HL essay: 1,200 to 1,500 words on one studied work, 20% of the HL grade

sections.heading: Honesty, drafts and the evidence trail
paragraphs: The evidence discipline on this page has a second function that is worth stating directly. A dated trail of drafts and marked responses is the clearest demonstration available that a student's submitted work is their own. In a subject assessed partly on written coursework, in a period when generated prose is trivially available, that trail protects the student in a way no assurance from a tutor can.

Our boundary is the same one we state on every page. A tutor teaches, explains criteria, questions a draft and gives feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor does not produce assessed work — not the HL essay, not an oral script, not a model Paper 2 answer for memorisation. Providers in this market sell completed coursework, one of them openly, and a student who submits bought work faces an IB malpractice finding that no refund covers. We also reference and link official IB subject documents rather than reproducing or supplying them, which is a copyright matter as well as an integrity one.

In practice this shapes what a session sounds like. A student who asks what to write gets a question back about what they think the passage is doing. Feedback names the criterion and the sentence; the rewriting is theirs, done between sessions, and the next draft is dated and kept. Where a draft's register shifts abruptly mid-paragraph we will ask about it. That is occasionally an awkward conversation and it is much better had with a tutor in February than with a coordinator in May.
bullets: A dated draft trail is the best available demonstration of authorship
Feedback names a criterion and a sentence; the rewriting belongs to the student
No essay, oral script or model answer is produced for a student at any price
Official IB documents are referenced and linked, never reproduced or supplied

sections.heading: Is a specialist worth it when the school already teaches Literature well?
paragraphs: Often not, and this is the question we would rather a family asked before paying than afterwards. Dubai's IB schools are inspected annually by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Plenty of Dubai Literature departments teach the subject very well, and buying a weekly hour that repeats the school's strongest activity is simply an expensive way to do the reading twice.

What a school rarely supplies in quantity is individually marked timed practice with criterion marks attached, because that is the most time-expensive thing a teacher can do and they are doing it for a cohort. If the gap in your child's provision is marked practice, outside support fills it precisely. If the gap is that your child has not read the books, no tutor fills that, and anyone who implies they can is selling exam technique as a substitute for the course.

On cost: published Dubai rates in October 2026 put qualified subject specialists online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, Unitors listing IB from AED 200 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table giving 200 to 450-plus. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 500 once travel is included. Those are other providers' figures, cited so you can check them rather than take ours on trust. The useful question is not the rate but how many marked responses the money buys, because that is the unit of progress in this subject.
bullets: KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band published scale
The gap a school rarely fills is individually marked timed practice
No tutor substitutes for reading the works; technique without reading caps at a low band
Judge the spend in marked responses bought, not in hours

process.title: Send the marked papers you already have
process.description: Not the report and not the predicted grade. The actual scripts with the teacher's annotations on them. Those annotations sort into four criteria, and sorting them is the first thing we do. It usually takes twenty minutes and it usually surprises the family.

process.title: We state which criterion is costing the grade
process.description: In writing, before any booking. If the answer is organisation, we will say the work is short and cheap. If it is interpretation, we will say it is months rather than weeks. If there is very little headroom, we will say that too and recommend a short block instead of a term.

process.title: A free trial run on a paper the school has already marked
process.description: The student brings a marked response and leaves able to explain which criterion each of their own paragraphs was serving and where the marks went. You get our reading of the mark pattern. No card is required and there is no obligation to continue.

process.title: Six weeks, one marked response a week
process.description: The student writes between sessions and the session works on the marked output. Each response carries a mark against each criterion and a date. The order of the six weeks is fixed: diagnose, target the lowest criterion, test it untimed, test it timed, transfer it to another component, then write cold.

process.title: A written cycle note at week six
process.description: Which criterion moved, by how much, which stayed flat, and what the next cycle targets. If nothing moved, the note says so. That document is the thing to read before renewing, and it exists so that nobody has to take a tutor's word for progress.

whyPoints.title: A mark on every response, not a comment
whyPoints.description: Every practice response comes back with a mark against each of the four criteria and a date. That is the only format in which week-to-week change is visible, and it is the format that distinguishes a student with an uneven profile from one who is uniformly low — two problems that look identical in a school report.

whyPoints.title: A written cycle note, including the flat cycles
whyPoints.description: At six weeks you get a note stating which criterion moved and which did not. Cycles that produced nothing are reported as such. A provider who only reports progress is not reporting.

whyPoints.title: No invented statistics
whyPoints.description: This page publishes no satisfaction percentage, no average improvement and no grade claim, because we cannot produce the underlying data. Competitors in this sector publish such figures without a sample size or a date; the right response to one is to ask for its n, its date and its method.

whyPoints.title: Works in translation treated as a real component
whyPoints.description: The translated works are where a stretched department runs short of time and where a Paper 2 comparison quietly loses half its strength. We treat that as a named repair job with its own block rather than as general reading.

whyPoints.title: Honest advice about not buying
whyPoints.description: Where a student has little headroom, or where the real gap is that the works have not been read, we say so. A short targeted block is often the right recommendation, and saying it costs us a booking and saves a family several thousand dirhams.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly, once
whyPoints.description: All UAE tutoring on this platform is one-to-one live online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not operate home visits in the UAE and holds no UAE office or centre. Knowing that up front saves a conversation.

faqs.question: My child is predicted a 5 in Literature and nobody can tell us why. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With the marked scripts rather than the prediction. A predicted grade is a single judgement with no component breakdown behind it, so it cannot tell you whether the problem is thin interpretation, loose structure, unargued analysis or language control. Those four need opposite responses. Sorting one marked Paper 1 response's annotations into the four criteria usually locates the loss in about twenty minutes, and it frequently lands somewhere the family did not expect — most often focus and organisation rather than insight.

faqs.question: What does my child's teacher mean by "develop your analysis"?
faqs.answer: Almost always the analysis and evaluation criterion, and specifically a missing step. The student has identified a feature of the text and stated an effect, without arguing how the feature produces the effect for a reader. "Relevance?" is a different criterion — organisation, meaning the paragraph has drifted from the guiding question. Underlined phrases and "expression" are the language criterion. A question mark beside a quotation means the reading has been asserted rather than shown. Sorting a page of annotations this way makes the shape of the problem visible.

faqs.question: How long before we can tell whether tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Six weeks, if one timed response is written and marked each week. One response can be a bad day and three can be a run of unfamiliar extracts; six across varied material show something real. What you should receive at week six is a written note saying which criterion moved, by how much, and which stayed flat. If a provider cannot produce that document, they do not have the evidence to support any claim about progress, including a positive one.

faqs.question: Which criterion is cheapest to improve in DP Literature?
faqs.answer: Focus and organisation, in most cases. A student whose readings are genuinely strong but whose essays wander is losing marks on a criterion that responds to planning discipline rather than to insight, and two or three cycles of work on paragraph openings and essay plans often moves it. The most expensive is knowledge, understanding and interpretation: a student asserting readings the text does not support needs wider and slower reading, which is months of work rather than a block of sessions.

faqs.question: Why do works in translation cause trouble if the class covered them?
faqs.answer: Because covering and studying are different, and translated works are what a stretched department covers fastest. The student experiences no problem — nothing went wrong in class. It surfaces in Paper 2, where a comparison is only as strong as its weaker half, so a thoroughly known novel paired with a half-read translated work produces a lopsided essay that loses marks on both halves. It surfaces again in the individual oral, where one extract comes from a translated work.

faqs.question: What should a student be able to say about a translated work?
faqs.answer: Three things, and they are routinely asked rather than hypothetical. What in the work is culturally specific and what travels across the translation. What it means that a particular phrasing is a translator's decision rather than the author's. And how the work connects to at least two other studied texts, since Paper 2 and the areas of exploration both reward connection. Dubai students usually speak more than one language themselves, and the ones who draw on that write noticeably stronger answers than those who treat translation as invisible.

faqs.question: How many works does my child actually have to study?
faqs.answer: A minimum of nine at Standard Level and thirteen at Higher Level, drawn across required ranges of literary form, period and region, with a required minimum studied in translation. The course is organised around three areas of exploration — readers, writers and texts; time and space; intertextuality — and seven central concepts run through them. Check the exact distribution requirements in the subject guide your school is teaching, since the IB revises guides between syllabus cycles and the split is not something to take from a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Can you predict the Literature grade my child will finish on?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. What can be described is the arithmetic behind band movement: which criterion gains are cheap, which are expensive, and how much headroom a particular mark profile leaves. A student already in the top band on three criteria and the second on one has very little room and needs a short targeted block, not a year of sessions. A student uniformly low across all four is not moving much in six weeks, and saying otherwise is how families end up disappointed in May.

faqs.question: Is there any point hiring a tutor if the school teaches Literature well?
faqs.answer: Often not, and we would rather you asked before paying. Many Dubai departments teach this subject very well, and buying a weekly hour that repeats the school's strongest activity is an expensive way to do the reading twice. What schools rarely supply in quantity is individually marked timed practice with criterion marks attached, because it is the most time-expensive thing a teacher can do for a cohort. If that is the gap, outside support fills it precisely. If the gap is unread books, no tutor fills it.

faqs.question: How do we check the individual oral before it happens?
faqs.answer: Time a rehearsal and mark it. The oral is marked out of forty across the four criteria, and the component is worth 30% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher Level. The checkable artefact beforehand is the student's own extract annotations plus their ability to speak for ten minutes without reading. Annotations that have become a script produce a delivery that sounds exactly like one, which costs organisation and language marks. That message is useful a month out and unwelcome a week out.

faqs.question: Should we keep my child's HL essay drafts?
faqs.answer: Yes, dated, every one. Two reasons. The trail shows a family what actually changed between drafts, which is the only way to judge whether supervision is doing anything. And it is the student's own record of their development if a question about authorship is ever raised — a real consideration in a period when generated prose is trivially available and language control is a quarter of the marks. A dated trail is better protection than any assurance a tutor can give.

faqs.question: What is the test for a good HL essay line of inquiry?
faqs.answer: State it, then ask whether a well-read person could answer it in two sentences from a summary of the work. If they could, it will produce an essay that describes rather than analyses, and no amount of good writing afterwards recovers the analysis marks. A usable line of inquiry is narrow enough to require evidence from specific passages and open enough that the answer is not obvious before the reading starts. Getting there usually means discarding three or four questions first.

faqs.question: Do you come to our villa in Dubai for Literature sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Dubai students work with us one to one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script on a shared screen. For this subject that is genuinely the stronger format: a response can be marked criterion by criterion while the student still remembers what they were attempting, and every mark and date is captured in the record rather than left on a loose piece of paper.

faqs.question: Why does my child run out of time on Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Usually because they planned six paragraphs. Paper 1 gives Standard Level candidates 75 minutes on one unseen extract and Higher Level candidates 135 minutes on two, and a response with an unfinished final third reads to an examiner as an argument that collapsed. Four well-developed paragraphs that finish score better than six that do not, because the organisation criterion rewards a complete shape. The fix is a planning habit rather than faster writing, and it shows up in the marks within two or three cycles.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both English A courses for siblings at different schools?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because the assessment architecture is shared — both courses have a Paper 1 guided analysis, a Paper 2 comparative essay, an individual oral on a global issue and an HL essay. What differs is the material: unseen literary extracts in Literature, unseen non-literary texts in Language and Literature. A tutor who drills only one of those is half-equipped. Where a single tutor can credibly cover both we will say so; where not, we would rather put two specialists on it.

faqs.question: What happens at the end of six weeks if nothing has changed?
faqs.answer: The cycle note says so, in writing, and we have the conversation about why. Sometimes the answer is that the targeted criterion was the expensive one and six weeks was never going to be enough, in which case the honest options are a longer plan or stopping. intro.heading: In Literature, the reading list is the syllabus
paragraphs: There is no content list in English A: Literature. There is a set of structural requirements and a prescribed reading list, and from those a school builds its own course. Two Dubai schools both running Higher Level Literature can share not a single text. That single fact explains most of what goes wrong when families buy tutoring for this subject: a tutor who arrives with their own favourite novels is not teaching your child's course, and six sessions on a text the school is not studying are six wasted sessions.

The requirements are worth knowing because they shape the year. Standard Level students study nine works; Higher Level students study thirteen. A minimum number must be works in translation, originally written in a language other than English, and a minimum number must be originally written in English, with a small allowance of freely chosen works beyond the prescribed list. The works between them have to span several literary forms, several periods and several regions, which is why a Literature course looks unbalanced from the inside and makes sense only when you see the grid it satisfies.

Then there is the allocation rule, which catches out more students than any other administrative detail in Group 1. A work used for one assessment component may not be used again for another. The individual oral needs two works. Paper 2 needs two. At Higher Level the HL essay needs one more. That is five works committed before anybody considers which the student actually knows well, and a student who discovers in February that their strongest novel is already spoken for has a real problem rather than a paperwork one.

What a tutor adds, in this subject specifically, is a second reader for texts the student may be meeting for the first time, and a method for the parts of the assessment nobody can revise for. Paper 1 is unseen. A student cannot prepare the passage; they can only prepare the procedure. That procedure is different for poetry than for prose, and most Dubai students arrive from an IGCSE where poetry was taught through a small anthology learned by heart, which is the opposite of what an unseen passage requires.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no accreditation from the IB, KHDA or any other authority, we have no centre in the UAE, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the country - home visits are a service we offer only in India. Dubai families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time by a named subject specialist, with a free trial lesson before any payment and a plan built from the school's own set works.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-literature-online-.programmesIntro: English A: Literature sits in Group 1 of the Diploma. In Dubai it is the less common of the two English A routes, offered mainly where a school has a strong literature tradition or a cohort that arrived from a literature-heavy British Year 11. The three notes below cover the routes in and what each needs in the first term.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Available at Standard and Higher Level. Both sit Paper 1, a guided analysis of previously unseen literary passages, and Paper 2, a comparative essay on studied works written without access to the texts, and both submit the individual oral. Higher Level adds the HL essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words and requires thirteen works rather than nine. The learner portfolio runs through the course and feeds the oral and the HL essay.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools offering Literature rather than Language and Literature tend to be those with large Group 1 cohorts able to run both, including several full-continuum IB schools in Al Barsha, Emirates Hills and Mirdif. Set works vary widely between them, so the first question in any session is which works your child's school has chosen and which are already allocated to a component.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language and Literature builds the analytical criteria the Diploma extends, and students who worked properly with a process journal recognise the learner portfolio. The jump into Literature is mainly one of reading volume: nine or thirteen works across two years is more sustained reading than most MYP courses require, and students who skim arrive at Paper 2 unable to recall anything precisely.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai school runs the full continuum, the same department usually teaches both phases, so reading habits formed in Year 9 travel straight into Year 12 unexamined. The practical first move for a Year 12 student is an honest audit of which set works have actually been read to the end, because Paper 2 is written from memory and a half-read novel is worth nothing in it.

programmes.name: IGCSE to Diploma handover
programmes.description: Most Dubai students entering Literature come from Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE English Literature, where a small number of texts are studied intensively and poetry is often learned from a set anthology. The Diploma reverses both: more works, less intensive coverage, and poetry that arrives unseen in an examination. Closing that gap is a term of work on procedure rather than on content.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools account for the largest share of Dubai private enrolment, so this is the commonest route in. Students arriving this way are typically strong on close reading of a familiar text and weak on an unfamiliar poem under time pressure, and a tutor's first job is usually to build a repeatable approach to an unseen passage.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-literature-online-.subjectsIntro: The list below is what is actually assessed in English A: Literature, with the neighbouring Group 1 and core courses Dubai students most often carry alongside it. Each entry names the format and the commonest reason marks go missing.

subjects.name: Paper 1: guided literary analysis
subjects.description: Two previously unseen passages from different literary forms, each with a guiding question. Standard Level students analyse one in 1 hour 15 minutes; Higher Level students analyse both in 2 hours 15 minutes. Worth 35% at both levels. Nothing about the passage can be revised, so the preparation is a procedure.

subjects.name: Paper 2: comparative essay
subjects.description: 1 hour 45 minutes, four general questions, two studied works compared, with no copy of either text in the room. Worth 35% at Standard Level and 25% at Higher. Recall of precise detail, rather than analytical ability, is the usual limiting factor.

subjects.name: Individual oral
subjects.description: Ten minutes of prepared analysis plus five minutes of teacher questions, examining a global issue across two works - one studied in translation and one originally written in English. Worth 30% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher. Both works are then unavailable for any other component.

subjects.name: HL essay
subjects.description: A 1,200 to 1,500 word essay on one work studied in the course, developed from the learner portfolio and worth 20% of the Higher Level grade. The work used here cannot be used elsewhere, which makes the choice a strategic decision as much as a literary one.

subjects.name: Works in translation
subjects.description: A compulsory part of the course - three works minimum at Standard Level, four at Higher. Students frequently treat the translation as transparent and analyse diction as though the author chose those English words, which is a distinctive and avoidable way of losing credit on criterion B.

subjects.name: Unseen poetry
subjects.description: One of the two Paper 1 passages is commonly a poem. For most Dubai students this is the single weakest area, because IGCSE poetry is usually taught from a studied anthology and the skills of reading an unfamiliar poem under time pressure are different ones.

subjects.name: The learner portfolio
subjects.description: Compulsory and not directly assessed, which is why it gets neglected. It is the source for both the oral's global issue and the HL essay's line of inquiry, so a thin portfolio in Year 12 turns into a search for a topic in Year 13.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The other Group 1 option, which replaces several literary works with non-literary bodies of work such as advertising, speeches and journalism, and whose Paper 1 is a non-literary text. Knowing the difference explains why the two courses cannot share a tutoring plan.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Competes with the HL essay for the same drafting weeks in Year 13 and rewards the same habit of arguing from evidence. Students comfortable with Literature's criterion B usually find the TOK exhibition manageable.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in English
subjects.description: A 4,000-word essay supervised by a school teacher. A tutor may discuss a research question, suggest reading, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts; the essay remains the student's work and the school supervisor stays the examining relationship.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB DP English A Literature online tutor in Dubai usually means
paragraphs: Three situations bring Dubai families to this search, and they need different first sessions. The commonest is a Paper 1 score that will not move. The student writes thoughtfully about the studied novels and then produces a thin response to an unseen poem, and everybody has concluded that they are simply not a poetry person. They are usually a person without a procedure, which is a different and much more fixable condition.

The second is reading debt. A student has nine or thirteen works to know well and has genuinely finished six of them. Nobody admits this to the school, the gap is invisible until a Paper 2 mock, and then an essay written from memory exposes it completely, because there is no text in the room to lean on. The honest first move is an audit of what has actually been read to the end, and a decision about which works to rescue and which to concede.

The third is allocation. The student has reached the middle of Year 13 and discovered that the work they know best is already committed to the individual oral and therefore unavailable for Paper 2 or the HL essay. This is an avoidable problem and almost nobody is warned about it in advance. A session with a sheet of paper and the list of thirteen works can usually sort it out, provided there is still time to choose differently.

All three are diagnosable from documents rather than from a conversation. Send the school's set work list, the most recent marked Paper 1, and an honest note of which works have been finished. That is enough to say what the first six weeks should contain and, as importantly, what they should not.

sections.heading: How a Literature course is built: nine works, thirteen works and the grid behind them
paragraphs: A school choosing a Literature course is satisfying a grid rather than picking favourites. The works must include a minimum number in translation and a minimum number originally written in English, with a limited allowance for freely chosen works outside the prescribed reading list. Between them they must cover several literary forms, several periods and several regions. That is why a Dubai Literature course can look eccentric - a Greek tragedy, a Japanese novel in translation, a contemporary American play - when it is in fact a careful solution to a set of constraints.

Knowing the grid helps a parent in two practical ways. It explains why the course cannot simply drop a work the student dislikes: removing it may break a form, period or region requirement. And it gives a sensible basis for the reading plan, because works differ enormously in the time they demand. A poetry collection and a nineteenth-century novel both count as one work and are not remotely the same amount of evening reading.

The table below sets out the structural requirements as they currently stand. Treat it as the shape of the course and confirm the detail with your child's IB coordinator, since the IB revises its subject guides on a cycle and the prescribed reading list itself is updated. We publish no IB examination or results dates anywhere on this page, because the IB's own site does not serve its calendar to automated checks and a second-hand date in a planning table is worse than no date at all.

One further practical note for Dubai specifically. Availability of set works matters more here than it does in a European city. Some translated works are hard to obtain locally in the edition the school is teaching, and page references matter for close reading. Sorting out editions in the first fortnight of Year 12 avoids a term of a student quoting from a different translation than the rest of the class.

sections.heading: Works in translation, and the mistake almost every student makes once
paragraphs: A minimum of three works at Standard Level and four at Higher must be works in translation, originally written in a language other than English. Students generally enjoy these texts. What they do very often, and what costs them credit, is to write about the English words as though the author chose them: commenting on the sibilance of a line in a Russian novel, or on a translator's idiom as evidence of the author's voice.

The correction is not to avoid language-level analysis but to relocate it. Structure, narrative method, imagery at the level of what is depicted, characterisation, the handling of time, and the cultural and historical situation of the work all survive translation and are entirely available for analysis. Sound patterning, puns, register in the original language and fine lexical choice do not survive, and a student writing confidently about them is writing about the translator.

This is also where a Dubai cohort has a genuine advantage that goes unused. Many students in the emirate read another language at a high level - Arabic, Hindi, Urdu, Russian, French, Malayalam - and some of them are reading a work translated from a language they actually know. A student who can say what the translation has had to flatten is doing precisely the kind of comparative cultural work the criteria reward, and it is the sort of insight no tutor can supply for them.

For the individual oral, one of the two works must be studied in translation and the other must have been originally written in English, which makes the translation question unavoidable rather than optional. Practising it early - a short written exercise on what can and cannot be claimed about a translated passage - removes the problem permanently in about two sessions.

sections.heading: Paper 1: two passages, two different kinds of failure
paragraphs: Paper 1 presents two previously unseen passages from different literary forms, each with a guiding question. Standard Level students write on one of them in seventy-five minutes. Higher Level students write on both in two hours and fifteen minutes, which is less time per passage than the SL allowance once planning is counted. Weighting is 35% at both levels, which makes this the largest single component and the only one that cannot be prepared by reading.

Prose and poetry fail differently, which is why practising them together hides the problem. On prose, the commonest failure is paraphrase: the student retells the passage with evaluative adjectives attached and never isolates a technique long enough to argue its effect. The fix is mechanical - choose three narrow claims about method before writing a word - and it usually lands within three or four marked attempts.

On poetry the failure is earlier. Students who met poetry through a studied anthology have learned to recall an interpretation rather than build one, and an unfamiliar poem offers nothing to recall. They freeze, or they write about theme at a level that could apply to any poem on the subject. The route in is form and voice: who is speaking, to whom, in what shape, and where the poem changes direction. A poem that turns in its sixth line has handed the student their argument.

The guiding question is the third thing students waste. It is there to point at a productive line of analysis, and a surprising number of scripts ignore it to write the essay the student would rather write. Reading the question twice and planning against it is worth more than any amount of literary vocabulary, and it is the single fastest correction available on this component.

sections.heading: The allocation puzzle: no work may be used twice
paragraphs: This is the section competitors do not write and the one that saves Dubai families the most trouble. A work used in one assessment component cannot be used in another. The individual oral uses two works, one in translation and one originally written in English. Paper 2 compares two works. At Higher Level the HL essay uses one more. That is five of the thirteen works spoken for, and the decisions interlock.

The sensible order of decision is the reverse of the order students usually take. Start with the HL essay, because it needs a work rich enough to support a narrow line of inquiry over 1,500 words and that is the scarcest requirement. Then fix the oral, where the translation constraint applies and where a global issue must be visible in both chosen works. Whatever remains strong goes to Paper 2, which needs two works that pair productively across many possible general questions rather than two the student happens to like.

Students get into difficulty by letting the oral be decided for them. It comes first in the calendar in most Dubai schools, the teacher suggests a sensible pairing, and the student agrees without checking what it costs later. Six months on, the two works they know best are unavailable for Paper 2, and the comparison has to be built from works they covered in a hurry in Year 12.

The fix is a single sheet of paper in the autumn of Year 12 listing every work, its form, its period, whether it is in translation, and how well the student actually knows it. The allocation falls out of that table in twenty minutes. It is the least literary thing a Literature tutor does and one of the most useful.

sections.heading: Where Literature marks are lost, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Every component in this course is marked against four criteria: knowledge, understanding and interpretation; analysis and evaluation; focus and organisation; and language. The mark allocations differ between components, so confirm them against the guide your child's school is teaching, but the criteria themselves are constant, which makes them a reliable diagnostic grid across all four assessments.

In practice the four produce four distinct student profiles, and knowing which one you are dealing with determines the term's work. The reader who understands deeply but cannot build an argument loses on organisation and gains fastest, usually within weeks. The reader who identifies technique accurately but never evaluates loses on analysis and takes a term, because it is a habit of mind rather than a gap in knowledge. These are not interchangeable problems and general advice helps neither.

The table below maps the symptom onto the criterion and the correction. It is deliberately narrow, because the most common feedback in a mock script's margin - be more analytical, develop your points, use more evidence - is unactionable. A student can act on an instruction to replace each evaluative adjective with a clause explaining the effect on a reader. They cannot act on an instruction to be more perceptive.

We do not publish outcome statistics anywhere on these pages, because we cannot produce the data behind them, and no tutor can promise a grade on a course where a third of the marks come from an unseen paper. What we can offer is a per-criterion record across marked work, so the pattern is visible to you rather than inferred.

sections.heading: Online delivery, in-home tutoring and what Dubai actually charges
paragraphs: Families in Dubai often begin by looking for a tutor who will come to the house, so it is worth setting out both the market reality and what we sell. IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and no line on this site should be read as an offer of one in Dubai.

For Literature the format turns out to matter less than the match. What the student needs is somebody who has read the works their school has chosen, or will read them, and who can mark an unseen passage against the criteria. That person is rarely the nearest person. Restricting the search to tutors who can drive to Arabian Ranches by five o'clock means selecting on geography for a subject where the set works differ school by school, which is the worst available basis for the decision.

The practical mechanics also favour a shared screen. An unseen passage is annotated live, the tutor's marks sit next to the student's, and both are saved. A recorded oral rehearsal can be reviewed together immediately. The reading itself happens alone either way, which is where most of the hours in this course actually go.

They are not an IB Gram price list and we do not publish one on these pages, because the rate for a specialist depends on level, component and availability; the route in is a free trial lesson and a consultation. sections.heading: Academic honesty, tutor permits and the Dubai school week
paragraphs: The individual oral, the HL essay and the Extended Essay must be the student's own work, and on a course this discursive the boundary needs stating rather than assuming. A tutor teaches the component, explains what a criterion asks for, discusses a text, questions a line of inquiry until the student sharpens it, and gives written feedback on drafts the student has produced. Nobody supplies prose, nobody rewrites a paragraph into their own voice, and nobody hands over a thesis to be adopted. An academic-honesty finding falls on the student, not on the tutor.

We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson documents. Subject guides, prescribed reading lists, past material and mark schemes belong to the boards; a tutor cites the official page and the school or family obtains the document properly. Any service advertising a downloadable bank of IB material for a Group 1 subject is a risk to your child rather than a convenience.

On permits the UAE position is specific. Private tutoring requires a work permit issued through MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without the permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so nobody should quote you an amount.

Two Dubai-specific constraints shape the week a reading plan has to fit into. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed by KHDA to teach, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Those lessons take real timetable space. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is why asking your child's own English teacher for paid sessions is the wrong route.

process.title: Send the set work list
process.description: The school's list of works for your child's level, plus the most recent marked Paper 1 and an honest note of which works have actually been finished. Those three things let a tutor plan a real course rather than a generic one, and they usually reveal the problem within half an hour.

process.title: See two named Literature tutors
process.description: You get names, the forms and periods each is strongest on, and Gulf Standard Time availability. If your child's works include something unusual, we say which tutor already knows it and which would be reading it alongside your child rather than pretending otherwise.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A working session on an unseen passage or a marked script, ending with a named diagnosis: which criterion is capping the grade, which works are at risk, and whether the allocation needs changing. You see that finding before deciding to continue.

process.title: Split the plan in two
process.description: We separate the unseen-paper procedure work from the set-works and recall work, and agree how many sessions each gets. Mixing them means the unseen work is always the thing that gets dropped when a set text deadline arrives.

process.title: Review at week eight
process.description: Per-criterion scores on four or five marked pieces, the recall bank tested, and the allocation sheet checked. We go through it with you and decide whether to continue, change the balance, change tutor, or stop.

whyPoints.title: Planned from your child's actual works
whyPoints.description: A Literature course is whatever nine or thirteen works the school chose, and two Dubai schools may share none of them. We plan from the school's list rather than from a standard reading list, because sessions on a text your child is not studying are sessions spent on somebody else's course.

whyPoints.title: Poetry and prose trained separately
whyPoints.description: The two Paper 1 forms fail for different reasons: prose drifts into paraphrase, poetry freezes for want of an interpretation to recall. Practising them in alternating weeks means both get fixed. Mixing them in one session usually means the weaker one is quietly skipped.

whyPoints.title: The allocation handled before it becomes a problem
whyPoints.description: No work may serve two components, so five works are committed at Higher Level before anybody considers preference. We put the whole list on one sheet in Year 12 and decide the order deliberately, which prevents the February discovery that the best novel is already spoken for.

whyPoints.title: Translated works treated as translations
whyPoints.description: Three works at Standard Level and four at Higher must be in translation, and students lose credit by analysing the translator's diction as the author's choice. Two short exercises fix this permanently, and a student who reads the original language can turn it into a genuine analytical advantage.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery and availability
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. If no Literature specialist is free in your window, or if nobody has read your child's unusual set work, we say so rather than booking the slot and leaving you to discover it.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source, claims without invention
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a market rate attributed to the provider that published it in October 2026. We publish no outcome statistics, no self-reported ratings and no grade promises, because a third of this course is an unseen paper and nobody can honestly promise a result on it.

faqs.question: How many works does IB English A Literature require at each level?
faqs.answer: Nine at Standard Level and thirteen at Higher Level, chosen by the school from the prescribed reading list with a limited allowance for freely chosen works. The totals matter less than their composition: a minimum number must be works in translation, a minimum number must have been originally written in English, and between them the works must cover several literary forms, periods and regions. That coverage grid is why a course cannot simply drop a work a student dislikes, and why two Dubai schools running the same level may share no texts at all.

faqs.question: How many works in translation does my child have to read?
faqs.answer: At least three at Standard Level and four at Higher Level, originally written in a language other than English. They are a compulsory part of the course rather than enrichment, and one of the two works used in the individual oral must be a translated one. The practical warning is about analysis: students routinely write about sound patterning or fine word choice in a translated text as though the author had selected the English words. Structure, imagery, narrative method and context are fair game; the translator's diction is not.

faqs.question: Is Paper 1 in English A Literature a poem or a prose extract?
faqs.answer: Both appear. The paper presents two previously unseen passages from different literary forms, each with a guiding question. Standard Level students choose one and write for seventy-five minutes; Higher Level students analyse both in two hours and fifteen minutes. It is worth 35% at either level, which makes it the largest single component and the only one that cannot be revised for. We practise poetry and prose in alternating weeks, because a student who freezes on an unfamiliar poem has a different problem from one who paraphrases prose.

faqs.question: Can my child use the same novel for Paper 2 and the HL essay?
faqs.answer: No. A work used for one assessment component cannot be used for another. The individual oral takes two works, Paper 2 takes two more, and at Higher Level the HL essay takes a fifth, so five of the thirteen are committed. The sensible order is to choose the HL essay work first, since it must sustain a narrow line of inquiry over 1,500 words, then the oral pairing with its translation constraint, then Paper 2 from what remains strongest. Deciding this in Year 12 avoids a difficult discovery in Year 13.

faqs.question: Why does my child do well on the studied novels but badly on unseen poetry?
faqs.answer: Because the two require different skills and most Dubai students learned poetry from a studied anthology, where the task is to recall and apply an interpretation. An unfamiliar poem offers nothing to recall, so the student either freezes or writes about theme in terms that would fit any poem on the subject. The route in is form and voice: who speaks, to whom, in what shape, and where the poem changes direction. A poem that turns in its sixth line has handed the student an argument. Three or four marked attempts usually produce visible movement.

faqs.question: Which two works should the individual oral use?
faqs.answer: One must have been studied in translation and the other originally written in English, and a single global issue has to be genuinely visible in both. Beyond that the choice is strategic, because both works become unavailable for every other component. Pick works the student knows well but which are not the only candidates for Paper 2 or the HL essay. The commonest mistake is accepting the first sensible pairing a teacher suggests, since the oral comes early in most Dubai schools' calendars and the cost only appears six months later.

faqs.question: Is English A Literature harder than Language and Literature?
faqs.answer: It is different rather than harder. Literature demands more sustained reading - nine or thirteen works against four or six - and its Paper 1 is an unseen literary passage. Language and Literature replaces several works with non-literary bodies of work such as advertising, speeches and journalism, and its Paper 1 is an unseen non-literary text, which brings its own difficulty for students who have never been taught text-type conventions. Dubai schools normally place students rather than letting them choose, so the useful question is what the chosen course demands, not which is easier.

faqs.question: What does the prescribed reading list actually constrain?
faqs.answer: It is the pool from which most of the course must be drawn, and it carries the form, period and region labels the school uses to satisfy the coverage requirements. A limited number of works may be freely chosen from outside it. For a parent the practical consequences are two: the school's apparently eccentric text choices are usually a solution to the grid rather than a preference, and works cannot be swapped casually mid-course because removing one may break a requirement that the rest of the list depends on.

faqs.question: How much does an online IB English Literature tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates in October 2026 run roughly AED 45-150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 for in-home visits including travel, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB specialist, with one premium provider publishing AED 650. Those figures belong to the providers who publish them and are quoted here with that attribution; they are not an IB Gram price list. We begin with a free trial lesson and a consultation, because the rate depends on level, component and who is actually available.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange tutors who visit homes in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Dubai families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the trade is clearly worth it: what a Literature student needs is somebody who has read the specific works their school chose and can mark an unseen passage against the criteria, and that person is very rarely the one who happens to live twenty minutes away.

faqs.question: My child has not properly finished several of the set works. What now?
faqs.answer: Audit honestly first, then triage. List every work and mark it finished, half-read or untouched, then decide which to rescue and which to concede. The works allocated to the oral, Paper 2 and the HL essay must be rescued, because Paper 2 is written without the text in the room and a half-read novel is worth nothing there. Works needed only for coverage can be read in summary with a few precise moments learned. Pretending the gap does not exist until a mock exposes it is the one approach that reliably fails.

faqs.question: How many sessions does unseen passage work usually take?
faqs.answer: On prose, three or four marked attempts commonly produce visible movement, because the correction is procedural: three narrow claims about method chosen before writing. On poetry it is usually six to eight, since the student is building an approach rather than adjusting one. Criterion D language problems are the exception and take considerably longer - a year rather than a term - and we say so rather than implying otherwise. Nobody can promise a grade on a component where the passage itself is unknown until the examination room.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Extended Essay in English Literature?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits. A tutor can discuss whether a research question is narrow enough to sustain 4,000 words, suggest critical reading, explain what the assessment criteria ask for, and give written feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor does not supply prose, does not rewrite sections, and does not provide the argument. The school supervisor remains the examining relationship and should see the drafts too. Any service offering to produce a finished Extended Essay is creating a malpractice risk that falls entirely on your child.

faqs.question: How do Dubai school holidays and Ramadan affect a Literature reading plan?
faqs.answer: They are the two best opportunities and the two commonest excuses. Long works are far easier to finish in a holiday block than in a Year 13 term, so a reading plan should deliberately place the longest translated work in a break rather than in a term week. During Ramadan the household day shifts and many families prefer post-Iftar sessions, which is simple to arrange when nobody is travelling. Internal deadlines do not move for either, which is the argument for front-loading reading into Year 12.

faqs.question: What if the school's set works are unusual and no tutor knows them?
faqs.answer: We tell you that directly rather than bluffing. For an unfamiliar work a good tutor reads it alongside your child and says so, which is genuinely useful because the student is also meeting it for the first time and the modelling of a first reading is instructive. What does not work is a tutor implying familiarity and teaching a general version of the text. If the works are unusual enough that nobody suitable is available, we say what the realistic alternative is instead of filling the slot.

From those a tutor can tell you which criterion is capping the grade, whether the works are allocated sensibly across the components, and what the first six weeks should contain. The trial lesson is free, the tutor is named before you book, and lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: In Literature, the reading list is the budget
paragraphs: English A Literature is built on works, and the number is not small. Standard Level students study nine, Higher Level thirteen, drawn across literary forms, periods and places, with a required share of works read in translation. Every assessed component draws on that body of reading: the unseen passages in Paper 1, the comparative essay in Paper 2, the individual oral built on two works, and at Higher Level a further essay on one of them. Nothing in the course can be faked around a gap in the reading, which is why the first question about cost is not what a tutor charges but how much of the list is genuinely finished.

That changes the arithmetic from the usual tutoring conversation. A student who has read everything and is losing marks on analysis needs scored essays, and in Dubai that is a specialist purchase in the published range of roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour. A student who has skimmed four of the works needs three weeks with the books and a reading plan, which costs almost nothing, followed by a much shorter paid block. Families routinely buy the first when they needed the second, and the money disappears into sessions discussing books the student has not read.

The expensive error in the other direction is paying for summaries. Providers will happily supply a condensed version of a novel at a specialist hourly rate, and it feels like progress because the student can then say something about the text. The marks do not follow. Paper 2 rewards a comparison argued from detail, the individual oral rewards extracts the student can handle closely, and the Higher Level essay rewards a narrow line of inquiry into one work. All three are visibly thin when the underlying reading was secondhand, and examiners read a great many thin essays.

So this page costs the subject from the reading list outward. It sets out what each state of the list costs to fix and what the honest alternative is; it prices the Dubai market by what the hour contains rather than by the name of the provider; it names the month of the school year when specialists are actually available; and it says which purchases in this course return nothing. Where the answer is to buy books and time instead of hours, that is written down, because nobody paid by the hour has any incentive to tell you.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own writing shared on screen. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. In this subject the online pool matters more than usual, because set works vary school to school and a family often needs somebody who has taught a specific translated text rather than somebody who lives within a twenty-minute drive of their villa.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-literature-tutor.programmesIntro: Families budget across more than the two Diploma years, and a student's starting position in Literature is largely set before DP1 begins. Each programme below leaves a different gap, and the gaps cost different amounts to close.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: English A Literature runs at Higher and Standard Level across both years, assessed through unseen passage analysis, a comparative essay, an individual oral on two works and, at Higher Level, an essay on a single studied work. Works cannot be reused across components, which constrains the whole plan. The practical consequence for a budget is that a weak work is not just a weak work; it removes an option from the allocation puzzle.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools choose their own set works within the IB framework, so two students in neighbouring schools can share nothing on their reading lists. Ask a prospective tutor which of your child's works they have actually taught before agreeing a rate, because that single answer changes the value of the hour more than the number attached to it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language and Literature builds analysis of extracts and introduces comparison, and students arrive in DP1 used to being taught texts closely in class. The gap it leaves is reading stamina: MYP rarely requires a student to finish thirteen substantial works in two years. Families from continuum schools should budget for a reading plan in the first term rather than teaching hours.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a large concentration of IB continuum schools, and the DP1 Literature cohort here is often half continuum students and half arrivals from British curriculum Year 11. The two halves need different purchases in the first term, and a provider selling both the same weekly hour is selling convenience rather than value.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE English Literature
programmes.description: IGCSE Literature covers three or four texts taught intensively, with extracts often available in the examination. Diploma Literature covers three times as many works with nothing in the room. Students make the transition on reading volume rather than on analytical ability, and the first term of DP1 is where that shows. Teaching hours help here; summaries do not.
programmes.countryNote: With UK curriculum at 37 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, this is the commonest route into Diploma Literature in the emirate. A student who read three texts in Year 11 and is now facing thirteen needs a reading schedule more urgently than an essay tutor, and the schedule can be built in a single hour.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: A Literature student registering an Extended Essay in English adds a fourth substantial text and 4,000 words of their own writing to the same two years. Theory of Knowledge draws on the same analytical habits. Both compete for the Literature budget, and one Group 1 specialist covering the essay craft across all three is the clearest package saving in the Diploma core.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai schools the internal deadlines for the core and the individual oral window frequently land in the same half-term, which produces the February spending spike families report. Mapping the clash in the first term turns an emergency block at compressed rates into a planned one.

dubai/ib-dp-english-a-literature-tutor.subjectsIntro: What a package costs depends on which subjects are covered together, and some combinations genuinely share an hour while others do not. subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: Nine or thirteen works, two unseen passages in Paper 1, a comparative essay, an oral on two works and a Higher Level essay. The budget is driven by reading completeness first and by marked essay practice second; summaries of unread works are the one purchase that reliably returns nothing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The sibling Group 1 course, with non-literary texts and a smaller literary load. Costs behave differently: marking timed unseen responses dominates the budget rather than reading volume, so a family switching course mid-DP1 should expect the spending pattern to change shape.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK essay rewards a controlled claim with acknowledged limits, which is the same discipline as a Paper 2 comparison. A Literature specialist can usually cover both inside one booked hour, and families funding them separately are often paying twice for the same teaching.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay in English
subjects.description: A 4,000-word research essay on a literary question, supervised by the school. Paid hours earn most at the research question stage and on one read of a near-final draft; the middle of the project is reading and writing the student must do themselves.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Shares source evaluation and essay architecture with Literature, and often shares a term's deadlines. Students losing marks for narrating rather than arguing will be doing it in both subjects, so one marking-led arrangement can cover the habit and a second tutor becomes avoidable.

subjects.name: Philosophy
subjects.description: Close reading of a prescribed text and tightly argued prose. A frequent pairing with Literature in Dubai IB schools, and one where the same tutor can realistically work across both, which is unusual and worth checking before funding two arrangements.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Heavy on precise written explanation under time pressure. Literature students who write expansively tend to lose marks here for the same reason, and the correction transfers, so sequence the subjects rather than buying parallel weekly hours in both.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Essay-based with a heavy reading load, which competes directly with the Literature reading plan for the same evenings. Budgeting for both means scheduling reading blocks rather than adding sessions; two tutors cannot create reading time that the week does not contain.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Included for budgeting honesty: there is no shared hour here. Maths is a separate specialist and a separate line, generally at the upper end of the published Dubai bands during an examination year, and families should plan it as an addition rather than a substitution.

sections.heading: What an IB DP English A Literature tutor in Dubai costs depends on the state of the reading list
paragraphs: Price any Literature support by asking one question first: how many of the set works has the student actually finished, closely enough to quote from? The answer sorts families into four situations with very different costs, and the table below prices each one. Three of the four are cheaper than the weekly-sessions arrangement most providers will propose, and one of them costs nothing at all.

This is the opposite of how the market sells. A provider quoting a rate per hour has no mechanism for telling a family that their problem is four unread novels and three weeks of evenings. The hourly conversation flattens every situation into the same product, and the student who most needs to be sent away to read is the one who will sit through the most sessions, because unread works generate an inexhaustible supply of things to discuss.

The AED figures in the table are arithmetic on published market bands rather than our quotation. The bands themselves come from providers' own pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026: budget online platforms from roughly AED 45 to AED 150, qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to AED 300, IB specialists AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, in-home visits AED 180 to AED 500, and premium named tutoring to AED 650.

The final row matters most in Dubai specifically, because set works differ between schools. A family whose child is studying an unusual translated work may find that no local tutor has taught it and that the useful specialist is somewhere else in the world. That is an availability problem rather than a pricing one, and it is the clearest practical argument for online delivery in this subject.
