dubai/ib-dp-environmental-systems-and-so.programmesIntro: ESS sits in the Diploma, but the skills it assesses are built earlier and used again in the Diploma core. These are the three levels a Dubai family is normally dealing with when they contact us about this subject.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences and Individuals and Societies
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme is where a student either learns to design an investigation or learns to follow one. Its science criteria reward the formulation of a testable question, controlled variables and evaluation of method, which is exactly the skill set the ESS investigation assumes. A student who has only ever completed teacher-designed practicals arrives in the Diploma able to run a procedure and unable to invent one, and that gap is the single commonest reason an ESS investigation stalls in Dubai.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai runs both routes to the Diploma: Middle Years to Year 11 in IB schools, and IGCSE in the larger British-curriculum sector. IGCSE students usually arrive with better examination technique and less experience of open-ended investigation design, because coursework has largely gone from those syllabuses. We check which of the two gaps a student has before billing any hours for either.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Environmental Systems and Societies
programmes.description: ESS is an interdisciplinary Diploma course that can satisfy either the sciences or the individuals and societies requirement, assessed through written papers and one individual investigation. Its distinctive demands are systems thinking, the explicit use of environmental value systems, and the handling of real data. Confirm the current component structure, availability at each level, and weightings with your school's IB coordinator before planning hours against them, because the subject guide is revised on its own cycle.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, ESS is often taught by a geographer or by a biologist, and which one it is changes what tutoring has to supply. A geographer-taught class tends to be strong on value systems and weak on the quantitative treatment of data. A biologist-taught class is usually the reverse. Ask your child's teacher which background they come from, because it predicts the gap more reliably than a predicted grade does.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and the Group 4 project
programmes.description: An Extended Essay in ESS is attractive to Dubai students because local environmental questions are genuinely under-researched, and it fails for the same reason the investigation fails: a question that cannot be answered with data the student can actually get. The Group 4 project adds a collaborative element assessed on participation rather than on output, and it is frequently the first time an ESS student works alongside the physicists and chemists.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai offers real research seams for an ESS Extended Essay: coastal change, urban heat, water reuse, desalination brine, waste streams, air quality and mangrove ecology. Access and permission are the constraint rather than the ideas. We spend the first supervision session testing whether the data exists and is obtainable by a school student, before any reading is done.

dubai/ib-dp-environmental-systems-and-so.subjectsIntro: ESS students in Dubai rarely take it in isolation. These are the related Diploma courses our tutors cover for the same families, with what each one actually demands.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.levels: Both levels, confirm availability with your school
subjects.description: Assessed through written papers and an individual investigation. Marks turn on systems thinking, explicit use of environmental value systems, and defensible treatment of data. The commonest losses are a case study described rather than applied, and a dataset analysed without a justified statistical test.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The science most often taken alongside or instead of ESS. Heavier recall load, a formal practical scheme and an internal assessment with tighter experimental expectations. Students who move from Biology to ESS usually gain on breadth and lose on the discipline of controlling a variable.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Shares ESS's fieldwork logic and diverges on content. Geography marks the handling of place, scale and process; ESS marks the handling of systems and values. One tutor can sensibly cover both for the same student, and the fieldwork planning transfers almost completely.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Relevant to ESS students working on water quality, soil, atmospheric pollutants or desalination. Useful for understanding what a measurement actually measures, which is where ESS investigations on chemical parameters most often go wrong before any statistics are applied.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics course that overlaps most usefully with ESS. Correlation, significance testing and sampling are taught here in a way the ESS guide assumes but does not teach. Students taking both have a measurable advantage on the investigation and often need fewer ESS hours overall.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Another Group 4 route Dubai students weigh against ESS. It demands human physiology recall and an investigation using human participants, with its own ethics requirements. The two subjects are chosen by similar students for different reasons and are worth comparing on assessment style rather than on reputation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Pairs well with ESS for students interested in resource use, externalities and policy. The diagrammatic discipline of Economics tends to sharpen ESS answers on resource management, and the vocabulary of market failure is directly usable in pollution-management questions.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Covers the governance half of environmental problems: treaties, sovereignty over resources, and why agreed policies are not implemented. ESS students who take it write noticeably better answers on international environmental agreements, because they can explain the failure mechanism rather than name it.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Overlaps with ESS on sustainability, life-cycle thinking and material choice. Useful for an ESS student whose investigation involves a built intervention, and for a design student whose project needs environmental justification that goes beyond asserting a material is green.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research. In ESS the risk is a question that sounds important and cannot be answered with obtainable data. Supervision through us is questioning and written feedback on the student's own drafts; the school's registered supervisor signs the work off.

dubai/ib-dp-environmental-systems-and-so.regionsIntro: Lessons are online, so where a family lives does not change who can teach them. It does change which sites are reachable for primary data, which school the child attends, and when a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Beachfront within walking distance for many households, which makes coastal transects, litter surveys and shoreline profiling genuinely feasible rather than theoretical. Check current municipal rules on any sampling before a student collects anything, and plan collection for early morning in the warmer months.

regions.name: Ras Al Khor and Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Close to the emirate's best-known mangrove and wetland habitat, where access is restricted and controlled. Observation from designated hides is possible; sampling is not, without permission. We plan investigations here around secondary data plus permitted observation rather than around collection students cannot lawfully do.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills
regions.note: A dense cluster of IB and British schools with large irrigated green spaces inside walking distance. Soil moisture, irrigation water use, microclimate and urban heat comparisons between shaded and unshaded ground are all workable here and are rarely attempted by candidates.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lake Towers
regions.note: High-rise living, so the workable investigations are vertical rather than horizontal: temperature and wind at different floors, balcony microclimate, building shading, waste streams at a single tower. Apartment families often assume ESS fieldwork is closed to them, and it is not.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Villa communities with landscaped planting and heavy irrigation, which makes water use and plant survival a measurable local question. Long school runs mean sessions here usually settle on weekend mornings or after 19:00, so investigation planning tends to happen in fewer, longer blocks.

regions.name: Al Qudra, Seih Al Salam and the desert fringe
regions.note: The nearest accessible desert and lake environments, used by Dubai schools for group fieldwork. Access varies by season and by conservation designation, and several areas are protected. Confirm the current position before planning a visit, and treat the drive time as part of the method.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Large school catchment with the Creek on its edge. Water quality, salinity gradients and bird counts along the Creek are realistic, and the area's mix of curricula means an ESS student here is often the only one in their year taking the subject.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: University campuses nearby, which matters for students wanting to ask whether ESS is accepted for environmental science and engineering routes locally. It is also one of the easier areas in which to arrange a supervised visit to an institutional laboratory through a school.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB World Schools that run ESS at Diploma level
schoolClusters.note: ESS provision in Dubai follows staffing rather than demand, and the subject tends to appear where a school has either a geographer or a biologist willing to take it on. KHDA inspects these schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Ask the coordinator who teaches ESS and what their subject background is.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools with sustainability provision ESS students draw on
schoolClusters.note: A number of Dubai schools have invested in on-site environmental infrastructure, from aquaponics and biodomes to monitored irrigation and waste-separation programmes. Where that exists, an ESS investigation can use the school's own site as a system with real data, which is usually a better study than an inaccessible natural one.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

dubai/ib-dp-environmental-systems-and-so.modesIntro: ESS support is worth buying in defined blocks, because the subject has a small number of expensive failure points and a lot of content that a capable student can read alone. These are the four blocks Dubai families book.

modes.title: Investigation feasibility block
modes.description: Three to five sessions, booked before any data is collected, which is the cheapest and highest-value block on this page. The work is interrogation: does this question have a measurable variable, can a school student lawfully obtain the data, how many replicates are realistic in a Dubai summer, and what will the statistics be if the data comes back as expected. Questions that cannot survive those four tests are discarded here rather than in March.

modes.title: Statistics and data-treatment block
modes.description: Four to six sessions on the quantitative half of the subject, which is where most Dubai ESS candidates lose avoidable marks. Test selection, the assumptions each test makes, what a significance value does and does not say, and how to present a result so an examiner can see the reasoning. Taught in whatever software the school uses rather than in a tool the student will never open again.

modes.title: Weekly papers block
modes.description: The standard arrangement through DP1 and into DP2, aimed at the written papers rather than the investigation. One timed question set a week, marked and returned before the next session, with teaching driven by the script. Systems diagrams and environmental value systems are practised every session because they are the two mechanics that appear across the whole paper.

modes.title: Paired sessions for two ESS students
modes.description: ESS suits paired teaching better than most Diploma sciences, because arguing about a value system with another student is closer to what the examination rewards than listening to an explanation is. Where two students at a similar stage share a session, the cost per family drops and the discussion quality rises. We only pair students where the levels and the school timeline genuinely match.

sections.heading: The two bills in ESS, and which one surprises people
paragraphs: A Dubai family pricing ESS support almost always prices the teaching and forgets the data. The teaching bill is predictable: an hourly rate inside the published Dubai bands, multiplied by however many weeks the family commits to. The data bill is not an invoice at all, which is precisely why it gets missed. It is paid in early planning hours, in transport to a site, in the equipment a school may or may not lend, in repeated visits when the first dataset turns out to be unusable, and in rescue hours when the analysis will not support a conclusion.

The reason this matters commercially is that the two bills trade against each other. Three well-spent hours testing a research question for feasibility before any collection happens routinely removes ten or more rescue hours later. That is the clearest cost argument in this subject and it runs in the opposite direction to how tutoring is usually sold, because it means buying help earliest when nothing appears to be wrong.

The table below separates the lines, says when each one lands in a Dubai Diploma year, and states plainly whether it can be avoided. The AED column applies other providers' published market bands rather than an IB Gram rate card, and the hours are planning estimates for a committed student rather than promises.

One line is worth reading twice. Rescue hours on a failed dataset are the only item here marked as almost entirely avoidable, and they are also the item Dubai families most often end up paying for. The sequence is always the same: a question chosen in a hurry around a school deadline, a collection trip made in whatever week was free, a set of numbers that turn out to be too few or too variable to test, and then a scramble in DP2 to extract a defensible conclusion from data that does not contain one. Nobody in that sequence behaved badly. The planning simply happened in the wrong order, and the bill arrived at the most expensive possible moment.

sections.heading: What primary data actually costs a Dubai ESS candidate
paragraphs: The investigation needs data the student has obtained, and Dubai makes that harder than a European textbook assumes. Summer temperatures rule out midday work for months. Most genuinely natural habitats near the city are either protected, access-controlled or a long drive away. Beaches and parks are municipal property with their own rules. And the school's own investigation window often falls in the hottest or the most congested part of the year.

None of that closes the subject. It changes which studies are sensible. The strongest Dubai investigations we see are small, repeatable and close to home: a shaded-versus-unshaded ground temperature study across a single compound, an irrigation and plant-survival comparison in a landscaped community, a vertical microclimate study up a tower, a waste-stream audit at one building, a salinity gradient along an accessible stretch of Creek. They look modest and they analyse cleanly, which is what the criteria reward.

The weakest are the ambitious ones: a mangrove biodiversity survey at a site the student cannot enter, a desalination impact study requiring data no school can obtain, a regional air-quality comparison built entirely from secondary sources and then presented as fieldwork. Those are not failures of effort. They are failures of feasibility checking, and they are detectable in twenty minutes by someone who has supervised the subject before.

The table lists site types a Dubai student can realistically use, what each yields, the access position to confirm before relying on it, and what to budget for. Confirm current access, permission and conservation rules with the relevant authority or through the school before any visit: designations change, and a student should never be the person who finds out the hard way.

sections.heading: Statistics is where ESS investigation marks are bought
paragraphs: Most of the avoidable marks in an ESS investigation sit in the analysis, and most Dubai candidates arrive unable to defend a statistical choice. The pattern is consistent: a sensible question, a reasonable dataset, a graph, and then a conclusion that asserts a relationship which the data was never tested for. An examiner reading that cannot award the analysis marks, however good the fieldwork was.

The reason is structural rather than anything to do with the student. ESS sits between a science and a social science, and the explicit teaching of statistical inference often falls between departments. The mathematics courses teach the tests; the ESS class teaches the content; nobody necessarily teaches the join. Where a student also takes Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, the join is usually already made, and those students need visibly fewer ESS hours.

The work itself is small and finite, which makes it good value. A student needs a decision procedure for choosing a test, an explicit habit of stating the assumptions that test makes, the ability to say what a significance value does and does not establish, and a presentation convention that lets an examiner follow the reasoning. Four to six sessions covers it for most candidates, and it is visible in the next draft rather than in a term's time.

The table maps the techniques that actually appear in ESS investigations against when each one is appropriate and the error we see most frequently. Treat it as a checklist against your child's draft rather than as a syllabus, and confirm the expectations for your cohort with the teacher who will mark it.

sections.heading: Costing ESS support by component instead of by the hour
paragraphs: An hourly rate tells a parent almost nothing about what a subject will cost, because it says nothing about how many hours each part of the assessment needs. Costing by component is more useful and much harder for a provider to inflate, since each line has an obvious deliverable attached to it.

The breakdown below is what we see for a reasonably diligent Dubai student working from roughly the middle of DP1. It assumes the school is teaching the course competently and that outside help is supplementing rather than replacing it. Where a school is covering ESS with a teacher whose background is elsewhere, the papers line roughly doubles and the investigation line stays about the same.

Two things are deliberately not in the table. There is no IB Gram rate, because the AED figures here are other providers' published market bands and our own pricing is set in the consultation after a free trial lesson. And there is no total, because a family that treats the components as a menu rather than a package usually spends less and gets more, by buying the feasibility and statistics blocks and self-serving the content revision.

Reading the lines against each other is the useful exercise. The investigation work, feasibility plus statistics plus draft feedback, comes to roughly ten to fifteen hours across two years and decides a component the student cannot retake independently. A term of weekly paper practice costs more hours than all of that combined and addresses a component the student can keep attacking until the examination itself. Families who have a fixed amount to spend almost always get more from the first group than the second, which is the opposite of how the market is usually sold to them.

Two further variables move these figures and both are worth asking about before committing. The first is whether the school's ESS teacher is a subject specialist, because a class being covered rather than taught shifts the papers line sharply upward. The second is how early the family makes contact, since every hour spent before data collection replaces something like two spent after it. Neither variable appears on a rate card, and both matter more than the hourly number does.

sections.heading: What a low ESS quote usually leaves out
paragraphs: A rate at the budget end of the Dubai market, somewhere in the AED 45 to 150 range that EdFlik and Tutopiya advertise, buys a real thing: an explanation of content by someone competent, often a university student. For a Dubai ESS candidate whose problem is that they have not read the material, that is good value and we would say so.

It stops being good value at the point the problem becomes assessment-shaped. The three things a budget rate almost never includes are marking turnaround between sessions, experience of supervising an investigation to the criteria, and the statistical judgement to say that a dataset will not support the conclusion a student wants. None of those is a matter of effort or goodwill. They are specific competencies, and the published specialist band of AED 200 to 450 is what the market charges for them.

The useful questions are therefore not about price. Ask how many ESS investigations the tutor has supervised, and to describe one that went wrong and why. Ask whether marking between sessions is inside the quoted rate or billed separately. Ask which statistical test they would expect for a comparison of two sites and why, and listen for whether assumptions get mentioned. Ask what they will refuse to do with a draft. A tutor who answers those four crisply is worth a specialist rate; one who cannot is worth a budget rate, and might be exactly right for a student who simply needs the content explained.
bullets: Marking turnaround between sessions, included or billed separately
Investigations actually supervised, and one that went wrong
A test choice justified with its assumptions named
A clear statement of what the tutor will refuse to do with a draft

sections.heading: Higher Level, Standard Level and what the difference costs in hours
paragraphs: ESS has historically been a Standard Level course and the current guide position on levels is something to confirm with your school's IB coordinator rather than with any tutoring page, including this one. What is stable is the planning logic: if your child is taking the subject at a level with additional content and an additional component, the extra material is where the hours go, and it is rarely absorbed by ordinary weekly lessons.

The practical advice is to treat any additional component as its own block with its own timetable, exactly as we do with the papers and the investigation. Students fail the extended material not because it is hard but because it is taught last, revised least and practised almost never. Scheduling it as a named block in the term before mocks is the difference between a component that holds a grade up and one that pulls it down.

Level choice also interacts with the degree route, and that is a cost question too. A student who needs a laboratory science for a quantitative degree may find that ESS at any level does not satisfy the prerequisite, in which case the right spend is on the science they actually need rather than on more ESS hours. We would rather say that at the consultation than sell a block that cannot help, and it is worth asking any provider the same question before committing to a term.

There is a scheduling consequence as well. Any additional component competes for the same weeks as the investigation write-up and the mock examinations, which in a Dubai school year tend to land close together. A family that books the extended material as a block in the term before mocks is buying time that exists. A family that leaves it until the investigation is also live is buying time that does not, and the usual outcome is that one of the two gets a fraction of the attention it needed. Ask the coordinator for the school's internal deadline dates early, and plan the blocks against those rather than against the calendar year.

sections.heading: ESS and the degree routes Dubai students actually apply to
paragraphs: Three separate gates get conflated here, and the conflation produces most of the bad advice circulating in Dubai parent groups. The first is the degree's own subject prerequisites, set by the university. The second is the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process, which concerns the certificate rather than the subject choice. The third is admissions judgement on the whole application.

On prerequisites, be concrete and check the course page for the entry year. Environmental science, sustainability, geography, policy and many business routes accept ESS without difficulty. Engineering and the physical sciences generally require Physics, Chemistry or Mathematics at a stated level, and ESS does not substitute for them. Medicine and the health sciences require Biology and Chemistry at the levels the school of medicine states. No tutor should be telling a family otherwise, and no page should be reassuring them in general terms when the university publishes the specific answer.

On equivalency, the published British-track rule as reported in July 2026 requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The American track requires English proficiency at IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, plus at least 450 in SAT Mathematics. One ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five. No IB points threshold has been verified for this page, so none is published. Check the current requirement on the Ministry's own channels, and note that equivalency is a process families complete with the authority directly.
bullets: Prerequisites are per course and per entry year: read the university's own page
ESS is accepted for environmental, geographic, policy and many business routes
ESS does not substitute for Physics, Chemistry or Biology where those are required
Equivalency concerns the certificate, not which Group 4 or Group 3 subject was taken

sections.heading: Honesty on data, databases and generated models
paragraphs: The investigation is submitted as the student's own work, and in a data subject the honesty questions are specific. Secondary data is permitted where the method says it is secondary and cites the publisher properly. Presenting a published dataset as fieldwork the student conducted is not a presentational shortcut, it is fabrication. The same applies to filling a gap in a dataset with a plausible figure, which happens more often than anyone admits and is the single fastest way to turn a weak investigation into a malpractice problem.

Generated text and generated models raise the same question in a newer form. A systems diagram produced by a language model, or an evaluation paragraph lightly edited from one, is not the student's work. In this subject such paragraphs are also easy to spot, because they are fluent, generic and never tied to the actual method used: a limitations section that would fit any investigation anywhere is the signature. Where a student has used any such tool, the school's own acknowledgement policy applies and the coordinator is the person to ask.

Our own rule is narrow and we state it before anyone pays. A tutor may ask any question about a draft and may not supply any sentence of it. That means the tutor can say that a conclusion is not supported by the test applied, that a graph does not answer the question, that a limitation is generic, or that the sample size will not bear the claim. It means the tutor does not propose the research question, does not write or rewrite any part of the submission, does not produce the diagrams, and does not invent or adjust a single data point.

We also do not reproduce or supply subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those belong to the board and are the school's to distribute. We reference them and cite the official source, which is what the examination boards ask of anyone writing about their qualifications.

sections.heading: Permits, delivery and what IB Gram does not do in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The route is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service for private tutor licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the ministry's app, website and e-services system. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here.

Two related points. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE, and claims no approval, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules in Abu Dhabi bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct points the same way, so a family anywhere in the UAE should not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by their own class teacher.

Delivery is online: one-to-one over live video, screen-shared, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school week and moved post-Iftar during Ramadan as standard. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. For ESS that is close to irrelevant to the teaching and helpful to the matching, because the useful tutor for this subject is the one who has supervised investigations before, not the one who lives nearby.

If no ESS specialist is free in your slot, we say so and say when one is likely, rather than assigning a biologist or a geographer quietly and letting you discover the substitution later. Where an adjacent specialist can genuinely help in the meantime, usually with statistics or with paper technique, we say exactly what they can and cannot cover. A free trial lesson comes first, with no card required to book it.

process.title: Send the research question, however rough
process.description: The most useful first document is whatever the student has written about their investigation idea, plus the school's investigation deadline and a recent marked paper response. A specialist can tell from the question alone whether the data exists, which is the information a Dubai family most needs before spending anything.

process.title: We check availability honestly before promising a slot
process.description: ESS specialists are thinner on the ground than Biology tutors across this region. We check the specific slot you need in Gulf Standard Time and tell you if nobody suitable is free, with an honest estimate of when one will be, rather than filling the slot with an adjacent subject teacher.

process.title: A free trial lesson spent on the real problem
process.description: The trial is a working session, usually spent testing the research question or marking one timed response. No card is required and nothing is charged if you stop there. You get a direct answer on whether the investigation plan is viable, which is worth having even if you go elsewhere.

process.title: A written plan by component, not by term
process.description: After the trial you receive a short plan naming which blocks apply, how many sessions each needs, and what exists at the end of each one. The AED context on this page is market data from other providers; your own quote is agreed in the consultation rather than read off a rate card.

process.title: Deliverables you can inspect
process.description: Marked timed responses, written draft feedback and the statistics decision record stay together in sequence. A parent who wants evidence can read three consecutive pieces of feedback and see whether the same fault recurs. That is also how we decide when a block is finished and should stop.

whyPoints.title: The data bill is on the page
whyPoints.description: Most providers quote the teaching and stay silent on the investigation logistics. We set out both, including the feasibility hours that prevent the expensive late rescue, so a Dubai family can see the whole cost of this subject before committing to any of it.

whyPoints.title: Feasibility first, which is the cheapest hour you will buy
whyPoints.description: Three hours testing a question for access, sample size and planned statistics routinely removes ten rescue hours in DP2. We sell that block first even though it is the smallest, because recommending it later would cost a family more and help them less.

whyPoints.title: Statistics taught explicitly, in the school's own software
whyPoints.description: Test selection, assumptions and interpretation are taught as a decision procedure in whatever tool the school already uses. This is where the investigation marks sit, and it falls between departments in a lot of Dubai schools.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here are other providers' published figures read in October 2026, with the provider named. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on honesty we will not move
whyPoints.description: A tutor may ask any question about a draft and may not supply any sentence, any diagram or any data point. We say that before a family pays, and we do not reproduce board materials such as guides, past papers or mark schemes.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around a real Dubai year
whyPoints.description: Collection windows are planned around summer heat and school fieldwork dates, sessions sit after school-run traffic, and Ramadan slots move post-Iftar as standard. For an investigation with a fixed school deadline, the calendar is part of the method rather than an afterthought.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai family budget for two years of ESS support?
faqs.answer: Treat it as components rather than a monthly subscription. A student whose school teaches the subject well typically needs a feasibility block of three to five hours, a statistics block of four to six, three or four hours of draft feedback, and then whatever paper practice the family wants. At the published Dubai specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour, the non-negotiable investigation work lands around AED 2,000 to 6,750 across the two years, with paper practice on top if you choose it. Those are other providers' published rates read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list; your own quote follows the free trial.

faqs.question: Why is ESS quoted at a higher rate than Geography in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Supply, mainly. Geography is taught in nearly every Dubai secondary school and the tutoring pool is deep, so quotes cluster in the AED 150 to 300 qualified-tutor band that Bestimate publishes. ESS is taught in fewer schools, and the people who can both teach the content and supervise a quantitative investigation to the criteria are a smaller group again, so quotes sit in the AED 200 to 450 specialist band. Content difficulty is not the mechanism. If a provider explains the premium by saying ESS is harder than Geography, ask instead how many ESS investigations they have supervised.

faqs.question: Does primary data for the ESS investigation have to cost anything?
faqs.answer: Usually not, if the study is designed around what the student can reach. The strongest Dubai investigations tend to use the school grounds, a residential compound or a single building: shaded against unshaded ground temperature, irrigation and plant survival, a vertical microclimate profile up a tower, a waste audit at one address. Those need borrowed equipment and repeated early-morning visits rather than money. Costs appear when a study depends on a distant or restricted site, which adds transport, timing constraints and the risk of refusal. Confirm access rules with the school or the relevant authority before relying on any site off the school grounds.

faqs.question: Which statistical test does my child need for the ESS investigation?
faqs.answer: That depends on the question and it should be chosen before collection, not after. A comparison of two sites or two treatments needs a test of difference; a relationship between two measured variables needs a correlation statistic, reported as correlation and not as cause; counts across categories need a test of association. The decision also has to be made early because it determines what shape the data has to be collected in, and a dataset gathered without a planned test frequently cannot support any. We teach the choice as a decision procedure with its assumptions named, and we expect the student to be able to justify it aloud.

faqs.question: Can two ESS students share a session without losing value?
faqs.answer: In this subject, often yes. The examination rewards the explicit application of environmental value systems and the weighing of competing positions, and arguing about those with another student is closer to the assessed skill than hearing an explanation is. A pair at a comparable stage reduces the cost per family and tends to raise discussion quality. The conditions matter: both students should be at a similar point in the course and on a similar school timeline, written feedback stays individual, and investigation supervision remains one-to-one because the questions are specific to each student's own data.

faqs.question: How many hours does investigation supervision usually take?
faqs.answer: For a student who starts early, around ten to fifteen hours in total across the whole process: three to five testing feasibility before collection, four to six on statistics and data treatment once data exists, and three to four on written feedback across drafts. For a student who arrives with data already collected that will not support a conclusion, the figure is higher and the outcome is worse, because some of those hours go on salvage rather than on improvement. That asymmetry is the strongest argument for buying the earliest block rather than the largest one.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start ESS support in DP1 or wait until DP2?
faqs.answer: Cheaper and better in DP1, and this is one of the few subjects where that is a cost claim rather than a sales line. The investigation is the component where late help is least effective, because the question, the access and the dataset are already fixed by the time a DP2 family typically makes contact. Starting in the second half of DP1 lets the feasibility work happen while the question can still change, which is when it is worth anything. If you are already in DP2, say so at the consultation and we will plan around the papers instead of pretending the investigation can be rebuilt.

faqs.question: Can my child collect usable data living in a Dubai apartment?
faqs.answer: Yes, and apartment families often assume otherwise. A tower is a research site with a vertical dimension most villa studies do not have: temperature and wind at different floors, balcony microclimate against interior, shading patterns across a day, lift and water use, waste separation at a single building. Each of those gives repeatable measurements inside walking distance and in air conditioning for much of the method. Building management consent is the thing to secure first, and any survey of residents needs their agreement. We plan the study around what the building allows rather than around what a textbook assumes.

faqs.question: Which software does an ESS candidate actually need?
faqs.answer: Whatever the school already uses, which in most Dubai schools is a spreadsheet. Descriptive statistics, a scatter plot with a correlation statistic, a test of difference and a clean table are all achievable in standard spreadsheet software, and an examiner is marking the reasoning rather than the tool. We deliberately teach in the school's software instead of introducing a statistics package the student will open twice and then abandon. If the school teaches a specific package, we use that. Nobody should be buying software licences for this subject.

faqs.question: Does ESS satisfy a science requirement for engineering at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Generally no, and this is worth checking rather than assuming. Engineering and physical-science routes normally require Physics, Chemistry or Mathematics at a stated level, and an interdisciplinary environmental course does not substitute for them. ESS is well accepted for environmental science, sustainability, geography, policy and many business routes. Read the course page for your child's entry year on the university's own site, because requirements change and no tutoring page should be the source. If the prerequisite is a laboratory science, the right spend is on that subject rather than on more ESS hours.

faqs.question: Can my child use an online database instead of collecting data?
faqs.answer: Secondary data is permitted where the method states clearly that it is secondary and cites the publisher properly, and for some Dubai questions a published long time series is genuinely the better evidence. What is not permitted is presenting a published dataset as fieldwork the student conducted, or filling a gap in a collected dataset with a plausible number. Both are fabrication rather than presentation, and both are detectable. If the investigation will rest on secondary data, design it as a secondary-data study from the start and confirm with the teacher that the cohort's expectations allow it.

faqs.question: Is it acceptable to use a generative tool to build a systems diagram?
faqs.answer: The submitted work has to be the student's own, and a diagram or paragraph produced by a language model is not. In ESS such output is also unusually easy to identify, because it is fluent and untethered: an evaluation that would fit any investigation anywhere, or a systems diagram with plausible labels and flows that do not match the method actually used. Where a student has used any such tool at any stage, the school's own acknowledgement policy governs what must be declared, and the IB coordinator is the person to ask. Our tutors do not produce diagrams, prose or data for a submission.

faqs.question: What does a low ESS tutoring quote usually leave out?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is effort. Marking turnaround between sessions is the first; a budget rate normally covers contact time only. Experience of supervising an investigation to the published criteria is the second, and it is what prevents a dataset that cannot support a conclusion. Statistical judgement is the third. A rate in the AED 45 to 150 range that budget providers advertise is good value for a student who simply needs content explained. It is poor value for one whose problem is assessment-shaped, which is most students who search for this subject by name.

faqs.question: Do ESS lessons need to be in person because of the practical work?
faqs.answer: No, and the practical work is the part online handles best. The fieldwork happens without a tutor present in any model, because it is the student's own investigation at their own site. What a session does is plan it beforehand and interrogate the data afterwards, both of which work better on a shared screen where the spreadsheet, the graph and the draft are all visible and the annotated version is saved rather than lost. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India, and for this subject the limitation costs a family nothing.

faqs.question: Does an ESS tutor working with Dubai students need a permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private lessons in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is issued free of charge for two years, the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18, and applications go through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service for private tutor licensing. Individuals operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure is quoted. Ask any UAE-resident tutor to show their permit.

faqs.question: What happens if no ESS specialist is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: We say so, and give an honest estimate of when a slot will open rather than quietly assigning a biologist or a geographer. For this subject the substitution matters: a strong biologist can teach the content and may still not know what the investigation criteria reward. Where an adjacent specialist can usefully help in the interim, normally on statistics or on paper technique, we state exactly what they will and will not cover so you can decide. Nothing is charged while you wait, and the free trial lesson still comes first once the specialist slot opens.

dubai/ib-dp-environmental-systems-and-so.closingHeading: Send the research question before you send anything else

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below supervise and read Extended Essays across the DP subject groups. Choose on subject fit first: a Biology essay and a History essay fail in completely different ways, and the person who can diagnose one is often not the person who can diagnose the other.

intro.heading: The Extended Essay is marked out of 34, and most families never see the breakdown
paragraphs: The letter grade is what appears on the transcript, so that is what Dubai parents ask about. Underneath it is a 34-mark scale split across five criteria, and the split is the most useful thing a family can know. Criterion A, focus and method, carries six marks. Criterion B, knowledge and understanding, carries six. Criterion C, critical thinking, carries twelve. Criterion D, presentation, carries four. Criterion E, engagement, carries six and is awarded from the student's three recorded reflections rather than from the essay at all.

Read that list again and the strategy becomes obvious. More than a third of the available marks sit in a single criterion that rewards analysis and the evaluation of evidence, and almost a fifth sit in a form most students fill in the week before submission. Meanwhile presentation, the thing students spend whole evenings on, is worth four. A student polishing formatting while Criterion C sits at a third of its potential is spending time in the wrong place, and no supervisor has the hours to keep pointing that out.

Which brings us to what an IB DP Extended Essay home tutor in Dubai is actually for. The supervisor is the right person for subject judgement and the official record, and the IB's guidance limits total supervision to a small number of hours across the whole project, including the three reflection sessions. That is enough for direction and nowhere near enough for drafting support. The gap is real, legitimate, and where outside help belongs: reading a draft against the criteria, pressing on a research question until it narrows, and making sure the reflections say something assessable.

This page is built around the component rather than around the city, because the component is what fails. Below you will find the criteria with their marks and the specific ways each one leaks; the research question problem, which caps more essays than any other single factor; what does and does not count towards the 4,000 words; how the reflections are assessed and why the form is not administration; the published mark bands behind each letter; what the Dubai market charges for this work and who published each figure; and how the essay interacts with UAE Ministry of Education equivalency and university applications from here.

Delivery, stated plainly. Home tutoring is the phrase Dubai parents search, and the market reality is covered in full further down: what an in-home tutor charges in this emirate, what travel does to a weekday evening, how families weigh it. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Dubai families are taught one-to-one over live video, and for a research essay the format carries an advantage that is specific rather than rhetorical: the work is a document, the tutor's comments live in it, and the version history shows exactly how the argument developed and who moved it.

One honesty note before the detail. Nothing on this page is an offer to produce assessed work. The Extended Essay must be the student's own research and the student's own prose, the reflections must record their own thinking, and the authenticity declaration at submission is theirs to sign. A tutor who edits an essay into their own voice has not helped; they have created a malpractice risk that lands on the student. Where the line sits is set out explicitly in its own section.

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Independent research is built across the IB continuum, and each programme leaves a student with a different half of the skill. Below is where each one helps and where it leaves a gap that shows up in a 4,000-word essay.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Extended Essay runs across both DP years: subject and topic chosen late in DP1, first reflection shortly after, research through the summer and the first DP2 term, submission before the exam session. It is externally assessed, graded A to E, and pairs with Theory of Knowledge in the matrix that awards up to three of the 45 diploma points. Students also sit internal assessments in six subjects and complete CAS, which is why the essay timetable collides with everything else.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the collision is sharper than most families expect, because the DP timetable here also carries the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons KHDA requires of every private school regardless of curriculum. Supervisor meetings get squeezed into break periods, and the summer between DP1 and DP2 - when most of the reading should happen - is also when a large share of Dubai families travel for six or seven weeks.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP personal project is the closest thing to rehearsal the IB offers: a self-directed piece with a process journal, a product and a report. Students who took it seriously arrive at the Extended Essay already knowing that a project needs a narrow aim and a record of decisions. The gap MYP leaves is academic apparatus - sustained engagement with published sources, and a citation habit strong enough to survive 4,000 words.
programmes.countryNote: A number of Dubai schools run MYP through Year 11 rather than switching to IGCSE, and their students usually handle the reflections better because the personal project journal taught them to write about their own process. Students arriving in DP1 from an exam-only Year 11 often write their first reflection as a summary of what they did rather than as an account of what they decided.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP core includes a reflective project rather than the Extended Essay. It is shorter, differently assessed and tied to the student's career-related study, so it does not substitute for an Extended Essay in a diploma application. The reason it belongs here is that Dubai families occasionally compare the two routes during a difficult DP1, and the research component is often the trigger for that conversation.
programmes.countryNote: Only a handful of Dubai schools offer CP, and any move between programmes is governed by registration deadlines your DP coordinator holds. A tutor's job in that discussion is to describe the research requirement accurately and then send you back to the school, not to advise on a registration decision.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Listed for continuity rather than support. The PYP exhibition in Year 6 is where IB students first run an inquiry of their own and then answer questions about it in public, which is structurally the same demand the Extended Essay makes eight years later. Parents who sat through a PYP exhibition evening recognise the viva voce immediately.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a deep PYP intake and a lot of movement between schools at Year 7, so plenty of DP students here did PYP at a different school from the one supervising their essay. It makes no difference to the assessment; it does mean the research habit may have been built somewhere nobody in the current school remembers.

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: An Extended Essay is written in a DP subject, and each subject fails in its own particular way. The grid below is the set of routes Dubai students most often take, with the specific thing that costs marks in each.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Popular and risky. Essays collapse when the student collects their own data without a controllable variable, or reviews literature without a question. Criterion C needs evaluation of method and limitation, not a description of results. Local fieldwork in Dubai conditions needs a realistic plan before any data is gathered.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Laboratory access is the binding constraint in most Dubai schools, which pushes students towards database or literature-based questions. Those can score highly, but only with genuine evaluation of source reliability. Marks vanish when the essay becomes a textbook chapter on a mechanism.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The strongest Physics essays narrow to one measurable relationship and treat uncertainty seriously. The weakest pick a topic from popular science writing and have no way to analyse anything. Criterion A is where the damage is done, because the method was never viable.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Under-chosen and often rewarding for Analysis and Approaches students. The trap is an essay that reproduces known proofs without an argument of its own. Examiners want mathematical reasoning applied to a question the student poses, with the limits of the model discussed.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The single most common route and the one with the most predictable failure: a question so broad that 4,000 words can only summarise. Historiography is the lever for Criterion C - weighing how different historians have read the same evidence, rather than narrating events.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Works best on a question with real data and a theoretical frame that can be tested against it. UAE and wider Gulf data is accessible and under-used. Essays lose marks by drifting into business commentary or by applying a diagram without evaluating whether it fits the case.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Requires a researchable question about an organisation and evidence beyond the company's own publicity. Primary research in Dubai is possible but needs permissions arranged early. The commonest loss is an essay that reports a company's strategy instead of analysing it.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Attracts students who then write a literature summary. The mark comes from comparing studies on methodology - sample, design, replication, cultural generalisability - and ethical constraints rule out most of the primary research students imagine doing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Category choice matters and is frequently got wrong, which costs Criterion A immediately. A tight question about technique in two or three texts beats a thematic survey of five. Close textual evidence is the engine of Criterion C here.

subjects.name: Language B and Language ab initio
subjects.description: The essay must be written in the target language for most categories, and the language itself is not separately assessed - but imprecise expression drags knowledge and critical thinking down with it. Source selection in the target language is the practical bottleneck.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Needs a question that can be answered by analysing works, not by describing an artist's life. Dubai and Sharjah give students access to exhibitions and collections that make genuine first-hand analysis possible, which examiners notice.

subjects.name: World Studies
subjects.description: A global issue examined through two DP subjects, with a local case and a genuine integration of both lenses. High ceiling, high difficulty: essays fail when the two subjects sit in separate halves rather than informing each other, and the local case is the usual anchor that saves it.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Spatial questions with primary or secondary data work well, and the UAE offers urban-growth and water-resource questions that are genuinely open. Marks are lost when the essay has no spatial dimension and becomes general environmental commentary.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Needs a political-science concept doing real work rather than a current-affairs narrative. Criterion C rewards weighing competing theoretical readings of the same case, and the hardest discipline is keeping the scope narrow enough to argue.

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities, and what each one asks us for first
dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Extended Essay enquiries arrive from across Dubai, and the first request differs by community in a way that tracks school cohort and supervisor load rather than geography alone. Here is the pattern we see.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Large DP cohorts in nearby schools and a parent group that compares supervisors closely. The common first ask is a second reader for a History or Economics draft where the supervisor's allotted hours have already been used up.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Mixed school attendance and long commutes to several DP schools, so after-school time is short. Requests here lean towards research-question clinics booked in a single evening rather than standing weekly slots.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: A newer DP population with a high proportion of science-route essays. The recurring problem is laboratory access for a Chemistry or Biology question, and the first session is usually about redesigning the question around what is actually available.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: Apartment living, high turnover, and students who often arrive mid-DP1 from another country. Essays here frequently need a subject change confirmed with the supervisor before any further work is worth doing.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to university libraries and several large schools, which makes secondary-source access easier than elsewhere in the city. Requests skew towards Psychology and Business Management, where source quality is the main constraint on Criterion C.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Villa communities with a long drive to most DP schools and limited local tutor supply. Families here value a fixed evening slot that cannot be lost to traffic, and reflections work is often done in short sessions after dinner.

regions.name: The Greens, The Views and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Dense, walkable, and heavily populated with DP2 students in the final submission term. The typical booking is a short block: final cut to 4,000 words, citation audit, and viva voce preparation.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Khawaneej
regions.note: Established eastern communities with large school cohorts and a strong preference for post-Maghrib sessions. During Ramadan nearly all of these bookings move to post-Iftar slots, which is why online scheduling matters here.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools with large DP research cohorts
schoolClusters.note: Where a school runs a big DP cohort, supervisor load is the constraint rather than supervisor quality: one teacher may hold six or eight essays alongside a full teaching timetable. Students we support attend schools across this group, and the request is almost always for a second reader rather than a replacement.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools with newer or growing DP provision
schoolClusters.note: Newer DP cohorts mean fewer supervisors who have taken an essay through a full cycle, and that shows up as late subject decisions and thin first reflections. Students we support attend schools in this group, and early research-question work pays for itself here more than anywhere else.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and central Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Long-running DP programmes with crowded timetables and a high proportion of students taking the science and mathematics routes. Students we support attend schools across this area, and laboratory access is the question that shapes most first sessions.

modes.title: Research question clinic
modes.description: One or two sessions, booked before anything else. The student brings a topic; the session converts it into a question that 4,000 words can actually answer, tests whether the sources and data exist, and checks the subject and category choice against what the essay will have to do. This is the cheapest intervention available and the one that changes the final grade most, because Criterion A failures are structural and cannot be repaired later.

sections.heading: The five criteria and where each one leaks marks
paragraphs: Every Extended Essay is marked on the same five criteria regardless of subject, and the mark allocation is public. Knowing the allocation changes how a student spends the last fortnight, and knowing the characteristic failure of each criterion changes how they spend the first one. The table below sets out both.

Criterion A, focus and method, is worth six marks and is decided almost entirely by the research question. A question that is too broad cannot be answered in 4,000 words, so the essay describes instead of arguing, and the damage then spreads into Criterion C. Examiners see this constantly: an essay that is competent, readable and capped at a C because the question was never answerable.

Criterion B, knowledge and understanding, is worth six and is the one most students already satisfy. It rewards correct use of subject-specific terminology and sources that belong to the discipline. Students lose marks here mainly by writing outside the subject they registered - an Economics essay that turns into business commentary, a Psychology essay that reads as sociology.

Criterion C, critical thinking, is worth twelve, more than a third of the total, and is where the grade is actually decided. It rewards analysis, discussion and evaluation. A paragraph that reports a finding earns little; a paragraph that weighs two findings against each other and names the limitation of both earns a great deal. The fastest diagnostic available is to count paragraphs: if more than half of them report rather than evaluate, the essay cannot reach the top bands no matter how well written it is.

Criterion D, presentation, is worth four - layout, structure, contents page, consistent referencing apparatus. It is the smallest allocation and the one students over-invest in. Criterion E, engagement, is worth six and comes from the three reflections rather than from the essay, which means a fifth of the available marks sit in a 500-word form that many students write in one sitting the night before. Those six marks are the cheapest on the paper and the most frequently abandoned.

sections.heading: The research question decides the grade before any research happens
paragraphs: If a session can only do one thing, it should fix the question. A narrow, arguable research question makes the rest of the project difficult but possible. A broad one makes it comfortable and caps it, because 4,000 words spread across a large topic can only summarise, and summary does not score in Criterion C.

The test we use is blunt. Can the question be answered with evidence the student can actually obtain, in roughly 3,000 words of analysis, in a way that someone could reasonably disagree with? If the answer to any part of that is no, the question is not ready. "To what extent did trade shape the development of the Gulf?" fails all three. "To what extent does the archaeological evidence from one specific site support claims about pre-oil trade routes?" passes, because the evidence base is finite and the conclusion is contestable.

Subject-specific versions of the same problem recur predictably. A Biology question needs a variable the student can control or a literature base they can genuinely evaluate. A Chemistry question has to survive the laboratory access their school will actually grant, which in most Dubai schools is limited, so database-led questions are often the honest choice rather than the lazy one. A History question needs historiography available in a language the student reads. An English question needs a textual feature narrow enough to track across two or three texts.

Timing matters as much as wording. The question should be settled before the summer between DP1 and DP2, because that summer is when the reading has to happen, and in Dubai it is also when a large share of families are away for six or seven weeks. A student who leaves Dubai in June without a settled question returns in late August with nothing done and one term to produce 4,000 words.

This is also where a tutor is most clearly within the honesty line. Pressing a student with questions until their own topic narrows is teaching. Handing them a research question is not, and a supervisor will usually notice, because the first reflection will not sound like the student. The output of a clinic session should be a question in the student's own words that they can defend in the viva.

sections.heading: What counts towards the 4,000 words and what does not
paragraphs: Almost every Extended Essay arrives at the submission term over length, and the cutting is done badly because nobody has checked the rules first. The word limit applies to the essay itself, and examiners are not required to read beyond it, which means an argument sitting in word 4,200 has effectively been deleted by the student rather than by the examiner.

The elements that count are the ones carrying the argument: the introduction, the body, the conclusion, and quotations inside the text. Footnotes count when they carry content rather than a reference, which is the rule most often misunderstood. A footnote saying "Smith, 2019, p.42" does not count; a footnote containing a sentence of explanation does. Students who move chunks of argument into footnotes to beat the limit are usually discovered, and the material is lost either way.

The elements outside the count are the title page, contents page, bibliography, reference list, appendices, maps, charts, diagrams, tables of raw data, and the reflections. Appendices are the most abused of these. An appendix exists for material an examiner may consult, not for analysis the student could not fit. Examiners are not obliged to read appendices at all, so an argument placed there is an argument not marked.

The practical sequence for cutting is: apply the rules first and see what the real count is, then remove description before analysis, then remove the second example wherever two make the same point, then tighten the introduction, which is almost always a third longer than it needs to be. Never cut Criterion C material to protect background context. Twelve marks sit in the analysis and six in knowledge.

Two smaller rules worth knowing. The reflections have their own ceiling of 500 words across all three, and that limit is separate from the essay. For most Language B and Language A category routes the essay is written in the target language, and the word limit is the same, which makes the drafting discipline tighter than students expect.

They have their own separate 500-word ceiling and carry Criterion E

sections.heading: The reflections carry six marks and are not administration
paragraphs: Criterion E is worth six of the 34 marks and is assessed entirely from the reflections form, completed across three recorded sessions with the supervisor. The total across all three is capped at 500 words. A student who writes all three in one sitting the week before submission is handing back a fifth of the paper, and it happens often enough that it is the single most predictable loss in the whole component.

The reflections are assessed on engagement with the research process, which means decisions rather than activities. "I read several articles about my topic and found them useful" records an activity. "I had intended to compare two data sets but the second had been collected on a different basis, so I narrowed the question to the first and treated comparability as a limitation" records a decision, a difficulty and a change of direction in one sentence. Examiners can tell the difference instantly.

The three sessions sit at natural points: early, when the question and approach are being settled; in the middle, when the research is underway and something has usually gone wrong; and at the end, in the concluding interview often called the viva voce. Each is a conversation with the supervisor, and the form records what the student took from it. Because the sessions are spaced, reflections written retrospectively tend to read as though nothing ever changed - which is itself evidence that they were written retrospectively.

There is a second function to the form that matters more than the marks. It is the record of the student's own engagement with their own project, and it is the first document anyone looks at if authorship is questioned. A student whose essay is strong and whose reflections are thin and generic has created a question about their work that they will have to answer. One whose reflections track real decisions has a straightforward answer ready.

A tutor's legitimate role here is narrow and useful: explain what the criterion rewards, ask what actually changed in the last month, and point out when a sentence is describing instead of deciding. The words must be the student's. We do not draft reflections, and a provider who offers to is offering something that will damage the student who accepts it.

sections.heading: What each letter is worth, and the failing condition
paragraphs: The 34 marks convert to a letter through published bands: A is 27 to 34, B is 21 to 26, C is 14 to 20, D is 7 to 13 and E is 0 to 6. Confirm the current table against the Extended Essay guide your DP coordinator holds before planning around it, but the shape is stable and the shape is what matters.

Two things follow from the bands. The first is that the gaps are wide, so single-criterion improvements move letters. Picking up four marks in Criterion C and two in Criterion E - a better analysis section and reflections written properly - is a six-mark swing, which is enough to cross a boundary from most starting positions. That is why diagnosing against criteria rather than giving general feedback is worth paying for.

The second is the failing condition. A grade E in the Extended Essay, or in Theory of Knowledge, is a failing condition for the diploma whatever the subject points total. Since E is 0 to 6 marks out of 34, it is genuinely hard to reach - but a non-submission or an essay that is substantially off-subject gets there. Every year a few students with good subject grades discover this late.

The letter also pairs with the Theory of Knowledge grade in the core points matrix, which awards between zero and three of the 45 diploma points. The arithmetic is worth doing before buying hours: if the Extended Essay sits at a high C and TOK at a secure B, the hours belong to the essay, because moving the essay by one letter is likely to be the cheaper point. If the essay is already a strong B and TOK is unaddressed, the reverse applies.

One practical note for Dubai families applying to UK universities. Offers are made on predicted points, and the Extended Essay predicted grade feeds the core points inside that prediction. A predicted grade set early in DP2 on the basis of a thin first draft is a prediction that follows the student through the whole application cycle, which is an argument for front-loading the work rather than for a final-term rescue.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the Extended Essay is where it is tested hardest
paragraphs: The Extended Essay carries the highest integrity risk of any DP component, because it is long, it is written mostly out of sight, and the market contains providers who will sell a finished one. Research for this project found a site advertising completed internal assessments at a published price. Buying assessed work is malpractice under IB rules, the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller, and it can end a diploma.

So the boundary needs stating rather than implying. A tutor may teach research method, explain each criterion and its mark allocation, press on a research question until the student narrows it themselves, read a draft and say which paragraphs report rather than evaluate, explain citation conventions, point out where a source is not reliable, and rehearse the viva voce. All of that is teaching, and none of it touches authorship.

A tutor may not supply a research question, write or rewrite any part of the essay, restructure it by moving the student's text around for them, draft reflections, or provide a model essay to be adapted. Our working test: if a sentence in the final essay could not have been produced by the student and cannot be explained by them in the viva, the line has been crossed regardless of intent. We do not produce assessed work, and we say so before a first session rather than after an awkward request.

Two further rules worth knowing. Published syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and subject guides are not ours to distribute, so we reference and link them rather than supplying copies - reproducing them is a copyright matter. And where a student has used a generative tool at any stage, that use has to be declared according to their school's policy; a tutor's job is to point them to the policy, not to help conceal anything.

The protective value of working honestly is underrated. A student with a full version history, three reflections that track real decisions, and the ability to talk about their own method for ten minutes has nothing to fear from an authenticity question. That record is a by-product of being taught properly, and it is the main reason we keep every draft in a shared document rather than emailing files back and forth.

sections.heading: What Extended Essay support costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: Most pages ranking for this search publish no price at all, and the ones that do quote US dollars. Below are the AED bands visible in this market as of October 2026, with the provider that published each figure named, organised by the stage of the project rather than by tier - because Extended Essay help is bought in blocks around deadlines, not by the year. These are market rates. They are not an IB Gram price list; our rate is quoted after the free trial, once the subject match is known.

The stage framing matters for a reason that saves money. A research question clinic is one or two hours and it is the highest-return purchase in the whole component, because Criterion A failures cannot be fixed later. Draft reading is the largest block and the one where a subject match actually matters, so it is worth paying a specialist rate for. Reflections and viva work is short. The final cut is short. A family that buys those four blocks spends materially less than one buying a weekly hour for eighteen months, and typically gets a better result because the work lands where the deadlines are.

For reference against the wider market: EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase publishes AED 270; Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 and specialist support at AED 200-450 or more; BartyED publishes AED 650. Monthly packages in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Three cautions on reading any of those numbers. Ask whether VAT is included before comparing two quotes, because providers here are inconsistent about it. Treat a rate justified by examiner experience as a claim about a specific person and ask how it was verified; examiner status confers no access to marking decisions or grade boundaries, and anyone implying otherwise is selling something that does not exist. And be wary of a provider who will not name the subject of the person reading a science essay, because a generalist reading a Chemistry draft cannot assess Criterion B.

For context on the household budget: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Against a flat fee bill, a few deadline-shaped blocks across two years is a finite and visible line rather than an open commitment.
