sections.heading: Online one-to-one against the in-home option for a research essay
paragraphs: The phrase parents search is home tutor, so the comparison deserves a straight answer. An in-home tutor in Dubai is a genuine option and for some needs it is the right one; it costs more per hour because the drive is inside the price. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and home visits are a service we run only in India. For the Extended Essay specifically, the online format has advantages that are structural rather than promotional.

The first is subject match. An Extended Essay is read properly only by someone who knows the subject's conventions - what counts as evidence in History, what a reliable database is in Chemistry, what historiography or replication actually means. The chance that such a person lives within a comfortable drive of Nad Al Sheba and is free at 6pm on a Wednesday is low. Removing the travel constraint changes the question from who is nearby to who can read this subject.

The second is that the work is already a document. A research essay lives in a file with comments, tracked versions and a bibliography that has to stay consistent across months. Reading it together on screen, with the tutor's comments stored beside the student's text, is simply the native format for the task. It also produces the version history that protects the student's authorship, which a kitchen-table conversation does not.

The third is the calendar. The Extended Essay timetable in Dubai runs through the DP1 summer, when many families are abroad for weeks, and through a DP2 term containing mocks, internal assessment deadlines and in some years Ramadan. Online sessions follow a family to another time zone, shift to post-Iftar slots for a month, and can be made up on a Saturday. None of that is available from a tutor whose availability depends on their own commute.

What in-home does better is worth saying plainly rather than hiding: a younger student who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, or a household where screen-based study is hard to supervise. That rarely describes a seventeen-year-old managing a 4,000-word research project. If you need someone at the door, that is a legitimate requirement and we would rather tell you now that this is not the service for it.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay, UAE equivalency and university applications from Dubai
paragraphs: Dubai families apply in several directions at once, and the Extended Essay sits differently in each. For UK applications it feeds the core points inside a predicted total and gives a genuine subject-specific talking point in a personal statement, particularly where the essay is in the subject being applied for. For North American applications it is evidence of independent research that admissions readers recognise. For UAE universities the relevant process is Ministry of Education equivalency, and the essay plays no direct part in it - which is worth knowing precisely because competitor pages imply otherwise.

On equivalency, the sourced position is this. For the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong; the published rule is five.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is published in the source we were able to verify, so this page states none. If you need the IB figure, read it on moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority page, or ask your school's university counsellor to confirm it in writing.

Two things we will not do. We will not describe equivalency or attestation as something IB Gram performs, arranges or guarantees - it is a government process with an official channel, and the channel is the place to do it. And we will not suggest that tutoring is required for equivalency, university admission or school progression. It is not, and implying it would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process.

What a tutor can usefully do is align the research with the application. A student intending to read Economics who has written a narrow Economics essay with real Gulf data has something concrete to discuss at interview and in a personal statement. A student who picked a topic because it sounded impressive usually has nothing to say about it six months later. That alignment is a conversation worth having in DP1, when the subject choice is still open, rather than in DP2 when it is not.

process.title: Send the question and the current draft
process.description: A short form: DP year, school, essay subject and category, the current research question in full, and the supervisor's next internal deadline. Attach whatever exists, including a draft you think is too rough to send. The rougher it is, the more useful the first reading.

process.title: Free trial with the criteria open
process.description: Sixty minutes with the student's own material on screen. The tutor scores what exists against criteria A to E, names which criterion is costing the most marks, and gives two specific changes. You keep the written diagnosis whether or not you book again. No card is taken to arrange it.

process.title: Choose a block, not a subscription
process.description: We recommend one of four blocks - question clinic, draft reading, reflections and viva, final cut - based on where the essay actually is. You see the recommended hours and what each block is meant to deliver before paying for anything.

process.title: Work in the student's own document
process.description: Drafts stay in one shared file with full version history. Comments are criterion-tagged and phrased as questions. Between sessions the student rewrites; nothing is rewritten for them, which is both the honest position and the only one that produces a defensible viva.

process.title: Re-score at the end of each block
process.description: Each block closes with a fresh criterion-by-criterion score against the first one, so improvement is a number rather than an impression. If a criterion has not moved, we say which and why, and change the approach or the tutor.

process.title: Stop when the essay is ready
process.description: Extended Essay help should end. When the final version is cut to length, cited consistently and the reflections are genuinely written, the work is done and we say so. Carrying a standing weekly slot past that point is a cost without a purpose.

whyPoints.title: Marked against the criteria, with the marks named
whyPoints.description: Every draft comes back scored criterion by criterion with the allocation stated - six, six, twelve, four, six. You can see where the marks are and where they are missing, which is not the same as being told the essay is coming along nicely.

whyPoints.title: The question gets fixed before the research starts
whyPoints.description: A broad research question caps a grade no matter how good the writing is, and it cannot be repaired in the final term. The cheapest session in this component is the one that narrows the question, so we push families to buy it first and sometimes buy nothing else.

whyPoints.title: Subject-matched reading, not generalist feedback
whyPoints.description: A Chemistry essay and a History essay fail differently, and only someone inside the discipline can assess subject terminology and source reliability. Online matching means the reader is chosen for the subject rather than for the drive to your community.

whyPoints.title: Reflections treated as six real marks
whyPoints.description: Criterion E is a fifth of the paper and most students abandon it. We work on the reflections as assessed writing, within the 500-word total, about decisions rather than activities - and we never draft them, because they must be the student's own.

whyPoints.title: Authorship protected by the way we work
whyPoints.description: One shared document, every version retained, comments phrased as questions rather than rewrites, and viva rehearsal on the student's own process. A student who has worked this way can answer any authenticity question in a straightforward way.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can audit
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider that published it with October 2026 as the as-of date, split by project stage so you can see what the component actually costs. Our own number is quoted after the free trial, once the subject match exists.

faqs.question: What can an Extended Essay tutor do that my child's supervisor cannot?
faqs.answer: Hours, mainly. The supervisor holds subject judgement and the official record, and IB guidance limits total supervision across the whole project to a few hours including the three reflection sessions. That is enough for direction and far short of what drafting support requires, especially where one teacher is supervising six or eight essays alongside a full timetable. A tutor adds reading time: criterion-by-criterion marking of successive drafts, pressure on the research question, and preparation for the concluding interview. The supervisor stays the authority on the subject and on the forms, and a good tutor tells the student to take disputed points back to them.

faqs.question: How many marks is each Extended Essay criterion actually worth?
faqs.answer: Thirty-four in total, split five ways: Criterion A focus and method, six marks; Criterion B knowledge and understanding, six; Criterion C critical thinking, twelve; Criterion D presentation, four; Criterion E engagement, six. Criterion C alone is more than a third of the paper, and Criterion E comes from the three reflections rather than from the essay. The practical consequence is that evening spent on formatting is competing for four marks while the analysis section is competing for twelve. Confirm the current allocation against the Extended Essay guide your DP coordinator holds, then plan the remaining weeks around where the marks actually are.

faqs.question: My daughter's research question feels too broad. Can that still be changed in DP2?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is usually worth doing. Narrowing a question in the first DP2 term normally means keeping most of the reading and changing the frame, which is far cheaper than it sounds. The decision has to go through the supervisor, because the subject and question are on the record. What cannot be fixed late is a question requiring data or sources the student has no way of obtaining - that needs a genuine change of direction, and the interim reflection is the right place to document it. A single clinic session is usually enough to establish which of the two situations you are in.

faqs.question: Do footnotes and appendices count towards the 4,000-word limit?
faqs.answer: Footnotes count when they carry content or explanation, and do not count when they contain only a reference. Appendices do not count, but examiners are not required to read them, so analysis placed in an appendix is analysis that will not be marked. The title page, contents page, bibliography, reference list, maps, charts, diagrams and raw data tables also sit outside the count. The reflections have their own separate ceiling of 500 words in total. Check the current rules in the Extended Essay guide before cutting anything, because students who cut without checking almost always remove analysis they did not need to lose.

faqs.question: How are the three reflections assessed and how long should they be?
faqs.answer: They carry Criterion E, worth six of the 34 marks, and the three together are capped at 500 words. They are assessed on engagement with the research process, which in practice means decisions rather than activities: what was intended, what went wrong, what changed as a result. Writing all three in one sitting near submission is the most common error, because retrospective reflections read as though nothing ever changed and examiners recognise that immediately. Write each one close to the session it records. A tutor can explain what the criterion rewards and point out where a sentence describes instead of deciding, but the words must be the student's own.

faqs.question: What mark range does a grade A Extended Essay need?
faqs.answer: The published bands are A at 27 to 34 marks, B at 21 to 26, C at 14 to 20, D at 7 to 13 and E at 0 to 6, out of the 34 available. Confirm the current table against the Extended Essay guide your school holds. The useful feature of those bands is their width: a six-mark swing, which is four marks gained in critical thinking plus two in engagement, crosses a boundary from most starting positions. That is why criterion-level diagnosis is worth more than general feedback - it tells you which four marks are realistically available in the time left.

faqs.question: Is a grade E in the Extended Essay enough to fail the whole diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes. A grade E in the Extended Essay, like a grade E in Theory of Knowledge, is a failing condition for the IB Diploma whatever the subject points total. Because E covers 0 to 6 marks out of 34, reaching it requires something substantial to have gone wrong - a non-submission, an essay significantly outside the registered subject, or a project that never developed past a first draft. It happens most often to students who lose the summer between DP1 and DP2 and then run out of term. If a supervisor signals that risk, escalate it with the school immediately rather than booking tutoring and hoping.

faqs.question: Which subject should my son choose for his Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: One he is taking, is reasonably strong in, and where the question he wants to ask can actually be researched with sources or data he can reach. Those three conditions eliminate most bad choices. Science routes depend on laboratory access, which in many Dubai schools is limited, so a database or literature question is frequently the honest option rather than a compromise. History needs historiography available in a language he reads. World Studies has a high ceiling and a high failure rate, because it requires two subjects to inform each other rather than sit in separate halves. The supervisor has the final word on registration.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Chemistry Extended Essay if our school limits laboratory time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that constraint is usually the first thing a session addresses. Limited laboratory access in Dubai schools pushes students towards questions built on published data, computational work or a literature base, and those can score at the top of the range provided the evaluation of source reliability is real. What fails is an experimental question designed around laboratory time the school was never going to grant - Criterion A collapses and Criterion C has nothing to work with. Redesigning the question around available evidence early is far cheaper than discovering the problem in the second term of DP2.

faqs.question: Will using a tutor create an academic honesty problem for the essay?
faqs.answer: Not if the boundary is kept, and the boundary is clear. A tutor may teach research method, explain the criteria, question a draft, point out where a paragraph reports instead of evaluating, explain citation conventions and rehearse the concluding interview. A tutor may not supply the research question, write or rewrite any part of the essay, restructure the student's text for them, or draft the reflections. Our test is whether the student could produce and explain every sentence themselves. Tell the supervisor a tutor is reading drafts; the schools we deal with are comfortable with it when the record shows the work developing.

faqs.question: When should the Extended Essay actually be started in a Dubai school year?
faqs.answer: Subject and topic late in DP1, question settled before the summer, and the bulk of the reading done across that summer. In Dubai this matters more than elsewhere because many families travel for six or seven weeks, so a student who leaves without a settled question returns with nothing done and one crowded term remaining. The DP2 autumn then collides with internal assessment deadlines in several subjects and, in some years, Ramadan. Your supervisor sets the internal deadlines and they are the ones to plan backwards from; we build a schedule that marks the weeks you already know will be lost.

faqs.question: What happens in the viva voce and can my child prepare for it?
faqs.answer: It is the concluding interview with the supervisor, held after the final version is submitted, and it is the basis of the third reflection. The student talks about what they researched, what proved difficult, what they would do differently and what they learned about the process. It also allows the supervisor to confirm the work is the student's own. Preparation is legitimate and simple: rehearse talking about real decisions rather than rehearsing a script. A student who has worked honestly finds it straightforward, which is one more reason the version history and the reflections are worth keeping properly as you go.

faqs.question: How much does Extended Essay help cost in Dubai, by stage?
faqs.answer: Market rates as of October 2026, published by the providers named: a research question clinic at the mid-market online band of AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IB from AED 200; draft reading at specialist rates of AED 200-450 or more, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate 200-450+; reflections, viva and final-cut work back at AED 150-300. In-home equivalents run AED 180-500 with travel inside the rate. Premium tutors marketed on examiner experience reach AED 650. Those are market figures rather than our prices; ours is quoted after the free trial, and ask any provider whether VAT is included.

faqs.question: Does the Extended Essay count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth being exact because some pages imply otherwise. Equivalency is a government process with its own requirements. For the British track, the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E. For the American track, English is satisfied by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 in reading and writing, and mathematics by SAT Math 450 or above. No verified IB points threshold is published here; read it on moe.gov.ae or ask your school's counsellor. We describe the process and never perform or guarantee it.

faqs.question: Can my child have Extended Essay sessions while we are abroad for the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the DP1 summer is the single most productive block for this component. Because lessons are online, a standing slot moves with the family to another time zone rather than stopping for seven weeks. Summer work is well suited to what the essay needs at that point: source gathering, reading notes organised against the question, and a first attempt at a structure. Returning to Dubai in late August with a draft section written is a different DP2 from returning with a topic. We do not send tutors to a UAE address - home visits are an India-only service - so nothing about travel interrupts the arrangement.

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tutor.closingHeading: Send the question first, the draft second
dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tutor.closingBody: The most useful thing you can do today takes five minutes: send your child's research question exactly as it currently stands, the essay subject, and the supervisor's next internal deadline. Book the free trial and bring whatever draft exists, however rough. You will leave that session with a criterion-by-criterion score out of 34, the name of the criterion costing the most marks, and two changes that would move it. If the answer is that the question needs narrowing and nothing else, we will tell you that and you can act on it without buying a block. If more is needed, you will see the recommended hours before paying anything.

intro.heading: Start from the symptom, not from the rubric
paragraphs: Most families looking for Extended Essay help in Dubai are holding a draft and a problem they cannot name. The student has put in real hours, the essay is the right length, the supervisor has written something short and encouraging, and a mock grade has come back lower than anyone expected. Reading the criteria at that point rarely helps, because criteria are written for examiners rather than for parents. What helps is working backwards from what the draft actually looks like on the page.

That diagnostic route works because weak Extended Essays fail in a small number of recognisable ways. The question is a topic rather than a question. The essay reports what sources say instead of arguing with them. The method is described once in the introduction and never again. The conclusion restates the introduction. The reflections read as administration. Each of those symptoms maps onto a specific criterion, and the mapping is stable enough that an experienced reader can usually identify the problem in the first two pages.

The marks make the stakes clear. The Extended Essay carries 34 marks across five criteria, lettered A to E, and they are not evenly weighted: critical thinking is the largest single block by a wide margin, which is why an essay that is well organised, correctly referenced and genuinely hard-working can still land in the lower bands. Confirm the current allocations against the Extended Essay guide your school's coordinator holds, since the rubric is revised periodically and a figure from an older cohort is worse than no figure at all.

What a session can do depends heavily on when it happens, and this page is explicit about that rather than optimistic. An hour spent on the research question in the first fortnight changes the ceiling of the whole essay. The same hour spent two weeks before a school's internal deadline cannot change the ceiling at all; it can lift presentation, tighten the argument's visible structure, and rescue the reflections, which is worth having and is not the same thing. Saying so costs billable hours and is the difference between help and reassurance.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft on screen and annotated while the student watches. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For a 4,000-word research essay that is the better arrangement anyway: the whole object of the work is a document, screen-sharing shows exactly which sentence is being questioned, and a Dubai family can choose a reader who knows their subject group rather than one who happens to live within a short drive of their community, which in a city this size is a meaningful difference.
bullets: Five criteria, 34 marks, with critical thinking carrying the largest block
Diagnosis organised by what a draft looks like, not by rubric language
An honest statement of what an hour cannot fix at each stage

Nothing written for the student: every word submitted is their own

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The Extended Essay belongs to the Diploma core, but what a student brings to it was formed earlier. The programmes below set the research habits a Dubai student arrives with, and each note names the habit that causes trouble in a 4,000-word essay.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate submits one Extended Essay of up to 4,000 words on a self-chosen research question, registered in a subject and supervised by a member of school staff. It is externally assessed against five criteria and contributes, with Theory of Knowledge, to the core points on the Diploma. The three reflection sessions with the supervisor are part of the assessment rather than a formality.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set their own internal deadlines, usually well ahead of the IB upload, and those dates are the ones that govern a family's planning. Ask the coordinator for the internal schedule in writing at the start of DP1; the commonest cause of a rushed essay in this city is a family working to the wrong date.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP Personal Project trains a student to plan, document and reflect on an extended piece of independent work, which is the closest preparation the IB offers for the Extended Essay. Students who took it seriously arrive able to keep a process journal. The habit it does not build is argument: the Personal Project rewards process, and the Extended Essay rewards a contested claim defended with evidence.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a large number of IB continuum schools, so a substantial share of Diploma candidates here have completed a Personal Project. Those students generally handle the reflections well and the critical thinking criterion badly, which is a useful thing to know before buying any hours at all.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE rewards accurate recall and well-structured answers to questions somebody else has set. Nothing in it requires a student to design a question, select a method, or decide which sources deserve trust. That is the gap: students arriving from a British-curriculum Year 11 write fluent, organised essays that report rather than argue, and the critical thinking criterion is where the shortfall appears.
programmes.countryNote: UK curriculum accounts for 37 per cent of enrolment across Dubai's private schools, making this the commonest starting point in the emirate. One hour spent in the first fortnight on what a research question must do saves a great deal later, because the question sets the ceiling for every criterion that follows.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together determine the Diploma core points, and the two reward overlapping habits: a controlled claim, evidence handled honestly, limitations acknowledged. CAS competes for the same evenings without feeding the essay at all. Mapping all three against the school's internal deadlines is part of any sensible plan for DP2.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai schools the Extended Essay internal deadline and the heaviest internal assessment weeks frequently land in the same half-term, which is the February crunch families describe. The clash is visible in October and almost invisible once it has arrived.

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: An Extended Essay is registered in a subject, and the commonest failures differ sharply between them. The notes below name what tends to go wrong in each subject group as Dubai students actually attempt it, which is a better guide to subject choice than a list of popular topics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Strong essays rest on data the student generated or sourced defensibly. The usual failure in Dubai schools is a question requiring laboratory conditions the school cannot supply, which produces a literature review wearing an experimental title and a weak method section.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Fieldwork and ethical constraints bite early. Essays fail when the question is answerable only with human subjects or protected sites, or when a small sample is treated as though it settles a question, which the critical thinking criterion punishes directly.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Questions are often either trivially answerable from textbooks or well beyond school apparatus. The marks sit in a question narrow enough to measure and an honest treatment of uncertainty, which students tend to leave as an appendix rather than as part of the argument.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A popular choice in Dubai and a frequent source of a descriptive essay. The failure is a question about an event rather than about an economic relationship, so the essay narrates a market and never applies theory as a tool of analysis.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Access to a real organisation is the strength and the trap. Essays weaken when primary access replaces analysis and the result reads as a consultancy report, or when a single interview is presented as evidence for a general claim about a sector.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source evaluation is the whole subject, and the commonest failure is a question too recent for a historical treatment or too broad to argue in 4,000 words. Strong essays narrow to a single contested interpretation and test it against sources that disagree.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Widely chosen and heavily literature-based. The weakness is an essay that summarises studies in sequence without evaluating method, sample or inference; the criterion rewarding critical thinking is where that pattern loses the most marks.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Needs a question about how a text works rather than about what it means. Essays stall when the student chooses a theme they admire and assembles agreement, producing appreciation rather than analysis and leaving the examiner nothing to be persuaded of.

subjects.name: World Studies
subjects.description: An ambitious option requiring a genuine issue of global significance examined through two disciplines. It rewards the strongest students and exposes the weakest, because an essay that uses two subjects loosely scores worse than a focused single-subject essay would have.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Chosen less often and frequently misjudged. The essay must do mathematics rather than describe it, with the student's own working at its centre, and the commonest failure is an exposition of a known result with no personal investigation inside it.

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-online-tutor.regionsIntro: What constrains an Extended Essay in Dubai is practical: access to data, access to a library or laboratory, and the hours in an evening once the commute is paid for. The notes below record what actually shapes essay work in each area.

regions.name: Dubai Academic City
regions.note: University campuses nearby, which matters for essays needing journal access or a subject expert to approach politely. Students here have an advantage in Economics and Psychology questions that depend on literature a school library will not hold.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Dense commercial district with real organisations within reach, which suits Business Management and Economics essays built on primary access. The risk is an essay that becomes a report about one company, so the analytical frame has to be fixed before any interview is arranged.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Apartment living with little quiet space and long evenings of extracurricular commitments. The practical constraint on essay work here is uninterrupted writing time rather than resources, which makes weekend blocks more productive than weekday hours.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Several large IB schools within a few kilometres, with varying laboratory and library provision. Families here are the most likely to discover mid-project that the school cannot supply the apparatus a science question assumes, which is a question problem rather than a school problem.

regions.name: Jumeirah
regions.note: Close to the oldest selective schools, where supervision tends to be well organised and internal deadlines are enforced. Essays from this area more often fail on an over-ambitious question than on a missed deadline, which is a different and more expensive failure.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer schools and families often funding two subjects at once. The useful intervention here is early and cheap: one hour on the research question in the first fortnight, rather than a block of hours once a draft exists.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Long school runs compress the evening, so essay work concentrates into weekends and holidays. Students here benefit most from a planning hour that puts the research question and the data collection ahead of the reading, because reading expands to fill whatever time exists.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Alserkal Avenue
regions.note: The city's arts and independent-studio district, which gives Visual Arts, Theatre and some World Studies essays access to practitioners and live work. Primary observation is genuinely available here and it strengthens exactly the criterion most essays are weak on.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh, Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Established selective schools with structured supervision and firm internal deadlines. Students here usually arrive with a workable schedule and an over-ambitious question, so the useful hour goes on narrowing scope rather than on scheduling.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Dubai Hills and Umm Al Sheif
schoolClusters.note: Large IB continuum schools where many candidates completed an MYP Personal Project. That cohort handles the reflections and the documentation well and tends to lose marks on argument, which is a specific and fixable diagnosis.

schoolClusters.city: Academic City, Mirdif and Al Warqa
schoolClusters.note: Big year groups, long commutes and proximity to university libraries. Essay work here concentrates into weekends, and the commonest avoidable loss is a strong draft undermined by reflections written in a single sitting the night before submission.

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-online-tutor.modesIntro: Extended Essay support is bought in four shapes, each matched to a stage of the project. All run one-to-one over live video with the draft shared on screen, and each one states what is returned in writing.

modes.title: Question clinic, first fortnight
modes.description: A single hour spent attacking a proposed research question until it either survives or is replaced. The tutor tests whether it is answerable in 4,000 words, whether the evidence exists and can be reached from Dubai, and whether a reasonable person could disagree with the answer. The highest-leverage hour in the whole project.

modes.description: One hour in which an existing draft is read as an examiner reads it and returned with a written diagnosis: the symptoms present, the criterion each one damages, and three prioritised changes ranked by marks at risk. Families use this when supervisor feedback has been brief or when a mock grade arrived unexplained.

modes.title: Staged supervision block
modes.description: Four to six hours spread across the project at the points where decisions are taken: question, method, first full draft, and the reflections. Deliberately not weekly, because the work between sessions is the student's own research and writing, and paying for company during it adds nothing.

The reflections carry marks of their own and reward genuine evidence of a changing process, which cannot be manufactured the night before.

sections.heading: What goes wrong in an Extended Essay, and what it costs
paragraphs: An IB DP Extended Essay online tutor in Dubai spends most of the first hour on diagnosis, because the symptoms in a draft are more informative than anything the student can say about it. A student rarely knows what is wrong with their own essay; they know it took a long time. An experienced reader looks for a short list of patterns and usually finds one of them inside two pages. The table below sets out the five that recur, the criterion each damages, and what a single hour does about it.

The most expensive of them is the first: a research question that is really a topic. The Impact of Social Media on Teenagers is a subject area, not a question, and an essay built on it can only survey. Because the question governs focus, method, the depth of knowledge a student can demonstrate and the amount of genuine argument available, a weak question suppresses four of the five criteria simultaneously. It is also the cheapest fault to fix in week one and the most expensive in month six.

The second most common is an essay that reports its sources. Students in Dubai schools are generally well trained in research and badly trained in disagreement, so the draft politely summarises five authors in sequence and concludes that the matter is complex. The criterion rewarding critical thinking carries the largest single block of marks on the whole essay, and it specifically rewards weighing evidence, identifying limitations and taking a defended position. A summary, however thorough, cannot score there.

Read the table as a triage tool rather than as a rubric. Identify the symptom, see which criterion it damages, then decide whether there is time to address the cause or only the consequence. That decision is the real content of a first session, and a tutor who tells a family in March that the question can still be rebuilt is being kind rather than useful.

sections.heading: The research question sets the ceiling before any research happens
paragraphs: Three tests decide whether a research question will carry an Extended Essay, and all three can be applied in ten minutes. Is it answerable in 4,000 words, or would a competent answer need a book? Does the evidence exist, and can a student in Dubai actually reach it? Could a reasonable, informed person disagree with the answer? A question that fails any of the three will cap the essay regardless of how much work follows, and students fail them in predictable ways.

The first failure is scale. Students choose questions that span a century, a country or an entire literature, because breadth feels safe and specificity feels risky. The opposite is true. An essay examining one measurable relationship in one defined context has room to establish method, present evidence and argue; an essay surveying a field has room only to introduce it. Narrowing is the single most common instruction a good supervisor gives and the one students resist hardest.

The second is access. A Dubai student can reach a great deal — university libraries in Academic City, organisations in Business Bay, practitioners in Al Quoz — and cannot reach some things at all. A question requiring a controlled laboratory environment a school does not have, or human subjects who cannot ethically be used, or archive material held in another country, is unworkable however interesting. Testing access before the reading starts is an hour that saves a month.

The third is arguability. If the answer is already settled in every source the student will read, there is nothing to think critically about and the heaviest criterion is closed off. This is why the strongest essays often look narrow and slightly awkward: they sit at a point where the evidence genuinely pulls in two directions. Students need permission to choose a question like that, and that permission is most of what the first session provides.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go missing, by subject group
paragraphs: The five criteria are the same in every subject, but the way students lose marks against them is strongly subject-specific, and knowing the pattern in advance is worth more than a generic checklist. The table below records what tends to go wrong in the subjects Dubai students choose most, what the examiner is looking for instead, and what remains fixable late, which is the column families need in February.

Science essays fail disproportionately on access rather than on ability. A question assuming apparatus or sample sizes a school cannot provide turns into a literature review with an experimental title, and the method criterion suffers accordingly. The honest move, taken early, is to choose a question answerable with available means; taken late, the only remaining option is to present the limits of the method explicitly and argue within them, which recovers something rather than nothing.

Humanities essays fail on scope and on the absence of disagreement. Economics questions about an event rather than a relationship produce narrative; History questions about a period rather than a contested interpretation produce survey; Psychology essays assemble studies without evaluating method or sample. All three are versions of the same fault, and all three are partially recoverable late, because reorganising existing material around a contested claim can be done inside a fortnight.

World Studies deserves a separate warning. It asks for a genuine issue of global significance examined through two disciplines, and it rewards ambitious students handsomely. It also punishes loose execution harder than any single-subject registration, because an essay using two subjects superficially scores below the focused single-subject essay the student could have written instead. Choose it on the strength of the question, not on the appeal of the label.

sections.heading: The reflections and the supervisor: marks most families never look at
paragraphs: Three reflection sessions with the supervisor are built into the Extended Essay process, and the student's written record of them is assessed. Families consistently treat this as paperwork, and students consistently fill it in retrospectively in one sitting shortly before submission. Both are mistakes, because the criterion rewarding engagement looks for evidence of a process that genuinely changed: a question narrowed, a method abandoned, a source that forced a rethink.

Retrospective reflections are easy to spot and hard to fake. They describe a smooth project in which everything went to plan, because that is what hindsight produces, and the examiner reads a student who did not encounter difficulty as a student who did not engage. A student who records, in the moment, that their first three sources all agreed and that they went looking for opposition has handed the examiner exactly the evidence the criterion asks for.

The supervisor's role is bounded in ways families should understand. A supervisor guides, holds the reflection sessions, confirms authenticity and comments on the work within the limits the Extended Essay guide sets; the amount of permitted comment on a draft is defined and is smaller than most students expect. That boundary is a reason to use an external reader, not a complaint about schools: a supervisor who cannot annotate a whole draft is following the rules, and a family who understands that stops interpreting brief feedback as indifference.

The concluding interview at the end of the process is also worth preparing for, in the narrow sense of being able to talk about one's own work. A student who can say what they would do differently, which source they trusted least and why, and where the argument is weakest is demonstrating engagement and authenticity at once. Rehearsing those answers is legitimate; supplying them is not, and the difference is visible to anybody who has sat through both.

sections.heading: The 4,000 words, and structural faults that look like style
paragraphs: The essay itself is limited to 4,000 words, and examiners are not required to read beyond it. What counts towards that total and what sits outside it is defined in the Extended Essay guide and includes rules on the abstract, contents, references, appendices and material in tables, so check the current version with your school's coordinator rather than relying on a figure circulating online. The practical consequence is simple: an essay 1,200 words over the limit is not a long essay, it is an essay whose last section may never be read.

Several faults that students experience as writing problems are really structural, and they are worth separating because the fixes differ. An essay that feels repetitive usually has no argumentative sequence, so each section restates the thesis instead of advancing it. An essay that feels thin usually has a question too broad for the available space. An essay that feels disorganised often has the method buried in the middle rather than established early and applied throughout.

Appendices are the commonest place a good essay quietly loses marks. Students move material there when the word count tightens, including analysis the argument depends on. Examiners are not obliged to treat appendix material as part of the argument, so an essay whose reasoning lives in Appendix C has hidden its best work. If something is load-bearing, it belongs inside the 4,000 words, and something else has to go.

Presentation carries its own marks, and they are the easiest on the paper to secure. Consistent referencing in one recognised style, a readable contents page, figures labelled and referred to in the text, and a reference list matching the citations is a checklist rather than a skill. It is also the part of the essay most often left to the final evening in Dubai schools, where the internal deadline and the heaviest internal assessment weeks tend to collide.

sections.heading: What one session can fix, stage by stage
paragraphs: The honest answer to what an hour achieves depends entirely on when the hour happens, and the table below sets that out explicitly, including the column saying what the hour cannot do. Families deciding whether to buy support in February deserve that column more than they deserve encouragement, and providers paid by the hour have no reason to supply it.

Early sessions change ceilings. A question clinic in the first fortnight can replace an unworkable question with a workable one, which raises the maximum mark available on four criteria at once. A method session before data collection can prevent an essay that cannot answer its own question. Neither of these can be recreated later: by the time a full draft exists, the question and the method are sunk costs and the work shifts to extracting the best available mark from what the student has.

Late sessions change execution. A diagnostic read two weeks before an internal deadline can reorganise an argument around a contested claim, rewrite a conclusion from the evidence actually presented, rescue reflections that were going to be filled in retrospectively, and tidy presentation to secure the marks that are simply there for the taking. That is a real improvement and it is not the same as a different essay. Describing it accurately is the point.

There is one stage where the right advice is to buy nothing. The middle months, after the question is settled and before a full draft exists, are reading, data collection and writing, and all of it is the student's own work. A weekly paid hour through that period produces conversation and a slightly guilty student. Checkpoints at decisions, with silence in between, consistently produce better essays for less money.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, the one thing a tutor must never touch
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is where academic honesty is tested hardest, because it is long, it is done largely out of sight, and the market contains people willing to sell a finished document. One provider researched for this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Under IB rules the consequence of submitting work that is not the student's own falls on the student, and it can reach the loss of the Diploma. No price makes that a reasonable trade.

The boundary for a tutor is narrow and entirely workable. A tutor may read, diagnose, question, explain a criterion, model a move on a different example, challenge a claim, and record what was discussed. A tutor may not put sentences into the student's document, choose the question on the student's behalf, restructure the text themselves, or supply the content of a reflection. Everything a school uploads must be written by the student, and a dated sequence of the student's own drafts is the simplest possible evidence that it was.

Two further restraints are worth stating plainly because competitors breach them. Past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge or Pearson; a legitimate provider cites and links them rather than distributing copies. And no tutoring provider should attach the name of a regulator — KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education — or of an examination board to language about approval, accreditation or authorisation unless it holds that permit and can show the number. IB Gram holds none and implies none.

Families should also know who may lawfully teach their child. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, any amount quoted to you is unverified. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules additionally bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school.

sections.heading: Dubai practicalities: data access, the calendar, and what the market charges
paragraphs: Dubai is a good city in which to research an Extended Essay, provided the question is chosen to suit it. University libraries in Academic City, a dense commercial sector within reach for Business and Economics questions, an arts district with working practitioners, and a school system of real scale — 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, according to the Dubai Media Office — all give a student material that does not exist in a textbook. What Dubai does not reliably give is specialised laboratory capacity in a school, which is why science questions need an access check early.

The calendar matters as much as the resources. Dubai school internal deadlines sit well ahead of the IB upload, Ramadan shortens the school day and shifts the household rhythm, and a large share of families travel for several weeks in summer. The summer between DP1 and DP2 is therefore both the best uninterrupted research window a student will get and the period when any arrangement depending on physical attendance collapses. Online delivery survives it, and sessions move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan on request.

This page does not publish an IB examination or results date. The IB's own site cannot be verified by automated checking, and an unconfirmed date on a page used for planning is worse than none; UAE schools sit the May session and your coordinator holds the current timetable and the internal deadlines that actually bind. Where dates are published and sourced, they show why early entry matters in every system: Cambridge's March 2027 series runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, its November 2026 timetable ending 19 November 2026.

On cost, published Dubai market rates are wide and worth knowing before any conversation. Budget online platforms advertise from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists run from about AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table showing AED 200 to AED 450 or more. In-home visits, where travel is inside the rate, run roughly AED 180 to AED 500, and premium named tutoring reaches AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Those are other providers' figures read in October 2026, not our price list. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in the UAE at all: Dubai sessions are one-to-one over live video, and the first diagnostic hour is free with no card required.

process.title: Send the draft and the internal deadline
process.description: Share whatever exists — a question, a plan, a part-draft or a full one — along with the subject of registration and the school's internal deadline rather than the IB date. Those two facts decide what is still possible, and most families send the second one wrongly because nobody told them the dates differ.

process.title: The free diagnostic hour
process.description: One hour, online and one-to-one, with no card required. The draft is read beforehand and returned with a written diagnosis: the symptoms present, the criterion each damages, and three changes ranked by marks at risk. If the honest finding is that the supervisor has it in hand, the document says so.

process.title: Decide between ceiling work and execution work
process.description: Early in the project the question and method can still be changed, which lifts the maximum mark available. Late in the project they cannot, and the work is extracting the best mark from what exists. The plan names which of the two you are buying, because conflating them is how families end up disappointed.

process.title: Checkpoints at decisions, silence in between
process.description: Sessions are placed at the question, the method, the first full draft and the reflections, not weekly. The reading, the data collection and the writing between them are the student's own work, and paying for company during that stretch adds cost without adding marks.

process.title: A final pass on the marks simply available
process.description: One hour before submission on referencing consistency, figure labelling, appendix placement and whether the reflections evidence a real process. These are the cheapest marks on the paper and the ones most often lost in the week when internal assessment deadlines collide with the essay.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before advice

The middle months are reading and writing the student must do alone, and we recommend buying nothing during them.

Finished coursework is sold in this market, and under IB rules the consequence of submitting it falls on the candidate, up to the loss of the Diploma.

whyPoints.description: A Chemistry essay and a World Studies essay fail in different ways, and a reader who knows the subject group spots the pattern in two pages. Online delivery means a Dubai family selects on that rather than on proximity, which is the whole practical argument for the format in a document-based component.

faqs.question: What is the first thing an examiner notices about a weak Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: The title. If it names a topic rather than asking a question, the examiner already knows the essay will survey rather than argue, and the focus criterion is compromised before the first page. The second thing is whether the introduction states a method and the body then uses it; essays that assert a method once and never return to it read as unplanned. Both are visible in two pages, which is why a diagnostic read is quick and why the first fortnight of the project is worth more attention than the last.

faqs.question: Our daughter's research question is really a topic. How is that fixed?
faqs.answer: By testing candidate questions against three requirements rather than defending the existing one. Is it answerable in 4,000 words? Does the evidence exist and can she reach it from Dubai? Could an informed person disagree with the answer? Usually two or three narrower questions emerge from the same topic and one of them survives all three tests. Done in the first fortnight this takes an hour and raises the ceiling on four criteria. Done once a full draft exists, the question is a sunk cost and only the framing of the argument can change.

faqs.question: Which criterion do Dubai students lose most marks on?
faqs.answer: Critical thinking, by a clear margin, and it carries the largest block of marks on the essay. Students here are generally well trained in research and poorly trained in disagreement, so a draft summarises several authors competently and concludes that the issue is complex. The criterion rewards weighing evidence, naming limitations and taking a defended position. Converting two summary sections into evaluation is the single highest-value late intervention available. Confirm the current mark allocations with your school's Extended Essay coordinator, since the guide is revised from time to time.

faqs.question: Can an online session really change a 4,000-word essay in one hour?
faqs.answer: It can change a specific thing, and the honest version names which. An hour early in the project can replace an unworkable research question, which lifts the maximum mark available across several criteria. An hour on a complete draft can reorganise the argument around a contested claim, rewrite a conclusion from the evidence actually presented, and move load-bearing material out of an appendix. What an hour cannot do late is raise a ceiling the question has already set. Any provider who implies otherwise is selling reassurance.

faqs.question: My son's essay reads like a summary of his sources. What is missing?
faqs.answer: Disagreement. A summary essay treats sources as a body of knowledge to be relayed; an argumentative essay treats them as witnesses to be cross-examined. The fix is structural rather than stylistic: identify a point where two credible sources pull in different directions, build a body section around weighing them, and state what the student concludes and why. Two sections rebuilt this way usually move more marks than a full rewrite, because the heaviest criterion rewards exactly that move and currently has nothing to score.

faqs.question: Is a Chemistry Extended Essay realistic if our school limits laboratory access?
faqs.answer: Only if the question is chosen to fit what is available, and that decision belongs at the start. A question assuming apparatus or controlled conditions the school cannot supply produces a literature review with an experimental title, and the method criterion suffers accordingly. Workable alternatives include questions answerable with simple apparatus, with secondary datasets handled rigorously, or with a computational approach. If the draft already exists and the access was never there, the remaining move is to state the method's limits explicitly and argue inside them.

faqs.question: What does an examiner mean by critical engagement with sources?
faqs.answer: That the student has judged the sources rather than collected them. Concretely: noting who produced a piece of evidence and why that matters, identifying what a study's sample or method does not support, preferring one account over another with a stated reason, and acknowledging what the essay's own evidence cannot settle. It is a habit rather than a section, and it should appear throughout the body. An essay that confines evaluation to a paragraph near the end has demonstrated awareness of the requirement rather than the requirement itself.

faqs.question: Our school's internal deadline has passed and the essay is unfinished. What now?
faqs.answer: Speak to the Extended Essay coordinator first, today, because internal deadlines and the school's own submission arrangements are theirs to manage and they will have seen this before. Then triage what exists: secure the presentation marks, rewrite the conclusion from the evidence actually present, convert one summary section into evaluation, and make sure the reflections record the real process including the difficulty. A late essay that argues something is worth considerably more than a complete essay that surveys, and that is where the remaining hours should go.

faqs.question: How many sources should an Extended Essay use?
faqs.answer: There is no required number, and chasing one is a common way to weaken an essay. What matters is whether the sources are appropriate to the question, handled critically, and genuinely used rather than listed. Twelve sources evaluated carefully will outscore forty summarised. In the sciences and mathematics the balance shifts towards the student's own data and working, where the essay must show investigation rather than exposition. Reference consistently in one recognised style and ensure every citation appears in the reference list; those are marks available for simple care.

faqs.question: Must the Extended Essay be registered in a subject my child already studies?
faqs.answer: Schools normally require registration in a subject the student takes, and some permit exceptions, so this is a question for the Extended Essay coordinator rather than for a tutor. What is reliably true is that an essay in an unfamiliar subject carries real risk: the student has to acquire the discipline's conventions, its standards of evidence and its way of arguing while also doing the research. Where the subject is available to them, choosing it on the strength of a good question is a safer basis than the appeal of an unusual registration.

faqs.question: Why do strong students lose marks in the reflections?
faqs.answer: Because they write them retrospectively, in one sitting, and hindsight produces a smooth account of a project that went to plan. The criterion rewarding engagement looks for evidence of a process that genuinely changed: a question narrowed, a method abandoned, a source that forced a rethink. A student who records in the moment that their first three sources all agreed, and that they then went looking for opposition, has supplied exactly what the examiner wants. Keeping brief dated notes throughout costs nothing and is difficult to reconstruct afterwards.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us what grade the essay will get?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who does is describing something nobody can deliver. An external examiner applies the criteria to the final submission, grade boundaries are set by the IB, and the essay forms part of the Diploma core alongside Theory of Knowledge. What an experienced reader can give is a judgement about where a draft currently sits against each criterion and which changes would move it, stated as a diagnosis rather than a prediction. Treat any promise of a particular grade, points total or improvement as a reason for scepticism rather than confidence.

faqs.question: What should my child have ready for a first Extended Essay session?
faqs.answer: Four things. The current question or title exactly as written. Whatever draft or plan exists, however rough and in whatever state. Any written comment the supervisor has given, because the permitted scope of that comment is limited and knowing what was said avoids repeating it. And the school's internal deadline, not the IB date. With those four the hour goes entirely on diagnosis, and a written statement of position comes back the same day rather than after a second session spent gathering context.

faqs.question: Does an Extended Essay tutor need to know my child's subject?
faqs.answer: For diagnosis, subject-group familiarity matters a great deal, because the failures are subject-specific: a Physics essay fails differently from a History essay and the fix is different too. For the generic marks — argument sequence, conclusion, referencing, appendix placement, reflections — a strong research-writing reader can work across subjects. Ask directly which subject groups a tutor has supervised or examined. Paying a specialist rate for someone meeting the discipline's conventions for the first time alongside your child is a poor trade and it happens in this market.

faqs.question: Can an Extended Essay tutor meet my child in person somewhere in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not arrange in-person tutoring anywhere in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we offer only in India. Dubai Extended Essay support is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft shared on screen and annotated while the student watches. For a component whose entire output is a document that is the stronger arrangement: the family chooses a reader who knows the subject group rather than one who lives nearby, and the arrangement survives summer travel.

Send the question, whatever draft exists and the school's internal deadline, and take the free diagnostic hour. You will receive a written statement of what the draft shows, which criterion each symptom damages, and three changes ranked by the marks they put at risk — including an honest note on anything the question has already made impossible. Act on it with us or without us; several families do exactly that and book nothing further.

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below have supervised or examined Extended Essays in specific Diploma subjects. We match by subject rather than by general essay experience, because a Biology research question fails for different reasons than a History one does.

intro.heading: Four thousand words, forty hours, and the one Diploma component with no lessons
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is a piece of independent research of up to 4,000 words, written in a subject the student chooses, with roughly forty hours of their own work behind it. There is no class, no syllabus and no past paper. A supervisor is allocated by the school and the IB recommends a total of three to five hours of supervision across the whole project, including three mandatory reflection sessions. For most students it is the first time they have been asked to produce something substantial with no weekly structure, and that is precisely why it goes wrong.

The marks are distributed in a way that surprises almost every family. Thirty-four marks are available across five criteria: focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and engagement. Critical thinking alone carries twelve of the thirty-four. Presentation carries four. A beautifully formatted essay with a full bibliography, a title page and consistent referencing that merely reports what the sources say is collecting from the smallest criterion and leaving the largest untouched.

The grade is then combined with Theory of Knowledge on a published matrix for up to three points towards the 45-point Diploma total, and a grade E in the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the Diploma regardless of subject grades. That makes it a component where the downside is larger than the upside: three points at best, no Diploma at worst. Dubai families usually discover the second half of that sentence late, often in the final term of DP2, when a supervisor mentions that the draft on file would not currently pass. The component rewards early attention and punishes nothing except being left alone.

The failure pattern is consistent and it is almost never about ability. A research question is chosen in DP1 that is interesting rather than answerable. Data collection or reading drifts over the summer. The first full draft reaches the supervisor at the point where only one comment is permitted, so the supervisor's single piece of feedback is spent on structural problems that should have been fixed months earlier. The reflections on the RPPF are then written in one sitting, which is visible to an examiner and costs marks under engagement.

What coaching does is supply the structure the component deliberately withholds. A specialist in the right subject narrows the research question until it can be answered within the limit, checks that the method can actually produce evidence, marks drafts against the criteria with the marks named rather than described, and keeps the reflection sessions honest and contemporaneous. IB Gram matches and the tutor coaches; the student does the research and writes it. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.programmesIntro: Independent research appears in every IB programme in a different form, and how well a student handled the earlier version predicts a great deal about the Extended Essay. These are the stages we work across.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Extended Essay runs from the second half of DP1 into DP2. The student picks a subject, agrees a research question with an allocated supervisor, carries out the research, and submits up to 4,000 words with a completed Reflections on Planning and Progress Form. Assessment is external, against five criteria worth thirty-four marks in total, and the resulting grade runs from A to E.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary widely in how early they start the process. Some allocate supervisors in January of DP1 and set a hard internal deadline before the summer; others begin after the DP1 examinations. Ask which model your child's school uses, because it changes when outside support is useful by about four months.

programmes.name: The Extended Essay with TOK and CAS
programmes.description: Two of the three core components carry marks and the third is a completion requirement. The Extended Essay is the largest single piece of writing in the Diploma; TOK is two short technically constrained tasks; CAS is portfolio and reflection work with no grade. All three are competing for the same evenings as six subjects' internal assessments.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Extended Essay final deadline frequently lands within a fortnight of subject internal assessment deadlines and university application dates. Students who get a complete draft in before that fortnight have a very different DP2 from those who do not, and the difference is scheduling rather than ability.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP personal project is the clearest precursor: a self-directed piece of work with a supervisor, a process journal and a report, assessed against criteria. Students who kept a genuine process journal in MYP5 usually produce credible RPPF reflections two years later. Students who wrote the journal retrospectively tend to repeat that habit.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a large IB continuum population alongside an even larger British-curriculum intake arriving at Diploma level from IGCSE. The IGCSE group has usually never managed a project of this length, and the first coaching session is about process rather than about content.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme has no Extended Essay. Its core includes the reflective project, which asks the student to examine an ethical dilemma arising from their career-related study. It is shorter than the Extended Essay and assessed against its own criteria, but the research and reflection habits transfer almost completely.
programmes.countryNote: A handful of Dubai schools offer the CP alongside the Diploma. Parents occasionally ask us for Extended Essay support when the component on the registration is the reflective project, so the first thing we confirm is which programme the student is actually enrolled in.

dubai/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.subjectsIntro: An Extended Essay fails in subject-specific ways, which is why we match by subject rather than by general writing ability. These are the subjects Dubai students choose most, with what each one demands and where each one goes wrong.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Popular and risky. A biology essay needs data the student can actually collect or defensible secondary data, plus statistical treatment the student can explain. The classic failure is an ambitious experiment with no controlled variable, run once, in a school laboratory with limited equipment, written up honestly and scoring badly on method.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Works well where the question is narrow and the chemistry is genuinely at Diploma level rather than below it. Common problems are reactions that cannot be run safely in a school laboratory and questions that reduce to a textbook explanation. Access to equipment should decide the question, not the other way round.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Rewards precision and punishes vagueness faster than any other science. A strong physics essay usually has a simple apparatus, a clear relationship to test, and a serious treatment of uncertainty. Essays that model something computationally need the model justified, not just run.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The subject where the critical thinking criterion is hardest to satisfy, because exposition is not evaluation. A mathematics essay needs the student to do something with the mathematics — compare approaches, test a claim, extend a result — rather than explain a known theorem well. It suits students who already read beyond the syllabus.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Needs a question with a real historiographical disagreement behind it and sources the student can reach. Dubai students often choose a topic with excellent regional interest and then find the primary material is not accessible in a language they read. Source availability should be checked before the question is fixed.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Strong when a theory is applied to a specific local market and tested against evidence. Weak when it becomes a description of an industry. A UAE-based question works well because data from official sources is available, provided the student treats the data critically rather than reporting it.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Attractive and heavily constrained: ethical limits on research with human participants mean most essays are literature-based. That is fine, but it raises the bar on critical evaluation of studies — method, sampling, replication — which is exactly where the twelve critical thinking marks sit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Works when the text choice is narrow and the argument is arguable. Students frequently choose three novels and produce a survey. One text, one well-framed question and sustained close analysis scores higher than breadth, and the subject-specific requirement is argument supported by the text itself.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Needs a real organisation and a question the available information can answer. The common failure is an essay about a global company built entirely from its own published material, with no critical distance. A smaller local organisation that will answer questions usually produces a better essay.

subjects.name: World Studies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary option built around a global issue and examined through two Diploma subjects. It can score very well and it is demanding: the integration of the two subjects has to be genuine rather than two halves bolted together, and the global issue must be addressed locally and in a wider frame.

sections.heading: Where the thirty-four Extended Essay marks actually sit
paragraphs: Almost no competitor page in this market publishes the criteria with their mark allocations, and it is the single most useful thing a parent can see. The Extended Essay is marked out of thirty-four across five criteria. Focus and method carries six marks and covers the topic, the research question and the methodology. Knowledge and understanding carries six and covers subject context and correct use of terminology. Critical thinking carries twelve. Presentation carries four. Engagement carries six and is assessed from the reflections on the RPPF.

That distribution explains most disappointing grades. Students allocate effort to the parts they can see: the bibliography, the title page, the contents list, the formatting. Those sit inside the four presentation marks. Meanwhile twelve marks are waiting for analysis, evaluation of evidence, discussion of limitations and a conclusion that follows from the argument rather than restating the introduction. An essay that reports accurately and evaluates nothing has a ceiling it cannot pass however well it is produced.

Engagement is the second misunderstood criterion. Six marks are awarded on the basis of the three reflections recorded on the Reflections on Planning and Progress Form, with a combined limit of 500 words. Reflections written in one sitting at the end read exactly like reflections written in one sitting at the end: they describe what happened rather than showing decisions being taken, difficulties being encountered and the approach changing. Six marks for 500 words is the best rate of return in the Diploma and the part students treat most casually.

When we mark a draft we start with critical thinking and engagement, because that is where twelve plus six of the thirty-four marks are. Presentation gets checked last and takes ten minutes. That order is the opposite of how most students work, and reversing it is often worth more than another month of reading.

sections.heading: The research question is the whole essay, decided in week one
paragraphs: A research question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words will not become answerable later. This is the one decision where outside help pays for itself several times over, because a specialist in the subject can usually tell within twenty minutes whether a question is viable, and a student cannot. The test is not whether the question is interesting. The test is whether a specific, evidenced answer exists and whether this student can reach the evidence in the time they have.

Three shapes of question fail predictably. The survey question invites a description of a field and produces an essay with no argument. The unanswerable question depends on evidence the student cannot obtain, which in Dubai often means primary material held elsewhere or in a language the student does not read. The already-answered question has a textbook answer, so the student can only explain it, which collects knowledge marks and almost no critical thinking marks.

The shape that works is narrow and comparative or evaluative. To what extent does one specific thing explain one specific outcome in one specified context. How does one named variable affect one measured quantity under stated conditions. The narrower the frame, the more room there is inside the word limit for the evaluation that carries twelve marks. Students resist this, because a narrow question feels like a small achievement, and the mark scheme disagrees with them.

Local context helps when it is used properly. A UAE-based economics, business or geography question has data available from official sources and an examiner who has not read forty versions of it. The question still has to be arguable rather than descriptive, and the data still has to be treated critically rather than quoted. A Dubai topic chosen for novelty and handled descriptively scores no better than any other descriptive essay.
bullets: Test evidence availability before fixing the question, not after
Narrow frames leave room for the evaluation that carries twelve marks
