sections.heading: The supervisor, the three reflections and the one permitted comment
paragraphs: The school allocates a supervisor and the IB recommends between three and five hours of supervision in total for the entire project, including the three mandatory reflection sessions. That is the whole formal support a student is entitled to, spread across roughly a year. It is not a shortfall in the school's provision; it is the design of the component, which is meant to be independent research. Understanding that number early changes how a family plans, because three to five hours will not absorb a student's disorganisation.

The supervisor may comment on one complete draft. One. That comment is the most valuable single intervention in the process and it is routinely wasted, because the draft that reaches the supervisor still has structural problems — a question that drifted, a method that produced thin evidence, a conclusion that restates the introduction. The supervisor spends their comment on the structure instead of on refinement, and the student has no further formal feedback. A draft marked against the criteria before it goes to the supervisor changes what that comment can achieve.

The three reflection sessions are assessed. They are recorded on the Reflections on Planning and Progress Form, limited to 500 words in total, and they feed the six engagement marks. The first comes early, around the question and the plan; the second at a mid-point, where the honest content is usually a difficulty and a change of approach; the third concludes the process and is typically accompanied by a short concluding interview, the viva voce. Reflections that record real decisions as they happen score; reflections reconstructed afterwards do not.

Nothing about this requires concealment. Tell the supervisor that your child is working with a tutor. A good supervisor will tell you which stage the student is behind on and what the school's internal deadlines actually are, both of which make outside coaching more useful rather than less.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay calendar, counted backwards from the submission
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a backwards calendar, and it is the artefact that prevents most Extended Essay failures. We count in weeks before the school's own internal final deadline rather than in calendar dates, because Dubai schools set that date anywhere from the start of DP2 to several months into it, and because IB session dates should be confirmed with your child's coordinator rather than taken from a tutoring website.

The structural insight is that the research has to stop long before the writing does. A student still collecting data four weeks out cannot evaluate it properly, and evaluation is where twelve of the thirty-four marks are. Working backwards, the complete draft should reach the supervisor six to eight weeks before the internal deadline, which means the research must be finished ten to twelve weeks out, which means the question must have been fixed and viable before the DP1 summer break.

The summer between DP1 and DP2 is the pivot. Students who go into it with a settled question and a reading list come back able to write. Students who go into it with a topic and good intentions come back having done nothing, which is a completely normal human outcome and the reason the DP1 internal deadline exists at all. If your child's school does not set one, set one at home.

The last four weeks should contain no new research. They contain redrafting, the formatting and referencing check, the third reflection and the viva voce, and the final word-count audit. A student who is still reading in that window is trading twelve critical thinking marks for a few knowledge marks, which is the worst exchange rate in the component.

sections.heading: The 4,000-word limit and the formatting rules that cost marks
paragraphs: The limit is 4,000 words and examiners are not required to read beyond it. An essay of 4,600 words is not a fuller essay; it is a 4,000-word essay whose conclusion was never read. Certain elements sit outside the count — the title page, the contents page, maps, charts, diagrams, tables of statistical data, equations and calculations, references and citations, the bibliography and any appendices — but the argument itself has to live inside the limit, and appendices cannot be used to smuggle argument out of it. An examiner is not obliged to read an appendix at all.

That last point is worth repeating because it produces a specific, avoidable loss. Students who discover the word count problem late move whole sections into appendices. The result is an essay whose evaluation is in a place the examiner need not look, marked as though the evaluation is absent. The correct response to being over the limit is to cut, and cutting is a skill: the first things to go are the literature summary, the methodology narrative and the restatement in the conclusion.

Presentation carries four marks and is the easiest criterion to secure. A title page with the research question, a contents page, numbered pages, consistent referencing in a single style throughout, and tables and figures that are labelled and referred to in the text. The IB does not prescribe a referencing style; it expects one style used consistently. Mixing two styles is the most common presentation error we see, usually because sources were collected at different times with different tools.

Finally, the integrity check. Essays are submitted electronically by the school and checked for academic integrity. Correct citation protects a student who has paraphrased closely; absent citation does not become safe because the source was obscure. Any wording taken from a source belongs in quotation marks with a reference, and material generated by a text tool must be acknowledged according to the school's own policy.

Title page, contents, charts, tables, equations, references and bibliography sit outside the count

sections.heading: What Extended Essay coaching costs in Dubai
paragraphs: Extended Essay support prices as subject-specialist work, because the useful version of it requires someone who knows how a research question fails in that specific subject. The published market in Dubai runs from roughly AED 45-65 an hour, where EdFlik advertises, up to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, which BartyED publishes. Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200. TutorChase shows AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200-450 or above, and in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350. Those are their published figures with their dates, quoted so you can check them.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages. What we publish is the model: a free trial lesson first, one per family, with no card details taken, and the specific tutor's rate agreed in writing before any paid session. For the Extended Essay the sensible purchase is a small number of sessions at the right moments rather than a standing weekly slot across a year. Two or three sessions on the research question in DP1 are worth more than ten sessions in the final month.

Three things move the price. Subject scarcity is the first: a specialist for a Mathematics or World Studies essay is harder to find than one for English or Business Management. Turnaround is the second, because a draft marked inside 48 hours before a deadline is a different service from one marked in a fortnight. The third is stage — deadline triage is priced as specialist work and is also the worst value for money, which we say before taking the booking rather than after.

For context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's economic incentives package. Against a Diploma-year fee, a four-session Extended Essay block is a minor line item. The expensive version is the one bought in week fifty-one.

sections.heading: Online coaching against an in-home Extended Essay tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: Dubai parents search for a home tutor, so here is the honest comparison. An in-home tutor costs more per hour because travel is inside the rate — the published bands put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-350 against AED 150-300 for a qualified online hour. Travel also makes the schedule brittle. During a drafting phase you may want a session moved by two days or a draft read at short notice, and a tutor crossing the city in evening traffic cannot do either.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. That is stated on every UAE page rather than discovered after a booking, because two providers in this market route UAE parents to numbers in another country without saying where the tutor is.

For this component the online format is the better tool rather than the acceptable substitute. The essay lives in a document, so the document is on a shared screen with the criteria beside it, annotated live. Mark allocations are named against the paragraph that earned them. The reflections sit in the same session, so they are written while the decision they describe is still fresh. Drafts and marked versions are kept, which means the progress from draft two to draft four is visible rather than remembered.

The decisive advantage is subject matching. The number of people within driving distance of Mudon who have supervised a Mathematics Extended Essay is close to zero. Online, the question becomes who is available in Gulf Standard Time, which is how a Dubai family gets a subject specialist instead of a generalist who is nearby. For the research question stage, that difference is the difference between a viable question and a year spent on an unviable one.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, permits and what to check before hiring anyone
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is submitted as the student's own independent research under the IB's academic honesty rules. A submission containing material the student did not produce is a malpractice matter, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on whoever supplied it. In this market that warning is concrete rather than theoretical: one site ranking for UAE IB searches openly sells completed Internal Assessments. Any provider offering to supply a finished essay, to rewrite a draft to completion, or to carry out the research on a student's behalf should end the conversation.

The legitimate version is still substantial. A tutor may test a research question, question a method, press on an argument until the student finds its weakness, mark a draft against the five criteria and name the marks, explain why a paragraph collects knowledge marks and no critical thinking marks, and teach a student to cut 600 words without losing the argument. The test we apply is whether the student can explain every change they are about to make. If they cannot, it was not their work.

Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE; official guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

One more boundary. We do not supply IB subject guides, Extended Essay guides, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because they are the IB's copyright. The current guide for your child's session comes from the school's IB coordinator, and a provider who offers to hand it over is telling you how they operate.

faqs.question: How long is the IB Extended Essay and what falls outside the word count?
faqs.answer: The limit is 4,000 words and examiners are not required to read beyond it. Several elements sit outside the count: the title page, the contents page, maps, charts, diagrams, tables of statistical data, equations and calculations, citations and references, the bibliography and any appendices. The argument itself must live inside the limit, and appendices cannot be used to move analysis out of it, because an examiner is not obliged to read an appendix. An essay that runs long is not a fuller essay; it is one whose conclusion may never be read, which is why cutting is a skill worth teaching early.

faqs.question: How many hours should my child expect to spend on the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: The IB recommends about forty hours of student work across the project. Spread over roughly a year that sounds modest, and the problem is never the total but the distribution: most students do five hours in DP1 and thirty-five in the last six weeks, which is the pattern that costs marks under critical thinking and engagement. A realistic shape is two to three hours a fortnight during the research phase, rising to weekly sessions of writing during drafting, with the reading finished ten to twelve weeks before the school's internal deadline.

faqs.question: What are the Extended Essay criteria and how many marks does each carry?
faqs.answer: Five criteria, thirty-four marks in total. Focus and method carries six marks and covers the topic, research question and methodology. Knowledge and understanding carries six. Critical thinking carries twelve — more than a third of the total — and covers analysis, evaluation of evidence and reasoned argument. Presentation carries four, for structure, layout and consistent referencing. Engagement carries six and is judged from the three reflections on the RPPF. The mark total converts to a grade from A to E, which then combines with Theory of Knowledge for up to three Diploma points. Confirm the current allocations with your child's coordinator.

faqs.question: Which subject should my child choose for their Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: The subject in which they can reach evidence, not simply the subject they enjoy most. Three practical filters help. Can the research actually be done here — laboratory equipment, accessible data, sources in a language the student reads? Is there a genuine disagreement or variable to examine, rather than a textbook answer? And is the subject one the student is taking, since knowledge and understanding assumes subject context? A strong essay in a straightforward subject beats an ambitious one in a subject where the student cannot obtain evidence, every time.

faqs.question: What is the RPPF and does it affect the Extended Essay grade?
faqs.answer: The Reflections on Planning and Progress Form records the three mandatory reflection sessions held with the supervisor, with a combined limit of 500 words, and it is the evidence for the engagement criterion worth six marks. Six marks for 500 words is the best rate of return in the component and the part most students treat as paperwork. Reflections that show real decisions — a method that did not work, a question that narrowed, a source that changed the argument — score. Reflections written in one sitting at the end describe events rather than thinking, and an examiner can tell.

faqs.question: How much supervision is a school required to give for the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: The IB recommends a total of three to five hours of supervision for the whole project, including the three mandatory reflection sessions, and the supervisor may comment on one complete draft. That is by design: the component assesses independent research. The practical consequence is that the one permitted draft comment is extremely valuable and is routinely spent on structural problems that could have been solved months earlier. Getting those fixed before the draft goes to the supervisor is the most useful thing external coaching does, and it is worth asking the school for their internal dates in DP1.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child narrow their Extended Essay research question?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the stage where coaching changes the outcome most. A subject specialist can usually judge in one session whether a question is answerable in 4,000 words with evidence the student can reach, and a sixteen-year-old cannot. The work is narrowing: converting a broad interest into a question with a specific, evidenced answer. The decision stays the student's and the final question must be agreed with the school supervisor, who knows the school's requirements. What a tutor contributes is the judgement about viability that otherwise only arrives after six wasted months.

faqs.question: Can a tutor proofread my child's Extended Essay before submission?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach proofreading and point out patterns — an inconsistent referencing style, tables that are never referred to in the text, a conclusion that restates the introduction — and the student then makes every change. What no tutor should do is edit the text to completion or supply replacement sentences, because the essay is submitted as the student's own work under IB academic honesty rules and the consequences of a breach land on the student. The useful test is whether your child can explain each change and why it earns marks. If they cannot, it was not their work.

faqs.question: What happens if the Extended Essay goes over 4,000 words?
faqs.answer: Examiners are not required to read beyond the limit, so the practical effect is that whatever sits past 4,000 words is likely not to be credited — usually the conclusion, which is where the argument is resolved. Moving sections into appendices does not solve it, because an examiner is not obliged to read appendices either. The real answer is cutting, and there is a reliable order: the literature summary, the narrative of what the student did and when, and any restatement in the conclusion. Those three cuts usually recover several hundred words without touching the analysis.

faqs.question: What is the viva voce in the Extended Essay process?
faqs.answer: It is a short concluding interview between the student and the supervisor, normally held as part of the third reflection session once the essay is finished. It is not an examination and carries no separate mark, but it informs the supervisor's comment and feeds the final reflection that supports the six engagement marks. Students who have genuinely done their own research find it straightforward; students who have not find it uncomfortable, which is part of why it exists. Treat it as a chance to articulate what was learned and what would be done differently.

faqs.question: How much does Extended Essay coaching cost in Dubai per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates give the range. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour, Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase shows AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200-450 or above, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are their figures with their dates. Extended Essay work prices at the specialist end, because the useful version requires someone who knows how a research question fails in that particular subject. IB Gram confirms the specific tutor's rate in writing after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai Diploma student start work on the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do. Counting backwards from a school's internal final deadline, the research should be finished ten to twelve weeks before it, the complete draft should reach the supervisor six to eight weeks before, and the final four weeks should contain no new reading. Working back from there, the research question needs to be settled before the summer break between DP1 and DP2. That summer is the pivot: students who enter it with a viable question and a reading list return able to write, and students who enter it with a topic and good intentions return with nothing.

faqs.question: Do universities actually look at the Extended Essay grade?
faqs.answer: Indirectly and sometimes directly. The grade combines with Theory of Knowledge for up to three points towards the 45-point total, and those points frequently decide whether an offer condition is met. Some admissions tutors ask about the essay at interview, particularly where the subject matches the course applied for, and a student who researched something relevant has a genuine advantage in that conversation. The more important point for a Dubai family is the downside: a grade E in the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the Diploma, independent of how strong the six subject grades are.

faqs.question: Can my child submit an Extended Essay in a subject they do not study?
faqs.answer: Schools generally discourage it and the criteria explain why. Knowledge and understanding assumes subject context and the correct use of subject terminology, which a student who has not taken the course usually lacks, and the available supervisors are the school's own subject teachers. There are exceptions, and World Studies offers a structured interdisciplinary route built around a global issue examined through two Diploma subjects. The decision belongs to the school, so ask the coordinator before the student invests reading time in a subject they are not taking.

faqs.question: Is a World Studies Extended Essay a good idea for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: It can be excellent and it is more demanding than it looks. A World Studies essay addresses a global issue through two Diploma subjects, and the integration has to be genuine rather than two half-essays joined together. It also needs the global issue grounded in a specific local context, which is where students based in the UAE have real material to work with. The risk is scope: two subjects inside 4,000 words leaves very little room, so the research question has to be narrower than it would be for a single-subject essay, not broader.

intro.heading: Film is the DP subject where the tutoring market and the syllabus barely overlap
paragraphs: An IB DP film home tutor in Dubai is a narrow brief. Dubai has a deep supply of Maths and Chemistry tutors, because every school runs those subjects and the demand is constant. Film is different. A minority of the emirate's IB World Schools offer it, cohorts are frequently in single figures, and the assessment has no past-paper culture at all. There is no Paper 1 to drill. There are four pieces of produced work, three of them written or recorded by the student, and the marks come from criteria that reward precise, evidenced claims about how a film was made.

That changes what tutoring is for. A parent hiring help for DP Maths wants more practice questions. A parent hiring help for DP Film wants someone who can watch a chosen extract, stop it on a frame, and explain why the student's paragraph about the lighting is description rather than analysis. That is a feedback job, done on a screen, with the film actually playing. It is the one DP subject where video delivery is arguably better than sitting at the same table, because both people are looking at the same timecode rather than one person's laptop.

The cost question follows from the scarcity. Dubai's market rate for a general online tutor runs from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour at the budget end, on EdFlik's and Tutopiya's own published figures. A qualified subject specialist sits higher, around AED 150 to AED 300, and the IB and A-Level specialist band runs AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table giving 200 to 450-plus. Film sits at the top of that range for the same reason a Latin tutor does: the pool is small and the person you want has marked the task.

In-home tutoring in Dubai costs more again. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors at 200 to 500, with monthly in-home packages advertised around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Those figures include travel, and travel is the problem. A Film specialist willing to drive from Al Quoz to Dubai Hills Estate for a 5pm session prices the drive into the hour, and the family pays for it twice: once in money and once in a session that cannot move when the school-run runs late.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai. Home visiting is a service we operate only in India, and every one of our UAE pages says so. For Dubai families the delivery is one-to-one live online, which is also how we can put a Film specialist in front of a student in Mirdif or Jumeirah without asking anyone to find one within a twenty-minute radius. The rest of this page sets out what the four tasks are worth, where the marks actually go, what the market charges, and what changes the number in this emirate specifically.

programmes.description: The two-year course covers film as an art form, as a technology and as a business, assessed through a textual analysis of a prescribed extract, a recorded comparative study, a film portfolio of three production roles, and at HL a collaborative film project made with other students. Nothing is examined in a hall. Everything is produced, uploaded and externally or internally marked against published criteria.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, DP Film cohorts are small and often taught by a single teacher who also carries Visual Arts or Design Technology. That means feedback cycles can be slow in the term when everyone's portfolio is due at once. Outside support is usually bought for exactly that window, not for the whole two years.

programmes.name: MYP Arts and Design, moving-image strand
programmes.description: MYP Arts assesses knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding, each on an eight-point scale. Students working on film in MYP build a process journal rather than a portfolio, and the habits they form there — recording intentions before shooting, citing influences — are exactly the habits DP Film rewards. Students who never learned to annotate their own process struggle with the DP portfolio.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running MYP into DP, including Dubai International Academy and GEMS World Academy, often let students sample moving-image work in MYP 4 and 5. We use that year to build the process-journal discipline, because the DP film portfolio is a journal with marks attached.

programmes.name: IGCSE Film Studies and Media Studies
programmes.description: Many Dubai students come into DP Film from a British-track Year 11 where they sat Media Studies or Film Studies rather than an IB course. The written-analysis skill transfers; the production self-evaluation does not, because IGCSE coursework rewards a description of what was done and DP Film rewards an argued account of why. Bridging that is a short, specific piece of work.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment at 37% (KHDA, 2024-25), so the IGCSE-to-DP transfer is the single most common route into Film here. Students arriving from the Indian curriculum, 26% of the market, usually have no moving-image coursework at all.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme media pathways
programmes.description: A smaller number of Dubai students take moving-image work inside the IB Career-related Programme, pairing DP courses with a career-related study in media production. The DP course they most often carry is Film, which means the same four tasks, the same criteria and the same deadlines, inside a different overall qualification.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Dubai is thin compared with DP, so CP Film students are frequently the only person in the building doing the task. Online one-to-one is often the only way they get subject-specific feedback at all.

dubai/ib-dp-film-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Film is rarely the only subject a Dubai Diploma student needs help with. These are the courses we most often run alongside it for the same student, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Film
subjects.description: Four assessed tasks at HL — textual analysis, comparative study, film portfolio and collaborative film project — and three at SL. Marks are lost on unevidenced claims about technique and on ignoring the word and time ceilings.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Comparative study, process portfolio and exhibition. Students who take Film and Visual Arts together are managing two portfolio-style subjects with overlapping deadlines, which is a scheduling problem as much as an academic one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, which for many cohorts includes film stills, advertisements and storyboards. The close-reading habit Film demands transfers directly into this paper.

subjects.name: Theatre
subjects.description: Director's notebook, research presentation and collaborative project at SL, plus a solo theatre piece at HL. The nearest neighbour to Film in assessment style: everything is produced and documented, nothing is sat in an exam hall.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: A design project plus examined papers covering human factors, resource management and sustainability. Often the subject a Film student takes for its production overlap, then discovers has a substantial written exam attached.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Papers on the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, plus an experimental study report. A common sixth subject for Dubai arts students, and the one where command terms catch them out.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy route with a graphical-calculator paper and a mathematical exploration. The usual maths choice for Film students, and the exploration is due in the same term as the film portfolio.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Covers organisational structure, marketing, operations and finance, with a research project. Relevant to the industry side of the Film course, which the textual analysis criteria do not test but the comparative study sometimes rewards.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects. Film students often write strong TOK exhibitions because they already think about how images make claims.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay. Film is a popular EE subject in Dubai and a difficult one, because the question has to be answerable from the films themselves rather than from what critics said about them.

dubai/ib-dp-film-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Where in Dubai our Film students live
dubai/ib-dp-film-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Film students in Dubai cluster around the schools that actually offer the course, which are not evenly spread across the emirate. These are the communities we most often schedule Film sessions for, and what the local timetable does to a session slot.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Alserkal
regions.note: Dubai's working arts district, and where many DP Film students shoot their portfolio footage. Sessions here are often booked around access to a location rather than around school hours, so weekend morning slots matter more than weekday evenings.

regions.name: Dubai Studio City and Motor City
regions.note: Production-industry families and a cluster of British-track schools. Students here frequently have better camera access than editing discipline, and the tutoring need is almost always the written components rather than the shooting.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer family housing feeding several IB and British schools, with long internal drives inside the community. A 4pm session rarely starts before 4.30pm in term time, so we schedule Film feedback blocks at 5pm or later.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Dense school cluster including Dubai International Academy Al Barsha. Film students here often share a teacher with Visual Arts, which bunches deadlines; sessions get busiest in the weeks before the portfolio submission window.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Older villa communities with a mix of IB and A-Level schools. Students commonly take Film alongside English A Literature, and the two subjects' essay deadlines land close together in the spring term.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Apartment living, short school runs, and students who can start a session at 4pm. The constraint here is editing-rig noise and shared rooms, so screen-shared review of a cut works better than asking a student to present aloud.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa'a
regions.note: Largely Indian and Arab-expatriate family housing with a long commute to the western IB schools. Film students from this side of the city lose the most time to travel, which is the clearest argument for online delivery in their case.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai IB schools
schoolClusters.note: The densest IB Diploma provision in the emirate sits along the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor and inland from it. Students we support in Film most often attend schools in this group, where Group 6 choice is widest and Film is more likely to run as a timetabled course rather than as an independent study.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and central Dubai IB schools
schoolClusters.note: Provision east of the creek is thinner and Group 6 options narrow quickly. Film students here are more likely to be one of two or three in a cohort, or to be taking the course with limited timetabled contact, which is where external subject feedback does the most work.

schoolClusters.city: British-track schools feeding DP Film
schoolClusters.note: Several Dubai schools run IGCSE to 16 and then a sixth form that is partly or wholly IB. Students crossing from Media or Film Studies at IGCSE into DP Film arrive with production confidence and written-analysis habits that need rebuilding against the DP criteria.

dubai/ib-dp-film-home-tutor.modesIntro: Film support is bought in bursts rather than evenly across two years, because the deadlines are bunched. These are the three patterns Dubai families actually use, all delivered one-to-one over live video.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the coursework year
modes.description: A fixed hour each week from the start of DP1 through to the portfolio submission window. The session rotates between extract analysis practice, comparative study source work and portfolio drafting, so no single task is left until the term it is due. This is the pattern that costs most over two years and produces the least panic in the final one.

modes.title: Task blocks around a single deadline
modes.description: A short, dense set of sessions aimed at one assessed task: four to six hours on the textual analysis, or a similar block on the comparative study script and source list. Families who are satisfied with the school's teaching but want a second reader on one piece of work buy this pattern, usually six to eight weeks before the internal deadline.

modes.description: Film has no written exam, so the final term is about upload integrity, word and time limits, and making sure every claim in the written components is evidenced from the film rather than from a review. Sessions in this pattern are shorter, more frequent, and heavily focused on cutting rather than adding.

sections.heading: What an IB DP film home tutor in Dubai actually costs, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Market rates for an IB DP film home tutor in Dubai are not a single figure. As of October 2026, published Dubai rates fall into four recognisable bands: budget online tuition from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject specialists online at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in, and IB or A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. The premium end exists too — one Dubai provider publishes AED 650 for a named examiner-level tutor. Those are other providers' published figures, cited so you can check them, not IB Gram's price list.

Film pushes a quote towards the upper half of the specialist band for three reasons, all of them supply-side. The teaching pool is small, because few Dubai schools run the course and fewer still have a second Film teacher. The marking is criterion-based rather than answer-based, so the useful tutor is someone who has applied those criteria, not someone who studied film at university. And the work arrives as video files and long written pieces, which take time to read properly before a session rather than during it.

What actually moves the number in Dubai specifically: whether the session is online or in-home, because the in-home band carries a drive across an emirate with real traffic; how close the deadline is, since availability tightens in the weeks before portfolio submission; whether the booking is a single task block or a standing weekly hour, with longer commitments usually priced lower per hour; and whether the family is buying one subject or two, because the second subject rarely costs the same again. VAT treatment of tuition is not something to take on trust from any provider's page, including ours — ask whether a quoted figure includes it and get the answer in writing.

sections.heading: The four assessed tasks, what each is worth, and what each one demands
paragraphs: DP Film has no examination paper. At Standard Level a student produces three pieces of assessed work; at Higher Level, four. The weightings differ between the levels, which matters enormously for where a family should spend tutoring money. At SL the film portfolio carries the largest single share of the grade; at HL the collaborative film project does. Spending six hours polishing a textual analysis when the portfolio is the heavier task is a common and expensive mistake.

The textual analysis asks the student to analyse a five-minute extract from a prescribed film, in no more than 1,750 words, using a documented set of film elements. It is externally assessed. The comparative study is a recorded multimedia piece of no more than ten minutes, comparing two films from different cultural contexts through a chosen area of film focus, submitted with a list of sources. Also externally assessed. Both reward argued, evidenced claims about construction and penalise plot summary.

The film portfolio covers three production roles across a series of short exercises, documented with the student's reflections and supported by a reel. The HL collaborative film project is a completed short film made by a group, with each student taking a single distinct role and writing an individual project report. These two are the production halves of the course, and they are where students most often discover that documentation, not shooting, is what is being marked. A tutor's job here is to read the documentation and say plainly where a reflection has described a decision without justifying it.

sections.heading: Where marks are actually lost in the textual analysis
paragraphs: The textual analysis is the task Dubai students most often ask for help with first, because it looks like an English essay and is therefore familiar. It is not an English essay. The criteria reward identification of film elements, an argued account of how those elements create meaning in the extract, and evidence drawn from the extract itself rather than from the film as a whole or from secondary writing about it.

The commonest failure is scale. A student writes about the film's themes when the task is about a five-minute extract, and spends 400 of their 1,750 words on context the examiner did not ask for. The second commonest is the unevidenced technical claim: a sentence saying the low-key lighting creates tension, with no reference to a specific shot, no account of how the lighting is achieved, and no distinction drawn between what the lighting does and what the editing does. The third is the word ceiling itself, which is not a target but a limit, and which students routinely breach and then cut badly.

What a session on this looks like: the extract plays, it stops, and the student is asked what is on screen and what in the frame is doing the work. Then they write one paragraph while the tutor watches. Then that paragraph is read against the criterion wording, line by line, and the gap between what the student meant and what they wrote is named. That is slow, specific and uncomfortable work, and it is the only thing that reliably moves a textual analysis mark. No tutor can promise a particular grade from it; what a tutor can promise is that the student will know which sentences are carrying marks and which are not.
bullets: Analyse the extract, not the film — context beyond what the extract shows earns little
Every technical claim needs a shot, a timecode and an account of how the effect is produced
Separate cinematography, editing, sound and mise-en-scene rather than blurring them
Treat 1,750 words as a ceiling and draft to roughly 1,600 so the cut is deliberate

sections.heading: The comparative study: the task that fails on sources, not on taste
paragraphs: The comparative study asks for a recorded piece of no more than ten minutes comparing two films from different cultural contexts through a declared area of film focus, with a list of sources submitted alongside. Students in Dubai have a real advantage here and usually waste it. They live in a city whose cinemas and streaming catalogues carry Arabic, South Asian and East Asian cinema alongside Hollywood, and they still pick two American films they already like.

The marks are not for the films. They are for the comparative frame: whether the chosen focus genuinely generates a comparison, whether the argument is sustained across both texts, and whether the evidence shown on screen supports what the voice-over claims. A study that cuts between two films without ever stating why those two illuminate each other reads as a playlist. A study that declares a focus — say, how each film's industrial context shaped its representation of family — and then holds it for ten minutes, reads as research.

The second failure mode is procedural and more serious. The source list is part of the submission, and a study that leans on a critic's reading without citing it is an academic-honesty problem rather than a weak essay. A tutor's role here is to make the student's own argument sharper and to insist that every borrowed idea is attributed. A tutor does not select the films, script the voice-over or assemble the recording. That boundary is not a disclaimer; it is what keeps the submission the student's own work and the student out of a malpractice hearing.
bullets: Declare one area of film focus and sustain it across both films for the full ten minutes
Choose films that genuinely differ in cultural context, which Dubai's viewing options make easy
Show the evidence on screen at the moment the voice-over claims it
Build the source list as you research, not the night before submission

sections.heading: Film deadlines counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session, and Dubai Film students therefore work to internal deadlines set by their school's IB coordinator through the preceding autumn and spring. The IB's own exam and results dates are published by the IB and should be confirmed with your school's coordinator rather than taken from any tutoring page, including this one. What can be planned with confidence is the shape of the year, because every Film cohort hits the same pinch points in the same order.

The useful exercise is to count backwards from the school's submission window rather than forwards from today. A comparative study needs its two films watched properly — twice each, at minimum — before a focus can be declared, and that watching is four to six hours of work nobody schedules. A film portfolio needs its three production roles completed as separate exercises, which cannot be compressed into one weekend because the reflections have to describe decisions made at the time. An HL collaborative project needs a group that is still speaking to each other in February.

This is where Dubai's calendar intrudes in ways no competitor page mentions. Ramadan shifts the school day and shortens afternoons, which removes exactly the after-school hours a group film shoot needs; in practice, HL groups who have not finished principal photography before Ramadan begins finish it in a rush afterwards. The winter break falls in the middle of comparative-study research for most cohorts, and the families who use it get a six-week head start on the ones who do not. Sessions can shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, and most of our Dubai Film students do exactly that.

sections.heading: Film in Dubai's KHDA-inspected schools, and what to do when your school does not run it
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects schools annually on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the published report is the only inspection evidence a parent should rely on. The emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment.

That 7% share is why Film provision is patchy. A subject taken by a fraction of a cohort inside a programme taken by a fraction of the emirate is always going to be timetabled thinly. Several Dubai IB schools offer Group 6 as a choice between Visual Arts and Music, with Film available only if enough students request it. Some run it as a supervised independent study, where the student is registered for the course but taught in a fraction of the contact time a timetabled class would get.

If your school does not run Film and your child wants it, there are three honest options and a tutor is only part of one of them. The school's coordinator can advise whether the subject can be taken as a self-taught course, which the IB permits for some subjects and not others, and that conversation belongs with the school rather than with us. A student can take a different Group 6 subject and pursue film outside the Diploma. Or, where the school registers the student for Film with limited contact time, external subject teaching fills the gap — which is the case we see most often from Dubai families, and the one online delivery is best suited to.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a subject built on other people's footage
paragraphs: Film is the DP subject where the honesty rules are least intuitive, because the raw material is work made by other people. A student quoting a novel in an English essay knows to put it in quotation marks. A student cutting a thirty-second clip into a comparative study often does not realise that the clip needs attributing, that the critic whose reading they paraphrased needs citing, and that an uncredited idea in a voice-over is the same offence as an uncredited sentence in an essay.

The boundary for a tutor is sharp and we state it on every page. A tutor teaches, explains the criteria, asks questions about a draft, and gives feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor does not produce assessed work. Not the textual analysis, not the voice-over script, not the portfolio reflections, not the project report. Any provider offering to supply a finished component is offering the student an IB malpractice finding, and the market has such providers in it — one competitor in this sector sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is not a service, it is an expulsion risk.

In practice this means our Film sessions generate questions rather than text. A tutor will tell a student that paragraph three asserts something the extract does not show, and ask what in the frame would support the claim. The student rewrites it. The tutor does not type the replacement. Families occasionally find that frustrating in the last fortnight before a deadline, and it is still the only version of this work that is safe for the student. We also do not reproduce or supply IB subject guides, past extracts or mark schemes — we reference the official documents and link to them, because reproducing them is a copyright problem on top of everything else.
bullets: Every clip, still and borrowed idea in a comparative study needs attributing
Feedback, questions and criterion explanation are what a tutor provides
No component of assessed work is produced for the student, at any stage, for any fee
Official IB documents are referenced and linked, never reproduced or supplied

sections.heading: What a Film grade does, and does not do, for a UAE university application
paragraphs: Parents paying specialist rates for a Group 6 subject reasonably ask what the grade buys. For UAE university entry the mechanism that matters is Ministry of Education equivalency, and it is worth being precise about what is actually published. For the British track, the MoE requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects.

For the American track, the published requirements include a mathematics score of at least 450 on the SAT Math test, and English proficiency evidenced by an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section. For the IB, no points threshold has been verified against the Ministry's own published material, so this page does not state one. Any figure you are shown for IB equivalency should be checked on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly before you rely on it, and no tutoring provider — including this one — performs or guarantees the equivalency process.

What that means for Film specifically: the grade contributes to the Diploma total like any other subject, and the subject itself is rarely a named prerequisite for a UAE degree outside media and communication programmes. Nobody should be told that tutoring is required for equivalency, admission or progression, because that is a false claim about a regulatory process. The honest case for Film tutoring is narrower and more useful: the subject carries four pieces of work that are marked against criteria most students never read closely, and a reader who knows those criteria changes what the student submits.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one versus an in-home Film tutor in Dubai: the honest comparison
paragraphs: The phrase in the URL is the phrase parents type, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. In-home tutoring in Dubai is a real, large and well-established market. It costs more per hour than online because the drive is in the fee, and it works well for subjects where a tutor needs to see a student's handwriting on paper, sit beside them through a long calculation, or keep a distractible fourteen-year-old at a table.

For DP Film it is the weaker option, and not for the usual reasons. The material is on a screen. The work is reviewed by scrubbing a timeline, pausing on a frame, and reading a draft alongside the criterion wording — all of which happens better with screen sharing than with two people angled at one laptop. The decisive factor, though, is supply. There are perhaps a handful of people in the entire emirate who have taught and marked DP Film, and the probability that one of them lives within a reasonable drive of any given Dubai community and has a free 5pm slot is low. Online removes the radius from the equation.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Our tutors do not attend a UAE address, and we do not quote for one; home visiting is an India-only service on this platform. What a Dubai family gets instead is a Film specialist in a scheduled live video session, with the student's own footage and drafts on screen, at a time set in Gulf Standard Time. If what you want is specifically a person in your living room, a local agency is the right call and we would rather say so than sell you something else.

process.title: Tell us the task and the deadline
process.description: Not the subject and the year group — the actual task. Textual analysis, comparative study, portfolio reflections or an HL project report, plus the school's internal deadline for it. Film support is scoped to tasks, and a date changes which tutor can take it on.

process.title: We check who is genuinely available
process.description: Film specialists are a small group, so we tell you honestly whether one can take the slot you need. If nobody suitable is free in Gulf Standard Time hours, we say so rather than putting a general humanities tutor on a Group 6 brief.

process.title: A free trial lesson, on real work
process.description: The trial uses the student's own draft or footage, not a sample exercise. By the end of it the student should know one specific thing about their work they did not know before, and you should know whether this tutor is worth paying for.

process.title: Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time, with written feedback after each
process.description: Each session ends with notes written against the criterion wording, so the student knows which criterion a comment belongs to. Those notes are the record you can take to a parents' evening or compare against the school's own feedback.

process.title: The block ends when the work is submitted
process.description: Task-block bookings finish at the deadline rather than rolling on. If the next task needs support, that is a new conversation with a new scope, which keeps the spend visible rather than ambient.

whyPoints.title: Rates on the page, with their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or rate survey that published it, with the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency Dubai families transact in.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level feedback, not film appreciation
whyPoints.description: Film tutoring goes wrong when it becomes a conversation about movies. Our sessions are built around the published criteria for the four assessed tasks, which is why the feedback names a criterion and a sentence rather than offering an opinion about the student's taste.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach, question and give feedback. No component of a DP Film submission is produced for a student at any price. That boundary is worth stating plainly in a market where completed Internal Assessments are openly sold.

whyPoints.title: Honest availability
whyPoints.description: Group 6 specialists are scarce and we disclose it. If no Film specialist can cover the hours you need, you will hear that before you pay rather than after, and we will say what the nearest useful alternative is.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that respects the Dubai calendar
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time, shift to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan, and are planned around the fact that a 4pm slot in Dubai Hills Estate in term time is really a 4.30pm slot.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated once, plainly
whyPoints.description: All UAE tutoring on this platform is one-to-one live online. We do not operate home visits in the UAE and do not hold a UAE office or centre. Knowing that before you enquire saves everyone a call.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP Film tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates as of October 2026 put budget online tuition at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject specialists online at AED 150 to 300, and IB or A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above — TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table gives 200 to 450-plus. Film sits in the upper half of the specialist band because the teaching pool is small. Those are other providers' figures, cited so you can check them. For our own pricing, the trial lesson and consultation are the honest route, and you should ask any provider whether a quoted figure includes VAT.

faqs.question: Why does DP Film cost more to tutor than DP Maths in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty. Every Dubai school runs Maths, so the pool of competent Maths tutors is deep and rates are competitive. Film is offered by a minority of the emirate's IB schools, often with one teacher per school, so the number of people who have actually applied the DP Film criteria is small. On top of that, Film work arrives as video files and long written pieces that have to be read and watched before a session rather than solved during it, which is unpaid preparation time a tutor prices into the hour.

faqs.question: Do you send a Film tutor to our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Dubai families get one-to-one live online lessons scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For DP Film that is usually the stronger option anyway, because the work is reviewed by screen-sharing a timeline and pausing on specific frames, and because removing the travel radius means you get a Film specialist rather than whichever tutor lives nearby. If you specifically want someone in the room, a local Dubai agency is the right call.

faqs.question: What exactly is assessed in IB DP Film, and is there an exam?
faqs.answer: There is no written examination. Standard Level students produce three assessed pieces and Higher Level students four. The textual analysis is a written analysis of a prescribed extract, capped at 1,750 words. The comparative study is a recorded multimedia piece of up to ten minutes with a list of sources. The film portfolio documents three production roles with the student's own reflections. Higher Level adds a collaborative film project — a finished short film made in a group, with an individual project report. The weightings differ between SL and HL, which changes where tutoring time is best spent.

faqs.question: My child's school offers IB but not Film. What are our options?
faqs.answer: Three, and only one involves a tutor. First, ask the school's IB coordinator whether the subject can be registered as a self-taught course, since the IB permits that for some subjects and not others — that answer has to come from the school. Second, take a different Group 6 subject and pursue film outside the Diploma. Third, where the school registers the student for Film but gives limited contact time, external subject teaching fills the gap. That third case is the most common enquiry we see from Dubai families and the one online delivery suits best.

faqs.question: How many words should the textual analysis actually be?
faqs.answer: The limit set out in the current subject guide is 1,750 words, and it is a ceiling rather than a target. In practice we ask students to draft to roughly 1,600 so the final cut is a deliberate editing decision rather than a panic. Students who write 2,100 words and then delete sentences at random usually remove the evidenced technical claims and keep the atmospheric description, which is exactly the wrong way round. Confirm the current limit against the subject guide your school is teaching, since the IB revises guides between syllabus cycles.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write the comparative study script?
faqs.answer: A tutor can explain the criteria, question the chosen area of film focus, point out where the voice-over claims something the footage does not show, and insist that borrowed ideas are attributed. A tutor cannot produce the script, choose the two films or assemble the recording. That is not a policy we invented to be difficult — producing any part of an assessed component is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor. Any provider offering a finished comparative study is selling an expulsion risk.

faqs.question: Which two films should my child compare for the comparative study?
faqs.answer: That choice has to be the student's, and a tutor who makes it for them has crossed a line. What we do is pressure-test the choice. The criteria reward a genuine comparative frame across different cultural contexts, so two American films the student already likes rarely generate one. Dubai students have an advantage worth using: Arabic, South Asian and East Asian cinema is widely available here. The practical test is whether the student can say in one sentence why these two films illuminate each other through their declared focus.

faqs.question: How does online tutoring work for a subject that involves editing and footage?
faqs.answer: Better than most parents expect. The student shares their screen with the edit open, and both people see the same timecode rather than one person leaning towards a laptop. Clips can be scrubbed frame by frame, drafts sit alongside the criterion wording in a second window, and feedback is typed into the document as it is given. What online cannot do is operate a camera on a shoot — but shoots are the student's own work and a tutor should not be on set regardless.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai Film student start getting outside help?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, and for narrower reasons. The comparative study needs both films watched properly — twice each at minimum — before a focus can be declared, which is four to six hours of work nobody schedules. The portfolio needs three production roles completed as separate exercises with reflections written at the time, so it cannot be compressed into one weekend. Starting in the autumn term of DP2 usually means a block of six to eight sessions. Starting in the spring term usually means triage.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan affect Film coursework and tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more than it affects most subjects. School hours shorten, which removes exactly the after-school window an HL collaborative group shoot needs, so groups who have not finished principal photography before Ramadan tend to finish it in a rush afterwards. Tutoring itself adapts easily — sessions move to post-Iftar timing and most of our Dubai students in this subject do exactly that. The planning point is to treat Ramadan as a production blackout for group work and a perfectly usable window for written components.

faqs.question: Does my child need a Film grade for a UAE university place?
faqs.answer: Film is rarely a named prerequisite for a UAE degree outside media and communication programmes; it contributes to the Diploma total like any other subject. Ministry of Education equivalency is the mechanism that matters, and for the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E. No verified IB points threshold exists in the sources we can cite, so check moe.gov.ae directly. Nobody should tell you tutoring is required for equivalency.

faqs.question: Does a DP Film tutor working with Dubai students need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted with suspicion. The official route is MoHRE's private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Film and English together for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. The written half of Film and the Paper 1 analysis in English A: Language and Literature draw on the same close-reading habit, and a teacher who has taught both can use one subject's work to sharpen the other. What does not transfer is the production side of Film, which needs someone who has marked the portfolio criteria. If a single tutor can cover both credibly we will say so; if not, we would rather put two specialists on it than stretch one.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: The student brings real work — a draft paragraph, a rough cut, a set of portfolio reflections — and the tutor reads or watches it before the session rather than during it. The hour is spent on that work, against the criterion wording. By the end the student should be able to name one specific thing about their own submission they did not know an hour earlier, and you should have enough to decide whether to book. The trial is free with no card required and no obligation to continue.

faqs.question: What if no Film specialist is available when we need one?
faqs.answer: We tell you. Group 6 specialists are a small pool and Film deadlines are bunched, so there are fortnights in the spring term when demand exceeds the people who can meet it. In that case we will say what the realistic wait is, and if a general humanities tutor would genuinely help with one part of the task — essay structure, for instance — we will scope it to that and price it accordingly rather than pretending it is subject coaching. Concealing a coverage gap is how families end up paying specialist rates for generalist teaching.

dubai/ib-dp-film-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the task, not the subject
dubai/ib-dp-film-home-tutor.closingBody: If your child is taking DP Film in Dubai and something specific is stuck — a textual analysis that describes instead of analysing, a comparative study without a real focus, portfolio reflections that narrate decisions rather than justifying them — say which task and which deadline, and we will tell you honestly whether a Film specialist can cover it. The trial lesson runs on your child's own work, in Gulf Standard Time, with no card required. All UAE tutoring on this platform is delivered one-to-one over live video; we do not operate home visits in the UAE. The AED figures on this page belong to the providers named beside them and were read in October 2026.

dubai/ib-dp-film-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Film at Standard and Higher Level and the subjects Dubai film students most often pair it with. Matching depends on experience of marking the written and recorded tasks, because being able to make films and being able to mark them against criteria are separate skills.

intro.heading: Where the money actually goes in a Dubai Film Diploma, and where the marks are
paragraphs: Film is the Diploma subject where families spend most and understand least what they are buying. The sequence is predictable. A student picks Film, becomes convinced they need a camera, then a lens, then a microphone, then a subscription to an editing suite, then a drone. Somewhere in that sequence a parent has spent more than a term of specialist tutoring would have cost, on equipment the assessment criteria do not mention. The marks are not in the kit. They are in four tasks, three of which are substantially writing and talking rather than shooting.

What is actually assessed is analysis and justification. A textual analysis of a short extract from a prescribed film. A recorded comparative study of two films from different cultural contexts, with a declared focus and a list of sources. A portfolio documenting the student's work in production roles, with reflections that justify decisions. And at Higher Level, a completed collaborative film made by a group, with each student's individual report. Nothing in that list rewards resolution, sensor size or a colour grade.

This matters financially because support for those four tasks is costable per task rather than per term, and almost nobody sells it that way. A textual analysis block is a finite number of hours with a finite output. A comparative study needs a focus tested early and a structure built once. A portfolio needs reflections pushed from narration into justification. The Higher Level group project needs roles documented and drift caught before February. Each is a discrete purchase with a known shape, which makes it possible to spend deliberately instead of buying an open-ended weekly hour and hoping.

The published Dubai market context is worth having in front of you. Collected in October 2026, other providers advertise roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour for budget online help, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, with one Dubai provider quoting AED 650 at examiner level. In-home visiting is published at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced into the fee. Those are other companies' numbers, published by them. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page; the trial lesson is free with no card required and the quote follows the task and the hours.

There is one Dubai-specific cost driver that no competitor page mentions: Film is taught in very few schools in the emirate, so specialist capacity is tiny and it is contested in exactly the same fortnight every year, when every DP2 cohort hits its internal upload deadlines together. Booking a textual analysis block in DP1 costs the same per hour as booking it in February and buys considerably more, because in February you are competing for the last available hours in a market of a handful of people.

Delivery is settled. Lessons run one to one, online, over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run in-person lessons in Dubai and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we provide only in India. For Film that is the better arrangement rather than a compromise, because reviewing an edit means both parties looking at the same frame at the same timecode, which a shared screen does properly and two people around one laptop do not.

dubai/ib-dp-film-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Film is one subject with two very different workloads, so it is worth separating them. These are the levels and the routes into them, with what each actually commits a Dubai family to.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Film at Standard Level
programmes.description: Three assessed tasks: a written textual analysis of an extract from a prescribed film, a recorded comparative study of two films from different cultural contexts with a source list, and a film portfolio documenting the student's work in production roles with justified reflections. No group project. The practical consequence is that a Standard Level student controls their entire grade individually, which makes the workload predictable and the support costable.
programmes.countryNote: Standard Level is the sensible default for most Dubai students, particularly those carrying two Higher Level sciences or a demanding maths route. It removes the one component whose outcome depends on other people's reliability, which in a small Dubai cohort can mean a group of three where one person withdraws.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Film at Higher Level
programmes.description: The same three individual tasks with different weightings, plus a collaborative film project: a completed short film made by a group, with each student taking a declared production role and submitting an individual report on their own contribution. It is the only component in the subject where a student's mark depends partly on other people turning up, and the only one with a genuine production schedule.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the collaborative project collides with Ramadan, half-term travel and exam leave, and small cohorts mean a group of three or four with no spare capacity if someone drops out. Higher Level is the right choice for a student genuinely heading into film or media, and an expensive choice for one who picked Film as a sixth subject.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme: Arts and Design, moving-image work
programmes.description: Moving-image work appears in MYP Arts and in MYP Design depending on the school, and students who have done either arrive able to operate software and rough out a sequence. What MYP rarely builds is shot-level analytical vocabulary or the habit of justifying a decision in writing, and both are what the Diploma pays for.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision for moving image varies enormously between Dubai schools, from a full media suite to one unit in a design rotation. A student entering DP1 from the lighter version can edit and cannot analyse, which is a cheaper gap to close than the reverse.

programmes.name: IGCSE Media Studies and Film Studies as feeders
programmes.description: Both qualifications teach textual analysis of moving image and some production, which maps onto the Diploma better than any other feeder. Students arrive able to name camera positions and editing patterns. What they do not arrive with is the discipline of a sustained declared focus across a ten-minute recorded study, or a source list that survives scrutiny.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools offer either qualification, so most Diploma Film candidates in the emirate start the subject from scratch at sixteen. That is the single biggest predictor of how many support hours a family ends up buying, and it is knowable in advance rather than discovered in DP2.

subjects.name: Film
subjects.description: Assessed through a written textual analysis, a recorded comparative study, a production portfolio with reflections, and at Higher Level a collaborative film with an individual report. subjects.name: Theatre
subjects.description: The closest neighbour in structure: also assessed through recorded presentations, a research-based task and a documented collaborative project. Students taking both can learn the recorded-presentation discipline once and apply it in two subjects, which is a real saving in hours.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Assessed entirely through submitted work with hard screen, word and character limits. Shares the comparative-analysis habit with Film, but its documentation load lands in the same autumn weeks, so the two calendars need planning as one.

subjects.name: Music
subjects.description: Useful for students scoring their own productions and directly relevant to the music-for-dramatic-impact territory. Also a documentation-heavy subject, so a student taking Film and Music is carrying two portfolios at once.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: The subject that most improves textual analysis marks in Film, because both reward close reading of a constructed text and both punish retelling the plot. Progress in one shows up in the other within a term, which makes it the best-value shared tutor in this cluster.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Strong support for the cultural-context requirement of the comparative study, where students are expected to place two films from different contexts in a researched frame rather than asserting a national mood.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Covers media, platforms and the social effects of digital technology, which gives a Film student a researched vocabulary for distribution, audience and algorithmic reach. A natural pairing for students interested in contemporary media rather than classical cinema.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Chosen by students heading towards production, distribution or media management. The internally assessed work falls in the same window as the film portfolio, so the autumn of DP2 needs a single plan rather than two.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The route most Dubai arts students take through the maths requirement and the one that keeps a Film timetable survivable. Still demanding on statistics and modelling, and worth protecting with a weekly slot in DP1.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: A film Extended Essay is popular in Dubai and frequently becomes a review of a director's work rather than an answer to a question. A tutor can question the scope and the sources and give feedback on the student's own drafts, and nothing more than that.

sections.heading: What Dubai families buy for Film, and what the criteria actually reward
paragraphs: This is the most expensive misunderstanding in the subject, so it belongs first. Film students and their parents spend on equipment because equipment is visible, purchasable and exciting, and because a student who owns a camera feels like a film-maker. The assessment criteria reward something else entirely: the ability to analyse how a sequence was constructed, to compare two films within a declared focus, to justify a production decision in writing, and at Higher Level to evidence an individual contribution to a group film.

None of those four things requires a camera better than a recent phone. A phone shoots at a resolution well beyond what any assessment needs, records usable sound at close range, and is always present, which matters more for a student production than any specification. Free and included editing software is sufficient for every task in the subject. What a student genuinely benefits from owning is a cheap external microphone and a way of holding the camera still, because sound and stability are the two things that make student work hard to watch and neither costs much.

The table below sets out the common purchases against what the assessment does with them. It is not an argument for spending nothing; it is an argument for spending in the right order. A family that spends on a microphone, a tripod and eight hours of specialist support will be in a better position than one that spends the same total on a camera body, and the second is what usually happens.

The clearest sign of a misallocated budget is a portfolio of beautifully shot material with reflections that explain nothing. Examiners mark the reflection. A student who can say why the shot is framed as it is, what they tried first, and what the change achieved will out-score a student with better footage and no account of it, every time.
