sections.heading: Who French ab initio is for, and what choosing wrong costs
paragraphs: French ab initio exists for students with little or no previous French. It is Standard Level only, there is no Higher Level route, and schools are expected to place students on the basis of genuine prior experience rather than preference. That sounds administrative until you price the consequences of getting it wrong, which in Dubai happens often because of how much students move between schools and curricula.

Two failure modes dominate. The first is a student placed in ab initio who already has real French: three years of MYP Phase 2 or 3, or a year at a French-medium school. They coast through DP1, find the ceiling in DP2, and discover that the course cannot stretch to reward what they already know. The second is a student placed in French B who has almost no French, usually because the school had no ab initio class to offer. They spend DP1 drowning, and the catch-up bill is the largest single tutoring cost we see on language acquisition subjects.

A diagnostic hour settles it, and it is the cheapest hour in the whole engagement. The tutor asks the student to speak for two minutes about their school day, read a short authentic text aloud and answer three questions on it, and write eighty words describing a photograph. What comes back shows the actual phase: whether the present tense is secure, whether past-time reference exists at all, whether reading is decoding or comprehension. That is a level recommendation your child's school can act on, and it is worth having before the DP1 subject choices are locked rather than after.

If the recommendation is a switch, timing is everything. Moving between ab initio and French B in the first term of DP1 costs a few weeks of rework. Moving in DP2 means abandoning either a literary component or a vocabulary base, and the tutoring hours needed roughly triple. The honest advice is sometimes to stay in the wrong course and play it well, and a tutor who will say that out loud is more useful than one who sells you the switch.

sections.heading: The four components you are buying hours for
paragraphs: French ab initio is assessed in four parts of equal weight, which is unusual and strategically useful. There is no single component worth half the grade, so no component can be written off. A family budgeting hours should spread them across all four rather than pouring everything into the one the student dislikes most, which is almost always the oral.

Paper 1 asks for two short written tasks on prescribed topics, chosen from a set of options, each with a specified text type, audience and purpose. The marks are not mostly about grammar. They are about whether the student produced the text type asked for: a blog entry that reads as an essay, or a formal letter written in the register of a message to a friend, loses on the message and conceptual criteria even when the French is clean. This is the single most teachable component and the one where tutoring hours convert most directly into marks.

Paper 2 is split between listening and reading, a quarter each. Listening is where Dubai students in particular struggle, because classroom French is spoken slowly and deliberately while the recordings are not, and because an answer lifted whole from the audio often answers a different question than the one asked. Reading punishes the habit of scanning for one recognised word and building an answer around it. Both respond to volume rather than cleverness: short, frequent, timed practice beats long sessions.

The individual oral is internally conducted and recorded, and it is worth the same 25 per cent as each paper. The student describes a photograph linked to one of the five prescribed themes, discusses it with the teacher, then holds a general conversation that reaches into at least one other theme. Two preparation failures recur: a six-sentence description that exhausts itself in ninety seconds, and a memorised monologue that cannot answer an unexpected question. Rehearsal on camera fixes both, and it is the one thing a student cannot practise alone.

Confirm the current component detail, timings and word ranges with your child's IB coordinator or the school's copy of the subject guide. The IB revises guides, and what is published on a tutoring page is no substitute for the document your child's teacher is working from.

sections.heading: A twenty-four-month budget for a DP1 starter
paragraphs: Spreading the cost across two years is cheaper than concentrating it in one term, and it produces a better grade. The table below is a planning model, not a quote: it maps what the hours do in each phase onto an indicative monthly band, using Bestimate's 2026 Dubai monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring scaled by session count.

The shape matters more than the totals. DP1 runs at one session a week and is about building something to assess: vocabulary across the five themes, the present tense, then the near future and the perfect, then the first text types. A family that holds one session a week from September to June in DP1 arrives at DP2 needing maintenance rather than rescue, and maintenance is the cheap end of this market. Skipping DP1 entirely and planning to buy intensity in DP2 inverts the cost: more hours, at a higher rate, in a worse market.

The DP1 summer is the decision most families get wrong in both directions. Full-rate sessions through July and August are usually poor value, because retention work does not need a specialist. Dropping French completely for ten weeks is worse, because an ab initio student loses topic vocabulary fastest of any language candidate. A fortnightly thirty-minute retention session, or structured self-study with a marked task at the end of August, costs very little and saves four weeks of re-teaching in September.

DP2 is where spend rises, and it should. Two sessions a week from January to the May session is the standard pattern: one on papers, one on the oral. Budget separately for the oral intensive, because it lands in a scarce window at a premium rate, and book it before the school announces its recording dates rather than after. Build a buffer for mock season too, when every subject wants the same evenings.

sections.heading: The permit costs nothing, so an unpermitted tutor saves you nothing
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

Read that against a quote. A tutor charging below the market floor is not charging less because they skipped a fee; there is no fee to skip. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount can honestly be quoted to you by anybody. What a parent can do is ask the question, because a tutor who holds the permit can say so in one sentence and a tutor who does not will change the subject.

There is a second rule worth knowing if you are in the habit of asking your child's own teacher. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK before relying on it, but the direction is unambiguous: your child's own French teacher is the wrong person to pay privately.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: in Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram does not hold one and does not operate premises in the UAE, which is why nothing on this page describes a centre, a branch or a licence we do not have. We ask tutors to hold the MoHRE permit, and we are explicit that doing so is not an endorsement by KHDA, MoHRE or anyone else.

sections.heading: Where French tutoring sits against Dubai school fees
paragraphs: Tutoring spend only makes sense next to the rest of the education bill, and Dubai gave families an unusual anchor this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family already at the top of its education budget, a flat fee year is the first chance in a while to redirect money rather than find more of it.

Supply is moving too. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. More IB schools means more ab initio cohorts, and in the short term it also means more newly assembled language departments teaching a course for the first time. Both effects raise demand for outside language support, which is part of why specialist rates in this city have not softened.

Set against that, a single weekly French session at the middle of the market is a small line item on a Dubai education budget and a large one on a monthly cash-flow statement. The useful comparison is not tutoring against school fees but tutoring against the alternatives for the same money: a group class at a centre, a cheaper generalist tutor at twice the hours, or no support and a resit. A resit is the expensive outcome, and it costs a year as well as money.

One number nobody should give you is a VAT ruling. The UAE treatment of tuition fees is a question for the Federal Tax Authority, not a tutoring page, so ask any provider plainly whether the AED figure they quoted includes VAT and get the answer in writing. That single question has moved more quotes than any negotiation.

sections.heading: What a French ab initio tutor may not do
paragraphs: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback. A tutor does not produce assessed work. For French ab initio the internally assessed component is the individual oral, which the student performs and the school records, and there is no coursework a tutor could ghostwrite even if asked. Where the boundary bites is in the written tasks a student submits to their teacher as classwork or mock evidence, and in any TOK or Extended Essay work running alongside French in DP2.

What is legitimate is substantial. A tutor can set a task to the same brief as Paper 1 and mark it against the published criteria. A tutor can annotate the student's own writing, name the error pattern and teach the fix. A tutor can rehearse a photograph description, record it, and show the student where the sixty-second mark fell. A tutor can supply model answers written by the tutor and clearly labelled as models, for study rather than submission.

What is not legitimate is writing or rewriting a sentence the student will hand in as their own, drafting an Extended Essay, or sitting in on a recorded oral. IB academic honesty rules put the consequence on the student, not the tutor, which is why a provider who offers to help with submitted work is selling your child the risk and keeping the fee. One page in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments; treat any offer in that direction as a reason to walk away.

We also will not sell you a grade. No tutor can promise a specific score in French ab initio, and anybody quoting a percentage of students who improved should be asked for the sample size, the dates and the method on the same page. What can be promised is specific work: a number of marked tasks, a number of recorded rehearsals, and a written note of where the marks are currently being lost.

process.title: Tell us the level question first
process.description: Before anything else, say where the French actually is: which MYP phase, how many years, whether the student can hold two minutes of speech. If the school has already placed your child in ab initio and the placement looks wrong, say that too, because it changes which tutor we look for.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one per student
process.description: A single trial lesson at no charge and with no card details taken. It is a real lesson, not a sales call: the tutor runs a short diagnostic, teaches something, and tells you at the end what they think the starting point is. You decide afterwards whether to continue.

process.title: Agree the plan and the rate
process.description: We set out session length, frequency and the rate in writing, including whether written-task marking happens inside or outside the hour. Ninety-minute blocks and sibling pairing are priced here, not negotiated later, and the oral intensive is flagged as a separate block to book early.

process.title: Teach, mark, record
process.description: Weekly sessions on a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. Written tasks go out between sessions and come back annotated against the criteria. Oral rehearsals are recorded so the student can rewatch them, which is the fastest route to fixing a description that runs out too soon.

process.title: Review every half term
process.description: A short written note: what has been marked, what the error pattern is now, what changed since the last note. If the pattern has not moved, we change the approach or the tutor. Nothing in that note is a grade prediction, because a prediction is the school's job.

whyPoints.title: The price is explained, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page carries its source and the month it was read. Three of the pages competing for this search publish no price at all and two quote in dollars. You can check our market bands against any quote you receive, including ours.

whyPoints.title: A specialist rather than the nearest tutor
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the match is made on subject and level, not on driving distance from your community. For a language with a small teaching pool in Dubai, that is the difference between a French ab initio specialist and a generalist who also speaks French.

whyPoints.title: Marking against the published criteria
whyPoints.description: Written tasks come back annotated against the assessment criteria rather than with a number at the top. Knowing that a task lost marks on text-type conventions rather than on grammar is what makes the next task better.

whyPoints.title: The oral treated as a component, not an afterthought
whyPoints.description: The individual oral is a quarter of the grade and the only part a student cannot revise alone. Rehearsals are recorded, reviewed and repeated across all five prescribed themes, and the intensive block is flagged early because the window is tight.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not do
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no premises in Dubai, no regulator endorsement, no grade promises, and no help with work your child must submit as their own. Each of those is a thing some provider in this market claims.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around a Dubai week
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set on Gulf Standard Time around school-run timings, activity schedules and the Ramadan calendar, including post-Iftar slots when families ask for them. A slot that survives the term is worth more than a cheaper slot that does not.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP French ab initio tutor in Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified language teacher working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour in Dubai, and an IB-experienced language acquisition specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. In-home visits across the emirate run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is inside the fee, and a small premium tier quotes AED 500 to AED 650. Those are the market's numbers, drawn from published provider rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, not an IB Gram price list. Our own rate depends on the match and is agreed in writing after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is French ab initio cheaper to tutor than French B?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, by a modest margin, and for a reason worth understanding. Ab initio is Standard Level only and carries no literary works, so there is no literature component to teach and the written tasks are shorter. French B at Higher Level requires two works of literature and longer written responses, which both lengthens preparation and narrows the pool of tutors who can mark it. In practice a Dubai family pays a similar hourly rate but needs fewer hours for ab initio in DP1. The exception is a late start: an ab initio student beginning in DP2 needs more hours than a French B student who is merely behind.

faqs.question: Does a native French speaker charge more in Dubai than a non-native teacher?
faqs.answer: Typically AED 30 to AED 80 an hour more, and the premium is about scarcity rather than teaching quality. Dubai's francophone teaching pool is sized around the French national curriculum community, so a native speaker who also knows how Paper 1 is marked against the IB criteria is genuinely uncommon here. For a beginner in DP1 that premium buys very little, because the first year is vocabulary, sound-to-spelling work and the present tense, all of which a well-qualified non-native teacher handles accurately. For DP2 oral rehearsal, where the student needs to hear natural pace and unscripted questions, it buys something real.

faqs.question: How many hours of French ab initio tutoring does a DP1 student actually need?
faqs.answer: One session a week through DP1, lifted to two a week from January of DP2, is the pattern that works for most Dubai students, plus a short block of three to six sessions for the individual oral before the school's recording window. That is roughly sixty to eighty hours across the two years. Families who compress the same spend into the final six months need more hours overall, pay a higher rate because they are buying in a scarce window, and get less from them, because ab initio marks depend on vocabulary breadth that takes months rather than weeks to build.

faqs.question: Why does a ninety-minute French session cost less per hour than a sixty-minute one?
faqs.answer: Because a language session has fixed overheads. Settling in, retrieving last week's vocabulary and warming up into French take roughly the same ten to fifteen minutes whatever the length of the lesson. In a sixty-minute slot that is a quarter of the time; in ninety minutes it is a sixth, so more of what you pay for is teaching. Tutors recognise this and typically price ninety-minute blocks AED 10 to AED 40 an hour below their hourly rate. The limit is attention: for a DP1 beginner, ninety minutes is usually the ceiling before quality falls away.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share one French ab initio session to cut the cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it reduces the per-student cost by roughly a quarter to two-fifths, but only when both students are genuinely at a similar stage. Two DP1 beginners who started the same course in the same term work well in one block. A DP1 beginner paired with a DP2 candidate preparing an individual oral does not, because the oral rehearsal is personal to the photograph and the themes chosen, and one student ends up watching. Ask for an honest assessment after the trial lesson rather than assuming the pairing will hold for two years.

faqs.question: Does an AED rate quoted by a Dubai tutor include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing. The UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than something a tutoring page should rule on, and providers in this market handle it differently: some quote inclusive figures, some add it, and some are not registered. The practical question for a parent is simple and specific: is the number you just gave me the number I will pay each month, and does it include VAT? Any provider who cannot answer that in a sentence has told you something useful about how they run their billing.

faqs.question: Is my child eligible for French ab initio if they studied French in Year 9?
faqs.answer: Possibly not, and this is worth resolving before DP1 subject choices lock. Ab initio is designed for students with little or no prior experience of the language, and schools are expected to place students on genuine prior learning rather than preference. A student who completed two or three years of MYP French at Phase 2 or above is usually a French B SL candidate. A student who did a year, stopped, and arrived in Dubai from a different curriculum may legitimately be an ab initio candidate. A single diagnostic hour, covering two minutes of speech, a short read-aloud and eighty words of writing, settles it clearly enough for the school to act on.

faqs.question: What does the individual oral add in preparation hours?
faqs.answer: Budget three to six focused sessions, concentrated in the four to six weeks before the school records. The oral is worth 25 per cent, the same as each paper, and it is the only component a student cannot practise alone. Those sessions cover photograph description across all five prescribed themes, the discussion that follows, and the general conversation that reaches into a second theme. Rehearsals are recorded so the student can see exactly where a description ran out of material. Book the block before the school announces its recording dates, because specialist diaries in Dubai fill as soon as those dates are published.

faqs.question: Do French ab initio rates in Dubai rise closer to the May session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the rise is sharper for languages than for most subjects because the oral windows concentrate demand into a few weeks. Late bookings into the oral window are commonly quoted AED 20 to AED 60 an hour above the ordinary rate, and the best-matched specialists are simply unavailable rather than more expensive. Mock season produces a second, smaller spike. A family booking oral rehearsal in November pays the ordinary rate and gets a choice of tutors; the same family booking in March pays the scarcity rate and takes whoever is free.

faqs.question: How do I check that a French tutor in Dubai holds the MoHRE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and ask early. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system with a two-working-day completion time listed on MoHRE's own service page. Because there is no fee, a tutor charging below market has not saved money by skipping it. A permit holder can confirm the position in one sentence. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted penalty figure as unverified.

faqs.question: What happens to the price if no French ab initio specialist is free?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting quietly. French ab initio is a narrow specialism and Dubai's pool is small, so there are weeks when nobody suitable is available at the slot you need. The options we put in front of you are an alternative slot with the right specialist, a French B tutor who has taught ab initio and can cover the shorter written tasks, or a wait with a date attached. Where the fallback tutor is outside the UAE, the lesson still runs on Gulf Standard Time and the rate is stated before you agree. What we will not do is fill the slot with a generalist and let you find out in week three.

faqs.question: Is online French tutoring in Dubai genuinely cheaper than a home visit?
faqs.answer: On the published bands, yes: AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified online teacher against AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the fee. The gap widens for outer communities, where a tutor spends forty to ninety minutes driving. The more important difference is which tutor you can reach. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. For a subject with a small teaching pool, online delivery means the match is made on French ab initio experience rather than on who lives within a twenty-minute drive.

faqs.question: Can a French ab initio tutor correct the work my child hands in?
faqs.answer: A tutor can mark work your child has written, annotate it against the assessment criteria, name the error pattern and teach the fix. A tutor cannot write or rewrite sentences that will be submitted as your child's own, and will not draft an Extended Essay or a TOK essay. For French ab initio the internally assessed component is the recorded individual oral, which the student performs alone with their teacher, so there is no coursework to ghostwrite in any case. IB academic honesty rules put the consequence on the student, which is why any provider offering to help with submitted work is selling your family the risk.

faqs.question: How does the KHDA fee freeze change what we can spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family at the limit of its education budget, that is the first flat year in a while and the first chance to redirect rather than find money. A single weekly French session at the middle of the market sits in the AED 600 to AED 1,200 monthly band on Bestimate's 2026 estimates, which for many Dubai households is now a reallocation rather than an increase.

dubai/ib-dp-french-ab-initio-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the diagnostic, then decide what to spend
dubai/ib-dp-french-ab-initio-tutor.closingBody: The cheapest hour in a French ab initio engagement is the first one, because it tells you what you are actually buying: whether the level is right, whether the gap is vocabulary or text types, and how many sessions a week the two years really need. Book the free trial lesson, one per student with no card details taken, and the tutor will run that diagnostic and say plainly what they think. You will get a rate in writing, the market bands on this page to check it against, and an honest answer about availability. Nobody in this market can promise your child a grade in French ab initio, and we will not. We can tell you where the marks are going now.

dubai/ib-dp-french-b-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach French B at Diploma level, SL and HL, to students in Dubai's IB and British schools. Each has worked with the current assessment model, which is the difference between a French conversation partner and someone who can tell you which of the thirty Paper 1 marks your child is losing.

intro.heading: The price of French B in Dubai is a supply story
paragraphs: Dubai is an unusual market for French tuition because the supply curve has two humps. The city holds a substantial francophone population, several French-curriculum schools and a steady flow of French, Lebanese, Maghrebi, Belgian, Swiss, Canadian and West African families. Native speakers who will teach are therefore easy to find and comparatively inexpensive. Tutors who have taught or marked the current IB French B assessment are a much smaller group, and the price difference between the two is wider in French than in almost any other Group 2 subject here.

That gap is what families are actually choosing between, and it is usually invisible on a listing. A native speaker can improve a student's spoken fluency and will often charge at the budget end of the Dubai market. What they generally cannot do is look at a Paper 1 script and say that the language marks are fine, the message marks are thin and conceptual understanding has been forfeited because a blog post was written where a formal report was asked for. Those are three different problems and only one of them is a French problem.

So this page is organised around money rather than around syllabus. What the Dubai market charges, with sources and dates. What moves the number: level, component, how close the school's oral recording window is, how many sessions a week, whether travel is priced inside the hour. What the realistic session count is for each component rather than a vague term-long commitment. And what the whole thing looks like next to a Dubai school fee bill, which is the comparison families actually make at the kitchen table.

Two framing points before the tables. Every AED figure on this page is a market rate from a named source with the month attached. None of them is an IB Gram price list: we start with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and quote against level, component and session length, because an oral intensive and a two-year HL programme are not the same purchase. And nothing here is a claim about any competitor's quality or legality, only about published rates in a market.

The delivery model is also a cost factor and we state it plainly rather than burying it. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. French B is taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The practical consequence for your budget is that no part of the hour you pay for is spent on Sheikh Zayed Road, and the tutor you get is chosen for French B rather than for postcode. That is a cost argument rather than a convenience one, and it is the reason the rate tables below compare usable minutes as well as headline figures.

IB and IGCSE specialists at roughly AED 200-450 and above

dubai/ib-dp-french-b-home-tutor.programmesIntro: What a family pays for French B depends heavily on where the student is coming from, because that decides how much of the course is new. These notes describe the three routes into French B that Dubai schools produce, and what each one leaves to buy.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: French B occupies the Group 2 slot at SL or HL, framed by five prescribed themes. Paper 1 is a written task in a named text type. Paper 2 is listening and reading and carries half the grade. The individual oral is internally assessed. Higher Level adds two literary works, a longer Paper 1 and a longer listening component, with around 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at SL.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families choosing French B at HL often do so for a European university application, which raises the stakes on the grade and therefore the realistic session count. That is the main reason an HL French B plan in this city costs more over two years than an SL one: it is not a higher rate, it is more hours against a harder internal component.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: French appears as Language Acquisition across six phases, assessed on listening, reading, speaking and writing criteria. A student leaving MYP5 in phase 4 or 5 is well placed for French B HL. Phase 3 points to SL, and the difference in required support hours between those two starting points is substantial.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai IB schools generally offer French as the main alternative to Arabic in Group 2, so French B classes here are large and mixed. A student at the lower end of a wide class is the commonest reason a Dubai parent starts pricing tutors in DP1 term one rather than in DP2.

programmes.name: IGCSE French
programmes.description: British-curriculum students in Dubai usually arrive at French B from IGCSE French, which trains accurate short answers and controlled writing tasks under tight constraints. It trains comparatively little extended argument and almost nothing of the conceptual framing that Paper 1 rewards.
programmes.countryNote: This is the route that most often leads a Dubai family to buy fewer hours than they need. An IGCSE grade 7 in French looks like a secure base, and the student's accuracy usually is secure. The gap is text type and message, which is cheap to fix and invisible until the first DP1 mock comes back.

programmes.name: Students from French-curriculum schools
programmes.description: Dubai has several French national curriculum schools, and students occasionally transfer from them into an IB school. A first-language francophone in French B is in a course below their level, in the same way an Arabic heritage speaker often is, and French A should be examined as an option first.
programmes.countryNote: Where a transfer student is placed in French B for timetable reasons, the honest tutoring answer is usually very few hours: exam technique and text type conventions rather than language work. We say so, because selling a two-year programme to a native speaker would be taking money for teaching them their own language.

dubai/ib-dp-french-b-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Pricing a French B plan means pricing components, since each one takes a different number of sessions to move. The entries below are the units we quote against, with the weighting or mark allocation attached.

subjects.name: Paper 1 written task
subjects.levels: SL 1 h 15 min - HL 1 h 30 min - 25%
subjects.description: One task from three, in a named text type on a prescribed theme, marked out of 30 across language, message and conceptual understanding. Typically three to five sessions to move if the problem is structure or text type, and considerably more if it is range of expression.

subjects.name: Conceptual understanding, criterion C
subjects.description: Audience, purpose, context and register for the text type requested. The cheapest component on the page to fix: two to three sessions on the conventions of letters, blogs, speeches, reports, reviews and diary entries, then enforcement on every subsequent piece of writing.

subjects.name: Paper 2 listening
subjects.description: Recorded French at natural pace with comprehension questions. Usually the most expensive component to shift because it needs exposure hours rather than teaching hours, which is why we set it as homework drilling and use session time for technique and review.

subjects.name: Paper 2 reading
subjects.description: Authentic texts with questions that reward precise location of information. Responds quickly to question-type work: four to six sessions sorted by question type generally produces more than a term of reading passages end to end.

subjects.name: Individual oral, SL
subjects.description: A visual stimulus on a prescribed theme, a conversation on it, then at least one further theme. Four to six sessions on unseen images in the weeks before the school's recording window is the standard block families buy, and the one with the most visible return.

subjects.name: Individual oral, HL
subjects.description: Starts from an extract from one of the two literary works studied. Preparation has to begin while the works are being taught, so the HL oral is a DP1 cost rather than a DP2 one. Starting it in DP2 is what makes HL plans expensive.

subjects.name: The two HL literary works
subjects.description: Studied for the oral rather than for the written papers, which is why students neglect them. Commonly set texts in Dubai schools include short contemporary novels and twentieth-century classics. Two or three sessions per work, done in DP1, removes most of the HL oral risk.

subjects.name: French grammar that carries marks
subjects.description: The subjunctive, the distinction between passé composé and imparfait, past participle agreement, pronoun order with y and en, and relative pronouns such as dont and lequel. A finite list, which makes it a costable piece of work rather than an open-ended one.

subjects.name: Register and the tu or vous decision
subjects.description: A formal email written in the second person singular undermines the register marks no matter how accurate the French is. One session, applied thereafter. Among the highest returns per AED spent anywhere on the course.

subjects.name: Spoken fluency and hesitation control
subjects.description: The one area where a non-specialist native speaker at the budget end of the Dubai market genuinely delivers value. Where fluency is the only gap, we will say that a cheaper conversation partner is the better purchase for part of the plan.

dubai/ib-dp-french-b-home-tutor.regionsTitle: French B across Dubai, and what each area does to the bill
dubai/ib-dp-french-b-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives changes the cost of tuition in Dubai more than it should, because in-home rates price travel inside the hour and because session timing is set by the commute. The notes below say what each cluster means practically.

regions.name: Oud Metha and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: The historic centre of Dubai's francophone school provision. French speakers are easy to find here, which holds the budget end of the market down, but French B specialists are no more common than anywhere else in the city.

regions.name: Academic City and Al Ruwayyah
regions.note: Campuses clustered together at the eastern edge, forty minutes from most residential districts at the wrong time of day. In-home rates quoted into this area usually carry the longest travel component in Dubai.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1 to 3
regions.note: Established villa districts with a long-standing French and Lebanese presence and short distances to several IB schools. Early-evening sessions are feasible here, which widens the pool of tutors willing to quote.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: Central, well served by schools, and the area where families most often compare an in-home quote against an online one directly. The travel component is small, so the comparison comes down to specialism rather than to logistics.

regions.name: Za'abeel and Trade Centre
regions.note: Apartment living with parents working nearby, so sessions can start earlier than the city average. Students here are often juggling French B against a demanding HL grid, which argues for shorter, more frequent slots.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Arjan
regions.note: Dense newer communities with large school catchments and heavy late-afternoon traffic on the Al Khail corridor. Any in-home quote for a 16:30 start in this area is pricing a journey as well as a lesson.

regions.name: The Lakes and Emirates Living
regions.note: Villa communities with established Diploma cohorts and a high proportion of HL French requests. HL plans bought in DP1 cost less in total than the same plan bought in DP2, and this cluster tends to buy early.

regions.name: Motor City and Green Community
regions.note: Western communities with limited school choice nearby and long cross-city school runs. The second journey of the day is the one that gets cancelled, which is the practical reason online delivery holds its schedule here.

schoolClusters.city: Oud Metha, Al Jaddaf and Academic City
schoolClusters.note: Dubai's francophone education centre. The French national curriculum schools here do not produce French B candidates, since their students sit the French baccalaureate, but their presence is why native French speakers are abundant and inexpensive in this city. The bilingual IB provision nearby is a different matter.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Al Barsha South
schoolClusters.note: Where most of our French B requests originate, from IB and British schools offering French as the principal Group 2 option. Classes are large and mixed, and the students who need paid support are usually at the lower end of a wide ability range rather than struggling in absolute terms.

A budget tutor, typically a university student or a generalist, starts between AED 45 and 150. An in-home one-to-one visit runs AED 180 to 500, with travel priced inside the billed hour. A premium named tutor can exceed AED 500. Those bands come from published rate cards and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026.

A package is cheaper per hour and less flexible; the trade is usually the cancellation terms.

sections.heading: A French speaker and a French B tutor are different purchases
paragraphs: This is the distinction that decides whether money spent on French in Dubai produces a grade change. The city has many fluent French speakers willing to teach, and at the budget end of the market they are good value for what they do, which is conversation, vocabulary and confidence. What they typically cannot do is mark a Paper 1 against the published criteria, explain why an otherwise good piece of writing scored two out of six on conceptual understanding, or prepare an HL oral from a literary extract.

The practical test is to ask a prospective tutor a question about marks rather than about French. How many marks is Paper 1 worth and how are they split? What is the difference between the SL and HL individual oral? How many literary works does HL require and what are they for? A French B specialist answers all three in a sentence each. A fluent speaker who has not taught the course will answer the first vaguely and the other two not at all, which is useful information rather than a criticism.

There is a sensible hybrid that almost nobody suggests because it reduces the sale. Where a student's written marks are adequate and the gap is spoken hesitation, the right purchase is a cheaper conversation partner for part of the plan and a specialist for a short component block, not a specialist weekly for two years. We will say so when the evidence points that way. The table sets out what each model actually delivers against what the Dubai market charges for it.

sections.heading: What moves the number for a Dubai family
paragraphs: Five variables account for almost all of the spread in quotes a Dubai family will receive for French B. Level, because HL carries two literary works, a longer Paper 1, a longer listening paper and around 240 recommended teaching hours against 150. Component, because marking written work between sessions costs tutor time that a conversation hour does not. Timing, because a block bought three weeks before the school's oral window achieves more per session than the same block bought three weeks after the result.

The fourth is frequency, which cuts both ways. Two shorter sessions a week usually produce more movement than one long one, particularly for listening, but they cost more in total and are harder to schedule around a Dubai school day. The fifth is delivery format, and this is the one families underweight. An in-home rate in the AED 180 to 500 band prices travel inside the hour, and in this city a 16:30 start in Al Barsha South or Academic City can mean a meaningful share of the session spent arriving.

Set all five against the thing that does not move. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. A fixed fee bill makes the tutoring line easier to judge: it is a marginal addition to a known total rather than a competing unknown, and families in our experience then decide it on whether the criterion marks move rather than on the hourly figure.

sections.heading: How many sessions does French B actually need?
paragraphs: Open-ended tutoring is the most expensive kind, and the commonest in this market, because nobody commits to a number. Here are the estimates we work from, stated as ranges and derived from component rather than from optimism. Conceptual understanding and text type conventions: two to four sessions, then enforcement at no extra cost on every later piece of writing. Paper 1 structure: three to five. Reading technique sorted by question type: four to six. The SL oral block before a school window: four to six.

Two components resist this. Listening does not respond to session count because it needs exposure hours, so the sensible plan uses sessions for technique and review and pushes the volume into homework drilling the student does alone. Range of expression, the difference between accurate French and interesting French, is a function of reading and writing volume over months. A tutor who implies either can be bought in six sessions is selling something that does not exist.

So a realistic French B SL plan for a student losing Paper 1 and oral marks is something like fifteen to twenty sessions spread across DP1 and DP2, not a weekly booking for two years. An HL plan with the two literary works and the HL oral runs higher, perhaps twenty-five to thirty-five, and costs materially less if the literary work is done in DP1. We put the estimate in writing at the consultation so it can be checked against what actually gets booked.

sections.heading: In-home French tuition in Dubai: what the AED 180-500 band buys
paragraphs: The in-home band exists and families should understand it even though we do not sell into it. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with home tutors more broadly at AED 200 to 500, and the premium over an online rate is substantially travel. In-home packages around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions appear in the same market, which is a different product again: two-hour sessions suit some students and exhaust others.

What that premium buys is a tutor who is physically present, which genuinely helps some students, and a tutor drawn from whoever will travel to your community, which helps none. For French in Dubai the second effect is milder than for Arabic A, because fluent French speakers are widely distributed across the city. For French B specialists it still bites: a parent in Motor City choosing from tutors willing to drive to Motor City at 17:00 on a Tuesday is choosing from a short list.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. French B here is taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. What that means for cost is simple: the full hour is teaching, the tutor is selected for French B rather than for proximity, and a session can be held at 19:30 on a weekday without anybody calculating a journey. Whether that is worth more than physical presence is a judgement a family should make with the trade stated, which is why it is stated here.

sections.heading: Where the French B marks actually are, and what each is worth fixing
paragraphs: Paper 1 is 25% of the grade, marked out of 30: twelve marks for language, twelve for message, six for conceptual understanding. Paper 2, listening and reading together, is 50%. The individual oral is 25% and marked out of 30 on language, message and interactive skills. Those numbers decide where money should go, and they usually contradict instinct, because the component students enjoy practising is writing and the component carrying half the grade is the one they skip.

The cheapest marks on the page are the six for conceptual understanding. A student who writes a well-argued essay where a formal letter was requested keeps most of the language marks and loses those six outright. Each text type has a short list of conventions: how it opens, how it addresses the reader, whether it carries a heading or a sign-off, whether the first person is appropriate, and whether tu or vous is correct. A page of notes and a fortnight of enforcement.

The French-specific grammar that carries real weight is also finite, which makes it costable. The subjunctive after particular triggers. Passé composé against imparfait, which is a meaning distinction rather than a tense choice. Past participle agreement. Pronoun order with y and en. Relative pronouns such as dont and lequel. We build a numbered list from the student's own marked work rather than teaching French grammar from the top, and the list shortens over a term as items stop appearing.

Paper 2 listening and reading together: 50% of the grade

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context against a Dubai school fee bill
paragraphs: Families decide tutoring spend relative to what they are already paying, so the context is worth setting out. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum accounting for 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, US 14% and International Baccalaureate 7%. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no fee increase for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

Against a fee bill that is fixed for the year, the arithmetic on tutoring becomes a marginal decision rather than a competing one. A weekly specialist session at the mid-band market rate across a school year is a visible but modest addition. A component block of five sessions before an oral window is smaller still, and it is the purchase with the clearest attributable effect, because the oral mark is recorded on a known date and either moved or did not.

The context cuts the other way too, and should. A family paying substantial fees is entitled to ask what the school is already providing for French B before buying anything: whether there is a clinic, whether past papers are marked, whether the oral window is published, and what the teacher's own diagnosis of the gap is. Several of the things families pay us for are available free inside the school if someone asks for them, and we would rather say that than sell around it.

sections.heading: What we will not charge you for
paragraphs: The free trial lesson has no card requirement and no obligation, and it is spent on a diagnostic rather than on a sales conversation: a marked piece of the student's writing, a criterion breakdown, and an estimated session count per component. The written estimate is yours whether or not you book, including if you take it to a cheaper tutor, which happens and is a reasonable thing for a family to do.

We will not sell a two-year weekly booking where the evidence points to two component blocks. We will not sell French B support to a native francophone placed in the course for timetable reasons beyond a few sessions of exam technique, because teaching someone their own language at a specialist rate is not a service. And we will not quote for listening improvement as though it were a six-session fix, since the volume that moves listening is exposure the student does alone.

Two further things that are not for sale at any price. No tutor will write, redraft or complete an assessed component: a French B oral is delivered by the student and any written coursework is theirs. And IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or the IB, holds no UAE office, and sends no tutor to a UAE address. Private tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years; ask any tutor to show you theirs.

process.title: Send a marked script and the school's oral window
process.description: Two documents settle most of the pricing conversation: the most recent marked French B written task and the date the school plans to record the individual oral. Together they say which component to buy and when the block has to happen to be worth buying.

process.title: Free trial, used for a criterion breakdown
process.description: The trial session re-marks that script on language, message and conceptual understanding and produces three numbers. No card is required and the breakdown is yours to keep, including if you use it to brief a different tutor.

process.description: The consultation produces a range per component: text type, Paper 1 structure, reading technique, the oral block, and whether listening belongs in sessions or in homework. A written estimate is checkable later, which an open-ended weekly booking is not.

process.description: Sessions run live online in Gulf Standard Time, usually after 18:00 on a Dubai weekday. Blocks have a defined finish point. Where a block ends and the marks have moved, we say so and stop rather than rolling into a standing weekly slot by default.

process.description: At the end of each block the criterion marks are compared with the estimate given at the start. If the plan underdelivered, we say which assumption was wrong. If a cheaper arrangement would now serve better, including a conversation partner for fluency, we say that too.

whyPoints.description: Three of the six pages ranking for this kind of query publish no price at all and the two that do quote US dollars. Every AED band here carries the source and the month it was read, so a quote from anyone can be checked against the market rather than against a feeling.

whyPoints.title: Session counts estimated per component
whyPoints.description: Open-ended weekly tutoring is the most expensive kind. We estimate a range per component in writing at the consultation, including the two components that cannot be fixed in a short block, so a family knows what they are committing to before they commit.

whyPoints.title: A straight answer on whether you need a specialist
whyPoints.description: Where the only gap is spoken hesitation, a cheaper fluent conversation partner for part of the plan is the better purchase and we will say so. Dubai has plenty of them. What they cannot do is mark Paper 1 to criteria, which is the work we are for.

whyPoints.description: In-home rates in Dubai price travel inside the hour and narrow the tutor pool to whoever will drive to your community. We do not sell into that band, so we set out the trade in plain terms and let a family weigh presence against choice of tutor.

faqs.question: How much does a French B tutor cost per hour in Dubai in AED?
faqs.answer: Published rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026, put budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-500 with travel inside the hour, and premium named tutors above AED 500. Monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Those are market figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Why is French B tutoring in Dubai cheaper at the bottom than other subjects?
faqs.answer: Because Dubai has a large francophone resident population and several French-curriculum schools, so fluent French speakers willing to teach are abundant. That holds the budget end of the market down in a way it is not held down for, say, Arabic A Literature. The specialist end behaves normally: tutors who have taught or marked the current IB French B assessment are a small group and priced accordingly. The unusually wide gap between those two bands is the single most important thing to understand before comparing French quotes in this city.

faqs.question: Does a native French speaker make a good French B tutor?
faqs.answer: For fluency and confidence, often yes, and at the budget end of the Dubai market that can be good value. For marks, usually not on its own. Paper 1 is scored out of 30 on language, message and conceptual understanding, and the six conceptual understanding marks turn on text type conventions rather than on French. Ask a prospective tutor how Paper 1 is marked, how the SL and HL orals differ, and what the two HL literary works are for. A specialist answers each in a sentence; a fluent speaker who has not taught the course generally cannot.

faqs.question: Is French B HL more expensive to support than SL?
faqs.answer: In total, yes, though not usually at a higher hourly rate. HL carries two literary works, a longer Paper 1 and a longer listening component, with around 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at SL. The HL individual oral starts from a literary extract rather than from an image, so preparation has to begin while the works are being taught. An HL plan started in DP1 typically runs twenty-five to thirty-five sessions across two years. The same plan started in DP2 costs more and delivers less, because the literary work has to be compressed.

faqs.question: How many French B sessions will my child actually need?
faqs.answer: Estimated by component rather than by term. Text type conventions and conceptual understanding: two to four sessions. Paper 1 structure: three to five. Reading technique sorted by question type: four to six. An SL oral block before the school's recording window: four to six. That puts a realistic SL plan at fifteen to twenty sessions spread across both years rather than a weekly booking for two. Two things resist estimation: listening, which needs exposure hours rather than sessions, and range of expression, which builds over months of reading and writing.

faqs.question: What does the AED 180-500 in-home band actually buy in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Physical presence, plus travel priced inside the billed hour, plus a tutor drawn from whoever is willing to drive to your community at that time of day. Bestimate's 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and home tutors more broadly at AED 200-500, with monthly in-home packages around AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Presence helps some students genuinely. The narrowing of the tutor pool helps nobody, and in Al Barsha South or Academic City at 16:30 the travel component is not theoretical.

faqs.question: Are monthly tutoring packages in Dubai better value than paying per hour?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour and less flexible, which is the usual trade. The Dubai market shows online packages around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home packages around AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions, as published in October 2026. The thing to read before signing is the cancellation and rollover terms, because a DP timetable contains mock weeks, school trips and exam leave that will collide with a fixed eight-session month. Where a package has a condition attached, that condition should be visible on the same screen as the price.

faqs.question: What are the cheapest marks to win on French B Paper 1?
faqs.answer: The six conceptual understanding marks, which turn on audience, purpose, context and register for the text type requested rather than on the quality of the French. A student who writes a strong essay where a formal letter was asked for keeps most of the language marks and forfeits those six. Each text type has a short, fixed set of conventions: opening, form of address, heading or sign-off, whether the first person fits, and whether tu or vous is correct. Two to four sessions of work, then enforcement on every later piece at no extra cost.

faqs.question: Which French grammar points are worth paying a tutor to fix?
faqs.answer: The finite ones, because they can be costed. The subjunctive after its common triggers. Passé composé against imparfait, which is a difference in meaning rather than a choice of tense. Past participle agreement. Pronoun order with y and en. Relative pronouns including dont and lequel. Register and the tu or vous decision, which is one session and applies to everything afterwards. What is not worth buying as a short block is range of expression, the gap between accurate French and interesting French, because that comes from reading and writing volume over months.

faqs.question: Can a French B tutor visit our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. French B is taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, which usually means a weekday evening or a weekend morning. The cost consequence is straightforward: the whole hour is teaching rather than partly travel, and the tutor is chosen for French B experience rather than for living near you. Whether that outweighs physical presence is a judgement we think families should make with the trade stated.

faqs.question: When should we book a French B oral block to get the most from it?
faqs.answer: Three weeks before the date the school intends to record the individual oral, which means asking for that date in DP1 rather than hearing about it in DP2. Specialist availability tightens before the May session and in the weeks around schools' internal recording and submission windows, which is when demand for French B oral blocks concentrates. Published rate bands do not generally change, but choice does, and a block booked late is a block taken at whatever times remain. The planning answer is to ask the school in DP1 for the date it intends to record the individual oral, then book the component block three weeks ahead of it. Same number of sessions, materially different return.

faqs.question: What is my child's school likely to provide for French B at no cost?
faqs.answer: More than many fee-paying families ask for. Marked past papers, a subject clinic or drop-in, the published date of the individual oral window, the two HL literary works with the department's own notes, and the teacher's specific diagnosis of where the marks are going. Dubai private school fees were confirmed by KHDA in May 2026 as not rising for 2026-27, so the fee line is fixed and already paid. It is worth asking for those four things before buying any hours, and we would rather say so than quote around them.

faqs.question: Is paying for a French B tutor worth it if my child is already at a grade 5?
faqs.answer: It depends which component is holding the 5, and that is a cheap thing to establish. If Paper 1 is losing message and conceptual understanding marks, a short block is good value because those marks are technique rather than language. If the 5 is held down by Paper 2 listening, the honest answer is that no small number of sessions will move it, and the money is better spent on structured daily exposure the student does alone with a tutor reviewing method monthly. The trial session's criterion breakdown tells you which case you are in.

faqs.question: My child is a native French speaker placed in French B. Should we pay for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Very little of it. A francophone in French B is in a course below their level, and the useful work is exam technique rather than language: text type conventions, how the oral is structured and marked, and how Paper 2 reading questions want their answers framed. That is a handful of sessions, not a programme. The larger question is whether French A is available and appropriate, which is a conversation for the Diploma coordinator in DP1 while the timetable can still move. Selling a native speaker two years of their own language at a specialist rate is not a service.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and does that affect the price?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it is free, so it should not affect the price. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Any tutor quoting a fee for their own licensing as part of your rate is quoting for something that costs nothing. Ask to see the permit; IB Gram holds no regulator licence and claims none.

dubai/ib-dp-french-b-home-tutor.closingBody: The expensive mistake in French B is not the hourly rate. It is buying two years of weekly sessions when the evidence pointed to two short component blocks, or buying a specialist for fluency work a cheaper conversation partner would have done better. Send the most recent marked task and the date of the school's oral window, and the free trial produces three criterion scores and a written session estimate, with no card required and no obligation. Sessions run one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time. If a cheaper arrangement would serve your child better, we will put that in the estimate.

dubai/ib-dp-french-b-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach Diploma French B at both levels. Each works from the current subject guide, marks written tasks against the published criteria grid before the lesson that discusses them, and prepares Higher Level orals on the literary works the student's own school has chosen.

intro.heading: Good French and a mediocre French B grade are entirely compatible
paragraphs: French B rewards a narrow set of behaviours, and a student can be a pleasant, capable user of French while doing almost none of them. The commonest profile we see in Dubai is a student at a 4 or 5 who speaks confidently, reads comfortably, writes fluently and scores in the middle because every written task comes out as the same well-made piece of prose. The task asked for a blog post, a formal letter, a set of guidelines or a speech. The student wrote an essay. That is a Criterion C problem, it is worth a band, and no amount of extra vocabulary fixes it.

The subject sits in Group 2 at Standard or Higher Level, framed by the five prescribed themes of identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation and sharing the planet. Paper 1 is a single piece of writing worth a quarter of the grade, 250 to 400 words at Standard Level and 450 to 600 at Higher Level, chosen from three tasks that each specify a text type. Paper 2 carries half the grade across listening and reading. The individual oral, internally assessed and externally moderated, carries the last quarter, and at Higher Level it is built on an extract from one of two literary works studied in French.

The thirty marks on Paper 1 are allocated across three criteria, and knowing the split changes how a student revises. Criterion A covers language, Criterion B covers message, and Criterion C covers conceptual understanding, which in practice means text type, register, audience and purpose. Students and parents both assume language carries everything. It does not, and the two criteria students neglect are the ones that move fastest, because conventions and task response are teachable in weeks while lexical range takes terms.

Dubai makes French B a more varied cohort than most cities would. The emirate licenses seventeen different curricula across 227 private schools on KHDA's 2024-25 figures, and its French-speaking population is substantial, so a single Diploma French B class can contain a student from a French-system school who has studied in French all their life, a bilingual child from a francophone household, and a British-curriculum student who finished IGCSE French with a grade 7. Those three students need different lessons and are sitting the same paper.

What one-to-one tuition over live video changes is which tutor the student gets. French B is a specialism inside a specialism: the teacher needs the current subject guide, experience of marking against the criteria grid, and at Higher Level a reading knowledge of the two works a particular Dubai school has chosen. Looking for that person within twenty minutes' drive of one community narrows the field to almost nobody. Looking for them online widens it to everybody, and the lesson is the same lesson.
bullets: Paper 1 is marked on three criteria totalling thirty marks, not on language alone
Each task names a text type, and the conventions of that text type are assessed
Paper 2 is listening then reading in one sitting, carrying half the final grade
Higher Level requires two literary works in French and bases the oral on one
All Dubai lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time

dubai/ib-dp-french-b-online-tutor.programmesIntro: French runs through the IB continuum in different forms, and a Dubai student's French history usually explains their Diploma placement better than any test does. The notes below set out what each programme assesses and what students typically carry forward.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: French B is a Group 2 language acquisition course at Standard or Higher Level, examined at the end of Year 13. Paper 1 writing carries 25 per cent, Paper 2 listening and reading carries 50 per cent, and the internally assessed individual oral carries 25 per cent. Higher Level adds two literary works studied in French and bases the oral on an extract from one of them rather than on a visual stimulus.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts are small relative to the British-curriculum population, with IB schools at 7 per cent of private-school enrolment against 37 per cent for UK schools on KHDA's 2024-25 figures. French B classes are consequently mixed in ability, often containing French-system transfers and IGCSE finishers in the same room, which is the strongest practical argument for one-to-one support.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: French is taught as language acquisition in phases, assessed on four criteria covering comprehension of spoken and visual text, comprehension of written and visual text, communication in response to text, and use of language in spoken and written form. The phase a student exits in is the best single predictor of whether French B Higher Level is a realistic Diploma choice.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP classes change composition constantly as families move between schools and countries. A student who arrives in Year 10 from a French-system school is often placed by conversation rather than by record, and ends up in a phase that understates what they can do in writing but overstates what they can do in analysis.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: French appears as an additional language woven into transdisciplinary units, with no external assessment. The useful indicator for a parent is whether the child can read an unfamiliar short text and write connected sentences by Year 6. Oral confidence at primary level often masks a reading and writing gap that only becomes visible in the MYP.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai primaries run substantial French provision alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic, which means some children carry two additional languages through primary. That is manageable, but it does mean the French hour and the Arabic hour compete directly for the same homework time in a Dubai week.

dubai/ib-dp-french-b-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: French B is rarely the only subject a Dubai Diploma family wants help with, and the pairings matter because deadlines collide. Each entry below notes what the subject assesses and where it overlaps with the work French B needs.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: The subject of this page. Marks concentrate and disappear in Criterion C: students write competent prose irrespective of the text type the task named. Teaching seven or eight recurring text types with models and checklists is the highest-value term of work available on the course.

subjects.name: French A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Group 1 route for students educated in French. It assesses literary and non-literary analysis rather than language acquisition, so a French-system transfer is often better placed here. Students who find French B unchallenging in the first term should raise it before the change deadline closes.

subjects.name: French ab initio
subjects.description: The beginners' course, restricted to students with little or no previous French and offered at Standard Level only. Its written tasks are much shorter and its topics prescribed. A student with IGCSE French behind them is not eligible, which surprises families every year.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside French by Dubai students building a language-heavy Diploma. The assessment model is identical, so criteria work transfers directly, but interference between two Romance languages is real and worth managing deliberately rather than hoping it resolves.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Its Paper 1 unseen analysis teaches exactly the audience and purpose reasoning Criterion C rewards in French. A student who can identify the conventions of a text type in English can be shown the same reasoning in French in a single session rather than a term.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Extended writing under time, with sources. For French B the transferable skill is paragraph architecture: claim, evidence, link back. Students often supply plenty of French content with no visible argument, which is a Criterion B loss rather than a language one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Included here for scheduling reasons rather than overlap. Its exploration deadline commonly lands in the same term as the French B oral window, and one of the two has to be moved forward in any realistic plan.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The internal assessment and the extended writing it requires compete directly with language practice in Year 13. Students taking both should expect the French hour to be the first thing sacrificed, which is precisely why it should be the one with a fixed weekly slot.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay and exhibition both demand that a student hold a position and qualify it. The same move earns Criterion B marks in French B, where students frequently describe rather than argue because they are concentrating on the language.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A Group 2 essay written in French is a demanding and genuinely distinctive choice. A tutor's role is teaching research method, narrowing a question, discussing sources and giving feedback on the student's own drafts, with no text supplied for submission.

dubai/ib-dp-french-b-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities and the French B students in them
dubai/ib-dp-french-b-online-tutor.regionsIntro: French B enquiries in Dubai come from two quite different populations: francophone families whose children are moving between systems, and English-medium families whose children took French to IGCSE. The notes below describe what each area tends to send us.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A long-established francophone presence alongside several British and IB schools. Enquiries here are often about placement rather than marks: whether a child educated partly in French belongs in French A or French B, which is a conversation for the Diploma coordinator.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: A dense school district where students frequently change schools without changing neighbourhood. French histories here are fragmented, with two or three different approaches behind one student, and the first job is auditing what grammar was actually covered.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: Heavily international and apartment-based, with many short-stay families. Students often arrive mid-Diploma from a French-system school abroad and need to adapt to the IB's criteria rather than to the language itself.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Mudon
regions.note: Villa communities with long school runs to the emirate's IB schools. The constraint on tuition here is travel on both sides, which is why an online slot can start at 4.15pm where a visiting tutor would start at 4.40pm.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to several university campuses and to schools serving the eastern communities. French B students here are often also considering French-taught degree routes, which changes what the oral practice is for.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Working parents, later evenings and a preference for sessions after 7pm. That timing is difficult to staff with a visiting tutor and straightforward over video, and it suits a subject where the student needs to be awake rather than fresh from sport.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Established family communities with mixed curriculum provision nearby. Students here more often come through IGCSE French than through a French-system school, which means solid grammar and no experience of the IB's text-type conventions.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai francophone and bilingual schools
schoolClusters.note: Students moving out of these schools into an IB Diploma, or sitting the Diploma within a bilingual one, make up a large share of French B enquiries. Their issue is usually the IB's assessment conventions rather than the French, which is a faster problem to fix.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB Diploma schools teaching French B
schoolClusters.note: French B runs in most of the emirate's Diploma schools at both levels, with the Higher Level literary works chosen school by school. That choice is the first thing a tutor needs before planning any oral preparation.
