dubai/ib-dp-french-b-online-tutor.modesIntro: French B support divides naturally by what is closest on the calendar. All three formats below are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and most students move between them across the two Diploma years.

modes.title: Text-type and writing programme
modes.description: A term of work through the recurring Paper 1 text types, one per fortnight, each with a model, a conventions checklist and a timed task the student writes and the tutor marks against the thirty-mark grid. The point is coverage of forms rather than volume of words, so that no task in the examination asks for something the student has never produced.
bullets: A model text and a checklist for each form covered
Timed tasks written at the real SL or HL word range
Marks reported as A, B and C separately so progress is visible per criterion
A running list of which forms are secure and which are untested

modes.title: Higher Level literature and oral block
modes.description: Work on the two literary works the student's school has chosen, with the oral rehearsed on extracts of the kind the school will use. Preparation covers the presentation, the follow-up discussion on the work, and the wider conversation that follows, because candidates who have only rehearsed the presentation collapse in the third phase.
bullets: Both of the school's chosen works read and discussed, not summarised
Extract practice under the school's own preparation conditions
Separate rehearsal of presentation, follow-up and general conversation
Recordings reviewed for range and sustained speech, not only accuracy

modes.title: Paper 2 listening and reading clinic
modes.description: Half the grade sits in a paper students practise least because it is awkward to do alone. Sessions run authentic audio twice, as the examination does, teach a note-taking routine before the second hearing, and work on reading questions that require inference rather than word-matching. An error log by question type replaces the vague sense that listening is hard.
bullets: Audio played twice with no pausing, exactly as in the paper
Note-taking taught as a technique before the second hearing
Reading practice focused on inference, reference and tone
Errors logged by question type to target the weakest category

sections.heading: What French B assumes a student can already do
paragraphs: The course assumes several years of prior French and builds on them without revisiting the foundations. It expects a student to handle the present, perfect, imperfect and future with reasonable accuracy, to use the conditional, to recognise and sometimes produce the subjunctive, to manage pronoun placement, and to read authentic text at a native register. None of that is taught in a Diploma French B classroom, because the time goes on themes, text types and assessment preparation. A student who arrives with gaps in those areas spends two years performing above their grammar and losing Criterion A marks on every task.

This is why the first useful thing a tutor can do is an audit rather than a lesson. Set a short diagnostic that forces each of those structures in turn and the picture becomes clear within half an hour: a student may be perfectly comfortable in the imperfect and incapable of placing two pronouns in the same clause, which is exactly the kind of specific gap that a classroom cannot see and a parent cannot describe. From that audit the term plan is obvious, and it looks nothing like a generic French course.

The second assumption is reading volume. Paper 2's reading section uses authentic text, and students who read nothing in French outside lessons meet an unfamiliar register in the examination. Fifteen minutes a day of French journalism does more for the reading paper than any comprehension exercise, and it also feeds the oral, because opinions need content. Dubai students have no shortage of access to French media; what they lack is the habit, and building it is a legitimate part of a tuition plan rather than homework padding.
bullets: Assumed structures: perfect and imperfect contrast, conditional, subjunctive recognition, pronoun order
A thirty-minute structured audit finds gaps a term of lessons would not
Authentic reading volume drives both Paper 2 and the oral's content
Classroom time goes on themes and assessment, not on revisiting grammar

sections.heading: The text types that decide Criterion C
paragraphs: Every Paper 1 task names the form the student must produce, and the conventions of that form are assessed. This is the part of French B that students are most reliably not taught, because it looks like presentation rather than language and so gets treated as a detail. It is not a detail. A student who writes an elegant essay in response to a task asking for a set of guidelines has misread the task, and the mark scheme says so under conceptual understanding, which also covers register and audience.

The forms recur. Across any sample of past tasks the same handful appear: a blog post, an article, a formal or informal letter, an email, a report, a speech, a set of instructions or guidelines, a review, a diary entry, an interview and a brochure or leaflet. That is a finite list and it can be taught. One form a fortnight, each with a model, a short list of conventions and one timed task, covers the ground in a term and converts a persistent Criterion C weakness into a strength.

The table below sets out the forms students most often meet, the conventions each one needs, and the error that costs marks in practice. Students should write at least one of each before the examination, because the first attempt at a form always goes badly and it is better that it happens in February. The same applies to register: a task naming a school magazine wants a different voice from one naming a letter to a local authority, and the two are easy to confuse under pressure.

sections.heading: Where the thirty Paper 1 marks actually go
paragraphs: Paper 1 is marked out of thirty across three criteria, and the split is public information that very few students can recite. Criterion A covers language and carries twelve marks. Criterion B covers message and carries twelve. Criterion C covers conceptual understanding and carries six. Knowing those numbers changes behaviour, because it shows that language is less than half the paper and that the two criteria students think of as presentation are worth eighteen marks between them.

Criterion A rewards range and accuracy in service of the task, not complexity for its own sake. A student who attempts the subjunctive and gets it wrong three times scores worse than one who writes accurate, varied French without it. This is worth saying plainly to ambitious students, who routinely sabotage their own scripts reaching for structures they cannot control. The productive version of ambition is lexical variety and sentence-length variation, both of which are low-risk and visible to a marker.

Criterion B rewards whether the task was answered: the ideas relevant, developed and organised so a reader follows them. Students lose these marks by writing everything they know about the theme rather than responding to the specific prompt. Criterion C, the smallest in marks, is where the largest proportional gain usually sits, because most students score low on it for a reason that takes a term to fix rather than a year. sections.heading: Tense, mood and the five errors that cap a French B script
paragraphs: Five error families account for most of the Criterion A losses we see in Dubai French B scripts, and they are predictable enough to be worth naming. The first is the perfect and imperfect contrast: students who can conjugate both choose between them by instinct, and instinct trained on English aspect produces the wrong choice in narrative. The second is agreement of the past participle, particularly with reflexive verbs and with a preceding direct object, which is a rule students know and do not apply under time pressure.

The third is pronoun order and placement, which collapses as soon as two pronouns appear in a clause, and which also produces awkward avoidance: students rewrite sentences to escape the problem and lose fluency doing it. The fourth is the subjunctive, usually attempted after the wrong triggers or avoided entirely in constructions where it is expected. The fifth is register leakage, where a formal task slides into spoken forms, with on replacing nous inconsistently, questions formed by intonation in written text, and informal contractions appearing in a letter addressed to an institution.

The remedy is a personal error log rather than a grammar course. A student who records their own recurring errors by category across a term, and reviews them before each timed task, eliminates most of them inside two months. That approach beats working through a grammar book because it targets the errors that actually appear in that student's French, which is a short and highly individual list. A tutor's contribution is accurate diagnosis, consistent marking against the criterion, and refusing to let the same error be rediscovered in April.
bullets: Perfect against imperfect chosen by English instinct rather than by aspect

sections.heading: Moving from a French-system school into Diploma French B
paragraphs: Dubai has a substantial French-system school population, and every year a group of those students moves into an IB Diploma school for Years 12 and 13. They arrive with French that is far stronger than the course assumes and with no experience of how the IB assesses anything. The result is often a disappointing first term, which parents read as a problem with the school and which is actually a problem of assessment literacy: the student is being marked on conventions nobody has explained.

The first question is whether French B is even the right course. A student educated in French may belong in French A, the Group 1 language and literature route, which assesses literary and non-literary analysis rather than language acquisition. Taking French B instead is not a disaster, since the grade will usually be high, but it wastes a Group 2 slot that another language could have filled. That decision has a deadline, normally early in Year 12, and it is worth raising in the first fortnight rather than after the first report.

Where French B is the right placement, the work is specific and short. The student needs the criteria explained, the text types taught, and the oral format rehearsed, because none of those exist in the French system they came from. Analytical writing habits learned there, particularly the explication de texte tradition, transfer well to Higher Level literature work. The table below maps the commonest transfers into Dubai Diploma schools and what each one needs first.

sections.heading: The Higher Level literature requirement and the oral built on it
paragraphs: Higher Level French B requires two literary works read in French, and the individual oral is built on an extract from one of them. This is the clearest structural difference from Standard Level, where the oral starts from a visual stimulus, and it catches out students who chose Higher Level for its reputation without reading the fine print. A novel in French is a serious piece of work for a Group 2 student, and two of them across two years needs planning from the first term of Year 12.

The schools choose the works, which means a tutor cannot prepare properly without knowing what they are. Dubai schools select widely, and there is no standard pair. What is consistent is the failure mode: students leave the reading until the oral window is announced, skim both works in a fortnight, and then try to discuss an extract from a text they do not know. The marks lost are not language marks. A candidate who cannot place an extract in its work has nothing to say about it, which costs message and interactive marks simultaneously.

Preparation that works treats the works as content to be learned rather than as reading to be completed. The student needs to know the shape of each text, its central concerns, a handful of key passages, and enough vocabulary to discuss it without reaching. Practice extracts should come from across both works, not only from the memorable chapters. And the general conversation phase, which follows the discussion of the extract, still ranges across the themes, so a student who has prepared only literature will stall in the third phase of their own oral.

sections.heading: French B, DELF, and what universities actually look at
paragraphs: Dubai families frequently ask how French B relates to DELF and DALF, the French ministry's own language certifications. They are different instruments with different purposes. French B is a Diploma subject graded one to seven, contributing to the total points on which university offers are made. DELF and DALF are standalone language certificates aligned to the Common European Framework levels and used primarily as proof of language competence, including for study in France. A student may hold both, and for some destinations both are useful.

What matters for admissions is which one the destination asks for. Universities in the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada and the UAE read the Diploma grade and the total points. French-taught programmes in France and francophone Europe often want a certificate at a specified framework level, and a Diploma grade will not substitute for it. The practical consequence is that a student aiming at a French-taught degree should check the requirement directly with the institution early, because preparing for a certificate examination is additional work with its own calendar.

Neither certificate is a requirement for anything a Dubai student does by default, and nobody should be pushed towards one as insurance. It is also worth saying that tutoring is not required for university admission or for Ministry of Education equivalency of a school certificate: equivalency is a process run by the Ministry, with its own documentary requirements, and it is described on the Ministry's own channels. We can explain how it works, and we do not perform it, guarantee it or influence it.
bullets: French B gives a Diploma grade and points; DELF and DALF give a framework-aligned certificate
UK, US, Canadian and UAE universities read the Diploma grade
French-taught programmes in France may require a certificate at a named level
Check the requirement with the institution before adding an examination

sections.heading: Fitting a weekly French hour into a Dubai term
paragraphs: A language subject is the first thing to be dropped from a busy week, because nothing is due. That is the practical reason French B grades drift in Year 13 while science grades hold: the science has a deadline every fortnight. The counter-measure is structural rather than motivational. A fixed weekly slot, agreed for the term rather than negotiated each week, survives a Dubai calendar of fixtures, trips, exam leave and Ramadan hours in a way a flexible arrangement does not.

Cost sits in that same practical frame. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support; monthly packages advertised elsewhere in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for in-home blocks. Those are other providers' published figures with their own dates, not our price list. The useful observation is that in-home provision costs more for the same teaching because travel is paid for somewhere.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Dubai lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and for a written-and-spoken language subject the format costs almost nothing. Scripts are annotated live on a shared screen, orals are recorded and reviewed, and audio plays under controlled conditions. It also removes the travel that makes a 4pm slot a 4.30pm start, which across two Diploma years is a meaningful number of recovered hours.

process.title: Send the level, the school and the two literary works
process.description: Standard or Higher Level, the Dubai school, and for Higher Level the two works the school has chosen. Those three facts determine which tutor can actually help, because oral preparation on an unknown text is guesswork. If the level is still being decided, say so, since that conversation is more urgent than any lesson.

process.title: A free 45-minute trial built around a structured audit
process.description: The trial costs nothing, runs for 45 minutes and takes no card details. It uses a diagnostic that forces the assumed structures in turn, plus a short timed writing task, so the output is a specific list of gaps rather than an impression. You receive that list in writing whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: A term plan by criterion, not by topic
process.description: The plan says which Paper 1 criterion is being targeted, which text types are being covered, and what the listening schedule is. Milestones are forms written and errors eliminated rather than hours attended, so there is something to check against at half term other than whether the lessons happened.

process.title: Weekly sessions with scripts marked in advance
process.description: Tasks are set between lessons and marked against the thirty-mark grid before the session that discusses them, with each comment naming its criterion. The error log travels across the course, so a participle agreement problem diagnosed in October is not rediscovered as a new finding in March.

process.title: Say so early if the fit is wrong
process.description: A tutor the student does not click with costs more than no tutor, because the hour becomes something endured. Tell us and we rematch at no charge. If no French B specialist is free at your preferred time, or none has read your school's chosen works, we will tell you that instead of making the booking work on paper.

whyPoints.title: Criteria are taught, not just applied
whyPoints.description: Students are shown the thirty-mark grid and where their own marks sit on it, because a student who understands that conceptual understanding is worth six marks revises differently from one who thinks the paper tests French. Every comment on a marked script names its criterion, which trains the habit of reading the mark scheme.

whyPoints.title: Text types covered as a finite list
whyPoints.description: The recurring Paper 1 forms are a closed set, and each is taught with a model, a conventions checklist and a timed task. That converts the single most common Criterion C weakness into a strength in a term, and it means no task in the examination asks for a form the student has never written.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level orals rehearsed on the school's own works
whyPoints.description: Preparation happens on the two literary works the student's school actually chose, with practice extracts drawn from across both texts rather than from the memorable chapters. The general conversation phase is rehearsed separately, because candidates who prepare only the literature stall in the last third of their own oral.

whyPoints.title: A structured audit before any teaching
whyPoints.description: French B assumes structures it never revisits, and the gaps are highly individual. A thirty-minute diagnostic that forces each assumed structure in turn produces a specific list, which is what the term plan is built from. Generic French courses skip this step and spend weeks teaching what the student already knew.

whyPoints.title: No text supplied for assessed work
whyPoints.description: On an Extended Essay in French, or any submitted component, a tutor teaches method, questions the argument and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is written for submission. IB malpractice consequences fall on the student, which makes this boundary a protection rather than a restriction.

whyPoints.title: A slot that survives the Dubai calendar
whyPoints.description: Sessions are fixed for the term on Gulf Standard Time, planned around fixtures and school trips, and shifted to post-Iftar times during Ramadan. Language subjects are the first casualty of a busy week precisely because nothing is due, and a term-long slot is the structural answer to that.

faqs.question: My child is fluent in French and stuck on a 5 in French B. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always the two criteria that are not about language. Paper 1 is marked out of thirty, with twelve marks for language, twelve for message and six for conceptual understanding. A fluent student who writes the same well-made prose whatever the task was asked for loses message and conceptual marks consistently, because the task named a blog post, a report or a set of guidelines and the conventions of that form are assessed. Teaching the recurring text types with models and checklists usually moves this profile faster than any vocabulary work.

faqs.question: How many marks is each French B Paper 1 criterion worth?
faqs.answer: Thirty marks in total: Criterion A for language carries twelve, Criterion B for message carries twelve, and Criterion C for conceptual understanding carries six. Criterion C covers text type, register, audience and purpose. The paper is a quarter of the final subject grade. Most students assume language is the whole paper, which leads them to reach for complex structures they cannot control while ignoring eighteen marks that depend on answering the task in the right form. The split is worth knowing before the next timed task.

faqs.question: Which text types come up most often in French B Paper 1?
faqs.answer: A finite set recurs: blog post, article, formal and informal letter, email, report, speech, instructions or guidelines, review, diary entry, interview and brochure. Each has conventions that are marked, so a student should write at least one of every form before the examination. The first attempt at any form always goes badly, and it is better that happens in February than in the examination hall. Working through one form a fortnight, with a model and a checklist, covers the whole list in a term.

faqs.question: What is different about French B at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Three things. Paper 1 asks for 450 to 600 words rather than 250 to 400. Two literary works must be read in French across the course. And the individual oral is built on an extract from one of those works rather than on a visual stimulus. The listening section of Paper 2 also runs longer. Students who choose Higher Level on reputation often miss the literature requirement, which is substantial work for a Group 2 student and needs to start in the first term of Year 12 rather than the final one.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to have read my child's set literary works?
faqs.answer: For Higher Level oral preparation, yes. The oral starts from an extract from one of the two works the school chose, and schools in Dubai select widely with no standard pair. A tutor working from a general knowledge of French literature cannot run useful extract practice on a text they have not read. Tell us the two titles when you enquire so we match accordingly. For Standard Level students the question does not arise, since the oral uses a visual stimulus linked to the five themes.

faqs.question: Is French B the right choice for a child who studied in a French-system school?
faqs.answer: It is worth questioning with the Diploma coordinator. A student educated in French may be better placed in French A, the Group 1 language and literature route, which assesses literary and non-literary analysis rather than language acquisition. French B will usually produce a high grade for such a student, but it uses a Group 2 slot another language could have filled. The decision has a deadline, normally early in Year 12, so it should be raised in the first fortnight rather than after the first report arrives.

faqs.question: Which grammar errors cost the most marks in French B writing?
faqs.answer: Five families account for most Criterion A losses: choosing between the perfect and imperfect by English instinct, past participle agreement dropped under time pressure, pronoun placement when two pronouns meet in one clause, the subjunctive attempted after the wrong triggers, and register leakage where spoken forms appear in a formal task. The efficient remedy is a personal error log rather than a grammar course, because each student's list is short and specific. Reviewing that list before every timed task eliminates most of them within two months.

faqs.question: How does French B compare with DELF or DALF?
faqs.answer: They do different jobs. French B is a Diploma subject graded one to seven that contributes to the total points universities read. DELF and DALF are standalone certificates aligned to Common European Framework levels, used mainly as evidence of language competence, including for study in France. Universities in the UK, US, Canada and the UAE read the Diploma grade. French-taught programmes in francophone Europe may require a certificate at a named level, which the Diploma grade does not replace, so check the requirement with the institution directly and early.

faqs.question: Can Paper 2 listening be practised properly in an online lesson?
faqs.answer: It is one of the components video handles well. Audio is shared directly rather than played through a room, so quality is better than most classroom speakers, and it can be played twice as the paper requires and then replayed for analysis afterwards, which is the part that teaches. Note-taking is taught explicitly before the second hearing, and errors are logged by question type so the student can see whether marks are going on detail, inference or speed. Weekly practice from early in Year 12 matters more than intensity later.

faqs.question: How much does French B tutoring cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-market tutoring, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised elsewhere in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for in-home blocks. Those are other providers' published figures with their own dates rather than ours. In-home provision costs more for the same teaching because travel time is paid for somewhere in the rate.

faqs.question: Do your tutors visit homes in Dubai for French lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Dubai lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a language subject the format costs very little: scripts are annotated live on a shared screen, orals are recorded and played back, and audio runs under controlled conditions. It also removes the travel that turns a 4pm booking into a 4.30pm start, which over two Diploma years is a substantial number of recovered teaching hours.

faqs.question: When should a French B student start oral preparation?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most schools require. At Standard Level, image description practice can begin in Year 12 because the skill is a structure rather than a body of knowledge. At Higher Level, both literary works should be read by the end of Year 12, since the oral depends on knowing them well enough to discuss an unseen extract. Intensive rehearsal belongs in the weeks before the school's internal recording window, which the Diploma coordinator usually sets early in Year 13 and which is worth asking for in the first fortnight.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both French B and Spanish B for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. The assessment model is identical across Group 2, so criteria work, text types and oral technique transfer between the two, and a tutor who teaches both can manage the interference between two Romance languages deliberately instead of leaving the student to sort it out. The constraint is genuine subject-level competence in both at Diploma register, which is less common than it sounds. We would rather match two specialists than one generalist.

faqs.question: Is extra French tuition needed for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency of a school certificate is a process the Ministry of Education runs, with its own documentary requirements, and it is not something tutoring is required for or can influence. For the British track the Ministry's published requirements concern accredited subject counts and minimum grades rather than language tuition. We can explain how the process works and point you to the official channel, and we do not perform it, guarantee it or speed it up. Nobody should be sold lessons on the basis that equivalency depends on them.

faqs.question: What happens if our preferred French B slot is not available?
faqs.answer: We say so plainly. Diploma French B, and particularly Higher Level with a specific pair of literary works, is a narrow specialism, so the honest options are usually a different time, a short wait for a specialist to free up, or a fortnightly rhythm with marked written work between sessions. What we will not do is place a general French tutor with a Higher Level student who has a literary extract oral in six weeks, because that hour helps nobody and the family discovers the problem too late to fix it.

No card details are taken for the trial. If what your child needs is a course change rather than a tutor, that is what the note will say.

intro.heading: A supply problem wearing a price tag
paragraphs: French B is not a harder course to teach than Spanish B or English B. It is a harder course to staff in Dubai. The city's large Francophone population is concentrated in French-curriculum schools that run the Baccalauréat rather than the Diploma, which means the pool of teachers who know both French and the IB French B criteria is genuinely thin. When a parent in Dubai is quoted an unexpected figure for French B, that is what the figure is measuring.

On published market rates, Dubai tuition runs from AED 45 an hour at the bottom of the online market to AED 650 at the examiner-tier top. The working band for a Diploma language candidate is AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB specialist, with in-home one-to-one published at AED 180 to AED 500 because two journeys are priced in. Those figures come from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table. They describe the market and they are not an IB Gram price list.

What scarcity does to those bands is specific. It compresses availability rather than inflating the headline rate: the figure quoted for French B looks like the figure quoted for Maths, and the difference shows up in which hours exist at all. A family asking for a 17:00 Gulf Standard Time slot in March is competing for a very small number of people, and the tutors who remain free at that point are the ones already carrying a full Year 13 load. Lead time therefore buys more in French B than negotiation does.

The second thing that moves a French B quote is where the student came from. A student who transferred out of a Lycée into an IB school has excellent French and no experience of the Diploma's text types, criteria or oral format - a short, targeted job. A student who has had French as a school subject in an English-medium Dubai school since Year 3 has the opposite profile: they know the assessment culture and have limited French. Those two students need different tutors and different numbers of hours, and quoting them the same thing is how money gets wasted.

Three of the six most visible pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which no UAE family transacts in. One asks the price question in its own frequently-asked list and then declines to answer it. That is why this page leads with the numbers and their sources. IB Gram's own figure is quoted after the free trial lesson, once level, component and session length are known.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school day. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE - sending a tutor to an address is a service we run only in India. For French B that is the point rather than a caveat: the specialist your child needs may be in Lyon, Montreal, Beirut or Mumbai, and the only thing that has to be local is the clock the lesson is set to.

dubai/ib-dp-french-b-tutor.programmesIntro: French appears at several points in a Dubai child's schooling, and which route they are on by Year 11 decides what French B will cost in hours. These are the IB programmes around it, with the French-specific detail rather than the general description.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: French B sits in Group 2 as a language-acquisition course at SL or HL. Three assessed components: productive writing in a named text type, listening and reading comprehension, and an individual oral. HL adds two literary works in French which supply the extract for the HL oral. For a Dubai student the Diploma is where French stops being a school subject and starts being an examined language.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai French B classes are frequently small and frequently mixed, holding students who speak French at home alongside students who have had two periods a week since Year 7. Schools cannot always stream them, so the class pace sits in the middle. That mix is the structural reason French B support is bought in Dubai more often than the enrolment numbers would suggest.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: French acquisition in the Middle Years Programme is assessed in phases against four criteria, internally, with no external paper. A student leaving MYP in Phase 4 or 5 is normally placed into French B HL and Phase 3 points towards SL. Because the phases are not tied to year groups, a student can remain in one phase for two years without the fact surfacing at a parents' evening.
programmes.countryNote: Many Dubai schools offer French as one of two or three language options from Year 7 and timetable it twice a week. Two periods a week for five years produces a student who can manage a conversation and has never written a formal letter in French. That is the commonest starting point for French B support in this city, and it is a register problem rather than a fluency one.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme builds additional-language learning into transdisciplinary units rather than teaching it as a separate subject. In Dubai, several continuum and bilingual schools run genuine French streams at primary level, where a substantial part of the week is taught in French. That early immersion is what separates a comfortable French B HL student at eighteen from a struggling one.
programmes.countryNote: The distinction worth checking is between a French stream and French lessons. A bilingual primary stream delivers hundreds of hours of French across subjects; two weekly French periods deliver a fraction of that. Both appear on a school profile as 'French from FS1', and they produce entirely different students by Year 12.

sections.heading: Why French B in Dubai is priced by scarcity rather than by syllabus
paragraphs: A Dubai parent comparing quotes across subjects will find French B sitting in the same published band as Chemistry or Maths, and will then discover that the hours they want do not exist. That is the shape of a supply constraint rather than a pricing one. The city has a large Francophone population, and most of it is inside French-curriculum schools running the Baccalauréat, where the teachers are excellent at French and have never marked an IB Paper 1 against three criteria.

The tutors who can do both - fluent French and the Diploma's criteria - are a small group, and they are not concentrated in the UAE. Many of them are in France, Canada, Lebanon or in Indian cities with large IB sectors, working to whatever clock their students need. That is why delivery format matters more in this subject than in almost any other: restricting the search to tutors who could reach a Dubai villa by 17:30 removes most of the people who are actually qualified.

The practical consequence for a family is that lead time buys more than negotiation. A block of eight sessions requested in September draws on specialists with open timetables. The same request in March competes for the residue, and the residue is expensive in availability even where the headline rate has not moved. Families who book French B support before the Year 12 summer break consistently get better tutors at better hours than families who wait for a disappointing mock. That is not a sales argument; it is arithmetic about a small pool.

sections.heading: The Dubai Francophone school map, and what it does to your options
paragraphs: Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with IB programmes accounting for roughly a fourteenth of enrolment. The French-curriculum schools inside that number are a distinct ecosystem: they run the French national programme to the Baccalauréat and they are where most of the city's French-speaking children are educated. They are not IB schools, and that single fact shapes every French B conversation in Dubai.

It produces two distinct student populations with opposite needs. The first is the transfer: a child educated in French to Year 10 or Year 11 who moves into an IB school, usually because the family is leaving the French system or relocating. Their French is strong and their understanding of the Diploma is nil. They sit French B because the school offers it, sometimes when French A would fit them better, and what they need is four to six hours of assessment literacy rather than French teaching.

The second is the option-subject student: educated in English, French as one of two or three language choices from Year 7, two periods a week for five years. They can hold a conversation and have never produced a formal register under time pressure. What they need is a term of marked writing. Telling these two students apart in the first conversation is the difference between a short effective engagement and a long vague one, and the table sets out where each kind of Dubai student typically comes from.

sections.heading: From the Baccalauréat to the Diploma: what actually has to change
paragraphs: A student moving out of a French-curriculum school into an IB school in Dubai is not learning French. They are learning a different assessment culture, and the gap is narrow, specific and almost always underestimated by both the family and the receiving school. French-system assessment rewards structured argumentation in a recognisable national form. The Diploma's French B rewards doing what a prompt instructed, in a named text type, for a stated audience, with conceptual understanding visible.

Four things have to change. The text types are new: a blog, a set of guidelines, a proposal, a review, each with conventions that carry marks. The criteria are new and are published, which means a student can be taught to predict their own mark - something the French system does not train. The oral is new: at SL a visual stimulus, at HL an extract from one of two literary works, both with a short sustained delivery and then questions. And the conceptual-understanding criterion rewards register awareness in a way that will feel to a Lycée student like being marked on something that was previously assumed.

None of this takes long. Four to six well-aimed sessions typically does it, which makes a transfer the cheapest French B engagement available in this city. What makes it expensive is leaving it alone on the assumption that a native-standard speaker will be fine, then discovering in a Year 13 mock that they have been writing excellent French answers to a question the paper did not ask. sections.heading: What a French B session costs in Dubai, and what the alternatives cost
paragraphs: The published figures are these. A university-student tutor working online is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to AED 300. An IB or IGCSE specialist is published at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. A named or examiner-tier tutor reaches AED 500 to AED 650. In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs AED 180 to AED 500, with travel in both directions included in that figure. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those bands are the market's, attributed to the pages and rate tables that published them in October 2026, and not ours. Where French B differs from the market's assumption is in what each tier can actually deliver. The bottom tier, in French, is often a fluent speaker with no IB experience - which for a Lycée transfer is useless, because the student already speaks better French than the tutor teaches. The middle tier is where the criteria knowledge lives. The top tier is rarely justified in a Group 2 subject.

The comparison worth making carefully is against the alternatives a Dubai family is really weighing: a group class at a tuition centre, a freelance French speaker found locally, or the school's own support. A group cannot mark four students' written tasks against criteria inside one lesson, which is the product in this subject. A fluent freelancer may not know what a text type is. The school's own clinic, where it exists, is already inside fees you have paid and should be tried first. IB Gram sells one model - one-to-one over live video - and makes no home visits in the UAE.

sections.heading: Where French B marks go: register, accents and the text type
paragraphs: French B written production is marked out of thirty across three criteria: language, message, and conceptual understanding. Dubai students lose marks in a consistent order. Conceptual understanding goes first, because the text type's conventions were not followed and the audience was not addressed. Message goes second, because the response answered the theme instead of the prompt. Language goes last, and it is usually the criterion parents assume is the problem.

Inside the language criterion, French has a specific tax that English does not. Accents are not decoration: a missing or wrong accent can change a word, and systematic accent errors read as carelessness to an examiner reading three hundred scripts. Agreement - gender, number, participle agreement in compound tenses - is the same. Neither is conceptually difficult and both bleed marks for months because nobody logged the pattern. A written task returned with the accent and agreement errors counted, rather than circled, changes behaviour within three weeks.

Register is the deeper problem and it is distinctly French. The gap between tu and vous, between spoken and written forms, between a formal letter's conventions and a blog's, is wider in French than in English, and a student whose French came from conversation has only one register. Asked for a proposal to a municipal authority they produce something fluent and inappropriately familiar. The remedy is the same content written twice, formally and informally, then compared line by line - unglamorous, quick, and the single most reliable French B intervention there is.

sections.heading: The HL literary works and the extract-based oral
paragraphs: Higher Level French B adds two literary works read in French, and those works supply the extract that starts the HL individual oral. That is the component with the longest lead time in the course and the one Dubai families leave latest, because nothing about it generates homework or a grade until the recording window arrives. A student who meets an extract from a work they skimmed in a fortnight has no textual memory to argue from, and the recording goes to the IB for moderation.

The oral itself is short and structured. The student speaks from the extract for a few minutes and then discusses it with the teacher. Marks sit in arguing from the extract rather than summarising it, in sustaining the delivery for the full time, and in handling the question phase with more than single sentences. Students who have rehearsed with unseen extracts five or six times, with playback, walk in having had the experience already. Students who have not are improvising in the one place where improvisation costs most.

The fix is a reading schedule, and it has to be set in Year 12. Dated reading, discussion at the end of each work rather than at the end of the year, and a quotation and context record the student builds themselves. The long UAE summer break between Year 12 and Year 13 is the natural window for most of it: no competing subjects, long uninterrupted stretches, and sessions that are easier to schedule than term-time ones. Families who use that window arrive in Year 13 with the HL load already handled.

sections.heading: French A, French B and the bilingual diploma for a Dubai family
paragraphs: A Francophone family in Dubai has a decision that English-speaking families do not, and schools rarely raise it. A student whose strongest language is French may belong in French A, the Group 1 studies-in-language-and-literature course, rather than in French B. Two Group 1 languages - French A alongside English A, for instance - can earn a bilingual diploma. French A with English B does not produce it, and nor does French B with anything.

Whether the award is worth pursuing depends on the student rather than on the certificate. Two Group 1 courses means two sets of studied works, two individual orals and, at HL, two separate essays landing in the same academic year as the Extended Essay. For a student who reads easily in both languages that is demanding and achievable. For a student who reads comfortably in one, it is a route to two mediocre grades instead of one strong one.

The constraint in Dubai is often availability rather than ability. French A requires a specialist the school may not have, and a school that offers only French B will place a native-standard French speaker there regardless of fit. That student will find the course undemanding, score well, and gain less than they could have. If that describes your child, the conversation to have with the Diploma coordinator is about whether French A can be timetabled at all - and if it cannot, whether the Extended Essay in French B is a way of giving the student something to stretch against.

sections.heading: Scheduling across time zones and around a Dubai week
paragraphs: Because the French B specialist pool is thin in the UAE and deep elsewhere, scheduling becomes part of the service rather than an afterthought. Gulf Standard Time is three hours ahead of central European time and eight to nine ahead of eastern North America, which means a 17:00 Dubai session is early afternoon in Paris and early morning in Montreal. Both are workable; neither happens by accident. Every slot IB Gram quotes is set in Gulf Standard Time, so a family is agreeing to a time on their own clock.

The Dubai week has its own shape. School days commonly end between 14:30 and 15:30, and the mandatory UAE subject periods - Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum - sit on top of six Diploma subjects plus the core. By the time a student is free, the usable window runs from about 16:30 to 21:30, Sunday to Thursday, with weekend mornings available. French B competes for those hours with everything else on the timetable.

Two UAE calendar points matter for planning. During Ramadan most families move sessions to after iftar and keep the weekly rhythm rather than suspending the month, which matters in a Year 13 spring. And the long summer break is the single most productive stretch in a French B two-year plan, because the HL literary works can be read without competing deadlines. Sessions in July and August are easier to book, including with tutors in European time zones who are themselves on holiday timetables.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and why a corrected draft is worth nothing
paragraphs: In a language subject the academic-honesty line is crossed more casually than anywhere else, because correcting French feels like helping. A tutor who takes a student's written task and returns it with the errors fixed has produced a document the student did not write and cannot reproduce. If the task is a practice piece, that is merely a waste of the session. If it forms part of the Extended Essay, it is a misrepresentation of the candidate's work.

What is useful is the opposite movement. Mark the task, count the error types, name the pattern, and hand it back for the student to correct themselves. Three weeks of that changes behaviour; three weeks of corrected drafts changes nothing except the student's confidence, which then collapses in an examination hall. The same applies to the oral: a tutor who scripts a response for memorisation builds something that disintegrates in the question phase, in a recording the IB moderates.

The boundaries worth stating plainly. A tutor may teach text types, drill registers, mark written tasks against the criteria, supply unseen stimuli and extracts, rehearse the oral, set reading and listening, and discuss an Extended Essay's scope and sources. A tutor may not write or rewrite any part of a submitted piece, dictate sentences, script an oral, or supply model answers for reproduction. One provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments for sale; that is an integrity breach we will not imitate. And we link to official IB, Cambridge and Pearson pages rather than redistributing syllabus documents or past papers, which are licensed to schools.

process.description: A Lycée transfer, a bilingual primary stream, five years of two periods a week, or French at home with English schooling. Those four backgrounds need completely different numbers of hours, and naming yours is what prevents a short job being sold as a long one.

process.title: Ask for the slot before the tutor
process.description: In French B availability is the binding constraint, so say which hours work in Gulf Standard Time at the enquiry stage. We would rather tell you that 16:30 on a Tuesday is not available and offer 18:00 than match a tutor you cannot actually book.

process.description: Forty-five minutes, one per family, no card details taken. The tutor sets a timed written task in a named text type, because that produces evidence rather than impressions. You get a written note of which criterion is leaking marks and roughly how many hours it should take.

process.title: Get the figure with its terms
process.description: Our rate is quoted after the trial, alongside the session length, what marking is included, the cancellation notice and whether the figure is inclusive of VAT. An hourly number without those four things is not comparable to anything.

process.title: Review against marked scripts at session six
process.description: Six sessions is enough to see whether accent and agreement errors have dropped and whether the conceptual-understanding mark has moved. If not, the plan changes or the tutor does. We look at marked work, not at reported confidence.

whyPoints.title: The search is not limited to the UAE
whyPoints.description: French B specialists are scarce in Dubai and plentiful elsewhere. Teaching one-to-one over live video means your child is matched on criteria knowledge rather than on who could reach your community by 17:30. faqs.question: Why is it so hard to find an IB French B tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the city's French-teaching capacity sits mostly inside French-curriculum schools running the Baccalauréat, where teachers are strong in French and have never marked an IB Paper 1 against three published criteria. The group who can do both is small, and it is not concentrated in the UAE: many are in France, Canada, Lebanon or Indian cities with large IB sectors. Restricting a search to tutors who could reach your community in person removes most of the qualified pool, which is why online delivery is the practical answer in this subject rather than a compromise.

faqs.question: Does French B cost more per hour in Dubai than Spanish B or English B?
faqs.answer: The published bands are broadly the same across Group 2 languages: roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB specialist, on figures published by providers in this market and by Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table. What differs is availability rather than the headline rate. Scarcity in French B shows up as missing hours at 16:30 to 18:00 Gulf Standard Time, and as fewer HL specialists, rather than as a visible premium on the quote.

faqs.question: My child moved from a Lycée into an IB school. How much French B support will they need?
faqs.answer: Usually four to six sessions, which makes this the cheapest French B engagement available in Dubai. Their French is not the problem. What they have never met is the Diploma's assessment culture: named text types with conventions that carry marks, three published criteria they can be taught to self-mark against, and an individual oral that is a short argued delivery followed by questions. Leaving it alone on the assumption that a native-standard speaker will be fine is how families discover in a Year 13 mock that excellent French answered the wrong question.

faqs.question: Should a French-speaking child in Dubai take French A instead of French B?
faqs.answer: Often yes on fit, and often no on availability. French A is the Group 1 course for a student whose strongest language is French, and two Group 1 languages can earn a bilingual diploma, which French B cannot. But many Dubai schools timetable only French B and will place a native-standard speaker there regardless. Ask the Diploma coordinator directly whether French A can be timetabled. If it cannot, consider an Extended Essay in French B as a way of giving a strong student something to work against.

faqs.question: How much of the French B grade is lost to accents and agreement errors?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter, and more than most students believe. Accents are not decorative in French: a missing or misplaced one can change the word, and systematic errors read as carelessness to an examiner working through hundreds of scripts. Participle and adjective agreement behaves the same way. Neither is conceptually hard, and both persist for months because nobody counted them. A written task returned with the error types counted rather than circled, and handed back for the student to correct, changes the pattern within about three weeks.

faqs.question: What does the tu and vous distinction have to do with marks?
faqs.answer: It is a register decision and register is explicitly assessed. French B's conceptual-understanding criterion rewards showing awareness of context, purpose and audience, and the choice between tu and vous is the most visible register signal in French. A student whose French came largely from conversation has one register and will use it for a proposal to a municipal authority, producing something fluent and inappropriately familiar. Writing the same content twice, once formally and once informally, and comparing line by line, is the fastest fix available in this subject.

faqs.question: How many French B tutored hours should a Dubai family budget for in total?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on the student's background. A Lycée transfer needs four to six. A bilingual-stream student with uneven orthography needs eight to twelve. A student with five years of two periods a week needs ten to fourteen for the register programme. A student who started French in Year 10 and is now in French B needs twenty-five or more, or a conversation about whether they are in the right course. Price the background, not the subject, and ask any provider to estimate hours before agreeing a rate.

faqs.question: When should the two HL literary works be read?
faqs.answer: Across Year 12, on dated schedule, with most of the reading done in the long UAE summer break before Year 13. Those works supply the extract that starts the HL individual oral, which is recorded and moderated, so a student who skimmed them has nothing to argue from. The reason families leave it late is that the works generate no homework and no grade until the recording window arrives. The summer break has no competing deadlines and sessions are easier to schedule then, including with tutors in European time zones.

faqs.question: Can a French B tutor correct my child's written French before they submit it?
faqs.answer: Not for anything submitted, and it is a poor use of a session even for practice. A draft returned with the French already fixed is a document the student did not produce and cannot reproduce under examination conditions, and where the piece forms part of the Extended Essay it is a misrepresentation of their work. What helps is marking: count the error types, name the pattern, hand it back for the student to correct. That changes behaviour. Corrected drafts change only confidence, which then fails in the hall.

faqs.question: How do lessons work if the French tutor is not in the UAE?
faqs.answer: They are booked in Gulf Standard Time, so you agree a time on your own clock and the tutor does the arithmetic. A 17:00 Dubai session is early afternoon in Paris and early morning in eastern Canada; both are routinely workable. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, and written tasks are submitted and returned marked between sessions. IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE - sending a tutor to an address is a service we run only in India - so the tutor's location affects nothing except the clock.

faqs.question: Is a local French speaker cheaper and good enough for French B?
faqs.answer: Cheaper, frequently, and usually not sufficient on its own. Published freelance rates in Dubai run from around AED 60 to AED 300 an hour, and a fluent speaker will improve a student's conversation. What they generally cannot do is mark a written task against the three French B criteria, teach the conventions of a named text type, or rehearse a moderated individual oral, because they have not read the course documents. Conversation practice has real value alongside criterion-level work. As a substitute for it, it tends to cost more over a year rather than less.

faqs.question: Do French tutors working with students in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Any individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years and applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Ask any tutor you engage, and verify on mohre.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Can we book French B sessions through the Dubai summer holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for this subject the summer is the most productive stretch in the whole two-year plan. The HL literary works can be read without competing deadlines, written production can be practised without school homework on top, and specialist availability is better than in term time. Many French tutors in European time zones are also on a lighter timetable then, which widens the choice of hours. Families who use July and August for the HL reading consistently arrive in Year 13 with the heaviest part of the course already behind them.

faqs.question: Does the quoted French B rate include marking and VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask every provider both questions and get the answers in writing before the first invoice. In a language subject the marked written task is the product, so an hourly figure that excludes criterion-level marking is not comparable with one that includes it. On tax, we will not state how UAE value added tax applies to tuition fees as a general matter, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation we do not hold. What any provider can tell you is whether their quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive of VAT.

faqs.question: What happens if no French B HL specialist is available for our slot?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date, rather than matched to a fluent French speaker with the subject name attached. HL French B requires someone who can teach the two literary works and rehearse an extract-based moderated oral, and that pool is small. The options are a different hour with the right specialist, a tutor in another time zone working to Gulf Standard Time, or a short wait. Delivery is online in every case, so geography is never the constraint; the constraint is how few people teach this course at this level.

dubai/ib-dp-geography-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Diploma Geography: the three core units, the optional themes a Dubai school has chosen for Paper 1, the Higher Level core extension, and the fieldwork report. Each one marks written work between sessions and sends the mark with the reason attached.

intro.heading: What visible progress in Diploma Geography looks like, six weeks at a time
paragraphs: Geography is the Diploma subject where parents most often cannot tell whether tutoring is working. The content feels familiar, the student sounds knowledgeable, and the grade stays at a 4 or a 5. That happens because Diploma Geography marks are not awarded for knowing about population change or coastal erosion. They are awarded for answering a command term inside a level descriptor, for treating data properly, and for a fieldwork report that satisfies six specific criteria. A student can know a great deal and score 6 out of 10 on every extended answer.

So the question to ask a Geography tutor is not whether your child is improving. It is what the evidence is. There are four pieces of evidence available, and all four can be produced inside a tutoring relationship. The first is a marked extended answer with the level descriptor named, because Paper 1 and Paper 2 both end in a 10-mark question chosen from two. The second is a Paper 2 Section A structured answer, where data manipulation and short definitions either happen or do not.

The third is the fieldwork report, which is the most measurable component in the whole subject. It is marked out of 25 against criteria A to F, each carrying its own allocation: 3 marks for the question and geographic context, 3 for method, 6 for quality and treatment of information, 8 for written analysis, 2 for the conclusion, 3 for evaluation. A draft can be read against those six letters and scored. A family can watch that score move across three drafts, which is as close to a measurable outcome as this subject offers.

The fourth is a command-term audit. Examine, evaluate, discuss, suggest, justify and analyse each demand a different structure, and most mid-band answers are the right content answering the wrong verb. A list of which terms a student currently handles and which they do not is cheap to produce and immediately actionable. IB Gram tutors keep that list and show it to you. Examine and evaluate are almost always the last two to come off it, in that order.

Those four artefacts exist whether or not anyone collects them, which is the frustrating part. A Dubai Diploma student writes extended answers every week in class and gets most of them back with a number and a tick. The work of tutoring is partly teaching and partly record-keeping: marking the same kind of question often enough that a trend line becomes real, and showing the trend to the person paying for it. A mock paper in February cannot change a grade that a weekly marked answer in October could have moved.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled around Dubai school hours in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address; home visits are offered only in India. For Geography that trade matters more than usual, because the teaching involves sharing maps, data sets, choropleth exercises and the student's own fieldwork spreadsheet on screen, which works better over a shared screen than over a kitchen table. The first lesson is free and there is no package to buy first.

Fieldwork report scored against criteria A to F across successive drafts

dubai/ib-dp-geography-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Geography arrives at IB Gram through three IB routes. The evidence a family should expect is different in each, because Middle Years criteria, Diploma markbands and the Career-related reflective project measure different things.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Geography
programmes.description: Three core units examined on Paper 2, two optional themes at Standard Level or three at Higher Level examined on Paper 1, a Higher Level core extension examined on Paper 3, and a fieldwork report of up to 2,500 words marked out of 25. Every component produces an artefact that can be marked and tracked, which is why progress here is unusually visible when somebody bothers to record it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's Diploma cohort is a small slice of a very large private sector: KHDA counted 387,441 students in 227 private schools in 2024-25, with the IB at 7 per cent of enrolment. Geography groups in Dubai Diploma schools are often smaller than History or Economics groups, so a student's own marked work is the only reliable comparison available to them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Individuals and Societies
programmes.description: Assessed on four criteria with descriptors rather than on Diploma markbands, and that difference is the gap students carry into DP1. Middle Years investigations reward process and reflection; Diploma extended answers reward a judgement answering a command term in a fixed number of minutes. The evidence worth collecting in MYP is timed writing, because that is what nobody has yet asked for.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma produce students who are comfortable with long investigations and uncomfortable with a 20-minute extended answer. Schools that switch to IGCSE at 14 produce the reverse. A first session identifies which of the two profiles a Dubai student has by marking one timed answer and one short investigation extract side by side.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme with Diploma Geography
programmes.description: Career-related students take Diploma courses alongside a career-related study and a reflective project. Geography is a common choice where the career pathway touches sustainability, hospitality or urban development. The syllabus and the marking are identical to the Diploma version; the difference is contact time and the fact that the student is often the only one in the school taking the subject at that level.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools offer the Career-related Programme compared with the Diploma, so a Career-related Geography student may have no classmates in the subject at all. That removes the informal evidence most students rely on, which makes a marked piece of work every week the only real measure of where they stand before a mock paper arrives.

dubai/ib-dp-geography-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: A Dubai school chooses which optional themes it teaches, and that choice decides half of your child's Paper 1. The list below covers the seven optional themes, the three core units and the Higher Level extension topics. Check your child's course outline before booking a tutor, because a Freshwater specialist is not an Extreme environments specialist.

subjects.name: Option A: Freshwater - drainage basins
subjects.description: Hydrographs, drainage basin stores and flows, flood management and competing demands on water. Students handle the physical processes adequately and lose marks on the management sections, where an extended answer needs named places and a judgement rather than a list of hard and soft engineering.

subjects.name: Option B: Oceans and coastal margins
subjects.description: Ocean currents and circulation, coastal processes and landforms, coastal management and ocean governance. The common failure is treating sediment cells descriptively. Marks come from explaining transfer between cells and applying it to a named coastline, which is a skill worth practising on the Gulf coast itself.

subjects.name: Option C: Extreme environments
subjects.description: Hot arid, semi-arid, periglacial and high-altitude environments, their processes and the opportunities and risks of using them. Dubai students have a genuine advantage here on arid processes and routinely waste it by not using local examples with precision.

subjects.name: Option D: Geophysical hazards
subjects.description: Earthquakes, volcanoes, mass movement, hazard risk and vulnerability, and management strategies. Case study discipline is everything: two events with dates, magnitudes and specific response failures outscore six events mentioned in passing every time.

subjects.name: Option E: Leisure, tourism and sport
subjects.description: Participation, tourism and sport at local to global scales, the growth of tourism hotspots and the sustainability of them. Often chosen because it looks easy, then marked harshly because students write opinion where the question wants a framework such as the tourism life cycle applied to a named place.

subjects.name: Option F: Food and health
subjects.description: Variations in food consumption and health, the global food system, and disease diffusion with barriers and strategies. Data-heavy, which suits students who are already strong on Paper 2 Section A and exposes those who are not.

subjects.name: Option G: Urban environments
subjects.description: Urban populations, economic activity, urban environmental and social stresses, and resilience and planning. The most useful option for a Dubai student doing urban fieldwork, because the theory and the primary data collection can be made to reinforce each other.

subjects.name: Core unit 1: Changing population
subjects.description: Population distribution, megacity growth, forced migration, ageing and gender inequality. Examined on Paper 2, where Section A wants precise definitions and correct manipulation of population data, not description of a pyramid.

subjects.name: Core unit 2: Global climate - vulnerability and resilience
subjects.description: Causes of global climate change, consequences, and mitigation and adaptation. The unit where students write the most and score the least, because the content is familiar from general reading and the answers drift into advocacy instead of geography.

subjects.name: Core unit 3: Global resource consumption and security
subjects.description: Changing demand for resources, the water-food-energy nexus and resource stewardship. Pairs directly with the UAE's own water and energy position, which gives a Dubai student locally verifiable examples that an examiner rarely sees.

subjects.name: Higher Level extension: power, places and networks
subjects.description: Global interactions, flows of people, money and data, and the role of powerful organisations. Examined on Paper 3 as one of two extended answers worth 12 marks each, where the demand is synthesis across the whole course rather than recall of one unit.

subjects.name: Higher Level extension: global risks and resilience
subjects.description: Geopolitical and economic risks, technology, and the resilience of places and systems. Paper 3 answers here need a clear line of argument sustained over twelve marks, which is a different writing task from anything on Paper 1 or Paper 2.

dubai/ib-dp-geography-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities and the fieldwork a Geography student can actually do nearby
dubai/ib-dp-geography-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Geography is the one Diploma subject where where you live affects the coursework, because the fieldwork report needs primary data from a real place. These notes are about data collection and session timing. Nobody is being sent to an address.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Beach profiles, sediment sampling and visitor surveys along a managed shoreline sit within walking distance, which makes Option B fieldwork genuinely achievable rather than theoretical for families here.

regions.name: Deira and Al Fahidi
regions.note: The best urban land-use mapping and pedestrian-flow counting in the emirate, with a clear transition between historic and commercial zones. Environmental quality surveys here produce the contrast an Option G investigation needs.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: High-rise microclimate transects work well: temperature, wind speed and shade measured along a single street at fixed intervals. Evening sessions from 7pm suit apartment households where a parent gets home late.

regions.name: The Sustainable City and Dubailand
regions.note: A purpose-built low-carbon community next to conventional suburban development gives an unusually clean comparison for urban resilience and resource consumption fieldwork, with permission usually easier to arrange than in a commercial district.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Barsha
regions.note: Dense school cluster and large planned communities. Questionnaire-based investigations on leisure provision and green space access are practical here, and weekend morning sessions are the norm rather than the exception.

regions.name: Al Qudra and Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Desert margin and irrigated landscape within reach, which is the strongest local setting for Option C arid processes. Heat makes anything between late May and September unusable outdoors before about 6am.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and International City
regions.note: Further from the Diploma school cluster, so long school runs and late arrivals home. Online sessions remove a 40-minute each-way tutor commute that in-home tutoring in this market charges for.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma Geography in the Barsha and Emirates Hills schools
schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of Diploma Geography teaching in Dubai. Groups here are big enough that a school runs residential or day fieldwork, so a student's primary data is usually collected with the class and the tutoring question becomes what to do with it.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma Geography in the coastal and creek-side schools
schoolClusters.note: Schools close enough to the shoreline or the creek for coastal and urban fieldwork to be done locally. Students here often have better primary data than their analysis sections deserve, which is exactly where criterion C and criterion D marks are lost.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma Geography in the villa-belt schools

sections.heading: The four pieces of evidence that show Geography tutoring is working
paragraphs: Diploma Geography produces more markable artefacts than almost any other subject in the group, and a family that collects them can answer the value-for-money question in six weeks rather than at results. The table below is the evidence pack IB Gram tutors keep for a Dubai Geography student. None of it requires a school report or a mock paper to generate, which matters because mocks arrive too late to change anything.

The reason this works better in Geography than in most subjects is the structure of the assessment. Both Paper 1 and Paper 2 end in a 10-mark extended answer chosen from two, marked against published level descriptors. Paper 3 at Higher Level is two 12-mark answers. Section A of Paper 2 is short, data-based and objectively right or wrong. So a tutor can produce a comparable mark every single week, from the same kind of question, and the trend line is real rather than impressionistic.

Watch two things in the numbers. The first is whether Section A accuracy and extended-answer marks move together or separately, because they are different problems: Section A is precision and definitions, extended answers are argument and command terms. A student strong on one and weak on the other needs a plan that says so. The second is whether the fieldwork score moves between drafts. A report that scores the same on criterion D across two drafts means the feedback was not understood, and that is a teaching problem to fix rather than a student failing.

sections.heading: Paper 1: the optional themes and the answer that decides the grade
paragraphs: Paper 1 examines the optional themes a school has chosen, two at Standard Level in 90 minutes and three at Higher Level in 135 minutes, and is worth 35% at both levels. Each theme is structured the same way: part A has structured short-answer questions, and part B asks for one extended answer chosen from two, worth 10 marks. Those 10-mark answers are where Standard Level grades are decided, because they carry a large share of the paper and are marked against level descriptors rather than a points list.

The pattern in mid-band Dubai scripts is consistent and fixable. Part A answers are competent. The extended answer contains everything the student knows about the topic, arranged chronologically or by category, with no sustained position answering the verb. An answer to 'examine the view that coastal management transfers risk rather than reducing it' that describes three management strategies cannot reach the top descriptor, however accurate the description is, because the examiner is looking for the view to be examined.

Sessions work on the plan rather than the prose. Thirty seconds of planning produces a line of argument, two or three places with specifics attached, and a destination for the final paragraph. Students resist this because planning feels like lost writing time, so the practice is deliberately timed: plan, write, mark against the descriptor, then rewrite only the first and last paragraphs. That cycle costs twenty minutes and moves more marks than an hour of content revision, which is why it recurs in almost every weekly session.
