dubai/ib-dp-geography-tutor.programmesIntro: Geography sits at the end of a pathway that starts long before the Diploma, and the habits that decide the grade are built in the earlier programmes: reading a map properly, describing a pattern before explaining it, and treating data as something to be interpreted rather than copied. Here is what each programme contributes.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Geography arrives through MYP Individuals and Societies, where criterion B on investigating and criterion D on thinking critically do most of the preparatory work. The useful inheritance is comfort with primary data collection and with evaluating a source. The gap is quantitative: MYP rewards a well-argued interpretation, while the Diploma also expects a correctly constructed graph and an appropriate statistical test.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP cohorts differ widely in how much fieldwork and data work they do, and the difference is visible within a fortnight of DP1. Departments here report the same pattern: students comfortable describing a place and uncomfortable calculating anything, which is the exact combination that produces a mid-band mark on any question carrying a figure.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Geography runs across both Diploma years in Group 3 at Standard or Higher Level. Candidates sit a paper on the school's chosen option themes, a paper on the compulsory core, and complete an internally assessed fieldwork report marked against lettered criteria. Higher Level adds a third paper on the core extension. Confirm current weightings and word limits in the IB subject guide at ibo.org.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Geography is offered less universally than Economics or Business Management, and where it runs the cohort is often small enough that the option themes are decided by whoever teaches the subject that year. That is why the first question before hiring is which themes the department teaches, not which tutor has the best profile.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. A CP candidate taking Geography sits the same papers and completes the same fieldwork report, so subject support is identical, and the research habits transfer directly to the reflective project.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools run the Career-related Programme, so a CP candidate taking Geography is usually alone on that route in their year. The practical consequence is calendar pressure rather than content: the reflective project and the fieldwork report land in overlapping weeks, and without planning in DP1 one of them is written badly in a hurry.

dubai/ib-dp-geography-tutor.subjectsIntro: Diploma Geography is a compulsory core, a set of option themes chosen by the school, a fieldwork report and a layer of quantitative technique that runs through all of it. Below is what a tutor works on with a Dubai candidate, and where the marks go missing in each part.

subjects.name: Changing population
subjects.description: Population distribution, megacity growth, ageing, forced migration and the indices used to measure inequality. Marks are lost on scale: a candidate describes a global pattern when the question named one country, or quotes a dependency ratio without saying what it implies for policy.

subjects.name: Global climate: vulnerability and resilience
subjects.description: The energy balance, atmospheric circulation, causes and consequences of warming, and the civil and governmental responses to it. The technical half carries the marks, and students who cannot explain the mechanism before describing the impact cap in the middle band.

subjects.name: Global resource consumption and security
subjects.description: Resource stewardship, water, food and energy security, waste, and the debates about limits to growth. This is the unit where UAE material is strongest, and where candidates most often rely on general assertion when a named scheme with a figure was available.

subjects.name: The option themes
subjects.levels: Chosen by the school, two at Standard and three at Higher Level
subjects.description: Freshwater, oceans and coastal margins, extreme environments, geophysical hazards, leisure and tourism, food and health, and urban environments. The department chooses, and a tutor who has taught different themes from your child's is the single commonest mismatch in this subject.

subjects.name: The Higher Level core extension
subjects.description: Power, places and networks, human development and diversity, and global risks and resilience, examined in a separate paper. It is conceptually the hardest part of the course and the part Higher Level candidates are least prepared for, because it is usually taught last.

subjects.name: The fieldwork report
subjects.description: An investigation built on the student's own primary data, marked against lettered criteria with a word ceiling. The marks sit in method, presentation of data and the quality of the analysis rather than in the writing, which is why a well-written report can still score in the middle.

subjects.name: Graphical and cartographic techniques
subjects.description: Choropleth and isoline maps, proportional symbols, flow lines, scatter graphs, dispersion diagrams, triangular graphs and population pyramids. Each has conventions, and marks are lost on the conventions rather than on the understanding behind them.

subjects.name: Statistical techniques
subjects.description: Measures of central tendency and spread, Spearman's rank correlation and chi-square, with the reasoning about when each is appropriate. Choosing the wrong test, or running the right test and failing to state what the result means, are the two recurring errors.

subjects.name: Command terms in Geography
subjects.description: Describe, explain, examine, evaluate, discuss and justify require different structures and carry different mark expectations. A candidate who explains when asked to examine has written a good answer to an easier question and will score accordingly, however accurate the content.

subjects.name: Case-study discipline
subjects.description: Named places, dated schemes, specific figures and a source for each. One page per unit is the working standard. Students who revise from thirty pages per unit know everything in general and nothing precisely, which is visible in every extended answer they write.

dubai/ib-dp-geography-tutor.regionsIntro: For a Geography family in Dubai the practical questions are when a session can start after the school run and whether the student still has the concentration left for a data question. Below are the communities the enquiries come from, with that in mind.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: The deepest band of Diploma provision in the emirate, and the band where Geography is most likely to run at Higher Level with three option themes. The requests here are usually for marked scripts and core-extension help rather than content teaching.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Quoz
regions.note: Short school runs, which makes a five o'clock start realistic, and families who tend to book ninety minutes. That suits this subject: a timed data question and the mark-by-mark read-back afterwards will not fit inside an hour.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Established Diploma schools and short commutes. A common request here is a late slot for a candidate also carrying Arabic as a first language, which has its own after-school demands on the same evenings.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Later bus arrivals push a realistic start past half past six, and smaller Diploma cohorts mean Geography is sometimes taught by a teacher whose main subject is something else. That shows up first in the statistical techniques.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown Dubai and DIFC
regions.note: Apartment living with short runs and students who are usually strong on urban content and weaker on the physical option themes. The useful purchase from this band is technique rather than teaching, bought as marked scripts.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, The Springs and Motor City
regions.note: Inland, with a forty-minute school run at the wrong hour and almost no local specialist supply. Weekend morning sessions are most popular here and are better for data work than a tired weekday evening.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Barsha, Emirates Hills and Dubai Hills band
schoolClusters.note: Where Geography is most reliably offered at both levels with a specialist department and a structured fieldwork programme. Families in this band generally want marked extended responses and help with the Higher Level core extension, which is usually taught last.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Deira and the Festival City corridor
schoolClusters.note: Smaller cohorts, where option themes are often driven by who teaches the subject that year and the quantitative side of the course can be thin. Requests from this corridor lean towards statistical technique and towards closing an option theme that was taught quickly.

modes.title: Techniques drilling, short and frequent
modes.description: Twenty minutes of every session spent on graphs, maps and statistics until the checklist is signed off: a choropleth drawn to convention, a Spearman's rank calculated and interpreted, a dispersion diagram read correctly. Short and frequent beats one long session, because these are motor habits rather than concepts.
bullets: A written checklist the student works through and signs off
Each technique produced unaided before it is marked as done
Interpretation always attached: a calculated value with no meaning stated earns little

modes.title: Extended-response marking across a term
modes.description: A timed extended response sat between sessions, marked before the session with the band named and three corrections written, and read back during the hour. Fortnightly through DP1 and weekly in the final term, because this changes a habit and habits need repetition rather than intensity.

Band named, three corrections, and the next attempt specified
A running list of recurring faults that the student maintains

sections.heading: What progress looks like when the content is already known
paragraphs: Most Dubai families who contact us about Geography have a child who is not short of knowledge. They can talk about desalination, the demographic transition and urban heat islands, and their notes are thorough. The marks sit at 5 or 6 anyway, and the school report says the student needs to develop their answers more fully, which is accurate and completely unactionable. For this candidate, progress is not more Geography. It is a measurable change in how an answer is built, and it can be tracked precisely.

Here is what the change looks like in sequence. In week one the extended responses describe where a judgement was required. By week three the student is naming a case study with a figure in every paragraph instead of in the first one. By week five the answers are shorter and the final paragraph answers the question rather than summarising the essay. By week eight the student can predict their own band before the tutor marks it. That last milestone is the real target, because a candidate who can mark themselves no longer needs to be marked.

None of that is visible unless somebody writes it down, which is why the artefacts matter more than the hours. A parent who has four marked scripts from four consecutive weeks can see whether the band moved and whether the same three corrections keep reappearing. A parent with four pleasant progress conversations has nothing to audit. Ask for the artefacts at the start rather than after a term, because by then the only remaining evidence is the mock grade and it will be too late to change the plan.

sections.heading: Reading a returned Geography script without knowing the markbands
paragraphs: Every Dubai parent has seen a Geography script covered in short marginal comments and had no idea what to do with it. The comments are a diagnostic if you know how to read them, and they fall into four recognisable groups. Each group points at a different problem and a different fix, and three of the four are quick. Knowing which one your child's script is full of is enough to tell a tutor what the first month should do.

The most frequent comment in Dubai scripts is some variant of develop or explain further, which almost never means write more words. It means a causal step is missing: the answer states a cause and an effect without the mechanism between them. The second group is where is your example, which means the paragraph asserted rather than supported. The third is read the question, which usually means the command term was answered as an easier one. The fourth concerns data, and appears only on questions with a figure or a map attached.

Count them before buying anything. If the script is mostly example comments, you have a content and case-study problem, which is a few hours per unit and closes permanently. If it is mostly develop comments, you have a technique problem, which takes a term of marking. If it is mostly data comments, you have the cheapest problem in the subject and it can be fixed in three or four short drills. If it is all four in equal measure, start with the data and the examples, because they move fastest and the confidence helps.

sections.heading: The techniques column: what a Geography candidate must be able to produce
paragraphs: Geography is a quantitative subject that students often choose believing it is not, and the techniques layer is where that belief gets expensive. The course expects candidates to construct and interpret specific graphs and maps to convention, and to select and apply statistical tests appropriately in the fieldwork report. These are not optional refinements. They appear in the examination, they carry marks in the internal assessment, and they are the part of the course least likely to be drilled in a crowded Dubai timetable.

The good news is that this is the most trainable part of the subject. Each technique has a short, fixed set of requirements, and twenty minutes at the start of a session is enough to work through one. A checklist makes it auditable: the student produces each technique unaided, the tutor checks it against the conventions, and it gets signed off. A Dubai parent with a signed checklist knows exactly what their child can and cannot do, which is more information than most school reports give in a year.

The recurring error across all of them is the same. A student calculates or draws correctly and then fails to say what it means. A Spearman's rank value with no statement of strength, direction and significance earns a fraction of the marks available. A choropleth with no key and no title loses marks a six-year-old would not lose. Teach the interpretation sentence as part of the technique rather than as a separate skill, and most of these marks stop leaking immediately.

sections.heading: The extended-response ladder, command term by command term
paragraphs: Dubai candidates lose more marks to command terms in Geography than to anything else, because the subject uses six of them with real distinctions between them and schools rarely teach those distinctions explicitly. Describe asks what the pattern is. Explain asks for the mechanism. Examine asks for the mechanism plus a consideration of what it means. Evaluate and discuss ask for competing positions weighed against each other. Justify asks for a decision defended against alternatives.

A student who answers an examine question with a good explanation has written a correct answer to a smaller question, and the markband will treat it accordingly. This is almost never a knowledge failure, which is why teaching the topic again does nothing. What moves it is the drill of answering a single topic twice under two different command terms in one session and comparing the two attempts against the descriptors. Candidates see the difference in one sitting, which is a better outcome than three explanations.

The ladder also fixes the length problem. Mid-band answers in this subject are usually too long, because the student is compensating for the missing move by adding more of the move they know. Once the structure is right, answers get shorter and score higher, which is the single most counter-intuitive thing to tell a hard-working student in Dubai and the one most reliably confirmed by the next marked script. Keep the previous attempt beside the new one when you read it back, because the comparison is what makes the point stick.

sections.heading: A ten-week evidence log and what each week proves
paragraphs: A plan with artefacts attached can be audited by anyone, so here is a ten-week shape with the evidence stated for each stage. It assumes a candidate whose content is broadly sound and whose marks sit in the middle, which is the most common Dubai profile for this subject. Adapt the units to your school's option themes, but keep the structure: produce something every week, mark it, and keep it.

Notice that the first full timed paper lands in week two rather than week eight. The point of early bad news is that there is still time to act on it. Notice also that the techniques checklist runs alongside everything rather than being scheduled as a block, because twenty minutes a week for ten weeks establishes these habits far better than one long session does. And notice the week-eight milestone, which is the student predicting their own band before the mark is revealed.

If the log fills up and the band has not moved by week six, the plan was wrong and should change. That happens, and the honest handling of it is what separates a plan from a subscription. The commonest cause is a misdiagnosis at the start, usually a technique problem treated as a content problem because the student seemed hesitant about the material. The second commonest is that the real problem was the fieldwork report all along and nobody looked at it, because everyone was busy with the written papers that felt more urgent.

sections.heading: Core units, option themes and what varies between Dubai schools
paragraphs: Geography is two courses in a trench coat: a compulsory core that every candidate sits, and a set of option themes chosen by the department. The core units on population, climate and resource security are the same in every school in Dubai. The option themes are not, and there are seven to choose from, which means two candidates in neighbouring schools can share nothing on one of their papers. A tutor match depends on this far more than on general subject experience.

The practical effect is the commonest wasted purchase in the subject. A family hires an excellent Geography tutor whose option themes are freshwater and urban environments, and the school teaches extreme environments and geophysical hazards. The core work is fine and half the examination is not covered, and the mismatch frequently surfaces only when a past paper is attempted. One email to the department before booking prevents it: ask which themes, in which order, and whether the Higher Level core extension has been started.

Transfers inside Dubai create the same problem in a sharper form. A student who moves school in DP1 may arrive having studied two themes their new school does not teach, and carrying none of the material for the ones it does. That is a real content gap of substantial size, not a settling-in issue, and it needs a counted plan rather than reassurance. Establish exactly which themes are missing, how many weeks each needs, and whether the school will provide its own notes before buying anything.

sections.heading: UAE material that doubles as case-study evidence
paragraphs: Geography candidates in Dubai have an advantage they almost never use: they live inside several of the course's set pieces. Water security in a hyper-arid environment, energy transition at scale, a planned city with a measurable heat island, food imported across a long supply chain, and a population structure unlike almost anywhere else. All of it is examinable material for the core units, and all of it is checkable against official sources, which is what turns an interesting fact into a mark.

The discipline is the same as in any case study: named, located, dated, sourced and used. A candidate who writes that the UAE depends heavily on desalination has written a true sentence that earns nothing. A candidate who names a specific plant, states its capacity with a date and a source, and connects it to the energy cost of water in a resource-security answer has written an examinable paragraph. The sourcing habit also transfers directly to the fieldwork report, where data provenance carries marks.

Two cautions. First, verify before citing, and prefer the official publisher over a news summary of it: the Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre, the relevant authority's own site, or the government portal at u.ae. Second, keep the geography in the answer. The course is marking physical and human processes, interrelationships and management responses, not opinions about policy, and a paragraph that stays on mechanism and evidence is both the safer and the higher-scoring choice.

sections.heading: The fieldwork report boundary, and what honesty looks like here
paragraphs: The fieldwork report has to be the student's own investigation, built on data the student collected, with the analysis and the evaluation theirs. A tutor may teach the techniques, explain what each criterion rewards, ask whether the data collected can support the conclusion being reached, and point out that a section does not answer the question it opened with. A tutor may not supply the text, choose the question, construct the analysis or rework a draft to completion.

In Geography specifically there is a data temptation worth naming. A student whose primary data came out messy, which is normal and often interesting, is tempted to tidy it. Removing inconvenient readings, or quietly inventing a few to smooth a line of best fit, is fabrication, and it is the one error in this component that cannot be argued down. The correct response is the one real geographers use: report the messy data, explain in the evaluation why it is messy, and say what you would do differently. Criteria reward that.

On materials, be careful what any tutor hands over. Reproducing IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is not permitted, and the right move is to reference the official page and link to it. The same applies to the published markbands your child's teacher can show you. Any provider offering a bundle of mark schemes as a selling point is offering something they should not have, which also tells you how they handle the honesty line on the report itself.

sections.heading: Cost, availability and how the lessons actually run
paragraphs: Published rates in Dubai run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise their from-prices, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, to the AED 200 to 450 and above specialist band on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, with BartyED quoting AED 650 at the premium end. Those are market figures rather than ours. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, which makes any independent comparison impossible before committing.

In an evidence-led plan the number to interrogate is not the rate but the marked work. Reading and marking a Geography extended response properly, with the band named and three corrections written, takes a tutor twenty to thirty minutes, and whether that happens between sessions is the difference between a plan and a conversation. Ask how many marked scripts the plan includes, over how many weeks, and whether the techniques checklist is part of it. Then compare totals rather than hourly rates.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, recorded so a student can rewatch a read-back, with annotated scripts shared as files so a parent can read exactly what was marked. Geography is a smaller subject in Dubai than Economics, so specialist coverage is thinner, and a request that needs specific option themes in a peak fortnight can take a week to fill; we say so rather than substituting. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE, and that service runs only in India.

process.title: Send the option themes and a recent marked script
process.description: The two things that make a first message useful are which option themes the department teaches and a photograph of a recently marked piece of work. The themes decide who is a genuine match. The script decides what the first month does, because the pattern of marginal comments on it identifies the problem better than any description of the symptoms.

process.title: A free diagnostic hour that produces a marked script
process.description: The first lesson is free, one per student, with no card details taken, and it is built around a timed extended response sat beforehand. It comes back with the band named, three corrections and a statement of which problem you actually have: content, technique or data handling. That artefact is the basis for everything that follows.

process.title: A plan stated in artefacts rather than in hours
process.description: The plan says how many marked scripts, which techniques will be signed off, how many case-study sheets the student will build, and what the total comes to. Compare the total against the AED bands published for Dubai. A plan measured only in hours cannot be audited by a parent, which is precisely why so many are written that way.

process.title: Monthly review against the log, including the option to stop
process.description: Each month brings the marked scripts, the checklist and a short written note on what has not moved. If the band is the same after six weeks and the same three corrections keep appearing, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes or ends. Stopping costs nothing beyond the sessions already taught.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can audit without reading a markband
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts with the band named, a signed techniques checklist, case-study sheets built by the student and a written monthly note. Four artefacts, all shareable as files. You should be able to see whether the grade is moving without taking anyone's word for it, including ours.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the department's option themes
whyPoints.description: Seven option themes exist and your child sits two or three of them, chosen by the school. A tutor who has taught different ones covers the core and misses half the examination, which is the most expensive mismatch in this subject. We ask for the themes in writing before suggesting anybody.

whyPoints.title: The quantitative layer treated as a checklist, not an afterthought
whyPoints.description: Choropleths, isolines, scatter graphs, Spearman's rank, dispersion diagrams and population pyramids each have conventions, and marks leak on the conventions rather than on the understanding. Twenty minutes a session until each is produced unaided and signed off, with the interpretation sentence taught as part of the technique.

whyPoints.title: Self-marking as the stated end point
whyPoints.description: The target is a candidate who can predict their own band before anyone marks it, because at that point the tutoring has done its job. Plans here are written to finish rather than to renew, and we would rather tell you the plan is complete than keep a weekly booking running until the examinations.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, which widens the specialist pool
whyPoints.description: There are no home visits in the UAE. For a subject taught in fewer Dubai schools than Economics, that is the difference between choosing among the Geography specialists willing to drive to your community at your hour and choosing among everyone who has taught your child's option themes.

faqs.question: What should I be able to see after four weeks of Geography tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four things, all of them physical. Four marked scripts, each with the band stated and three specific corrections written on it. A techniques checklist showing which graphs, maps and statistical tests your child can now produce unaided. At least one one-page case-study sheet the student built themselves. And a short written note saying what has moved and what has not. If the only evidence after four weeks is a conversation about how the sessions are going, there is nothing to audit and no basis for deciding whether to continue.

faqs.question: My child's Geography script is covered in develop comments. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Almost never that they should write more words. It means a causal step is missing: the answer states a cause and an effect with the mechanism between them left implied. The fix is structural rather than content-based. Write every paragraph as because, therefore, so what, and cut whatever does not serve that chain. It is a habit rather than a gap, so it takes a term of fortnightly marked responses rather than a weekend of teaching. Most candidates who do this produce shorter answers that score higher, which surprises hard-working students considerably.

faqs.question: Which statistical tests does a Geography candidate need to be able to apply?
faqs.answer: Measures of central tendency and spread, including the interquartile range, plus Spearman's rank correlation and chi-square, together with the reasoning about when each is appropriate. Confirm the current requirements in the IB subject guide at ibo.org, since guides are revised. The recurring error is not the arithmetic: it is a correct coefficient reported with no statement of strength, direction or significance, which earns a fraction of the marks available. Teach the interpretation sentence as part of the test rather than as a separate skill and most of those marks stop leaking straight away.

faqs.question: Does my child need to draw maps and graphs by hand in the examination?
faqs.answer: Candidates are expected to construct and interpret graphical and cartographic representations to convention, and the conventions are where marks go rather than the artistry. A choropleth needs sequential shading, a stated class interval, a key and a title. An isoline map needs interpolation between known points at a consistent interval. A scatter graph needs the independent variable on the horizontal axis and units labelled. None of that requires drawing skill, and all of it requires practice. Twenty minutes a session for a few weeks usually clears the whole checklist.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether the problem is content or technique in Geography?
faqs.answer: Read the marginal comments on a recently marked script and count them. If most say where is your example or evidence, the problem is content and case-study discipline, which is two to four hours per unit and closes permanently. If most say develop or explain further, the problem is technique, which takes a term of marking. If most relate to a figure or a map, it is data handling, the fastest fix in the subject. If the comments are evenly spread, start with examples and data because they move quickest and the early improvement helps everything else.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe, explain and examine in a Geography answer?
faqs.answer: Describe asks what the pattern is, stated with values and locations from the resource. Explain asks for the mechanism linking cause to effect. Examine asks for that mechanism plus a consideration of its implications or interrelationships. A student who answers an examine question with a strong explanation has answered a smaller question well and will be marked accordingly, which is why teaching the topic again changes nothing. The drill that works is answering one topic twice under two different command terms in a single session and comparing both attempts against the descriptors.

faqs.question: Why do Geography students lose marks on graph interpretation?
faqs.answer: Because they describe the resource instead of using it. A question that supplies a graph expects values quoted from it, anomalies identified, and the pattern connected to the geography being asked about. Mid-band answers mention that the graph shows an increase and then write a general paragraph that could have been written without the graph at all. The rule that fixes it quickly: every paragraph in a resource-based answer must contain a number taken from the resource. Three or four short drills under that rule usually clears the problem entirely.

faqs.question: Should Geography case studies be local to the UAE?
faqs.answer: Some of them, not all. Examiners reward named, located, dated and sourced examples wherever they come from, and a candidate in Dubai has unusually good local material for resource security, urban environments and population structure. Using it is an advantage because the student can explain it with more confidence. The discipline is verification: prefer the official publisher over a news summary, and check the Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre, the relevant authority's own site, or the government portal at u.ae. Keep the paragraph on physical and human processes rather than on policy opinion.

faqs.question: How recent does a Geography case study need to be?
faqs.answer: Recent enough to be defensible, which in practice means the student can say when the data was published and why it still describes the situation. A twenty-year-old example of a management scheme is fine if the scheme is still the relevant one and the student says so. What costs marks is an undated assertion, or a figure the candidate cannot source, because an examiner has no way to credit it. A practical rule: every case-study sheet carries a date and a source line next to each figure, written when the sheet is built rather than hunted for later.

faqs.question: How many Geography extended responses should a student write before the mocks?
faqs.answer: Enough that writing one to the clock stops being an event, which for most candidates means one a fortnight through DP1 and one a week in the final term. The number matters less than the conditions: a response written over two evenings with notes open teaches very little, while one written cold in the examination's time allowance and marked against the descriptors teaches a great deal. Ask any prospective tutor how many marked timed responses their plan contains and across how many weeks, because that figure is the mechanism that moves this grade.

faqs.question: What evidence should a Geography tutor give me each month?
faqs.answer: The marked scripts themselves, shared as files rather than described; the techniques checklist with the signed-off items visible; any case-study sheets the student has produced; and a written note of no more than a paragraph saying which band the responses now reach and what has not changed. The last part matters most. A monthly note that reports only improvement is a sales document. One that names what is still failing is a plan you can act on, and it is also the thing that lets you decide to stop.

faqs.question: Is Geography content the same at every Dubai school?
faqs.answer: The core is; the option themes are not. Every candidate sits the same three core units on population, climate and resource security, and the department chooses two option themes at Standard Level or three at Higher Level from a list of seven. Two students in neighbouring Dubai schools can therefore share nothing on one of their papers. That is why the first question before hiring is which themes your child's school teaches, and the second is whether the Higher Level core extension has been started, since it is usually taught last.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on a fieldwork draft, and where is the line?
faqs.answer: Feedback is allowed and useful; production is not. A tutor may teach the techniques, explain what each criterion rewards, ask whether the data collected can support the conclusion being drawn, and point out that a section has drifted from its own question. A tutor may not supply text, choose the question, construct the analysis or rework a draft to completion. One Geography-specific warning: messy primary data should be reported and explained in the evaluation, never tidied. Removing or inventing readings is fabrication and it is the one error in this component that cannot be argued down.

faqs.question: What does Geography tutoring cost in Dubai, and what should be included?
faqs.answer: Published rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 at the budget end, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, to AED 200 to 450 and above for a Diploma specialist on Bestimate's 2026 table, with BartyED at AED 650 for premium named tutoring. In an evidence-led plan the figure to interrogate is the marked work rather than the rate: marking an extended response properly takes a tutor twenty to thirty minutes. Ask how many marked scripts are included, whether the techniques checklist is part of the plan, and what the total comes to.

faqs.question: Can we stop midway if the plan is not working?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a plan should be written so that stopping is a normal option rather than an awkward conversation. If six weeks of marked scripts show the same band and the same three corrections, the diagnosis was wrong. The usual causes are a technique problem treated as a content problem, or a fieldwork report nobody looked at while everyone worked on the papers. Either way the right response is to change the plan or end it. Stopping costs nothing beyond the sessions already taught, and no package should lock a family in past that point.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to know which option themes my child's school teaches?
faqs.answer: It is the single most important matching question in this subject, and it is routinely skipped. Seven option themes exist, your child sits two or three, and a tutor who has taught the other four will cover the core well and miss half the examination. The mismatch usually surfaces only when the first past paper is attempted, by which point a term has gone. Email the department for the themes, the order they are taught, and the Higher Level core extension schedule, then ask any prospective tutor what they have taught and when.

intro.heading: Three students, one German B class, and why generic tuition fails all of them
paragraphs: Walk into a German B lesson at a Dubai IB school and you will find three populations sitting together. The first arrived from German-medium education, sometimes from the city's German-curriculum school, sometimes from Germany, Austria or Switzerland directly. Their spoken German is strong, their academic register is untested, and their written accuracy is often worse than their fluency implies because they learnt the language by using it rather than by studying it. The second group has studied German as a school subject for five or six years, usually two lessons a week. Their grammar is better taught and their vocabulary is narrower. The third group are heritage speakers: one German-speaking parent, fluent conversation, almost no reading, and an accent that misleads every adult who meets them.

A tutor who treats these three the same wastes everybody's money. The transfer student needs register and written accuracy, not vocabulary. The school learner needs volume and confidence, not more grammar explanation. The heritage speaker needs reading, writing and in some cases a frank conversation with the Diploma coordinator about whether German B is the right placement at all. The first question any competent German B tutor should ask is which of the three they are looking at, and the answer comes from a marked piece of writing rather than from a conversation.

Dubai makes the mix more pronounced than it would be in a European school, because the city's population turns over constantly. A German B set of eight can easily contain students who have been in Dubai for eleven years and students who arrived in August. The teacher is covering five prescribed themes, two literary works for the Higher Level candidates, and three different starting points, inside the same timetabled hours. That arithmetic, not any failing of the school, is why families here buy German outside school.

The useful evidence is also different for each group. For a transfer student, the thing to watch is error type: case endings and word order in subordinate clauses are the two that persist longest in students who learnt German by ear. For a school learner, watch range: the number of distinct structures available under time pressure. For a heritage speaker, watch reading comprehension on unfamiliar text, which is almost always the weakest skill and the one that makes the receptive paper a nasty surprise. None of those is visible in a report grade, and all of them are visible in a marked task.

On the search phrase itself: people type home tutor, and in Dubai that generally means somebody driving over. IB Gram does not do that in the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. German B support reaches Dubai families as one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time. For this subject that constraint is close to irrelevant and occasionally an advantage, because German B teaching is a narrow specialism, the Higher Level literary works narrow it further, and the chance that the right person lives twenty minutes away is small.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-home-tutor.programmesIntro: German appears at several points in a Dubai IB school and the label on the timetable does not always match what the student needs. These are the stages, and what each assumes the student can already do.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: German B sits in Group 2 and is assessed through a written task, a paper combining listening and reading, and a recorded Individual Oral. Higher Level candidates additionally study two literary works originally written in German, and their oral is built on an extract from one of them rather than on a visual stimulus. The five prescribed themes frame the whole course at both levels, which keeps the content predictable even as the demand inside each component rises at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Higher Level decision is often made on timetable availability rather than on reading history, which is the wrong basis. A student who has never read a novel in German should not meet two of them for the first time in DP2 while also sitting five other subjects. That conversation belongs in the first term of DP1.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP German reports by phase and by four criteria covering spoken and visual comprehension, reading comprehension, communication, and accurate use of language. Read as evidence, the criterion split is far more useful than the phase number: a student strong on comprehension criteria and weak on the language-use criterion is a classic heritage-speaker profile, and it predicts exactly the problems German B will expose.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools place MYP German students by phase, and families moving between schools in the city often find the same child placed in different phases by two institutions. Where that happens, a marked written task is the only neutral evidence available, and it is worth having before the transfer rather than after.

programmes.name: German A: Language and Literature
programmes.description: The Group 1 route for students whose German is a first language, studied as literature and textual analysis rather than as language acquisition. It is the only German course that can contribute towards the bilingual diploma, and it is a genuine option for strong transfer students from German-medium schooling. The teaching required is closer to literary criticism than to language teaching, and it is a different tutoring purchase entirely.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools run German A, because the cohort needed to timetable it is rarely there. Families who want it sometimes find the school can offer it as a school-supported self-taught Standard Level option, which is a demanding route and should be discussed with the coordinator early rather than assumed.

programmes.name: German ab initio
programmes.description: The beginner route, restricted to students with little or no previous German and available at Standard Level only. It appears here because families sometimes propose it for a struggling German B student. Eligibility rests on prior exposure, so a student with years of German behind them does not qualify however much they are struggling, and the alternative is usually a level change within German B rather than a course change.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai school offers both German B and German ab initio, the sets are often taught in the same block by the same teacher, which limits how far a mid-year move is practical. Ask the coordinator what is actually possible before planning around it.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Group 2 at a Dubai IB school is a small number of languages at several levels, and a German B student is usually choosing between these. Each description is about what the course demands rather than what it covers.

subjects.name: German B Higher Level
subjects.description: Two literary works in German, longer written responses, denser reading texts, and an Individual Oral built on a literary extract. The literary element is what makes Higher Level a genuinely different course: a student can speak excellent German and still be unprepared to discuss a novel's narrative perspective under assessment conditions, which is where most Dubai HL candidates lose ground.

subjects.name: German B Standard Level
subjects.description: The same three components without the literary works, with the oral based on a visual stimulus connected to one of the prescribed themes. For a student whose German is functional but inaccurate, Standard Level with serious work on case and word order produces a better outcome than Higher Level with thin coverage of two books.

subjects.name: German ab initio
subjects.description: Beginner German for students with little or no prior exposure, examined at Standard Level. The vocabulary expectation is set by the prescribed topics, which makes it trackable. It is not a fallback for a weak German B student; eligibility turns on previous study, and the coordinator applies that rule.

subjects.name: German A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Group 1 German for first-language speakers, taught as literary and textual analysis. The only German route that counts towards the bilingual diploma. Rarely timetabled in Dubai, sometimes available as a school-supported self-taught Standard Level option, and a serious commitment if taken that way.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: The most widely available Group 2 language in Dubai IB schools and a useful comparator. French B students lose marks on agreement and tense; German B students lose them on case and clause order. The error profiles are different enough that a tutor strong in one is not automatically useful in the other.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Structurally identical to German B with a very different grammar load: subjunctive mood and tense control rather than case endings and verb-final subordinate clauses. Families running German B for one child and Spanish B for another should expect two separate specialists rather than one tutor covering both.

subjects.name: Mandarin B
subjects.description: Included because scheduling collides: Mandarin teaching capacity in Dubai often sits outside the Gulf time zone, and a household running both Mandarin and German tuition needs the week planned rather than booked twice. Character learning also competes for the same memorisation time German vocabulary needs.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic under KHDA's mandatory subject requirements, regardless of the licensed curriculum, and non-Arab students follow their own stream. A German B student is therefore carrying two languages beyond English in the school week, and the total minutes are worth counting before anything is added.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in German B
subjects.description: A 4,000-word essay written in German on an aspect of German-speaking culture, supervised within the school. A tutor's role is limited to process coaching: framing a researchable question, evaluating sources, and giving feedback on the student's own drafts. It is usually bought in short blocks around the school's internal checkpoints.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-home-tutor.regionsIntro: German B requests reach us from across Dubai, and what differs by area is the shape of the week rather than the teaching. These are the patterns behind the scheduling conversations we have most often.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: A long-settled expatriate belt with several German-speaking households and short school runs, so weekday sessions at 4.30pm are workable. Students here often have German-speaking friends nearby, which helps fluency and does nothing for written accuracy or reading.

regions.name: Oud Metha, Zabeel and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Close to the older school corridor and to Dubai's German-curriculum provision, which is where many German B transfer students in the city come from. Traffic on Sheikh Rashid Road makes late-afternoon in-home visits unreliable and makes a fixed online slot the stable option.

regions.note: Dense IB territory with several Diploma cohorts inside a few kilometres, so German B candidates here are competing for the same small pool of local tutors before mocks. Booking the slot in the autumn term rather than the spring is the practical lesson.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and DIFC
regions.note: Apartment living, parents with long office hours, and students who get home late. Evening sessions after 7pm are more common here than anywhere else in the city, and recorded oral practice has to be scheduled around shared living space.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and The Springs
regions.note: Villa communities with gated access and long internal roads, which is where visiting-tutor arrangements quietly lose fifteen minutes at each end. Weekend morning sessions work well here and suit the slower, heavier work that case and word-order repair requires.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Several IB and British schools within a short radius and a high proportion of students sitting two languages beyond English. Counting total weekly language minutes before adding German tuition is particularly worthwhile for families in this belt.

regions.name: Mirdif and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Mixed curriculum catchment, smaller IB cohorts per school, and German B sets that can be as small as five or six students. Individual feedback inside the school day is limited by the arithmetic rather than by willingness, which is the usual trigger for outside help here.

schoolClusters.note: The heaviest concentration of Diploma candidates in the city, and the belt where Group 2 demand spikes after the DP1 end-of-year report. Students we support attend schools across this corridor, and German B enquiries here are most often about Higher Level literary preparation.

Sessions are built around the student's own writing, with each error class tracked separately so a parent can see which have cleared and which are persisting rather than reading a general comment about accuracy.

sections.heading: Sorting the three intakes before spending anything
paragraphs: The first hour of German B tuition should be diagnostic and nothing else. A short written task, a timed reading section, and five minutes of unprepared speech produce enough evidence to place a student in one of the three profiles, and the profile determines everything that follows. Doing this properly costs one session. Skipping it routinely costs a term, because the default assumption in language tuition is that the student needs more vocabulary, and for two of the three profiles that is the wrong diagnosis.

The transfer student out of German-medium schooling is the most commonly misdiagnosed. Their spoken German is better than their tutor's expectations and their written accuracy is worse, because they acquired the language in use and were never drilled on endings. Marks leak on case, on adjective declension, and on register: an informal spoken style transferred into a formal written task reads to an examiner as a control problem rather than as a stylistic choice. The work is narrow and unglamorous, and it moves the written mark quickly.

The school learner is the easiest to help and the slowest to improve. Five or six years of two lessons a week produces accurate but narrow German: a reliable present tense, a small stock of structures, and a vocabulary that covers the textbook and not the paper. The job is range and volume, built over two to three terms, with reading as the main vehicle. The heritage speaker is the hardest case, because everything that is visible is strong and everything that is weak is invisible until a timed reading paper is attempted.

sections.heading: German B assessment, and what changes between Standard and Higher Level
paragraphs: German B is assessed through three components. A written task responding to a stimulus carries a quarter of the grade. A paper combining listening and reading carries half. The recorded Individual Oral carries the remaining quarter. Those proportions are the same at both levels, which is why the phrase harder at Higher Level is misleading: the weighting does not shift, the demand inside each component does, and the single largest shift is the arrival of two literary works.

At Standard Level the oral is built on a visual stimulus connected to one of the five prescribed themes. At Higher Level it is built on an extract from one of the two literary works studied, which converts a quarter of the grade into a literary conversation. A student who has read both works properly finds this the most predictable component in the course. A student who has read summaries finds it the least predictable, because the extract cannot be anticipated and a summary gives no vocabulary for discussing how a passage is written.

The table sets the two levels side by side on the dimensions that actually change what tuition should contain. Treat the operational detail as something to confirm: component timings, word bands and the school's internal dates all come from the current subject guide and the Diploma coordinator rather than from a tutoring page. sections.heading: The grammar debt: where German B marks actually go
paragraphs: German loses marks in patterns, and the patterns are specific enough to name. Four error classes account for most of what examiners penalise in the written task, and all four are visible in any two-paragraph sample of a student's writing. Case is the largest: accusative and dative confusion after prepositions that take either, and genitive avoided entirely. Adjective declension is the second, because the ending depends on gender, case and the article in front of it, and students who learnt by ear never internalised the table.

Word order is the third and the most damaging to comprehension. The verb goes to the end in subordinate clauses, the order shifts in questions and after certain conjunctions, and students who transfer English structures produce German that is understandable and clearly wrong. The fourth is register: du against Sie inside a single piece of writing, or spoken contractions in a formal letter. Register is the cheapest to fix and the most frequently left unaddressed, because it looks like a slip rather than a skill gap.

Orthography deserves a line of its own. Material written before the spelling reforms uses conventions that no longer apply, and students who have practised from older textbooks or family-owned books carry ß and ss habits that are now wrong. It costs a small number of marks and it is trivial to fix once somebody notices. Nobody notices it in conversation, which is precisely why a marked written sample is worth more than an hour of talking at the start of an arrangement.

sections.heading: What Higher Level candidates must actually do with the two literary works
paragraphs: The literary requirement is the part of German B Higher Level that families understand least and that costs the most when neglected. Two works originally written in German are studied across the course, and the Individual Oral is built on an extract from one of them. The student is not writing a literary essay; the demand is to discuss a passage in German, connecting it to the work as a whole and to wider ideas, in a recorded conversation with their teacher.

That demand needs three things a conversation class never supplies. First, the works actually read, in German, slowly, with the vocabulary of the text absorbed rather than skimmed. Second, a register for talking about writing: narrative voice, structure, imagery, how a scene is built. Most fluent speakers, including heritage speakers and transfer students, have never used that register in German and reach for English concepts translated badly. Third, practice on extracts the student has not pre-prepared, because the extract in the assessment will be unseen.

The honest boundary is worth stating here because this is where offers of help become offers of malpractice. A tutor may teach the vocabulary of literary discussion, work through extracts the student has not seen, ask the questions an examiner might ask, and give feedback on the student's own notes. A tutor may not supply a prepared analysis, a script for the oral, or a set of answers for a passage the student will meet in the assessment room. The first list raises a mark. The second is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: Keeping German alive in a city where nothing outside the lesson is in German
paragraphs: A German B student in Dubai hears German in two places: the classroom and, for some, at home. English runs everything else, Arabic is on every sign, and the incidental exposure that a student in Europe gets for free does not exist here. That absence is the single biggest structural disadvantage for German B candidates in this city, and it is also the cheapest thing to fix, because it needs attention rather than money.

What works is boring and specific. Twenty minutes of German reading a day, chosen by the student rather than assigned, beats an hour of grammar once a week for building the structural range that the written task rewards. German audio during the school run, with no comprehension task attached, builds the listening tolerance the receptive paper assumes. Writing one paragraph a day about something that happened, corrected weekly rather than daily, produces more usable error data than any worksheet. None of this is tutoring, and all of it multiplies what tutoring achieves.

The seasonal risk is the long summer. Six or seven weeks with no German, in a language with the morphological load German carries, costs more than it would cost in Spanish or French: the endings go first and the confidence goes with them. Short maintenance sessions through August, or simply a reading commitment, is the difference between restarting in September and continuing. Families who travel in term time face the same problem in a smaller version, and the error log is what makes the resulting gaps findable rather than mysterious.

sections.heading: Heritage speakers, and the placement conversation nobody wants to have
paragraphs: A fluent heritage speaker in German B is a genuine problem and it is usually discussed too late. Language B is an acquisition course. A student who grew up speaking German at home may be substantially beyond what the course assumes in speaking and listening, and substantially below it in reading and formal writing. The result is a lopsided profile: comfortable in the oral, exposed in the receptive paper, and inconsistent in the written task where register and accuracy are assessed rather than fluency.

There are two legitimate directions. If the school offers German A: Language and Literature, that is where a genuinely first-language speaker belongs, and it is the only German route that can contribute towards the bilingual diploma. Few Dubai schools timetable it, and some can offer a school-supported self-taught Standard Level option instead, which is demanding and needs a realistic conversation about reading stamina before anyone commits. The alternative is German B done properly, with the reading and writing deficit treated as the actual syllabus.

What a tutor should not do is help a family engineer a placement. The coordinator decides, the IB's own rules on appropriate placement govern it, and the useful contribution from outside is evidence: a marked written task, a timed reading score, and an honest note on what the student can and cannot do. Take that to the school. We will produce it; we will not argue a case to a school on a family's behalf, and we would be worth less if we did.

sections.heading: German after the Diploma: what the next requirement actually is
paragraphs: Families often choose German B with a German-speaking university in mind, and the requirement at the far end is not the one they expect. German universities set their own admission and language rules, and they generally ask for a recognised proof of German proficiency for German-taught programmes, assessed through tests such as TestDaF or the DSH, or through recognised certificates at the level the programme specifies. A Group 2 Diploma subject and a language-proficiency certificate are different instruments, and one does not automatically substitute for the other.

The practical sequence is to check the individual university and programme, and the central application service where one applies, rather than relying on a general rule. Requirements differ between a German-taught degree and an English-taught one, between universities, and sometimes between faculties inside a university. Where a school-leaving qualification needs assessing for direct entry, that is also a university-level question with a published answer. None of this is something a tutoring provider decides, and no tutoring is required for any of it.

What German B does contribute is the substance those tests measure: reading unfamiliar academic text, writing in a formal register, and listening to German that was not produced for a classroom. A student aiming at a German-taught degree is better served by Higher Level with the two literary works taken seriously than by Standard Level with a certificate bolted on at the end. sections.heading: Ramadan, the Dubai calendar and when German revision actually happens
paragraphs: Revision plans written in September assume a school year that Dubai does not have. Reduced school hours during Ramadan, the Eid holidays, a mid-term break in February, and the long summer all land on the Diploma calendar, and a two-year language course absorbs them badly if nobody plans around them. German is more exposed than most subjects, because morphological accuracy degrades over a gap in a way that content knowledge does not.

Ramadan is the one most often handled badly by tutoring providers. Sessions scheduled for late afternoon during fasting hours are the worst possible slot for sustained concentration, and cancelling the month outright costs a beginner or a Higher Level literary reader more than it saves. The arrangement that works is a move to post-Iftar timing by agreement, with shorter sessions and lighter cognitive load: reading and listening rather than new grammar, consolidation rather than new material.

The rest of the calendar needs the same kind of planning. February half-term is the natural slot for a receptive paper clinic, because it sits far enough before the exam period for the findings to be actionable. The Higher Level literary reading belongs in DP1 and the first term of DP2, not in the final weeks. The summer wants maintenance rather than progress. Mapping the tuition plan onto the actual Dubai school calendar at the start of DP1, rather than booking a weekly slot and hoping, is the single administrative step that saves the most wasted hours.

February break: the natural window for a timed receptive paper clinic
HL literary reading belongs in DP1, not in the final term
Summer: maintenance sessions, because German endings degrade fastest over a gap

process.title: Say which of the three profiles your child is
process.description: Transfer from German-medium schooling, long-term school learner, or heritage speaker at home. If you are not sure, say that too and send a recent piece of German writing. The profile decides the first six weeks of work, and getting it wrong is the most common reason German tuition in this city produces a pleasant relationship and a static grade.

process.title: One diagnostic session, before any teaching
process.description: A short written task, a timed reading section, and five minutes of unprepared speech, marked and returned with the error classes named. It takes an hour, it is yours to keep, and it will tell you whether the issue is case, range, register or reading. No teaching happens until that evidence exists.

process.title: Split the work into the three jobs
process.description: Weekly accuracy repair, Higher Level literary preparation as a term-length block, and a receptive clinic placed near the February break. Buying them separately costs fewer total hours than one open-ended weekly arrangement, because each has its own natural length and stops when it is done.

process.title: Fix the slot around the real Dubai week
process.description: After the school run, before the evening collapses, on Gulf Standard Time, with Ramadan timing agreed in advance rather than improvised and summer maintenance decided in May. Scheduling is the quiet reason most tutoring arrangements fail here, and it is settled in one conversation.

process.title: Review on error classes, not on impressions
process.description: Each month, a summary showing which error classes have cleared, which are persisting and which are new. That is what a review should turn on. If the classes are not moving, we change the approach or the tutor rather than adding hours, and if the honest answer is fewer hours, we say so.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis first, because three different students share the class
whyPoints.description: Transfer students, school learners and heritage speakers need different work, and German tuition that starts with vocabulary helps only one of them. One diagnostic hour sorts it, and the finding is written down in terms a parent can use at the next school meeting.

whyPoints.title: Error classes tracked, not accuracy described
whyPoints.description: Case, declension, word order, register, orthography and structural range are logged separately, so a monthly summary shows what has cleared and what has not. General comments about accuracy improving are the main reason families cannot tell whether German tuition is working.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level literary work treated as a real requirement
whyPoints.description: Two works in German and an oral built on an unseen extract is a specific demand that conversational fluency does not cover. We buy it as a term-length block with a reading schedule, and we do not supply prepared analyses or scripts, which is where parts of this market cross into malpractice.

whyPoints.title: Built for a city with no German outside the lesson
whyPoints.description: Dubai gives a German B student almost no incidental exposure, so the plan includes what happens between sessions: daily reading, untasked audio, a paragraph a day. Those habits cost nothing and determine how much the paid hours achieve.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the actual Dubai calendar
whyPoints.description: Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing with lighter content, the February break takes the receptive clinic, and summer gets maintenance rather than silence. Plans that ignore the local calendar lose weeks that nobody budgeted for.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, no regulator approval or examination-board partnership claimed, no promised grades, no predicted scores, no finished coursework, and no IB exam date on the page because none could be verified for this project. What a tutor may and may not do is stated rather than implied.

faqs.question: How much German does my child need before starting IB German B in Dubai?
faqs.answer: German B assumes prior study rather than fluency, so two or more years of the language as a school subject is the usual entry point, and the placement decision belongs to the school's Diploma coordinator. What matters more than the number of years is the shape of what exists: a student with accurate but narrow German is in a better position than one with fluent but unmonitored German, because range is easier to build than accuracy is to retrofit. Send a recent piece of written German with any enquiry; it says more about readiness than a description of how long the subject has been studied.

faqs.question: Is German B Higher Level realistic for a student who left German-medium school at 14?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the deciding factor is reading rather than speaking. Higher Level requires two literary works originally written in German and an Individual Oral built on an unseen extract from one of them. A student who left German-medium education at 14 usually has the spoken fluency and may never have read a novel in German for study. If the reading schedule starts in DP1 and the register for discussing writing is built deliberately, Higher Level is a reasonable choice. If the works are met in the final term, Standard Level done well is the better outcome.

faqs.question: Which literary works are studied in IB German B Higher Level?
faqs.answer: The works are chosen by the school from the options the course allows, so there is no fixed national list and two Dubai schools may study entirely different pairs. Ask the subject teacher which two works your child's class is studying and when each will be read, because that schedule is what a tutoring block should be built around. A tutor who arrives with their own preferred texts rather than working with the school's choices is adding reading load rather than preparing the student for the assessment they will actually sit.

faqs.question: My child speaks German at home — is German B the right course?
faqs.answer: It may not be, and this is worth raising with the coordinator early. Language B is an acquisition course, and a heritage speaker is often beyond it in speaking and listening while being behind it in reading and formal writing. The usual result is a lopsided profile: comfortable in the oral, exposed in the receptive paper. Where a school offers German A: Language and Literature, that is the route for a genuine first-language speaker, and it is the only German option that can contribute towards the bilingual diploma. Bring a marked written task and a timed reading score to that conversation.

faqs.question: Where do German B students lose the most marks in the written task?
faqs.answer: In four places, consistently. Case endings after prepositions that take either accusative or dative. Adjective declension, where the ending depends on gender, case and the preceding article. Verb position in subordinate clauses, where English word order transfers across and produces German that is comprehensible and clearly wrong. And register, with du and Sie mixed inside one piece, or spoken contractions in formal writing. The first three take weeks to months of corrected writing. Register usually takes two or three sessions, which makes it the best-value fix available in this subject.

faqs.question: Does German B use the current German spelling conventions?
faqs.answer: Yes, current standard orthography applies, which catches a specific group of students in Dubai: those who have practised from older textbooks, from family-owned books, or with a tutor working from pre-reform material. The ß and ss conventions changed, and writing by the older rules costs a small but avoidable number of marks in the written task. It is a one-session fix followed by a proofreading habit. It is also invisible in conversation, which is why a marked written sample at the start of an arrangement is worth more than an hour of talking.

faqs.question: How do we keep German going in Dubai when nobody at home speaks it?
faqs.answer: With small daily habits rather than more paid hours. Twenty minutes of self-chosen German reading a day builds the structural range the written task rewards, faster than a weekly grammar session. German audio during the school run, with no comprehension task attached, builds the listening tolerance the receptive paper assumes. One written paragraph a day about something ordinary, corrected weekly rather than daily, produces more usable error data than any worksheet. In a city with no incidental German, those habits determine how much the tutoring achieves.

faqs.question: Can a German B tutor help with the Higher Level Individual Oral?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may teach the vocabulary of literary discussion, work through extracts the student has not pre-prepared, ask the kinds of question an examiner asks, coach the timing so the discussion is not squeezed, and give feedback on the student's own notes. A tutor may not supply a prepared analysis, write a script, or rehearse the specific extract the school will use. The second list is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the tutor who offered it.

faqs.question: Will IB German B meet a German university's language requirement?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and this needs checking programme by programme. German universities set their own admission and language rules, and German-taught programmes generally ask for a recognised proficiency result from a test such as TestDaF or the DSH, or a certificate at the level the programme specifies. A Group 2 Diploma subject and a proficiency certificate are different instruments. Check the individual university, the specific programme and the central application service rather than relying on a general rule. What German B supplies is the underlying skill those tests measure.

faqs.question: Is the workload gap between German B SL and HL as large as people say?
faqs.answer: The weightings are identical — a quarter for the written task, half for the receptive paper, a quarter for the oral — so the gap is not in the mark scheme. It is in the two literary works and the denser reading. Reading two books in German across two years is a real addition to a timetable already carrying five other subjects and the core. For a student who reads willingly, Higher Level is manageable. For one who does not read in any language, Standard Level with serious accuracy work usually produces a better Diploma total.

faqs.question: How many German B sessions a week does a Dubai Diploma student need?
faqs.answer: One a week is the normal shape for accuracy repair, with a short written task due between sessions so there is something to mark. Higher Level candidates add a term-length literary block rather than a second weekly hour, and most students want a short receptive clinic near the February break. That pattern uses fewer total hours than an open-ended weekly arrangement running for two years, because each job has a natural length and stops when it is finished rather than when the term ends.

faqs.question: Can German lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the arrangement we recommend rather than pausing the month. Late-afternoon sessions during fasting hours are the worst slot for sustained grammar work, and cancelling outright is costly in a language where accuracy degrades over a gap. The workable version is a later start after Iftar, shorter sessions, and lighter cognitive load: reading and listening rather than new material, consolidation rather than new structures. Agree the timing before Ramadan begins rather than improvising it in the first week.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a German tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. German B teaching reaches Dubai families as one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time, with marked work and the error log kept in a shared file. For this subject the trade is a good one. German B teaching is a narrow specialism, Higher Level literary preparation narrows it further, and the chance that the right person for your child's profile happens to live a short drive away in this city is small.

faqs.question: What should a German B tutor show us after one term?
faqs.answer: A monthly summary by error class, showing which of case, declension, word order, register, orthography and structural range have cleared, which are persisting and which are new. Plus the marked written tasks those findings came from, and for Higher Level candidates a record of which literary extracts have been worked through. That is the useful evidence. A term of positive verbal feedback with nothing written down is the most common thing families receive and the least possible to act on.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover German B and the Arabic our school requires?
faqs.answer: In practice, no, and it is better not to try. Arabic in a Dubai private school is a mandatory subject under KHDA requirements with its own curriculum, its own streams for Arab and non-Arab students, and its own language of instruction rules; German B is a Group 2 Diploma course. The skills, the material and the assessment have nothing in common. What is worth doing is counting the total weekly language minutes your child already carries across English, Arabic and German before any tuition is added, because that total is usually higher than the timetable suggests.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the diagnosis, not the timetable
dubai/ib-dp-german-b-home-tutor.closingBody: German B in Dubai fails for a predictable reason: three different kinds of student share one class, and tuition bought without a diagnosis defaults to vocabulary work that helps only one of them. One diagnostic hour — a written task, a timed reading section, five minutes of unprepared speech — tells you whether the real issue is case, range, register or reading, and it is yours to keep whatever you decide next. Send the school, the level, the profile you think fits and the weekly windows that survive the school run, and you will get a named German B teacher, a slot on Gulf Standard Time and a 30-minute trial at no charge. Teaching runs online, one-to-one, with no home visits in the UAE.
