intro.heading: German B at HL and SL, measured by the faults that actually cost marks
paragraphs: German B is the IB Diploma course for students who already have some German behind them. It runs at both Higher and Standard Level, it shares the five prescribed themes with every other language acquisition course, and at Higher Level it adds two literary works that reshape the oral entirely. In Dubai it is rarely a free choice. Families arrive in the emirate mid-posting, or plan to leave it, and German is the language that has to keep moving regardless of which school the child lands in.

That continuity problem is what makes German B tuition in Dubai different from German B tuition in Hamburg. A student may have done four years of German at a German-curriculum school, switched into an IB Diploma, and now be asked to write in a register they have never been taught, on themes they have never studied, with grammar habits formed in a bilingual playground rather than a grammar book. The German is often better than the grade suggests, and the grade is held down by three or four repeatable faults.

Those faults have names. Case endings after prepositions. Verb-final word order in subordinate clauses. Auxiliary choice between haben and sein in the perfect. Adjective endings in the dative. A student making six of those per hundred words in September is not bad at German; they have four habits to retrain. Counting them is more useful than discussing them, because a count can fall and a discussion cannot. The same logic applies to the receptive papers: a student who misses four listening answers because an unknown word stopped them has a technique problem with a measurable size, not a general weakness in German.

That counting is the method this page describes. Each marked task produces an error profile: how many faults, of which family, per hundred words written. The profile goes in a file with a date. Over a term the shape of the profile changes, and a parent can see which fault family is closing and which is stuck. When a family asks whether tuition is working, the answer is a table rather than an adjective, and when a fault family refuses to move, the method changes instead of the hours increasing.

Lessons run online. IB Gram matches Dubai families with one-to-one tutors over live video with the student's own drafts and past papers screen-shared. We do not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is an India-only service. For German B that restriction costs a Dubai family very little, because the constraint on quality here is finding someone who has taught this syllabus at the level the student sits, and that person is rarely the nearest German speaker to your community.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-online-tutor.programmesIntro: German rarely starts in Year 12. The route a Dubai student took through the earlier programmes decides whether German B SL, German B HL or a Language A course is the honest placement, and it also decides which fault families they arrive with.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language Acquisition runs in six phases rather than year groups. Students reaching Phase 4 or 5 in German have the vocabulary and the tense range for German B, though phase descriptors say nothing about accuracy. A Phase 5 student can still be making systematic case errors, because MYP assessment rewards communication over grammatical precision.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP cohorts include many students who speak German at home but have never written it formally. Those students test high on a phase descriptor and then lose written marks for exactly the reasons a heritage speaker would: spoken fluency without written case control. A tutor's first job with them is a written diagnostic, not a conversation.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: German B sits in Group 2 and satisfies the Diploma's language acquisition requirement at either level. Two external papers and one internally assessed individual oral make up the grade. Higher Level candidates also study two literary works, which become the basis of the oral and are the part most students underestimate in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma timetables are tight because KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed curriculum. A German B HL student therefore has literary works to read with no timetabled reading slot, which is why the HL reading schedule is usually the first thing a tutor plans rather than the last.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP includes a compulsory language development strand assessed by portfolio rather than on the 1 to 7 scale. Students use German in it where the career-related study points towards engineering, hospitality or logistics, all of which have German-speaking employers with a presence in the Gulf.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools licensed for the DP also run the CP, so a CP German portfolio student is usually one of very few in their school. Tuition here is about evidence of reflection and language growth over time, not about Paper 1 technique, and the session shape looks nothing like a German B HL session.

programmes.name: Deutsches Internationales Abitur route
programmes.description: Not an IB programme, but the route many German-speaking families in Dubai consider as the alternative. It teaches German as a first language throughout, so a student transferring out of it into IB German B is usually over-qualified for the course and may be better placed in German A: language and literature.
programmes.countryNote: The existence of a German-curriculum school in Dubai shapes the German B population in the IB schools. Students who left that route, or never joined it, make up most German B rooms in the emirate, and their prior learning varies far more widely than a single phase number on a transfer report suggests.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: German B is almost never the subject a family worries about first. The list below is what Dubai students usually carry alongside it, and the point of listing them is scheduling: a German B HL reading plan has to survive the deadlines these subjects impose.

subjects.name: German B
subjects.description: Five prescribed themes, two external papers, one individual oral, plus two literary works at Higher Level. Written accuracy is where the level difference bites hardest, because the Higher Level word band leaves more room for a case error to recur.

subjects.name: German A: language and literature
subjects.description: The Group 1 route for students who use German as a school or home language. Worth knowing because a heritage speaker misplaced in German B often finds the course easy and still loses marks on formal register, which the B criteria reward and the playground never taught.

subjects.name: German ab initio
subjects.description: For genuine beginners, Standard Level only, with no literary component. A student transferring into Dubai with two years of casual German sometimes belongs here rather than in B SL, and the entry test rather than the transcript should decide.

subjects.name: English A: language and literature
subjects.description: The commentary skills built here transfer into the German B HL oral, where the student discusses an extract from a studied work. Students who analyse in English competently can usually be taught to do the same thing in German with a scaffold.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Frequently paired with German by students aiming at German-speaking engineering or economics faculties. Its exploration deadline typically lands in the same term as the German oral window, which is the collision a tutor should plan around.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A common Higher Level alongside German for students looking at technical universities. The internal assessment competes directly with HL literary reading for evening hours in the spring of Year 12.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: German B students taking History often choose twentieth-century European topics, which builds background knowledge that genuinely helps with the literary works and with the Social organization theme.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries across the course, each with a submission date. Students carrying Economics HL and German B HL feel the pressure in Year 12, and the German reading is what usually gets dropped first.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Popular in Dubai cohorts and a sensible pairing for students considering a German-speaking business school. Its own written work overlaps in skill with German B Paper 1 planning, which can be exploited rather than resented.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools for students who are not Arab nationals, timetabled separately from Arabic as a first language under KHDA rules. It occupies a slot parents often assume could become more German, and it cannot.

sections.heading: German B in Dubai is usually a continuity decision
paragraphs: Very few Dubai families choose German B because German appealed to them. They choose it because German is already in the child's history and dropping it would waste years, or because the family expects to move to a German-speaking country and wants the language maintained at a level a university there will take seriously. The search for a German B tutor therefore tends to come with a second question attached: does this grade still work if we leave the UAE in two years?

That shapes what good tuition looks like. A student who will sit the Diploma in Dubai and then study in Zurich or Munich needs the language to be genuinely usable, not just examinable. A student who will take the Diploma to a British or North American university needs the grade, and the fastest route to the grade is fault-family retraining rather than broad enrichment. Those two briefs pull in slightly different directions and it is worth saying out loud which one applies before the first session.

The Dubai context adds a third factor. The emirate has a German-curriculum school and a set of IB schools with German in Group 2, and students move between them and in from Europe at every point in the year. A German B class in a Dubai school can hold a child who has written German essays since Year 5 next to one who has had German twice a week on a carousel. Teaching to the middle of that room is nearly impossible, which is the gap one-to-one work fills.

What follows is organised around that gap. The level decision first, then the fault families that hold Dubai German B candidates back, then the measurement that shows whether they are closing, then the oral, then the regulatory questions a family here actually has to answer about equivalency and timetabling.

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level: what the literary works change
paragraphs: German B is examined at both levels, and the difference is not simply more of the same. Higher Level candidates study two literary works, and those works become the basis of the individual oral. A Standard Level candidate's oral starts from a visual stimulus linked to one of the five prescribed themes; a Higher Level candidate's oral starts from an extract taken from one of the works they have read. That is a different skill, requiring a different kind of preparation, and it is where most of the level gap actually lives.

The written components scale as well. Paper 1 asks for one task in a defined text type, and the expected length band is higher at Higher Level than at Standard Level, which has a counter-intuitive consequence: a longer piece gives a recurring case error more opportunities to appear. A student whose accuracy is marginal is sometimes better served by a strong Standard Level grade than by a Higher Level grade capped by the same four faults repeated across six hundred words.

Paper 2 covers listening and reading at both levels, with the listening section longer at Higher Level. Volume of unseen practice is the only thing that reliably moves this component, which makes it the easiest part of the course to plan and the hardest to make a student do. There is no technique shortcut that substitutes for hours of German arriving at natural speed.

sections.heading: The four fault families that cost German B candidates most
paragraphs: German accuracy errors are not random, and that is the useful thing about them. A candidate's written work almost always shows the same small set of faults, appearing again and again in new sentences. Classifying them turns a page covered in red into a list of four retraining targets, and a list of four targets can be worked through in a term. The alternative, which is correcting each error as it appears, teaches nothing durable because the student never sees the pattern.

Case after prepositions is the largest family in most Dubai German B files. Prepositions that take the accusative, the dative, or either depending on motion are a fixed, learnable set, and a student who has never systematically learned them will guess at them forever. The fix is not more writing; it is a short daily drill on the preposition groups until the ending becomes automatic, followed by writing tasks designed to force those prepositions into use.

Word order is the second. German places the verb second in a main clause and final in a subordinate clause introduced by conjunctions such as weil, dass or obwohl, and a student who writes long English-shaped sentences will break that rule every time a clause gets complicated. This fault is particularly common in strong students, because they attempt ambitious sentences. Short-sentence discipline, then controlled expansion, is the route through it.

The third family is auxiliary and participle formation in the perfect tense, where the choice between haben and sein and the handling of separable prefixes both go wrong. The fourth is adjective endings, which depend on case, gender and whether an article precedes. Both are closed systems, both are drillable, and both reward a student who accepts two weeks of tedium over a year of guessing.

sections.heading: Errors per hundred words: the number that makes progress visible
paragraphs: A parent asking whether German tuition is working deserves better than an impression. The measurement used here is simple arithmetic: take a marked task, count the faults, classify each one, divide by the number of words written and multiply by a hundred. The result is an error rate per hundred words, broken down by family. It takes a tutor about four minutes per task and it turns the question into a table with dates on it.

The breakdown matters more than the total. A student who moves from nine faults per hundred words to six has improved, but the interesting question is which three disappeared. If case errors fell and word-order errors did not, the preposition drilling worked and the clause work has not started yet. If the total is flat but the task length doubled, accuracy per word improved while the headline number stayed still, which is exactly the situation that gets misread as stagnation.

This measurement also protects against the two common failures of language tuition. The first is comfortable conversation, where a student enjoys sessions and the written error rate never moves, because speaking and writing accuracy are different skills. The second is a tutor doing too much: if the error rate on supervised work is low and on unsupervised work is high, the student is being carried rather than taught. Comparing the two is the cleanest diagnostic available.

Reviews happen at the ten-session mark. A fault family that has not closed in ten weeks is a signal to change approach, not to add hours. Perhaps the drilling was too abstract, or the writing tasks never forced the structure into use, or the student has an underlying gender-assignment problem that makes case endings unfixable until it is addressed. All of those are visible in a classified count and invisible in a general sense that things are going reasonably well.

sections.heading: The individual oral at each level
paragraphs: At Standard Level the German B oral begins with a visual stimulus connected to one of the prescribed themes. The student describes the image and then develops a conversation with the teacher that moves from the image into the theme and then more widely. The skill is a sequence: describe, interpret, connect. Practised against a timer on unseen images, it becomes reliable within a few weeks, and it is the most trainable quarter of the Standard Level grade.

At Higher Level the oral starts from an extract taken from one of the two literary works studied. The student presents on the extract, placing it in the work and commenting on how it is written, then discusses the works and the themes more broadly. This is closer to a literature oral than a language one, and students who have read the works properly do well while students who have read summaries are exposed within ninety seconds.

The preparation that works at Higher Level is a quotation bank organised by theme, built while reading rather than afterwards. A student with twenty quotations they can place and comment on has material for any extract that appears, because extracts connect to the rest of the work. Rehearsing commentary aloud, in German, is the part students skip, and it is the part that separates a fluent reader from a fluent speaker about reading.

Both levels share one risk: the memorised script. A fully rehearsed oral sounds wrong to an experienced teacher, collapses when the conversation turns, and sits uncomfortably close to the line on academic honesty. The alternative is rehearsing structures rather than content, so the student has reliable ways to open, to buy a second, to ask for a repetition and to steer towards material they know, with the actual words generated live.

sections.heading: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency: what is sourced and what is not
paragraphs: Families planning to use a UAE university, or to keep that option open, eventually meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process. It is the mechanism by which a non-Emirati school certificate is recognised for local admission, and it has published requirements that differ by curriculum. It is worth understanding early because the requirements are about subject counts and grades, not about tutoring, and a tutor who implies otherwise is inventing urgency.

For the British track the requirements are documented. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competing site in this market publishes a requirement of six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong, and the correct figure is five.

For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold that this project has been able to read on a Ministry source, so none is published here. Any site quoting you a specific IB points number for equivalency should be asked where it came from.

What this means for a German B family is narrow and useful. German B is a Group 2 subject within a Diploma, and equivalency looks at the Diploma rather than at the language subject individually. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of the equivalency process. Verify your own case with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation authority, and treat the table below as a map of where to look rather than as a decision.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects and the German B timetable squeeze
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. One of its requirements has direct consequences for a German B student's week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point.

The organisational rules are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and KHDA states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length so long as the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, and the use of different or additional content for the mandatory subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited.

Stack that against six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay and the arithmetic explains itself. There is no spare period in which a German B HL student reads two literary works. The reading has to be scheduled into evenings and holidays deliberately, in dated blocks, or it does not happen. That scheduling is one of the more valuable things a weekly tutor contributes, and it costs nothing.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with German B work
paragraphs: Every component of German B except the external papers passes through the school, which means the question of whose work it is comes up in practice rather than in theory. The position IB Gram tutors hold to is narrow and stated before the first session. A tutor teaches a structure, marks what the student produced, classifies the fault, explains the rule and sets the next task. The student generates every sentence that reaches a teacher or an examiner.

That rules out several things families sometimes expect. No tutor supplies German text for submission. No tutor edits a draft into prose the student could not have built. No tutor prepares a memorised oral and no tutor is present during an assessed component. The IB treats supplied content as malpractice and the consequence falls on the candidate, so a service willing to cross that line is selling a risk rather than an advantage.

Machine translation has made this both easier to do and easier to detect. A paragraph generated by a translation tool reads differently from a paragraph produced by a Year 12 student with a known error profile, and teachers who mark German every year notice the discontinuity immediately. There is also a practical argument that lands better with students than the ethical one: a tool is unavailable in the examination room, so every task written with one is a task that taught nothing.

The marking convention that follows from all this is worth stating plainly, because it frustrates students at first. Feedback names the fault type and the rule. It does not supply the corrected sentence. A student who is told that a dative ending is missing after a preposition has to retrieve the ending themselves, and that retrieval is the thing that moves the error rate. Being handed the right answer feels more efficient and changes nothing measurable.

process.title: Confirm the level before anything else
process.description: German B HL and SL need different preparation, and HL carries two literary works. We establish which level the student is registered for, which works the school has set, the most recent grade, and the date of the school's oral window. Everything else is planned from those four facts.

process.title: Free trial with a written diagnostic
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, no card details taken. The hour includes a timed written task in the correct word band, marked with every fault classified, so the session ends with an error profile rather than an introduction. You see the classified marking before committing to anything.

process.title: Fault families ranked, two chosen
process.description: The tutor ranks the fault families by error rate and picks the top two as the term's targets. Attacking all four at once produces no measurable movement in any of them. The ranking and the chosen targets are written down and sent to you.

process.title: Weekly task, classified marking, drilled session
process.description: A timed task each week, marked and classified before the session begins. The session drills only the chosen families and then forces them into new writing. The error rate per hundred words goes into the file with the date and the task length.

process.title: Ten-session review with the count in front of us
process.description: At session ten we look at the chart. A family that has closed is replaced by the next one down. A family that has not moved means the method was wrong, so the drilling changes. If the match itself is the problem we say so and move the student.

whyPoints.title: Faults are counted, not described
whyPoints.description: Error rate per hundred words, classified by family, with the task length recorded so the figures are comparable. It is arithmetic rather than opinion, and it exposes the difference between a student improving and a student being carried.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level literature is planned, not hoped for
whyPoints.description: Two literary works with no timetabled reading slot is the standard HL problem in Dubai. We build a dated reading schedule in term one and a thematic quotation bank alongside it, because the HL oral stands on that work.

whyPoints.title: Level advice given honestly
whyPoints.description: A longer Paper 1 band gives a recurring fault more chances to appear. Sometimes a solid Standard Level grade is the better outcome, and we will say so in Year 11 while the change is still administratively simple.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: German B specialists are thin on the ground in any single Dubai community. Live video means the tutor is chosen for having taught this course at this level, which is the only variable that reliably predicts useful sessions.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around the Dubai year
whyPoints.description: Sessions sit after the school run on Gulf Standard Time, shift to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, pause for mock weeks and follow a family through travel. The weekly cycle is short enough to survive a disrupted month.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed credentials
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or the IB, and does not suggest otherwise. Where a regulator matters we explain its role and link to its own channel.

faqs.question: Should my child take German B at Higher Level or Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Look at written accuracy first and reading stamina second. Higher Level adds two literary works and a longer Paper 1 band, which means a recurring case or word-order fault has more opportunities to cost marks. A student who reads German prose without reaching for a dictionary and whose error rate is already low belongs at Higher Level. A student still guessing at endings in October of Year 12 will often finish with a better Diploma total at Standard Level, where the same accuracy produces a higher grade. Raise it with the IB coordinator in Year 11, while a change is still a form rather than a negotiation.

faqs.question: What literary works will my child study for German B HL?
faqs.answer: The school chooses them, within the IB's framework, and the choice usually varies by teacher and by year group. Ask the German teacher for the two titles and the term each one is covered in, because that single piece of information drives the entire Higher Level plan. Once the titles are known a tutor can build a dated reading schedule, a quotation bank organised by theme, and extract practice from the same works. Students who wait until the oral window to engage with the texts are the ones who struggle, since the oral starts from an extract and summaries do not survive a follow-up question.

faqs.question: My child speaks German at home but writes it badly. Which course is right?
faqs.answer: That is the classic heritage-speaker problem and it needs a written diagnostic rather than a conversation. Spoken fluency acquired at home builds vocabulary and intonation and teaches almost nothing about case endings, adjective agreement or formal register, because nobody speaks in formal register at the dinner table. Some of these students belong in German A: language and literature, where literary analysis rather than language accuracy carries the marks. Others are correctly placed in German B and simply need the written system taught from scratch. A timed task marked with every fault classified usually makes the answer obvious within an hour.

faqs.question: How is an error rate per hundred words actually calculated?
faqs.answer: Take a marked task, count every fault, classify each one by family, divide the total by the number of words the student wrote and multiply by a hundred. Record the task length alongside the figure, because accuracy per word is what you want to compare, not raw fault totals from pieces of different lengths. The breakdown by family is the part that guides teaching: a falling case count with a flat word-order count tells you exactly which drill worked and which has not started. It takes roughly four minutes per task and it is the difference between a chart and an impression.

faqs.question: Why do German case endings keep going wrong even after months of work?
faqs.answer: Usually because the underlying gender assignment is unreliable. Case endings depend on gender, so a student who is not certain whether a noun is masculine, feminine or neuter cannot produce the right ending no matter how well they know the case rules. The second common cause is that prepositions were learned individually rather than as groups taking the accusative, the dative, or either depending on motion. Fixing the symptom fails in both cases. The sequence that works is gender first, in bulk, then preposition groups as sets, then writing tasks engineered to force those prepositions into every other sentence.

faqs.question: Do you run German lessons at our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tuition is something we offer only in India. German B tuition for Dubai families runs one-to-one over live video, with the student's marked tasks and past papers shared on screen so both people annotate the same document. For this subject the arrangement is an advantage rather than a compromise: German B specialists at Higher Level are scarce in any single Dubai community, and matching online means the tutor is chosen for having taught the course at the level your child sits.

faqs.question: Will German B help with admission to a university in Germany or Switzerland?
faqs.answer: It can contribute, and it is not by itself a language qualification for a German-medium degree. Institutions in German-speaking countries set their own language evidence requirements, commonly through recognised proficiency tests, and those requirements differ between universities and between degree programmes. The only reliable source is the admissions page of the specific institution, read for the specific course and intake year. What German B does give a student is the underlying competence to meet such a requirement with modest additional preparation, which is a real advantage over starting from nothing in a gap year.

faqs.question: How much German reading should an HL student do each week?
faqs.answer: Enough that both literary works are finished well before the oral window, which in practice means a dated schedule rather than a weekly target. Divide each work by the number of weeks available, add a buffer for the two or three weeks every Diploma student loses to collisions with other subjects, and write the dates down. Twenty to thirty minutes on five days beats two hours on a Sunday, because retention of narrative detail decays and quotation banks need building as you read. The students who struggle are not slow readers; they are the ones who never scheduled it and arrived at the oral with summaries.

faqs.question: Can a tutor correct a German draft before my child submits it?
faqs.answer: A tutor can mark it, classify every fault by family, explain the rule behind each one and set a rewrite. A tutor cannot edit the draft into prose the student could not have produced, supply replacement sentences, or polish it to a standard the error profile does not support. The IB treats supplied content as malpractice and the penalty lands on the candidate. There is also a practical reason the stricter line is better: being handed a corrected sentence changes nothing measurable, while retrieving the right ending unaided is the act that moves the error rate.

faqs.question: Is it worth using a translation tool to check German homework?
faqs.answer: For checking a single word, occasionally. For producing or rewriting a task, no, on two grounds. A teacher who marks German every year sees the discontinuity between a tool-generated paragraph and the same student's known error profile, and that is a malpractice conversation nobody wants. The more persuasive argument for most students is simpler: the tool is not available in the examination room, so every task written with one is practice the student did not get. If a student cannot produce a paragraph unaided, that is the information the tutor needs rather than something to be hidden.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools offer German in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Group 2 staffing changes year to year, so your school's course booklet and IB coordinator are the only dependable source. In broad terms, German appears more often in the larger continuum schools and in schools with a strongly multilingual intake, including the Creek-side cluster and the Al Barsha concentration. Smaller or newer Diploma cohorts may offer German B in one year and not the next depending on numbers and staffing. If a school cannot run German B Higher Level, students occasionally take Standard Level instead or discuss alternative Group 2 options, and both of those conversations run through the coordinator.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a German B student usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session suits accuracy retraining, because the cycle is a task, classified marking, then drilling, and that cycle needs a week of space to work. Higher Level students in the term before the oral often move to two shorter sessions, since extract work and accuracy drilling compete badly for the same hour. Year 13 students whose accuracy is acceptable and whose Paper 2 is weak sometimes do better with one session plus independent listening volume, because listening improves with hours rather than with explanation. We would rather describe the honest shape than sell the larger block.

faqs.question: Can sessions be rearranged when my child is travelling between Dubai and Europe?
faqs.answer: Yes, and German B families do this more than most, because trips to German-speaking countries are often part of the point. Sessions run over live video, so a lesson can take place from a grandparent's kitchen in Vienna as easily as from a villa in Meydan, allowing for the time difference. What needs protecting during travel is the weekly cycle rather than the specific hour: if a task is written and marked, the session can shift by two days without losing anything. Tell the tutor the travel dates in advance and the sequence gets planned around them.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit from the authorities?
faqs.answer: An individual offering private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure quoted to you is unverified.

faqs.question: What if no German B Higher Level tutor is free when we enquire?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a realistic timeframe, instead of substituting a general German speaker. German B Higher Level is a narrow specialism, and in a given fortnight the pool may be fully committed. The options we would put to a family are a short wait for a named tutor, a tutor who covers German B Standard Level and has taught the Higher Level literary component recently, or a focused block on the single most urgent component. Which of those makes sense depends on how near the school's oral window is. Concealing a coverage gap behind a poor match is how a term gets wasted.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-online-tutor.closingHeading: Count the faults, then close them one family at a time
dubai/ib-dp-german-b-online-tutor.closingBody: If your child is taking German B in a Dubai school and the grade sits below what their spoken German suggests, the problem is almost certainly a small number of repeating faults rather than a general weakness. Book the free trial lesson, one per family with no card details required. The hour produces a timed written task in the correct word band, marked with every fault classified by family, and a ranked list of what to attack first. You will see the error rate per hundred words before deciding anything, and you will be able to watch it move.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB DP German B at Standard and Higher Level. They mark against the published criteria rather than giving a mark out of ten, keep an error log across sessions so patterns are visible, and record oral rehearsals so a student can watch their own word order collapse and then fix it.

intro.heading: How to tell whether German B tutoring is working, six weeks in
paragraphs: Most tutoring in this city is sold on inputs and reported on feelings. A family buys an hour a week, and after two months they are told the student is more confident. Confidence is real, and it is not evidence. For German B there is a better standard available, because every part of this subject produces something that can be kept, scored and compared: written tasks marked against three published criteria, listening and reading answers that are right or wrong, and an individual oral that is recorded.

That matters more in German than in most language subjects, because German errors are structural rather than lexical. A student does not drift gently towards accuracy. They guess the case after a two-way preposition, they put the verb in second position inside a subordinate clause where it belongs at the end, they reach for the Perfekt where the written register wants the Präteritum, and they apply an adjective ending from the wrong column. Those are four distinct error families, each with its own fix, and conversation practice will not reveal which one is doing the damage. A marked script will.

So the honest question to ask a German B tutor is not whether your child is improving. It is: show me the four most recent marked tasks, tell me the criterion scores on each, name the error family you targeted between task two and task three, and show me whether it moved. A tutor who can answer that in two minutes is working to evidence. A tutor who answers with a general impression may still be teaching well, but neither of you can tell.

Dubai makes the evidence question sharper for a practical reason. German B cohorts here are small, often a combined Standard and Higher Level group of a handful of students, and in a group that size a school's internal marks move for reasons that have nothing to do with the student: one strong classmate leaves, the teacher changes, an assessment is set at a different difficulty. Independent marked evidence is the only stable reference a Dubai family has, and it is the thing a tutor is uniquely placed to produce.

The rest of this page is the evidence specification: which artefacts a German B engagement should produce and how often, what the first diagnostic session must isolate, how Paper 1 is marked criterion by criterion, the four German error families and the diagnostic question that identifies each, a twelve-week cycle written out week by week, how recorded orals are used, and finally what evidence cannot do. Teaching is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students meet German through the language development core requirement rather than as an examined subject, so the evidence is a portfolio of documented development rather than criterion-scored tasks. The artefacts are different and the reporting cadence is different.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools run the CP, so families often reach this requirement without a clear sense of what evidence satisfies it. Support is short, and the measure of success is whether the portfolio stands up, not whether a paper score moved.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-tutor.subjectsIntro: The grid below lists the language acquisition courses we teach, described by what each one produces as measurable evidence, since that is the subject of this page.

subjects.name: German B
subjects.description: Highly diagnosable. Structural errors recur in predictable families, which means a marked task identifies the cause rather than just the symptom. Progress is visible within three marked tasks if the right family is targeted, and invisible for a term if the wrong one is.

subjects.name: German B HL literature
subjects.description: Evidence here is a recorded three to four minute response to an extract from one of the school's two chosen works, re-recorded a month later on a different extract. Comparing the two recordings is the only honest measure of whether discussion range has grown.

subjects.name: German ab initio
subjects.description: For genuine beginners, Standard Level only, with two short written tasks rather than one long one and no literature. Evidence is coverage-based: whether the student can produce five sentences and a minute of speech on each prescribed topic rather than recognise vocabulary on a slide.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: The same assessment architecture, a different error profile. French errors cluster in sound-to-spelling and in tense formation rather than in case and word order, so the diagnostic questions differ even though the marking criteria are identical.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Written accuracy arrives earlier than in German for most learners, so the evidence pattern inverts: Spanish students often show criterion gains on message and conceptual understanding first, with language scores already respectable.

subjects.name: Mandarin B
subjects.description: Reading speed is the measurable constraint. A timed reading log kept across a term shows progress more reliably than paper scores, because a student can understand everything and still run out of time in the exam.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Directly relevant in Dubai, where KHDA requires Arabic in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. A Diploma student taking Arabic B typically also sits in the school's mandatory Arabic stream, and the two produce different kinds of feedback.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Shares the internally assessed oral season with German B, so the two compete for the same DP2 rehearsal weeks. Families booking both should fix the order of the oral windows before booking either set of sessions.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Produces drafts rather than scores, and the drafts must be the student's own. A tutor comments on the student's thinking and the student's writing; the exhibition and the essay are written by the student alone.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-tutor.regionsIntro: The evidence cycle on this page runs identically wherever you live, because the lesson is delivered over video. What changes by community is the hour a session can hold without being cancelled, and a cancelled session produces no evidence at all.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Dense with international schools and with the in-home tutors who serve them, which is why diaries here fill first and why a family that needs a specific subject specialist rather than a nearby one gains most from online matching.

regions.name: Dubai Media City and Knowledge Park
regions.note: A working-parent corridor where sessions land after seven in the evening. Late slots are fine for recorded oral rehearsal and poor for accuracy work on cases, so the evidence cycle here is usually sequenced with writing at weekends.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Long school-bus routes mean a student may not sit down before five. A fixed five-thirty slot that survives the term produces twelve marked tasks; a four o'clock slot that collapses twice a month produces seven, and the difference shows in the review.

regions.name: The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Established villa communities a considerable drive from where language tutors cluster, so in-home quotes here carry heavy travel loading. The same budget online buys additional marking time, which is what actually generates evidence.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah
regions.note: A long-settled European community, so German is more often a heritage language here than a classroom one. That produces the fluent-but-uncriterioned profile, where language scores are strong and message and conceptual marks are not.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Jumeirah Islands
regions.note: Activity-heavy weekday schedules push sessions to weekend mornings, which are the slots language specialists lose first in the DP2 spring. Booking the weekend slot in September is worth more than negotiating the rate in February.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park and Green Community
regions.note: Outer communities where the practical choice has historically been whichever tutor would make the drive. For a subject with as few Dubai specialists as German B, online delivery changes the pool rather than merely the price.

regions.name: Mirdif and Rashidiya
regions.note: A mixed-curriculum area with a strong British-school presence, so German is commonly a second additional language started late. Those students need the error-family diagnostic first, because their gaps are structural rather than general.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Diploma schools German B students come from
schoolClusters.note: Students booking German B support through IB Gram attend Diploma schools across the emirate. Small combined-level sets are the norm, which is why independently marked tasks are the only stable reference point a family has across a two-year course.

schoolClusters.city: German-speaking community schools in Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Dubai has a long-established German-speaking population, and students moving from German-medium education into the Diploma arrive fluent but unfamiliar with the IB's criteria and text types. Their evidence profile is the inverse of the usual one.

sections.heading: The artefacts a German B engagement should produce
paragraphs: Progress in a language is invisible week to week and obvious across a term, which is why it has to be recorded rather than remembered. The table lists the artefacts a German B engagement should generate, who makes each one, what it actually proves and how often it should appear. A family holding these can answer the question honestly without relying on anyone's impression, including the tutor's.

Two of them do most of the work. The first is a criterion-scored written task, weekly, annotated rather than merely marked. Scores alone are weak evidence because task difficulty varies; scores plus annotation plus a named target are strong, because the next task tests the target. The second is the recorded oral taken on an unseen stimulus at a fixed interval, which is the only way to compare speaking performance against itself rather than against a memory of last term.

The error log is the least glamorous artefact and the most diagnostic. It is a running list of every structural error with its family tagged: case after a two-way preposition, verb position in a subordinate clause, past-tense register, adjective ending. After four weeks the distribution is unmistakable, and it is frequently not what either the student or the school believed. A student convinced they are bad at cases quite often turns out to be making almost all their case errors after one specific set of prepositions, which is a fifty-minute fix rather than a term's work.

What is not evidence: a mark out of ten with no criteria behind it, a comment that the student is engaging well, a percentage improvement with no sample size or method, or a predicted grade from anyone other than the school. We do not issue predicted grades, and any provider quoting a success statistic should be asked for the number of students, the dates and the method on the same page as the claim.

sections.heading: The first session is a diagnostic, not a lesson
paragraphs: A first German B session spent teaching is a wasted session, because nobody yet knows what to teach. The useful first hour is a set of probes designed to isolate error families, and it should produce a written finding rather than a warm feeling. Each probe is short, and together they take under an hour.

The probes are specific. Translate four sentences that each force a different case after a two-way preposition, and the case problem either appears or it does not. Write two sentences joined by a subordinating conjunction, and verb position shows itself immediately. Narrate the same short event twice, once as speech and once as a written report, and the Perfekt and Präteritum choice becomes visible. Describe a person with three adjectives before the noun, and the adjective ending column either is known or is being guessed. Read one short authentic-style text aloud and answer two questions pointing to the supporting words.

The table below sets out what each probe reveals and what we most often find in a Dubai cohort, where students arrive from very different German backgrounds. The fluent heritage speaker and the Year 10 late starter sitting in the same combined class produce almost opposite findings, and a tutor who begins teaching before establishing which one they have will spend six weeks on the wrong thing.

The output of the diagnostic should be written down and given to the family: the error families ranked, an estimated time to change each, and which one will be targeted first. That document is also the baseline against which the six-weekly review compares. Without a baseline, every later claim about progress is unfalsifiable, which is precisely how tutoring in this market usually gets reported.

sections.heading: Marking Paper 1 criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Paper 1 is a single written task chosen from three options, each naming a text type, an audience and a purpose. In the current guide it is marked on three criteria: language, message and conceptual understanding, carrying twelve, twelve and six marks. Check the exact allocations against your child's subject guide, because they belong to the IB, but the shape is what matters here. Grammar and vocabulary account for less than half the total.

This is why criterion-level marking changes a family's understanding of their own child. A student who scores well on language and badly on message is not weak at German; they are writing the wrong text. A student who scores respectably on both and loses the conceptual marks has not registered the audience and purpose they were given. Two students with the same overall mark can need entirely different teaching, and a single number at the top of a script hides that completely.

The practical cycle is three tasks long. Task one is marked across all three criteria with no target set, to establish the baseline. The lowest criterion becomes the target, and task two is written to a brief that tests it specifically. Task three checks whether the gain held when attention moved on, because a change that survives inattention is a change and anything else is compliance. Families should expect to see those three scripts together, not one at a time.

For German specifically, the language criterion rewards accurate structure more than ambitious vocabulary. A task written in controlled German with correct cases and verb positions scores better than one reaching for impressive nouns and losing control of the clause. Telling a student to write less ambitiously is counterintuitive advice that frequently gains three or four marks immediately, and it is the clearest example of why criterion-level evidence beats general encouragement.
bullets: Language, message and conceptual understanding at roughly 12, 12 and 6 marks

sections.heading: The four German error families, and the question that identifies each
paragraphs: Almost every structural error in a German B script belongs to one of four families, and each has a diagnostic question that identifies it in under a minute. This is the difference between German and most other B subjects: the errors are systematic, so they are fixable systematically rather than by general exposure.

Case selection is the first family, and it is usually narrower than students fear. Most case errors in Dubai scripts cluster after the prepositions that take either accusative or dative depending on whether movement is involved, rather than being spread evenly across all four cases. The diagnostic question is simply whether the error rate changes when those prepositions are removed from the task. If it does, the fix is a focused two to four weeks on motion versus position, not a term of grammar.

Verb position is the second. A student who knows perfectly well that the verb goes to the end of a subordinate clause will still leave it in second position when writing at speed, because the rule has not yet become automatic. The diagnostic is accuracy under timing against accuracy without it; a large gap means automation work, which is short sentences at volume rather than explanation. Explanation has already happened, often for years.

Past-tense register is the third and the one schools flag least. German draws a distinction between the spoken and written past that English does not, and a student who writes a formal report in the conversational past loses language and conceptual marks simultaneously. The fourth family is adjective endings, where students pick from the wrong column because they are reading the article rather than the case and gender. The table pairs each family with its symptom, its diagnostic question and the work that changes it.

sections.heading: A twelve-week cycle, written out
paragraphs: Evidence only means something on a schedule, so here is one term laid out. The cycle assumes one weekly session with marking between, a recorded oral every third week, and a written review at week six and week twelve. It is deliberately unremarkable: the value is that each week produces something a parent can look at.

Weeks one to three establish the baseline and target the first error family. The diagnostic in week one, the first marked task in week two, the first recorded oral in week three. By the end of week three a family should have a written statement of the error families in priority order, two criterion-scored scripts and one recording. If any of those three is missing, the engagement is already not producing evidence.

Weeks four to eight are the working middle, and they are where most tutoring quietly loses its thread. The protection is the retention check: the error family targeted in week four is retested in week seven, on a task that is not about it. If the gain held, the next family begins. If it did not, the same family continues, and the review says so rather than moving on to keep the sessions feeling fresh.

Weeks nine to twelve add exam conditions, because accuracy that survives timing is the only accuracy that counts in May. The second recorded oral is compared directly with the first from week three, which is the single most convincing artefact in the whole set. The week twelve review compares like with like: same criteria, same stimulus type, different task. Nothing in it predicts a grade, because predicting is the school's job and a prediction would be the least useful line on the page.

sections.heading: Why the recorded oral is the most useful thing we keep
paragraphs: The individual oral is internally conducted and recorded by the school, and it carries a quarter of the grade. At Standard Level it starts from a visual stimulus linked to one of the prescribed themes; at Higher Level it starts from an extract from one of the two literary works the school chose. Because the real thing is a recording, a rehearsal recording is an unusually faithful simulation, which makes it the best evidence in the set.

The mechanics matter. Rehearsals use a stimulus the student has genuinely not seen, under the real preparation conditions, and are marked against the same criteria every time. Changing the stimulus type between recordings destroys comparability, which is how families end up with four recordings that cannot be compared with each other. Keeping the format fixed and the content unseen is what makes the April recording meaningful next to the November one.

The second reason to record is that students do not believe descriptions of their own speech. Tell a student their word order collapses when they are thinking, and they will disagree. Show them ninety seconds of themselves doing it, and the next rehearsal is different. For the German error families in particular, which are structural and therefore audible, watching is worth more than being told, and it shortens the fix by weeks.

At Higher Level the recordings carry an extra job. They show whether the student can discuss a literary extract rather than retell it, which is the commonest Higher Level failure and the one a combined-level Dubai class has least time to address. A monthly extract response, recorded, is the only way to see that range growing. Ask any prospective Higher Level tutor which two works your child's school chose before agreeing anything, because a tutor working from different texts is rehearsing the wrong thing.

sections.heading: What evidence cannot do
paragraphs: Evidence tells you what has happened. It does not tell you what will happen, and a tutor who converts a marked-task trend into a promised grade has stopped doing the thing that made the evidence valuable. We do not issue predicted grades for German B. The school does that, with access to a full cohort and the school's own assessment history, and our review notes are written to be useful alongside that rather than in competition with it.

Nor does evidence justify statistics. A provider in this market claiming that a percentage of their students improved should be asked, on the same page, for the number of students, the dates covered and the method of measurement. Without those three, the figure is decoration. We publish none, which is a deliberate choice rather than an oversight: at the scale these pages operate, an unsourced number repeated across hundreds of URLs is hundreds of liabilities.

Two more limits worth stating plainly. A tutor can mark, annotate and teach; a tutor cannot write or rewrite work your child submits as their own, cannot draft an Extended Essay or a TOK essay, and has no part in a recorded individual oral beyond rehearsal beforehand. IB academic honesty rules place the consequences on the student. And on tutor status: we ask tutors to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's own channels. Holding it is a legal requirement for the tutor, not an endorsement of IB Gram by anyone.

For completeness on the things families often ask in the same breath: IB Gram operates no premises in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge endorsement, and does not offer home visits in the Emirates. Market rates in this city, from published provider rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table read in October 2026, run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified language teacher online and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB-experienced specialist. Our rate is agreed in writing after the free trial lesson.

process.title: Send two marked scripts before anything else
process.description: A written task with the teacher's annotations and, if one exists, a recording of an oral practice. Those two documents tell a German B tutor which error family is live, which is more useful than any report card and takes five minutes to read.

process.title: Free trial lesson run as a diagnostic
process.description: One lesson at no charge, one per student, with no card details taken. It runs the probes rather than teaching: case after two-way prepositions, verb position timed and untimed, the two past registers, adjective endings, and three minutes of unprepared speech.

process.title: Receive the baseline in writing
process.description: Error families ranked in priority order, an estimated time to change each, and the one that will be targeted first. You keep that document whatever you decide next, and every later review is compared against it rather than against a memory.

process.title: Weekly task, weekly marking, three-week oral
process.description: One criterion-scored task a week with marking done outside the paid hour, an error log updated every session, and a recorded oral on an unseen stimulus every third week against the same criteria so the recordings remain comparable.

process.title: Six-weekly review that can say no
process.description: A short written note comparing like with like: what was targeted, whether it moved, what happens next. If the targeted family has not shifted in six weeks, the method or the tutor changes. The note contains no predicted grade and no percentage claim.

whyPoints.title: Artefacts, not impressions
whyPoints.description: Every six weeks you hold marked scripts with criterion scores, an error log, two comparable oral recordings and a written review. You can judge the engagement yourself rather than taking anybody's word, including ours.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level marking
whyPoints.description: Language, message and conceptual understanding scored separately on every task. Two students with the same total mark often need opposite teaching, and a single number at the top of a script hides exactly that.

whyPoints.title: Error families, not error lists
whyPoints.description: German errors are systematic. Tagging each one by family turns thirty scattered corrections into one diagnosis, and a diagnosis has a time estimate attached to it rather than an indefinite plan.

whyPoints.title: Recordings kept and compared
whyPoints.description: Oral rehearsals on unseen stimuli at a fixed interval, marked the same way each time. A student in April watching themselves in November is the most convincing evidence available for an internally assessed component.

whyPoints.title: Reviews that are allowed to report failure
whyPoints.description: If the targeted error family has not moved in six weeks, the review says so and something changes. A reporting process that can only produce good news is not reporting.

whyPoints.title: Specialist matching over proximity
whyPoints.description: German B has few specialists in Dubai, and at Higher Level the right tutor is one who has read the two works your child's school chose. Teaching over live video makes that the selection criterion instead of driving distance.

faqs.question: How will I know whether German B tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: Ask for four things after six weeks: the marked written tasks with criterion scores on each, the running error log, two oral recordings made on unseen stimuli and marked the same way, and a written review comparing all of it with the week-one baseline. If the targeted error family's score has moved and the gain survived a task that was not about it, the teaching is working. If the only available answer is that your child seems more confident, you have no evidence either way, however good the lessons may be.

faqs.question: Why does my child make case errors in German that seem random?
faqs.answer: They are usually not random. In most Dubai scripts, case errors cluster after the prepositions that take either the accusative or the dative depending on whether movement is involved, rather than spreading evenly across all four cases. The diagnostic is quick: set a task that avoids those prepositions and see whether the error rate falls. If it does, the problem is narrow and typically takes two to four weeks of focused work on motion versus position, not a term of general grammar revision.

faqs.question: My child knows the verb goes to the end of a subordinate clause but still gets it wrong. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the rule is known and not yet automatic, which is a different problem with a different fix. The test is accuracy timed against accuracy untimed: a student who is correct when unhurried and wrong under pressure needs automation rather than explanation, and explanation has usually already happened for years. Automation means producing many short subordinate clauses at speed until the ordering stops requiring thought. It typically takes three to five weeks and it is boring, which is why it tends to get skipped in favour of something more interesting.

faqs.question: What are the Paper 1 criteria for German B and how are the marks split?
faqs.answer: In the current guide the single written task is marked on language, message and conceptual understanding, carrying twelve, twelve and six marks respectively. Confirm the allocations against your child's subject guide, since they are the IB's to revise. The important consequence is that fewer than half the available marks are grammar and vocabulary. A student scoring well on language and poorly on message is not weak at German; they have written the wrong kind of text for the audience and purpose the task specified, which is a different and much faster fix.

faqs.question: Should a German B tutor mark work inside or outside the lesson?
faqs.answer: Outside, and the answer changes the effective value of your hour by a third. Marking during a session consumes teaching time and produces a conversation rather than an artefact. Marking between sessions produces an annotated script with criterion scores that you can keep and compare, and leaves the paid hour for teaching the fix. Ask any prospective tutor directly whether marking is inside or outside the hour, because two quotes at the same AED rate can mean very different amounts of teaching.

faqs.question: How often should oral rehearsals be recorded for German B?
faqs.answer: Every third week, on a stimulus the student has genuinely not seen, under the real preparation conditions, and marked against the same criteria each time. Consistency is what makes the recordings worth keeping: changing the stimulus type between sessions produces four recordings that cannot be compared with one another. Recordings also change behaviour in a way that advice does not. A student who disputes that their word order collapses under pressure stops disputing it after watching ninety seconds of themselves doing it.

faqs.question: My child is fluent in German at home but scoring badly. What is going on?
faqs.answer: This is the commonest profile in Dubai's German-speaking community and it has a clear signature: strong language scores, weak message and conceptual understanding. Fluency hides nothing in conversation and everything in a scored task, because the IB is assessing whether the student produced the required text type for a stated audience and purpose, not whether they speak well. A single diagnostic written piece in the first fortnight identifies it, and the work that follows is text types and criteria rather than more German.

faqs.question: What does a useful six-weekly progress note look like?
faqs.answer: Four sections and no adjectives. What was targeted and why, the criterion scores for every task marked in the period, whether the targeted family moved and whether the gain survived a task that was not about it, and what changes next. At Higher Level it should also state how much of each literary work has been read and whether extract responses have grown beyond plot summary. What it must not contain is a predicted grade, which is the school's responsibility, or a percentage figure without a sample size, dates and method.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell me what grade my child will get in German B?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers one is overstepping. Predicted grades come from the school, which has the full cohort, the assessment history and the moderation context. What a tutor can honestly report is what has been marked, what moved and what did not, with the scripts available for you to read. Treat any grade promise, score guarantee or published improvement percentage without a stated sample size and method as a reason to ask harder questions rather than as reassurance.

faqs.question: Which two literary works does German B HL require, and when should they be read?
faqs.answer: Higher Level requires two literary works, and the school chooses them, so there is no universal list. Ask your child's teacher for the titles during the first term of DP1 and give them to any prospective tutor before agreeing a rate, because a tutor working from different texts is rehearsing the wrong oral. Reading should be finished well before the spring: the DP1 summer is the natural window for the second work, since reading travels in a way that grammar instruction does not.

faqs.question: How many marked German tasks should a term produce?
faqs.answer: Around twelve if the slot genuinely holds weekly, which is the real argument for a fixed session time rather than a flexible one. A slot that collapses twice a month produces seven, and seven scripts across three months is too thin to show a trend reliably. Twelve lets you see a baseline, a targeted change, a retention check and then the next family, which is the full diagnostic cycle. The count itself is worth asking about at the six-week review, because it quietly explains most disappointing terms.

faqs.question: Does German B tutoring have to follow my child's school scheme of work?
faqs.answer: It should know it and not be bound by it. The school's sequence determines which assessments are coming and therefore what has to be ready when, so a tutor needs the scheme. But the error family costing your child marks may not be the topic the class is on, and a tutor who only ever follows this week's classwork is doing homework support rather than diagnosis. The honest arrangement is to run the error-family cycle underneath, and surface to the school's topic in the week before each assessment.

faqs.question: Is German B tutoring in Dubai available during Ramadan and the holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the evidence cycle is one of the better reasons to keep something running. Sessions commonly shift to post-Iftar slots or to late weekend mornings during Ramadan, and because teaching is over live video a family travelling in the summer can hold the slot across a time-zone change rather than cancelling. The DP1 summer is also the natural window for Higher Level reading. What matters for evidence is continuity of interval: a recording every third week only means something if the third weeks keep happening.

faqs.question: What will a German B tutor not do with my child's work?
faqs.answer: A tutor will set tasks, mark them against the published criteria, annotate your child's own writing, maintain the error log, record and mark oral rehearsals, and supply model texts clearly labelled as the tutor's own for study. A tutor will not write or rewrite anything your child submits as their own, will not draft an Extended Essay or TOK essay, and has no role in the recorded individual oral itself. IB academic honesty rules put the consequences of malpractice on the student, so any offer of help with submitted work hands your family the risk.

dubai/ib-dp-german-b-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the baseline before you buy the term
dubai/ib-dp-german-b-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step in German B is not a lesson, it is a diagnostic that produces a document: error families ranked, a time estimate against each, and the one being targeted first. Book the free trial lesson, one per student with no card details taken, and that is what the hour will do. You keep the written baseline whatever you decide afterwards, and every review from then on compares against it rather than against anyone's recollection. Nobody here will predict a grade for your child, publish an improvement percentage, or touch work that has to be theirs. What we will do is show you the scripts.

dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Diploma Global Politics: the source-based paper, the essay paper, the engagement project and, at Higher Level, the two case studies presented orally. Each confirms your cohort's assessment model before planning anything, then marks written work between sessions.

intro.heading: Start by confirming which Global Politics course your child is sitting
paragraphs: Global Politics is a young Diploma subject that has already been revised once, and the revision is the first thing a Dubai family should pin down. A guide first taught from September 2024 sits alongside the model examined through 2025, and the two do not carry identical component names or weightings. Students in different year groups at the same Dubai school can therefore be preparing for differently weighted assessments, and a tutor who assumes the older model will build a revision plan that misallocates months of work. Nothing on this page is a substitute for the figures your school's IB coordinator gives you in writing.

That is why the first session is diagnostic rather than instructional. A tutor asks for the school's subject outline, establishes which guide the cohort follows, confirms the weighting of each component for that cohort, and only then decides what the student should spend time on. It is unglamorous and it is the highest-value hour in the whole engagement, because the difference between a 40 per cent essay paper and a 25 per cent one changes everything about what a weekly session should contain.

Once the model is fixed, the subject's own difficulty becomes visible. Global Politics is marked on concepts, not on opinions. The course is built around sixteen key concepts, four to each core unit, and essays are credited for using those concepts analytically with evidence from named, dated cases. Students who read widely and care about world events routinely score in the middle because they write a strongly held position with no conceptual framework behind it. That is a teachable problem and it is the most common one in this subject.

The components that produce evidence are generous here. Paper 1 works from a source booklet and ends in an extended evaluative question. Paper 2 asks for essays drawing on the units and the key concepts. The engagement project is a 2,000-word report on the student's own political engagement. At Higher Level there are two case studies presented orally, recorded and internally assessed. Each of those is an artefact that a tutor can mark, score and show you, which is why progress in Global Politics can be made as visible as progress in Maths.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled around Dubai school hours in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For this subject the trade is clear: Global Politics specialists are a small group even globally, and a Dubai family choosing from those available at 7pm on a Tuesday has a much wider choice online than within a twenty-minute drive. The trial lesson is free and no package has to be bought first.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Global Politics
programmes.description: Four core units examined across a source-based paper and an essay paper, an engagement project of up to 2,000 words on the student's own political engagement, and at Higher Level two case studies explored and presented orally. programmes.countryNote: Global Politics is offered by a minority of Dubai Diploma schools, which has a practical consequence: groups are small, teachers often carry the subject alongside History or Economics, and there is rarely a second specialist in the building. Dubai's IB cohort is itself a small share of a very large sector, with KHDA recording 387,441 private-school students in 227 schools for 2024-25 and the IB at 7 per cent of enrolment.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Individuals and Societies
programmes.description: The groundwork for Global Politics is conceptual rather than factual. Middle Years investigations that ask students to apply a concept to a case, rather than to report on an issue, build exactly the habit the Diploma course credits. Students who arrive able to define power, legitimacy and sovereignty precisely start DP1 months ahead of those who arrive well informed.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students reach DP1 from several different Middle Years and IGCSE backgrounds, and the gap is rarely knowledge. It is the ability to write a paragraph in which a concept does analytical work. Sessions diagnose that by marking one short piece against the Diploma expectation, which usually shows a student describing a situation accurately and never naming the concept at stake.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme with Diploma Global Politics
programmes.description: Career-related students take at least two Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a service-learning requirement.
