programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai school offers the Career-related Programme, a Global Politics student may be the only candidate in the subject that year. The practical effect is that there is no class discussion to learn from, and discussion is how this subject is normally learned. One-to-one sessions substitute for that directly, since the teaching method is argument rather than exposition.

dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Global Politics is organised around four core units and sixteen key concepts, with an additional extension at Higher Level. These are the parts of the course IB Gram's tutors teach. Check which units your school sequences first, because Dubai schools differ and the order changes what a tutor should start on.

subjects.name: Unit: Power, sovereignty and international relations
subjects.description: The conceptual foundation of the course: power in its forms, sovereignty and its limits, legitimacy, and interdependence between states and other actors. Students handle examples well and define the concepts loosely, which caps essay marks because the concept is what the examiner is crediting.

subjects.name: Unit: Human rights
subjects.description: Human rights frameworks, claims and contested interpretations, justice, liberty and equality as concepts rather than slogans. The unit where opinion most often replaces analysis, and where a tutor's main job is teaching a student to set out a contested position fairly before evaluating it.

subjects.name: Unit: Development
subjects.description: Contested meanings of development, measurement and indicators, globalisation, inequality and sustainability. Data-literate students do well here. The common failure is treating a development indicator as a fact rather than as a choice about what to measure, which is precisely the analytical move the unit wants.

subjects.name: Unit: Peace and conflict
subjects.description: Definitions of peace, conflict and violence, non-violence, conflict dynamics and resolution. Requires precision about terms a student thinks they already know. An essay that uses violence and conflict interchangeably has already lost the conceptual marks before the evidence arrives.

subjects.name: The sixteen key concepts
subjects.description: Four concepts anchor each unit, and they are the currency of the subject. Power, sovereignty, legitimacy and interdependence; human rights, justice, liberty and equality; development, globalisation, inequality and sustainability; peace, conflict, violence and non-violence. Every essay should be using at least two of them analytically.

subjects.name: Paper 1: the source-based paper
subjects.description: A short source booklet with questions of increasing weight, ending in an extended evaluative question that asks for a judgement using the sources and the student's own knowledge. The final question carries the most marks and is the one most often started with too little time left.

subjects.name: Paper 2: the essay paper
subjects.description: Essays chosen from questions spanning the core units, with Higher Level writing more of them in a longer paper. Marked for a sustained argument that uses the key concepts with named, dated evidence. Breadth of reading is not the differentiator; conceptual discipline is.

subjects.name: The engagement project
subjects.description: A report of up to 2,000 words in which the student examines a political issue through their own engagement with it, connecting experience to the course's concepts and theory. Internally assessed. Choosing an appropriate, lawful and genuinely achievable engagement is the whole game.

subjects.name: Higher Level extension: global political challenges
subjects.description: Two case studies on political challenges, researched independently and presented orally, recorded for internal assessment and moderation. The only component in the subject that is examined by speech rather than writing, and the one students prepare for last.

subjects.name: Case study discipline
subjects.description: Not a unit, but the skill that separates a 5 from a 7. A usable case needs a name, a date range, the actors involved, the contested interpretations, and the concept it illustrates. Two cases known to that standard beat a dozen mentioned in passing in every single component.

sections.heading: Which guide is your cohort sitting, and why the answer changes the plan
paragraphs: Global Politics has been revised, and in a subject this small that revision is poorly communicated to parents. A guide first taught from September 2024 runs alongside the assessment model examined through 2025, and the component names and weightings differ between them. Two students at the same Dubai school in consecutive year groups can be sitting differently structured assessments. A tutor who assumes one model and plans accordingly will put months of revision into a component that carries less weight for that cohort than assumed.

The fix is a question, asked in the first session and answered in writing by the school. What guide does this cohort follow, what are the components, and what is each one worth. Any Diploma coordinator can answer that in a sentence. The figures in the table below are given with their source stated rather than asserted as current, because the responsible position for a page like this one is to show you what to confirm rather than to publish numbers your child will revise against.

The reason this matters more in Global Politics than elsewhere is the spread of component types. This subject examines by source paper, by essay, by internally assessed report and, at Higher Level, by recorded oral presentation. Those four demand different preparation on different timescales. An oral component that is worth a fifth of the grade needs rehearsal time blocked out months ahead; an essay paper worth twice that needs weekly marked writing instead. Getting the proportions right is the difference between a plan and a guess.

sections.heading: Why well-read students score fives in this subject
paragraphs: The most common profile in Dubai Global Politics is a student who follows world events closely, argues confidently, writes fluently, and sits at a 5. The reason is structural rather than intellectual. This course credits the analytical use of its own concepts. An essay that explains a situation accurately and never names the concept at stake has not done the task, however informed it is, because the examiner is reading for whether power, legitimacy, sovereignty or interdependence has been used to do work.

There is a second habit behind it. Students bring positions to this subject, which is healthy, and then write to defend them. The markbands reward setting out a contested interpretation fairly and then evaluating it, which is a different intellectual act from arguing a case. An essay on human rights that treats one interpretation as obviously correct and does not represent the alternative seriously has capped itself in the middle bands before the evidence appears.

The repair is specific and quick to teach. Each paragraph begins by naming the concept it is testing, states the strongest version of the position it is examining, applies the concept to a named and dated case, and arrives at an evaluative sentence. Four paragraphs built that way score higher than a flowing argument twice the length. Sessions mark essays with a two-column audit: concepts named, concepts actually used. The gap between those two columns is usually the grade.

The side effect is that essays get shorter and better at the same time, which students find counter-intuitive and parents find reassuring. A fluent writer producing nine hundred words of informed commentary is working harder for fewer marks than a student producing six hundred words in four disciplined paragraphs. Sessions therefore spend time cutting as well as building, and the first thing to go is the introduction that surveys the whole issue before the argument begins.
bullets: Name the concept at the start of the paragraph, not in the conclusion
State the strongest version of the position you intend to evaluate
Attach each concept to a named, dated case with actors identified
Finish each paragraph with an evaluative sentence, not a summary

sections.heading: The key concepts, and what an essay has to do with each
paragraphs: Sixteen concepts carry this course, four to a unit, and they are the most under-taught part of it. Students learn them as definitions to be recited in an introduction. They are tools for analysis, and the difference shows in a single paragraph. Sovereignty recited is a sentence about supreme authority within a territory. Sovereignty used is a paragraph that tests whether a named intervention respected or eroded it, and reaches a judgement.

The table below sets out what each concept group has to do in an answer. It is the single most useful page of notes a Global Politics student can own, because it converts a vocabulary list into a set of instructions. A student who can do the right analytical move with four or five concepts reliably will outscore one who can define all sixteen, and this is the only subject in the group where that statement is unambiguously true.

Working through it has a side effect worth having. Concepts cut across units, so a case used for peace and conflict is usually also a case about sovereignty and legitimacy. A student who builds five or six cases properly and learns to read each of them through three or four concepts has a usable bank for both papers and for the Higher Level orals. That is what replaces the frantic accumulation of examples most students attempt in the final term.

One exercise does most of this work. Take a single case the student already knows and write four short paragraphs on it, one per concept, each ending in a judgement. The first two are usually easy and the last two force real thinking, which is the point. Doing that on five cases over a term gives a student twenty paragraphs of practised analysis and a demonstrable grasp of how the concepts behave under pressure, and it is far more efficient than reading about a sixth case.

sections.heading: Paper 1: the source booklet and the question that decides the paper
paragraphs: Paper 1 gives a short booklet of sources on a political issue and asks a sequence of questions of rising weight, finishing with an extended evaluative question that asks for a judgement drawing on the sources and the student's own knowledge. That final question carries the most marks on the paper and is routinely attempted with the least time, which is the most fixable problem in the whole subject.

Two habits fix it. The first is reading the final question before reading the sources, so the earlier answers are built while the destination is already known. The second is an allocation rule: time divided by marks, written on the paper at the start, and adhered to even when an early question feels worth more attention. Students who do this well finish the evaluative question properly rather than running out of paper and conviction simultaneously.

The source handling itself rewards a specific scepticism. These are political sources, so provenance is not a formality: who produced this, for which audience, and what does that do to the claim it makes. A student who can say that a government statement is weak evidence of conditions on the ground and strong evidence of how a state wished to be perceived has made the move the paper is testing. That is the same intellectual habit the essay paper rewards, which is why the two components are practised together rather than separately.

Dubai students bring an advantage to this paper that they rarely use. Growing up in a city where international news arrives through several different national media traditions at once makes the idea of a source having an audience and a purpose intuitive rather than abstract. Sessions make that explicit by putting two reports of the same event side by side and asking not which is true but what each one was written to do. Students who have done that exercise a few times stop writing about bias and start writing about purpose.
bullets: Read the final evaluative question before reading the sources
Write a time-per-mark allocation on the paper before answering anything
Treat provenance as analysis: audience and purpose, not just author
Bring own knowledge to the final question; the sources alone cap the mark

sections.heading: The engagement project: choosing something appropriate and achievable
paragraphs: The engagement project asks a student to engage with a political issue in practice and then examine that experience against the course's concepts and theory, in a report of up to 2,000 words. The component fails at the choosing stage far more often than at the writing stage, and in the UAE context the choice deserves real thought rather than enthusiasm. The engagement has to be lawful, appropriate, approved by the school, and genuinely achievable by a sixteen-year-old in Dubai within a term.

The good news is that Dubai offers more than most cities. Humanitarian and development organisations, large international institutions, community and charitable work, environmental and sustainability initiatives, and the emirate's substantial Model United Nations circuit all provide routes into real engagement with real issues. A student can volunteer with a community organisation, work on a local sustainability initiative, participate in a structured simulation, or interview practitioners in a sector, and all of those give a report something to analyse. What they cannot do is produce the analysis by themselves.

Two practical rules save the report. Get written school approval for the engagement before it begins, because an engagement the school will not accept is a term wasted. And keep a contemporaneous log while it happens, two or three sentences per occasion: what happened, who was involved, which concept it touched, what surprised you. Students who reconstruct an engagement from memory three months later write a thin report about an interesting experience. Students with a log write an analysis. A tutor can teach the connection between experience and theory, read one draft against the criteria and give written feedback; the report itself has to be the student's own work from start to finish.
bullets: Confirm school approval in writing before the engagement starts
Choose something lawful, appropriate and completable within a term
Keep a log of two or three sentences per occasion while it happens
Connect each experience to a named concept, not to a general theme
The 2,000 words are for analysis; narrative should take up as little as possible

sections.heading: The Higher Level extension: two case studies, delivered out loud
paragraphs: Higher Level students research two case studies on global political challenges and present them orally, recorded for internal assessment and moderation. This is the only component in the subject examined by speech, and it is the one students prepare for last, because speaking tasks feel like something that can be done at short notice. They cannot. An argument that reads well on paper often collapses when spoken, because the listener has no ability to re-read a sentence.

Structure for the ear is a learnable thing. Signpost the argument at the start so the listener knows where it is going. Make one claim per stretch of speech rather than stacking qualifications. Name the case, the date range and the actors early, because an audience that is still working out who is involved is not following the analysis. Return to the question explicitly at the end instead of trailing off at the time limit. None of that is natural, and all of it comes from rehearsing to the clock and watching the recording back.

Case selection is the other half. A challenge that is too large produces a survey rather than an analysis, and too narrow produces description. The workable scale is a challenge that can be examined through three or four of the course's concepts, with evidence from a bounded set of events and actors. Sessions test two candidate challenges against that standard before any research begins, then rehearse, record and critique. Students who have watched one of their own recordings improve more in that twenty minutes than in a week of reading.
bullets: Signpost the argument in the first thirty seconds of speaking
Name the case, the dates and the actors before the analysis starts
Rehearse to the clock and watch the recording back at least once
Pick a challenge that fits three or four concepts, not a whole region

sections.heading: Making progress visible in a subject marked on concepts
paragraphs: Global Politics is a subject where parents are especially dependent on somebody else's judgement, because an articulate teenager sounds impressive discussing world affairs regardless of whether their essays are improving. The answer is to insist on artefacts. Every component in this subject produces something that can be marked and compared over time, and a tutor who keeps those produces an honest record rather than a reassuring impression.

The pack below is what IB Gram tutors keep for a Dubai Global Politics student. The concept audit is the distinctive item and the most useful: a two-column list of concepts named in an essay against concepts that did analytical work in it. A student whose two columns start to converge is improving, and that convergence happens weeks before any grade moves, which makes it the earliest honest signal available.

Read the case bank alongside it. Five or six cases known with names, dates, actors and contested interpretations is a stronger position than a long list of examples, and it is countable. If the bank is not growing in depth across six weeks, the sessions are producing discussion rather than preparation. That is a conversation to have at six weeks rather than at the mock, and the point of writing it down is that the conversation becomes possible at all.

The pack has a second use that parents appreciate once they see it. It gives a student something to show their school teacher, who is marking twenty or thirty scripts and has limited room for individual diagnosis. A marked essay with a concept audit attached is a specific question a teacher can answer in two minutes, and the answer is usually worth more than an hour of general advice. Tutoring that makes a student easier for their own teacher to help is doing more than it is being paid for.

sections.heading: Sources, honesty and the permit question in the UAE
paragraphs: A subject about contested politics needs a clear line on what a tutor does with sources and drafts. A tutor may teach how to read a source critically, explain what the markbands credit, discuss a position the student has taken, suggest the kinds of material that exist on a question, read one draft and give written feedback. A tutor may not supply paragraphs, write a report, or hand over analysis for a student to submit. The engagement project and the Higher Level case studies are internally assessed and the student signs for the authorship of both.

Generative tools deserve naming directly in this subject, because the temptation is highest where the writing is argumentative. A student can use them to find reading or to check their own grammar. A student cannot use them to produce sentences that go into an assessed piece, and Dubai schools increasingly ask candidates to show a research process. A short log kept while the work happens makes that straightforward. Official IB material, past papers and markschemes are linked at their source rather than reproduced, which is both a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

On the regulatory question that no competitor page in this search answers properly: private tutoring in the UAE requires the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask any tutor whether they hold it. Dubai's schools are overseen by KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK; Sharjah by SPEA; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or endorsement from any of those bodies, or from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: What Global Politics tutoring costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: Rates read from Dubai providers' own published pages in October 2026 put shared online sessions from about AED 33 to AED 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to AED 300, in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 500, and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. A named premium tutor advertises AED 650. Monthly packages are quoted at AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. None of those are IB Gram prices; IB Gram quotes per match in AED per 60 minutes after a free trial.

Global Politics sits at the specialist end for a supply reason rather than a prestige one. The subject is taught in a minority of schools worldwide, so the pool of tutors who have taken a cohort through both papers, an engagement project and the Higher Level orals is genuinely small. A Dubai family restricting that pool further to people willing to drive to their community at 6pm is choosing from a very short list, and the travel premium in the in-home band is what pays for that drive.

Three questions separate a useful quote from a vague one. Is the rate per 60 minutes or per session. Is marking between sessions included or billed on top. And has this tutor taught the Higher Level extension through to a submitted recording, which is the component least likely to be covered by someone who has only taught Standard Level. A provider that will not answer those three before the first lesson is unlikely to become clearer afterwards, and three of the six most visible pages in this search publish no price at all.

process.title: Confirm the cohort's guide and weightings
process.description: Before anything is planned, the school confirms in writing which guide your child's year group follows and what each component is worth. A Diploma coordinator answers that in one message. It is the difference between a revision plan and a guess, and it is the first thing a tutor should ask you for.

process.title: Send the subject outline and one marked essay
process.description: The outline shows which units have been taught and in what order. A marked essay shows whether the issue is conceptual discipline, evidence depth, or writing under time. With both, the trial lesson starts on the real problem instead of spending itself on diagnosis.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session, no cost, no card, no package. Watch for whether the tutor audits concept use in your child's own writing or delivers an interesting talk about international relations. The first moves marks in a subject assessed on concepts. The second is available free on any podcast.

process.title: Block out the oral component early at Higher Level
process.description: The two recorded case studies are worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade and are the component students leave until last. Rehearsal dates go in the calendar months ahead, with at least two timed run-throughs and a playback, because speaking to a clock is learned by doing it badly first.

process.title: Review the evidence pack every six weeks
process.description: Marked essays with the concept audit, timed Paper 1 final questions, the depth of the case bank, the engagement draft against its criteria, and any oral recording. If the two columns of the concept audit are not converging after six weeks, the plan or the tutor changes.

whyPoints.title: The cohort question gets asked first
whyPoints.description: Global Politics has been revised, and the component weightings a student should revise against depend on which guide their year group follows. IB Gram tutors confirm that with the school before planning anything, rather than assuming a model and discovering the mistake in a mock.

whyPoints.title: Marked on concepts, taught on concepts
whyPoints.description: Essays come back with a two-column audit: concepts named against concepts that did analytical work. That gap is usually the grade, and it narrows weeks before any mark moves, which makes it the earliest honest signal of progress available in this subject.

whyPoints.title: The oral component is actually rehearsed
whyPoints.description: The Higher Level extension is two case studies delivered out loud and recorded. Tutors rehearse it to the clock and watch the recording back with the student, because an argument that reads well often collapses when spoken and nobody discovers that during the submission.

whyPoints.title: Engagement choices tested before they start
whyPoints.description: The project fails at the choosing stage more than at the writing stage. A session tests whether an engagement is lawful, appropriate, school-approved and completable in a term by a student in Dubai, which prevents the commonest and most expensive mistake in the component.

whyPoints.title: Depth over breadth in the case bank
whyPoints.description: Five or six cases known with names, dates, actors and contested interpretations beat a dozen mentioned in passing in every component. The bank is written down and reviewed monthly, so growth in depth is countable rather than a matter of anyone's impression.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly: online, one-to-one
whyPoints.description: Sessions run over live video on Gulf Standard Time around school hours and prayer times. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. In a subject with few specialists anywhere, that is what makes a real match possible.

faqs.question: Has the IB Global Politics course changed, and does it affect my child?
faqs.answer: A revised guide was first taught from September 2024, alongside the assessment model examined through 2025, and the component names and weightings are not identical between them. Two year groups in the same Dubai school can therefore be sitting differently weighted assessments. Ask your IB coordinator in writing which guide your child's cohort follows and what each component is worth. Any tutor you engage should ask you for the same information before planning revision, because the difference between a 40 per cent essay paper and a 25 per cent one changes what a weekly session should spend its time on.

faqs.question: Why does my child argue well about politics and still score a 5?
faqs.answer: Because the subject credits the analytical use of its own concepts rather than the quality of a position. An essay can explain a situation accurately, write fluently and never make power, legitimacy, sovereignty or interdependence do any work, and that caps it in the middle bands. The second habit behind it is defending a position instead of evaluating competing interpretations fairly. The repair is paragraph-level: name the concept first, state the strongest version of the view you are testing, apply it to a named dated case, and end with an evaluative sentence rather than a summary.

faqs.question: What are the sixteen key concepts in Global Politics?
faqs.answer: Four anchor each core unit. Power, sovereignty, legitimacy and interdependence sit with power and international relations. Human rights, justice, liberty and equality sit with the human rights unit. Development, globalisation, inequality and sustainability sit with development. Peace, conflict, violence and non-violence sit with peace and conflict. Students learn them as definitions to recite and the marks are for using them as tools. Sovereignty recited is a sentence about supreme authority. Sovereignty used is a paragraph testing whether a named intervention respected or eroded it, reaching a judgement.

faqs.question: How long is the Global Politics engagement project and what goes in it?
faqs.answer: The report runs to a maximum of 2,000 words and examines a political issue through the student's own engagement with it, connecting that experience to the course's concepts and theory. It is internally assessed. The word limit is the real constraint: students write narrative about what they did and run out of space for analysis, which is what the criteria credit. Keep the description of the engagement as short as it can be while remaining clear, and spend the words on what the experience revealed when read through the relevant concepts.

faqs.question: What counts as suitable political engagement for a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Something lawful, appropriate, approved by the school in advance, and genuinely completable by a sixteen-year-old within a term. Dubai offers more routes than most cities: humanitarian and development organisations, community and charitable work, sustainability initiatives, large international institutions, and a substantial Model United Nations circuit. Volunteering with a community organisation, contributing to a local environmental project, participating in a structured simulation or interviewing practitioners in a sector all give a report real material. Get the school's approval in writing before starting, because an engagement the school will not accept costs a whole term.

faqs.question: Should my child keep a log during the engagement project?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single cheapest thing that improves the report. Two or three sentences per occasion: what happened, who was involved, which concept it touched, what was unexpected. Students who reconstruct an engagement from memory three months later write a thin report about an interesting experience. Students with a contemporaneous log write analysis, because they have specific moments to read through the course's theory. It takes a couple of minutes each time and it also makes the authorship of the work easy to evidence if anyone ever asks.

faqs.question: What is the Higher Level extension in Global Politics?
faqs.answer: Higher Level students research two case studies on global political challenges and present them orally, recorded for internal assessment and moderation. It is the only component in the subject examined by speech, which is why it is both distinctive and neglected. An argument that reads well on paper often collapses when spoken, because a listener cannot re-read a sentence. Signposting, one claim at a time, naming the case and actors early, and returning explicitly to the question at the end are all learned by rehearsing to the clock and watching the recording back.

faqs.question: How should a case study for the oral presentation be chosen?
faqs.answer: By scale. A challenge that is too large produces a survey instead of an analysis, and one that is too narrow produces description. The workable size is a challenge that can be examined through three or four of the course's concepts, with evidence drawn from a bounded set of events and actors. Test two candidates against that standard before any research begins, because research time spent on an unworkable case is not recoverable. The second test is whether the student can state the challenge, the actors and the contested interpretations in sixty seconds without notes.

faqs.question: How many case studies does a Global Politics student actually need?
faqs.answer: Five or six known properly, not a dozen known vaguely. A usable case carries a name, a date range, the actors involved, the contested interpretations of what happened, and the concepts it illustrates. Because concepts cut across units, a case built to that standard is usable in several essays and often in the oral component too. The frantic accumulation of examples in the final term is what students do instead, and it produces answers full of references that cannot survive a follow-up question. Depth here is also countable, which makes it trackable.

faqs.question: Why do students run out of time on the Paper 1 evaluative question?
faqs.answer: Because they read the sources before reading the final question, then answer the earlier questions generously, and arrive at the most heavily weighted question with the least time. Two habits fix it. Read the final question first so earlier answers are written with the destination known. Then write a time-per-mark allocation on the paper before answering anything and hold to it even when an early question feels interesting. The final question also needs the student's own knowledge: an answer built only from the sources caps itself regardless of how carefully they are handled.

faqs.question: Is Diploma Global Politics harder than A Level Politics?
faqs.answer: They are different rather than ranked, and several Dubai schools offer both, so the comparison is worth making before option forms are signed. Diploma Global Politics requires an internally assessed engagement project, examines through concepts rather than institutions, and at Higher Level adds a recorded oral component. A Level routes concentrate more of the grade in terminal written papers and tend to be heavier on specific political systems. A student who writes strongly under time pressure may prefer one; a student who works steadily and presents well may prefer the other.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the engagement project without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth stating. A tutor may discuss whether an engagement is suitable and feasible, teach how experience connects to the course's theory, explain what the assessment criteria credit, read one draft and give written feedback on where it falls short. A tutor may not supply paragraphs, provide analysis or hand over any text for the report. The student signs for the authorship of this component and of the Higher Level recordings. One provider visible in this search sells completed assessed work; the consequence of using it falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: What does Global Politics tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Figures read from Dubai providers' own pages in October 2026: shared online sessions from about AED 33 to AED 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors AED 150 to AED 300, in-home visits AED 180 to AED 500, IB specialists AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with one named premium tutor advertising AED 650. Monthly packages appear at AED 799 for eight online sessions. Global Politics sits at the specialist end because the subject is taught in a minority of schools worldwide, so experienced tutors are genuinely scarce. IB Gram quotes per match in AED per 60 minutes after a free trial.

faqs.question: My child is the only Global Politics student in their year. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more in this subject than in most, because the course is normally learned through argument with other people. A student with no classmates has nobody to disagree with, and disagreement is the mechanism by which they learn to represent a position they do not hold. One-to-one teaching substitutes for that directly, since the method is discussion rather than exposition. Small or single-candidate groups are common in Dubai, where Global Politics is offered by a minority of Diploma schools and often taught by a teacher who also carries History or Economics.

faqs.question: Does a Global Politics tutor working in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Anyone providing private tutoring in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a separate educational services permit from KHDA. IB Gram holds no approval or endorsement from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

intro.heading: Global Politics rewards argument, and punishes current affairs
paragraphs: Students choose Global Politics because they follow the news and enjoy arguing about it. That enthusiasm carries them through DP1 and then stalls, because the course is not about events. It is about sixteen key concepts, four compulsory units, and the ability to use a concept as an analytical tool rather than as a label. A student who writes four pages on a conflict without naming legitimacy, sovereignty or interdependence has written journalism, and journalism scores in the lower bands however well informed it is.

The second thing families discover late is how much of the grade is internally generated. Every candidate completes a piece of engagement work: they involve themselves in a political issue in a real, documented way, and then produce an analytical report of around two thousand words connecting that experience to the course's concepts and theory. Higher Level candidates add two recorded presentations on global political challenges. None of those three things is a timed paper, and none of them gets much individual supervision in a school running one Politics teacher across two year groups.

Dubai cohorts make this sharper. Global Politics classes here are often small, sometimes fewer than ten students, taught by a teacher whose main subject is History or Economics. The discussion in those rooms is usually excellent, because the students come from a dozen national backgrounds and bring genuinely different starting assumptions. What the discussion does not produce on its own is paragraph discipline: a claim, a concept, evidence, a counter-position, and a judgement that answers the question asked.

An IB DP global politics online tutor in Dubai is therefore mostly an editor and a marker rather than a lecturer. The content is not voluminous. A student can be taught the whole of the Human Rights unit in a handful of hours. What takes time is writing twelve essay answers, each marked against the band descriptors, until the student stops narrating and starts arguing. That work is individual by nature, which is exactly what a class of nine cannot deliver and an hour one-to-one can. It is also cumulative, so the same twenty hours spread across DP1 and DP2 are worth considerably more than twenty hours bought in the final term.

Delivery for UAE families is over live video, one-to-one, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are not part of what IB Gram sells anywhere in the Emirates; that service exists only in India, and we would rather state it here than have it surface after a booking. The compensating benefit is specific to this subject: Global Politics specialists are not thick on the ground in any city, so selecting from everyone who can teach your child at seven in the evening beats selecting from everyone who can reach Jumeirah Village Circle by then.

dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Dubai students arrive at Diploma Global Politics from three directions: MYP Individuals and Societies, an IGCSE in History or Global Perspectives, or no social science at all beyond Year 9. The third group is larger than schools expect, and they need the concept vocabulary built from nothing. Here is how the IB programmes Dubai schools run feed into this course.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies in the MYP uses four assessment criteria, one of which is explicitly about thinking critically. Students who have been marked against that criterion arrive at Global Politics already used to the idea that an unsupported opinion scores nothing. The MYP personal project is also their only prior experience of self-directed work with a documented process, which is the nearest thing to the engagement project.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai runs a large MYP population, and several schools take students straight from Year 11 MYP into the Diploma. Those candidates are usually the strongest discussants in a Global Politics class and the weakest at timed writing, because MYP assessment is rarely done under a clock. A diagnostic essay in the first fortnight of DP1 is worth more for them than a term of content.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Global Politics sits in Group 3 and is built around four compulsory units and a set of key concepts applied across all of them. Assessment combines a source-based paper, an essay paper, internally assessed engagement work, and at Higher Level two recorded presentations on global political challenges drawn from different topics. Standard and Higher Level share the core; Higher Level adds breadth and the oral component.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Global Politics is frequently the smaller option against History in the same Group 3 block, which means timetabling can put it against a science or a second language. Families should check before DP1 whether taking it forces a Higher Level choice elsewhere, because that constraint has pushed more than one capable candidate into Standard Level for scheduling reasons rather than ability.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Career-related Programme students take at least two Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and language development. Global Politics works unusually well in that combination, because the reflective project and the engagement work both ask for documented involvement in a real issue rather than for recall.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Dubai schools run the Career-related Programme, so a CP student taking Global Politics is often working largely alone on it. The practical risk is overlap: the reflective project and the engagement report must be genuinely separate pieces of work on separate issues, and a tutor checking that early saves an awkward conversation with the coordinator later.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no politics content, but it does build the habit the Diploma course depends on: asking who decides, who benefits and who is left out. The exhibition in the final PYP year is a student's first piece of independent, documented enquiry, and the better it is supervised the easier the MYP personal project and the engagement project become later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's PYP provision is extensive and many of those primaries sit on the same campus as a Diploma school. Where families switch out at Year 7 into a British curriculum and then return to the Diploma at sixteen, the gap shows up less in knowledge than in tolerance for ambiguity, which Global Politics requires more of than any other Group 3 subject.

dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: There is no option menu in Global Politics. Every candidate studies the same four units, which means a tutor can be matched on teaching quality rather than on syllabus coincidence. What varies is depth and the case studies a school has chosen. Below is the content a tutor works across, with what each part assesses.

subjects.name: Power, Sovereignty and International Relations
subjects.description: The nature and types of power, state sovereignty and its limits, legitimacy, the role of intergovernmental organisations and non-state actors, and theories of international relations. The marks go to students who can apply a theoretical lens deliberately rather than describe a dispute.

subjects.name: Human Rights
subjects.description: The nature and evolution of rights claims, codification, monitoring and enforcement, cultural relativism against universality, and the politicisation of rights. The most reliable source of marks and the easiest unit to write badly, because moral language crowds out analysis.

subjects.name: Development
subjects.description: Contested meanings of development, measurement and its limitations, factors that enable or obstruct it, and the pathways different states have taken. Numerical literacy matters here: a student who cannot explain what a composite index conceals will struggle on the data elements of Paper 1.

subjects.name: Peace and Conflict
subjects.description: Definitions of peace, violence and conflict, causes and parties, conflict dynamics, and approaches to resolution including non-violence and post-conflict transformation. Students default to narrating a war; the questions almost always ask about a process or a typology instead.

subjects.name: Key Concepts: power, legitimacy, sovereignty, interdependence
subjects.description: These four are the load-bearing concepts of the course and the ones examiners look for first. A paragraph that names one and then uses it to explain something scores; a paragraph that mentions it in passing does not. Worth drilling as a vocabulary exercise early in DP1.

subjects.name: Key Concepts: justice, liberty, equality, inequality
subjects.description: The normative cluster, and where students most often slide from analysis into advocacy. The course does not ask whether something is unjust; it asks how competing conceptions of justice explain the positions actors take. Rewriting one essay with that distinction enforced usually moves a grade.

subjects.name: Key Concepts: development, globalisation, sustainability
subjects.description: The concepts that connect the Development unit to the other three. Candidates who hold these well can answer synthesis questions that reward reaching across units, which is where the top band on Paper 2 usually sits.

subjects.name: The Engagement Project
subjects.description: Documented personal engagement with a political issue, plus an analytical report of around two thousand words connecting that experience to the course. Known as the engagement activity under the previous guide. The component with the largest gap between what students do and what the criteria reward.

subjects.name: Paper 1: Source Analysis
subjects.description: Four sources, a sequence of structured questions rising in demand, and very little time. Marks are lost to students who paraphrase sources rather than compare and evaluate them, and to anyone who writes the long final answer without reserving the minutes for it.

subjects.name: Paper 2: Comparative Essay Writing
subjects.description: Essays drawn from across the four units, rewarding a clear line of argument, two or three concepts used precisely, contemporary examples with dates, and an explicit counter-position. Higher Level candidates write more of them in a longer paper.

subjects.name: HL Extension: Global Political Challenges
subjects.description: Case studies of contemporary challenges, presented orally and recorded, drawn from different topic areas so that a candidate cannot cover the same ground twice. Assessed on the quality of political analysis rather than on presentation polish, which students consistently get the wrong way round.

subjects.name: Pairing Global Politics with History or Economics
subjects.description: Many Dubai candidates take two Group 3 subjects. The overlap in skills is real but the writing conventions differ: History rewards historiography and sourced causation, Economics rewards diagrams and models, Global Politics rewards conceptual framing. Students who write all three the same way lose marks in at least two of them.

dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-online-tutor.regionsIntro: What changes across Dubai for this subject is practical rather than geographic: when a session can start, how small the school's Politics cohort is, and whether the engagement project can realistically involve something local. These are the districts the enquiries come from most often.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Apartment living with short school runs, so a 4.30pm start is usually achievable. Cohorts here skew towards students whose parents work in professional services, and engagement projects often involve a charity, a chamber of commerce initiative or a university-run programme rather than anything requiring travel.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: A dense band of Diploma provision with several schools within a few minutes of each other, which means students sometimes know candidates at other schools sitting the same paper. Useful for comparing marked work, and a reason to be careful that engagement projects remain individual.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing communities with long commutes to the older Diploma schools, so sessions here commonly cannot start before 5.30pm. Families in this band more often ask for one longer weekly session rather than two shorter ones, and weekend mornings are popular for essay marking.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Motor City
regions.note: Villa communities feeding a small number of large schools, where Global Politics classes can be sizeable enough to be taught by a subject specialist. Support here tends to be essay-focused rather than content-focused, because the teaching is usually solid and the individual feedback thin.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Small, internationally mobile cohorts with a high rate of mid-course arrival. Students joining in DP2 from a school on a different guide are the common case, and the first job is working out which units were taught and in what depth before any essay work starts.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to several universities, which makes the engagement project unusually practicable: student societies, model United Nations circuits and public lectures are all within reach. Sessions here are often scheduled later because of the distance back from school.

regions.name: The Greens and Emirates Living
regions.note: Established, walkable communities with short school runs and families who have often been in Dubai for a decade. Candidates here frequently take Global Politics alongside History, and the support they need is usually about keeping the two writing styles apart.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej and Mushrif
regions.note: The eastern edge of the city, where the drive to a Diploma school can exceed forty minutes each way. That commute is the single strongest argument for online delivery in this band, because it is an hour a day that can go to marked essay work instead.

schoolClusters.city: Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf and the Downtown corridor
schoolClusters.note: Newer Diploma provision, often with small Group 3 cohorts and teachers covering two subjects. Families here most often want someone to mark essays weekly, because the class is too small to generate much comparative feedback and the teacher is stretched across two year groups.

schoolClusters.city: The Meadows, Arabian Ranches and Sports City
schoolClusters.note: Larger, longer-established Diploma schools where Global Politics is more likely to be taught by a specialist. The requests from this band skew towards the Higher Level presentations and the engagement project, both of which get less class time than the written papers anywhere.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Nad Al Sheba and Dubai Silicon Oasis
schoolClusters.note: A band with a wide spread of Diploma sizes. Some schools here run Global Politics only when enough students opt for it, so a candidate may find the subject withdrawn after DP1 selections. Checking that the option will actually run before committing is a conversation worth having in Year 11.

dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-online-tutor.modesIntro: Global Politics support divides into content teaching, essay marking and supervision of the internally assessed work. The second is where almost all the measurable gain is, and it is the one a weekly conversational hour quietly avoids. These are the session shapes that work.

modes.title: Weekly essay cycle
modes.description: One session a week, with an essay written between sessions and marked before the next one starts. The session is spent on the marked script with the band descriptors open, not on new content. Twelve cycles across DP1 and DP2 is usually enough to move a student from narrating to arguing, which is the whole game in this subject.
bullets: An essay question set at the end of every session, answered to time
Marked against the published descriptors before the next session
One structural fault worked on at a time, not five at once
Recordings kept so the student can rewatch the marking commentary

modes.title: Engagement project supervision
modes.description: Four to six sessions placed around the internally assessed component: choosing an issue that is genuinely political and genuinely accessible, planning documented engagement, then checking the report's analytical frame against the criteria. The tutor comments on the student's own draft once. No text is supplied and nothing is rewritten for them.
bullets: Issue tested for political content, access and ethical workability
Engagement planned so there is something real to analyse afterwards
Concepts and theory chosen before the report is drafted, not after
One round of criterion-referenced comments on the student's draft

modes.title: Higher Level presentation coaching
modes.description: Three to four sessions for the recorded global political challenges component. Case studies chosen from different topic areas, each one built as an argument with a position rather than a briefing, then delivered to camera and reviewed. Most candidates improve more in two rehearsals than in a term of reading.
bullets: Two distinct challenges selected so the cases do not overlap
Each presentation structured as a claim defended, not a summary
Timing rehearsed to the limit, because overrun is self-inflicted
Recorded, watched back, and cut rather than padded

modes.title: Source paper sprint
modes.description: A short block in the final term aimed entirely at Paper 1. Students practise the question sequence under time, learn to allocate minutes against mark tariffs, and drill comparison and evaluation of sources rather than paraphrase. Six sessions is usually enough, because the skill is narrow and highly trainable.
bullets: Full source papers sat to time from the first session
Minutes allocated by mark tariff and the allocation enforced
Comparison language practised until it becomes automatic
The long final answer planned in two minutes, every time

sections.heading: What a Global Politics tutor in Dubai is actually hired to fix
paragraphs: Four problems bring Dubai families to this search, and they are not equally urgent. The commonest is a student who is articulate in class and mid-band on paper, which is an essay-structure problem. The second is engagement work that has drifted: an issue chosen in October, no documented involvement by February, a report due in weeks. The third is a Higher Level candidate who has never recorded a presentation. The fourth is a mid-course arrival who does not know which units their new school has taught.

Each of those has a different first session. The essay problem needs a marked script and the band descriptors side by side. The engagement problem needs a triage conversation about what can still be documented honestly in the time left. The presentation problem needs a camera and a stopwatch. The mid-course arrival needs a syllabus audit against their new school's scheme of work, which takes twenty minutes and saves a term of guessing.

What none of them needs is a lecture on the four units. Global Politics has less content than History or Economics, and almost no student fails on recall. They fail on application: a well-informed paragraph that never names a concept, an essay that reaches a conclusion the evidence does not support, a presentation that describes a crisis for nine minutes and analyses it for one. Hours spent on marked writing are worth several times hours spent on content, and a tutor who proposes the reverse is selling the easier product.
bullets: An articulate student scoring mid-band has a structure problem, not a knowledge gap
Engagement work that has not started by February needs triage, not planning
The Higher Level presentations are a performance component nobody rehearses
A mid-course arrival needs a unit audit before anything else happens

sections.heading: The four core units, and what each paper does with them
paragraphs: Every Global Politics candidate studies the same four units, which is why this subject is easier to tutor well than Geography or History: there is no option menu, so a tutor who knows the course knows your child's course. What varies between Dubai schools is depth and choice of case studies, and those are visible in the student's own notes within a session.

The two written papers use the units differently, and students who revise as though they do not are the ones who feel ambushed. The source paper takes a single unit per paper and tests whether a candidate can read, compare and evaluate material under time pressure. The essay paper ranges across all four and rewards synthesis, so a candidate who has revised each unit in a sealed box struggles the moment a question asks them to bring development and peacebuilding into the same argument.

The table below sets out what each unit is for and the usual failure mode. Read it alongside your child's notes. If a unit's notes are a chronology of events with no concept vocabulary in the margins, that is the unit to work on first, regardless of what the last report card said. Exact component weightings and durations are published in the subject guide your child's school holds, and they have changed between guides, so confirm them with the coordinator rather than with a search result. The same guide lists the command terms, and that list is the one document worth reading alongside the student's own notes.

sections.heading: The engagement project, and why it goes wrong in February
paragraphs: The internally assessed component is unlike anything else in Group 3. A student engages with a political issue in a documented, real way and then writes an analytical report of roughly two thousand words connecting that engagement to the course's concepts, theory and comparable examples. It was called the engagement activity in the previous guide and the engagement project in the current one; ask the coordinator which applies, because the criteria are not identical.

What goes wrong is nearly always sequencing rather than ability. Students choose a broad issue, plan to engage with it later, and then discover in February that they have reflections but no documented engagement, or engagement but no political analysis to hang on it. The report is then written backwards from whatever happened, and the analytical criteria punish that immediately, because the connection between experience and theory reads as retrofitted.

The fix is a chain with dates in it. Issue narrowed and tested for access by a fixed point in DP1. Engagement planned and begun while there is still time for it to fail and be replaced. Concepts and theoretical framing chosen before the report is drafted, so the engagement is interrogated rather than described. One supervised round of comments on the student's own draft. The table counts that chain backwards in relative windows, because schools set their own internal deadlines and those are always earlier than the external ones. Ask the coordinator for the department's dates in writing at the start of DP1 and plan against those rather than against anything published externally.

sections.heading: Paper 1: the source paper that looks easy and is not
paragraphs: Students relax when they see the source paper, because the material is in front of them and nothing has to be remembered. Then they run out of time. The question sequence rises in demand, and the final question carries a large share of the marks while sitting at the end of a paper where the earlier answers have already eaten the clock. A candidate who writes generously on the two-mark opener has usually lost the paper before they reach the part that matters.

The skills are narrow, which is good news, because narrow skills are trainable. Reading a source for its argument rather than its topic. Comparing two sources on a specific point rather than summarising each in turn. Evaluating a source by its origin, purpose and limitations in a sentence rather than a paragraph. And constructing the long final answer as an argument that uses all four sources plus the candidate's own knowledge, which is the single most practised thing in a source-paper block.

In sessions this looks mechanical and it is meant to. Minutes are allocated against mark tariffs and the allocation is enforced with a timer. Comparison sentences are drilled until the construction is automatic. The final answer gets a two-minute written plan every single time, because candidates who plan it reach a judgement and candidates who do not stop when the time runs out. Six focused sessions typically move a student a band on this paper, which is a better return than almost any content revision.

sections.heading: The case-study audit: what counts as current in this subject
paragraphs: Global Politics is marked on contemporary relevance. A student quoting examples their teacher first used five years ago is handing the examiner a signal that they have not read anything themselves. That is not a content problem, it is a maintenance problem, and it is fixable in two sessions with a spreadsheet. The target is three or four examples per unit, each with a named actor, a date, one quantitative detail where relevant, and a sentence saying which concept it illustrates.

Choosing examples also has an ethical and practical dimension that matters in this region. The course asks for multiple perspectives on contested questions and for analysis rather than advocacy. A candidate writing about any politically sensitive matter should be framing competing positions and the concepts behind them, not arguing a cause, and should be taking the school's guidance on topic suitability. Good tutoring reinforces that standard rather than treating it as an obstacle, because the band descriptors reward exactly that balance.

The audit below is the version we run with students in the first month. It is deliberately unglamorous: a list of what a stale example looks like next to what a usable one contains. Most Dubai candidates discover they have a dozen half-remembered cases and need four solid ones per unit, which is a weekend of work rather than a term. Keep the file open for the whole of DP2 and replace an example whenever a better documented one appears, because a case that was current in DP1 may not be by the exam.
