sections.heading: The Higher Level extension: two recorded presentations nobody rehearses
paragraphs: Higher Level candidates present case studies of contemporary global political challenges orally, recorded, drawn from different topic areas so that the same ground cannot be covered twice. It is the component with the widest gap between effort and marks, because students prepare it as a research task and it is assessed as an analytical one. A candidate who has read widely and arrives with nine minutes of narrative will be beaten by one who has read half as much and spends the time defending a position.

The practical failures are consistent. Choosing two challenges that overlap, so the second presentation repeats the analysis of the first. Running over time, which is entirely self-inflicted and costs structure. Spending the opening two minutes on background that the examiner does not need. And presenting without a thesis, so there is nothing for the analysis to be analysis of. All four are visible on a first recording and correctable on a second.

Coaching this is unglamorous and quick. Pick the two challenges and check they are genuinely distinct. Write each presentation as a claim with three supporting moves and one acknowledged objection. Rehearse to camera, watch it back with a stopwatch, and cut rather than add. Three sessions is normally the whole intervention, and because it is recorded rather than live, a Dubai student can practise in the evening with a tutor in another time zone without any of the scheduling pain that a live oral would involve.

sections.heading: What Dubai candidates bring to this subject, and the one blind spot
paragraphs: A Global Politics class in Dubai is an unusual resource. Students in the same room commonly hold citizenship of a dozen states and have lived under several different systems of government, which means the discussion of sovereignty or development starts from genuinely divergent priors rather than from one national consensus. That is the condition the course is designed for, and candidates from these cohorts are often strikingly good at the multiple-perspectives requirement that students in more homogeneous classrooms find artificial.

The blind spot is domestic political process. Many Dubai candidates have never observed an election campaign, a legislative committee or a municipal consultation at close quarters, and it shows when a question asks about mechanisms rather than outcomes. Answers describe what states want and skip how decisions actually get made. Reading two or three detailed accounts of a policy process end to end fixes this faster than any amount of theory, and it also supplies the institutional vocabulary the band descriptors reward.

The engagement project is where both the strength and the blind spot show. Students in Dubai have good access to international organisations, university programmes, chambers, charities and model United Nations circuits, so documented engagement is practicable. What they often lack is a sense of what makes an engagement political rather than charitable. Volunteering is not, on its own, political engagement; volunteering and then analysing how provision is decided, funded and contested is. That distinction is the first thing a supervision session should settle.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the component is about personal involvement
paragraphs: The engagement report is assessed work and the usual rules apply, with one extra wrinkle: the engagement itself must be real. A documented account of something that did not happen, or an account borrowed from a sibling's project two years earlier, is a malpractice finding rather than a weak piece of work. Students under deadline pressure are tempted here precisely because the component is self-reported, and a supervisor who asks for contemporaneous documentation early removes the temptation.

On the writing itself, the boundary is the one that applies across the Diploma. A tutor may comment on a student's own draft once, name a criterion that is not being met, point at an unsupported claim, or ask why a concept has been chosen. A tutor may not supply sentences, reorganise the argument on the student's behalf, or hand back a version that needs only accepting. Ask any prospective tutor how they handle a draft, and treat the word editing as a reason to keep looking.

Sources need the same discipline. Material read during the engagement has to be cited where it is used, including interviews, organisational documents and anything taken from a website. Services in this market do sell finished coursework, and the consequence of buying it falls on the candidate, not the seller: a malpractice finding can cost the Diploma rather than the subject grade. Saying this plainly is a differentiator in a search results page that contains at least one business selling completed assessments.

sections.heading: Matching, scheduling and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Global Politics specialists are scarcer than Economics or History specialists everywhere, and the UAE is no exception. The honest position is that a specific combination of Higher Level, engagement-project supervision and a seven o'clock Dubai slot is not always available locally. Where it is not, the realistic options are a tutor in a time zone whose working day overlaps a Dubai evening, a different weekly slot, or a short wait. A History teacher who has never taught the course is not an equivalent, and we would rather say that than fill the hour.

Scheduling has its own Dubai specifics. Sessions normally start between half past four and seven, depending on the school run, and families in the outer communities need the later end of that. Ramadan shifts everything: many families prefer late evening sessions after iftar, or a pause with a compressed block afterwards, and that works better when it is planned in advance rather than improvised. Summer is usually the best time to do engagement-project groundwork, because nothing else is competing for the hours.

Lessons are delivered live over video, one-to-one, and nothing is sent to a UAE address. Recordings are shared so a marked essay discussion can be rewatched in April. The free first lesson is one per student, needs no card details, and is used as a diagnostic rather than a sales call: an essay marked, a read on what the actual problem is, and an estimate of hours. If the answer is that your child does not need paid tutoring, that is a legitimate outcome of the hour and it gets said.

process.title: Send the marked work, not the report card
process.description: The useful first message carries one marked essay, the level your child sits, and where the engagement project has reached. A grade on a report tells a tutor nothing about whether the problem is structure, concepts or timing. A marked script with an examiner's or teacher's comments on it tells them most of what they need before the first session starts.

process.title: A diagnostic essay in the free first lesson
process.description: The first lesson is spent on one essay question from a taught unit, written to time or brought in advance, then marked against the published descriptors with the student watching. You get the band, the specific reason for it, and an honest estimate of how many sessions the fix takes. One free lesson per student, no card details taken.

process.title: Fix the chain before the content
process.description: Before any content planning, the internally assessed work gets a date chain: when the issue is settled, when engagement begins, when the analytical frame is chosen, when the draft is ready. Content teaching slots around that. Families who do it the other way round arrive at February with a well-taught student and an unwritten report.

process.title: One essay, marked, every week
process.description: The engine of this subject is a weekly written answer marked against the descriptors, with one structural fault addressed at a time. Twelve of those changes how a student writes. Twelve hours of discussion does not. Sessions run on the marked script rather than on a slide deck, and the script goes back with the marks visible.

process.title: Rehearse the oral components on camera
process.description: Higher Level candidates record a presentation in the session, watch it back with a stopwatch, and cut it. The first recording is always too long and too descriptive; the second is usually close to the band they want. This is three sessions of work that students postpone for a year because it feels uncomfortable.

process.title: Review at the mocks and stop when it is done
process.description: After the mock session the plan gets rebuilt from the marked papers rather than from habit, and if the evidence says the student no longer needs the hour, we say so. A candidate consistently in the top band on both papers with a submitted report is finished, and continuing to bill them is the easiest kind of waste to avoid.

whyPoints.title: Essays marked against the descriptors, weekly
whyPoints.description: Almost all the movable marks in Global Politics sit in how a student writes, and that only changes through marked answers with the band descriptors open. A weekly essay cycle is the core of what is sold here, not an optional extra bolted onto content teaching that the school is already doing competently.

whyPoints.title: The internally assessed work treated as a project with dates
whyPoints.description: The engagement component fails on sequencing far more often than on ability. It gets a chain with deadlines attached from the first session: issue, access, documentation, analytical frame, one feedback round. That chain is the difference between a report that analyses an experience and one that describes it from memory.

whyPoints.title: The Higher Level orals actually rehearsed
whyPoints.description: Two recorded presentations on distinct global political challenges, prepared as arguments rather than briefings, delivered to camera and cut rather than padded. Because the component is recorded, it can be coached across time zones without any of the scheduling difficulty a live oral would create.

whyPoints.title: Concept vocabulary drilled early
whyPoints.description: Power, sovereignty, legitimacy, interdependence, justice, development: these are tools, not labels. Sessions in DP1 include deliberate vocabulary work so that by DP2 a student reaches for a concept automatically when framing a paragraph. That habit is worth more on the essay paper than any single case study.

whyPoints.title: Analysis before advocacy, stated as a standard
whyPoints.description: The course asks for competing perspectives weighed, not causes argued. Tutors here hold that line, take the school's guidance on topic suitability seriously, and coach students to frame contested questions through the concepts rather than through their own position. That is both the ethical standard and the one the descriptors reward.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live, one-to-one and online, on Gulf Standard Time; we do not send tutors to addresses in the Emirates. Where no Global Politics specialist is free in your slot, you are told that rather than matched with a near miss, including what the alternatives and their trade-offs are.

faqs.question: What does an IB Global Politics tutor actually do in a session?
faqs.answer: Mark and rebuild writing, mostly. A typical hour opens with an essay the student wrote during the week, marked against the published band descriptors, and spends the time on why it sat where it sat: a claim without a concept, evidence without a date, a conclusion the argument did not earn. Content teaching happens when a diagnostic shows a genuine gap, which is less often than families expect, because this course has less material than History or Economics. If a tutor proposes to spend the first month explaining the four units, ask what marked work they will produce instead.

faqs.question: What are the four core units in IB Global Politics?
faqs.answer: Power, sovereignty and international relations; human rights; development; and peace and conflict. Every candidate studies all four at both levels, which is why this subject is easier to match a tutor to than Geography, where schools pick from an option menu. What varies between Dubai schools is depth and choice of case studies rather than content. The units are not meant to be revised in isolation: the essay paper rewards candidates who can bring development and peacebuilding, or rights and sovereignty, into the same argument, so sealed-box revision is a predictable way to lose marks.

faqs.question: What is the engagement project in IB Global Politics?
faqs.answer: The internally assessed component. A student engages with a political issue in a documented, genuine way and then writes an analytical report of roughly two thousand words connecting that engagement to the course's concepts, theory and comparable examples. The previous guide called it the engagement activity and the current one calls it the engagement project, with criteria that are not identical, so ask the coordinator which applies. It is the component with the largest gap between what students do and what the criteria reward, because the engagement is the easy part and the analytical framing is what carries the marks.

faqs.question: How long should the Global Politics engagement report be?
faqs.answer: Around two thousand words, but confirm the exact limit and what is excluded from the count in the subject guide your school holds, because it differs between guides and schools enforce it strictly. The practical point is the allocation rather than the ceiling. Students routinely spend a thousand words describing what they did and then compress the analysis into the last few paragraphs, which inverts the criteria. Draft the analytical sections first and let the description of the engagement fill whatever space is left. Trimming is then a matter of cutting narrative rather than cutting argument.

faqs.question: Can a tutor choose my child's engagement issue for them?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to is a problem rather than a shortcut. The choice has to be the student's, defended by them, and approved through the school. What a tutor legitimately does is interrogate the choice: is this genuinely political rather than charitable, can the engagement actually be arranged and documented in the time available, and is there theory and a comparable example to analyse it against. That conversation is worth an hour on its own, because an unworkable issue discovered in February costs far more than one discarded in October.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Global Politics at Higher and Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level candidates cover the core in greater depth, sit a longer essay paper, and add two recorded presentations on contemporary global political challenges drawn from different topic areas. Standard Level candidates sit the source paper, the essay paper and the engagement work without the oral component. Component weightings differ between the levels and between guides, so confirm them with your child's coordinator. In tutoring terms the real difference is the oral: it needs rehearsal on camera, it is the component students postpone longest, and it is where three sessions buy the most.

faqs.question: What are the Higher Level global political challenges presentations?
faqs.answer: Two case studies of contemporary political challenges, presented orally and recorded, drawn from different topic areas so the same analysis cannot be used twice. They are assessed on the quality of political analysis rather than on presentation polish, which students get backwards: they arrive with excellent research and nine minutes of narrative. Each presentation needs a thesis, three supporting moves, one acknowledged objection, and a conclusion inside the time limit. Because it is recorded rather than live, it can be rehearsed with a tutor in any time zone, which removes most of the scheduling difficulty.

faqs.question: How is the Global Politics source paper marked?
faqs.answer: Through a rising sequence of structured questions on a small set of sources, with the final question carrying a large share of the marks. That structure is the trap: candidates write generously on the low-tariff openers and arrive at the most valuable question with no time. The marks go to precise comparison of sources on a specific point, evaluation by origin, purpose and limitation in a sentence rather than a paragraph, and a final answer that uses the sources together with the candidate's own knowledge. Minutes should be allocated by mark tariff and the allocation enforced with a timer in practice.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Politics essay score lower than their History essay?
faqs.answer: Because the two subjects reward different conventions and most students write them identically. History rewards sourced causation, historiographical awareness and chronological control. Global Politics rewards conceptual framing: a claim, a concept used as a tool, contemporary evidence with a date, an explicit counter-position, and a judgement that answers the question asked. A strong History essay transplanted into Politics reads as well-informed narrative, which sits mid-band. Students taking both subjects need the distinction made explicit and then practised, which usually takes three or four marked essays rather than a term.

faqs.question: Which case studies should a Dubai Global Politics student use?
faqs.answer: Recent ones the student has read about themselves, kept to three or four per unit, each carrying named actors, a year, a quantitative detail where relevant, and a note of which concept it illustrates. Examples inherited from a teacher's older slides read exactly as what they are. On contested or politically sensitive material the course asks for competing perspectives analysed through the concepts rather than a position advocated, and the school's guidance on topic suitability should be followed. Candidates who hold a small, current, well-documented set outperform those carrying a dozen vague ones.

faqs.question: Is Global Politics a useful subject for law or international relations at university?
faqs.answer: It is well regarded for politics, international relations, development studies and area studies, and it demonstrates exactly the written argument and source-handling that those degrees assess. For law, admissions tutors generally care more about evidence of analytical writing than about the specific Group 3 subject, so Global Politics competes well with History rather than beating it. Check individual prerequisites, because some programmes name History or a language specifically. What the subject does not do is substitute for a Higher Level requirement a course states explicitly, and no tutoring changes that.

faqs.question: How many Global Politics sessions does a Dubai student usually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect for content and more than they expect for writing. A realistic shape is twelve to eighteen weekly essay cycles spread across the two Diploma years, four to six sessions around the engagement project, and for Higher Level candidates three on the recorded presentations. That is roughly twenty to twenty-eight hours in total, placed where they do work rather than concentrated in the final term. A student starting in DP2 with the engagement work unfinished needs the same hours compressed, which is harder and less effective but still worth doing.

faqs.question: How should politically sensitive topics be handled by a student in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Academically, and with the school's guidance. The course requires multiple perspectives on contested questions and assesses analysis rather than advocacy, so the standard the band descriptors set is also the sensible standard here: set out competing positions, identify the concepts and interests behind them, and reach a judgement that the evidence supports. Topic choice for the engagement project should be cleared through the school's coordinator, who knows what is appropriate in their context. A tutor's job is to reinforce that framing, not to encourage a student towards material their school has advised against.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring suit a discussion-based subject like this?
faqs.answer: It suits it better than it suits a practical science. The work is reading, marking and argument, and all three transfer to video without loss: a marked script on a shared screen is easier to read together than one passed across a table, and the session recording means the marking commentary can be rewatched the week before the exams. For the Higher Level presentations, video is actually the native format, since the component is recorded anyway. The one thing a screen cannot supply is supervision for a student who will not work unless an adult is in the room.

faqs.question: What if my child's Dubai school has only one Global Politics teacher?
faqs.answer: That is the normal case rather than a warning sign, and it has two consequences. First, feedback volume is limited, because one teacher covering both Diploma years cannot mark weekly essays for every candidate. Second, the internally assessed components get less individual supervision than the written papers. Both are exactly what outside support is for. Ask the department how many rounds of written feedback the engagement report receives internally and how often full essays are marked, then buy the gap rather than duplicating what the school already does well.

faqs.question: Does Global Politics count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency rules are set by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority, not by us, and the published detail differs by curriculum track. For the British track, Gulf Today reported the requirement as five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels. No IB points threshold has been confirmed from an official Ministry source for this project, so we publish none. Check the current requirement on the Ministry's own channels before planning subject choices around it.

dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-online-tutor.closingHeading: Send one marked essay and we will tell you what the problem is
dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-online-tutor.closingBody: The fastest way to find out whether your child needs Global Politics support is to send one marked essay and say where the engagement project has got to. The free first lesson is spent marking a timed answer against the published descriptors and telling you honestly whether the gap is structure, concepts, evidence or timing, and roughly how many hours it takes to close. One free lesson per student, with no card details taken. Lessons run live and one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, and nothing is delivered to an address in the Emirates.

intro.heading: The same result, bought twice, at two completely different prices
paragraphs: Global Politics is an unusually honest test of when to buy tutoring rather than how much to pay for it. Published rates in Dubai run from AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya's budget end and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik's, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, to the AED 200 to 450 and above specialist band on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, with BartyED publishing AED 650 for premium named tutoring. Those are the market's numbers. What nobody publishes is the far more consequential figure: how many hours the same improvement takes depending on when you start.

The arithmetic is stark in this subject. A candidate supported from the first term of DP1 builds a case-study record as the course is taught, learns concept-led writing on low-stakes essays, and chooses an engagement focus with time to do it properly. That is roughly twelve to eighteen hours across two years. The same candidate reached after the DP2 mocks needs the case-study record built retrospectively from memory, the writing habit changed under deadline pressure, and the engagement component rescued, which is twenty-five hours in a term and a smaller movement at the end of it.

The second thing families underestimate is how specialised this apparently general subject is. Global Politics is not current affairs and it is not history. It is a concept-led course in which answers are built out of the course's own analytical vocabulary and supported by case studies the student has prepared. A well-read, articulate Dubai teenager who writes a fluent essay about a conflict without using the course's concepts will score a 4 or a 5, repeatedly, and no amount of additional reading changes that. A tutor who has not taught the course will not spot it.

The third is the engagement component, which is the part most likely to go wrong and the least likely to be covered in a quote. It needs a focus that is lawful and appropriate for a student living in the UAE, agreed with the school, non-partisan, and genuinely achievable alongside five other subjects. Choosing badly is expensive in time rather than money, and families rarely discover the problem until the school's internal deadline makes it visible. Settle it in DP1 and the component is manageable; leave it to February and it dominates everything.

So this page is ordered by what actually decides the invoice. It opens with the published Dubai tiers and what each one can and cannot do in this subject, then prices the same improvement at three starting points so the cost of waiting is visible. After that come the case-study record, the concept-led writing move, the engagement component, and the screening question that separates a subject specialist from a capable essay tutor. The last sections cover the calendar counted backwards, what a parent can verify before paying, and what we do when nobody suitable is free.

dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-tutor.programmesIntro: Global Politics exists only in the Diploma years, but its demands are recognisable earlier in the IB continuum: handling contested evidence, holding two positions at once, and writing to a concept rather than around a topic. Here is what each programme a Dubai school runs contributes.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Individuals and Societies builds the groundwork through criterion C on communicating and criterion D on thinking critically, where students learn to evaluate competing accounts rather than report one. The useful inheritance is comfort with disagreement. The gap is vocabulary: MYP rewards a well-argued position in plain language, while the Diploma expects the course's own analytical concepts to carry the argument.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP cohorts are often strong on discussion and weaker on written structure, partly because class debate is a natural fit for an international student body with wide experience. Departments here report the same DP1 pattern annually: articulate students whose first Global Politics essays read as well-informed opinion rather than as concept-led analysis.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Global Politics runs across both Diploma years in Group 3 at Standard or Higher Level, built around core thematic units and a set of analytical concepts, with written papers and an engagement component in which the student investigates a political issue through their own involvement with it. Higher Level adds an extension. The course has been revised, so confirm the current structure in the IB subject guide at ibo.org.
programmes.countryNote: Global Politics is offered in a minority of Dubai Diploma schools, and where it runs the cohort is often very small. A candidate may be one of three or four in their year, which makes an outside specialist the only person other than the teacher who can discuss the subject with them at the level the examination expects.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Global Politics pairs naturally with career studies in business, law or international relations, and a CP candidate sits the same papers and completes the same engagement component, so subject support is identical.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools run the Career-related Programme. For a CP candidate taking Global Politics the practical risk is calendar collision: the reflective project, the career-related study and the engagement component all want the same months, and in a small cohort there is no peer group going through the sequence alongside them to compare notes with.

dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-tutor.subjectsIntro: Global Politics is a set of core thematic units, a layer of analytical concepts that carry every answer, and a component built on the student's own engagement with a political issue. Below is what a tutor works on with a Dubai candidate.

subjects.name: Power, sovereignty and international relations
subjects.description: States, non-state actors, intergovernmental organisations, legitimacy and the different forms power takes. Marks go missing when a candidate describes an institution rather than analysing how power operated in a specific episode, which is what the question almost always asks.

subjects.name: Human rights
subjects.description: Rights frameworks, claims and contestation, enforcement and the gap between declaration and practice. Strong candidates handle contested cases with precision and restraint; weaker ones write moral commentary, which the markbands do not reward however strongly felt.

subjects.name: Development
subjects.description: Contested meanings of development, measurement, pathways and the role of aid, trade and debt. This is the unit where quantitative evidence helps most, and where Dubai candidates most often assert a general picture when a named indicator with a date was available.

subjects.name: Peace and conflict
subjects.description: Causes and types of conflict, intervention, peacebuilding and justice after violence. The most popular unit with students and the one most prone to narrative answers, because the material is dramatic and the concepts get left behind in the storytelling.

subjects.name: The analytical concepts
subjects.description: The course's own vocabulary is the spine of every good answer: it tells the examiner which lens the candidate is applying. Confirm the current concept list in the subject guide, because it was revised, and then use the concepts as the structure of a paragraph rather than as decoration.

subjects.name: The source-based paper
subjects.description: Short and extended responses built on unseen stimulus material. The evaluative question is where the paper is won or lost, and candidates routinely run out of time on it because they over-wrote the earlier parts, which are worth considerably less.

subjects.name: The essay paper
subjects.description: Extended responses requiring a concept-led argument supported by prepared case studies. A candidate with two well-recorded case studies per unit can answer almost anything; a candidate relying on memory of the news cannot, however informed they are.

subjects.name: The engagement component
subjects.description: An investigation of a political issue through the student's own engagement with it, written up within a stated limit. Confirm the current name, length and requirements with the coordinator. Most failures trace to a focus chosen late or too broad to investigate within the time available.

subjects.name: The Higher Level extension
subjects.description: Additional work on global political challenges, assessed through presented work rather than a written paper. It is routinely under-rehearsed because it sits outside the examination timetable and therefore outside most revision plans until very late.

subjects.name: Case-study discipline
subjects.description: Named actors, dates, outcomes, a concept the case illustrates, and a source for each claim. One page per case, two cases per unit, built during the course. This single habit distinguishes almost every top-band candidate from a well-read mid-band one.

sections.heading: What each price tier can actually do in this subject
paragraphs: Global Politics sits in an awkward place in the Dubai market. It looks like a general humanities subject, so it is often quoted at general humanities rates, and a well-read tutor can hold an interesting conversation about any topic in it. That conversation is not what the examination rewards. The course is built on its own analytical concepts, and an answer that does not deploy them scores in the middle no matter how informed it is, so the tier you buy matters more here than in a subject where content knowledge is most of the grade.

The table below sets out the published bands with what each tier reliably delivers. The pattern is consistent: the lower tiers are good at information and discussion, and the specialist tier is what you need for the three things that actually move this grade, which are concept-led writing, the engagement component and the Higher Level extension. Paying the specialist rate for general discussion is a waste, and paying the general rate for the specialist jobs is a term spent pleasantly without a change in the mark.

One claim to treat carefully at the top of the market. No tutor should be presented as a current IB examiner without evidence, and examiner status must never be implied to give access to marking, grade boundaries or unseen paper content. Nor should any provider describe itself as approved, accredited or licensed by the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds none of those. What a tutor can legitimately offer is what they have taught, a method, and a marked script you can read for yourself.

sections.heading: Why the same improvement costs roughly half as much in DP1
paragraphs: This is the figure no competitor page in this search will give you, and it matters more than any hourly rate. The cost of support in Global Politics is driven almost entirely by when it starts, because two of the three jobs are cumulative. A case-study record built while a unit is being taught takes twenty minutes per case. The same record built in April from half-remembered reading takes an hour per case and is less accurate. The engagement component chosen in DP1 is a manageable piece of work; chosen in February it is a crisis with a deadline attached.

Essay technique behaves differently again. It is not cumulative, but it is slow: it changes over a term of marked attempts, not over an intensive fortnight, because what is being replaced is a habit of writing fluent informed prose with a habit of writing concept-led argument. A student can be told the difference in ten minutes and will need six marked essays to do it reliably under timed conditions. That is a calendar constraint rather than a money constraint, which is why February purchases buy less than their price suggests.

The table below prices the same improvement at three starting points, using the published specialist band rather than any price of ours. Read the final column rather than the money column. A DP1 start can realistically aim at a grade change and a comfortable engagement component. A post-mock start can realistically aim at a grade change on the written papers only. A final-month start can aim at technique on one paper and better question choice, which is worth having and is not the same product.

sections.heading: The case-study record: the cheapest asset in this subject
paragraphs: Ask a top-band Global Politics candidate what they did differently and the answer is almost never that they read more. It is that they kept a record. Two case studies per core unit, one page each, built while the unit was being taught, with named actors, dates, outcomes, the concept the case illustrates and a source for every claim. Eight pages by the end of the course. A candidate with that folder can answer almost any essay question on the paper; a candidate relying on a general awareness of world events cannot, however well informed they are.

The format matters more than the volume, which is why the table below specifies it. A case recorded as a narrative is useless under exam pressure because the student has to reconstruct the argument while writing. A case recorded as a concept with evidence attached is immediately deployable: the student knows which question it answers, which concept it illustrates, and which two facts support the claim. Converting a student's existing notes into that format is often the single most productive two hours in a whole plan.

Keeping it honest is part of the exercise. Every figure wants a date and a source, and students should prefer the original publisher over a summary of it. Where a case is contested, the record should note the disagreement rather than choosing a side, because that disagreement is usable material in an evaluative answer. This habit also protects the student: a candidate who has recorded where every claim came from cannot accidentally reproduce a model-generated assertion as if it were established fact.

sections.heading: Concept-led writing: the move that separates a 5 from a 7
paragraphs: The commonest profile in a Dubai Global Politics class is a student who is genuinely interested in the world, reads widely, argues well in discussion, and scores 5. The essays are fluent and accurate and could have been written by a bright student who had never taken the course. That is precisely the problem. The markbands reward analysis conducted through the course's own concepts, and an essay that reaches a sensible conclusion without that machinery has demonstrated general intelligence rather than subject learning.

The repair is narrow and teachable. Each paragraph should name the concept it is using, apply it to a specific case, and say what the application shows about the question. Named concept, specific evidence, consequence for the argument. Once a student writes three paragraphs in that shape, the difference against their previous work is visible to them without anybody explaining it, which is why this is taught by marking rather than by lecturing. Six marked essays is the typical distance between the two habits.

There is a related failure worth naming because it is common in articulate students: moral commentary. A paragraph that explains why a situation is unjust is not analysis, and markbands do not reward strength of feeling. The higher-scoring version takes the same conviction and converts it into mechanism: which actor had what power, what the constraint was, what the framework permitted, and what the evidence shows about the outcome. Students find this a relief rather than a restriction once they see the marks it produces.

sections.heading: The engagement component: time, feasibility and choosing well in the UAE
paragraphs: The engagement component asks a student to investigate a political issue through their own engagement with it, and then to write that up within a stated limit. Confirm the current name, length and precise requirements with your child's coordinator, because the course has been revised and tutoring websites are slow to catch up. What has not changed is the failure mode: a focus chosen late, or chosen too broadly, leaves a student with a deadline and nothing to analyse.

Choosing well in the UAE means choosing something lawful, appropriate and agreed with the school, which is less limiting than it sounds. Non-partisan, issue-based engagement is both the safest and the strongest option: climate and water governance, humanitarian and refugee support through a registered organisation, access to education, public health, or the sustainable development agenda. The course does not require domestic political activity and a student should not be looking for any. It requires genuine engagement with an issue and honest analysis of what that engagement revealed.

Then test feasibility before any time is committed. Can the student actually engage, with whom, by when, and what will they be able to describe afterwards? A focus that depends on access nobody has agreed to give is a focus that fails in month three. This is where two hours of supervision in DP1 saves ten hours of rescue work in DP2, and it is the part of a quote families most often forget to ask about. Confirm explicitly whether engagement supervision is inside the plan or billed separately.

sections.heading: Why the cheaper non-specialist option rarely works here
paragraphs: Every subject has a version of this question and in Global Politics the answer is unusually clear. A good general humanities tutor brings real value: essay discipline, paragraph structure, timing, and the habit of answering the question asked. Those transfer from History or English and they are worth paying for if that is the diagnosed problem. What does not transfer is knowing which concept a given question is actually about, and that is the thing standing between a 5 and a 7 for most candidates in this emirate.

The failure is quiet, which is what makes it expensive. Sessions are enjoyable, the student talks confidently, essays come back with sensible comments about structure, and the mark does not move. Two months later the diagnosis is the same as it was at the start. The parent concludes that tutoring does not work for this subject, when what happened was that a structural problem was treated with structural help while the actual problem was subject-specific and untouched.

The screening question that separates the two takes thirty seconds. Give a prospective tutor a past essay title and ask which concepts a strong answer would be built on and why. A specialist names them, explains what each one lets the candidate argue, and mentions a case that illustrates it. A generalist talks about structure and balance, which is good advice about essays and no advice at all about this course. Ask it before you book, and ask whether they have taught the revised course or the previous version.

sections.heading: The Global Politics year counted backwards
paragraphs: No page competing for this search publishes a calendar, which is a strange omission in a subject where the calendar determines the cost. Two of the three components are deadline-driven and school-set rather than examination-driven: the engagement write-up and, at Higher Level, the presented extension work. Both get dearer the later they start and both are governed by the Diploma coordinator's internal dates rather than by the IB's. Get those dates in DP1 and the plan writes itself.

Work backwards from the written papers. Before them sit the mocks, which are the only free diagnostic a family gets. Before those sits the school's internal submission window for the engagement write-up, usually weeks ahead of the IB's own deadline. Before that sits the engagement activity itself, which needs real time. And before everything sits the choice of focus, which is a DP1 decision in every well-run plan and a February emergency in every badly run one.

Be cautious with IB dates from any tutoring source, this one included. UAE schools sit the May session and results reach candidates during the following summer, but the windows change between years and the IB is the publisher. Confirm every date with your child's coordinator or at ibo.org before planning around it. For a sibling sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications in the same household, note that Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and that using the wrong zone timetable is the family's risk to manage.

sections.heading: Permits, trial conditions and what a Dubai parent can verify
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated, and knowing the detail gives you a question that sorts the professionals from the opportunists quickly. Individuals offering private lessons need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount you see quoted.

There is a second rule worth knowing in a small-cohort subject. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy, but the principle is sound anywhere in the country: your child's own classroom teacher is not the right person to hire privately, however convenient it looks.

On money, settle three things in writing before paying. Whether the quoted figure includes VAT. What the condition on any free trial is, since a trial with an undisclosed condition is not free; ours is one lesson per student with no card details taken. And what happens if the tutor becomes unavailable mid-term. Add a fourth for a lead form: ask what personal data about your child is collected, why, and how it is deleted, since UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection applies and a form asking for a school, grades and a photograph with no stated purpose deserves a question.

sections.heading: Availability, delivery and the honest version of getting started
paragraphs: Global Politics is offered in a minority of Dubai Diploma schools, so the specialist pool is small and we would rather say so than quietly allocate a general humanities tutor to a subject-specific job. A Standard Level request on a weekday evening is usually matched within a few days. A Higher Level request that also needs extension rehearsal, in the fortnight before a mock series, is the hardest booking in this subject's calendar and sometimes cannot be filled at the hour asked for. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Sessions are recorded so a student can rewatch a read-back instead of relying on notes taken while being corrected, essays are annotated and shared as files so a parent can read exactly what was marked, and the Higher Level presented work can be rehearsed to camera, which is a genuine advantage of this format. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India, and this page states it rather than leaving it to be discovered later.

In-home tuition does exist in this market, published at AED 180 to 350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table with some home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. The premium buys presence, and in a subject this thinly offered it also narrows the field severely: a family in The Springs hiring locally is choosing among Diploma Global Politics specialists willing to drive inland for a 6.30pm start, which may be a list of nobody. Online, the same family chooses among everyone who teaches the course at that hour, which is the entire argument for this format in one sentence.

process.title: Tell us the level, the deadlines and the engagement status
process.description: A useful first message names the level, the school's internal deadline for the engagement write-up, whether a focus has been agreed, and whether the Higher Level extension has been started. Those four facts set the plan and therefore the total, because in this subject the calendar drives the cost far more than the hourly rate does.

process.title: A free diagnostic hour built on one timed essay
process.description: The first lesson is free, one per student, with no card details taken. It is built around an essay sat beforehand, returned with the band named, the concepts that should have carried each paragraph identified, and three specific corrections. That single artefact shows whether you are buying concepts, case studies or structure.

process.title: A plan with the hours, the total and the deadlines on it
process.description: The plan states which component comes first and why, how many marked essays are included, whether engagement supervision is inside it, and what the whole thing costs. Compare that against the AED bands published for Dubai in the first table on this page. A plan with no total cannot be evaluated by anybody.

process.title: Monthly review, with the plan written to finish
process.description: Each month brings the marked essays and a short written note on which band they now reach and what has not changed. The target is a student who can name the concepts a question needs before anyone prompts them. At that point the plan should end rather than renew as a standing weekly booking.

whyPoints.title: Priced by what each tier can actually do
whyPoints.description: The published Dubai bands are on this page with the provider that published each one named, and so is what each tier cannot do in this subject. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which leaves a parent nothing to compare a quote against.

whyPoints.title: Timing treated as the real cost driver
whyPoints.description: Two of the three jobs in this subject are cumulative, so a DP1 start buys the same improvement for roughly half the hours of a post-mock start. We say that plainly even when it means telling a February enquiry that the engagement component is now whatever it already is.

whyPoints.title: Concept-led writing taught by marking, not by lecturing
whyPoints.description: Named concept, specific evidence, consequence for the argument. Students see the difference against their own previous work within three paragraphs, which is why this is taught through marked essays rather than explained in a session. Six marked essays is the usual distance between the two habits.

whyPoints.title: Engagement supervision priced inside the plan
whyPoints.description: The component most likely to go wrong is the one most often left out of a quote. Our plans state how many sessions cover the engagement focus, the activity and the write-up, pinned to the school's internal deadlines rather than to the examination session.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, because the specialist pool here is small
whyPoints.description: There are no home visits in the UAE. For a subject offered in a minority of Dubai schools, that is the difference between choosing among the specialists willing to drive to your community and choosing among everyone who teaches the course at your hour, which in this subject is a much shorter and a much longer list respectively.

faqs.question: What does an hour of Global Politics tuition in Dubai buy at each price tier?
faqs.answer: At AED 33 to 150, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise their from-rates, you get content explanation and general awareness building. At AED 150 to 300, which is where general humanities tutors and many qualified subject teachers sit, you get essay structure and some marking. At AED 200 to 450 and above, the specialist band on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, you get the three things that actually move this grade: concept-led writing, the case-study record and engagement supervision. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Match the tier to the diagnosed job rather than to the budget.

faqs.question: Why is Global Politics cheaper to fix in the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Because two of the three jobs are cumulative. A case study recorded while the unit is being taught takes about twenty minutes; rebuilt in April from half-remembered reading it takes an hour and is less accurate. An engagement focus chosen in DP1 is an ordinary piece of work, while the same choice made in February is a deadline emergency. Essay technique is the exception: it is not cumulative but it is slow, needing around six marked essays across a term. Together that is why a DP1 plan is typically twelve to eighteen hours and a post-mock plan twenty to twenty-five.

faqs.question: What should a case-study record actually contain?
faqs.answer: One page per case, two cases per core unit, each containing the named actors, the dates, the outcome, the concept the case illustrates, and a source line against every figure. The format is what makes it usable: a case recorded as a narrative has to be reconverted into an argument while writing under time pressure, whereas a case recorded as a concept with evidence attached is immediately deployable. Where a case is contested, note both readings and why each reads the evidence that way, because that disagreement is directly usable in the evaluative half of an answer.

faqs.question: Can a general humanities tutor teach Global Politics at a lower rate?
faqs.answer: For some jobs, genuinely yes. Essay discipline, paragraph structure, timing and answering the question asked all transfer from History or English, and if that is the diagnosed problem then a general tutor at AED 150 to 300 is good value. What does not transfer is knowing which concept a question is really about, which is the gap between a 5 and a 7 for most candidates. The failure is quiet: pleasant sessions, sensible comments on structure, and a mark that does not move for two months. Diagnose first, then choose the tier.

faqs.question: How do we know whether the problem is content or concept-led writing?
faqs.answer: Read a marked essay. If the facts are thin or wrong, it is content, and that closes in a few hours per unit. If the essay is accurate, fluent and well organised and still scores in the middle, it is almost certainly the concepts: the answer reaches a sensible conclusion without using the course's analytical machinery, which is exactly what the markbands do not reward. A third possibility worth checking is moral commentary, where the paragraph explains why something is unjust rather than analysing which actor held what power under what constraint.

faqs.question: My child writes well but never uses the course's concepts. Is that the issue?
faqs.answer: It is the most common single issue in this subject, and the repair is narrower than it sounds. Each paragraph should name the concept it is using, apply it to a specific prepared case, and state what that application shows about the question asked. Named concept, specific evidence, consequence for the argument. Once a student has written three paragraphs in that shape the difference against their earlier work is obvious to them without explanation, which is why this is taught through marked essays. Expect about six marked attempts before the habit holds under timed conditions.

faqs.question: How much tutoring time does the engagement component realistically need?
faqs.answer: Three to five sessions, if they are placed correctly. One to test whether the focus can actually be investigated and is lawful, appropriate and agreed with the school. One to plan the engagement itself and the note-keeping that goes with it. One or two to read the write-up against each requirement with the criteria open. Booked as milestones against the school's internal deadlines rather than as a weekly slot. Confirm the current name, length and requirements with your child's coordinator, because the course has been revised and tutoring sites are slow to update.

faqs.question: Can an engagement activity be done entirely online?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and for a student in Dubai with a crowded timetable that can be the practical choice. Remote involvement with a registered organisation working on an issue, structured correspondence, participation in a documented programme, or sustained research engagement with practitioners can all support the component. What matters is that the engagement is genuine, that the student keeps notes as it happens rather than reconstructing them, and that the school agrees it meets the requirements. Confirm the format with the coordinator before committing time, since schools interpret the expectations with some variation.

faqs.question: Does the Higher Level extension need separate paid sessions?
faqs.answer: Usually three to five, and they are the most reliably under-bought hours in this subject. The extension work is presented rather than written, sits outside the examination timetable, and therefore falls outside most revision plans until the final fortnight. Rehearsing it out loud and to time is the whole job, and it is work that video delivery happens to suit well because the student can practise to camera and watch the recording back. At the published specialist band that is roughly AED 600 to 2,250, and it is the cheapest discrete purchase available at Higher Level.

faqs.question: Is a package or pay-as-you-go better for an essay subject like this?
faqs.answer: A standing arrangement suits the essay-marking job, because that work is continuous and needs a rhythm of one attempt per fortnight or week. It suits the engagement and extension work badly, since those cluster around school deadlines and a monthly block pays for the quiet weeks in between. Monthly online packages advertised in the emirate sit around AED 799 for eight sessions, and in-home blocks at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Ask for the session length in minutes, whether unused sessions carry over, and what notice a cancellation needs.

faqs.question: What should the free first lesson produce in Global Politics?
faqs.answer: A marked essay, not a conversation. Ask for one timed response sat beforehand, returned with the band named, the concepts that should have carried each paragraph identified, and three specific corrections. A specialist produces that and can tell you within the hour whether you are buying concepts, case studies or structure. A generalist returns comments about balance and organisation and proposes a package. The marked script is also what lets you judge whether a quoted total at the AED 200 to 450 specialist band is reasonable for the job in front of you.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for extra sessions in the final month?
faqs.answer: For some things only, and it is worth being honest about which. A final month can realistically change question choice, timing, and performance on the evaluative part of the source paper, which is where candidates most often run out of clock after over-writing the earlier questions. It cannot build a case-study record from nothing or rescue an engagement component that is already submitted. Eight to twelve intensive hours at the published specialist band is roughly AED 1,600 to 5,400, and it is a real product; it is simply not the same product as a plan started a year earlier.

faqs.question: How do we check that a tutor has taught the current version of the course?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they have taught the revised Global Politics course or the previous one, when they last taught it, and what changed between them. A specialist answers concretely. Then set a short test: give them a past essay title and ask which concepts a strong answer would be built on and why. Naming the concepts, explaining what each lets a candidate argue, and offering a case to illustrate one takes a specialist thirty seconds. Advice about structure and balance with no concept named is advice about essays rather than about this subject.

faqs.question: What can a tutor not do with the engagement write-up?
faqs.answer: Supply the text, choose the focus, construct the analysis, or rework a draft to completion. What a tutor may do is explain what each requirement rewards, ask whether the engagement as described can support the conclusion being drawn, test the feasibility of a focus before time is spent on it, and point out where a section has stopped answering its own question. The component rests on the student's own involvement, so it is one of the harder pieces of work to fake and one of the easier ones for a moderator to doubt. The boundary belongs in writing before the first session.

faqs.question: Does my child need to follow the news daily to do well?
faqs.answer: No, and daily news consumption is a surprisingly poor substitute for what the examination wants. The paper rewards prepared cases analysed through the course's concepts, not breadth of current awareness, and students who rely on general knowledge of events write confident mid-band essays. A better habit is narrower: two well-recorded cases per core unit, kept to one page each with dates and sources, reviewed periodically. Fifteen minutes a week maintaining that record is worth more marks than an hour a day of reading, which many well-informed candidates in Dubai find difficult to accept.

faqs.question: What happens if no Global Politics specialist is available at our hour?
faqs.answer: We say so and give you a date, rather than filling the slot with a general humanities tutor. Global Politics is offered in a minority of Dubai Diploma schools, so the specialist pool is small, and the hardest booking in the calendar is a Higher Level request needing extension rehearsal in the fortnight before a mock series. The options are an adjacent hour with the specialist you chose, a dated waiting slot, or a different tutor with their actual experience stated plainly before you book. No page competing for this search discloses a coverage limit at all.

dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-tutor.closingHeading: Buy the calendar, not the hour
dubai/ib-dp-global-politics-tutor.closingBody: In Global Politics the decision that moves the invoice is when you start, not what you pay per hour. If your child is in DP1, the cheapest useful step is a session on the case-study record and the engagement focus, both of which get dearer every month they are left. If the mocks have already happened, say so and we will price what can realistically change rather than what sounds better. Tell us the level, the school's internal deadlines and whether the engagement focus is agreed. The first lesson is free, one per student, with no card details taken. Lessons run live and one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time; there are no home visits in the UAE, and that service runs only in India.

dubai/ib-dp-hindi-b-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The teachers listed below work on Hindi B at both levels: Devanagari accuracy, the register system, the written task types, listening on unfamiliar speakers, and the Individual Oral. Every match begins with a 30-minute trial lesson at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken.

intro.heading: Why fluent Hindi at home produces a 4 on paper
paragraphs: A Dubai parent whose child has spoken Hindi since birth reasonably expects Hindi B to be the easy subject on the Diploma timetable. It frequently is not, and the reason is specific rather than mysterious. Hindi B does not assess whether a student can hold a conversation. It assesses writing in Devanagari to an academic standard, reading unfamiliar text under timing, listening to speakers the student has never heard, and sustaining a recorded discussion in a register they almost certainly do not use at home. Household fluency covers one of those four and partially covers another.

The script is the first place marks go. A student who speaks fluently and writes rarely produces Devanagari with inconsistent matras, missing nukta where meaning depends on it, and anusvara and chandrabindu used interchangeably. Each of those is a small deduction, each is invisible in speech, and together across a written task they add up to a grade. It is also the single most fixable thing in the subject: a few weeks of dictation and copy-correction clears most of it, which is why a marked written sample is the only sensible way to start.

Register is the second. Spoken Hindi at home in a Dubai household is informal, often mixed with English, and frequently a family dialect rather than standard Hindi. The written task expects consistent formality appropriate to the text type, and the discrimination between aap, tum and tū has to be maintained across a whole piece rather than chosen sentence by sentence. Students slip mid-paragraph, and the examiner reads that as weak control of the language rather than as a small inconsistency.

The third is reading, and it is the quietest. Half the grade sits in the receptive paper, covering listening and reading. A student who speaks Hindi and does not read it has recognition vocabulary that looks adequate and collapses on unfamiliar text types: a newspaper editorial, a formal letter, a public notice. Nothing in household conversation prepares anybody for inference questions on a text they have never encountered, and nothing in a conversation-based tutoring arrangement fixes it either.

Dubai is the right city to be having this conversation in. Indian-curriculum schools account for roughly 26 per cent of private-school enrolment here, so there is no shortage of Hindi speakers. Hindi B sets inside IB schools are nonetheless small, and teachers who can mark Devanagari against the Group 2 band descriptors are scarcer than the number of Hindi speakers in the city suggests. The search phrase is home tutor, and in Dubai that usually means someone arriving by car. IB Gram does not do that in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Hindi B teaching arrives as one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the script on a shared screen where both parties can see what was actually written.

dubai/ib-dp-hindi-b-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Hindi appears at more than one point in a Dubai student's school career, and the version studied before the Diploma determines how much ground Hindi B has to make up.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Hindi B is a Group 2 language acquisition course assessed through a written task, a receptive paper combining listening and reading, and a recorded Individual Oral. Higher Level adds two literary works originally written in Hindi, with the oral built on an extract from one of them rather than on a visual stimulus. The five prescribed themes frame the content at both levels, so the territory is defined even where the student's prior Hindi is uneven.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Hindi B set often mixes students from Indian-curriculum primaries, students who moved from an international school where Hindi was a two-period option, and household speakers with no formal Hindi at all. A Diploma teacher is covering all three in the same timetabled hours, which is the arithmetic behind most outside tuition in this subject.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Hindi reports by phase and against four criteria that separate listening, reading, speaking and writing. For a household Hindi speaker the criterion profile is the useful part of the report: high comprehension scores beside a low score on accurate language use is the classic pattern, and it predicts precisely the written-task problems Hindi B will expose two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools differ in how early they start Devanagari writing, and students who moved schools mid-primary sometimes skipped the year it was taught properly. Where a student speaks well and writes hesitantly, that gap in the timeline is usually the explanation, and it is worth asking about before assuming a learning difficulty.

programmes.name: Hindi A: Language and Literature
programmes.description: The Group 1 route for students whose Hindi is a first language, studied as literature and textual analysis rather than language acquisition. It is the only Hindi route that can contribute towards the bilingual diploma, and it demands reading stamina in Hindi rather than conversational comfort. Tutoring for it resembles literature support and is a different purchase from Hindi B work.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Dubai schools timetable Hindi A, because the cohort rarely justifies a set. Some can offer it as a school-supported self-taught Standard Level option, which is a serious commitment for a student who speaks Hindi but has never read a full novel in it. Ask the coordinator what is genuinely available before planning around it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Hindi and the CBSE route
programmes.description: Dubai students reach the Diploma from two very different pre-16 Hindi experiences. Cambridge IGCSE Hindi as a Second Language is an examined qualification with its own syllabus code and paper structure. CBSE runs two Hindi courses at class 10 with different demands. Neither maps directly onto Hindi B, and the mapping matters because it determines whether the student needs script work, range work, or both.
programmes.countryNote: A student arriving in a Dubai IB school from a CBSE class 10 is often stronger on literature-style comprehension and weaker on the functional writing Group 2 rewards. One arriving from IGCSE Hindi as a Second Language is usually the reverse. Naming which route the student came from is the single most useful fact in a first enquiry.

dubai/ib-dp-hindi-b-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: A Dubai IB school's Group 2 block decides what is actually possible, and a Hindi B student is usually weighing these options. Each note is about demand rather than content coverage.

subjects.name: Hindi B Higher Level
subjects.description: Two literary works originally written in Hindi, longer written responses, denser reading, and an Individual Oral built on an unseen extract from one of the works. For a household speaker who has never read extended Hindi prose, this is a reading commitment rather than a language one, and it needs a schedule from DP1 rather than a scramble in the final term.

subjects.name: Hindi B Standard Level
subjects.description: The same three components without the literary works, with the oral based on a visual stimulus linked to one of the prescribed themes. For a student whose spoken Hindi is strong and whose Devanagari is unreliable, Standard Level with disciplined script and register work usually produces a better Diploma total than Higher Level thinly covered.

subjects.name: Hindi A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: First-language Hindi taught as literary and textual analysis, and the only Hindi route counting towards the bilingual diploma. Rarely timetabled in Dubai, occasionally available as a school-supported self-taught Standard Level option. The reading load is the deciding factor, not the speaking.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Hindi as a Second Language
subjects.description: The pre-Diploma qualification many Dubai students take, with its own syllabus and paper structure published by Cambridge. Worth naming in a tutoring enquiry because the writing conventions rewarded there are closer to Group 2 functional writing than the CBSE literature route is, which changes what has to be built in DP1.

subjects.name: Urdu B
subjects.description: Frequently considered alongside Hindi by Dubai families, and a genuinely different course because of the script. Students who speak both and read neither sometimes assume one choice is easier; the shared spoken vocabulary does not transfer to the written assessment, where Nastaliq and Devanagari are entirely separate skills.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Listed because it is the alternative many Dubai students take when the Hindi B set is full or the timetable blocks clash. The error profile is unrelated: tense and mood control rather than script and register. A family switching a child between them should expect to start the diagnostic process again from scratch.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: The best-supplied Group 2 language in Dubai IB schools, and the usual fallback where Hindi B cannot be timetabled. Supply matters here: a student in a well-staffed French set may get more individual feedback inside school than one in a Hindi set of five, which changes how much outside help is needed.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school under KHDA requirements regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students. A Hindi B candidate therefore carries three languages in the school week, and counting the total minutes is worth doing before adding a fourth commitment.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Hindi B
subjects.description: A 4,000-word essay written in Hindi on an aspect of culture in the Hindi-speaking world, supervised inside the school. The tutor's role is process coaching only: framing a researchable question, evaluating sources and giving feedback on the student's own drafts. Writing in Devanagari at that length is itself a skill worth practising early.

dubai/ib-dp-hindi-b-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Hindi B enquiries reach us from across Dubai, and what differs by area is the household language pattern and the shape of the week rather than the teaching itself.

regions.name: Al Nahda and Al Qusais
regions.note: A long-established Indian expatriate belt where Hindi is spoken daily and read rarely. Students here usually arrive with strong listening and speaking and a script that has not been used for formal writing since primary school, which is exactly the profile that benefits from dictation work.

regions.name: Karama, Oud Metha and Bur Dubai
regions.note: Older, denser neighbourhoods with short school runs and apartment living. A recorded oral attempt needs a planned quiet half hour here rather than a spontaneous one, and families tend to put the monthly recording at the weekend.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Mixed Indian, British and IB catchments inside a short radius, and a high proportion of students carrying the school's mandatory Arabic stream alongside Hindi. This is the part of the city where total weekly language minutes most often turn out to be higher than anyone had counted.

regions.name: International City and Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: Long bus journeys into the school clusters further west, so a Diploma student is often home late and tired. Short, frequent sessions work better here than one long evening block, particularly for script accuracy work that depends on concentration.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and Al Furjan
regions.note: Apartment communities with large family networks nearby, which helps spoken fluency and masks reading weakness almost completely. Families here are often surprised by a low receptive-paper mock score, because every social signal suggested the Hindi was strong.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Villa communities with easier weekend mornings and heavily committed weekday evenings. Saturday sessions suit the slower work: copy-correction, reading unfamiliar text types and the sustained writing practice the Extended Essay in Hindi requires.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Frequent international travel in and out of term time, which leaves specific topic gaps rather than general weakness. The coverage list and the error log are what make those gaps findable instead of being mistaken for a general decline.

sections.heading: What Hindi B assesses, component by component
paragraphs: Hindi B is assessed through three components and the proportions explain most of what goes wrong. The written task, a single piece produced in response to a stimulus in a set text type, carries a quarter of the grade. The receptive paper, combining listening and reading, carries half. The recorded Individual Oral carries the remaining quarter. The weightings are the same at Standard and Higher Level; what rises at Higher Level is the demand inside each one, plus the arrival of two literary works.

Set against the way families buy Hindi help, those numbers are awkward. The instinct is to buy conversation, because speaking is what a parent can hear and what a student enjoys. The oral is a quarter of the grade and is also the component a household speaker is least likely to fail. The paper carrying twice the weight rewards reading unfamiliar text and hearing unfamiliar speakers, and improves through volume and timed practice rather than through discussion. If a budget stretches to one component, the arithmetic says the receptive paper.

Component timings, word bands and the school's internal dates should be confirmed against the current subject guide and with the Diploma coordinator. This page publishes no IB exam or results date: the IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project, and an unconfirmed date on a page like this is worse than none. The weightings are the stable part, and they are what a tuition plan should be built on.

sections.heading: Devanagari: the marks the script quietly takes
paragraphs: Script errors are the most under-discussed mark loss in Hindi B, because they do not exist in speech and so no adult in the student's life has ever noticed them. A student who speaks Hindi daily and writes it occasionally produces work with matras placed by habit rather than by rule, nukta omitted where it changes the word, and anusvara and chandrabindu used as if interchangeable. Individually small; collectively, across a written task, a grade.

The good news is the speed of repair. Script accuracy is a motor and perceptual skill, which responds to short frequent practice far better than to long explanation. Dictation from unfamiliar text, copy-correction of the student's own handwriting, and a weekly retest of the previous fortnight's errors will clear most of the pattern inside a term. Typing is a poor substitute: an input method quietly fixes some of the very errors the exam will penalise, so the practice has to be handwritten and photographed if it is to be useful.

There is one Dubai-specific wrinkle worth naming. Students who learnt their Hindi reading from signage, film subtitles and messaging apps have encountered a great deal of Devanagari in forms that are not standard: transliterated English, abbreviations, and informal spellings. That exposure builds confident recognition and unreliable production. It is not a deficiency of effort and it is invisible until somebody asks for a handwritten paragraph on a topic the student has not chosen.

Legibility under time pressure is the last piece and the one most often missed. Handwriting that is perfectly clear for a paragraph degrades sharply in the final third of a timed task, when the student is racing the clock and the hand is tired. Examiners mark what they can read. Four to six sessions of deliberately timed handwritten practice, with the last page compared against the first, usually corrects both the pace and the deterioration, and it costs very little because the language work is already done.
