sections.heading: Register: aap, tum and the problem of family Hindi
paragraphs: Hindi encodes social relationship in its grammar, and Hindi B assesses whether a student controls that system rather than whether they are aware of it. The written task requires a register appropriate to the text type and maintained across the whole piece: a formal letter does not drift into the second person a student uses with a cousin, and an article does not switch address halfway through. Students who learnt Hindi socially choose register per sentence by instinct, and instinct is inconsistent.

The specific failure is almost always mid-piece drift. A student starts a formal letter correctly, relaxes by the third paragraph, and finishes in the voice they would use at home. An examiner reads that as weak control of the language rather than as a lapse of attention. The second failure is the opposite: over-formality applied indiscriminately, where a student who has been told to be formal produces a text message to a friend written like a government notice, which misses the text type conventions instead.

Register responds fast to the right practice and not at all to the wrong one. Explaining the system takes ten minutes and changes nothing. Writing the same content twice, once formally and once informally, and then marking both for consistency, changes a great deal. A running log of formality slips with the surrounding context noted makes the pattern visible: most students slip in the same place every time, usually when the content becomes emotionally engaging and attention moves from form to meaning.

sections.heading: What one 60-minute Hindi B session can fix, and what cannot be fixed in one
paragraphs: Families book Hindi tuition at two moments: the start of DP1, and three weeks before a mock. The honest answer about what a single session achieves differs enormously between those two, and being clear about it is more useful than selling a package. Some things in this subject genuinely move inside an hour, because they are rule-based and the student already has the underlying language. Others are volume problems and no single session touches them.

Inside one hour: the nukta list for the words that actually matter to this student, the anusvara and chandrabindu rule, the structure of a formal letter in Hindi, the question types in the reading paper that reward scanning rather than reading, and the timing discipline for the Individual Oral so the discussion is not crushed by an over-long presentation. Each of those is a discrete fix with a visible effect on the next piece of work, and a tutor who spends a pre-mock hour on general conversation has wasted it.

Not inside one hour, or ten: reading fluency on unfamiliar text types, listening tolerance for unfamiliar speakers, structural range in writing, and the vocabulary for discussing literature at Higher Level. Those are accumulation problems measured in terms. A provider who implies otherwise three weeks before an exam is selling reassurance. The useful pre-exam conversation is about which discrete fixes remain available, which is a short and specific list rather than a programme.

The distinction also governs when a family should start. A student in DP1 with a term and a half ahead of them should be spending it on the accumulation problems, because that is the only window in which they move. A student six weeks from a final paper should be spending every hour on the discrete list, because the accumulation work will not land in time and attempting it crowds out the fixes that would. Both plans are legitimate. Running the DP1 plan in the final six weeks is the mistake that wastes the most money in this subject.

sections.heading: Hindi B against Hindi A, and against the CBSE Hindi left behind
paragraphs: Three Hindi routes get confused with each other in Dubai, and the confusion costs students. Hindi B is a Group 2 acquisition course. Hindi A: Language and Literature is a Group 1 course for first-language speakers, taught as textual analysis, and it is the only Hindi option that can contribute towards the bilingual diploma. CBSE Hindi, which many Dubai students studied until class 10, is a different qualification with a literature-weighted shape that does not map onto Group 2 functional writing.

A student arriving from CBSE class 10 Hindi is usually stronger than their Hindi B classmates on literary comprehension and weaker on the functional text types the written task rewards: the formal letter, the article, the blog, the report. They also tend to be better at handwritten Devanagari, because they have been doing it in examinations. The gap is register flexibility and text type range, and it is a term of work rather than a reconstruction.

A household speaker with no formal Hindi schooling is the opposite profile and needs the opposite plan. The question of whether a strong student should be in Hindi A rather than Hindi B is for the Diploma coordinator, and the useful contribution from outside is evidence rather than advocacy: a marked written task, a timed reading score, and an honest note on reading stamina. Few Dubai schools timetable Hindi A, and where it is offered as a school-supported self-taught option the reading load deserves a frank conversation before anyone commits.

sections.heading: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency: what each curriculum must show
paragraphs: Families studying an international curriculum in Dubai eventually meet equivalency, the process by which the Ministry of Education assesses a school-leaving certificate for use in the UAE. It is worth understanding early and it is not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or influences. Nor is tutoring required for it: equivalency is a documentary process about qualifications, not about preparation.

The British-track requirements are published. Students must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That five-subject count is worth knowing precisely, because at least one ranking competitor page in this market publishes six and families act on it.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the International Baccalaureate, no points threshold is published on a source this project could verify, so none appears here. Verify the IB position on moe.gov.ae or with the relevant attestation authority, and treat any site quoting an IB points figure without naming its source with scepticism.

sections.heading: Hindi alongside the Arabic every Dubai school must teach
paragraphs: A Hindi B candidate in Dubai is carrying more language than the subject list suggests. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

That has practical consequences for a tutoring plan. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs for at least 25 minutes. Add the school's English provision and a Group 2 language, and a Dubai Diploma student can be in language lessons for a substantial share of the week before any private tuition is considered. Counting those minutes honestly is the first thing to do before buying more.

There is a second constraint worth knowing. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, and schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. That is a real limit on how Arabic support can be described and delivered, and it is one reason this page treats Hindi B and the school's Arabic requirement as separate problems with separate specialists rather than something one tutor absorbs.

sections.heading: What a Hindi B tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: Group 2 has two places where help can cross into malpractice, and both are relevant to Hindi B. The Individual Oral is assessed as the student's own unscripted performance. The Extended Essay, where a student chooses to write one in Hindi, is assessed as the student's own research and writing under school supervision. Offers that cross those lines are available in this market, and declining them is not caution but self-preservation on the student's behalf.

A tutor may explain how each component is marked, run practice against stimuli and extracts the student has not seen, read a draft and say where it is weak, question an argument, point to a source the student has not considered, and model a text type on an entirely different topic. A tutor may not supply a script for the oral, write into the student's draft, produce finished work, or prepare answers to the specific stimulus the school will use. The second list is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student.

The same boundary applies to materials. Official subject guides, past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB and are not ours to distribute; the place to read them is through the school or ibo.org. A tutor arriving with a folder of copied papers is not providing an advantage, and for unreleased material it is a serious exposure. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and nothing on this page should be read as implying otherwise.

Not allowed: scripts for the oral, writing into a draft, or finished work produced for the student

process.title: Send a handwritten Hindi paragraph with the enquiry
process.description: Not a typed one. A photograph of two handwritten paragraphs on an ordinary topic tells a Hindi B teacher more than any description of how the subject is going, because matra placement, nukta and conjunct handling are all visible in it and none of them are visible in conversation or in a typed message.

process.title: Name the pre-Diploma route
process.description: CBSE class 10 Hindi, Cambridge IGCSE Hindi as a Second Language, MYP Hindi by phase, or household Hindi with no formal schooling. Each produces a different profile and a different first six weeks. It is the fact families most often leave out and the one that changes the plan most.

process.title: One diagnostic hour before any teaching
process.description: A handwritten task, a timed reading section on an unfamiliar text type, and a short unprepared spoken turn, marked and returned with the error classes named. No teaching happens until that evidence exists, and the diagnostic is yours to keep whether or not you continue with us.

process.title: Split script work from register work from the receptive clinic
process.description: Script accuracy runs as short frequent sessions and finishes. Register and written task discipline runs fortnightly across a term. The receptive clinic sits near the February break. Three jobs with three natural lengths uses fewer hours than one weekly slot running for two years.

process.title: Review on error counts, and stop what has finished
process.description: A monthly count by error class, so cleared classes can be dropped from the plan rather than kept in it. When the script work is done, the hours go to the receptive paper or they stop. A match that is not producing movement is replaced, and where fewer hours is the honest answer we say so.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from handwriting, not from conversation
whyPoints.description: Household fluency hides every one of the errors Hindi B penalises. A handwritten sample, a timed reading section and one unprepared spoken turn locate the real problem in an hour, and the finding is written in terms a parent can take to the next school meeting.

whyPoints.title: The hours go where the weighting is
whyPoints.description: Half the Hindi B grade sits in the receptive paper, which attracts the least attention because comprehension practice feels less like a lesson than talking does. We put the time there and say so when a family asks for conversation instead, including when that means recommending fewer hours.

whyPoints.title: Script work treated as a finite job
whyPoints.description: Matra, nukta, anusvara and conjunct errors are motor and perceptual, they respond to short frequent practice, and they finish. We run them as a block with error counts per class and then stop, rather than keeping a weekly slot alive after the problem has cleared.

whyPoints.title: Accurate about the routes and the rules
whyPoints.description: Hindi B does not contribute to the bilingual diploma; Hindi A can. CBSE Hindi does not map onto Group 2 functional writing. Equivalency is a documentary process nobody tutors for, and the published British-track rule is five IGCSE or GCSE subjects, not six. We would rather correct these early than let them surface in DP2.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we are not
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no regulator or examination-board approval claimed, no promised grades, no statistic without a date and a source, and no IB exam date because none could be verified for this project. The limits of what a tutor may do with assessed work are stated plainly rather than left vague.

whyPoints.title: Reachable specialists rather than nearby ones
whyPoints.description: There are many Hindi speakers in Dubai and few teachers who mark Devanagari against the Group 2 band descriptors. Online one-to-one on Gulf Standard Time widens the pool to whoever is genuinely free at that hour, with the marked work and the error log kept in one shared file.

faqs.question: My child speaks Hindi at home — will IB Hindi B be an easy subject?
faqs.answer: Often not, and the reason is specific. Hindi B assesses writing in Devanagari to an academic standard, reading unfamiliar text under timing, listening to speakers the student has never heard, and sustaining a recorded discussion in a register most households do not use. Conversational fluency covers one of those four. The usual pattern is a strong Individual Oral beside a weak receptive paper and an inconsistent written task, which is how a confident Hindi speaker ends up at a 4. Send a handwritten paragraph with any enquiry; it reveals more than a description of how fluent the child sounds.

faqs.question: Is Hindi B offered at Higher Level, and what does that add?
faqs.answer: Yes, Hindi B is examined at both Standard and Higher Level. Higher Level adds two literary works originally written in Hindi, longer written responses, denser reading texts, and an Individual Oral built on an unseen extract from one of the works rather than on a visual stimulus. For a household speaker who has never read extended Hindi prose, that is a reading commitment rather than a language one, and it needs a schedule running from DP1. Where reading stamina is the problem, Standard Level done thoroughly usually produces a better Diploma total.

faqs.question: How much do Devanagari handwriting errors actually cost in Hindi B?
faqs.answer: Enough to move a grade, which surprises families because the errors are invisible in speech. The recurring ones are matras placed by habit rather than rule, nukta dropped where it distinguishes one word from another, anusvara and chandrabindu used interchangeably, and conjunct consonants avoided. Each is a small deduction and they accumulate across a written task. They are also the fastest thing in the subject to repair: short daily dictation, copy-correction of the student's own handwriting, and a weekly retest clears most of the pattern within a term.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Hindi B and Hindi A in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Hindi B is a Group 2 language acquisition course assessing functional writing, listening, reading and an oral. Hindi A: Language and Literature is a Group 1 course for first-language speakers, taught as literary and textual analysis, and it is the only Hindi route that can contribute towards the bilingual diploma. The deciding factor between them is reading stamina in extended Hindi prose rather than how fluently the student speaks. Few Dubai schools timetable Hindi A; some can offer it as a school-supported self-taught Standard Level option, which deserves a frank conversation first.

faqs.question: My child studied CBSE Hindi until class 10 — where does that leave them in Hindi B?
faqs.answer: Usually ahead on handwritten Devanagari and literary comprehension, and behind on the functional text types Group 2 rewards: the formal letter, the article, the report, the blog. CBSE's Hindi courses are literature-weighted and examined differently, so the transition work is register flexibility and text type range rather than a reconstruction of the language. That is typically a term of fortnightly marked writing. Naming the pre-Diploma route in a first enquiry is the single most useful fact a Dubai family can give a Hindi B tutor.

faqs.question: Which register should a Hindi B student use in the written task?
faqs.answer: Whichever the text type requires, maintained consistently across the whole piece. The commonest loss is not ignorance of the system but drift: a formal letter that opens correctly, relaxes by the third paragraph and finishes in the voice the student uses with a cousin. An examiner reads that as weak control of the language. The second commonest is uniform over-formality that misses the conventions of an informal text type. The practice that works is writing the same content twice in two registers and marking both for consistency.

faqs.question: Does taking Hindi B count towards the IB bilingual diploma?
faqs.answer: No. The bilingual diploma rests on two Group 1 language and literature subjects, or a Group 3 or Group 4 subject studied and assessed in a language other than the student's Group 1 language, subject to the IB's own grade requirements. Group 2 acquisition courses do not qualify, however strong the student's Hindi is. Hindi A: Language and Literature can contribute, which is one reason the placement conversation with the Diploma coordinator is worth having in DP1 rather than discovering the rule in the final year.

faqs.question: Will Hindi B help with UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a documentary assessment of a school-leaving certificate and no tutoring is required for it. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold appears on a source this project could verify, so none is published here. Check moe.gov.ae or the relevant attestation authority directly rather than relying on a tutoring site.

faqs.question: Can Hindi B lessons work over video when the script has to be handwritten?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the handwriting requirement is exactly why the arrangement has to be set up properly. The student writes by hand on paper, photographs the page, and uploads it; the tutor annotates the image and both look at the same marked script on a shared screen. What does not work is typing practice, because an input method silently corrects some of the very errors the exam penalises. Any provider who runs Hindi B writing practice entirely in a typed document is training the wrong skill, whatever the format of the lesson.

faqs.question: Where do Hindi B students lose marks in the receptive paper?
faqs.answer: On inference questions and on unfamiliar text types. A household Hindi speaker has recognition vocabulary that looks adequate and then collapses on an editorial, a public notice or a formal letter, because nothing in daily conversation uses those conventions. The listening section catches a second gap: speakers whose accent and vocabulary sit outside the family's own. The fix is volume plus timed practice on text the student has not met before, concentrated near the February break rather than spread thinly across two years.

faqs.question: What can one 60-minute Hindi B session realistically fix before a mock?
faqs.answer: Discrete, rule-based things with a visible effect on the next piece of work: a personal nukta list for the words that matter to this student, the anusvara and chandrabindu rule, the structure of a formal letter in Hindi, the reading-paper question types that reward scanning rather than close reading, and timing discipline for the oral so the discussion is not crushed. What one session cannot do is build reading fluency, listening tolerance or structural range. Those are accumulation problems measured in terms, and any provider implying otherwise three weeks out is selling reassurance.

faqs.question: Does my child need Hindi B tuition if the school already requires Arabic?
faqs.answer: That is a question about total load rather than about either subject. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students, and KHDA calculates the instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. Add English and a Group 2 language and a Diploma student may already be in language lessons for a large share of the week. Count those minutes before adding anything, and treat Arabic and Hindi as separate problems with separate specialists.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Hindi tutor to homes in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Hindi B teaching reaches Dubai families as one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time, with handwritten work photographed, annotated and kept in a shared file alongside the error log. The trade is favourable for this subject: Dubai has a great many Hindi speakers and relatively few teachers who mark Devanagari against the Group 2 band descriptors, and proximity is the wrong filter to apply when the pool is that narrow.

faqs.question: How many Hindi B sessions a week do Dubai Diploma students usually take?
faqs.answer: The shape matters more than the count. Script accuracy wants short sessions three times a week for a few weeks and then stops, because it is a motor skill that responds to spacing. Register and written task work wants one fortnightly session with a marked piece in between. The receptive clinic is a short intensive block near the February break. Run that way, most students use fewer total hours across the two Diploma years than they would with a single weekly slot held open from DP1 to the final term.

faqs.question: Can a Hindi B tutor help with an Extended Essay written in Hindi?
faqs.answer: Within the limits that apply to all supervised coursework, yes. A tutor may help frame a researchable question, discuss how to evaluate sources, explain the assessment criteria, and give feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph into the draft, or produce finished work. The supervision itself belongs to the school. One practical point: writing 4,000 words in Devanagari is a stamina skill in its own right, and students who have only ever written short pieces should practise length well before the first draft deadline.

intro.heading: Fluent at home, marked in Devanagari: what Hindi B really tests
paragraphs: Hindi B is the IB Diploma's language acquisition course in Hindi, offered at Standard and Higher Level, with two literary works added at Higher Level. In Dubai it is studied overwhelmingly by students from Indian-expatriate families, and that fact changes the whole shape of the problem. These students almost never lack Hindi. They lack the written, formal, Devanagari-accurate Hindi that a Paper 1 task is marked against, and the distance between the two is wider than most families expect.

The pattern repeats across every Dubai cohort. A student converses easily with grandparents, follows Hindi film dialogue without subtitles, and then scores 4 because a written task carries fifteen matra errors, three conjunct consonants written as separate letters, and a register borrowed from conversation rather than from a formal letter. None of that is a Hindi problem. It is a script problem and a register problem, and both are teachable in a way that fluency is not.

The second thing that makes this subject distinctive in Dubai is the transition it usually follows. Many Hindi B candidates spent years in a CBSE or ICSE classroom where Hindi was assessed through set textbook chapters, grammar exercises and literature questions with known answers. IB Hindi B assesses unseen texts, defined text types written for a stated audience, listening at natural speed and an oral built on a stimulus. The knowledge transfers; the examination habits do not, and the gap between them is where the first term usually goes.

This page is built around what the course assesses rather than around general Hindi improvement. It covers placing a heritage speaker correctly between Hindi A, Hindi B and ab initio, the components and what each is worth, the specific script faults that cost marks, the register problem, what to do when a Dubai school cannot staff Hindi in the Diploma, and the gap between an Indian-curriculum Hindi background and an IB Hindi B paper. Each of those is a separate repair with its own method, and conflating them is the usual reason a term of weekly lessons produces no visible change in a grade.

Delivery is online. IB Gram matches Dubai families with one-to-one tutors over live video, with the student's own handwritten work photographed and annotated on screen. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we offer only in India. For Hindi B the online route is frequently the only route, because a school that cannot timetable a Hindi B class is not likely to have a Hindi B specialist living in the next community either. Matching on experience of this syllabus at this level, rather than on who is closest to your address, is the whole point of working this way.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Hindi B sits in Group 2 and satisfies the language acquisition requirement at either level. The grade comes from two external papers and one internally assessed individual oral, with Higher Level candidates also studying two literary works that form the basis of their oral. Written accuracy carries more weight than most incoming students assume.

programmes.name: Indian national curricula
programmes.description: Not IB programmes, but the background most Dubai Hindi B candidates arrive from. programmes.countryNote: The Indian curricula account for a large share of Dubai private-school enrolment, which is why the CBSE-to-IB transition is a routine event in this emirate rather than an unusual one. programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP requires additional language learning without a separate examination, and Hindi appears in that slot in several Dubai continuum schools. The reason for listing them is timing: Hindi writing practice is the first thing that gets dropped when three deadlines collide.

subjects.description: Five prescribed themes, two external papers and an individual oral, plus two literary works at Higher Level. The marks turn on written Devanagari accuracy, text-type conventions and formal register rather than on conversational range.

subjects.name: English A: language and literature
subjects.description: Almost universal in Dubai Diploma cohorts. The analytical writing built here transfers usefully into the Hindi B Higher Level oral, where a student comments on an extract from a studied work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A frequent pairing for students whose strengths sit in languages and humanities. Its exploration deadline often falls in the same weeks as the Hindi oral window, which is the clash worth planning for in advance.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Widely taken across Dubai schools. Its own written work rewards structure and audience awareness, which is exactly the habit a Hindi B text-type task requires, so the two can be taught to reinforce each other.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries across the course with fixed submission dates. Students carrying Economics Higher Level alongside Hindi B usually lose Hindi writing practice in the spring term unless the schedule is set deliberately.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: A common Higher Level for students aiming at medicine or engineering. Its internal assessment competes directly with Hindi B Higher Level reading for evening hours, and the Hindi reading is the one with no hard deadline attached.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Essay-heavy and popular in this market. The planning discipline it builds, naming the question's demand before writing, is the single most transferable habit into Hindi B Paper 1 tasks.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools for students who are not Arab nationals, streamed separately from Arabic as a first language under KHDA rules. It occupies a timetable slot that cannot be converted into more Hindi.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Part of the Diploma core rather than Group 2. Together with the Extended Essay it can contribute up to three points to the total, which matters when a family is weighing whether to push for a 6 in Hindi or protect points elsewhere.

sections.heading: What the Hindi B search usually means in a Dubai household
paragraphs: The families who search for Hindi B support in Dubai are rarely worried about whether their child can speak Hindi. The worry is a report card that does not match what they hear at the dinner table. A student who argues comfortably with a grandparent in Hindi has come home with a 4, and nobody in the house can work out how that is possible. The answer is usually visible in ninety seconds of looking at a marked written task.

Hindi B is assessed on written production in Devanagari, on comprehension of unseen material at natural speed, and on an oral that moves from a stimulus into developed discussion. Spoken fluency helps with exactly one of those and only partially, because the oral rewards development of ideas rather than ease of chat. Written production is where most marks are lost, and written production in a script the student has rarely had to use carefully is a different skill from speaking.

There is a second, quieter issue. Many Dubai students in this position have been praised for their Hindi their whole lives, by relatives and sometimes by teachers, and discover in Year 12 that the praise was about fluency and the marks are about accuracy. That is demoralising, and handling it honestly matters. The useful framing is that they are not bad at Hindi; they have never been taught the written system, because nobody teaches a native speaker to spell.

So the first session on this page is a short handwritten task, photographed and marked with every script and register fault classified. The resulting profile usually shows three or four repeating faults rather than a general weakness, and three or four faults can be closed in a term. That diagnosis changes the conversation at home from disappointment to a list.

sections.heading: Hindi A, Hindi B or ab initio: placing a heritage speaker honestly
paragraphs: The placement decision is more consequential in Hindi than in most Group 2 languages, because the range of prior learning among Dubai students is enormous. One student reads Hindi novels. Another speaks three dialects and cannot write a sentence. A third learned songs and greetings and nothing else. These three cannot sit in the same course and all be correctly placed, and the school's entry assessment, not the family's sense of fluency, should decide.

A student who reads literary Hindi comfortably and can analyse a text in it may belong in Hindi A: literature, which sits in Group 1 and is assessed on literary analysis rather than language acquisition. Placing such a student in Hindi B often produces an easy 6 or 7 and wastes a Group 1 option they could have used for a language they would actually have been stretched by. That is a planning loss rather than a grade loss, and it is worth catching in Year 11.

A student who speaks fluently but cannot write is the standard Hindi B candidate, and Hindi B is designed to be winnable for them once the script and register are rebuilt. The ab initio route is for genuine beginners and exists only at Standard Level; a confident speaker is not eligible for it regardless of how weak the writing is, because the eligibility condition is about prior experience of the language rather than about current written accuracy.

The table sets out the decision in the terms a school assessment actually uses. Take it to the IB coordinator rather than arguing from fluency, because the school has to defend the placement when work is moderated.

sections.heading: The components, and where the marks actually sit
paragraphs: Hindi B is built from two external papers and one internally assessed oral. Paper 1 is productive writing: one task, in a defined text type, for a stated audience and purpose, within a word band that differs by level. Paper 2 is receptive and covers listening and reading on unseen material. The individual oral is conducted and marked inside the school and then moderated, which is why its deadline usually falls months before the written papers.

The productive paper is where Dubai students most often lose ground, and the reason is rarely vocabulary. A task asks for a formal letter to a school principal, or a blog entry, or a set of instructions, and each of those has conventions: an opening, a register, a sign-off, a relationship with the reader. A student who writes excellent conversational Hindi in the shape of a text message has capped the mark before the examiner reaches the grammar. These conventions are closed sets and can be learned in a fortnight.

The receptive paper rewards two different disciplines. Listening is answered once, at speed, with no replays; a student who stops to decode one unfamiliar word loses the next two answers, which is a technique failure with a technique cure. Reading rewards locating the exact phrase a question wants rather than paraphrasing it loosely, and students trained on set texts find this harder than students trained on unseen material, because their instinct is to recall rather than to search.

The oral is the most winnable component for this student population. At Standard Level it begins from a visual stimulus linked to a prescribed theme; at Higher Level it begins from an extract taken from one of the two literary works studied. Dubai Hindi speakers tend to be comfortable talking, and the marks come from developing an idea rather than from fluency alone, so the trainable element is the move from description into argument.

sections.heading: Devanagari: the script faults that quietly cost a grade
paragraphs: Script accuracy is the single most under-taught element of Hindi B for heritage speakers, and it is also the most mechanical to fix. The faults are a short list, they repeat, and each has a drill. A student who knows that their three recurring problems are the short and long i matras, the nukta, and conjuncts written as separate consonants has a two-week project rather than a vague deficiency.

Matra confusion dominates. The short and long vowel markers change meaning, and a speaker who has never had to choose between them in writing will guess based on sound, which is unreliable because the spoken distinction is weaker than the written one. The remedy is paired word lists where the only difference is the matra, written repeatedly, then dictation. It is dull and it works within weeks, which is the best combination available in this subject.

Conjunct consonants are the second family. In handwriting, learners frequently break a ligature into two separate letters or form it in a way that reads as a different cluster. Examiners mark what is on the page. A student who writes clearly but forms conjuncts inconsistently is losing marks they would never lose in speech, and the fix is handwriting practice on a defined set of the most frequent clusters rather than on the whole inventory.

The remaining faults are smaller and still worth naming: the nukta omitted from borrowed words, anusvara and chandrabindu used interchangeably, the shirorekha broken or run through punctuation, and gender agreement failing in writing where it is automatic in speech. Classified marking turns the whole set into a checklist, and a checklist is something a student can finish.

sections.heading: Register: why the Hindi that works at home loses marks on paper
paragraphs: Register is the other half of the heritage-speaker problem and it is harder to accept than the script. The Hindi most Dubai students use daily is a conversational blend, often carrying English vocabulary, informal verb forms and a tone built for family. The Hindi a Paper 1 task rewards is formal, uses the Sanskritised vocabulary a newspaper or an official letter would use, and maintains a consistent relationship with a stated reader. Mixing the two is visible on the first line.

This is not a judgement about which Hindi is better. It is a statement about what the criteria measure. A formal letter to a principal that opens like a message to a cousin has already lost marks on conceptual understanding, regardless of how correct the grammar turns out to be. Teaching register therefore means teaching a second vocabulary deliberately, as paired lists: the spoken word a student already uses, next to the formal equivalent the examination expects.

Text types provide the scaffolding. Each has furniture that does not change: how a formal letter opens and closes, how a blog addresses a reader, how a speech signals its structure, how instructions are sequenced. A student who learns that furniture has a reliable frame into which their existing Hindi can be poured. Without it, every task starts from nothing and the register drifts back towards conversation by the second paragraph.

The practice that works is short and repetitive. One task per week in a named text type, written to the correct word band, marked with register faults classified separately from script faults so the two counts move independently. Students who see their register count fall while their script count holds steady learn something useful about where to put the next fortnight of effort.

sections.heading: If your Dubai school cannot run Hindi in the Diploma
paragraphs: This is a real situation in Dubai and families are often given a confused answer about it. Group 2 staffing depends on numbers, and a school with four interested students may not timetable Hindi B in a given year. What happens next depends on rules families rarely know, so it is worth getting them from the IB coordinator in writing rather than from a tutoring site, including this one.

The point most often misunderstood is self-teaching. The IB's school-supported self-taught arrangement applies to a Language A literature course at Standard Level, not to a Language B course. A student whose school cannot staff Hindi B therefore cannot simply study Hindi B independently and sit the papers. A sufficiently literate student may instead be able to take Hindi A: literature at Standard Level on the self-taught basis, which satisfies a different group and changes the whole subject combination. Confirm the current regulations with your coordinator, because the IB updates them.

That shifts the decision from a language question to a Diploma-structure question. Taking Hindi A: literature self-taught means the student needs another Group 2 language, which for most Dubai students means French, Spanish or Arabic, possibly at ab initio level. Keeping Hindi out of the Diploma entirely means choosing a different Group 2 course and treating Hindi as a family rather than an academic matter. Neither is wrong; they are different trades.

Private tuition changes what is possible in one of these branches and not in the others. A self-taught Hindi A literature candidate is the student who most needs sustained one-to-one support, because the school provides a supervisor rather than a teacher. A student who simply has no Hindi option in their school cannot be made into a Hindi B candidate by a tutor, and anyone who implies otherwise is selling something that will not reach an examination entry.

sections.heading: From CBSE or ICSE Hindi into an IB Hindi B paper
paragraphs: Dubai's Indian curricula account for a large share of private-school enrolment in the emirate, so the move from CBSE or ICSE Hindi into IB Hindi B happens constantly here. The content a student carries over is genuinely useful: grammar has usually been taught explicitly, the script has been written for years, and vocabulary from set texts is broad. What does not carry over is the examination behaviour, and the first term is mostly spent replacing it.

In the Indian systems a Hindi examination largely rewards learned material. Questions attach to studied chapters, formats repeat predictably year on year, and a diligent student can prepare by covering known ground thoroughly. IB Hindi B asks for responses to texts nobody has seen, written to a brief that names an audience and a purpose, and comprehension of recordings played once. Preparation by coverage does not help with any of that, which is disorienting for students who have been rewarded for it.

The retraining is specific. The student has to learn to read a task brief as a set of instructions, to plan before writing rather than starting at the first sentence, to search a text for an exact phrase rather than recalling what the chapter said, and to keep writing when a listening recording moves past something they did not understand. These are four habits, each with its own drill, and all four are easier to install in Year 12 than in Year 13.

The opposite transition has a different shape and comes up less often in Dubai: a student leaving IB Hindi B for a CBSE board examination has to rebuild memorised content fast. Where a family is weighing the two systems against each other, the honest summary is that Indian-curriculum Hindi rewards depth on known material and IB Hindi B rewards transfer to unknown material, and a student's temperament is a legitimate factor in the choice.

sections.heading: What a session fixes, and what it cannot
paragraphs: Worth being blunt about the boundaries. A weekly one-to-one Hindi B session can rebuild script accuracy, install formal register, teach text-type conventions, train listening technique, build a Higher Level reading schedule, and raise the quality of oral development. Those are the things that move a Hindi B grade and they are all teachable. A tutor who promises more than that is describing something else.

What a session cannot do is produce assessed work. The IB requires that what reaches a teacher or an examiner is the candidate's own, and a tutor who supplies Hindi text, rewrites a draft to a standard the student could not reach, or rehearses a memorised oral has created a malpractice risk that falls on the student rather than on the tutor. IB Gram tutors mark, classify, explain the rule and set a rewrite. The student generates every sentence.

Nor can a session substitute for hours. Listening comprehension improves with volume of exposure at natural speed, not with explanation, and Higher Level literary works have to be read by the person sitting the oral. A tutor's contribution to both is scheduling and accountability: a dated plan, and a conversation each week about whether it happened. That is less exciting than a technique and it is often the difference between a 4 and a 6.

The honest summary of the offer is a method rather than an outcome. Classified marking of handwritten work, separate counts for script and register faults, text-type furniture taught as fixed sets, listening practised cold, and a review at session ten where a fault family that has not closed changes the method rather than adding hours. No grade can be promised by anyone, and a service promising one should be treated with real scepticism.

process.title: Establish the level and the real starting point
process.description: We confirm whether the student is registered for Hindi B at Standard or Higher Level, what their most recent score was, whether the school has set literary works, and when the oral window opens. For Higher Level the two work titles matter more than anything else in the plan.

process.title: Free trial with a handwritten diagnostic
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, no card details taken. The student handwrites a short task, photographs it, and the tutor marks it with script faults and register faults classified separately. The hour ends with a profile rather than an introduction.

process.title: Two fault families chosen, written down
process.description: The tutor ranks the fault families by frequency and picks the two that matter most this term. Working on everything at once produces no visible movement in anything. You receive the ranking and the chosen targets in writing after the trial.

process.title: Weekly task, classified marking, rewrite
process.description: One timed task a week in the correct word band, handwritten, marked before the session with script and register counts kept apart. The session drills the chosen families, then the student rewrites. Counts and dates go into a file you can open.

process.title: Review at session ten
process.description: We look at the two counts together. A family that has closed is replaced by the next one down. A family that has not moved means the drill was wrong, so the drill changes rather than the hours increasing. If the match is poor we say so and move the student.

whyPoints.title: The script is taught, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Nobody teaches a fluent speaker to spell, which is exactly why heritage speakers lose Hindi B marks. Matras, conjuncts, nukta and anusvara are taught as a finite checklist with drills attached, and the count is tracked.

whyPoints.title: Register treated as a second vocabulary
whyPoints.description: Formal Hindi is built deliberately through paired lists against the spoken form, and text-type furniture is learned as fixed sets. Register faults are counted separately from script faults so each one can be seen moving.

whyPoints.title: Work marked in Devanagari, by hand
whyPoints.description: Tasks are handwritten, photographed and annotated on screen, because the examination is handwritten and conjunct formation only goes wrong on paper. Typed practice hides the exact faults that cost marks.

whyPoints.title: Straight answers about school staffing

faqs.question: My child speaks Hindi fluently but scored 4. How is that possible?
faqs.answer: Because Hindi B is marked on written production in Devanagari, comprehension of unseen material and developed oral discussion, and conversational fluency contributes meaningfully to only part of that. A typical marked task from a fluent Dubai speaker carries matra errors, conjunct consonants broken into separate letters, English vocabulary inserted where formal Hindi was required, and a register borrowed from family conversation. None of those are Hindi problems in the ordinary sense; they are an untaught written system. The useful step is a short handwritten task marked with faults classified, because it usually reveals three or four repeating problems rather than a general weakness, and three or four problems close in a term.

faqs.question: Should a strong Hindi reader take Hindi A literature instead of Hindi B?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it is worth asking in Year 11 rather than Year 13. Hindi A: literature sits in Group 1 and is assessed on literary analysis in Hindi, while Hindi B sits in Group 2 and assesses language acquisition. A student who reads Hindi novels and can discuss how a text is written is often under-stretched in Hindi B, where they may score well without learning much, and they have spent a Group 1 slot they could have used differently. The test is not fluency but analysis: can the student say something about how a passage is constructed, in Hindi? The IB coordinator decides placement.

faqs.question: Which matra and script errors cost the most marks in Hindi B writing?
faqs.answer: Short and long vowel matras cause the most damage, because getting them wrong can change the word and the examiner marks what is on the page. Conjunct consonants come next: learners who acquired clusters by sight often break a ligature into two letters when writing by hand. After those, the recurring faults are the nukta omitted from borrowed vocabulary, anusvara and chandrabindu used interchangeably, and a broken shirorekha. All of them respond to paired word lists and dictation within a few weeks, which is why classified marking matters more than general correction.

faqs.question: Why does formal Hindi matter if my child communicates well?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 1 asks for a defined text type written for a stated audience, and the criteria reward register as well as accuracy. A formal letter to a principal that opens in the tone of a message to a cousin has lost marks on conceptual understanding before the grammar is assessed. Formal Hindi uses vocabulary and verb forms that family conversation does not, so it has to be built deliberately as a second vocabulary: paired lists with the spoken word on one side and the formal equivalent on the other. Text-type openings and closings are fixed furniture and can be learned in a fortnight, which makes this one of the cheapest grade gains available.

faqs.question: Does Hindi B at Higher Level really require reading two books?
faqs.answer: Yes. Higher Level candidates study two literary works, and the individual oral starts from an extract taken from one of them, followed by discussion of the works and the themes. Summaries do not survive follow-up questions, because an extract connects to the rest of the text and a teacher can ask about that connection. The practical problem in Dubai is that no Diploma timetable contains a reading period, so the reading has to be scheduled into evenings and holidays in dated blocks. Ask the teacher for the two titles early; that single piece of information drives the whole Higher Level plan.

faqs.question: Can my child self-teach Hindi B if the school does not offer it?
faqs.answer: Not as a Language B course. The IB's school-supported self-taught arrangement applies to a Language A literature course at Standard Level, not to Language B, so a student whose school cannot staff Hindi B cannot study it independently and sit those papers. A sufficiently literate student may be able to take Hindi A: literature at Standard Level on that self-taught basis instead, which satisfies a different subject group and changes the whole combination. Confirm the current position with your school's IB coordinator in writing, because IB regulations are updated and a tutoring site is not an authority on your entry.

faqs.question: How does CBSE Hindi differ from IB Hindi B in practice?
faqs.answer: The knowledge overlaps and the examination behaviour does not. Indian-curriculum Hindi largely rewards learned material: questions attach to studied chapters, formats repeat, and thorough coverage pays. IB Hindi B asks for responses to texts nobody has seen, writing to a brief that names an audience and a purpose, and comprehension of a recording played once. A student who has been rewarded for coverage finds that disorienting. The retraining is four habits: read the brief as instructions, plan before writing, search a text rather than recall it, and keep going when a recording moves past an unknown word.

faqs.question: Do you provide a Hindi tutor who comes to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. Hindi B support for Dubai families is delivered one-to-one over live video, with handwritten work photographed and annotated on screen so the tutor marks the same page the student wrote. For this subject the online route is often the only realistic one, because a school that cannot timetable Hindi B is unlikely to have a Hindi B specialist living in the next community, and matching online removes distance from the decision entirely.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fix written Devanagari accuracy?
faqs.answer: For a fluent speaker with three or four recurring faults, expect visible movement in six to eight weeks of weekly marked tasks and daily short drills, and a stable improvement over a term. The reason it is comparatively fast is that these faults are mechanical and finite: a fixed list of frequent conjuncts, a fixed set of matra pairs, a short list of nukta words. The reason it is not instant is that handwriting habits are motor habits and need repetition rather than understanding. Nobody can promise a grade from this, but of all the problems in this subject it is the most tractable.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around double-shift school timings in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they often have to. Several of the large Indian-curriculum schools in the older Dubai clusters run shifted timetables, and siblings in the same household can be on different ones, which makes a single fixed family slot impossible. Online sessions can sit wherever the gap actually is, including early morning before a late shift or 19:00 after an early one. During Ramadan most families shift to post-Iftar times. What needs protecting is the weekly cycle of task, marking and rewrite rather than a particular hour on a particular day.

faqs.question: Will a tutor correct my child's Hindi writing before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: A tutor marks it, classifies each script and register fault, explains the rule behind each one and sets a rewrite. A tutor does not supply Hindi sentences, rewrite a draft to a standard the student could not reach, or rehearse a memorised oral. The IB treats supplied content as malpractice and the penalty falls on the candidate. The stricter line is also the effective one: a student handed a corrected sentence learns nothing measurable, while a student who has to retrieve the right matra themselves is doing the act that lowers the fault count.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough for Hindi B?
faqs.answer: For script and register rebuilding, yes, provided the student writes a task between sessions. The cycle is task, classified marking, drilling, rewrite, and that cycle needs a week of space. Higher Level students in the term before the oral often add a second shorter session, because extract work and accuracy drilling compete badly for the same hour. Students whose accuracy is acceptable and whose listening score is not are usually better served by one session plus independent listening volume, since listening improves with hours of exposure rather than with explanation.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools offer Hindi in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: It varies by year and by staffing, so the course booklet and the IB coordinator at your own school are the only dependable source. Broadly, Hindi appears more often in Group 2 where a school has a large Indian-curriculum population alongside an IB stream, which in Dubai means the older Bur Dubai and Al Quoz corridors and some of the larger group schools. Newer or smaller Diploma cohorts frequently cannot staff it. If the answer is no, the options are a different Group 2 language or, for a literate student, a Group 1 Hindi literature route, and both of those need the coordinator's confirmation.

faqs.question: Do tutors in the UAE need to be licensed to teach my child privately?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published.

faqs.question: What if no Hindi B tutor is available when we get in touch?
faqs.answer: We say so with a timeframe rather than placing a general Hindi speaker and hoping the syllabus knowledge turns out to be there. Hindi B is a narrow specialism and in a given fortnight the pool may be fully committed, particularly at Higher Level where the literary works are involved. The alternatives we would put to a family are a short wait for a named tutor, a Standard Level specialist for the components that do not depend on the works, or a focused block on whichever component is most urgent. Which is sensible depends on how close the school's oral window sits.

Book the free trial lesson, one per family and no card details required. From there a term's plan either makes sense to you or it does not, and you will be judging it on marked evidence rather than on a promise.

intro.heading: Why a city full of Hindi speakers still has a Hindi B problem
paragraphs: Dubai has no shortage of people who speak excellent Hindi. The Indian curriculum accounted for 26 per cent of private-school enrolment in the emirate in 2024-25, inside a sector of 387,441 students across 227 schools and 17 different curricula. A family looking for someone to converse with their child in Hindi has an abundant market and can buy at the bottom of the published rate band, around AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. That is not the problem a Hindi B family actually has.

The problem is that most Hindi B candidates in this city are not learning Hindi. They already speak it, often daily at home, and they are losing marks on things fluency does not touch: reading Devanagari at exam speed, choosing between formal and informal address consistently, producing the text type a task demanded rather than the content it suggested, and writing with matra accuracy that a lifetime of speaking never required. Those are literacy and register problems, and the tutor who can diagnose them is in the same scarce tier as any other IB language specialist, at AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and above.

That gap between abundant supply and scarce skill is the whole economics of Hindi B in Dubai, and it explains the quotes families find confusing. A relative, a neighbour or a conversation tutor will charge very little and will genuinely help a weaker speaker. For a home-fluent student, those hours buy almost nothing, because the thing costing marks is not spoken Hindi. Paying AED 100 an hour for the wrong work is more expensive than paying AED 300 for the right work, and families discover this somewhere around the first mock.

There is a second decision sitting underneath the cost question, and it is worth settling before any money moves. Hindi is available in the Diploma as a Group 2 language acquisition course and also as a Language A literature course, including as a school-supported self-taught option at Standard Level in some schools. A genuinely home-fluent student in Hindi B may be in a course that cannot reward what they can already do. Confirm the options with your child's IB coordinator, because the right course choice changes the tutoring bill far more than any negotiation over an hourly rate.

Everything below is specific to this market: the three Hindi B student profiles and what each actually costs, why script literacy is the hidden expense for a fluent speaker, the course-fit question in detail, where Paper 1 marks go in Hindi, what KHDA's mandatory Arabic requirement does to an Indian-curriculum family's timetable and budget, and a term-by-term plan with the questions that reliably cut a quote. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Hindi B is a Group 2 language acquisition course at Standard and Higher Level. programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Hindi B sets inside IB schools are often small while the surrounding community is overwhelmingly Hindi-speaking, which produces an odd classroom: strong speakers with widely differing literacy. programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Hindi runs in phases, and the phase a student reaches by Year 11 depends mostly on reading. A student who read Devanagari texts regularly through MYP arrives in DP1 ready for Higher Level; one who spoke Hindi at home and read it rarely arrives fluent and slow on the page.

The result is a student whose spoken Hindi is native and whose written Hindi stopped developing in Year 7, and no transcript records that split.

programmes.name: Moving from an Indian-curriculum school into the Diploma
programmes.description: A student arriving from CBSE or ICSE has usually studied Hindi as a formal school subject with grammar instruction and set texts. programmes.countryNote: This is one of the most common transitions in Dubai and it needs the shortest, most targeted tutoring of any Hindi B profile. Six to ten sessions on IB text types and criteria converts existing Hindi into IB marks. Paying for two years of general Hindi support in this case is money spent on something the student already has.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students meet Hindi through the language development core requirement rather than as an examined Group 2 subject. There is no Paper 1 and no individual oral; the requirement is documented development over time, recorded as a portfolio.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools run the CP, and families often reach the language development requirement unclear about what counts as evidence. Support here is short and inexpensive relative to a two-year Diploma engagement, and it should end once the portfolio is credible.

sections.heading: What you are actually buying, and what it costs in Dubai
paragraphs: Published market rates in this city, read from provider rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table in October 2026, run from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour at the budget end, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified language teacher working online, AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB-experienced specialist, and AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the fee. Those bands are the market and not an IB Gram price list.

For Hindi specifically, the interesting feature is how differently the supply sits across those tiers. The bottom tier is unusually deep here, because Dubai has a very large Hindi-speaking population and conversation capability is abundant. The top tier is no deeper than it is for French or German, because knowing how a Paper 1 task is marked against language, message and conceptual understanding is a professional skill rather than a linguistic one. So the spread you will be quoted for Hindi is wider than for any other Diploma language in this city, and the cheap end is genuinely cheap.

That makes the key question not how much but what for. The table below separates the kinds of hour, what each produces, and what it cannot do however many of them you buy. The right-hand column is the one families most need, because the commonest expensive mistake in Hindi B is buying twenty hours of the cheapest product for a problem that product cannot touch.

One structural point about our own position: IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages, because the rate depends on the match and on which of the three profiles applies. What we publish is the market with its sources, so that any quote, including ours, can be checked against it. The first lesson is free, one per student, with no card details taken, and the rate is agreed in writing afterwards.

sections.heading: Three Hindi B profiles, three different bills
paragraphs: Almost every Hindi B enquiry from Dubai falls into one of three profiles, and the sensible spend differs by a factor of four between them. Establishing which one applies takes a single diagnostic session, and getting it wrong is the main reason families here feel they have spent money without result.

The home-fluent student is the largest group. They speak Hindi daily, read Devanagari slowly, and write with matra errors that never mattered in speech. Their work is literacy and register, eight to twelve focused sessions, and it is finished rather than ongoing. They do not need weekly tutoring for two years, and a provider who sells them that is selling comfort.

The curriculum transfer is the cheapest to help. A student arriving from CBSE or ICSE has formal Hindi instruction behind them, including grammar and set texts, and lacks only the IB's framing: text types, the three Paper 1 criteria, audience and purpose as marked features, and the shape of the individual oral. Six to ten sessions converts what they already have into marks. This is the profile most often mis-sold a two-year plan.

The genuine learner is the smallest group in Dubai and the most expensive: a student with limited Hindi at home taking the subject anyway, often for timetable reasons. They need what any language learner needs, which is volume over time, one session a week across two years, and the cheapest conversation hours have real value for them precisely because fluency is the gap. sections.heading: Script literacy: the cost a fluent speaker never expects
paragraphs: A student who has spoken Hindi since infancy can be functionally slow at reading it, and the two facts sit together comfortably until an exam applies a clock. Reading speed is the single most under-diagnosed issue in Hindi B in this city, because nobody checks it. A parent hears fluent Hindi at dinner and reasonably concludes the subject is safe.

The symptoms are specific. A student reads a short text accurately but at perhaps half the speed required to finish the reading paper with time to check. They write confidently and place matras inconsistently, because the vowel marks were never needed in speech. They confuse similar consonant forms under time pressure. And in listening they perform well, which disguises the reading problem further, since both sit inside the same Paper 2.

The work is measurable, which is what makes it worth paying specialist rates for. Time a short passage at the start, record the figure, and re-time every third session on comparable material. Keep a written log of matra and spelling errors so the pattern is visible rather than anecdotal. Within eight to twelve sessions reading speed typically moves enough to change the reading paper, and the engagement can honestly end, which is rare in tutoring and should be the stated plan from the beginning.

This is also the clearest case against the cheapest hours. A conversation tutor will not time a passage, will not log matra errors and has no reason to, because conversation is the product. The AED 100 difference between a conversation hour and a specialist hour buys a measurement, and without the measurement nobody, including the student, can tell whether the problem exists.

Log matra and spelling errors so the pattern is visible, not anecdotal

sections.heading: Hindi B or Hindi as a Language A: the question that changes the bill
paragraphs: Before buying hours, settle the course. Hindi appears in the Diploma both as a Group 2 language acquisition subject and as a Language A literature course, and in some schools Language A literature can be taken at Standard Level as a school-supported self-taught option. Which of those a home-fluent student should be in is a decision for your child and their IB coordinator, and it has a larger effect on two years of spending than any rate negotiation.

The argument for asking the question is simple. A genuinely home-fluent student in a language acquisition course is working inside a ceiling built for learners, and the work that gains them marks is literacy and criteria rather than language. Some students are much better served by a literature course that assesses what they can actually do with the language, and some are not, particularly if their reading speed is the very thing that is weak. Nobody can answer it from a webpage, which is precisely why it should be a conversation with the school rather than an assumption.

What a tutor can honestly contribute is evidence for that conversation: a timed reading figure, a marked written task with criterion scores, and an assessment of whether the student can discuss a text rather than summarise it. Bring those to the coordinator and the discussion becomes concrete. Arriving with an opinion and no evidence usually ends with the status quo.

Treat anyone who answers this question instantly with caution, in either direction. A provider who recommends the more expensive option within five minutes of meeting your child has not assessed anything, and a provider who refuses to discuss it at all is avoiding the only decision on this page that might reduce what you spend. Confirm what your child's school actually offers, because self-taught options are school-dependent and not universally available.

sections.heading: Where Paper 1 marks go in Hindi, and why register does the damage
paragraphs: Paper 1 asks for a written task that names a text type, an audience and a purpose. In the current guide it is marked on language, message and conceptual understanding, carrying twelve, twelve and six marks; confirm the allocations against your child's subject guide. The consequence is that fewer than half the marks are grammar and vocabulary, and a fluent Hindi speaker can lose the rest without noticing.

Register is where it happens. Hindi marks social relationship grammatically, and a student writing to an unfamiliar adult, a public audience and a close friend must handle each differently and consistently. The commonest script error is drift: a task opens formally and slides into the register the student uses at home halfway down the page. Spoken fluency actively encourages that slide, because in conversation the register is set by the person in front of you rather than by a brief on a page.

Text types do the rest of the damage, and they are the same conventions any Diploma language candidate has to learn. A letter needs its greeting and sign-off, an article needs a headline and a reader, a speech needs an audience addressed out loud, a diary entry needs a voice. A student who has written each one once with criterion feedback stops losing those marks permanently. One text type per session is the most efficient use of a Hindi B hour for a fluent speaker, and it is work that finishes.

The teaching cycle is three tasks: a baseline marked across all three criteria, a targeted task testing the weakest one, and a retention check on a task that is not about it. A gain that survives inattention is a gain. Families should expect to see all three scripts together with the criterion scores, rather than a verbal report that the student is doing better.
bullets: Roughly 12, 12 and 6 marks across language, message and conceptual understanding
Register drift mid-task is the signature error of a fluent speaker
One text type per session, written and marked, is the efficient pattern
Three-task cycle: baseline, targeted task, retention check

sections.heading: The mandatory Arabic timetable, and what it does to your budget
paragraphs: An Indian-curriculum family in Dubai budgeting for Hindi support is usually budgeting for Arabic support in the same term, and the reason is regulatory rather than academic. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The detail matters for planning. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

Two practical consequences follow. The first is competition for evenings: a student carrying Hindi B, the mandatory Arabic stream and six Diploma subjects has fewer genuinely free slots than the week appears to offer, so a Hindi plan that assumes two sessions a week is often a plan that will not hold. The second is that the content restriction on mandatory subjects limits what any tutor can legitimately offer for the Arabic stream, which is worth knowing before paying anybody for it.

sections.heading: A term-by-term plan, and the questions that cut a quote
paragraphs: Because most Hindi B work is a block rather than a subscription, the plan looks different from other language subjects. For a home-fluent student the shape is a script and register block early in DP1, an IB text-type block alongside it, light maintenance through the middle, a Higher Level literature block if applicable, and an oral rehearsal block before the school records. Total engagement is often twenty to thirty sessions across two years rather than eighty.

The timing that matters most is the oral window. Individual orals are internally conducted and recorded inside a window each school sets, and those windows cluster across the emirate, so language specialists are scarcest and most expensive in the same few weeks. Book that block before the school publishes its dates. At Higher Level the literature reading has to be finished before extract discussion can start, which makes the DP1 summer the natural window because reading travels and grammar teaching does not.

Four questions reliably reduce a Hindi B quote or improve what it contains. Ask whether marking happens inside or outside the paid hour, since that single answer can change the effective rate by a third. Ask what the engagement's end point is and what measure defines it. Ask whether the tutor has read the two literary works your child's school chose, if Higher Level applies. And ask whether the quoted AED figure includes VAT, in writing, which is a question for the provider rather than something a tutoring page should rule on.

Ask about the permit too. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system with a two-working-day completion time on MoHRE's own service page. Because there is no fee, nobody charging below market has saved money by skipping it. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is unverified.
bullets: Is marking inside or outside the paid hour?
What is the end point of this engagement, and what measure defines it?

Does the AED figure include VAT, confirmed in writing?
