sections.heading: What we will not do, and what nobody can promise
paragraphs: A tutor can set tasks, mark them against the published criteria, annotate your child's own writing, time reading passages, log errors, record oral rehearsals and supply model texts clearly labelled as the tutor's own work for study. A tutor cannot write or rewrite anything your child submits as their own, cannot draft an Extended Essay or TOK essay, and has no role in the recorded individual oral itself. IB academic honesty rules place the consequences of malpractice on the student, which is why any offer of help with submitted work hands your family the risk while the provider keeps the fee.

Nobody can promise a grade in Hindi B, and we will not. Any provider quoting a percentage of students who improved should be asked, on the same page as the claim, for the number of students, the dates and the method. Self-published star ratings in this market have been found contradicting themselves inside a single page. What can be promised is specific: a number of marked tasks, a reading speed measured and re-measured, a recorded rehearsal, and a written note of where the marks are going.

On equivalency, which Dubai families often raise in the same conversation: for the British track the Ministry of Education requirements are documented, namely five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No IB points threshold has been published that we can verify on the ministry's own pages, so we state none. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees; it runs through the official channel.

Our limits, plainly: IB Gram holds no endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge, operates no premises in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, and does not offer home visits in the Emirates. Hindi B for Dubai families is taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the first lesson free, one per student, and no card details taken.

process.title: Say which profile fits, or let the diagnostic decide
process.description: Tell us whether Hindi is spoken at home, how much Devanagari reading your child has done, and whether they are arriving from an Indian-curriculum school. Those three answers usually identify the profile, and the profile determines whether you need ten sessions or two years.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the reading timed
process.description: One lesson at no charge, one per student, with no card details taken. The tutor times a short reading passage and writes the figure down, sets eighty words of writing, and checks register handling. You get a plain statement of which profile applies and what the block should contain.

process.title: Agree the block and its end point
process.description: Scope in writing: how many sessions, what measure defines completion, whether marking sits inside or outside the hour, and whether Higher Level literature runs as a separate costed block. A Hindi B engagement that cannot describe its own end point is a subscription rather than a plan.

process.title: Measure, mark, re-measure
process.description: Reading speed re-timed every third session on comparable material, a matra and spelling log kept in writing, and one criterion-scored written task a week annotated against language, message and conceptual understanding. Oral rehearsals recorded on unseen stimuli.

process.title: Finish, or say why not
process.description: When the measures move, the block ends and we say so rather than proposing more hours. If they have not moved in six weeks, the method or the tutor changes. Either way you get a short written note with the numbers in it and no predicted grade.

whyPoints.title: We price the work, not the language
whyPoints.description: Hindi conversation is abundant and cheap in Dubai, and for a home-fluent student it is the wrong product at any price. We say which kind of hour your child needs before quoting one, including when the cheapest option is genuinely the right one.

whyPoints.title: Reading speed actually measured
whyPoints.description: A timed passage in the first session, written down, and re-timed every third session. It is the most under-diagnosed issue in Hindi B in this city, and nobody can tell whether it is the problem until somebody puts a clock on it.

whyPoints.title: Blocks with end points
whyPoints.description: Most Hindi B work finishes. A script and register block runs eight to twelve sessions, an IB conversion block for a curriculum transfer six to ten. We state the end point and the measure up front rather than rolling into a standing monthly charge.

whyPoints.title: The course-fit question raised early
whyPoints.description: Hindi exists in the Diploma as a language acquisition subject and as a Language A literature course, with self-taught options in some schools. We bring evidence to that conversation with your coordinator rather than an opinion, and it can reduce two years of spending.

whyPoints.title: Criterion marking, not a mark out of ten
whyPoints.description: Fewer than half the marks in a written task are grammar and vocabulary. Scoring language, message and conceptual understanding separately is what reveals that a fluent speaker is losing marks on register drift rather than on Hindi.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not

faqs.question: Why would a child who speaks Hindi at home need a Hindi B tutor?
faqs.answer: Because spoken fluency and examined literacy are different things. The typical Dubai candidate speaks Hindi daily, reads Devanagari at roughly half the speed the reading paper requires, places matras inconsistently because speech never needed them, and lets written register drift from formal to familiar halfway down a task. None of that is visible in conversation and all of it costs marks. The useful first step is to time a short reading passage and mark one written task against the criteria, which takes under an hour and settles whether there is a problem at all.

faqs.question: How much should I pay for Hindi tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which kind of hour you need. Published market rates read in October 2026 run AED 45 to AED 150 for conversation and homework support, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified teacher doing script and register work, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB-experienced specialist marking against the criteria. Hindi has an unusually deep supply at the bottom tier in this city because so many people speak it well, and no deeper supply than any other language at the top tier, because criterion marking is a professional skill rather than a linguistic one.

faqs.question: Is cheap Hindi conversation tutoring a false economy?
faqs.answer: For a home-fluent student, yes. Twenty hours of conversation at AED 100 will not change Devanagari reading speed, matra accuracy or text-type marks, because none of those is a speaking problem, and the family ends up AED 2,000 down with the same mock result. For a student who genuinely lacks fluency, the same hours are good value and the cheapest effective product available. The question is never whether the rate is low but whether the hour addresses the gap, and one diagnostic session answers that before any money moves.

faqs.question: Should a home-fluent student take Hindi B or Hindi as a Language A?
faqs.answer: That is a decision for your child and their IB coordinator, and it is worth raising early because it affects two years of spending more than any rate negotiation. Hindi appears in the Diploma both as a Group 2 language acquisition course and as a Language A literature course, with school-supported self-taught Standard Level options available in some schools. A tutor's useful contribution is evidence for the conversation: a timed reading figure, a marked task with criterion scores, and an assessment of whether the student can discuss a text rather than summarise it. Confirm what your school actually offers.

faqs.question: What is the fastest way to improve Devanagari reading speed?
faqs.answer: Timed reading on comparable material, repeated often and recorded. Time a short passage in the first session and write the number down, read short texts daily rather than long ones weekly, and re-time every third session on material of similar difficulty so the figure means something. Keep a written log of the consonant forms and matras that cause hesitation, because the list is usually short and specific rather than general. Most home-fluent students see a meaningful shift inside eight to twelve sessions, at which point the block can honestly end.

faqs.question: My child is moving from CBSE into the IB Diploma. How much Hindi support is needed?
faqs.answer: Usually six to ten sessions, which makes this the cheapest profile in the subject. A CBSE or ICSE student arrives with formal grammar instruction and set-text experience behind them, so they already have the Hindi. What they lack is the IB's framing: the text types, the three Paper 1 criteria, the fact that audience and purpose carry marks of their own, and the format of the individual oral. One text type per session with criterion feedback converts existing ability into marks. Be sceptical of a two-year plan sold to this profile.

faqs.question: What does register drift mean in a Hindi written task?
faqs.answer: It means a task that opens in the register the brief required and slides into the one the student uses at home. Hindi marks social relationship grammatically, so writing to an unfamiliar adult, a public audience and a close friend each demand different and consistent choices. Spoken fluency encourages the slide, because in conversation register is set by the person in front of you rather than by a brief on a page. It is the signature error of a fluent candidate and it responds quickly to paired tasks: the same content written twice, once formally and once informally.

faqs.question: How many sessions does Hindi B need in total?
faqs.answer: For a home-fluent student, often twenty to thirty across the two years rather than eighty: a script and register block early, an IB text-type block alongside it, light maintenance, a Higher Level literature block if it applies, and an oral rehearsal block before the school records. For a student with limited Hindi at home who is taking the subject anyway, it is a conventional weekly engagement across both years, because the gap is fluency and fluency is volume over time. The profile decides, and a diagnostic session establishes the profile.

faqs.question: Does KHDA's Arabic requirement affect a Hindi B student's timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth planning around. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in the first-language Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies streams. For a family budgeting tutoring, the practical effect is fewer genuinely free evenings than the week appears to offer, so a plan assuming two Hindi sessions a week often will not hold.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the mandatory Arabic stream as well?
faqs.answer: Within limits that are worth understanding first. For the mandatory UAE subjects, KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, and schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. That constrains what any outside tutor can legitimately offer for the mandatory stream, as distinct from Arabic taken as a Diploma Group 2 subject, where ordinary tutoring applies. Ask any provider to be explicit about which of the two they are proposing to teach.

faqs.question: When should Higher Level Hindi literature work be booked?
faqs.answer: Early, and as a separately costed block. Higher Level requires two literary works chosen by the school, and the Higher Level oral is built on an extract from one of them, so the reading has to be finished before extract discussion can begin. The DP1 summer is the natural window because reading travels in a way that teaching does not. Ask any prospective tutor which two works your child's school selected before agreeing a rate, since a tutor working from different texts is rehearsing the wrong oral at the same price.

faqs.question: What should I ask to bring a Hindi B quote down?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Is marking inside or outside the paid hour, because that single answer can change the effective rate by a third. What is the end point of this engagement and what measure defines it, because most Hindi B work should finish rather than roll on. Has the tutor read the two literary works the school chose, if Higher Level applies. And does the quoted AED figure include VAT, confirmed in writing. A provider who answers all four clearly is usually worth more than one who is cheaper.

faqs.question: Do Hindi tutors in Dubai need a permit, and does it cost them anything?
faqs.answer: They need one and it costs nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time listed on MoHRE's own service page. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount quoted to you as unverified.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Hindi tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Hindi B for Dubai families is taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market alternative is priced on this page for comparison at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the fee. For this subject the gain from teaching online is not mainly price: it is that the match can be made on criterion-marking experience rather than on which fluent Hindi speaker is willing to drive to your community at five o'clock.

dubai/ib-dp-hindi-b-tutor.closingHeading: Time the reading before you buy the hours
dubai/ib-dp-hindi-b-tutor.closingBody: Hindi B in Dubai is the rare subject where the cheapest tutoring is abundant and often beside the point. Before paying anybody, have someone time a short Devanagari passage, mark one written task against the three criteria, and tell you which of the three profiles your child fits. Book the free trial lesson, one per student with no card details taken, and that is what the hour will do. You will get the numbers in writing, the market bands above to check any quote against, and a stated end point for the block. Nobody can promise a grade in Hindi B, and anyone quoting an improvement percentage should be asked for the sample size, the dates and the method.

dubai/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma History: the four-question source paper, two world history topics, the Higher Level regional option and the historical investigation. Each one quotes a rate before the first session, and the first session is a free trial you can walk away from.

intro.heading: What an IB DP History home tutor in Dubai actually costs, and what the fee is paying for
paragraphs: Families searching for an IB DP history home tutor in Dubai are usually asking two questions at once: what does this cost, and is it worth paying for a subject the child is already passing. The honest answer to the first is a range rather than a price. Rates read from Dubai providers' own public pages in October 2026 start near AED 33 an hour for a shared online slot and reach AED 650 an hour for a named premium tutor, with qualified subject specialists clustering between AED 200 and AED 450. Diploma History sits towards the top of that cluster at Higher Level, for one reason: Paper 3 is a regional option that only a minority of tutors have taught through to a final grade.

An hourly figure is buying three separate things, and most quotes do not separate them. The first is the live hour itself. The second is the marking that happens outside it, which for History means reading a 15-mark essay properly against the markbands and writing back something more useful than a tick. The third is subject knowledge narrow enough to matter: a tutor who knows that Question 2 on Paper 1 rewards origin and purpose, not a complaint about bias, saves a student four marks a paper. A rate that looks low usually has the second and third items removed from it.

The in-home figure in Dubai carries a cost nobody puts on the invoice. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. The gap between that and the online band is travel, and travel is also what shrinks your choice of tutor. A family in Mirdif choosing from the tutors willing to drive to Mirdif at 5pm on a Tuesday is choosing from a much shorter list than a family choosing from every Diploma History specialist available at that hour.

IB Gram works the other way round. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around school hours and prayer times. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is a deliberate trade: your child gets a History specialist who has taught the Americas or Europe regional option, rather than whoever happens to live twenty minutes away. The trial lesson is free, with no card needed, and no package has to be bought before it.

The rest of this page is built around the number. There is a table of what the Dubai market charges and who publishes each figure, a breakdown of what changes a quote, the assessment structure that explains why Higher Level costs more, the three sections of the historical investigation, the Diploma year counted backwards from the May session, the line a tutor may not cross on coursework, and the permit question every Dubai parent should ask before paying anyone.

dubai/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.programmesIntro: History reaches IB Gram's tutors through three IB routes, and the teaching is different in each. A Middle Years student is building the habit of using evidence; a Diploma candidate is being marked against published markbands; a Career-related student is sitting the same Diploma History course with less timetabled contact.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme History
programmes.description: The course every search for a DP History tutor is about. Students sit a one-hour source paper on one prescribed subject, a 90-minute paper covering two of twelve world history topics, and at Higher Level a 150-minute paper on one of four regional options. Alongside the papers sits the historical investigation, 2,200 words, marked out of 25 by the school and moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB Diploma cohort is a minority of a very large private sector: KHDA recorded 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with the IB accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment against 37 per cent for UK curricula. One practical effect is that a Diploma History class in Dubai is often small, so a student who falls behind on Paper 3 has few classmates to compare notes with.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Individuals and Societies
programmes.description: The feeder course. MYP History is assessed on four criteria rather than markbands, which means strong MYP writing can still be the wrong shape for Diploma Paper 2. The habits worth fixing early are using a source rather than describing it, and answering a command term instead of writing everything known about a period.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the MYP straight into the Diploma, so students arrive in DP1 having never sat a timed essay under exam conditions. Others switch their cohort to IGCSE at 14 and then into the Diploma, which produces the opposite gap: confident timed writing, no experience of criterion-referenced coursework. Sessions start by identifying which of the two gaps a Dubai student has.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme with Diploma History
programmes.description: Career-related students take at least two Diploma courses, and History is a common choice alongside business or sports-related pathways. The syllabus and the markbands are identical to the Diploma version, so the teaching is the same. What differs is timetabled contact time, which is often lower, and the reflective project running in parallel.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a smaller number of schools offering the Career-related Programme than the Diploma, and a Career-related History student can end up as the only one in a school taking that subject. That is the clearest case for one-to-one teaching: there is no class to be taught alongside, and the published markbands are unforgiving about essays written without feedback.

dubai/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Diploma History is not one syllabus, it is a set of routes a school picks from. These are the ones Dubai schools most often teach, and the ones IB Gram's History tutors cover. Check your child's choices against the school's own course outline before booking, because Paper 1 and Paper 3 are not interchangeable between schools.

subjects.name: Paper 1: The move to global war
subjects.description: Japanese expansion in East Asia 1931-41 and Italian and German expansion 1933-40. The most commonly taught prescribed subject in Dubai. Source work centres on Manchuria, Abyssinia and the Rhineland, where students confuse the chronology of League of Nations responses and lose the Question 4 judgement mark.

subjects.name: Paper 1: Rights and protest
subjects.description: The civil rights movement in the United States 1954-65 and apartheid South Africa 1948-64. Rich in photographs and speeches, which is where students over-trust a visual source. Value and limitations marks come from naming the photographer's purpose, not from observing that a photograph is staged.

subjects.name: Paper 1: Conflict and intervention
subjects.description: Rwanda 1990-98 and Kosovo 1989-2002. The newest of the five prescribed subjects and the one with the thinnest textbook coverage, so a tutor's own source selection matters more here. Students struggle to separate causes of conflict from the stated justifications for intervention.

subjects.name: Paper 2: Authoritarian states (20th century)
subjects.description: Emergence, consolidation and the aims and results of domestic policy, examined across two regions. The most popular Paper 2 topic worldwide and the one most often answered badly, because students write a narrative of one leader instead of a comparative argument answering the command term.

subjects.name: Paper 2: Causes and effects of 20th-century wars
subjects.description: Long and short-term causes, practices and effects, again across two regions. The trap is scale: an essay on the causes of the Second World War that stays in Europe cannot access the top markband, because the examiner is looking for two regions properly used, not mentioned.

subjects.name: Paper 2: The Cold War - superpower tensions and rivalries
subjects.description: Rivalry, mistrust and accord, leaders and nations, and Cold War crises. Chronologically huge and therefore the hardest to revise late. Sessions build a crisis-by-crisis grid with dates, actors and outcomes, because Paper 2 essays here fail on precision rather than argument.

subjects.name: Paper 2: Independence movements (1800-2000)
subjects.description: Origins and rise of independence movements, methods, and the challenges of newly independent states. Taught less often in Dubai, which means fewer revision resources and a stronger case for one-to-one teaching built on the school's own case studies.

subjects.name: Paper 3: History of Europe
subjects.description: One of four regional options, worth 35% of the Higher Level grade on its own. Three essays in 150 minutes from a wide choice of eighteen sections. Students arrive at this paper with less preparation than any other component because schools teach it in DP2.

subjects.name: Paper 3: History of the Americas
subjects.description: The regional option chosen by many Dubai schools with North American teaching staff. Same shape as the European option: three essays, 15 marks each, 150 minutes. Revision is manageable only if a student narrows to five or six sections and knows them in real depth.

subjects.name: Internal assessment: the historical investigation
subjects.description: A 2,200-word investigation on a question of the student's own choosing, in three sections: identification and evaluation of sources, the investigation itself, and a reflection. Marked out of 25 by the school, then moderated. Worth 25% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher Level.

dubai/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities, their Diploma schools, and what the commute does to a History session
dubai/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Dubai changes two things about tutoring: which Diploma schools are realistic, and what time a session can actually start. The notes below are about scheduling and school clusters, not about sending anyone to an address.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Served by Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and the Dubai Hills schools. Buses release late, so a 6pm start works better than 5pm for a DP2 student who also has a Paper 3 reading list to get through.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: The densest school cluster in the emirate, with both Diploma and A Level options within a few kilometres. History groups here are often large enough to be taught as a class, which makes one-to-one useful mainly for Paper 1 source technique.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Apartment-heavy, with families commuting into Media City and Internet City. Sessions land best between 7pm and 9pm once a parent is home, and a quiet room matters more than it does in a villa community.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Further from the Diploma cluster on the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor, so school runs are long and in-home tutoring here carries the heaviest travel premium in the market. Online removes that premium entirely.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Motor City
regions.note: Villa communities with established Diploma feeders nearby. Weekend mornings are genuinely viable here, which suits timed Paper 2 essay practice better than a weekday evening after seven hours of school.

regions.name: Deira, Al Garhoud and Festival City
regions.note: Older Dubai, with long-established private schools running both Indian and international curricula. Students switching from a CBSE background into Diploma History need extra work on argument structure rather than content recall.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Mostly apartments, with students bussed out to schools in Barsha, Nad Al Sheba or Jumeirah. Evening traffic on the Al Khail corridor is the practical reason many of these families book online rather than in-home sessions.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma History along the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor
schoolClusters.note: The schools most Dubai families mean when they say they want a Diploma History tutor. Several run the Middle Years Programme underneath the Diploma, so students reach DP1 with coursework experience but little timed essay practice.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma History in Jumeirah, Mirdif and the northern communities
schoolClusters.note: A second cluster, smaller and more spread out. Diploma History groups in these schools can be in single figures, which is why a student who misses two weeks of the regional option has very little to catch up against.

schoolClusters.city: Villa-community Diploma schools: Ranches, Hills and Meadows
schoolClusters.note: Schools serving the villa belt, several of which offer both the Diploma and A Levels, so a History student may be choosing between the two routes in Year 11 and needs the assessment difference explained before choosing.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges for Diploma History tuition
paragraphs: A Diploma History tutor in Dubai costs between AED 150 and AED 450 an hour at the qualified-specialist end of the market, with cheaper shared-online options below that and named premium tutors above it. Every figure in the table was read from the provider's own published page in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price: IB Gram quotes per match, after a free trial lesson, because a Standard Level student needing Paper 1 technique and a Higher Level student starting the Europe regional option are not buying the same hour.

Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. That is the single most useful thing to know before you ring anyone: a page that will not name a currency UAE families transact in is not going to name a rate either. The figures below are published, dated and attributable, and you should expect any tutor you contact to be equally specific before the first session rather than after it.

Read the monthly row carefully. An advertised AED 799 package for eight online sessions is close to AED 100 an hour, which sounds cheaper than everything above it until you check session length and whether marking is included. An AED 1,599 in-home package for four two-hour visits is AED 200 an hour, with travel folded in. The per-hour figure is the only comparable number, and working it out before you sign is worth more than any discount on offer.
bullets: Ask for the rate per 60 minutes, not per session, before the first lesson
Ask whether marking between sessions is included or billed separately
Ask whether the tutor has taught your child's exact Paper 1 and Paper 3 options
Ask what happens to unused hours if the match does not work

sections.heading: Six things that move a History tutoring quote in this emirate
paragraphs: The same tutor will quote two different numbers to two Dubai families in the same week, and the reasons are predictable. Level is the largest single factor. Higher Level History carries Paper 3, a 150-minute paper on one regional option worth 35% of the grade, and the pool of tutors who have taught a regional option through to a final grade is much smaller than the pool who can teach Paper 1 source skills. Scarcity sets that price, not prestige.

Proximity to the session is the second factor. A family booking in September for a May sitting is buying a weekly slot at a standard rate. A family booking eight weeks out is buying scarce evening hours in the busiest period of the tutoring year, and intensive blocks are quoted accordingly. The third is session length: a 90-minute slot usually costs less per hour than a 60-minute one, because the tutor's preparation and marking is spread over more teaching time.

The remaining three are worth asking about explicitly. Whether marking is included changes the real cost of an hour more than any headline rate. Whether the tutor teaches your child's exact options matters, because a History tutor who has taught Rights and protest but not The move to global war will spend your first three sessions learning the material. And in-home delivery adds a travel premium that varies by community: the same tutor charges a Mirdif family more than a Barsha family for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching. Online removes that line from the invoice.
bullets: Higher Level costs more because Paper 3 specialists are genuinely scarce

sections.heading: Paper 1: twenty-four marks, four questions, one hour
paragraphs: Paper 1 is the component where tutoring produces the fastest measurable change, because the four questions reward a technique rather than a body of knowledge. The paper gives four sources on a prescribed subject and asks four questions worth 3+2, 4, 6 and 9 marks, for 24 in total, in sixty minutes. A student who has learned the shape of each question can gain several marks within a handful of sessions without learning any new history at all.

The two questions that cost Dubai students most are the 4-mark value and limitations question and the 9-mark judgement. On the first, students write about bias in the abstract. The marks are in origin, purpose and content: who produced this, why, and what that does to its usefulness for the specific question asked. A speech given to rally supporters has a purpose that limits it as evidence of public opinion and makes it valuable as evidence of how a government wanted to be heard. That sentence is the mark.

The 9-mark question fails on time and coverage rather than on argument. It needs all four sources and some of the student's own knowledge, and it is routinely attempted with eleven minutes left and three sources used. The fix is mechanical: allocate on the mark weighting, roughly two and a half minutes per mark, and write the Question 4 plan before answering Question 3. Sessions run this to the clock until the allocation is automatic rather than intended.

sections.heading: Why Higher Level History costs more: how the grade is assembled
paragraphs: Standard Level and Higher Level History share Paper 1 and Paper 2 and the historical investigation. Higher Level adds Paper 3, and that single addition reorders everything. At Standard Level, Paper 2 is the biggest component at 45%, so the sensible tutoring priority is two world history topics taught to essay standard. At Higher Level, Paper 2 drops to 25% and Paper 3 arrives at 35%, which means the largest component of the grade is a paper most schools begin teaching in DP2.

That is the structural reason a Higher Level quote is higher. It is also the reason a Higher Level student who starts tutoring in February is in a worse position than a Standard Level student who starts at the same time. Three essays in 150 minutes on a regional option, chosen from eighteen sections, is not a technique problem that can be drilled in six weeks. It is a knowledge problem, and knowledge takes months.

The practical plan differs by level and is worth stating plainly to any tutor you speak to. A Standard Level student should be spending roughly half of session time on Paper 2 essay construction and most of the rest on Paper 1 technique, with the investigation handled in a short block. A Higher Level student should narrow Paper 3 to five or six sections early in DP2, learn those properly, and treat Paper 1 as the component to be polished in the final weeks because it responds to drilling faster than anything else.

sections.heading: The historical investigation: 2,200 words, three sections, twenty-five marks
paragraphs: The internal assessment is the component where a tutor's role has to be described precisely, because the rules are strict and the consequences of breaking them fall on the student. The investigation is a 2,200-word piece on a question the student chooses, in three sections: identification and evaluation of sources, the investigation itself, and a reflection on what doing the work revealed about the discipline. The school marks it out of 25 and the IB moderates.

Most lost marks are structural rather than historical. Section 1 asks for an evaluation of two sources using origin, purpose, value and limitation, and students instead summarise what the sources say. The investigation section needs an argument with evidence, not a chronology. The reflection is short and is routinely treated as an afterthought, when it is the easiest section to do well in because it asks a question the student can actually answer: what did researching this teach you about how historians work.

Question choice is the other half of the problem, and it happens before any writing. A question that cannot be answered with sources a student in Dubai can reach is a question that will produce a weak investigation however hard they work. Sessions test a question against real availability first: library access through the school, open archives, published collections. A tutor teaches that process, reads one draft and writes feedback against the published criteria. The investigation itself has to be the student's own work from the first word to the last, and no IB Gram tutor supplies finished coursework for a student to submit.
bullets: Section 1: two sources evaluated on origin, purpose, value and limitation
Section 2: an argued investigation, not a narrative of events
Section 3: a short reflection on the historian's method, worth easy marks
The 2,200-word limit excludes footnote citations but not quotations in the body
Test the question against sources that are genuinely reachable before writing

sections.heading: The Diploma History year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Nobody in this search publishes a calendar, and it is the single most useful thing a parent can be given. The table below counts backwards from the May session that Dubai schools sit, in relative terms rather than dates. That is deliberate. IB session and results dates in this project have not been confirmed against ibo.org, which blocks automated checking, so the only dates you should act on are the ones your school's IB coordinator gives you in writing.

Two deadlines on the list are set by your school rather than the IB, and they are the ones that bite. The internal deadline for the historical investigation usually sits around six months before the session, which means the work is being done in the same term as the heaviest content teaching for Paper 3. Families who treat the investigation as a DP2 problem discover that it collides with the only term available for learning the regional option.

The useful habit is to work from the table in reverse at the start of DP1 and mark two dates in a shared calendar: the school's investigation deadline and the week mock papers are sat. Everything else arranges itself around those two. A tutoring plan built this way costs less overall, because the expensive hours are the ones bought in a panic eight weeks before a paper. Ramadan falls inside the revision window in the current cycle, which shifts evening study later for many Dubai households and is worth planning for rather than discovering in week one.

One more entry belongs on any family's version of this table, and it is the enquiry upon results window after grades are published. A remark or a category-two enquiry has to be requested through the school within a fixed period, and the decision is usually made in a few rushed days in July when families are travelling. Ask the IB coordinator in DP2, not in July, what the school's internal cut-off is and what evidence it wants before it will submit one.

sections.heading: Where a History tutor has to stop: academic honesty in practice
paragraphs: This search returns at least one provider selling completed internal assessments. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring, it is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student rather than the seller. A candidate found to have submitted work that is not their own faces an IB malpractice investigation and can lose the Diploma. No price makes that a reasonable risk, and any page offering it should end your consideration of that provider.

The boundary itself is not vague once it is stated. A tutor may teach the skills a component needs, explain what the markbands reward, discuss a question the student has chosen, point towards the kinds of source that exist, read a draft the student has written, and give feedback in writing on what is weak and why. A tutor may not supply text for the student to use, rewrite paragraphs into a final form, or hand over an answer to be submitted.

The practical test a parent can apply is simple. Ask what the tutor sends back after reading a draft. Feedback that names criteria and asks questions is teaching. A returned document with new sentences in it is not, and a student who submits it has a problem that no grade improvement compensates for. IB Gram tutors work on the student's own writing, and the authorship declaration a candidate signs is one the student should be able to sign honestly.

The same boundary applies to materials. Published IB, Cambridge and Pearson papers, mark schemes and subject guides are referenced and linked to their official source rather than copied into a handout, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Generative tools sit in the same category: a student may use them to find reading, and may not use them to produce sentences that go into an assessed piece. Dubai schools increasingly ask candidates to log their research process, and a student who has been taught to keep that log has an easier conversation if the question is ever asked.
bullets: A tutor teaches technique, explains markbands and gives written feedback
A tutor never supplies text or finished coursework for submission
Ask to see what feedback on a draft actually looks like before booking
Published past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked, never copied out

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and checking a Dubai tutor is allowed to teach
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and most parents are never told this. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you as fact.

MoHRE's own service page is titled 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee, and states a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app and e-services system. That is the route to point any tutor towards, and the answer to the awkward question of whether yours holds one is simply to ask. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram is neither approved nor endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no page here should suggest otherwise.

Dubai's schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is a rule worth knowing before accepting a well-meant offer from inside the staff room.
bullets: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free and valid for two years
No fine amount is published for tutoring without a permit; treat any figure as unverified
KHDA inspects Dubai private schools from Outstanding to Very Weak
Ask any tutor directly whether they hold the MoHRE permit

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of a Dubai school-fee budget
paragraphs: A tutoring decision is made inside a household budget that is already carrying school fees, and the figure that matters is annual rather than hourly. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For families planning two years of Diploma support, that stability is the one fixed point in the calculation.

Work the arithmetic forwards rather than backwards. One weekly hour at the specialist band through a 36-week school year sits between roughly AED 7,200 and AED 16,200 across the year, depending on where in the band the tutor falls. Two hours a week doubles it. A short investigation clinic of four sessions is a one-off cost. A pre-session intensive block is a third line. Most Dubai families who get good value buy one weekly hour across DP1 and DP2 rather than a large block in the final term, because the cheaper hours are the early ones.

The supply question belongs in the same conversation. Diploma History specialists who have taught a specific regional option are not evenly available across every evening hour in Gulf Standard Time, and a page that pretends otherwise is hiding something. If no UAE-based specialist covers your child's exact option at the hour you need, IB Gram says so and offers the nearest alternative, which may be a tutor teaching from India on the same Gulf Standard Time slot. The rate is quoted before the trial, and nothing is booked until you have seen the teaching.
bullets: One weekly specialist hour across a 36-week year: roughly AED 7,200-16,200
KHDA confirmed no private-school fee increase for 2026-27 on 22 May 2026

process.title: Tell us the options, not just the subject
process.description: Diploma History is a set of routes. The useful first message names the prescribed subject for Paper 1, the two world history topics for Paper 2, the regional option if your child is at Higher Level, and the stage the historical investigation has reached. That one paragraph decides which tutors are a genuine match.

process.title: See the rate before the trial
process.description: IB Gram quotes per match rather than publishing a single price, because a Standard Level technique block and a two-year Higher Level plan are different pieces of work. The quote arrives with the proposed tutor and the proposed hour, in AED, per 60 minutes, with marking stated as included or not.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session at no cost, with no card details and no package attached. Watch for one thing in particular: does the tutor mark the student's actual writing in the session, or talk about history. The first moves a grade and the second is a lecture your child can get free on the internet.

process.title: Fix a weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: A repeating hour set around school pick-up, bus times and prayer times, with Ramadan timings adjusted when the session would otherwise sit across Iftar. The slot pauses for school exam weeks and holidays without being lost, because consistency across two Diploma years is what produces movement.

process.title: Review the evidence every six weeks
process.description: Marked Paper 1 questions, timed Paper 2 essays with band scores, and the state of the investigation, reviewed together. If the marks are not moving after six weeks of consistent work, the match or the plan changes. That review is the point at which a different tutor is offered rather than argued against.

whyPoints.title: The rate is named before you commit
whyPoints.description: Three of the six most visible pages in this search publish no price and two quote in US dollars. IB Gram quotes in AED, per 60 minutes, before the trial lesson, and states whether marking between sessions is included. You can compare that figure against the published market table on this page.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the option, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A History tutor who has taught Rights and protest is not interchangeable with one who has taught The move to global war, and a Paper 3 specialist in the Americas is not a Europe specialist. Matching happens at that level, which is why the first question asked is about options rather than grades.

whyPoints.title: Marking is where the grade moves
whyPoints.description: A 15-mark Paper 2 essay read properly against the markbands produces more improvement than an hour of content revision. Every weekly plan includes one marked piece of written work between sessions, with feedback that names the band and the reason, not a grade and a tick.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Competitors in this search sell completed internal assessments. IB Gram tutors teach the skills, explain the criteria, discuss the student's chosen question and give written feedback on a draft. No text is supplied for submission, because the risk of that falls entirely on your child.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed up front
whyPoints.description: Diploma History specialists for a specific regional option are not available in every evening hour. When no UAE-based tutor covers the exact option at the time you need, you are told, and offered the nearest alternative on the same Gulf Standard Time slot with the rate stated beforehand.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is online and the page says so
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The trade is deliberate: a specialist in your child's exact paper instead of whoever is within driving distance.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP History tutor in Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates in October 2026 run from about AED 33 an hour for shared online sessions to AED 650 for a named premium tutor. Qualified subject specialists cluster between AED 200 and AED 450, and in-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is priced in. Higher Level History sits towards the top of the specialist band because the Paper 3 regional option is taught by a smaller pool of tutors. Those are market figures read from providers' own pages, not IB Gram prices. IB Gram quotes per match in AED, per 60 minutes, before the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why does Higher Level History cost more per hour than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Because of Paper 3. Higher Level students sit a 150-minute paper on one regional option, writing three essays worth 15 marks each, and that paper alone is 35% of the grade. The pool of tutors who have taught a regional option through to a final grade is much smaller than the pool who can teach Paper 1 source technique, and scarcity sets the rate. Standard Level students sit Papers 1 and 2 and the investigation only, where Paper 2 is the largest component at 45%. The teaching plan is genuinely different, not just priced differently.

faqs.question: Is the Paper 3 regional option worth paying a specialist rate for?
faqs.answer: At Higher Level, yes, and earlier than most families think. Paper 3 is 35% of the grade, offers three essays from eighteen sections, and is taught in DP2 in most Dubai schools, which leaves the largest component of the grade as the least rehearsed. A tutor who has taught that option helps a student narrow to five or six sections and learn them in real depth rather than skimming all eighteen. Paper 1 technique can be drilled in weeks; Paper 3 knowledge cannot, so paying for the scarce skill early costs less overall than paying for panic hours later.

faqs.question: How many hours of History tutoring does a DP2 student usually need?
faqs.answer: A weekly hour across DP1 and DP2 is the pattern that produces the most movement for the least money, because the marking between sessions is where improvement happens. Families starting in DP2 typically need more: one weekly hour plus a short investigation block of three to five sessions, and often a pre-session block focused on Paper 3 at Higher Level. A student arriving eight weeks before the session is buying the scarcest hours of the tutoring year at the worst rate. There is no fixed number, and any tutor who quotes one before seeing marked work is guessing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the historical investigation without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth stating clearly. A tutor may discuss the question the student has chosen, teach how source evaluation is assessed, explain what the three sections are marked on, point towards the kinds of source that exist, read one draft and give feedback in writing on what is weak and why. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite paragraphs into a final form, or hand over anything for submission. The investigation has to be the student's own work throughout. One provider in this search sells completed assessments; that is malpractice and the consequence falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: What does the 2,200-word limit on the historical investigation include?
faqs.answer: The limit covers the written content of all three sections: the identification and evaluation of sources, the investigation itself, and the reflection. Quotations inside the body count towards it. Citation footnotes and the bibliography do not form part of the word allowance, though footnotes used to carry argument rather than references are a problem examiners notice. Students most often go over by writing a narrative Section 2, then cut the reflection to fit, which loses marks in the easiest section of the three. Planning the word split before drafting is the fix: the investigation section should take the largest share.

faqs.question: My child writes long Paper 2 essays and still scores 8 out of 15. Why?
faqs.answer: Length is rarely the problem and is often a symptom. Essays in the 7-9 band usually have knowledge but no sustained argument answering the command term, and they stay inside one region when the topic requires two used properly rather than mentioned. An essay on the causes of a twentieth-century war that remains in Europe cannot reach the top bands however detailed it is. The repair is structural: a plan that states a judgement in the first paragraph, paragraphs that each advance that judgement with precise evidence, and 45 minutes of practice until the shape is automatic.

faqs.question: Does paying more for an examiner-branded History tutor change the mark?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. Examiner experience can be genuinely useful, because someone who has applied markbands at scale explains them more precisely than someone who has read them. What it does not provide is access to papers, grade boundaries or marking in progress, and any suggestion otherwise should end the conversation. Ask two questions before paying a premium: what evidence is there of current examiner status, and which Paper 1 and Paper 3 options has this person actually taught. The second question predicts the mark more reliably than the first, and the premium in this market is often attached to the first.

faqs.question: Which Paper 1 prescribed subject is easiest to pick up at short notice?
faqs.answer: The move to global war, for a practical reason rather than an intellectual one: it is the most widely taught prescribed subject in Dubai, so textbook coverage, past questions and source collections are abundant. Rights and protest is similar, with the added difficulty that its photographic sources tempt students into over-reading a visual. Conflict and intervention is the thinnest on resources, which makes a tutor's own source selection matter more. You do not choose this, though. The school does, and a tutor who has not taught your child's option will spend the first sessions learning it.

faqs.question: Can History sessions avoid Dubai school pick-up and bus times?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the scheduling is more flexible than in-home tutoring allows because nobody is driving. Apartment communities such as Dubai Marina and Business Bay usually settle on a 7pm to 9pm slot once a parent is home. Villa communities including Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills often prefer a weekend morning, which suits timed essay practice far better than a weekday evening after seven hours of school. Ramadan timings are adjusted so a session does not sit across Iftar, and the slot holds through school exam weeks rather than being surrendered to them.

faqs.question: Does a History tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: A permit is required, and it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Are there cheaper times of year to buy History tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Effectively yes, though it is about availability rather than discounts. Weekly slots booked in the first term of DP1 are bought at standard rates with a real choice of tutors and hours. The same request eight weeks before the May session competes for the scarcest evening hours of the year, and intensive blocks are priced accordingly. The cost difference across two Diploma years is substantial, and the grade difference is larger, because content built over eighteen months cannot be compressed into six weeks at any price. Early hours are both cheaper and worth more.

faqs.question: How should a Dubai family budget History tutoring alongside school fees?
faqs.answer: Work in annual terms. One weekly specialist hour across a 36-week school year falls roughly between AED 7,200 and AED 16,200 depending on where in the market band the tutor sits, with an investigation clinic and a pre-session block as separate one-off lines. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package, so the fee side of the budget is stable for planning purposes. Most families who report good value bought one consistent weekly hour rather than a large block late on.

faqs.question: What happens if no Dubai-based DP History specialist is free at our hour?
faqs.answer: You are told before booking rather than after. Specialists for a specific Paper 3 regional option are not available in every evening hour in Gulf Standard Time, and pretending otherwise is how families end up with a tutor learning the option alongside the student. When no UAE-based match exists for the exact option and time, IB Gram offers the nearest alternative, which may be a History specialist teaching from India on the same Gulf Standard Time slot, with the rate stated beforehand. Lessons are online in either case, so the delivery does not change.

faqs.question: Is the historical investigation mark moderated, and can a tutor predict it?
faqs.answer: The school marks the investigation out of 25 and the IB moderates those marks, which can move a whole cohort up or down. A tutor can tell you what the published criteria reward and where a draft currently falls short of them, and that is useful. A tutor cannot predict a final mark, and anyone offering a number is selling confidence rather than information. The honest version is a reading of the draft against each section's criteria with the weaknesses named, which is what a student can act on in the time remaining before the school's internal deadline.

dubai/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the rate, the options and one free lesson
dubai/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.closingBody: Send three things: your child's Paper 1 prescribed subject, the two world history topics for Paper 2, and the Paper 3 regional option if they are at Higher Level. Add where the historical investigation has reached and the hours that work in Gulf Standard Time. You get a proposed tutor, a rate in AED per 60 minutes with marking stated as included or not, and one free trial lesson with no card and no package attached. If the teaching does not convince you, nothing is owed and nothing is booked. If it does, the slot is fixed weekly and the marked work starts the following week.

dubai/ib-dp-history-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach Diploma History rather than history in general. Each has marked source-based answers against the per-question mark allocations and essays against the published criteria, and each will say which of a student's problems is worth paying to solve.

intro.heading: Three kinds of spending, and only two of them are worth the money
paragraphs: History is the Diploma subject where the relationship between money spent and marks gained is least obvious, because the subject looks like reading. A parent sees a student with four hundred pages to get through and reasonably concludes that more teaching will help. Some of it will, in a specific and limited way, and a surprising amount of it will not, because a tutor cannot read the books on the student's behalf and the books are where a large part of the grade comes from.

There are three categories of spending in this subject, and keeping them apart is the whole of a sensible budget. The first is a skill you buy once: the source-based paper. It has four questions with fixed mark allocations and an entirely learnable method, and a student who is taught that method properly keeps it for two years. Four to six marked sessions typically does it. This is the best value purchase in Diploma History by a wide margin, and nobody in this market advertises it as such because it does not produce a recurring booking.

The second is marking you keep buying: essays. A fifteen-mark essay needs an argument, a structure, evidence deployed rather than listed, and a judgement that answers the question asked. That improves through repeated marked practice and plateaus without it. A class of twenty-eight in a Dubai school cannot have twenty-eight essays individually annotated every week, which is the arithmetic reason that one-to-one essay marking is worth a specialist rate. It is a recurring cost and a family should budget for it as one.

The third category is reading, and it cannot be bought. Content knowledge in History comes from sustained engagement with the material: the textbook, the set reading, the historiography where the course expects it. A tutor who spends an hour summarising a chapter is selling the student a worse version of something they already own. There is a narrow exception, which is structuring the reading so it is done efficiently and in the right order, and that is one session rather than a term's worth.

Everything numerical below carries its source. The AED bands come from named competitor price pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate survey. The regulatory material comes from u.ae, KHDA and MoHRE. Where a figure could not be verified, including every IB examination and results date, this page says so rather than inventing one. Read the first table, which sorts the components into those three spending categories, before you ring anybody.

One further note on sequence, since it changes the total more than the hourly rate does. The finite work belongs early and the recurring work belongs later, which means a budget spread evenly across two years buys less than the same budget spent deliberately. A source-paper block in the first term of DP1 is secure for the rest of the course. One session testing an investigation question before any research starts removes weeks of remedial drafting. Essay marking then runs across the terms where it is needed rather than all of them. Specialist availability also tightens as the examination series approaches and rates firm up rather than soften, so a family planning in October chooses from a wider pool at a lower point in the published band than a family planning in February.

programmes.description: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE History both carry source work and essay writing, with a shorter answer length and a narrower content span than the Diploma. sections.heading: The one component where tutoring is cheap, and the one where it is not
paragraphs: A direct answer first. In Diploma History, the best value a family in Dubai can buy is a short finite block on the source-based paper, because that paper rewards a fixed method across four questions with published mark allocations and the method, once learnt, holds for two years. The worst value is content re-explanation, because the class teacher and the textbook already supply it and a tutor summarising a chapter is selling an inferior copy of something the family already owns.

Between those sits essay marking, which is the recurring cost and the one families most often underestimate. A fifteen-mark essay improves through repeated marked practice and plateaus without it, which means the spending does not finish the way source-paper work does. Any honest plan says this out loud, because the alternative is a family who budget for six weeks and are surprised in February.

The table below sorts the components into those three categories. The final column is the one to read twice: it says whether the spending ends, recurs, or should never have started. Nothing like it exists on any competitor page in this market, which is odd, because it is the first thing any experienced History teacher would tell a parent who asked honestly.

The method for using it is a diagnostic. One session attempting a source-paper question set and one timed essay, both marked, tells a family which row their money belongs in. That diagnostic is the free trial here, and its output is a written note rather than an impression. A family who buys a term of weekly hours without it is choosing a row at random, and the rows differ in value by a factor that matters.

sections.heading: The source paper, question by question, with the marks beside each
paragraphs: The source-based paper is examined on a prescribed subject chosen by the school, and its structure is the same whichever subject that is. Four questions, twenty-four marks in total, each rewarding a distinct and learnable behaviour. Students lose marks here not through ignorance but through writing the wrong kind of answer for the mark allocation printed beside the question, which is why this is the component where a short block of teaching produces the largest measurable gain.

The first question has two parts worth three and two marks, asking what a source conveys. It wants content, accurately read, in proportion to the marks. Students write a paragraph where two sentences would score full marks, and the minutes come out of the mini-essay at the end of the paper. The second question, worth four marks, asks for the value and limitations of a source with reference to its origin, purpose and content, and those three words are the structure. An answer that discusses reliability in general terms without anchoring it in origin, purpose and content is answering a different question.

The third question, worth six marks, asks the student to compare and contrast two sources. The marks are in the linkage: an answer that describes source A and then describes source B has not compared anything, however accurate both descriptions are. A linked structure, where each point addresses both sources together, is the whole technique and it is quickly taught. The fourth question, worth nine marks, is a mini-essay requiring the sources and the student's own knowledge in combination, and it is where timing failures land because it comes last.

The table sets out the four questions with their marks, what each tests and the error that recurs. Read the final column as a practice list. Each of those errors is procedural, which means marked attempts fix it, and that is why the block finishes rather than running all year. A provider proposing weekly source-paper work across a full term is proposing to be paid for something that should be complete by half term.

sections.heading: Paper 2: two essays, two topics, and why the second topic doubles the marking
paragraphs: The world history paper requires two essays, each drawn from a different one of the twelve world history topics, and schools choose which two topics they teach. That structure has a direct cost consequence that families rarely anticipate. Essay technique is one skill, so it transfers between topics. Content is two separate bodies of material, so revision does not transfer at all. A student who is confident in one topic and shaky in the other has a content problem in half the paper and no technique problem anywhere.

That distinction is worth money. A tutor marking essays across both topics in rotation is buying technique improvement once and applying it twice, which is efficient. A tutor re-teaching the content of the weaker topic is doing work the student should be doing from the textbook, which is not. The correct response to a weak second topic is usually a reading plan plus essays on that topic specifically, so the marking exposes the content gaps and the student fills them by reading.

The essays themselves reward argument over narrative, and this is the structural failure that dominates the component. A student who tells the story of the event accurately, in chronological order, with a conclusion summarising what happened, will sit in the middle bands however much they know. An essay that scores above that takes a position in the first paragraph, organises the body around the analytical factors rather than the chronology, deploys specific evidence in support of each factor, and reaches a judgement that answers the question as asked.

The practical teaching sequence is a plan structure that survives pressure. Students can produce a good essay with two hours and no stress; the paper gives them considerably less. Building a repeatable plan shape, practising it against a clock until it becomes automatic, and marking the results with the argument strand commented separately from the factual strand is what converts knowledge into marks. That is recurring work, it is the main thing worth a specialist rate in this subject, and a family should plan for it across a term rather than a fortnight.

sections.heading: Higher Level: the regional option paper and what the extra weight costs
paragraphs: Higher Level students sit a third written paper on a regional option, choosing a region and studying several sections within it, examined through three essays. It carries a substantial share of the Higher Level grade, which both lowers the share held by the other components and raises the total volume of essay writing considerably. A family budgeting for Higher Level History should expect the recurring marking cost to be meaningfully higher than at Standard Level, and should expect it for a structural reason rather than a vague one.

The content span is the other cost driver. The regional option covers a wider body of material than a single world history topic, and that material must be known in enough specific detail to supply evidence for three essays rather than one. There is no efficient substitute for reading here, and a tutor who offers one should be treated with scepticism. The useful intervention is sequencing: deciding which sections to secure first, which to leave until later, and what the minimum evidence base for each looks like.

The compensating advantage is that the essay skill is identical. A Higher Level student who has had essays marked properly on the world history topics does not need separate technique coaching for the regional option; they need the same marking applied to different content. Families are sometimes sold the regional option as a distinct product requiring its own block of coaching, and that is usually a way of selling the same skill twice.

One scheduling point follows from the structure. Three papers plus an internally assessed investigation makes the final two terms of Higher Level History dense, and the regional option is frequently the component left until last because it is taught last. Mapping it into the revision calendar in DP1 rather than discovering it in DP2 is both cheaper and less distressing, and it is the kind of planning a single early session can set up.

sections.heading: The historical investigation: 2,200 words across three sections
paragraphs: The internally assessed component is a historical investigation on a question of the student's own choosing, capped at 2,200 words and assessed across three sections worth twenty-five marks in total. The structure matters for budgeting because the three sections are very unequal in both marks and word count, and students routinely allocate their effort in inverse proportion to the marks available.

The first section identifies and evaluates the sources, carrying six marks, and requires two sources evaluated for value and limitations with reference to their origin, purpose and content. The skill is identical to the one taught for the source paper's second question, which means a student who has done the source-paper block already owns most of this section. That overlap is a genuine saving and worth knowing about before paying for separate investigation coaching.

The second section is the investigation itself, carrying fifteen marks and most of the word count. It wants a focused question answered with evidence and a clear argument, with different perspectives considered where the question invites them. The commonest failure is a question too broad to answer in the words available, and it is a planning failure rather than a writing failure. Testing a question for answerability takes one session and prevents the expensive outcome, which is a student discovering in the final draft that the question was never answerable with the sources they can reach.

The third section is a reflection carrying four marks, connecting the investigation to the methods and challenges historians face. It is short, it is specific, and it is the section students most often write as an afterthought at two in the morning. Written properly it refers back to concrete difficulties the student actually met, which is only possible if the investigation was conducted deliberately. The academic-honesty position across all three sections is simple: the student researches and writes every word, and a tutor teaches, questions and comments on the student's own drafts.

sections.heading: What Dubai charges for History, and why essay subjects price differently
paragraphs: The published bands apply to History as to any Diploma subject. A qualified online subject tutor in Dubai is advertised at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and an IB or IGCSE specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, as of October 2026. In-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the rate. Budget online provision, usually delivered by university students, starts well below those figures. Each band in the table traces to a named publisher.

Essay subjects price differently from problem-based subjects for a reason worth understanding. Marking a fifteen-mark History essay properly takes a specialist a substantial fraction of a lesson's length, because there is no answer key and the judgement has to be made against criteria and then explained to the student in a way they can act on. A provider quoting at the bottom of a band is almost always quoting for contact time alone. The question to put directly is whether written work is marked and returned inside the rate, and how many scripts a term includes.

The final column in the table estimates the hours typically needed for each kind of work in this subject, which is the figure families actually want and which no competitor page supplies. Read it as a planning aid rather than a quotation: a student's starting point changes the numbers, which is what the free diagnostic exists to establish. Monthly package pricing circulating in Dubai includes around AED 799 for eight online sessions at the budget end, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits at the mid tier.

Local context helps frame the total. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate students at 7 per cent of enrolment, so Diploma specialists are serving a minority curriculum and price accordingly. KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, which means a two-year tutoring plan is being budgeted against a flat school fee rather than a rising one.
