sections.heading: UAE Social Studies, Arabic and Islamic Education alongside Diploma History
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market mentions this at all, and it is a real part of a Dubai History student's week. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with those requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. These sit alongside the Diploma rather than inside it, and they occupy timetable space that a family planning tutoring needs to account for.

The organisational rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two further details affect any plan. Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. And for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is not permitted, which is a genuine constraint on how support for them may be described by anyone.

The practical upshot for a History family is scheduling rather than content. More discrete mandatory blocks means less timetable slack, so a fixed protected weekly slot outperforms a flexible arrangement that erodes. Ramadan moves the whole pattern later and a post-Iftar slot is a normal request that costs nothing extra over video. On examination timing, this page publishes no IB dates: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing here is confirmed from the IB directly, and the session windows belong with the school's Diploma coordinator or ibo.org.

sections.heading: Sources, past papers and what a tutor may not supply
paragraphs: History is the subject where requests for material are most common and most often misplaced. Families ask for mark schemes, past papers, syllabus documents and subject guides, and the answer on these pages is consistent: those documents belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor may reference them, cite the official address, and link out. Supplying them as downloads is not something any legitimate provider should be doing, whatever the price.

The same boundary covers the historical investigation, in a form specific to this subject. A tutor may teach source evaluation, question whether an investigation's question is answerable, point out that a section is under-evidenced, note that a reflection has drifted into generality, and comment on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not locate and summarise the student's sources for them, nor author any part of the submission. Research is the skill being assessed, so outsourcing it removes the thing being marked.

There is a historiography caution worth making explicitly. Where a course expects engagement with differing historical interpretations, a student needs to have read enough to represent those interpretations honestly. A list of historian names attached to one-line positions, collected from a revision site, is detectable and weak: an examiner can tell the difference between a student who has read an argument and one who has memorised a label. A tutor can point a student towards what is worth reading, and that is a legitimate and useful service; reading it is still the student's job.

One market caution to close on. At least one operator in this search results page sells completed internal assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach, it triggers IB malpractice procedures, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. Any provider offering finished work, model investigations to submit, or memorisable essays presented as examination answers should be declined. The honest alternative is less convenient and it is the only one that survives scrutiny.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP History online tutor in Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures as of October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a Diploma or IGCSE specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IB rates from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate survey covers the specialist band. Those are market rates from the sources named, not a price list for this platform. In History the more important question is how many hours you need, because the source-paper work finishes in four to six sessions and essay marking recurs.

faqs.question: How many marks is each question on the source paper worth?
faqs.answer: The paper carries twenty-four marks across four questions. The first has two parts worth three and two marks, asking what a source conveys. The second, worth four marks, asks for value and limitations with reference to origin, purpose and content. The third, worth six marks, asks for comparison and contrast of two sources. The fourth, worth nine marks, is a mini-essay using the sources together with the student's own knowledge. Confirm the current allocation with the school's coordinator. Writing the wrong length for the marks printed beside a question is the most common avoidable loss on this paper.

faqs.question: How do I find out which prescribed subject my child's school teaches?
faqs.answer: Ask the class teacher or the Diploma coordinator, and do it before buying any revision material. The source paper is examined on one prescribed subject chosen by the school from a published set, and the content differs entirely between them. Students who revise from an online resource covering a different prescribed subject waste real time, and it happens often enough to be worth checking explicitly. The same applies to the two world history topics for the essay paper and, at Higher Level, to the regional option. Three questions to the coordinator saves a term of misdirected work.

faqs.question: Why does the second world history topic need as much work as the first?
faqs.answer: Because essay technique transfers between topics and content does not. The paper requires two essays from two different topics, so a student who is confident in one and shaky in the other has a content gap covering half the paper with no technique gap anywhere. The efficient response is a reading plan for the weaker topic plus marked essays written specifically on it, so the marking exposes the gaps and the student closes them by reading. Paying a tutor to re-teach that topic's content is paying for work the textbook already does.

faqs.question: How long is the historical investigation allowed to be?
faqs.answer: The current limit is 2,200 words across the whole investigation, covering all three assessed sections. The allocation between sections should follow the marks rather than the student's enthusiasm: the investigation itself carries the large majority of both the marks and the words, source evaluation takes roughly a fifth, and the reflection is short. Confirm the limit with the school's coordinator before drafting begins. Cutting an over-length draft late is the worst outcome, because what gets removed under time pressure is almost always argument rather than padding.

faqs.question: What belongs in the reflection section of the investigation?
faqs.answer: A short, specific account connecting the investigation the student actually did to the methods and challenges historians face: the limits of the available sources, the problem of perspective, the gaps the student could not fill, the choices made about what counted as evidence. What loses marks is generic commentary about history as a discipline that could have been written without doing any investigation at all. Written properly it refers back to concrete difficulties encountered, which is only possible when the research was conducted deliberately rather than assembled at the end.

faqs.question: Can a tutor choose my daughter's investigation question for her?
faqs.answer: A tutor can test a question she has proposed, which is the useful thing, and should. The test is practical: is it narrow enough to answer in 2,200 words, do sources exist that she can actually reach, and does it invite more than one perspective. A tutor handing her a question removes the first piece of historical judgement the component assesses. The honest version is that she brings two or three candidate questions, the tutor questions each one, and she chooses. That single session prevents the expensive outcome of discovering in the final draft that the question was never answerable.

faqs.question: Is the Higher Level regional option worth paying extra hours for?
faqs.answer: It needs extra hours of essay marking rather than a separate block of technique coaching, and that distinction matters financially. The regional option is examined through three further essays and carries a substantial share of the Higher Level grade, so the volume of marking rises. The essay skill itself is identical to the one used on the world history paper, so a student already having essays marked properly does not need a second course of technique teaching. Families are sometimes sold the regional option as a distinct product, which is usually the same skill charged for twice.

faqs.question: How do you teach source evaluation over live video?
faqs.answer: The sources sit on a shared screen and get annotated live, which works better than passing a printed sheet across a table. The student marks up origin, purpose and content as they read, the tutor can see the order in which they notice things, and that order is where the teachable material is. Timed attempts are then written and marked offline with the mark allocation written beside each answer, and returned before the next session. For a paper that is mostly about reading closely under pressure, sharing the reading in real time is a genuine advantage of the format.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give my son past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider who offers to should prompt a question about what else they are willing to distribute. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or supplying them is copyright infringement. What a tutor can legitimately do is reference them, cite the official source, and point to where a school or a student may lawfully access them through the school's own subscription. Schools hold the appropriate access, so the coordinator is the right first stop for practice material.

faqs.question: Does Dubai's mandatory Social Studies requirement overlap with Diploma History?
faqs.answer: They run in parallel rather than overlapping usefully. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs in the Arabic first-language, Islamic Education and Social Studies strands. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For the mandatory subjects, additional or different content without prior Ministry permission is not permitted. The practical effect on a History family is scheduling: more discrete blocks means less timetable slack for a weekly tutoring slot.

faqs.question: How many essays a week should a History student be writing before the examinations?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect, written properly, rather than many written quickly. One timed essay a week, marked and reviewed before the next is attempted, produces more improvement than three written without feedback, because the point of the exercise is to act on the marking. In the final month the useful pattern shifts towards plans rather than full essays: a plan takes fifteen minutes, exposes whether the student can structure an argument under pressure, and can be reviewed quickly. Full timed essays then confirm that the plan survives being written out.

faqs.question: Is History a harder Diploma subject than Geography?
faqs.answer: They are demanding in different ways, so the comparison is a poor basis for a choice. History carries a heavy reading load, a source-based paper with its own method, and essays that reward sustained argument. Geography carries more diverse content, quantitative elements, and a fieldwork-based internal assessment with a distinct planning burden. Students who read widely and write well usually find History the better fit; students who prefer applied data and a structured investigation often prefer Geography. Choose on the student's working habits, and check target university requirements before either is dropped.

faqs.question: My child's class has moved on from a topic they never understood. What now?
faqs.answer: Separate the content gap from the technique gap before spending anything, because they need different responses. A content gap in a topic already taught is closed by reading, a clear sequence and some retrieval practice, and that is cheap or free. What a paid hour adds is a reading order and a set of marked essays on that topic, so the marking shows precisely which parts of the content are still missing. Buying a tutor to re-deliver the lessons the class has already had is the expensive version of the same outcome, and it is slower.

faqs.question: Does starting History late cost more than starting a science late?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is the reading rather than the teaching. A science student joining late faces a finite set of concepts and problem types that can be taught in sequence. A History student joining late faces a body of material that has to be read, and nobody can read it for them, so the catch-up time is largely the student's own and cannot be compressed by buying hours. What paid hours do add is a sequence for the reading and marked essays that show whether it is landing. Start earlier where that is still possible.

dubai/ib-dp-history-online-tutor.closingHeading: Find out which kind of spending you actually need
dubai/ib-dp-history-online-tutor.closingBody: The free trial lesson for Diploma History marks two things: a source-paper question set and one timed essay. You receive both annotated and a written note saying whether your money belongs in the finite source-paper block, in recurring essay marking, or in neither because the real gap is reading the student has to do themselves. Sessions for UAE families run online, one to one, in Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school day. If no Diploma History specialist is free in your window, we say so at the enquiry rather than after a block has been paid for.

intro.heading: Three different problems arrive under the same enquiry
paragraphs: Dubai parents searching for a History tutor almost always describe the same symptom: the child reads widely, talks about the subject at dinner, revises conscientiously, and comes home with a 4 or a 5. Underneath that symptom sit three unrelated problems. The first is content, where a topic was taught while the student was away or covered too fast to stick. The second is the essay, where the argument is sound but stops one rung short of the band above. The third is the historical investigation, where the question chosen in week one cannot be answered with the sources available.

They need different purchases. A content gap is a two-to-four hour job per topic and closes permanently. An essay problem is a repeated-marking job that takes a term and never finishes in a single intensive weekend. An investigation problem is a research-supervision job measured in milestones against the school's own deadlines. Buying a weekly hour and hoping it covers all three is how a Dubai family spends two terms and sees a mock grade that has not moved, which is the pattern behind most of the enquiries that reach us in February.

Diagnosis is cheap and most families skip it. One timed essay, sat under exam conditions and marked against the published band descriptors, separates the three in an afternoon. If the content is accurate and the structure is orderly and the mark is still 9 out of 15, the problem is not knowledge. If the student cannot produce the detail to support a claim, it is. If the essay is strong and the investigation has no question, the plan should start at the investigation and the essays can wait a month.

This page is about what the examination actually rewards, because History is a subject where effort and marks come apart more visibly than anywhere else in the Diploma. A candidate can know a topic thoroughly and write about it for forty minutes and score in the middle, and the reason is almost never that they needed to read more. It is that the examination is marking a specific set of moves, and nobody has ever shown them what those moves look like on paper.

There is one more thing a Dubai family needs before buying anything, and it is not about teaching at all. The prescribed subject for the source paper, the two world history topics and, at Higher Level, the regional option are all chosen by your child's school rather than by the IB. Three decisions, made before the class began, determining which revision material is useful and which tutor is a real match rather than a plausible one. One email to the department settles them, and it is the cheapest thing on this page.

dubai/ib-dp-history-tutor.programmesIntro: History as a named subject exists only in the Diploma years, but the habits that decide the grade are formed earlier: handling a source sceptically, supporting a claim with evidence, and writing to a question rather than around a topic. Here is what each IB programme a Dubai school runs contributes.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Individuals and Societies assesses knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Criterion D is the direct ancestor of Diploma source work, since it rewards analysing and evaluating evidence rather than reporting it. Students who were marked rigorously against it arrive able to question a document's origin, which is most of the battle on the source paper.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP cohorts vary in how much formal essay writing they do before Year 12, and the gap shows up fast. Departments here report the same DP1 pattern annually: students who are comfortable with sources and uncomfortable with sustained argument, because MYP assessment rewards organised explanation while the Diploma rewards a thesis carried through to a conclusion.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: History sits in Group 3 across both Diploma years. Candidates sit a source-based paper on a prescribed subject, an essay paper on world history topics, and submit a historical investigation of up to 2,200 words. Higher Level candidates add a third paper on a regional option with three essays. Confirm the current structure and weightings in the IB subject guide at ibo.org.
programmes.countryNote: History is widely offered in Dubai Diploma schools, usually alongside Economics, Geography and Business Management in a Group 3 block, so a student choosing it is often choosing against Business Management rather than against another humanities subject. KHDA inspects these schools annually on a six-band scale and the published reports name subject-level strengths worth reading.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. A CP candidate taking History sits the same papers and submits the same historical investigation as a Diploma candidate, so subject support is identical, and the reflective project often draws on the same research habits.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of Dubai schools run the Career-related Programme, which means a CP candidate taking History is often the only one on that route in their year group. The consequence is practical: the reflective project and the historical investigation compete for the same weeks, usually the first term of the second year, and one of them will slip unless both are calendared in advance.

dubai/ib-dp-history-tutor.subjectsIntro: Diploma History is one skills paper, one or two essay papers and one piece of independent research. Below is what a tutor works through with a Dubai candidate, and where the marks are actually lost in each part.

subjects.name: The source paper
subjects.description: Four questions across a set of sources on a prescribed subject, worth 24 marks in total. It rewards four specific moves rather than wider reading, and the marks are lost almost entirely on the final question, where candidates narrate the sources instead of using them to answer the question with their own knowledge woven in.

subjects.name: World history topics
subjects.levels: Standard and Higher Level, essay paper
subjects.description: Two essays from two different topics chosen by the department. The second topic is routinely under-prepared because the department teaches it later, which means the second essay in the examination is written with half the material of the first. It is the most predictable weakness in the subject.

subjects.name: The Higher Level regional option
subjects.description: Three essays in two and a half hours on a regional option the department chooses. The constraint is stamina and breadth: candidates who have revised two sections thoroughly and one not at all find the third question is the one that fits what they know, and write it with nothing to say.

subjects.name: The historical investigation
subjects.description: An independent investigation of up to 2,200 words across three sections: the identification and evaluation of sources, the investigation itself, and a reflection on the methods and challenges of the historian. Most lost marks trace back to a question that was too broad to answer in the space allowed.

subjects.name: Source evaluation
subjects.description: Judging value and limitations from a source's origin, purpose and content rather than from a memorised formula. Candidates who write that a source is limited because it is biased earn almost nothing; those who explain what a specific author's specific purpose does to the specific claim earn the mark every time.

subjects.name: Argument and thesis construction
subjects.description: A thesis that answers the question in the first paragraph, is argued through the body, and is restated with more precision at the end. This is the single most common gap between a mid-band and a top-band script, and it is structural rather than knowledge-based, which is why it moves quickly with marking.

subjects.name: Specific evidence and chronology
subjects.description: Named people, dated events, precise terms and figures where they exist. The examination distinguishes sharply between a supported claim and an asserted one, and most Dubai scripts in the middle bands are full of claims that are accurate and unsupported.

subjects.name: Historiography and interpretation
subjects.levels: Essay papers, especially at Higher Level
subjects.description: Awareness that historians disagree, and the ability to use that disagreement to sharpen an argument rather than to decorate it. Name a school of interpretation and the reason it reads the evidence that way; a list of surnames with no position attached adds nothing to the mark.

subjects.name: Command terms in History
subjects.description: Examine, evaluate, discuss, to what extent and compare and contrast require different structures, and the wrong structure caps a script however much the student knows. Practising two command terms on one topic in a single session shows a candidate the difference faster than any explanation.

subjects.name: Timing and question choice
subjects.description: Three essays in 150 minutes allows roughly fifty minutes each including planning, and Higher Level candidates routinely spend seventy on the first. Question choice is a trainable skill: two minutes spent rejecting a question properly is worth more than ten minutes of writing in the wrong one.

dubai/ib-dp-history-tutor.regionsIntro: For a History family in Dubai the practical questions are when a session can start after the school run and how late a student can realistically write a timed essay. Below are the communities the enquiries come from, with that in mind.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: The deepest band of Diploma provision in the emirate, where History usually runs at both levels with a specialist department. Requests here concentrate on essay marking and on the Higher Level regional paper rather than on content teaching.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Long-established Diploma schools and short school runs, so a five o'clock start works most days. A common ask here is a late slot for a candidate also taking Arabic as a first language, which carries its own after-school load.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Quoz
regions.note: Short commutes and families who prefer ninety-minute sessions, which suits this subject: a timed essay and the mark-by-mark read-back afterwards do not fit inside an hour, and splitting them across two weeks loses the thread.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Later bus arrivals push a realistic start past half past six, and smaller Diploma cohorts mean History is sometimes taught in a combined Standard and Higher Level class. That shows up first in the second world history topic, which gets compressed.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown Dubai and DIFC
regions.note: Apartment living with short runs and confident, widely read students whose essays are often structurally weak rather than thin. The purchase from this band is usually marking across a term, not teaching.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, The Springs and Motor City
regions.note: Inland communities where a school run can take forty minutes each way at the wrong hour. Weekend morning sessions are most popular here, and they suit essay work better than a tired weekday evening does.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Barsha and Emirates Hills Diploma band
schoolClusters.note: Where History is most reliably taught by a specialist at both levels, with the prescribed subject and the world history topics settled early. Families in this band usually want marked essays and Higher Level regional paper work rather than content teaching.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Deira and the Festival City corridor
schoolClusters.note: A mixed band where some departments run History with small cohorts and the second world history topic is often taught late. Requests from this corridor lean towards closing content gaps and finding an answerable investigation question before the school deadline.

dubai/ib-dp-history-tutor.modesIntro: History support divides into three shapes that cost and behave differently: content repair, essay marking across a term, and investigation supervision pinned to school deadlines. The commonest mistake is buying one weekly hour and expecting it to serve all three.

modes.title: Content repair, bought by topic
modes.description: Two to four hours on a single topic that was missed or rushed, taught properly and then tested with a timed question rather than a quiz. This is the only History purchase that closes permanently: once the topic is secure it does not return, which is why it is cheapest when bought in the term the topic was taught.
bullets: One topic finished before the next is started
A timed question at the end, marked, not a verbal recap
A one-page chronology the student builds and the tutor questions

modes.title: Essay marking across a term
modes.description: An essay written between sessions, marked before the session, and read back mark by mark during it. Weekly or fortnightly, continuing for at least a term, because the thing being changed is a habit and habits need repetition. One intensive weekend of essay teaching changes almost nothing that lasts to the examination.
bullets: The essay is always sat before the session, never written during it
Marked against the published band descriptors with the rung named
A running list of the three recurring faults, updated every time

modes.title: Investigation supervision by milestone
modes.description: Three to five sessions placed at the points where a historical investigation fails: testing whether the question can be answered with obtainable sources, evaluating two sources properly, reading a draft against each section's requirements, and checking the reflection says something about method rather than about feelings.
bullets: Question narrowed and tested before a month is spent on it
Sources evaluated on origin, purpose and content, not on bias
The student writes every word; the tutor reads, questions and points at criteria

sections.heading: What a History examiner rewards, and what a candidate usually supplies instead
paragraphs: The gap between a well-read student and a high-scoring one is almost always the same gap, and it is visible in the first two sentences of an essay. A top-band script opens by answering the question. A middle-band script opens by introducing the topic. From that point the two essays diverge further: the first spends every paragraph advancing a position with named evidence, the second spends every paragraph explaining what happened and arrives at a judgement only in the final line, where there is no time left to argue it.

Examiners are marking for a thesis, for specific support, for balance where the question requires it, and for a conclusion that follows from the argument rather than announcing one. What candidates supply instead is coverage. A Dubai student who has read three books on a topic feels obliged to show that, and the result is a long, accurate, well-organised narrative that scores in the middle because it never settles what the question asked. The reading was not wasted; it was spent on the wrong output.

This is why the diagnosis matters more than the hours. A student who writes narrative instead of argument does not need more content, and the tutor who responds to a 9 out of 15 by teaching the topic again has misread the script. What moves that mark is repeated marking against the descriptors, with the rung named each time and a shorter essay attempted next. Most candidates in this position write less and score more within six weeks, which is counter-intuitive enough that it has to be shown rather than explained.

sections.heading: The mark ladder on a fifteen-mark essay, rung by rung
paragraphs: Dubai parents are rarely shown what each band actually looks like, so a mark feels arbitrary. It is not. The bands describe recognisable kinds of script, and once a student can identify which kind they have just written, the next rung becomes a specific task instead of a vague instruction to do better. The table below paraphrases the progression in plain language; the official wording lives in the IB subject guide and the published markbands, which your child's teacher can show you.

Two rungs account for most stalled candidates in this emirate. The first is the move from organised narrative to argument, which means deciding what the answer is before writing and letting every paragraph serve it. The second is the move from argument to judgement, which means weighing the factors against each other rather than listing them and then asserting a conclusion. Both are structural. Neither requires a single additional fact, which is why they respond to marking rather than to teaching.

Use the ladder as a shared vocabulary rather than as a grading tool. After each marked essay, the useful question is not what mark did you get but which rung did you stop at and what would have moved it. Students who can answer that about their own work start marking themselves, and self-marking is the point at which tutoring becomes unnecessary, which is the outcome a plan should be aiming at rather than a standing weekly booking.

sections.heading: The detail audit: what counts as specific evidence
paragraphs: Ask a Dubai History candidate in the middle bands to support a claim and you will usually get a sentence that is true, relevant and unsupported. The examination draws a hard line between a claim and a supported claim, and the difference is almost always one named person, one date, one figure or one precise term. Candidates believe they are being specific because the claim is accurate. Accuracy is not specificity, and the mark scheme is not interested in the difference as a matter of opinion.

The audit is a fifteen-minute exercise that changes essays permanently. Take a marked essay and underline every claim. Beside each one, write the single piece of evidence that supports it. Where nothing can be written, the claim was asserted, and the student has just found their own pattern. Most candidates discover that they can support the first half of each paragraph and not the second, because the second half is where the argument was being invented as they wrote.

Building the stock of detail is then a mechanical job rather than a reading project. For each topic, the student assembles a one-page sheet: the people worth naming, the dates that matter, three or four figures or statistics with their source, and the two or three terms the examination expects. Six topics at one page each is a revision resource no textbook provides, and it is the single most useful thing a tutor and a student can produce together in DP1.

sections.heading: Source skills as four separate moves
paragraphs: The source paper is not a knowledge test and it rewards four distinct moves, each of which can be taught separately and practised to the point of being automatic. The first is comprehension: saying what a source actually claims, in the student's own words, without importing anything. The second is value and limitations, judged from a source's origin, its purpose and its content, each considered separately and each tied to the specific claim being made rather than to the document in general.

The third move is comparison. Two sources are compared and contrasted on substance, not on format, and the answer is organised point by point rather than source by source. A script that describes source A for a paragraph and then source B for a paragraph has not compared anything, and that structural error is the commonest avoidable loss on the paper. The fourth move is the extended question, where the sources are used as evidence inside the student's own argument, with their own knowledge woven in and attributed to itself.

Where candidates lose marks is predictable enough to drill in three sessions. On value and limitations they write that a source is biased, which earns nothing because every source has a perspective; the mark comes from saying what this author's purpose does to this claim. On comparison they narrate. On the final question they summarise the sources and forget their own knowledge entirely. None of this is about reading more history. It is about four moves and the discipline to make them in the order the paper asks.

sections.heading: Finding out what your child's school actually teaches
paragraphs: History is the Diploma subject where the department's own choices determine the most, and where Dubai parents most often do not know what those choices were. The prescribed subject for the source paper is selected by the school. The two world history topics are selected by the school. At Higher Level the regional option is selected by the school. Three decisions, all made before your child arrived in the class, all determining what revision material is useful and which tutor is a genuine match.

Getting the answers takes one email and is worth sending in the first weeks of DP1. Ask for the prescribed subject, both world history topics, the Higher Level regional option and its sections, the department's internal deadlines for the historical investigation, and the date of the mock series. Put all of it in one message and keep the reply. Families who do this buy tutoring that matches the paper; families who do not frequently buy three months of help on a topic their child will never be examined on.

The same information is what lets you screen a tutor in two minutes. A specialist asked about a specific prescribed subject will say what the source set usually contains and where candidates lose marks in it. A generalist will say that the skills transfer, which is partly true and completely insufficient at Higher Level, where the regional option carries three essays and no amount of transferable skill compensates for not knowing the content. Ask for the specifics before you book anything.

sections.heading: The historical investigation as a research problem, not an essay
paragraphs: The investigation fails in week one far more often than in month four. A student picks a subject they find interesting, writes a question that would take a monograph to answer, and discovers at the draft deadline that 2,200 words cannot hold it. The test that prevents this is mechanical: name the two sources you will evaluate, name what each one lets you say, and state the answer you expect to reach. A question that cannot survive those three sentences will not survive the word limit either.

Narrowing is the skill, and it is counter-intuitive for a bright student. A question about the causes of a war is unanswerable; a question about whether one specific document shaped one specific decision in one specific month is answerable, evidenced, and scores higher precisely because it is small. Dubai students with good English and wide reading resist this hardest, because narrowing feels like a reduction in ambition. It is the opposite: the smaller question is the one that can be argued properly in the space allowed.

The three sections then do different jobs and should be written in a deliberate order. The source evaluation section wants two sources assessed on origin, purpose and content, each tied to this investigation's question rather than described in general. The investigation itself wants an argued answer with evidence. The reflection wants something genuine about the methods and limits of historical knowledge, drawn from what actually happened during the research, not a general essay about objectivity written in the last hour.

sections.heading: Chronology, memory and a revision schedule that holds
paragraphs: Two years of History is more content than any student can hold in short-term memory, and the commonest revision failure in Dubai is a candidate who revises everything shallowly in April and knows nothing precisely in May. What works is narrower and earlier: one page per topic built during the year, reviewed on a schedule, and tested with timed questions rather than reread. The page is the resource; the timed questions are the testing; the rereading is the activity that feels productive and does the least.

The schedule below is a ten-week shape that families can adapt. It assumes a Higher Level candidate with a source paper, two world history topics and a three-section regional option, and it deliberately front-loads the second world history topic, because the department usually taught it last and the student therefore knows it least. It also places the first full timed paper in week three rather than week nine, on the principle that you want the bad news early while there is still time to act on it.

Build the schedule around what the student will be examined on rather than around what feels unfinished. The regional paper carries three essays and most candidates have revised two sections properly, so the third section is where the hours should go even though it is the least pleasant. The source paper rewards practice on the four moves rather than content revision, so it needs fewer hours than students expect and more frequent short sessions. The investigation is finished by this stage and should take none.

sections.heading: Honesty, translated sources and AI summaries of scholarship
paragraphs: The historical investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the period, explain what each section requires, ask whether a source actually supports the claim being made, and point out that a paragraph has drifted from the question. A tutor may not supply the text, choose the question, construct the argument or rework a draft to completion. Crossing that line produces a malpractice finding against the candidate rather than against the tutor, and it is also the thing the essay mills in this search are selling.

Two practical issues arise more often in Dubai than elsewhere. The first is translated material. Working with a translated source is legitimate and common, and the honest version requires saying so: name the translation used, note that the student is reading at one remove, and treat that as a limitation in the evaluation, which is exactly the kind of methodological awareness the reflection section rewards. Pretending to have read an original is both dishonest and easy to detect.

The second is generative AI. A model-written summary of a historian's position is not a reading of that historian, and students who rely on one write sentences that sound authoritative and cite nothing checkable. Worse, if the model has invented a position, the candidate has attributed a view to a named scholar who never held it. The school's own policy governs any use of these tools and declaring it is the only safe route. Note also that no tutor should be circulating IB, Cambridge or Pearson mark schemes or syllabus documents: reference the official page and link to it instead.

sections.heading: What History support costs in Dubai, and how the lessons run
paragraphs: Published rates in this emirate run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise their from-prices, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, to AED 200 to 450 and above for a Diploma specialist on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table. TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for premium named tutoring. None of those is our price list; it is the market you are shopping in, which is more than three of the six pages competing for this search will tell you.

In an essay subject the figure that matters is not the hourly rate but whether marking happens between sessions. Reading a fifteen-mark History essay properly, with the rung named and three specific corrections written, takes a tutor twenty to thirty minutes. If that work is not happening, you are paying for a conversation about history rather than for the mechanism that actually moves a mark. Ask directly: is the essay sat before the session, marked before it starts, and is that inside the quoted rate?

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, recorded so a student can rewatch a read-back rather than relying on notes taken while being corrected. Scripts are annotated and shared as files, so a parent can read what was marked. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. In-home tuition does exist here, published at AED 180 to 350 an hour with some home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and the premium buys presence while narrowing the choice to those willing to drive to your community at your hour.

sections.heading: KHDA, the department and the mandatory UAE subjects
paragraphs: In Dubai, private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools annually on a six-band scale. The published report is a genuinely useful document for a History family, because it comments on teaching quality at subject level and on student attainment in the Diploma. If a department has been flagged for inconsistent teaching in Group 3, that is worth knowing before you assume the problem sits with your child.

Elsewhere in the country the regulator differs, which matters for families who move. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project, which tells you how shallow the local detail usually is.

The other scheduling constraint is federal. Private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies alongside their licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring these arrangements from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, calculating the time on a 40-minute lesson unit, and prohibiting combined classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies. Add that to six Diploma subjects and the core, and most Dubai Year 12 weeks have one usable weekday evening plus part of a weekend for an essay and its marking.

process.title: Send the department's four answers with your first message
process.description: Name the prescribed subject, the two world history topics, the Higher Level regional option if applicable, and the school's internal deadline for the investigation. Those four facts decide who is a genuine match and what the plan should do first. Without them any tutor is guessing, and guessing in this subject means revising content your child will not be examined on.

process.title: A free diagnostic essay, marked against the descriptors
process.description: The first lesson is free, one per student, with no card details taken, and it is built around a timed essay sat beforehand. It comes back with the rung named, three specific corrections and a statement of whether the problem is content, argument or timing. That single artefact is what tells you which of the three purchases you need.

process.title: A written plan with the number of marked essays stated
process.description: In an essay subject the useful plan says how many essays will be sat and marked, over how many weeks, and what the total comes to. Compare that against the AED bands published for Dubai. A plan that quantifies discussion hours but not marked scripts is quantifying the wrong thing entirely.

process.title: Review monthly, and aim at self-marking
process.description: Each month brings the marked scripts and a short note on which rung the essays now reach. The target is a student who can name their own rung and the fix before anyone tells them, because at that point the tutoring has done its job and should end rather than continue as a standing weekly booking.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the department's topics, not to the subject name
whyPoints.description: The prescribed subject, both world history topics and the Higher Level regional option are chosen by your child's school, so a tutor who has not taught them is a partial match at best. We ask for those choices in writing before suggesting anybody, because at Higher Level the regional paper carries three essays and transferable skill does not substitute for content.

whyPoints.title: Marked essays counted in the plan
whyPoints.description: Marking a fifteen-mark essay properly, with the rung named and three corrections written, takes twenty to thirty minutes. Plans here state how many essays will be sat and marked over how many weeks, because that number is the mechanism that moves a History grade and an hourly rate on its own tells you nothing about it.

whyPoints.title: The band ladder used as shared vocabulary
whyPoints.description: Students who can name the rung they stopped at and the fix that would move it start marking their own work. We teach the ladder deliberately for that reason, and we treat a plan as finished when self-marking arrives rather than renewing it indefinitely.

whyPoints.title: A written boundary on the investigation
whyPoints.description: The historical investigation is the student's own work. We teach the period, read drafts against each section's requirements and ask the questions a moderator would ask. We do not supply text, choose the question or construct the argument, and we say so in writing, because the pages selling the alternative in this search are selling a malpractice finding.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, which widens the pool rather than the postcode
whyPoints.description: There are no home visits in the UAE. The practical gain is selection: a family in Mirdif is choosing among everyone who has taught their child's regional option at half past six, rather than among the Diploma History specialists willing to drive to Mirdif at that hour for an in-home rate.

faqs.question: What separates a 10 out of 15 History essay from a 13?
faqs.answer: Usually balance and judgement rather than content. A 10 typically has a clear argument, good evidence and only a gesture towards the other side, while a 13 engages the counter-argument properly and reaches a conclusion that follows from weighing the two rather than announcing a view. Neither difference requires an extra fact. The fix is specific: write one paragraph arguing the opposite case as strongly as possible, then answer it in the next paragraph. Three or four marked essays with that single instruction moves most candidates who have been stuck in the upper middle band for a term.

faqs.question: Why does my child's History essay run out of time in the examination?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the first essay was over-written. Three essays in 150 minutes allows about fifty minutes each including planning, and candidates routinely spend seventy on the one they feel most confident about, leaving thirty for the hardest question on the paper. The repair is practice to the clock rather than practice in general: plan in five minutes, write in forty, stop. Families are often surprised that shorter essays score higher, because a tight forty-minute essay that argues and concludes beats a sixty-minute narrative that never settles the question asked.

faqs.question: What counts as specific evidence in an IB History answer?
faqs.answer: One named person, one date, one figure, or one precise term attached to the claim being made. The examination draws a hard line between an accurate claim and a supported one, and most mid-band scripts are full of claims that are true and unsupported. A useful test: underline every claim in a marked essay and write the single piece of evidence beside it. Where nothing can be written, the claim was asserted. Students usually find they can support the first half of each paragraph and not the second, because the second half was being invented while writing.

faqs.question: How many named examples does a History student need per topic?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most Dubai candidates try to carry, and better organised. One page per topic is the working standard: the handful of people worth naming, the dates that actually matter, three or four figures with their source, two or three precise terms, and two historiographical positions with the reason each reads the evidence that way. Six topics at one page each is a complete revision resource and it fits in a folder. Students who revise from thirty pages per topic know everything shallowly in April and nothing precisely in May, which is the most common revision failure in the subject.

faqs.question: How do we find out which topics my child's Dubai school teaches for History?
faqs.answer: Email the department and ask for all of it at once: the prescribed subject for the source paper and its case studies, both world history topics and the order they are taught, the Higher Level regional option and its three sections, the internal deadlines for the historical investigation, and the mock examination window. Keep the reply. Those choices are made by the school, not by the IB, and they determine which revision material is useful and which tutor is a genuine match. Families who skip this step frequently buy a term of help on content their child will never sit.

faqs.question: What is the difference between evaluating a source's origin and its purpose?
faqs.answer: Origin is who produced it, when, and in what position to know. Purpose is what they were trying to achieve by producing it. The two generate different values and different limitations, and the marks come from connecting each to the specific claim being discussed rather than to the document in general. Writing that a source is biased earns almost nothing, because every source has a perspective. Writing that an author in a particular office, writing for a particular audience in a particular year, had reason to understate a specific thing earns the mark reliably, every time it is done properly.

faqs.question: Is it a problem that my child memorises dates but cannot build an argument?
faqs.answer: It is a solvable problem, and it is the opposite of the usual one. A student with secure chronology has the raw material that most candidates lack; what is missing is the structure that turns it into marks. The sequence that works is short: decide the answer before writing, state it in the first paragraph, make every paragraph serve it, and end each paragraph with a sentence saying why it matters to the question. Four or five marked essays with those four instructions typically moves such a student two rungs, because nothing has to be learned, only reorganised.

faqs.question: How should a History student revise two years of content in ten weeks?
faqs.answer: Front-load the topic taught last, which is usually the second world history topic and the one known least, and put the first full timed paper in week three rather than week nine so the bad news arrives while there is still time. Then give the hours to the weakest section of the Higher Level regional option, because that paper carries three essays and most candidates have revised two sections properly. Keep the final week for retrieval only: review the one-page sheets, write five-minute plans for past questions, and stop writing full essays. No new content after week nine.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child narrow a historical investigation question?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the most valuable thing a tutor does in the component. Narrowing is a teachable skill and bright students resist it, because a smaller question feels less ambitious. The test is mechanical: name the two sources you will evaluate, say what each one lets you claim, and state the answer you expect to reach. A question that cannot survive those three sentences cannot survive 2,200 words either. What a tutor must not do is choose the question, construct the argument or write any part of the investigation, and that boundary belongs in writing before the first session.

faqs.question: Is it acceptable to use a translated source in the historical investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the honest handling of it earns marks rather than costing them. Name the translation used, acknowledge that the student is reading at one remove from the original, and treat that distance as a limitation in the source evaluation. That is precisely the kind of methodological awareness the reflection section rewards, because it is a real constraint historians work with constantly. What is not acceptable is presenting a translated reading as engagement with the original, which is both dishonest and straightforward for a moderator to spot in the way the source is discussed.

faqs.question: What are the rules about AI summaries of historical scholarship?
faqs.answer: The school's own academic-honesty policy is the binding document, and it should be read before any use. The practical risk is specific to this subject: a model-generated summary of a historian's position is not a reading of that historian, and a student relying on one writes authoritative-sounding sentences that cite nothing checkable. If the model has invented a position, the candidate has attributed a view to a named scholar who never held it, which a moderator will treat seriously. Declare any use, and read at least one real page of any scholar whose name appears in the investigation.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level History need a different tutor from Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because of the regional option. Higher Level candidates sit a third paper with three essays on a regional option chosen by the department, and that content is specific: a tutor who has taught one option is not automatically useful for another, and three essays in one paper leaves no room to avoid an unfamiliar section. The source paper and the world history topics are shared between the levels, so a Standard Level specialist can be an excellent match there. Ask which regional option and which three sections before booking, and ask what the tutor has taught.

faqs.question: How many essays should a History candidate write before the examinations?
faqs.answer: Enough that writing one stops being an event, which for most candidates means one a fortnight through DP1 and one a week through the final term, all sat to the clock and all marked. The number matters less than the conditions: an essay written over two evenings with the notes open teaches very little, while a forty-minute essay written cold and marked against the descriptors teaches a great deal. Ask any prospective tutor how many marked timed essays their plan includes and over how many weeks, because that number is the mechanism that moves the grade.

faqs.question: Does Diploma History help with a law or politics degree application?
faqs.answer: It is well regarded for both, because it evidences exactly the skills those degrees assess: sustained argument, handling of evidence, and the ability to weigh competing interpretations. Some law programmes name it among preferred subjects, though very few require any specific subject beyond general entry requirements. The honest position is that it helps and does not gate: read the published entry requirements for the specific universities on your child's list rather than relying on general advice, and treat the overall points total as the thing most offers actually turn on.

faqs.question: What does History tuition cost in Dubai, and what should the hour include?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 at the budget end, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, to AED 200 to 450 and above for a Diploma specialist on Bestimate's 2026 table, with BartyED quoting AED 650 at the premium end. In an essay subject the figure to interrogate is not the rate but the marking: reading a fifteen-mark essay properly with the rung named and three corrections written takes twenty to thirty minutes. Ask whether the essay is sat before the session, marked before it starts, and whether that sits inside the quoted rate.

faqs.question: Can essays be marked between sessions rather than during them?
faqs.answer: That is the only arrangement worth paying a specialist rate for. An essay written during a session consumes the hour you are paying for and produces a script nobody has marked. The efficient shape is the reverse: the student sits the essay to the clock between sessions, the tutor marks it before the session with the rung named and three specific corrections, and the hour is spent entirely on the read-back and on the next attempt. Confirm before booking whether marking happens between sessions and whether it is included in the rate or billed separately.

dubai/ib-dp-history-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one timed essay and a department email
dubai/ib-dp-history-tutor.closingBody: If your child sits Diploma History at a Dubai school, two cheap actions will tell you more than any amount of research. Email the department for the prescribed subject, the two world history topics, the Higher Level regional option and the investigation deadlines. Then take the free first lesson, built around one timed essay sat beforehand and marked against the band descriptors with the rung named. Between them those two artefacts identify whether you are buying content, argument or timing. One free lesson per student, no card details taken. Lessons run live and one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time; there are no home visits in the UAE, and that service runs only in India.

intro.heading: Two problems in one search
paragraphs: The phrase a parent types usually encodes a logistical problem as well as an academic one. The academic part is a Diploma subject that has stopped responding to effort, or an internally assessed component drifting towards a deadline. The logistical part is that a Grade 12 timetable in Dubai leaves almost nothing spare, and adding a journey to the evening feels impossible. Home tutoring reads like the answer to both at once, which is why the search exists.

The academic problem deserves the longer answer, because the Diploma fails in specific places and generic tutoring misses them. Six subjects across the groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard, graded 1 to 7 on a 45-point total, with internally assessed work in every subject and three core components running alongside. That is nine or ten separate deadlines competing for the same evenings, and a DP2 student in trouble is very often not short of understanding. They are short of sequence.

The logistical problem has a cleaner solution than most families expect. The reason a home visit appeals is that it removes the student's journey, and online one-to-one removes it too, while also removing the tutor's journey. In Dubai that second removal matters more than it sounds, because a late-afternoon crossing consumes most of another session in each direction, and that time is inside every published in-home rate whether a provider itemises it or not.

There is a harder consequence of the drive, and it decides more than the money. A visiting tutor has to be someone who can physically reach your community at the hour your child is free, which means the pool is set by geography rather than by subject. For mainstream Standard Level subjects in central Dubai that pool is deep enough not to matter. For Higher Level Chemistry in Al Furjan, or Design Technology anywhere, it frequently contains nobody suitable at any hourly rate. That is the part of the in-home trade nobody prices, because it does not show up as a cost. It shows up as a competent generalist teaching a Higher Level course they have never marked, and at Diploma level the marked work makes that visible inside a fortnight.

So the honest position is stated up front rather than buried. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, in Dubai or any other emirate; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Diploma support for UAE families is delivered one student with one tutor over live video, with the student writing on a shared whiteboard the tutor annotates. Dirham figures on this page are market rates with the publisher named, and the single commitment made is a free first lesson, one per student and one student per family, with no card details collected.

dubai/ib-dp-home-tutor.programmesIntro: This page is about the Diploma, but two of the three IB programmes feed into it and the handover is where a lot of Dubai students come unstuck. Here are the three, with what each hands on to the next and where the join tends to break.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects selected across the groups, normally three Higher Level and three Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, with internally assessed work in every subject. Alongside them sit Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, and a small number of points come from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination. The award conditions attached to the core and to individual grades are set out by the school's Diploma coordinator, who is the person to ask.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts sit the May session, and each school runs its own internal deadlines for drafts and uploads well ahead of it. Those internal dates, not the examination window, are what actually constrain a Grade 12 student's time, and the first question any Dubai Diploma plan should answer is which school's calendar applies. New Diploma provision is also expanding here, with three of the seven schools opening for the 2026-27 intake offering the IB.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four lettered criteria per subject, each out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade by the school, with the Personal Project in the final year. Students arrive in the Diploma from here with good research habits, familiarity with criterion language and, frequently, less content than students coming from IGCSE. The gap that bites is depth in the sciences and algebraic fluency, both of which are cheap to fix in the first Diploma term.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai continuum schools run the Middle Years Programme to Grade 10 and then offer a choice between the Diploma and a British route, which means the decision and the grade problem often arrive together for a Grade 10 family. An honest read on whether Higher Level will be viable is worth more at that point than a term of general support.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no external examination, ending in the PYP Exhibition. Relevant to a Diploma page only because the habits built here, particularly written explanation and the expectation of justifying a method, are the ones the Diploma later rewards heavily. Dubai families who move into the IB later frequently find that is the part their child has not been asked for before.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's primary IB cohort is large and highly mobile. For families planning a long run through to the Diploma in this emirate, the practical thing to know is that KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies provision begins in these years and continues alongside whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for.

dubai/ib-dp-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects by group, with the component that decides the grade in each and the thing a DP2 student most often has not been taught explicitly. These are the subjects Dubai families most frequently request at Diploma level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Group five, and the subject most likely to be the reason a Diploma total is lower than expected. At Higher Level the marks go on working presented out of the order the mark scheme credits, on proof structure and on calculus set up well then executed carelessly. The exploration needs genuine mathematics applied to something the student chose, and vague aims cap it early.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Group four. Long answers need a sequence most students have never been shown: define, state the relationship, substitute, evaluate. Unit and significant-figure discipline leaks marks across every paper. The internal investigation stands or falls on a measurable, controllable research question, which is usually worth a session of its own in DP1.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Group four. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry most Higher Level losses. One unfamiliar mechanism tells you whether the student understands electron behaviour or has memorised arrows, and if it is the latter, bonding has to be rebuilt before any past paper work is worth doing.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Group four, and marked far more precisely than it looks. Command terms separate a 4 from a 6, and a student who writes everything they know lands in the middle every time. The statistical treatment in the investigation is where internally assessed marks are most often left unclaimed.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Group three. Diagram accuracy and the final evaluation sentence carry marks students concede without noticing, and Higher Level adds quantitative work rewarding arithmetic care. The internally assessed commentaries need article selection supervised early, because an article too broad or too old cannot support the required diagram and theory.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Group three. Theories must be applied to the stimulus rather than recited, and the pre-released Higher Level case study rewards structured preparation across months rather than an intensive before the paper. Ratio and investment appraisal work is where careless candidates concede the easiest marks available.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Group one. The unseen non-literary paper rewards an explicit analytical method, and most students have never been given one. The individual oral needs a global issue narrow enough to defend with two supporting extracts. Higher Level adds an essay on a studied work, which is where planning discipline shows.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Group two. Productive skills decide the grade and students over-prepare receptive ones. The written task is marked on message, language and conceptual understanding of audience and purpose. Weekly corrected speaking practice is the single fastest-moving component in the subject and the hardest to get in a group.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Group two, and in Dubai the subject with the widest spread of starting points in any classroom, from household fluency with weak script to no prior exposure. Support has to be matched to the actual starting point rather than the course title, which is why individual work is usually the only format that functions here.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Group three. Studies must be used as evidence for an argument rather than listed, and research methods vocabulary is examined directly. The experimental study rewards a simple replicable design over an ambitious one, and ethical commentary carries marks students routinely skip.

sections.heading: In-home against online for a Diploma student in Dubai
paragraphs: The home-tutoring question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is published across sources in the AED 180 to 500 per hour range, with Bestimate's 2026 table at 180 to 350 and some home tutors quoted up to 500, and monthly in-home packages appearing at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. For a family that wants a person in the room, those are the real numbers and they are not unreasonable for what they involve.

What the premium pays for is travel, and in this city travel is expensive in a specific way. A tutor crossing Dubai in the late afternoon gives up most of another session in each direction, which is why the in-home band sits above the online band for identical expertise. The cost is real rather than invented, and it is also why in-home sessions tend to be longer and later than a tired Grade 12 student can use well.

The dimension that matters more, though, is the pool. A visiting tutor must live or work within reach of your community at the hour your child is free. For Standard Level mathematics in Al Barsha that constraint is harmless. For Higher Level Chemistry in Al Furjan, or Design Technology or Music anywhere in the emirate, it often means the available visiting tutor is a competent generalist rather than a subject specialist, and at Diploma level that difference shows up in the marking within a fortnight.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Diploma support here is one student with one tutor over live video. sections.heading: The Diploma's six groups, and where each one loses marks
paragraphs: A Diploma total is built from six subject grades plus core points, and families chasing a number often do not know which group is costing them. Setting out the groups properly makes the diagnosis possible: a student at 32 points with two Higher Level sciences at 4 has a different problem from a student at 32 with a 3 in a group two language, and they need different purchases.

The pattern across groups is consistent enough to use. Group one and group three lose marks on argument and judgement: evidence assembled without a conclusion. Group four loses them on precision and on investigation design. Group five loses them on presentation of working and on interpretation. Group two loses them almost entirely on productive skills, which is the hardest thing to practise in any group setting. Group six loses them in the written components students did not expect to matter.

Choosing which subject to support first is therefore an arithmetic question rather than a sentimental one. Recoverable marks per hour of work is the right measure, and it usually points at a subject where the student is at 4 or 5 with a technique problem rather than at the subject they dislike most. A tutor who cannot help a family make that ranking is not giving the most valuable advice available.

The table names each group, what it covers, the choices Dubai students commonly make within it, and the dominant failure mode. Use it to work out which single subject is worth starting with, rather than spreading a budget across three.

sections.heading: DP1 and DP2, stage by stage, with the decision at each point
paragraphs: The Diploma is two years with a very uneven distribution of pressure, and families who plan it as a steady run are surprised twice: once in the autumn of the second year when the internally assessed components all arrive together, and again in the final term when there is no slack left. Mapping the stages makes the pressure visible early enough to do something about it.

No specific dates appear here, deliberately. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing on this page has been confirmed from the primary source, and an unverified date inside a revision plan is worse than no date. Every deadline that matters is either set by your child's school or published by the IB, and the Diploma coordinator is the person who can confirm both. What can be planned without dates is the sequence, which is what the table does.

The useful habit is to treat each stage as ending in a decision rather than a date. Does the Higher Level choice still look right. Is the research question answerable. Has the error class identified in the autumn actually moved. Is the Extended Essay going to be finished on the school's timetable or on an optimistic one. Each of those decisions is cheap to make early and expensive to make late.

For a family buying support, the stage table also indicates when to spend. The autumn of DP1 is the cheapest point per mark because there is time for a changed habit to settle. The autumn of DP2 is the busiest and the most consequential. The final term is for timed marked papers and nothing else, because new content learned there has no time to become reliable.
