intro.heading: A coursework mark you cannot account for is a record-keeping problem
paragraphs: A Diploma student carries roughly six internally assessed components, one per subject, and each is marked by the school against published criteria before the IB moderates the result. The marks matter: in most subjects the internal component is a meaningful share of the final grade, and unlike an examination it is produced slowly, in the open, over weeks. That should make it the most transparent part of the Diploma for a family. In practice it is the least, because almost nobody keeps the record that would make it transparent.

The pattern is familiar in Dubai. A student works on a science investigation or a mathematics exploration for a term, submits a draft, receives a comment, submits a final version, and a mark appears. The mark is lower than hoped. Asked what happened, the student says they did what the teacher said. Asked which criterion lost the marks, nobody knows. Asked whether the second version was better than the first, nobody can demonstrate it, because the first version was overwritten and the feedback was verbal.

The work on this page is organised to make that impossible. Every draft that passes through a session is kept, dated and scored against each criterion, and the score is written down with the reason attached. When the next version arrives it is scored again, and the two sit side by side. Movement is then a matter of record rather than of opinion: criterion B went from the lower band to the middle one on this date because the student added an uncertainty analysis, and here are both versions.

That record does three jobs at once, which is why it is worth the small effort of keeping it. It tells a family whether paid support is working, within about three weeks and without anybody needing to understand the subject. It gives the student an authorship trail — their own dated versions, in their own words — which is the simplest possible answer if anyone ever asks whether the work is theirs. And it makes the conversation with the school specific: not my child deserves more, but criterion C scored here and here is why.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own document shared on screen and annotated while they watch. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For coursework that is the better arrangement: the object of the work is a file, screen-sharing shows exactly which line is under discussion, and the family selects a reader who has marked that subject's component before rather than whoever happens to live within a short drive of their community.

dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-online-t.programmesIntro: Internally assessed work exists at every level of the IB, and a student's habits with it are formed long before DP2. The programmes below set what a Dubai student brings to their Diploma coursework, with a note on the habit that costs marks.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Each Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component with its own criteria, format and length conventions: a scientific investigation, a mathematical exploration, a historical investigation, a business research project, a language oral and so on. The school marks them and the IB moderates a sample. Confirm every weighting and length limit against the current subject guide, which your school holds, because they differ by subject and are revised periodically.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set their own internal draft deadlines, and those dates, not the IB upload, are what a family should plan around. The commonest avoidable loss here is a student whose only feedback round was spent on presentation because the substantive work arrived too late to change.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assesses every subject against four criteria and trains students to read a rubric and locate themselves in a band. That is the single most useful habit for Diploma coursework, and students from continuum schools usually have it. What MYP does not build is the discipline of keeping versions, because its tasks are shorter and feedback is continuous.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a high concentration of IB continuum schools, so a large share of the Diploma cohort arrives rubric-literate. Those students benefit most from a scoring record rather than from teaching, because they can act on a band descriptor once somebody shows them where their own draft sits in it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE coursework, where it exists, is tightly specified and heavily scaffolded, and much of the qualification is assessed by written papers. Students arriving from a British-curriculum Year 11 are used to being told what a good answer contains. Diploma coursework asks them to design the task, which is a different skill, and the first draft usually shows a well-written piece of work answering nobody's question in particular.
programmes.countryNote: With UK curriculum at 37 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, this is the commonest route into Diploma coursework in the emirate. One scored read of a first draft in the opening weeks of the component tells a family precisely which of the two problems they have, and it is usually not the one they expected.

programmes.name: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS
programmes.description: The core adds a 4,000-word research essay, an assessed essay and exhibition, and an unmarked but mandatory experiential programme, all competing with six internal components for the same months. None of them can be rescued at the same time as the others, which is why ordering the work by marks at risk beats ordering it by nearest deadline.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai schools the heaviest coursework weeks and the Extended Essay internal deadline tend to land in the same half-term. A family holding a dated record of each component's current criterion scores can order that fortnight rationally; a family without one orders it by whichever teacher sent the most recent email.

dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-online-t.subjectsIntro: Internal assessment means something different in each subject, and so does the evidence that it is improving. The notes below say what the component is and what visible change looks like in it, which is the thing a family can actually check between drafts.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: An individual scientific investigation. Movement between drafts shows up as a research question narrowed to something measurable, controlled variables actually controlled, and an evaluation that names specific limitations rather than apologising generally.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: A scientific investigation where data handling carries most of the weight. Visible improvement looks like uncertainties propagated rather than mentioned, graphs with error bars that are used in the argument, and a conclusion tied to the data instead of to the textbook.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: An investigation in which the treatment of uncertainty is usually the difference between bands. A second draft that moves has quantified uncertainty, justified the number of trials, and discussed whether the relationship found is the one the theory predicts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A mathematical exploration marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Improvement looks like notation made consistent, a genuine personal reason for the topic, and mathematics used rather than quoted.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: An exploration more often built on real data, which brings its own failure mode: a dataset described at length and modelled thinly. A draft that has moved shows a model fitted, tested and criticised, with the limitations of the data stated plainly.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A historical investigation with a sources section, an investigation and a reflection. Visible movement is a question narrowed to something answerable from available sources, and an evaluation that weighs two accounts against each other rather than describing each in turn.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A portfolio of commentaries on published articles rather than a single piece of work, which changes what evidence looks like: three separate short pieces, each applying a different part of the syllabus, each needing its own diagram used as analysis.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A research project on a real organisation. The commonest drift is towards description of the company, and a draft that has improved shows tools applied to a defined research question with the limitations of the evidence acknowledged.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: An experimental study written up formally. Movement appears in the method section first: a procedure specified tightly enough to replicate, ethical considerations handled properly, and an analysis that matches the design rather than the hypothesis.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: An individual oral on a global issue with extracts. Evidence of progress is narrowing: a global issue specific enough that two extracts can genuinely demonstrate it, with a recording that stays on the issue rather than touring the works.

sections.heading: What a marked internal assessment draft proves, and what it only suggests
paragraphs: An IB DP internal assessment online tutor in Dubai is useful in direct proportion to the record they leave behind. Families are routinely offered things that look like evidence of progress and are not: an encouraging verbal report, a teacher's predicted grade, a tutor's confidence, a student's own sense that the work is better now. None of those survives contact with a criterion. The table below separates what genuinely proves something from what merely resembles proof.

The distinction matters because the two are priced the same. An hour of pleasant discussion about a mathematics exploration and an hour producing a scored annotated version of it cost identically in this market, and only one of them leaves a family able to answer the question they came with. The useful test of any coursework arrangement is simple: at the end of it, what document exists that did not exist before, and what number is written on it?

There is a second reason to insist on the record, and it concerns the student rather than the family. A dated sequence of versions in the student's own words is the plainest evidence of authorship available, and it costs nothing to keep. Coursework is produced out of sight over weeks, the market contains providers selling finished work, and a student who can show their own drafting history is in a straightforwardly better position than one who cannot.

The last row of the table is the one families find hardest to accept. A teacher's predicted grade is not evidence about a specific component; it is a professional judgement formed across a whole subject, and it can be generous or harsh for reasons that have nothing to do with the coursework in question. Treating it as a measurement is the commonest way a family discovers a problem two weeks before submission instead of two months before it.

sections.heading: Draft one to draft two: what movement actually looks like
paragraphs: The abstract claim that coursework improves is worth replacing with a concrete account of what changes between versions. The table below follows a science investigation, the component Dubai students most often seek help with, through a normal two-cycle arc. Nothing in it is unusual or heroic. It is what a competent drafting process looks like when somebody scores each version and the student does the work in between.

The useful feature of this sequence is where the movement sits. Almost none of it comes from better writing. It comes from a research question narrowed until it is measurable, from variables actually controlled rather than listed, from uncertainty quantified instead of mentioned, and from an evaluation that names a specific limitation and its effect on the conclusion. Those are substantive changes a student makes to their own work, which is why the gap between sessions is the part of the arrangement that produces the marks.

Two warnings belong with the table. The criterion names and mark totals differ between subjects and are set by the current subject guide your school holds, so the column describing what is under test is framed by what it examines rather than by a letter that may change. And the movement shown is typical rather than promised; a student who has not collected usable data cannot be drafted into a strong investigation, which is exactly why the question and method clinic exists before any of this starts.

What the sequence rules out is also valuable. If a second scored read on the same component shows no movement on any criterion, something specific is wrong: the student did not make the changes, the changes were the wrong ones, or the diagnosis missed the real problem. All three are findings, and all three are better discovered in week four than after submission. A record makes that visible; a weekly conversation does not.

sections.heading: Reading a supervisor's comment on coursework
paragraphs: Dubai teachers write coursework feedback under real time pressure, often across a hundred pieces of work, and the result is compressed. Parents are rarely given the key, and students frequently act on the surface meaning rather than the intended one. Decoding it is free and is the highest-return ten minutes available to a family, because it converts feedback the school has already supplied into instructions the student can follow.

Several comments recur across subjects with stable meanings. More detail on your method almost never means write a longer method; it means the procedure is not specified tightly enough for somebody else to repeat it. Discuss your results means the analysis has reported numbers without interpreting them against the question. Your evaluation is general means the limitations named could apply to any investigation in any subject, which earns nothing. Consider your personal engagement, in a mathematics exploration, means the topic has no visible reason for existing beyond its convenience.

A second class of comment is about scope, and it is the one students most often misread as encouragement to add. Narrow your focus, be more selective and this is ambitious are all instructions to remove material, not to explain it better. Coursework length conventions are set by the subject guide and are tighter than students assume, so adding to a draft that is already over its conventions compounds the problem the comment was raising.

There is also a boundary visible in these comments that families should understand rather than resent. A supervisor's permitted involvement in coursework is defined, and the amount of comment they may give on a draft is limited. A teacher who writes three lines on a twelve-page investigation may be following the rules rather than neglecting your child, and a family who understands that stops reading brevity as indifference. It is also a sound reason to use an external scored reader, whose role is explicitly to mark and diagnose rather than to supervise.

sections.heading: A six-week record across two components
paragraphs: Most Dubai families arrive needing help with more than one component, because the coursework weeks cluster. The six-week shape below handles two at once without pretending that both can be worked in parallel. It alternates, and it is built so that the student always has three weeks of their own work in front of them while the other component rests.

The sequence front-loads measurement. Weeks one and two score what exists on both components, which is the only way to decide which one deserves the hours. A family that chooses by nearest deadline usually spends its money on the component that was already in decent shape, because the deadline that arrived first was the one the school scheduled first, not the one at greatest risk.

The final column is the point of publishing this at all. Everything in it can be checked by a parent who has never studied the subject: a document exists or it does not, a score is written on it or it is not, two versions sit side by side or only one does. Nobody needs to judge whether a mathematics exploration is good to verify that it has been scored twice and that the second score is higher.

If a fortnight passes with no new artefact on either component, the cause is almost always one of three things in a Dubai school year: a clash with the Extended Essay internal deadline, a week of mocks nobody flagged, or data that was never actually collected and a student covering for it. All three show up in the record quickly, and the third is the one worth checking first, because it is the only one that cannot be solved by rescheduling.

sections.heading: Why the mark the school gives is not always the mark that arrives
paragraphs: Internally assessed work is marked by the school and moderated by the IB, which samples work from each school and checks whether the marks awarded match the standard. If the school has been generous across the sample, marks can come down; if it has been harsh, they can go up. The adjustment applies to the cohort rather than to an individual appeal, and it means a mark a teacher writes on a draft is an informed prediction rather than a final result.

This is the strongest practical argument for a record. A student whose work holds up against the published criteria when read by somebody outside the school is in a different position from one whose mark depends on a generous internal standard. The record does not change how moderation works, and nothing a tutor does can. What it does is tell a family, before submission, whether the mark they have been shown is likely to survive an external reading.

It also changes which feedback is worth acting on. A comment that reflects a school's house style — a preferred structure, a favoured referencing format, a particular way of laying out a method — is worth following for the sake of the relationship and carries little weight externally. A comment about whether the evaluation names specific limitations goes directly to a criterion. Distinguishing between them is most of what an external scored read supplies, and students cannot reliably do it themselves.

None of this is a reason to treat the school as an adversary. A subject teacher marking a hundred coursework pieces, with their own cohort's results on the line, is in general applying the criteria as carefully as time allows, and they know the student. The family's job is narrower: to make sure the student's work is strong against the published descriptors rather than strong relative to the class, because moderation reads the former and the class ranking is invisible to it.

sections.heading: Six components, one second year: ordering by marks at risk
paragraphs: The structural problem of DP2 is not that coursework is hard; it is that six components, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge all have internal deadlines inside the same two terms, and schools set them independently. Families respond by working on whatever is due next, which is the one ordering guaranteed to be wrong, because the nearest deadline carries no information about where the marks are.

Ordering by marks at risk requires two facts per component: roughly what share of the subject grade it carries, and roughly where the current draft sits against the criteria. The first is in the subject guide the school holds. The second is a scored read. With both, the arithmetic is usually unambiguous: a component sitting in a low band on a heavily weighted subject deserves the hours, and a component already in a solid band does not, even if it is due on Sunday.

The honest part of this is that something will be left imperfect, and the plan should name it in writing. A student with three deadlines in a fortnight cannot bring all three to their best, and pretending otherwise produces three mediocre submissions instead of two good ones and one adequate one. Writing down which component is being allowed to sit at its current level is uncomfortable and it is the decision that most improves the total.

Two Dubai-specific factors belong in the ordering. Laboratory and apparatus access is finite and timetabled, so a science component whose data collection has not happened may be constrained by the school calendar rather than by the student. And Ramadan changes the household rhythm and the school day; sessions move to post-Iftar slots readily, but the quantity of deep work available in those weeks is lower, and a plan built on the assumption that it is not will fail.

sections.heading: The authorship trail, and who may lawfully teach your child
paragraphs: Coursework is where academic honesty is most exposed, because it is produced over weeks and out of sight, and the market contains providers who sell finished work. One researched competitor advertises completed Internal Assessments outright. Under IB rules the consequence of submitting work that is not the student's own falls on the candidate and can reach the loss of the Diploma. The record described on this page is, among other things, the simplest protection against ever being in that position.

The boundary for a tutor is narrow and completely workable. A tutor may read, score against the criteria, explain what a descriptor is asking for, model a move on a different example, ask the questions that expose a gap, and record what was discussed and what changed. A tutor may not put sentences into the student's document, choose the research question on the student's behalf, restructure the text themselves, or supply the content of an evaluation or reflection. Every word a school uploads must be the student's own, and dated versions in the student's own words demonstrate that without anyone having to assert it.

Two further restraints are worth stating because competitors breach them. Past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge or Pearson; a legitimate provider cites and links them rather than distributing copies, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright one. And no tutoring provider should attach the name of a regulator — KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education — or of an examination board to language about approval, accreditation or authorisation unless it holds that specific permit and can produce the number. IB Gram holds none and implies none.

On permits, the position is clear and useful to know before paying anyone. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule has been published, any amount quoted to you is unverified. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules additionally bar school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so the idea of hiring your child's own subject teacher privately is an arrangement to decline.

sections.heading: Dubai practicalities, and what coursework support costs here
paragraphs: Dubai's private-school sector taught 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, according to the Dubai Media Office, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment and UK curriculum 37 per cent. The scale has a direct effect on coursework: large cohorts mean a subject teacher may be marking a hundred internally assessed pieces, and detailed per-student criterion commentary at that volume is not realistic however good the teacher is. A second scored reader is a practical response rather than a criticism.

The emirate's calendar shapes the work too. Schools set their own internal draft deadlines ahead of the IB upload, and those are the dates that bind. Ramadan shortens the school day and shifts the evening; sessions move to post-Iftar slots on request, but the amount of deep work available in those weeks is genuinely lower and a plan should say so. The summer between DP1 and DP2 is the best uninterrupted stretch for data collection and first drafts, and it is also when a large share of Dubai families travel, which an online arrangement survives and an in-person one does not.

This page does not publish an IB examination or results date. The IB's own site cannot be verified by automated checking, and an unconfirmed date is worse than none for a family planning around it; UAE schools sit the May session, and your DP coordinator holds the current timetable and the internal deadlines that matter more. Where dates are published and sourced they make the same point about early deadlines: Cambridge's March 2027 series runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with its November 2026 timetable ending 19 November 2026.

On price, published Dubai market rates are wide. Budget online platforms advertise from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150 to AED 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists run about AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table showing AED 200 to AED 450 or more. In-home visits, with travel inside the rate, run roughly AED 180 to AED 500, and premium named tutoring reaches AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026 and not our price list. IB Gram arranges no home visits in the UAE: Dubai coursework support is one-to-one over live video, and the first diagnostic hour is free with no card required.

process.title: Send the draft and the school's own deadline
process.description: Share whatever exists, the subject and level, and the school's internal draft deadline rather than the IB date. Incomplete work is more useful than a tidy summary, because the gaps are the diagnosis, and most families send the wrong deadline because nobody told them the two differ.

process.title: The free scored read
process.description: One hour, online and one-to-one, no card required. The draft is read beforehand, scored against every criterion, and returned annotated with two or three changes ranked by marks at risk. That document is the first entry in the record, and it is yours whether or not anything is booked afterwards.

process.title: Agree the cycle and keep both versions
process.description: A drafting block is agreed as scored read, student revision, second scored read, final check, with a deliberate gap for the student's own work. Nothing is overwritten: each version is kept dated with its scores, which is what makes movement a matter of record rather than of opinion.

process.title: Revise alone, then be scored again
process.description: The two to three weeks between sessions are the student's. A tutor reads, scores, questions, models and records, and supplies no sentences for the document. The second score sits beside the first, naming which criterion moved and because of what change the student made.

process.title: Review the record, then stop or reorder
process.description: If criterion scores moved, the remaining hours go to the component with the most marks still at risk. If they did not, the diagnosis was wrong or the changes were not made, and the arrangement changes. Continuing to buy hours the record does not support is the commonest overspend here.

whyPoints.title: The record is the product
whyPoints.description: Dated drafts, a score and a reason against each criterion, and the change between versions written down. A family can judge the arrangement from that within three weeks without understanding the subject, and can stop without an awkward conversation because the evidence makes the decision.

whyPoints.title: The gap between sessions is deliberate
whyPoints.description: Two to three weeks of the student's own revision is where the marks actually come from. We recommend buying nothing during it, which costs billable hours and consistently produces better coursework than a weekly arrangement over the same period.

whyPoints.title: Ordered by marks at risk, not by deadline
whyPoints.description: Working on whatever is due next is the one ordering guaranteed to be wrong. Scoring every existing draft first makes the arithmetic clear, and the plan names in writing which component is being allowed to sit at its current level, because something always is.

whyPoints.title: An authorship trail the student owns
whyPoints.description: Versions in the student's own words, each dated, are the plainest evidence of authorship available and cost nothing to keep. Providers in this market sell finished coursework; under IB rules the consequence of submitting it falls on the candidate, up to the loss of the Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Readers who have marked that component
whyPoints.description: A Chemistry investigation and a mathematics exploration fail in different ways against different criteria. Online delivery means a Dubai family selects on whether the reader has marked that subject's component rather than on who covers their area, which for coursework is the decisive question.

whyPoints.title: A stated fallback instead of a placement
whyPoints.description: When no specialist in a particular subject's component is free, we say so and offer a different slot, a generic research-writing read on the parts that are subject-neutral, or a wait. Placing a generalist and describing them as a specialist is how the upper bands in this market get justified.

faqs.question: How do we know an internal assessment draft has actually improved?
faqs.answer: By holding two dated versions, each scored against the same criteria, and reading the scores side by side. That is the only comparison that settles it. A draft can read more fluently and score identically, because in most components the marks sit in the method, the data handling and the evaluation rather than in the prose. If a second scored read shows no movement on any criterion, that is a finding worth having in week four: either the changes were not made, or they were the wrong ones, or the original diagnosis missed the real problem.

faqs.question: What should a scored coursework read come back with?
faqs.answer: Four things, in writing. A score against every criterion with one sentence of reasoning each. Annotations on the draft itself showing where the problem sits. Two or three changes ranked by the marks they put at risk, so the student knows what to do first. And an honest note of anything that can no longer be changed, such as data that was never collected or a question too broad to rescue this late. A read that comes back as general encouragement has cost an hour and left no record.

faqs.question: Can we find out the criterion score before the school marks the work?
faqs.answer: You can find out where a draft currently sits against the published criteria, which is not the same as knowing the mark. An external reader applies the descriptors and reports a band with reasons; the school then marks the submitted version and the IB moderates a sample from the cohort. The value of the earlier reading is timing rather than prediction: it arrives while there is still a feedback round and a revision left, which is the only point at which the information is worth anything.

faqs.question: My daughter's coursework mark came out below the mark on her draft. How?
faqs.answer: Three ordinary explanations. The final version may differ from the draft that was commented on, sometimes in ways that lost marks. A teacher's comment on a draft is an informed prediction rather than a mark, and the submitted work is marked afresh. And the IB moderates a sample from each school, so if the cohort's marks sat above the standard they can be adjusted downwards. None of this is an appeal route for one student. It is an argument for checking the work against the published descriptors before submission rather than after.

faqs.question: How many drafts of an internally assessed component does a student get?
faqs.answer: Schools differ, and the supervisor's permitted involvement in coursework is itself defined, so one substantive feedback round is common and two is generous. That constraint decides when outside help is worth having: before the school's feedback round, so the student uses it on the remaining problems rather than on the obvious ones. Families who commission a scored read after the school's only round have paid for information they can no longer fully act on. Ask the coordinator how many rounds your child's subject allows.

faqs.question: What evidence shows my child wrote their coursework themselves?
faqs.answer: A dated sequence of their own versions, kept rather than overwritten, plus a brief note of what each outside session covered. That costs nothing to maintain and it is the plainest answer available if anybody ever asks. It also helps the student, because the reflection elements several components require are much easier to write from real notes than from memory. Any provider who discourages keeping this trail, or who returns work with changes already made in the document, is telling you something important about their model.

faqs.question: Our school gives one round of feedback. Is a second outside reader allowed?
faqs.answer: Getting feedback on your own work is a normal part of learning and is not what academic honesty rules prohibit. What they prohibit is submitting work that is not the student's own. A reader who scores a draft against published criteria, explains what a descriptor asks for and questions the student's reasoning is doing something legitimate; a reader who edits the document to completion is not. Keep the dated versions, keep a note of what each session covered, and tell the supervisor you are getting the work read if you are in any doubt.

faqs.question: How long after starting support should a coursework score move?
faqs.answer: One full drafting cycle, which in practice is three to five weeks: a scored read, two or three weeks of the student's own revision, then a second scored read. Movement appears first on the criteria that respond to specific technical changes, such as specifying controls or propagating uncertainties. Criteria rewarding deeper understanding move more slowly and sometimes not at all this late, which an honest first read says in advance. A provider predicting a particular mark by a particular date is describing something nobody can deliver.

faqs.question: Which component should we work on when three are due at once?
faqs.answer: The one with the most marks at risk, which is rarely the one due first. That requires two facts per component: roughly what share of the subject grade it carries, which is in the subject guide the school holds, and where the current draft sits against the criteria, which is a scored read. A component already in a solid band does not need the hours even if its deadline is nearest. Write down which component is being left at its current level; something always is, and naming it improves the total.

faqs.question: Should we keep a tutor's annotated version of a draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the date, alongside the student's own version from before and after. It is part of the authorship trail and it is also the only way to verify later that the advice given was the advice acted on. Keep it as a separate file rather than merging the annotations into the working document, so the student's own text stays clearly their own. Families who maintain this file find it answers most questions about progress without anyone needing to reopen the subject matter.

faqs.question: What does a weak data section look like in a science investigation?
faqs.answer: Numbers presented and then abandoned. The symptoms are consistent: raw data tabulated without uncertainties, a graph with a line of best fit and no error bars, no justification for the number of trials, and a conclusion that agrees with the textbook rather than with the data gathered. Strong sections treat uncertainty as part of the argument and state what the data cannot support. That shift is usually two or three hours of the student's own work after one scored read, and it is the single largest movement available in most science components.

faqs.question: Can a parent judge coursework without understanding the subject?
faqs.answer: You can judge the record, which is enough. Does a dated draft exist? Is there a score against each criterion with a reason? Is there a second dated version with a second score? Is the second score higher, and does the note say which change moved it? Those four questions require no subject knowledge and they expose a stalled arrangement within three weeks. What a parent cannot do is assess whether an exploration is mathematically interesting, which is exactly why the scoring is written down.

faqs.question: Does the IB ever raise an internally assessed mark rather than lower it?
faqs.answer: Moderation works in both directions. The IB samples work from each school and compares the marks awarded against the standard; a school that has marked harshly across its sample can see marks adjusted upwards, just as a generous school can see them come down. The adjustment applies to the cohort rather than to an individual request. The practical consequence for a family is the same either way: work that holds up against the published descriptors when read from outside the school is in a stronger position than work that depends on a lenient internal standard.

faqs.question: Does online support work for practical and laboratory components?
faqs.answer: For the laboratory work itself, no, and nobody should claim otherwise; the apparatus and the school's safety supervision are the school's. For everything the marks actually depend on, yes. The question's design, the method's specification, the handling of uncertainty, the construction of graphs, the evaluation and the write-up are all document work, and they carry most of the available marks. Screen-sharing shows precisely which line or which figure is under discussion, which is more exact than looking at a page over somebody's shoulder.

faqs.question: Is in-person coursework supervision available from IB Gram in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. We do not arrange in-person tutoring anywhere in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we offer only in India. Dubai coursework support is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own document on screen and annotated while they watch. For internally assessed work that is the stronger arrangement: the family selects a reader who has marked that specific subject's component rather than whoever covers their area, and the arrangement survives the weeks when the family travels.

dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-online-t.closingHeading: One scored read, and you will know where you stand
dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-online-t.closingBody: If a coursework mark has arrived that nobody can account for, the useful first step is one hour and costs nothing. Send the draft, the subject and the school's internal deadline, and take the free scored read: it comes back with a score and a reason against every criterion, annotations on the draft itself, two or three changes ranked by the marks they put at risk, and an honest note on anything that can no longer be changed. Keep the document whether or not you book anything further. It is the first entry in a record most families never get.

intro.heading: Six internal assessments, six sets of criteria, one eight-week window
paragraphs: Internal assessment is not a single task. It is the collective name for the component in each Diploma subject that the school marks and the IB moderates, and every subject's version is different. In the sciences it is a scientific investigation. In mathematics it is an exploration. In history it is a historical investigation with three defined sections. In economics it is a portfolio of three commentaries. In Language A it is an individual oral. The weight differs too: around 20 per cent of the final grade in several subjects, 25 in others, and 30 in some at Standard Level.

That variation is why a parent searching for an internal assessment tutor in Dubai usually needs more than one answer. A student struggling with the Biology investigation has a research-design problem. The same student struggling with the Maths exploration has a personal-engagement and mathematical-communication problem, measured against completely different criteria with a different mark total. Advice that transfers between the two is thin, and a generalist essay tutor cannot supply either.

The second structural feature is moderation. The school marks the IA and submits a sample to the IB, which moderates those marks and can adjust the whole cohort's marks up or down. A student can therefore receive a mark from their teacher that is not the mark that appears on the final certificate. Families in Dubai meet this for the first time in July, usually with no explanation available, and the scenario is common enough that it deserves a section rather than a footnote.

The third is scheduling. Internal deadlines for IAs are set by the school, not by the IB, and Dubai schools tend to cluster them. A DP2 student can face a Chemistry investigation, a Maths exploration, an Economics commentary and the Extended Essay final submission inside six weeks, in the same term as university applications. No single deadline is unreasonable; the stack is. Most of the value in IA coaching is deciding which of the six to get out of the way early, and which can safely be left until the others are banked.

IB Gram matches your child with a subject specialist who works one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the Dubai school day. The first conversation is usually triage: which IAs are due when, what each is worth, and which one is closest to losing marks that cannot be recovered. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. A free trial lesson comes first, one per family, with no card details taken, and the student does the designing, the collecting and the writing throughout.

dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tutor.programmesIntro: Internally assessed work appears long before the Diploma, and how a student handled the earlier version usually predicts the IA. These are the stages we cover and what the internal component looks like at each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Each of the six subjects carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth to a third of the subject grade. The school marks it against published criteria and the IB moderates. Deadlines are set internally, which is why two students in the same city can face completely different IA calendars depending on which school they attend.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools differ sharply in how early they set IA deadlines. Some require a Chemistry investigation before the DP1 summer; others run everything in DP2 term one. Ask for your child's full internal deadline list in writing at the start of DP2 — it is the single document that makes the year plannable.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assessment is entirely criterion-based, with four criteria per subject and no external paper in most schools. Students who learned to read a criterion strand and write to it have a large head start on IA work. Those who treated criteria as administrative detail arrive in the Diploma writing fluent work that does not address the strands.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has substantial IB continuum provision, so a DP1 class often mixes students with five years of criterion-based marking and students who have never seen it. The second group needs the criteria taught explicitly before their first IA draft, not after it comes back.

programmes.name: IGCSE and the pre-Diploma route
programmes.description: Most IGCSE subjects assess practical skills through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than through extended coursework. Students arriving from that route into the Diploma have strong examination technique and limited experience of designing an investigation of their own, which is the first gap a science IA exposes.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment, so the IGCSE-to-Diploma transfer is the most common path into IB here. For these students the first science IA is usually the hardest single piece of work in DP1, and the problem is design rather than content knowledge.

programmes.name: IAs alongside the Extended Essay, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: Six internal assessments do not arrive alone. They share a calendar with a 4,000-word Extended Essay, two TOK tasks and a CAS portfolio that must be completed for the Diploma to be awarded. The core components have their own deadlines, and the school sets those too, which is how a six-week pile-up forms.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the heaviest stacking typically falls between November and February of DP2, overlapping university application deadlines. Families who sequence deliberately — hardest IA first, lowest-weight IA last — lose fewer marks than families who respond to whichever deadline is nearest.

dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tutor.subjectsIntro: An IA is subject-specific down to the mark scheme, so these entries describe what the internal component actually is in each subject and what it tends to cost students in Dubai.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The scientific investigation, worth around a fifth of the subject grade and marked across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Most marks are lost in design: an uncontrolled variable, a single trial, or a question the available equipment cannot actually answer. Fixing the design before data collection is the only cheap intervention.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same investigation structure as Biology, with the added constraint of what a school laboratory can safely run. Strong chemistry IAs usually have simple apparatus and a clear quantitative relationship. Weak ones attempt an ambitious synthesis and produce data too noisy to analyse, which costs marks under both data analysis and conclusion.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Rewards precision about uncertainty more than any other group 4 subject. A good physics investigation states its uncertainties, propagates them, and discusses what they mean for the conclusion. Students who present a graph with no error treatment lose marks they could have secured with an hour of work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration, marked out of twenty across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The common failure is mathematics at the wrong level — either below the course or copied from a source the student cannot explain. Personal engagement cannot be added afterwards.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same exploration criteria applied to modelling and data. Students here often have genuinely interesting datasets and treat them descriptively, which collects presentation marks and little else. The work is making the mathematics do something the student can justify.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A portfolio of three commentaries on published news articles, each within a tight word limit, each marked against the same criteria including diagrams, terminology, application, analysis and evaluation. The usual loss is a summary of the article rather than an application of theory to it, plus diagrams that are drawn but never explained.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation, in three sections with defined mark allocations, inside a word limit near 2,200 words. Section one evaluates two sources and is where most avoidable marks sit. Students over-write section two and leave the reflection thin, which is the reverse of where the marks are easiest to collect.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: An experimental study based on a published study, with ethical constraints that shape what is possible. Marks are lost in the introduction, where the link between the chosen study and the student's own hypothesis has to be explicit, and in evaluation, where students describe limitations rather than assess their effect on the findings.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: A fieldwork investigation with a written report inside a word limit. Dubai offers unusually good fieldwork material — urban growth, coastal change, microclimates, transport use — and the constraint is usually the quality of data collection rather than the topic. Secondary data needs the same critical treatment as primary.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral, internally assessed and worth more at Standard Level than at Higher. Marked across knowledge and interpretation, analysis and evaluation, focus and organisation, and language. Students prepare content and neglect timing, then run out of time before the second text gets its analysis.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: The exhibition is internally assessed and moderated, with the curatorial rationale and the selection of works both assessed. Students treat the rationale as a label rather than as an argument about the work's coherence, which is where marks are lost even by strong practical artists.

dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tutor.regionsTitle: Where IA requests come from across Dubai, and which subject
dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tutor.regionsIntro: IA enquiries cluster by school rather than by district, and the subject differs with the cohort. These notes describe the pattern we see in each part of the city.

regions.name: Oud Metha, Al Jaddaf and Dubai Healthcare City
regions.note: Large senior cohorts with strong science uptake, so most requests here are group 4 investigations. Laboratory access in these schools is usually good, which moves the problem to research design: a question narrow enough for one controlled variable and enough trials to analyse.

regions.name: Emirates Living, The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Established Diploma families, often with both Maths AA and a science IA running at once. The useful first session here is triage rather than teaching: deciding which of the two is closer to losing marks that cannot be recovered later.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Islands
regions.note: Villa communities feeding British-curriculum schools that run the Diploma at sixth form. Students arrive from IGCSE with good examination technique and no experience of designing an investigation, so the first science IA is the hardest piece of work in DP1.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Rashid City and Meydan
regions.note: Newer schools with cohorts still in their first Diploma cycles, where internal deadlines are sometimes set late and then compressed. Requests from this area tend to arrive with two weeks left, and the honest answer is about protecting the criteria that can still move.

regions.name: Al Nahda, Al Twar and Al Qusais
regions.note: Dense school provision on the north side with long evening commutes across the city. Sessions here are scheduled online by preference at 7pm or later, and a fortnightly rhythm during data collection works better than weekly.

regions.name: Dubai Production City and Arjan
regions.note: Mixed curricula with smaller Diploma cohorts, which means a subject teacher may be the only specialist in the school. Students benefit most from a marked draft by someone other than the person who will also mark the final submission.

regions.name: Tilal Al Ghaf and Dubailand
regions.note: Fast-growing family areas with new schools and geographically scattered cohorts. Geography and Economics IAs are common here, and local data — community growth, transport, retail footfall — is genuinely available if the collection method is planned.

regions.name: Al Safa, Al Wasl and Za'abeel
regions.note: Long-established schools near the centre with experienced IA teaching, so requests are late-stage and precise: one marked draft against the criteria before a school deadline, usually in Economics or History.

schoolClusters.note: Established provision close to the centre, with science-heavy Diploma cohorts. Group 4 investigations are the most common IA request from this cluster, and laboratory access is rarely the limiting factor.

dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tutor.modesIntro: IA support is bought at specific moments in the life of a piece of coursework. These are the four shapes Dubai families use, and the right one depends on whether data has already been collected.

modes.title: Design session, before any data exists
modes.description: One or two sessions at the point where the student has a topic and nothing else. The tutor tests whether the question can be answered with the equipment, data or sources available, checks the controlled variables or the method, and makes sure enough trials or sources are planned to allow real analysis later.

modes.description: For the student who has results and does not know what to do with them. Sessions cover processing, uncertainty, graph choice, statistical treatment the student can explain, and the gap between a result and a conclusion. This is where the largest criteria in most science and maths IAs are won or lost.

Triage is usually worth more than an extra month of content teaching.

sections.heading: What an IB internal assessment actually is, subject by subject
paragraphs: An internal assessment is the component of a Diploma subject that the school marks and the IB moderates. The phrase hides enormous variation. The group 4 sciences share one model — a scientific investigation marked across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — while mathematics uses an exploration marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. History uses a three-section investigation. Economics uses a portfolio of three commentaries on news articles. Language A and Language B both use an individual oral.

The practical consequence is that there is no such thing as general IA advice. A student told to improve their evaluation has been given actionable guidance in Chemistry, where evaluation is a named criterion worth a quarter of the marks, and vague guidance in mathematics, where the equivalent criterion is reflection and is worth three marks out of twenty. Matching a tutor to the subject, rather than to coursework in general, is the whole of the quality question here.

Weight varies as well, and it varies between levels inside the same subject. Several subjects place internal assessment at around a fifth of the final grade at both levels. Others weight it more heavily at Standard Level than at Higher, because the Higher Level course adds an external component that takes a share. Economics and History both follow that pattern, as does Language A. A student at Standard Level is therefore often risking more of their grade in the internally assessed component than their Higher Level classmate in the same subject.

Because those figures are revised when subject guides are revised, treat the table below as a map rather than as an authority, and confirm each number against the current guide for your child's session through the school's IB coordinator. What does not change is the shape of the problem: six components, six mark schemes, six internal deadlines, and one student.

sections.heading: The criteria letters and the marks behind them
paragraphs: Research for this page found that no competitor page in the UAE tutoring market names a single IA criterion with its mark allocation. That is the clearest information gap in the cluster, because the criteria are exactly what a student needs in order to know what to do next. A criterion is not a topic; it is a strand with a mark range and a descriptor, and work is placed in a band by whether it matches the descriptor rather than by how much effort it shows.

In the group 4 sciences the scientific investigation is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Half the marks therefore sit in what the student does after the data exists, which is the opposite of how most students allocate their time. A beautifully conducted experiment written up with a conclusion that restates the result and an evaluation that lists generic limitations is collecting from two criteria and leaving two untouched.

The mathematics exploration is marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest share, and personal engagement is the one that cannot be retrofitted — it is visible in whether the student chose something they have a reason to care about and did something of their own with it. The historical investigation is marked across three sections with the investigation itself carrying the largest block and the reflection carrying the smallest, which is where students misallocate words.

Reading the criteria with the student in front of their own draft is the most useful hour in IA support. Most students have never read the descriptors for the band above the one they are in, and once they do, the next revision is obvious rather than arbitrary.

sections.heading: Length limits, and why going over them costs more than going under
paragraphs: Every IA has a limit and the limits are not advisory. The group 4 scientific investigation runs to around 3,000 words. The historical investigation sits near 2,200. An Economics commentary is capped at a few hundred words each, which is the tightest constraint in the Diploma and the reason Economics IAs reward ruthless cutting. The mathematics exploration is governed by a recommended page range rather than a word count. The individual orals are governed by minutes, not words.

Exceeding a limit does not add information; it removes it, because material beyond the limit need not be credited. The predictable casualty is the end of the document, which in almost every IA is where the evaluation or conclusion lives — and in the sciences that is half the mark scheme. Students who discover the problem late tend to move content into appendices, which does not help: an examiner is not obliged to read an appendix, so analysis parked there is marked as absent.

Coming in short is the lesser error but still costs. A scientific investigation at 1,400 words has usually skipped the evaluation of method and the discussion of uncertainty, which are named criteria. An Economics commentary that is short has usually described the article instead of applying theory to it. The right length is the length at which every criterion has been addressed with evidence, which is why planning against the criteria rather than against the word count produces the right number by accident.

There is also a formatting dimension worth ten minutes before submission: a clear title, the research question stated, labelled tables and figures referred to in the text, a consistent citation style, and raw data placed where the criteria expect it. None of that is difficult and all of it is routinely lost.

sections.heading: Moderation: why the mark your teacher gives is not always the mark that arrives
paragraphs: Internal assessment is marked by the school and moderated by the IB. The school submits a sample of marked work along with its marks, and the IB checks whether the school has applied the criteria as the IB applies them. If a school has marked generously, the cohort's marks can be adjusted down; if it has marked severely, they can be adjusted up. The adjustment applies at cohort level rather than being negotiated student by student.

This is the mechanism behind one of the more upsetting conversations a Dubai parent can have in July: a Chemistry IA that came back from the teacher with a strong mark, and a final subject grade that does not reflect it. Nobody has made an error. The school's marks were moderated, and the student's own mark moved with the cohort's. Understanding this in DP1 changes how a family reads internal feedback — a teacher's mark is an informed prediction against the criteria, not a banked result.

The practical defence is to write work that would survive a moderator who has never met the student. Moderators see the document and the criteria and nothing else: no knowledge of the school, the laboratory, the dataset's provenance or the effort behind it. Anything the student assumed the reader would know has to be on the page. This is also why a marked draft from someone outside the school is useful — an outside reader notices the assumptions a teacher fills in automatically.

One further point for students repeating a session. Schools can usually carry forward internally assessed marks for a candidate retaking examinations within the permitted period rather than requiring the coursework again, but the rules and the window are specific. Ask the IB coordinator before assuming either way, because the answer changes what a retake year looks like.

sections.heading: The DP2 pile-up, and how to sequence six internal deadlines
paragraphs: Internal assessment deadlines are set by the school, which is the single most important fact about them. The IB sets the dates by which the school must submit marks and samples; the school decides when your child's draft and final version are due, and schools work backwards from the submission date with their own margin. Two Dubai students in neighbouring communities can therefore face completely different calendars for identical subjects.

What they have in common is clustering. Because every department works back from the same submission window, the deadlines converge, usually in the middle of DP2 and frequently in the same weeks as the Extended Essay final submission and university applications. Add Ramadan's shortened school days in some years and the practical working time inside that window shrinks further. No single deadline in the list is unreasonable; the list is.

Sequencing is therefore the highest-value hour of IA support available, and it is almost never bought. The order should be set by marks at risk rather than by which date is nearest: a Standard Level Economics portfolio worth around 30 per cent of that subject's grade outranks a Higher Level component worth 20 per cent of another, and a science investigation with no data collected yet outranks a draft that only needs tightening, because data collection cannot be compressed.

Ask for the full internal deadline list in writing in the first fortnight of DP2, put every date on one calendar with the component's weight beside it, and work out where the collisions are while there is still room to move. Every IA emergency we are called into was visible on that calendar months earlier.

sections.heading: The line a tutor must not cross on an internal assessment
paragraphs: Every IA is submitted as the student's own work under the IB's academic honesty rules, and the school's coordinator authenticates it. A submission containing material the student did not produce is a malpractice matter, and the consequences land on the student — up to the loss of the Diploma — rather than on whoever supplied the material. In this market the warning is specific rather than abstract: research for these pages found a site ranking for UAE IB searches that sells finished coursework outright, priced per piece.

The legitimate scope of support is wide enough that nobody needs to cross the line. A tutor may test whether a research question is answerable with the available equipment. They may insist on controlled variables before data collection. They may teach a statistical treatment and make the student explain it back. They may mark a draft against the criteria, name the marks, quote the descriptor for the band above, and refuse to accept a conclusion the data does not support. They may teach a student to cut 400 words without losing a criterion.

What a tutor may not do is supply any part of the submitted document, rewrite a section to completion, carry out the analysis on the student's behalf, or produce the data. Our tutors return drafts with questions, annotations and criterion judgements rather than with replacement text. The test is whether the student can explain every change and why it earns marks; if they cannot, the work has stopped being theirs.

Tell your child's teacher that a tutor is involved. There is nothing to conceal in criteria-based coaching, and a teacher who knows will usually be clearer about which criterion the draft is weakest on. We also do not distribute IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes, which are the IB's copyright — the current guide comes from the school's coordinator.
bullets: The coordinator authenticates every IA as the student's own work
A tutor may design-check, teach analysis, mark against criteria and teach cutting

sections.heading: What internal assessment support costs in Dubai
paragraphs: IA support prices as subject-specialist work, because the useful version requires someone who knows the criteria for that subject and has seen how students lose marks against them. The published Dubai market gives the range: EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33-52, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase shows AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200-450 or above and in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Each of those is that provider's own published figure.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages. The model is a free trial lesson first, one per family and no card details taken, then the specific tutor's rate confirmed in writing before any paid session. For IA work the sensible purchase is small and timed: one or two sessions at the design stage, one analysis clinic once data exists, one criteria-marked read before the school deadline. A standing weekly slot across DP2 is rarely the right shape for coursework that has a fixed end point.

Three factors move the number. Stage is the first and largest: a design session before collection is ordinary subject tutoring, while a marked draft returned in 48 hours before a deadline is specialist work with a scheduling cost. Subject scarcity is the second — Psychology and Geography specialists are harder to find at Diploma level than Biology or Economics. The third is multiplicity: a student needing three subjects' IAs read in one fortnight is buying three specialists, not one tutor.

For context on the overall spend, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's economic incentives package. Against a Diploma-year fee, two or three well-timed IA sessions are a small line. The expensive pattern is unplanned hours bought in the last fortnight across three subjects at once.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home IA tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai search for a home tutor, so the comparison belongs here in full. An in-home tutor costs more per hour because travel sits inside the rate: published bands put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-350 against AED 150-300 for a qualified online hour. Travel also fixes the timetable, and IA work does not respect timetables. A draft arrives on a Thursday night, a deadline moves, a dataset turns out to be unusable. Any of those needs a session within two days, which is the thing an in-home arrangement cannot do.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We say that on every UAE page because two providers in this market route UAE parents to numbers in another country without disclosing where the tutor sits.

For internal assessment the online format has a concrete advantage: the work is a document and a dataset, and both live on a shared screen. A spreadsheet of results is manipulated together, with the student driving. Uncertainty calculations are worked live. A draft is annotated against the criteria with the descriptor visible beside it. Every marked version is kept, so the progress from draft one to draft three is evidence rather than recollection — which also matters if a school later asks how the work developed.

The decisive factor is subject matching. A Dubai family needing a Psychology IA read against its criteria needs a Psychology specialist, not whoever teaches sciences and lives nearby. Online, availability becomes a question of Gulf Standard Time rather than driving distance, and a student can see a different specialist for each of three subjects in the same week.
