process.title: List every IA and its deadline
process.description: The first useful message is a list: subject, level, what the component is, the school's internal deadline, and how far the draft has got. Six lines of that tells us which specialists to shortlist and in what order. If you do not have the deadlines, ask the coordinator for them in writing — most Dubai schools will send the full list on request.

process.title: Send the draft, the data or the design
process.description: Whatever exists: a method outline, a spreadsheet of raw results, two paragraphs of an introduction. For a science IA the design and the data matter more than the prose. For an Economics portfolio, send the articles chosen. A specialist can usually judge in one reading whether the problem is design, analysis or expression.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with the weakest criterion named
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, no card details taken. The tutor marks what exists against the subject's criteria and names which one is costing the most. For a student at the design stage, the tutor says plainly whether the planned method can produce analysable data. You finish with a position rather than an impression.

process.title: Agree the sessions, the rate and the turnaround
process.description: Before any paid session we confirm in writing how many sessions, the tutor's rate, the slot in Gulf Standard Time, and how quickly a draft comes back marked. Turnaround is the detail that matters in the fortnight before an internal deadline and the one most often left vague elsewhere.

process.title: Work in the student's own document
process.description: Sessions happen in the student's file on a shared screen, with the criteria open beside it. The student makes every edit while the tutor questions. Each session ends with two or three specific changes and the reason each one earns marks. You get a short written note afterwards, not a dashboard.

process.title: Stop when the component is submitted
process.description: Once the IA is in, that block ends. If another subject's deadline is next, we schedule against that date and, where the subject differs, with a different specialist. Carrying on weekly after submission would be billing for a component that cannot change.

whyPoints.title: One specialist per subject, in the same week
whyPoints.description: A Chemistry investigation and a History investigation are marked against different criteria, so we match per subject rather than sending one tutor for all coursework. Online delivery is what makes three specialists in one fortnight practical for a Dubai family.

whyPoints.title: Marks named, criterion by criterion
whyPoints.description: Feedback says which criterion is leaking and what the descriptor for the band above actually requires. Most students have never read that descriptor, and reading it with their own draft open is the hour that changes the next revision.

whyPoints.title: Design checked before data is collected
whyPoints.description: The cheapest marks in any science or geography IA are in the method, and they are unrecoverable once collection is finished. One session before the student starts is worth more than three after, which is also why we say no to design work that has already been overtaken.

whyPoints.title: Written for a moderator, not for the teacher
whyPoints.description: The IB moderates school marks, and a moderator sees the document and the criteria with no knowledge of the school or the dataset. An outside reader notices the assumptions a familiar teacher fills in without realising.

whyPoints.title: The student produces the work
whyPoints.description: Our tutors question, mark and teach cutting. They do not supply text, run the analysis or produce the data. In a market where a ranking site sells finished coursework by the piece, that boundary is the first thing to check about anyone you hire.

whyPoints.title: Market rates quoted with their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is another provider's published rate, attributed with provider and date. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars that UAE families do not transact in.

faqs.question: What is an IB internal assessment and how much of the subject grade does it carry?
faqs.answer: It is the component of each Diploma subject that the school marks and the IB moderates, and its form depends entirely on the subject: a scientific investigation in the group 4 sciences, an exploration in mathematics, a three-section investigation in History, a portfolio of commentaries in Economics, an individual oral in the language subjects. The weight runs from around a fifth to around a third of the final grade for that subject, and in several subjects it is heavier at Standard Level than at Higher Level because the Higher course adds an external component. Confirm the exact figure for your child's subject with the IB coordinator.

faqs.question: Is the IA worth the same in every Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: No, and the differences matter when deciding where to spend time. Several subjects place internal assessment at about 20 per cent of the final grade at both levels. Others weight it more heavily at Standard Level — Economics, History, Psychology, Geography and Language A all follow that pattern, with Standard Level figures commonly in the 25 to 30 per cent range. The practical consequence is that a Standard Level student can have more of a subject grade riding on coursework than a Higher Level classmate in the same room. Those weightings are revised when subject guides are revised, so check the current guide.

faqs.question: How is a science IA marked and what are the criteria?
faqs.answer: The group 4 scientific investigation is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Half the available marks therefore sit in what happens after the data exists, which is the reverse of how most students allocate effort. A carefully run experiment with a conclusion that restates the result and an evaluation listing generic limitations is collecting from two criteria and leaving two empty. Reading the descriptor for the band above the current one, with the draft open, is the fastest route to the next few marks.

faqs.question: How long should a mathematics exploration be?
faqs.answer: The exploration is governed by a recommended page range rather than a word count, and length is rarely the real problem. It is marked out of twenty across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and the two criteria students lose most often are personal engagement and use of mathematics. Engagement cannot be retrofitted: it shows in whether the student chose something they have a genuine reason to explore and did something of their own with it. Mathematics copied from a source the student cannot explain fails on communication as well as on engagement.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an IA without breaking IB academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the legitimate scope is wide. A tutor may test whether a research question can be answered with the available equipment, insist on controlled variables before collection, teach a statistical method and make the student explain it back, mark a draft against the criteria and name the marks, and teach a student to cut 400 words without losing a criterion. What no tutor may do is supply any part of the submitted document, rewrite a section to completion, run the analysis, or produce the data. The test: your child should be able to explain every change and why it earns marks.

faqs.question: What is moderation and can it lower my child's IA mark?
faqs.answer: The school marks internal assessment and submits a sample to the IB, which checks whether the school applied the criteria as the IB does. If a school has marked generously the cohort's marks can be adjusted down, and if it has marked severely they can be adjusted up. The adjustment is applied at cohort level, not negotiated individually. This is why a strong mark from a teacher is an informed prediction rather than a banked result, and why work should be written for a moderator who knows nothing about the school, the laboratory or where the dataset came from.

faqs.question: My child's IA deadline is in two weeks. What can realistically still change?
faqs.answer: More than you would think, and less than the student hopes. With a fortnight left, new data collection is usually off the table, so the gains sit in the criteria that depend on writing: evaluation, conclusion, reflection, and the formatting and length requirements. In a science investigation those are worth a substantial share of the marks. The first session should be triage — what exists, which criterion is weakest, and what to abandon. What nobody should promise is that two weeks can repair a flawed research design, because it cannot.

faqs.question: How many words is the History internal assessment?
faqs.answer: The historical investigation sits near 2,200 words and is structured in three sections: an identification and evaluation of sources, the investigation itself, and a reflection. Marks are distributed unevenly across those sections, with the investigation carrying the largest block, and the common error is to over-write the investigation and leave the source evaluation and reflection thin. Material beyond the limit need not be credited, and because the reflection usually sits last, it is the part that gets cut by accident. Plan the word allocation against the mark allocation before drafting, and confirm the current limit with the subject guide.

faqs.question: Which internal assessments do Dubai Diploma students find hardest?
faqs.answer: Two stand out in our enquiries. The first science investigation in DP1 is the hardest for students arriving from IGCSE, because the IGCSE route assesses practical skills through a written paper and gives little experience of designing an investigation from scratch. The second is the mathematics exploration, where students who are strong at examination questions struggle with an open task that asks them to choose something and justify it. Both are design problems rather than knowledge problems, which is why they respond to one session before the work starts far better than to three sessions afterwards.

faqs.question: If my child retakes a session, do they have to redo the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Often not. Schools can usually carry forward internally assessed marks for a candidate retaking examinations within a permitted period, rather than requiring the coursework to be produced again, but the rules and the window are specific and they are the school's to apply. Ask the IB coordinator directly before planning a retake year, because the answer changes everything about how those months are spent: a student carrying forward coursework marks can focus entirely on the external papers, while a student who must submit new coursework is effectively repeating the course.

faqs.question: How much does IA support cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates give the range rather than a single figure. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 at the budget online end; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase shows AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200-450 or above; BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are their figures with their dates. IA work prices at the specialist end because criteria-based marking is specialist work, and fast turnaround before a deadline costs more than a session booked a month ahead.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover internal assessments in two different subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is usually the wrong question to optimise for. Two subjects' IAs are marked against different criteria with different mark totals, so what matters is whether the tutor knows both mark schemes rather than whether they are comfortable with both topics. Where a genuine overlap exists — Biology and Chemistry investigations share a structure, Maths AA and AI share the exploration criteria — one specialist can cover both well. Across a science and a humanities subject we would rather match two specialists, which online delivery makes practical inside the same week.

faqs.question: Does the school mark the IA or does the IB?
faqs.answer: The school marks it and the IB moderates. That is different from the external components, which an IB examiner marks without the school's involvement, and it changes how a student should approach the work. Because the first reader is the subject teacher, the school's own guidance and internal deadlines carry real weight. Because the second reader is a moderator with no context, nothing can be assumed on the page. Writing for both at once — following the school's requirements while explaining everything a stranger would need — is the practical skill the component rewards.

faqs.question: How many sessions does an internal assessment usually take?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect, if they are bought at the right moments. A typical pattern is one design session before data collection, one analysis clinic once results exist, and one criteria-marked read before the school's deadline: three sessions across two or three months. A student who already has a complete draft and needs it placed against the criteria usually needs one. Where more is genuinely useful is a student carrying three or four IA deadlines at once, and even then the extra hour is best spent on sequencing rather than on content.

faqs.question: What should my child bring to a first internal assessment session?
faqs.answer: The subject's criteria if the school has issued them, the internal deadline, and whatever work exists — a method outline, a spreadsheet of raw data, two paragraphs of a draft, or the three articles chosen for an Economics portfolio. For a science IA, the design and the data matter far more than the prose. It also helps to know what the school's laboratory can actually provide and whether technician time is available, because that constrains what method is realistic more than anything the student decides.

dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tutor.closingHeading: Send the list of deadlines first
dubai/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tutor.closingBody: The most useful thing you can send is six lines: subject, level, what the component is, the school's internal deadline, and how far each draft has got. From that we can say which specialists to shortlist and in what order, and which deadline is closest to costing marks that cannot be recovered. The trial lesson is free, one per family, with no card details taken, and it ends with the weakest criterion named rather than a general impression. Sessions are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and your child designs, collects and writes the work themselves.

intro.heading: The front-loaded language: why Mandarin B behaves differently
paragraphs: Every Group 2 language asks a student to learn vocabulary, grammar and exam technique. Mandarin asks for all three plus an orthography that has to be built character by character, and that extra demand is not spread evenly across the two Diploma years. It lands at the front. A student who can speak and listen comfortably, which describes most Mandarin B candidates in Dubai who have a Chinese-speaking parent, can still be badly behind on production by the middle of DP1, because producing a character from memory is a different skill from recognising it on a page.

That recognition-production gap is the single most useful idea in this subject. Reading comprehension rewards recognition: the student sees a character in context and retrieves its meaning. The written task rewards production: the student must produce the character correctly from nothing, with the right components in the right places, at speed, under exam conditions. Students routinely have thousands of characters in recognition and a few hundred in reliable production, and no school report distinguishes between the two. A diagnostic that tests them separately is the only way to know which problem you are paying to fix.

Tone is the second structural difference. In Spanish or German a pronunciation error makes a student sound foreign. In Mandarin it can make them say a different word, and in a recorded Individual Oral that is a comprehension issue rather than an accent issue. Dubai students who speak Mandarin only at home often have tone patterns inherited from one regional variety, and students who learnt Mandarin at school often have tones that are accurate in isolation and collapse in connected speech. Those are different problems with different remedies.

The third difference is supply, and it is practical rather than linguistic. Mandarin teaching capacity sits overwhelmingly in East Asia, which is four hours ahead of Gulf Standard Time. A 5pm slot in Dubai is 9pm in eastern China, and a tutor who teaches a full day there has limited appetite for it. The consequence for Dubai families is that Mandarin B scheduling is a real constraint rather than an afterthought, and a slot that works is worth protecting once you have it. Hiring within driving distance narrows the pool further still.

On the phrase people search: home tutor usually means somebody arriving by car. IB Gram does not do that in the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Mandarin B support reaches Dubai families as one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time, with character work written by hand, photographed and marked on a shared screen. For this subject the online format is close to a necessity rather than a compromise, because the people who can mark Mandarin B against the Group 2 band descriptors are mostly not in this city.

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Mandarin appears at several points in a Dubai student's school career and the character foundation laid at each stage determines how heavy the Diploma feels.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Mandarin B is a Group 2 acquisition course assessed through a written task, a receptive paper combining listening and reading, and a recorded Individual Oral. Higher Level adds two literary works originally written in Chinese, with the oral built on an extract from one of them rather than on a visual stimulus. The five prescribed themes frame the content at both levels, but the character demand inside each component is what decides how hard the course feels in practice.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Mandarin B sets are usually small and mixed: a few students with a Chinese-speaking parent, a few who studied Mandarin as a school subject from Year 7, and occasionally one who began in Year 9. The character gap between those groups is wider than the gap in any other Group 2 language, and it is the reason a single class teacher cannot close it inside the timetable.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Mandarin reports by phase and against four criteria separating listening, reading, speaking and writing. The criterion split matters more here than in any other language, because a student can sit comfortably in a middle phase on comprehension criteria while producing very few characters from memory. That profile is survivable in MYP and becomes visible within weeks of starting the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary widely in how early they begin character writing rather than pinyin, and students who changed schools between Year 6 and Year 9 frequently missed the year it was taught systematically. Where speaking is strong and writing is hesitant, that gap in the timeline is usually the whole explanation.

programmes.name: Chinese A: Language and Literature
programmes.description: The Group 1 route for students whose Chinese is a first language, studied as literary and textual analysis rather than acquisition. It is the only Chinese route that can contribute towards the bilingual diploma, and it demands sustained reading in Chinese rather than conversational comfort. Tutoring for it is literature support and a different purchase entirely from Mandarin B work.
programmes.countryNote: Rarely timetabled in Dubai because the cohort seldom justifies a set, though some schools can offer it as a school-supported self-taught Standard Level option. For a student who speaks fluently and reads slowly, that route is demanding and the reading stamina question should be settled honestly before anyone commits to it.

programmes.name: Mandarin ab initio
programmes.description: The beginner route for students with little or no previous Mandarin, examined at Standard Level only. The vocabulary expectation is bounded by the prescribed topics, which makes the character load finite and trackable, and that boundedness is the main reason it is a sensible choice for a genuine beginner. Eligibility rests on prior exposure and the coordinator applies the rule.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students sometimes choose Mandarin ab initio for interest and then compare workloads with the Spanish or French beginner sets around February. The comparison is unflattering and a late switch is rarely possible, so the character commitment deserves a frank conversation in the first fortnight of DP1.

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: What is actually available depends on the school's Group 2 block. These are the routes a Mandarin B student is weighing, described by the demand each makes rather than by the content it covers.

subjects.name: Mandarin B Higher Level
subjects.description: Two literary works originally written in Chinese, longer written responses, denser reading, and an Individual Oral built on an unseen extract from one of the works. For a student whose Mandarin came from home, this is a reading project rather than a language one: extended Chinese prose uses characters and registers that daily conversation never touches.

subjects.name: Mandarin B Standard Level
subjects.description: The same three components without the literary works, with the oral based on a visual stimulus linked to a prescribed theme. For a student with strong speech and unreliable character production, Standard Level with serious production work usually yields a better Diploma total than Higher Level with two books skimmed in translation.

subjects.name: Mandarin ab initio
subjects.description: Beginner Mandarin with the vocabulary bounded by the prescribed topics, examined at Standard Level. The bounded character list is the attraction. It is not a fallback for a struggling Mandarin B student, because eligibility turns on prior exposure and the Diploma coordinator applies that rule rather than a tutor or a parent.

subjects.name: Chinese A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: First-language Chinese taught as literary and textual analysis, and the only Chinese route counting towards the bilingual diploma. Rarely available in Dubai, occasionally as a school-supported self-taught Standard Level option. Reading stamina in extended Chinese prose is the deciding factor, not speaking fluency.

subjects.name: Japanese B
subjects.description: Included because the scripts invite a false comparison. Japanese uses kanji alongside two syllabaries, so a student who handles Chinese characters has a partial head start in reading and none at all in grammar. Families considering both should treat them as unrelated commitments rather than as neighbouring choices.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: The most common alternative when a Mandarin set cannot be timetabled or the option block clashes. The workload profile is the opposite: no orthographic barrier, but tense and mood control to master. A student moving between them should expect a completely new diagnostic rather than a transfer of progress.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: The best-supplied Group 2 language in Dubai IB schools, and the usual destination for students who decide the Mandarin character load is incompatible with their other five subjects. Supply affects feedback: a student in a well-staffed set often gets more marked work inside school than one in a Mandarin set of four.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school under KHDA requirements regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students. A Mandarin B candidate is therefore learning two non-Latin scripts in the same school week, which is worth planning for rather than discovering.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Mandarin B
subjects.description: A 4,000-word essay written in Chinese about an aspect of culture in the Chinese-speaking world, supervised inside the school. The tutor's role is process coaching only. Producing that length in characters is a stamina skill in itself, and students who have only written short pieces should practise length long before the first draft deadline.

sections.heading: Recognition against production: the measurement nobody takes
paragraphs: A Mandarin B diagnostic that asks a student to read a passage and answer questions measures recognition. A diagnostic that asks them to write a paragraph from a prompt measures production. In Mandarin those two numbers can be separated by a factor of several, and almost no school report distinguishes them. A student who reads comfortably and writes with gaps looks, on paper, like a student doing fine, right up until a written task is marked under timed conditions.

The practical test takes twenty minutes. Give the student a short reading comprehension and a short writing prompt on the same theme, and mark both. Where recognition is high and production is low, the plan is character production drilling, handwritten, short and frequent, with a retest cycle. Where both are low, the plan is vocabulary volume first and production second, because there is nothing to produce. Where production is adequate and reading comprehension is weak, the problem is not characters at all but text types and inference, and character drills would waste the term.

This is the most common misdiagnosis in the subject and it is expensive. Families who know their child speaks Mandarin well assume the problem must be effort or motivation, and buy more hours of the same lesson. The measurement that separates the two skills costs one session and redirects everything that follows. It also gives a parent something to compare against three months later, which matters in a subject where progress is slow and invisible for long stretches.
bullets: Test reading comprehension and written production on the same theme, separately

Low on both: vocabulary volume first, production second

sections.heading: Mandarin B assessment, and where the characters actually bite
paragraphs: Mandarin B is assessed through three components. The written task, one piece in a set text type responding to a stimulus, carries a quarter of the grade. The receptive paper, covering listening and reading, carries half. The recorded Individual Oral carries the remaining quarter. The proportions are identical at Standard and Higher Level; what changes at Higher Level is the demand inside each component plus the two literary works.

The character load does not fall evenly across those components, which is the thing worth understanding before buying any tuition. The written task is pure production under time pressure. The reading section needs recognition only, which is why strong readers can carry that part of the paper while failing the written task. The listening section needs no characters at all beyond what is required to record an answer, and the oral needs none. A family that understands this can target hours precisely instead of buying general Mandarin.

Component timings, word bands and the school's internal dates should be confirmed against the current subject guide and with the Diploma coordinator rather than taken from any tutoring page. This page publishes no IB exam or results date, because the IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project. The weightings and the structure are the stable part, and they are enough to plan on.

One consequence of that uneven distribution deserves spelling out. A student can be strong on three of the four assessed elements and still finish two grades below where their family expected, because the written task is the only component where production is tested and it is worth a quarter on its own. Conversely a student who fixes production and nothing else moves one component and leaves the half of the grade sitting in the receptive paper untouched. Reading the component table as a budget rather than as a description is what stops both of those outcomes.

sections.heading: The character workload, planned backwards from DP2
paragraphs: Character work has a property that makes it unlike anything else in the Diploma: it cannot be compressed. Vocabulary in a Latin-script language can be crammed, badly, in the final weeks. Character production cannot, because retention depends on spaced retrieval over months and the failure mode of cramming is that nothing is available under exam pressure. A Mandarin B plan therefore has to be written backwards from the final term, and the implication is uncomfortable: the most valuable work happens in DP1, when nobody feels urgency.

The planning unit is the week rather than the term. Twenty minutes of handwritten production practice, four times a week, sustained across DP1, produces a student who writes fluently in DP2. Two hours on a Saturday produces a student who recognises a great deal and freezes on a blank page. Both arrangements cost the same and one of them works. This is the clearest case in all of Group 2 tutoring where the session pattern matters more than the number of hours purchased.

The table below plots the work backwards. It is deliberately conservative, and the point of it is to show which decisions have deadlines. The Higher Level reading cannot start in the final term. The production habit cannot start in the final term either. What can usefully be left late is timed exam technique, the receptive-paper clinic and the oral timing discipline, which is why a family who has the production work in hand has real options in DP2 and a family who does not has very few.

sections.heading: Tones, pinyin and what the oral actually rewards
paragraphs: Tone in Mandarin is not accent, it is meaning, and that changes how an error is treated in a recorded assessment. A tone mistake can produce a different word, so what reads in another language as a pronunciation slip reads here as a comprehension problem for the listener. That is the reason tone deserves attention in a Group 2 course where other languages would treat pronunciation as cosmetic.

Two distinct problems turn up in Dubai. Students who learnt Mandarin at home frequently have tone patterns inherited from a regional variety, consistent within the family and different from the standard the course assumes. Students who learnt at school often have tones that are accurate when a syllable is produced alone and that collapse in connected speech, where tone sandhi and sentence rhythm take over. The first needs targeted contrast work on specific syllables. The second needs work on phrases and sentences, and isolated drills actively waste time.

Pinyin sits underneath both and is worth a frank word. It is a learning tool and a typing method, not an orthography the exam accepts in place of characters. Students who have done most of their Mandarin on a phone or laptop have been producing characters by selecting them from a list after typing pinyin, which is recognition dressed up as production. That habit is the single most common hidden cause of a weak written task in Dubai Mandarin B candidates, and it is why every piece of practice in this subject should be handwritten.
bullets: A tone error can change the word, which makes it a meaning problem in the oral

sections.heading: Simplified or traditional: settle it before anyone starts teaching
paragraphs: Candidates are registered for a character set, and a student taught in one and examined in the other is in avoidable trouble. Dubai families arrive with every combination: a parent educated in traditional characters, a school teaching simplified, a student who reads both inconsistently, and a tutor whose own training sits on one side. The question is settled with the Diploma coordinator, in writing, in the first fortnight, and everything afterwards follows that answer.

The practical consequence is about the household as much as about the tutor. Where a parent writes traditional characters and the school examines in simplified, well-meant help at home introduces inconsistency into exactly the component that penalises it. The reverse is equally true. It is better to agree a household rule early, with the parent's own writing kept out of the student's practice, than to discover mixed forms in a marked task in DP2.

For tutoring specifically, ask the question before the trial lesson rather than after it. A tutor who has taught only simplified characters can usually read traditional and should not be teaching production in it. This is one of the few places in Group 2 where a mismatch between tutor and school is invisible for months and then expensive, and it is settled by one email to the coordinator.

There is a reading-side consequence too, and it is the one worth knowing if your child genuinely moves between both sets. Passive familiarity with the other set is an asset: it widens what the student can read outside the course, from subtitles to books relatives send. It becomes a liability only at the point of production, where a mixed script in one written task reads to an examiner as carelessness rather than as breadth. So the household rule is narrow on purpose. Read whatever is available in either set; write in one, consistently, for two years.
bullets: Confirm the registered character set with the Diploma coordinator in writing
Keep household help in the same set the school examines, not the parent's own
Ask a prospective tutor which set they teach production in, before the trial

sections.heading: Mandarin B, Mandarin ab initio and Chinese A compared
paragraphs: Three Chinese routes exist in the Diploma and the choice between them is usually made on the wrong evidence. Mandarin B assumes prior study. Mandarin ab initio is for students with little or no previous Mandarin and runs at Standard Level only, with the character load bounded by the prescribed topics. Chinese A: Language and Literature is a Group 1 course for first-language speakers and the only Chinese route that can contribute towards the bilingual diploma.

The wrong evidence is speaking. A student who speaks Mandarin fluently at home may belong in any of the three depending entirely on reading and writing, and placement by conversation is how a student ends up in Chinese A unable to read a novel, or in Mandarin B bored for two years. Reading stamina and character production are the deciding measurements, and they are measurable in one session. The decision itself belongs to the school's coordinator against the IB's placement rules.

The bounded character list is why ab initio is genuinely a reasonable choice for a genuine beginner rather than a soft option. It is also why it is not a rescue route for a struggling Mandarin B student: eligibility rests on prior exposure, and a student with years of Mandarin behind them does not qualify however much they are struggling. Where that situation arises, a level change within Mandarin B is usually the available option, and it is a conversation to have early in DP1 rather than after the first reporting cycle.

sections.heading: The time-zone problem, and how Dubai families solve it
paragraphs: Mandarin B is the one Group 2 subject where scheduling is a structural issue rather than a convenience. The deepest pool of qualified Mandarin teachers sits roughly four hours ahead of Gulf Standard Time, which means a conventional Dubai after-school slot of 5pm or 6pm falls late in their evening. Teachers do take those slots, and the good ones fill them first and keep them for the long term, which is why a workable Mandarin slot is worth more than a slightly better rate.

The arrangements that actually hold are the counter-intuitive ones. Early weekend mornings in Dubai are the middle of the day in East Asia, which is when the strongest teachers have genuine capacity rather than residual willingness. A 7.30am Saturday session is unpopular with teenagers and is frequently the best match available in this subject. Short weekday sessions before school, used for character production rather than for anything cognitively demanding, are the second pattern that works.

Hiring within driving distance in Dubai compounds the problem rather than solving it. The pool becomes those Mandarin teachers who both live nearby and are free in the local evening, which for a Group 2 specialist marking against band descriptors is a very small set. Online delivery on Gulf Standard Time is not a compromise here; it is the mechanism that makes a specialist reachable at all. IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE, and for this subject the format follows the supply rather than the other way round.

sections.heading: HSK, Chinese-taught degrees and what Mandarin B is worth afterwards
paragraphs: Families often choose Mandarin B with a longer plan attached, and it is worth being precise about what the Diploma subject does and does not deliver. Chinese proficiency for admission to a Chinese-taught degree is normally evidenced through a standardised proficiency test rather than through a school qualification, and universities set the level they require themselves. The HSK framework has been under revision, so the level structure should be checked with the examining body or test centre rather than assumed from an older description.

A Group 2 Diploma subject and a proficiency certificate are different instruments and one does not substitute for the other. What Mandarin B supplies is the underlying skill those tests measure: reading unfamiliar text, writing in a controlled register, and listening to speakers who are not teachers. A student aiming at a Chinese-taught programme is better served by Higher Level with the literary reading taken seriously than by Standard Level plus a certificate obtained hurriedly at the end.

For everything else, the honest answer is that Mandarin B functions as a Diploma subject like any other, contributing points and sometimes satisfying a specific language requirement where a university names one. It does not contribute to the bilingual diploma. No tutoring is required for any admissions process, and no provider should present a language certificate or an equivalency step as something it performs or guarantees. The verification always belongs with the institution.

The timing of a proficiency test is the one place where a plan is genuinely useful. Sitting it in the middle of DP2, alongside internal deadlines and the written components, tends to produce a mediocre result in both. The students who manage it well either sit the test at the end of DP1, when the character work is current and the Diploma pressure is lower, or they leave it until after the final examinations. Deciding which of those two it will be, in DP1, is worth more than any amount of preparation squeezed into the wrong term.

sections.heading: Materials, honesty and the limits of a Mandarin tutor
paragraphs: Two parts of Mandarin B are assessed as the student's own work: the Individual Oral, which is unscripted, and an Extended Essay where a student chooses to write one in Chinese. Both attract offers that cross the line. A tutor may explain how the components are marked, run practice on stimuli and extracts the student has not seen, read a draft and say where it is weak, question an argument, and model a text type on a different topic. A tutor may not supply a script, write into a draft, produce finished work, or prepare answers for the specific stimulus the school will use.

Materials deserve the same clarity. Official subject guides, past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB and are not ours to redistribute; the place to read them is through the school or ibo.org. A tutor who arrives with a folder of copied papers is offering a liability rather than an advantage, and for unreleased material a serious one. Character lists and vocabulary sets a tutor has written themselves are a different matter entirely and are a reasonable part of the work.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and nothing here implies otherwise. No school named on this page is a client or partner. No statistic appears without a date and a source, which is why there is no satisfaction figure, no average score and no claim about outcomes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and it is reasonable to ask any tutor whether they hold it.

process.title: Confirm the character set first
process.description: One email to the Diploma coordinator asking which character set your child is registered for, and the answer in writing. This sounds administrative and it is the single most consequential fact in the whole arrangement, because a tutor teaching production in the other set will not be found out for months.

process.title: Measure recognition and production separately
process.description: A short reading comprehension and a handwritten writing prompt on the same theme, marked and reported as two numbers rather than one. Those two numbers decide whether the next term is character drilling, vocabulary volume or text type work, and they take twenty minutes to produce.

process.title: Build the session pattern around the time zone
process.description: Early weekend mornings in Dubai land in the middle of the East Asian day, which is where the real teaching capacity is. Short weekday slots before school suit production practice. We will tell you which windows have genuine availability rather than pretending every hour is equally possible.

process.title: Run production as a habit, not a lesson
process.description: Twenty minutes of handwritten production four times a week beats two hours once, at the same cost, because retention depends on spacing. The tutor sets and marks it; the habit belongs to the student. This is the part of the plan that determines what DP2 looks like.

process.title: Review on the two numbers, every term
process.description: The recognition and production scores are re-measured each term on comparable tasks, and the plan changes on the basis of the gap between them rather than on a renewal date. When production has caught up, those hours stop or move to the receptive paper. If the numbers are not moving, we change the approach or the tutor.

whyPoints.title: Recognition and production measured as two numbers
whyPoints.description: In Mandarin those skills diverge by a wide margin and no school report separates them. Measuring both takes one session and determines everything that follows, and the pair of numbers gives a parent something concrete to compare against a term later in a subject where progress is otherwise invisible.

whyPoints.title: Handwritten practice, for the whole course
whyPoints.description: Pinyin input selects characters for the student, which is recognition wearing production's clothes, and it is the commonest hidden cause of a weak written task. Work is handwritten, photographed and marked on component structure, including in the final weeks when the temptation to type is strongest.

whyPoints.title: Planned backwards from the final term
whyPoints.description: Character retention depends on spaced retrieval over months and cannot be compressed, so the valuable work happens in DP1 when nobody feels urgency. We publish what must be in place by when, including the things that become effectively impossible if left late.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around where the teachers actually are
whyPoints.description: Most Mandarin teaching capacity sits four hours ahead of Gulf Standard Time, which makes an early Dubai weekend morning a better match than a conventional weekday evening. We say which windows have real availability instead of booking the convenient hour and hoping.

whyPoints.title: The character set settled in writing
whyPoints.description: Simplified or traditional is confirmed with your school before teaching starts, and household help is kept in the same set the school examines. A mismatch here is invisible for months and then costs marks in the component least able to absorb it.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we do not claim
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no regulator or examination-board approval, no promised grades, no statistic without a date and a source, and no IB exam date because none could be verified for this project. What a tutor may and may not do with assessed work is stated rather than implied.

faqs.question: How many characters does my child need for IB Mandarin B?
faqs.answer: The expectation is set by the course guide and the school's own vocabulary list rather than by a round number a tutoring site can quote, and it differs between Standard and Higher Level. The more useful question is how many characters your child can produce from memory as opposed to recognise on a page, because those two totals diverge sharply in Mandarin and only one of them helps in the written task. Ask for both to be measured separately at the start. A student with strong recognition and weak production needs a completely different plan from one who is short on both.

faqs.question: Will my child be examined in simplified or traditional characters?
faqs.answer: Candidates are registered for a character set, and the answer comes from your child's Diploma coordinator rather than from a tutor or a parent. Get it in writing in the first fortnight. It matters because a student taught production in one set and examined in the other is in avoidable trouble that stays invisible for months. It also governs household help: where a parent writes in the other set, their well-meant corrections introduce inconsistency into the exact component that penalises it, so agree a household rule early.

faqs.question: Is Mandarin B much harder than Mandarin ab initio?
faqs.answer: They differ most in how bounded the character load is. Ab initio runs at Standard Level only and its vocabulary expectation is defined by the prescribed topics, which makes the workload finite and trackable. Mandarin B assumes prior study and draws on broader authentic text, so the character demand has no natural ceiling. Ab initio is not a rescue route for a struggling Mandarin B student, because eligibility rests on prior exposure and the coordinator applies that rule. Where a Mandarin B student is drowning, a level change within the course is usually the realistic option.

faqs.question: My child speaks Mandarin at home but cannot read it — which course fits?
faqs.answer: That profile needs measuring rather than guessing, because speaking tells you almost nothing about placement in Chinese. Reading stamina and character production are the deciding measurements and both can be tested in a single session. A fluent speaker who reads slowly is usually wrong for Chinese A: Language and Literature, which demands extended literary prose, and is often well placed in Mandarin B with serious production work. The decision belongs to the school's coordinator against the IB's placement rules; what helps that conversation is a marked diagnostic rather than an opinion.

faqs.question: Do tones really affect the Mandarin B Individual Oral mark?
faqs.answer: They affect comprehensibility, which is what the criteria care about. A tone error in Mandarin can produce a different word, so what would be a harmless accent feature in another language becomes a meaning problem for the listener. Two patterns show up in Dubai: home learners carrying tones from a regional variety, and school learners whose tones are accurate in isolation and collapse in connected speech. The first needs contrast work on specific syllables; the second needs phrase and sentence work, where isolated drills actively waste time.

faqs.question: Can Mandarin B writing practice be done by typing?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most important practical point on this page. Typing Mandarin means entering pinyin and selecting a character from a list, which is recognition rather than production. A student who has done most of their written Mandarin on a device has been quietly outsourcing the exact skill the written task assesses, and the deficit only appears when they face a blank page under timing. All practice should be handwritten, photographed and marked, for the whole course, including in the final weeks when typing is most tempting.

faqs.question: What do the two Higher Level literary works involve in Mandarin B?
faqs.answer: Two works originally written in Chinese are studied across the course, chosen by the school rather than from a fixed national list, and the Higher Level Individual Oral is built on an unseen extract from one of them. The demand is to discuss a passage in Chinese, connecting it to the work and to wider ideas. That needs the works genuinely read in Chinese, plus a register for talking about writing that daily conversation never supplies. Ask the subject teacher which two works the class is studying and when each will be read.

faqs.question: Does IB Mandarin B satisfy a Chinese university's language requirement?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Chinese-taught degree programmes normally require a standardised proficiency result at a level the university sets, and that is a separate examination from a Diploma subject. The proficiency framework has been under revision, so check the current level structure with the examining body or test centre rather than relying on an older description, and check the requirement with the specific university and programme. What Mandarin B supplies is the underlying skill those tests measure, which is why Higher Level suits a student with that plan.

faqs.question: Why is it so hard to book a Mandarin B tutor at 5pm Dubai time?
faqs.answer: Because the deepest pool of qualified Mandarin teachers sits roughly four hours ahead of Gulf Standard Time, so a 5pm Dubai slot is late evening for them. The arrangements that hold are counter-intuitive: an early Saturday morning in Dubai is the middle of the working day in East Asia, which is when the strongest teachers genuinely have capacity. Short weekday slots before school work too, used for character production rather than demanding work. Once you have a slot that functions, protect it; continuity is worth more here than a slightly better hourly rate.

faqs.question: Does Mandarin B contribute to the IB bilingual diploma?
faqs.answer: No. The bilingual diploma rests on two Group 1 language and literature subjects, or a Group 3 or Group 4 subject studied and assessed in a language other than the student's Group 1 language, subject to the IB's grade requirements. Group 2 acquisition courses do not qualify at either level. Chinese A: Language and Literature can contribute, which is one reason the placement conversation is worth having properly in DP1. Families reading summaries rather than the regulations often discover this in the final year, when nothing can be changed.

faqs.question: When should character production work start for a Dubai Diploma student?
faqs.answer: In the first term of DP1, and that is not a sales position but a property of the skill. Character retention depends on spaced retrieval over months, so twenty minutes of handwritten production four times a week across DP1 produces a student who writes fluently in DP2, while two hours once a week at the same total cost produces one who recognises a lot and freezes on a blank page. Bulk character acquisition is effectively impossible in the final six weeks, which is why the plan is written backwards from the final term.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Mandarin tutor to a Dubai address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Mandarin B teaching reaches Dubai families as one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time, with handwritten character work photographed, annotated and kept in a shared file. For this subject the format follows the supply rather than the other way round: hiring within driving distance would narrow the pool to Mandarin teachers who both live nearby and are free in the local evening, which for a Group 2 specialist is a very small set indeed.

faqs.question: What should a Mandarin B tutor send us after each session?
faqs.answer: The marked handwritten work with component-level corrections rather than a tick, the production and recognition scores from any retest, and a note of which items were first met four or eight weeks earlier so retention is visible rather than assumed. Once a month, the recorded oral attempt. That record is what makes a slow subject legible: character work shows almost no visible change week to week, and without the numbers a family has nothing to judge the arrangement by except the student's mood.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Mandarin B and Chinese A for siblings?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it is worth asking directly rather than assuming. They are different courses with different purposes: Mandarin B is language acquisition assessed on functional writing, listening, reading and an oral, while Chinese A is a Group 1 literature and textual analysis course. A teacher comfortable in both exists; many strong Mandarin B teachers do not teach literary analysis and should not pretend to. What should not happen is merging the two students into one session, which shortchanges both and saves very little.

faqs.question: Our family travels to East Asia in term time — can the Mandarin schedule follow?
faqs.answer: Yes, and travel to a Mandarin-speaking environment is one of the few genuine advantages a Dubai family has in this subject. The schedule shifts to the local time for the duration, which is usually easier rather than harder given where the teaching capacity sits. What needs planning is the coursework calendar: Higher Level literary reading and the school's internal deadlines do not move, so map the trip against them in advance. Listening gains from immersion are real; character production still needs the daily handwritten habit while away.

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-home-tutor.closingHeading: Settle the character set, then measure the two numbers
dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-home-tutor.closingBody: Mandarin B is the one Group 2 course where the session pattern matters more than the hour count, because character production depends on spaced practice over months and cannot be rescued late. Two administrative steps come before any teaching: confirm in writing which character set your child is registered for, and have recognition and production measured as separate numbers. Send those two answers with the level, the school and the windows your family can genuinely defend, and you will get a named Mandarin B teacher, a realistic slot on Gulf Standard Time, and a 30-minute trial lesson at no charge. Teaching runs online, one-to-one, with no home visits in the UAE.

intro.heading: Characters, tones and handwriting: what actually limits a Mandarin B grade
paragraphs: Mandarin B is the IB Diploma language acquisition course in Chinese, taught at Standard and Higher Level, with two literary works added at Higher Level. Of all the Group 2 languages a Dubai student can take, it has the steepest mechanical workload, and the reason is the writing system. A student learning Spanish or German meets new vocabulary and knows how to write it the moment they can say it. A student learning Mandarin meets new vocabulary, learns to say it, learns to recognise it, and then has to learn to produce it stroke by stroke, which is a separate act of memory.

That separation is why Mandarin B grades so often sit below what a student's spoken ability suggests. Recognition is easy and feels like knowledge. A student reading a text on a screen, with context and a dictionary a tap away, experiences fluency. The same student facing a blank page in a timed paper discovers that half the characters they thought they knew are only recognisable, not retrievable. The gap between recognition and production is the single most reliable predictor of a disappointing Mandarin B result.

Tones are the second structural problem and they cost marks twice. Produced incorrectly, they damage the oral. Heard imprecisely, they damage listening comprehension, because a mis-heard tone turns a known word into an unknown one and the recording does not wait. Most students who struggle with Mandarin listening do not have a vocabulary problem; they have a tone-discrimination problem that nobody has ever tested separately from their vocabulary.

This page treats the subject as those two problems plus a set of smaller ones. It covers the honest character arithmetic, how the HSK scale many parents already know relates to IB levels, the components and their weightings, the handwriting-against-typing question that the examination settles in one direction, where Dubai candidates lose marks component by component, why daily contact matters more here than in any other Group 2 language, and the academic-honesty position in a subject where a translation tool produces flawless output in seconds.

Lessons run online. IB Gram matches Dubai families with one-to-one tutors over live video, with handwritten character practice photographed and annotated on screen. We do not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is an India-only service. For Mandarin B this makes practical sense: the constraint on quality is finding a tutor who has taught this syllabus at this level and can mark handwritten characters properly, and that person is very unlikely to live in your community. Stroke order, character balance and consistent script choice all have to be seen on the page to be corrected, which a shared screen handles perfectly well and a phone call does not.

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Mandarin appears at every stage of the IB continuum in Dubai, and the route a student took through it decides their character inventory rather than their conversational range. The character inventory is what limits the Diploma grade.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP requires additional language learning without a separate examination, and Mandarin is a common choice in Dubai continuum schools. Teaching at this stage is oral, song-based and thematic, with character work usually limited to recognition of a small set. Children leave able to speak and greet, with very little writing behind them.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the additional-language slot competes with KHDA's mandatory Arabic requirement, which applies to every private school in the emirate regardless of licensed curriculum. A PYP child therefore carries Arabic plus Mandarin, and the Mandarin half rarely gets the handwriting time that a character-based script needs to stick.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language Acquisition runs in phases, and Mandarin phases move more slowly than alphabetic languages because each phase carries a character load as well as a grammatical one. A student in Phase 3 or 4 has a workable base for Mandarin B; a student in Phase 2 may be better served by ab initio.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP Mandarin classes are frequently taught with heavy use of digital tools and pinyin input, which builds recognition and conversation efficiently and leaves handwriting behind. Students arriving in Year 12 from that background often read far better than they write, and the written papers are where the grade is decided.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Mandarin B sits in Group 2 and satisfies the Diploma's language acquisition requirement at either level. Two external papers and one internally assessed individual oral make up the grade, and Higher Level candidates also study two literary works that become the basis of their oral.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma students carry six subjects plus the core and the emirate's mandatory subjects, which leaves no timetabled space for the daily character review that Mandarin needs. The students who do well are the ones whose review happens in short daily blocks outside school, which is a scheduling problem rather than a teaching one.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP includes a compulsory language development strand assessed by portfolio rather than on the 1 to 7 scale. Mandarin is a logical choice where the career-related study points at trade, logistics or hospitality, all of which have substantial China-facing activity in the Gulf.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of Dubai schools licensed for the DP also run the CP, so a CP Mandarin portfolio student usually works largely independently. Tuition here targets evidence of growth and reflection rather than Paper 1 technique, and a session looks nothing like Mandarin B exam preparation.

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Mandarin B is one of six Diploma subjects, and the reason for listing the usual companions is time. Character review is daily work with no deadline attached, which makes it the first thing to disappear when a dated deadline arrives in another subject.

subjects.name: Mandarin B
subjects.description: Five prescribed themes, two external papers and an individual oral, plus two literary works at Higher Level. The limiting factor is character production under time, not conversational range, and the two improve on completely different schedules.

subjects.name: Mandarin ab initio
subjects.description: For genuine beginners, Standard Level only, with a much smaller character expectation and no literary component. A student with two years of casual Mandarin sometimes belongs here, and the school's entry assessment rather than a transcript should settle it.

subjects.name: Mandarin A: language and literature
subjects.description: The Group 1 route for students who use Chinese as a school or home language. Relevant to any Mandarin B family with a heritage speaker in it, because a student who reads Chinese comfortably may be in the wrong subject group entirely.

subjects.name: English A: language and literature
subjects.description: Near-universal in Dubai Diploma cohorts. The analytical habits it builds transfer into the Mandarin B Higher Level oral, where the student comments on an extract rather than simply describing an image.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A frequent pairing for students targeting engineering or economics faculties. Its exploration deadline usually lands in the same weeks as the Mandarin oral window, and the character review is what gets sacrificed.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries with fixed submission dates across the course. Students taking Economics Higher Level alongside Mandarin B tend to lose two or three weeks of daily character work each term unless the schedule is protected deliberately.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Widely taken in this market and a sensible partner for students interested in China-facing trade. The written work rewards audience awareness, which is the same instinct a Mandarin B text-type task requires.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A demanding Higher Level whose internal assessment competes with Mandarin literary reading for evening hours in Year 12. Students carrying both need the Mandarin reading scheduled before the Physics deadline is announced, not after.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Students here are practised at describing and interpreting images, which is precisely the Standard Level oral task when a photograph appears as the stimulus. The transfer is worth using rather than leaving to chance.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools for students who are not Arab nationals and streamed separately from Arabic as a first language under KHDA rules. It takes a timetable slot that cannot become Mandarin review time.

sections.heading: The character arithmetic nobody does at enrolment
paragraphs: A useful conversation about Mandarin B starts with an inventory rather than an aspiration. How many characters can the student recognise in context? How many can they recognise in isolation? How many can they write by hand, unprompted, correctly? Those three numbers are always different, and the third is usually a fraction of the first. The grade depends mostly on the third, because a written paper requires production from a blank page.

Estimates of the character and word load needed to read unseen texts comfortably at this level vary by source and by text difficulty, and anyone quoting a single authoritative figure is overstating what is known. What is not in dispute is the shape of the problem: the load is in the thousands of items rather than the hundreds, each item needs separate work for recognition and for production, and the only mechanism that holds thousands of items in memory is frequent review spread over months.

This has a direct consequence for how tuition should be bought. A weekly hour with no daily review between sessions will not move a Mandarin B grade, because an hour a week cannot carry a review load of that size. A weekly hour that sets, checks and adjusts a daily twelve-minute review block can, because the hour becomes a management meeting for a process that runs seven days a week. Families who understand that distinction get value from tuition in this subject; families who treat the lesson as the work do not.

The uncomfortable part is that this is the honest answer rather than the appealing one. Mandarin B is the one Group 2 subject where a tutor cannot compensate for absent daily practice with better teaching, and saying so early is more useful than discovering it in February of Year 13. A student willing to do twelve minutes a day has a real path. A student who is not should be having a different conversation, possibly about ab initio.

sections.heading: HSK and IB Mandarin B: two scales that do not translate cleanly
paragraphs: Many Dubai parents arrive already fluent in one measurement scale, and it is usually not the IB's. HSK is the standardised Chinese proficiency test most families have encountered, through a weekend language school, a previous posting, or an older sibling. The natural question, which level of HSK equals Mandarin B Standard Level, has no clean answer, and the reason is worth understanding because it affects what preparation is useful.

HSK measures proficiency against vocabulary bands. The long-established version of the test ran six levels, with each level associated with an approximate cumulative vocabulary count, and a revised standard with nine levels has since been published; the official HSK channels are the place to confirm current structures and counts rather than any tutoring site. Mandarin B, by contrast, measures what a student can do with texts organised around five prescribed themes, including a written task for a named audience and an oral that develops ideas.

The two therefore overlap without mapping. A student with a solid intermediate HSK result may still score poorly in Mandarin B because they have never written to a text-type brief or developed an argument aloud. A student with no HSK history at all may do well in Mandarin B because their course taught exactly those skills. HSK preparation materials are useful for vocabulary volume and useless for Paper 1 technique, and knowing which is which saves a term of misdirected effort.

The table sets out the comparison in terms of what each instrument actually measures, with the vocabulary counts marked as indicative rather than authoritative. Treat it as a translation aid for a family conversation, not as an equivalence any institution would recognise.

sections.heading: The components, and what each is worth
paragraphs: Mandarin B is assessed through two external papers and one internally assessed individual oral. Paper 1 asks for one written task in a defined text type, for a stated audience and purpose, within a word band that differs by level. Paper 2 covers listening and reading on unseen material. The individual oral is conducted and marked inside the school and then moderated by the IB, which is why the school's internal date for it typically falls well before the written papers.

The written paper is where the character problem becomes a mark problem. Everything a student cannot produce by hand is unavailable, and a candidate working around a gap, substituting a simpler word because the right character will not come, loses marks on range as well as on accuracy. This is the component that rewards the daily review most directly, and it is also the one where a student's self-assessment is least reliable, because reading practice feels like preparation for it and is not.

The receptive paper splits into listening and reading, and in Mandarin these fail for different reasons. Listening fails on tone discrimination and on the absence of a note-taking system, since the recording plays once and a student who stops to decode loses the following answers. Reading fails on character coverage: an unknown character in a key position can make a sentence unreadable in a way that an unknown word in an alphabetic language rarely does, because there is no sounding-out route to a guess.

The oral is more winnable than students expect, at both levels. At Standard Level it begins with a visual stimulus linked to a prescribed theme; at Higher Level it begins from an extract taken from one of the two literary works studied. Tones matter here, and so does the move from describing to interpreting, which is trainable within weeks on unseen images or extracts.

sections.heading: Handwriting or typing: the examination settles it
paragraphs: Modern Mandarin teaching leans heavily on pinyin input, and with good reason. Typing on a phone or laptop lets a learner produce text far above their handwriting level, because the input method converts a phonetic guess into a correct character and the student only has to recognise the right option in a list. It is how Mandarin is actually used by most people most of the time, and it is a legitimate skill. It is also recognition rather than production, and the written papers are handwritten.

This creates a specific failure that is almost invisible until a timed paper exposes it. A student who has done all their practice by typing has been rehearsing selection from a menu. Faced with a blank page they can hear the word, know what it means, and be unable to produce the strokes. Their teacher may not have detected it, because classwork and homework are often typed, and their own sense of their ability is formed by the typed experience.

The remedy is not ideological, it is diagnostic. Character inventories should be tested by hand, from a prompt in English or from a spoken cue, with a blank sheet and no device. The resulting list splits into three groups: automatic, retrievable with effort, and recognition only. Only the first two are available in an examination. Running that test once at the start is often the most informative hour a Mandarin B student spends, and it frequently reframes the family's understanding of the grade.

Schools make their own decision about whether a course uses simplified or traditional characters, and consistency within a response is expected, so confirm which script your child's course uses with the teacher or IB coordinator before buying any practice material. Mixing scripts in one piece of writing is an avoidable loss, and material bought from the wrong tradition quietly teaches the mixing.

sections.heading: Tones cost marks twice, so they get two error logs
paragraphs: Mandarin has four tones plus a neutral tone, and they carry meaning rather than decorating it. A student who produces the wrong tone has said a different word, and a student who hears the wrong tone has heard a different word. Those are two separate failures with two separate cures, and treating them as one vague weakness is why tone problems persist for years in otherwise capable learners.

Production errors show up in the oral and are comparatively easy to work on, because the student can hear a recording of themselves against a model. The discipline that works is narrow: a short list of minimal pairs where the only difference is tone, practised daily, recorded weekly, with a log of which pairs are still unreliable. Students resist recording themselves and benefit from it more than from any amount of correction in the moment, because the evidence is undeniable.

Discrimination errors are the more damaging and the less noticed. A student with a good vocabulary who scores badly in listening is often failing to distinguish tones at speed, which makes a known word unknown mid-sentence. The test for this has to be separate from vocabulary: minimal pairs the student knows well, played at natural speed, scored. If that score is poor, more vocabulary work will not raise the listening mark, and the fix is tone-discrimination drilling.

Keeping two logs makes the diagnosis visible. A student whose production log is improving while their discrimination log is flat has been practising the wrong half. Over a term both should move, and when one refuses to, that is the signal to change the drill rather than to add hours. This is the same principle that governs character review, and in Mandarin it is the only honest way to tell progress from activity.

sections.heading: Where Dubai Mandarin B candidates lose marks
paragraphs: The failure modes in this subject are consistent enough to list, and naming them precisely is more useful than a general assessment. The first is the production gap already described: characters recognised but not retrievable, which caps Paper 1 regardless of comprehension ability. The second is the substitution habit, where a student systematically writes around the words they cannot produce, which costs range marks even when accuracy survives.

The third is text-type blindness. Paper 1 names an audience and a format, and each format carries conventions: how a letter opens and closes, how a blog addresses its reader, how a speech signals its structure. Dubai students who write strongly in English frequently transfer English register and English conventions, which the criteria do not reward. These conventions are closed sets and can be learned in a fortnight, making this the cheapest available gain in the subject.

The fourth is listening collapse, driven by tone discrimination and the absence of a note-taking shorthand. The fifth is thematic gaps: the five prescribed themes bound the vocabulary demand, which is genuinely good news, but a theme squeezed out of Year 12 reappears in the examination and no general fluency covers for vocabulary never taught. The sixth, at Higher Level only, is literary works read only in summary form, a shortcut that survives until the first follow-up question in the oral.

Each of these has a different cure and a different timescale. Text-type conventions move in two weeks. Tone discrimination moves in six to eight. Character production moves over months and only with daily review. A plan that treats them as one problem will produce movement in the fast one and none in the slow ones, which is exactly the pattern that makes families conclude tuition does not work.

sections.heading: Daily contact, spaced repetition and the Dubai calendar
paragraphs: Mandarin review is the one language task that genuinely cannot be batched. Character retention responds to frequency rather than to total hours, which means twelve minutes on six days beats ninety minutes on one. That is a scheduling claim rather than a teaching claim, and it is the reason a Mandarin B plan has to be built around the shape of a Dubai family's year rather than around a lesson slot.

Several features of that year matter. Dubai schools shorten the day during Ramadan and energy in the late afternoon falls, so a fixed 17:00 session is often the worst hour of the day during the month; most families move to a post-Iftar slot or a weekend morning. Mock examination fortnights swallow all review time unless it is deliberately shortened rather than abandoned, because a stopped deck decays fast and restarting costs more than maintaining. Summer and winter breaks, often involving travel, are where the largest gains or the largest losses happen.

The practical answer is a review block small enough to survive a bad week. Twelve minutes is chosen precisely because it can be done in a car, in a waiting room or before bed on a day when nothing else got done. A plan requiring forty-five minutes of daily review is a plan that will be abandoned in the third week of a Dubai term, and an abandoned plan produces worse results than a modest one that holds.

The weekly session then has a management function alongside its teaching one. Was the deck reviewed? Which items keep failing? Is the schedule still realistic given what the other five subjects are doing this month? Those questions take four minutes and they protect the whole project. A tutor who never asks them is teaching Mandarin without managing the only variable that determines whether the teaching sticks.
