sections.heading: Academic honesty where a tool produces flawless output
paragraphs: Mandarin raises the integrity question more sharply than most subjects, because the available tools are extremely good. A translation engine produces natural Chinese instantly, and a pinyin input method will turn a half-remembered sound into a correct character without the student ever retrieving it. A student can therefore submit work far beyond their actual level with no effort and, unlike in some subjects, the output contains no obvious tell in the language itself.

The position IB Gram tutors hold to is stated before the first session. A tutor teaches structures, marks what the student produced, classifies the fault, explains the rule and sets the next task. The student generates every character that reaches a teacher or an examiner. No tutor supplies Chinese text for submission, converts a draft into prose the student could not have built, or rehearses a memorised oral. The IB treats supplied content as malpractice and the consequence falls on the candidate.

The argument that lands with students is practical rather than moral. In the examination there is no input method and no translation engine, only a blank page and whatever is retrievable from memory. Every task completed with a tool is a task that produced no retrievable memory, which means the student arrives at the paper with a record of good homework and an empty inventory. The tool has not helped them; it has hidden the gap until it was too late to close.

The marking convention that follows is deliberately slower. Feedback names the fault and the rule rather than supplying the correction, and a character that will not come is logged rather than looked up. That frustrates students in week one and is the only approach that moves an inventory, because the act of retrieval under mild difficulty is the act that builds memory. Being handed the right character feels efficient and teaches nothing.

faqs.question: How many Chinese characters does my child need for Mandarin B?
faqs.answer: Estimates vary by source and by text difficulty, so treat any single authoritative-sounding figure with caution. What matters more is that the load runs into the thousands of items and that each item needs separate work for recognition and for handwritten production. The practical approach is to measure rather than estimate: test the student's inventory by hand, from a prompt, with no device, and sort the results into automatic, retrievable with effort, and recognition only. Only the first two categories are usable in an examination. That measurement usually reframes the family's understanding of the grade within an hour.

faqs.question: My child reads Chinese well but writes badly. Why does that happen?
faqs.answer: Because recognition and production are different memory tasks, and most modern Mandarin practice trains only the first. Typing with a pinyin input method converts a phonetic guess into a correct character and asks the student only to pick it from a list, which is recognition wearing the costume of writing. Reading on a screen with a dictionary a tap away feels like fluency for the same reason. The examination papers are handwritten, with no input method and no dictionary, so everything in the recognition-only category is unavailable. The fix is hand-testing inventories and a daily spaced-repetition block on production.

faqs.question: Does HSK level tell us anything about likely Mandarin B performance?
faqs.answer: It tells you something about vocabulary volume and almost nothing about examination technique. HSK measures proficiency against vocabulary bands; Mandarin B measures what a student can do with unseen texts organised around five prescribed themes, including a written task for a named audience and an oral that develops ideas. A student with a respectable intermediate HSK result can still score poorly in Mandarin B, never having written to a text-type brief. Confirm current HSK structures on the official HSK channels rather than on a tutoring site, and use HSK material for vocabulary volume only.

faqs.question: Should we practise Mandarin writing by typing or by hand?
faqs.answer: Both, for different purposes, with handwriting protected. Typing is how Chinese is actually used and it builds recognition and reading speed efficiently. Handwriting is what the examination requires, and only handwriting builds retrieval from memory. The failure to avoid is doing all practice by typing, which produces a student whose homework looks strong and whose timed paper collapses, with neither the student nor the teacher having detected the gap. A reasonable split is typed work for volume and reading, and at least one timed handwritten task every week with no device present.

faqs.question: Why does my child score badly in Mandarin listening despite good vocabulary?
faqs.answer: Most often because of tone discrimination at speed rather than vocabulary. A mis-heard tone turns a known word into an unknown one mid-sentence, and the recording does not wait. The test has to be separated from vocabulary: take minimal pairs the student already knows well, play them at natural speed, and score the result. If that score is poor, more vocabulary work will not raise the listening mark. The cure is daily minimal-pair drilling plus a note-taking shorthand that keeps the hand moving past anything unfamiliar, and it typically takes six to eight weeks to show.

faqs.question: Simplified or traditional characters: which should my child use?
faqs.answer: Whichever the school's course uses, and consistently within any one piece of writing. Schools make this decision themselves, so confirm it with the Mandarin teacher or the IB coordinator before buying practice material, because material bought from the other tradition quietly teaches a student to mix the two. Mixing within a response is an avoidable loss of marks that has nothing to do with language ability. If a family has a heritage reason to prefer one script and the school teaches the other, that is a conversation to have with the school in Year 11 rather than a problem to solve privately.

faqs.question: Do you send a Mandarin tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. Mandarin B support for Dubai families runs one-to-one over live video, with handwritten character practice photographed and annotated on screen so the tutor marks the strokes the student actually produced. For this subject the trade is clearly favourable: a tutor who has taught this syllabus at this level and can mark handwriting properly is unlikely to live in your community, and online matching makes experience rather than distance the deciding factor.

faqs.question: How much daily Mandarin practice is realistic alongside six Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Around twelve minutes, and the number is deliberately small. Character retention responds to frequency rather than to total hours, so six short sessions beat one long one, and a block that can be done in a car or before bed is one that still exists in week ten of term. Plans built around forty-five minutes a day get abandoned in the third week of a Dubai term, and an abandoned plan does more damage than a modest one, because a stopped deck decays quickly and restarting costs more than maintaining ever did.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan and mock examination weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this subject the review block matters more than the lesson slot. Dubai schools shorten the day during Ramadan and late afternoons become unworkable for most families, so sessions usually shift to post-Iftar or to a weekend morning. During mock fortnights the sensible move is to cut daily review to five minutes on failing items rather than dropping it, because a deck left untouched for two weeks loses more than those two weeks. Tell the tutor the dates in advance and the schedule is built around them rather than repaired afterwards.

faqs.question: Is Mandarin B Higher Level realistic for a student who started in Year 10?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the character inventory and on willingness to do daily review, not on how many years appear on a transcript. Higher Level adds two literary works and a longer written band, both of which magnify a production gap: more words written means more opportunities for a missing character to cost marks. A student with four years of typed practice and a thin handwritten inventory will often achieve a better Diploma total at Standard Level. Raise it with the IB coordinator in Year 11 while a level change is still administratively simple, and decide on measured evidence.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write a Mandarin task before my child submits it?
faqs.answer: A tutor can mark it, classify each fault, explain the rule and set a rewrite. A tutor cannot supply Chinese text, convert a draft into prose the student could not have built, or rehearse a memorised oral. The IB treats supplied content as malpractice and the penalty lands on the candidate. There is also a practical argument that matters more to most students: in the examination there is no input method and no translation engine, so a task completed with either produced no retrievable memory and hid the gap until it was too late to close.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools offer Mandarin in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: It varies year to year with numbers and staffing, so your own school's course booklet and IB coordinator are the only dependable source. In broad terms Mandarin appears more often where year groups are large enough to fill a Group 2 class, which in Dubai means the established international clusters rather than the newer outer communities. Smaller or newer Diploma cohorts may offer it at Standard Level only, or not at all in a given year. If the answer is no, the realistic options are a different Group 2 language or, for a heritage reader, a Group 1 Chinese route.

faqs.question: What does the Higher Level oral actually require my child to do?
faqs.answer: At Higher Level the oral starts from an extract taken from one of the two literary works studied. The student comments on the extract, places it within the work and then discusses the works and the prescribed themes more broadly. Reading summaries does not survive this, because an extract connects to the rest of the text and a teacher can ask about that connection. The preparation that works is a dated reading plan for both works and a quotation bank organised by theme, built while reading rather than afterwards, with commentary rehearsed aloud in Mandarin rather than in English.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with my child in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published.

faqs.question: What happens if no Mandarin B specialist is free when we ask?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a realistic timeframe, rather than placing a general Chinese speaker and leaving you to discover the syllabus knowledge is absent. Mandarin B is a narrow specialism, and at Higher Level, where the literary works are involved, the pool is narrower still. The options we would put to a family are a short wait for a named tutor, a Standard Level specialist for the components that do not touch the works, or a focused block on whichever component is most urgent. Which makes sense depends on how near the school's oral window sits.

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-online-tutor.closingBody: If your child is taking Mandarin B in a Dubai school and the grade does not match how comfortably they read, the gap is almost certainly between recognition and handwritten production. Book the free trial lesson, one per family and no card details required. The hour produces three numbers: characters that are automatic, characters retrievable with effort, and characters recognised only. Add a minimal-pair tone check and a short timed task and you have a profile that tells you what the next term should do, measured rather than assumed.

intro.heading: What Mandarin B actually assesses, and why Dubai families ask for help in DP1
paragraphs: Mandarin B is a language acquisition course. It is not for a student whose strongest language is Mandarin — that student belongs in Chinese A Language and Literature, and a Diploma coordinator in Dubai will usually say so during option sheets. Mandarin B assumes some prior learning, moves through five prescribed themes, and assesses what your child can do with the language rather than how much grammar they can recite. Three components carry the grade: Paper 1 is a single piece of writing in a specified text type, Paper 2 is listening plus reading, and the individual oral is marked by the teacher and moderated externally.

The split matters because it is where family expectations and the real exam diverge. Parents in Dubai often judge Mandarin progress by vocabulary lists and character worksheets, which is the part of the subject that is easiest to see. The examination rewards something else: whether a response is appropriate to its audience and purpose, whether the register fits a blog post rather than a formal letter, and whether a conversation keeps moving when the examiner asks something unscripted. A student can know eight hundred characters and still land in the middle band because the message was thin.

The second pressure is mechanical. Mandarin is written in characters, and characters have to be produced from memory with a pen, in a room, against a clock. Recognition and production are different skills and they decay at different rates. A student who reads a passage comfortably on a screen can stall in Paper 1 because three of the characters they need will not come back. This is the single most common gap we are asked to close, and it responds well to short, frequent, tested practice — which is exactly what a weekly fifty-minute session plus a daily ten-minute routine looks like.

The third is the oral. The individual oral in Mandarin B is worth a quarter of the grade and is the component students prepare for least well, because it feels like a conversation and therefore feels unpreparable. It is not. The criteria reward language, message and interactive skills, and interactive skills is where a Dubai cohort tends to lose marks — a long memorised presentation followed by one-word answers scores lower than a shorter presentation followed by a real exchange. Rehearsing that exchange with someone who is not the class teacher, and who will push back, changes the mark.

IB Gram works as a matching platform. You describe the level, the character set, the school's timeline and the component that is causing trouble; we propose a Mandarin specialist and run a free trial lesson — one per family, no card details taken — before anything is booked. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For a language subject that is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise, because the pool of Diploma-level Mandarin teachers inside any single Dubai community is small.

Paper 2: listening and reading, 50% of the grade — the largest single block
Individual oral: 25%, marked internally and moderated by the IB
HL adds two literary works; the HL oral starts from an extract from one of them
Character production, not recognition, is where timed papers are usually lost

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-tutor.programmesIntro: Mandarin sits in a different place in each programme, and the jump between them is the moment most Dubai students need support. These are the stages we cover, with what the Mandarin component looks like inside each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Mandarin B sits in Group 2, language acquisition, at either Standard or Higher Level. Assessment is Paper 1 writing, Paper 2 listening and reading, and the individual oral. HL carries two literary works and a longer Paper 1 task. Students sit the course over two years, with the oral usually scheduled in the second half of DP2 and the written papers in the May session that Dubai schools use.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP cohorts are unusually mixed in Mandarin. One class can hold a student who did MYP Mandarin for five years, a student who arrived from a Beijing international school, and a student who began in DP1 because the school required a second language. A tutor working one-to-one is diagnosing which of those three a student actually is before teaching anything.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language Acquisition runs in phases rather than levels, and a student finishes in one of six phases depending on where they started. The phase reached at the end of MYP5 is the single best predictor of whether Mandarin B HL is realistic. MYP assessment is criterion-based across listening, reading, speaking and writing, with no external paper, which is why the first timed Paper 2 in DP1 is a shock.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai IB continuum schools run Mandarin from the primary years, so a DP1 class may contain students with seven years of exposure sitting beside students with two. Coordinators in Dubai tend to place generously; a tutor's first job is often to check honestly whether the placement will hold through DP2.

programmes.name: Language B alongside the DP core
programmes.description: Mandarin B does not sit alone. The same student is writing an Extended Essay, building a TOK exhibition and completing CAS, and all three compete with character practice for the same evenings. Language subjects lose out in that competition because the work is incremental and nothing is due tomorrow. A weekly fixed session protects the time that would otherwise be reallocated to whatever has the nearest deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai school calendars put the heaviest internal deadline stack between November and February, which is also when Mandarin oral recordings are typically scheduled. Families who plan language support as a two-year drip rather than a pre-exam sprint come through that window in better shape.

programmes.name: IGCSE and pre-DP Mandarin
programmes.description: Many Dubai students reach Mandarin B through Cambridge IGCSE Mandarin Chinese as a Foreign Language rather than through MYP. That route builds solid controlled writing and weaker spontaneous speech, because the IGCSE speaking component is shorter and more structured than the DP individual oral. Students arriving from it usually need oral stamina more than they need vocabulary.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment, so the IGCSE-to-DP transfer is common here in a way it is not in continuum-only systems. We treat the first term of DP1 as a bridging term for these students rather than assuming the IGCSE grade transfers as a level.

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-tutor.subjectsIntro: Group 2 is the part of the Diploma where Dubai schools offer the widest spread and the thinnest in-house specialist cover. These are the language courses we are asked for most, with what each one actually demands.

subjects.name: Mandarin B
subjects.description: The core of this page. Writing in a prescribed text type, listening and reading under time, and a moderated individual oral. HL adds two literary works and a longer written task. Marks are lost on register, on message development and on characters that will not surface under pressure rather than on grammar rules.

subjects.name: Mandarin ab initio
subjects.description: A separate course for students with little or no prior Mandarin, built on three themes and a defined syllabus of functions. It is not a softer Mandarin B: the assessment still includes a written paper, a listening and reading paper and an oral, and the vocabulary ceiling is lower but the accuracy expectation is high.

subjects.name: Chinese A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The right course for a student whose strongest language is Mandarin. Assessment moves to paper one guided analysis, paper two comparative essay, the individual oral on a global issue and, at HL, the HL essay. Students sometimes land here after being wrongly placed in Mandarin B, and the skills do not transfer directly.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: The same assessment architecture as Mandarin B, which makes it a useful reference point for parents. Five themes, Paper 1 text types, Paper 2 listening and reading, individual oral. French B students tend to lose marks on tense accuracy where Mandarin B students lose them on character production.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Widely offered across Dubai IB schools and often the fallback when a Mandarin placement is withdrawn. Shares the Language B criteria exactly, so a student switching in DP1 keeps the skill of writing to audience and purpose and rebuilds only the lexical base.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Relevant in Dubai beyond Group 2, because KHDA requires Arabic for all students in private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. A student taking Mandarin B still sits mandatory Arabic lessons, and the two scripts compete for the same handwriting practice time.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Taken by students whose schooling has been in another language, common in Dubai's Chinese, Japanese and Korean family communities. Pairs frequently with Chinese A, and the pairing is what makes a bilingual diploma possible for those students.

subjects.name: German B and Japanese B
subjects.description: Smaller cohorts, often taught by a single teacher per school, which is where availability problems start. These are the courses where a Dubai family is most likely to be told the school cannot offer additional support, and where online matching makes the practical difference.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Taken alongside Mandarin B and relevant to it: the TOK exhibition rewards precise expression, and students who have learned to control register in a second language often write tighter TOK prose. Graded A-E and combined with the Extended Essay for up to three points.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Included because of the timetable, not the content. In Dubai schools, Mandarin B and Maths AI often sit in the same option block, and a student dropping one to protect the other is a decision worth making with the subject requirements for their university shortlist on the table.

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-tutor.regionsIntro: Mandarin teaching is not spread evenly across Dubai. These notes describe where the Diploma-level demand sits, which school clusters generate it, and what a weekday evening realistically looks like in each area.

regions.name: International City and Warsan
regions.note: Dubai's largest concentration of Mandarin-speaking households, anchored around the Dragon Mart trading community. Demand here is often the reverse of the rest of the city: students who speak Mandarin fluently at home but cannot write it at Diploma standard, and who are frequently mis-placed into Mandarin B when Chinese A would fit better.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: The densest cluster of IB Diploma schools in Dubai, and the area that generates most of our Mandarin B enquiries. Students here usually have continuous Mandarin from the primary years, so the work is refinement — register, message development, oral stamina — rather than foundation building.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: Apartment living, long lift waits and a 4pm school-run window that swallows an hour. Families here schedule Mandarin at 6.30pm or later, and the main constraint is that the student has already done two hours of homework before the session starts. Short, high-intensity character drills work better here than long lessons.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: A high proportion of relocating families, which means Mandarin B students who joined the course mid-stream from a different curriculum. The diagnostic question in this area is usually which phase of MYP or which IGCSE route they came from, because the gap is rarely where the school assumes it is.

regions.name: Mirdif, Festival City and Al Garhoud
regions.note: Served by established IB schools on the Deira side of the creek, with a commute that makes any in-person evening arrangement expensive in time. Mandarin sessions here are almost always scheduled online by preference rather than as a fallback, and a 7pm start is normal.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, Arabian Ranches and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa communities feeding the longest-established Diploma cohorts in the city. Mandarin B here is often a third or fourth language choice for a student already carrying two HL sciences, so the realistic ask is a maintenance session that protects the grade rather than a programme that raises it two bands.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing, younger family profile, and a school mix that is mostly British curriculum with IB appearing at Diploma level only. Mandarin students here tend to arrive from IGCSE Mandarin Chinese and need spontaneous speech work before anything else.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Quoz
regions.note: Newer school openings and a parent population that compares tutoring options carefully on price. The honest answer here is that a Mandarin specialist costs what the market charges for a scarce language rather than what a generalist charges, and the rate table further down this page sets out those bands.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: The Diploma heartland of Dubai, and where most Mandarin B teaching in the emirate happens. Students from these schools generally reach DP1 with continuous Mandarin behind them, so the tutoring brief is component-specific rather than remedial.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Dubai Festival City and Al Garhoud
schoolClusters.note: IB continuum schools on the Deira side, several running language acquisition from the primary years. Mandarin cohorts here are smaller, which makes one-to-one cover harder to find locally and online matching more useful.

schoolClusters.note: Long-established and newer Diploma cohorts in the villa belt. Option blocks here are tight, and Mandarin B frequently competes with a second science or with Maths AA for the same slot.

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-tutor.modesIntro: Mandarin responds to frequency more than to length. These are the three shapes of support Dubai families use, and the one we recommend depends entirely on how far your child is from their oral recording date.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, fifty minutes
modes.description: The default for a DP1 or DP2 student working through the course. One live video session a week, with a short daily character routine between sessions that the tutor sets and checks. The session is split: a tested recall block, a text-type block aimed at Paper 1, and ten minutes of unscripted conversation in Mandarin so the oral is never cold.

modes.title: Oral sprint block
modes.description: Four to six sessions concentrated in the weeks before the individual oral. Each session records a full-length oral under conditions, marks it against language, message and interactive skills, and then rebuilds the weakest criterion. Students hear themselves, which does more for interactive skills than any amount of advice about them.

modes.title: Paper clinic before the May session
modes.description: Timed Paper 1 and Paper 2 practice in the final term, marked and returned with the mark scheme logic explained rather than the answers handed over. Useful for students whose coursework is strong and whose timed performance is not, which in Mandarin is most of them.
bullets: Papers sat to the real duration, SL and HL timings respected
Listening practice at genuine speed, not slowed classroom audio
Reading sections attacked question-first to protect time

modes.title: Holiday intensive
modes.description: Short daily sessions through the Dubai school breaks, when the timetable finally stops competing. Most useful for students switching route — ab initio to B SL, or B SL to B HL — and for arrivals mid-course who need a concentrated bridge rather than a weekly drip.
bullets: Three to five short sessions a week over two or three weeks

sections.heading: What a Mandarin B tutor in Dubai is usually hired to fix
paragraphs: An IB DP Mandarin B tutor in Dubai is hired for a component, not for the subject. Families arrive with one of four descriptions, and the right first session is different for each. The first is slow character production: the student reads fluently and freezes in Paper 1. The second is listening speed: classroom audio has been comfortable, the past-paper audio is not. The third is a flat individual oral, usually a well-memorised presentation attached to a conversation that goes nowhere. The fourth is placement — a student in the wrong course, where no amount of tutoring fixes the structural mismatch.

Separating those four takes about forty minutes of diagnostic work. We ask for a recent piece of written work, a recording of an oral if one exists, and the school's assessment calendar. A student who scores well on reading comprehension and badly on written production has a retrieval problem and needs a daily routine. A student who scores badly on both has a vocabulary base problem and needs the themes rebuilt. A student who performs well in class and poorly in timed conditions has an exam-technique problem, which is the fastest of the four to shift.

The fourth case deserves honesty rather than a sales answer. If your child speaks Mandarin at home and has been placed in Mandarin B, they may be capped by the course rather than by their ability, and a Diploma coordinator can still consider Chinese A in DP1. If your child began Mandarin in DP1 with no prior learning and has been placed in Mandarin B rather than ab initio, the gap is structural and the conversation to have is with the school. We will say so in the trial lesson rather than sell two years of sessions against a placement that will not hold.

What a session does not do is replace the class. The tutor works from the same five themes and the same subject guide the school uses, follows the school's internal deadlines, and does not introduce a parallel syllabus. In a language subject that discipline matters more than in most, because a second set of vocabulary lists is actively unhelpful.
bullets: Bring one recent written task, one oral recording if available, and the school's deadline calendar
Reading strong but writing weak means a retrieval problem, not a knowledge problem
Strong in class and weak under time means technique, which moves fastest
Placement mismatches are a school conversation, not a tutoring one

sections.heading: The Mandarin B assessment model, component by component
paragraphs: Mandarin B is assessed through two external papers and one internally assessed oral that the IB moderates. The weightings are identical at Standard and Higher Level — 25 per cent for Paper 1, 50 per cent for Paper 2, 25 per cent for the individual oral — but the durations and the demands are not. HL sits a longer Paper 1 task and a longer listening section, and the HL oral starts from an extract from one of the two literary works studied rather than from a visual stimulus.

The half of the grade carried by Paper 2 is the part Dubai families underestimate most. It is a receptive paper: listening first, then reading, both point-marked rather than criterion-marked. There is no credit for effort and no partial credit for approximately the right idea. The practical consequence is that Paper 2 improves through volume and timing rather than through explanation, and that it is the component a tutor can shift fastest in a short engagement.

Paper 1 is a single piece of writing in one of the prescribed text types, chosen from a small number of tasks. The task length for Mandarin is specified in characters rather than words, and the subject guide gives the range for each level — ask the school's Mandarin teacher for the current figure rather than relying on a tutoring website. What is stable is the marking: language, message and conceptual understanding, with conceptual understanding rewarding the student who chose the right register and format for the audience named in the task.

The individual oral is marked by the class teacher against language, message and interactive skills, then moderated by the IB. Because it is internal, its timing varies between Dubai schools by several months. Ask for your child's recording date in the first week of DP2; it is the single most useful date in the Mandarin calendar and the one families most often learn too late.

sections.heading: Characters: the workload nobody puts on the timetable
paragraphs: Character production is the distinctive labour of Mandarin B and the one schools cannot timetable enough of. Reading a character is recognition; writing it from memory is recall, and recall decays. A student who met a character in October and has not written it since will probably not produce it in May. This is not a measure of intelligence or effort — it is how memory behaves — and it is why a daily ten-minute routine beats a weekly ninety-minute session for this specific skill.

The second complication is the choice of character set. Mandarin B candidates write in either simplified or traditional characters and must be consistent across the paper. Dubai schools serving mainland Chinese families generally teach simplified; schools with a Taiwanese or Hong Kong intake may teach traditional. A tutor has to match the school, and a student who has been drilled by a tutor in the other set has been made slower, not faster. We confirm the set in the first session and record it on the match.

Stroke order is the part parents are most tempted to let go, and it is worth defending. Correct stroke order makes a character faster to write, more legible under pressure and easier to retrieve, because the motor sequence carries part of the memory. In timed conditions legibility is a mark issue: an examiner who cannot read a character cannot credit it. Screen-shared stroke work in a live session, where the tutor watches the hand move rather than only sees the finished product, is one of the few things online delivery does better than a worksheet.

The routine that works is unglamorous. A running list of characters that have failed twice or more, tested at the start of every session, with anything mastered removed and anything new added. Most students carry between forty and eighty live items at any time. The list shrinks through DP2 if it is maintained and balloons in March if it is not.
bullets: Recognition and production are separate skills; papers test production
Simplified or traditional must match the school and stay consistent
Stroke order protects speed, legibility and recall under exam pressure
A failed-twice list, tested weekly, is the mechanism that actually works

sections.heading: Ab initio, Mandarin B SL or Mandarin B HL: choosing the route that will hold
paragraphs: Option-sheet season in Dubai produces more Mandarin problems than the course itself does. Three routes exist and they are genuinely different courses rather than three difficulty settings. Mandarin ab initio is Standard Level only, built for students with little or no prior learning, and organised around a defined syllabus of themes and functions. Mandarin B assumes prior learning and works across five broad themes with no closed vocabulary list. Chinese A is for students whose strongest language is Mandarin and is a literature course, not an acquisition course.

The decision should be driven by evidence rather than ambition. For a student coming out of MYP Language Acquisition, the phase reached at the end of MYP5 is the most reliable indicator. For a student coming from IGCSE Mandarin Chinese as a Foreign Language, the grade matters less than the speaking component performance, because the DP oral is longer and far less structured. For a heritage speaker, the honest test is writing: fluent speech with weak character production points to Mandarin B, while strong reading and writing point to Chinese A.

Higher Level adds two literary works and a longer written task, and the HL oral begins from a literary extract. That is a substantial addition for a student who wants Mandarin as a fifth or sixth subject alongside two HL sciences. In Dubai, where Diploma option blocks are tight and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons also take timetable space, we see more students helped by taking Mandarin B SL well than by taking HL badly.

If a route change is needed, the window is narrow. Schools can usually move a student between levels or courses during the first term of DP1 and rarely after the oral has been scheduled. A trial lesson in September that identifies a mismatch is worth more than a year of tutoring that papers over one.

sections.heading: The individual oral, and the three ways Dubai students lose marks on it
paragraphs: A quarter of the Mandarin B grade is decided in roughly twelve to fifteen minutes with the class teacher. The structure is a short presentation — from a visual stimulus at SL, from a literary extract at HL — followed by discussion on the stimulus and then broader discussion covering at least one further theme. Three criteria apply: language, message, and interactive skills. The third is the one that separates grades in a Dubai cohort, and it is the one least practised.

The first failure mode is the memorised monologue. A student who delivers four flawless minutes and then answers follow-up questions in three words has demonstrated preparation rather than interaction. Interactive skills reward understanding a question, responding to it, and keeping an exchange going without the examiner carrying it. The fix is unscripted practice with someone who will ask the awkward second question, which is hard to arrange inside a class of fifteen.

The second is thematic narrowness. The discussion is supposed to range across at least one theme beyond the stimulus, and a student who has prepared only identities will stall when the conversation moves to sharing the planet. We work the five themes as a rotating schedule through DP2, so that by the recording date every theme has produced at least one real conversation rather than one set of notes.

The third is silence management. Students lose fluency marks not when they do not know a word but when they stop. A handful of rehearsed repair phrases — asking for a repeat, rephrasing, buying a second — keeps the exchange alive and keeps the language criterion intact. These are coachable in two sessions and almost never taught explicitly.
Recording matters more than advice. A student who hears their own oral alongside the criteria usually diagnoses two of these three themselves, which is a faster route to change than being told.
bullets: Interactive skills, not vocabulary range, is where Dubai cohorts usually drop
Prepare all five themes on rotation, not the stimulus theme alone
Rehearse repair phrases so a pause does not become silence

sections.heading: What Mandarin tuition costs in Dubai, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Mandarin is a scarce-supply language in the Dubai tutoring market, and the rate reflects that rather than reflecting the difficulty of the subject. Published market rates in Dubai run from roughly AED 45-65 an hour at the budget online end, where EdFlik advertises, to AED 650 an hour for a premium named tutor, which is the figure BartyED publishes. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's 2026 rate table for Dubai puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200-450 or above.

Those are market figures published by other providers, quoted here with their source and their date so you can check them. They are not IB Gram's price list. What we publish instead is the shape of the model: a free trial lesson before anything is booked, one trial per family, no card details taken, and a rate confirmed in writing with the specific tutor before the first paid session. For a language with a thin specialist pool, the rate is set by who is actually available at Diploma level rather than by a tier chart.

Four things move the number for Mandarin specifically. A Higher Level student with two literary works needs a tutor comfortable with literary discussion in Mandarin, which narrows the pool. A student needing traditional characters narrows it further. A session inside the 5pm-7.30pm Gulf Standard Time window — when every Dubai family wants it — prices differently from a 9pm or weekend-morning slot. And an oral sprint block in the four weeks before a recording is priced as specialist work rather than as maintenance tuition.

The cost worth putting beside those numbers is school fees. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's economic incentives package. Against a Diploma-year fee, a weekly language session is a small marginal addition — but it is still worth buying with a diagnosis rather than buying by the hour indefinitely.

sections.heading: Online Mandarin tuition against an in-home tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: The phrase parents search for is a home tutor, so it deserves a straight answer. An in-home Mandarin tutor in Dubai costs more per hour than an online one, because travel is inside the price, and the published bands above show the gap: roughly AED 180-350 for an in-home hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified online hour. Travel also shapes availability. A tutor who can reach Arabian Ranches at 5pm and Mirdif at 7pm cannot do both on the same evening, which is why in-home schedules are rigid and why cancellations cost more.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We state that rather than leaving it to be discovered after a booking, because two competitors in this market route UAE parents to numbers in another country without saying so.

For Mandarin the online format is not a compromise. The constraint on in-home Mandarin tuition in Dubai is geography: your child gets a Diploma-level Mandarin specialist only if one lives within a reasonable drive of your community, and across most of the city there is no such person. Online, the pool becomes every available Diploma Mandarin teacher who can work in Gulf Standard Time. For a Higher Level student who needs literary discussion in Mandarin, that difference decides whether specialist support exists at all.

The format also suits the subject mechanically. Characters are written on a shared screen where the tutor watches the stroke sequence in real time. Listening practice plays at full quality through headphones rather than through a room. Orals are recorded and replayed against the criteria, which is the single most effective thing we do and which an in-home session rarely produces. Written work is annotated on the file and kept, so a pattern across six tasks is visible rather than remembered.

sections.heading: Mandarin B alongside the mandatory UAE subjects on a Dubai timetable
paragraphs: A Dubai Diploma student taking Mandarin B is not only taking Mandarin. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and its published guidelines state that these requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those lessons occupy real timetable space beside six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS.

The arrangement is more specific than most families realise. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met.

The practical consequence for a Mandarin student is handwriting fatigue and competing script practice. A student maintaining Arabic script for a mandatory lesson and Chinese characters for Mandarin B is doing two kinds of production practice that neither teacher sees together. We plan the character routine around the Arabic timetable rather than against it, which usually means character recall in the morning and nothing script-heavy on a day with a double Arabic period.

One boundary is worth stating. KHDA guidance is clear that for the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, and that schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. If your child needs help with mandatory Arabic, that conversation belongs with the school rather than with a Mandarin tutor working outside the approved content.

sections.heading: Permits, academic honesty and what a Mandarin tutor may not do
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. Official guidance states that the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE app, website and e-services system.

Anyone providing private tutoring in the UAE without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you — if a provider cites a specific figure, treat it as unverified. A separate rule applies in Abu Dhabi, where ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school; the MoHRE permit code of conduct carries a similar restriction. The practical reading for a Dubai family is simple: your child's own Mandarin teacher is the wrong person to hire privately.

Academic honesty in a language subject looks different from academic honesty in an essay subject, and it is still the line that matters most. A tutor may teach vocabulary and structures, model a text type, mark a practice task against the criteria, explain why a register is wrong and rehearse an unscripted conversation. A tutor may not write any part of a Paper 1 response that will be submitted, may not script an individual oral for a student to deliver, and may not produce work the student then presents as their own. The oral is internally assessed; a scripted performance is a malpractice exposure for the student, and expulsion risk is not worth a mark.

We also do not supply IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes as downloads. Those are the IB's copyright, and a tutor who offers to hand them over is telling you something about how they operate. The right route is the school's IB coordinator and the IB's own published material.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps is specific: Mandarin B SL, DP1, simplified characters, oral in February, Paper 2 listening is the problem. That sentence lets us shortlist two or three Mandarin specialists rather than send a generic match. Add the school name if you are comfortable doing so, because the oral schedule varies between Dubai schools.

process.title: Send one written task and one recording
process.description: A recent Paper 1 style task and, if the school has produced one, an oral recording. Those two artefacts tell a Mandarin specialist more in ten minutes than a report card does in a term. We use them to decide whether the problem is retrieval, vocabulary base or exam technique before the trial lesson rather than during it.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with a diagnosis at the end
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, no card details taken. The tutor runs a short diagnostic, then tells you plainly what they think the gap is and how many weeks they expect it to take. If the honest answer is that the student is in the wrong course, they will say so and you will have lost nothing.

process.title: Agree the rate and the slot in writing
process.description: Before the first paid session the specific tutor's rate, the session length and the weekly time in Gulf Standard Time are confirmed in writing. Slots inside the 5pm-7.30pm window are the ones Dubai families compete for, so a 7.30pm or weekend-morning start is often easier to protect across a whole term.

process.title: Run the weekly cycle and keep the failed list
process.description: Each session opens with a test of the running character list and closes with the next week's routine. Written tasks are annotated and kept, so by the sixth task the pattern is visible rather than remembered. You get a short written note after each session rather than a dashboard.

process.title: Switch the tutor rather than the plan if the fit is wrong
process.description: If two sessions in the match is not working, say so and we will propose a different Mandarin specialist. Language tuition depends on the student being willing to talk badly in front of someone, and that either happens with a particular person or it does not. Changing tutor early costs a fortnight; persisting costs a term.

whyPoints.title: The specialist pool is not limited by your postcode
whyPoints.description: Diploma-level Mandarin teachers are thin on the ground in any single Dubai community. Online matching replaces the question of who lives near Al Furjan with the question of who is available in Gulf Standard Time, which for Higher Level literary work is the difference between a specialist and whoever is nearest.

whyPoints.title: Orals are recorded and marked against the criteria
whyPoints.description: A quarter of the grade sits in one conversation, and most students never hear themselves have it. Each oral rehearsal is recorded, marked against language, message and interactive skills, and replayed. Students diagnose their own interaction problems faster than any explanation achieves.

whyPoints.title: Character work is watched, not just collected
whyPoints.description: On a shared screen the tutor sees the stroke sequence as it happens, which is where speed, legibility and recall are built. A worksheet returned the next week shows the finished character and hides the habit that made it slow.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, with their source
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are other providers' published figures, quoted with the provider and the date so you can check them. Three of the six competitor pages we examined for this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis you can act on without us
whyPoints.description: The trial lesson ends with a view on whether the problem is retrieval, vocabulary, technique or placement. If it is placement, the useful next step is a conversation with the Diploma coordinator, and we will tell you that instead of selling a programme around it.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on what a tutor will do
whyPoints.description: We teach, model, mark and rehearse. We do not write Paper 1 responses, script orals, or supply IB documents as downloads. In a market where one ranking site sells completed Internal Assessments, the boundary is worth stating in writing.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP Mandarin B tutor in Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai span a wide band. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour at the budget online end, Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase shows AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts specialist IB and IGCSE tuition at AED 200-450 or above, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are their figures with their dates, not ours. Mandarin usually prices towards the specialist end because the Diploma-level pool is small, and Higher Level literary work narrows it further. IB Gram confirms the specific tutor's rate in writing before the first paid session, after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is Mandarin B the right course if my child already speaks Mandarin at home?
faqs.answer: Often not. Mandarin B is a language acquisition course, and a heritage speaker placed in it may be limited by the course rather than by their own ability. The honest test is writing rather than speech: a student who talks fluently but cannot produce characters at Diploma standard usually belongs in Mandarin B, while a student whose reading and writing are both strong is better served by Chinese A Language and Literature, which is a literature course with a different assessment model. Raise it with the Diploma coordinator in the first term of DP1, because schools can rarely move a student after the individual oral has been scheduled.

faqs.question: My child writes Chinese characters too slowly in timed papers. Can that be fixed?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more reliable things to fix, because the cause is mechanical rather than conceptual. Slow production usually means the character is being recalled rather than written automatically, and the motor sequence has not been rehearsed recently enough. The routine that works is a running list of characters that have failed twice or more, tested at the start of every session, with ten minutes of daily practice between sessions. Stroke order matters here: a correctly sequenced character is faster and more legible, and an examiner who cannot read a character cannot credit it. Expect visible change over six to eight weeks, not one.

faqs.question: Should my child take Mandarin ab initio or Mandarin B SL?
faqs.answer: Ab initio is a Standard Level course designed for students with little or no prior Mandarin, organised around a defined set of themes and functions. Mandarin B assumes several years of prior learning and works across five broader themes with no closed vocabulary list. The deciding evidence is usually the MYP phase reached at the end of MYP5, or for students arriving from Cambridge IGCSE Mandarin Chinese, performance in the speaking component rather than the overall grade. A student beginning Mandarin in DP1 is almost always better placed in ab initio, and a placement that is too ambitious tends to surface in DP2 when it cannot be changed.

faqs.question: Does the Mandarin B listening section use audio at native speed?
faqs.answer: Yes. Paper 2 listening assesses comprehension of spoken Mandarin at natural speed across a range of text types, which is why students who have been comfortable with classroom audio can be caught out by past papers. Classroom recordings are often slightly slowed or heavily contextualised; examination audio is neither. The practical fix is volume and condition: listening practice at full speed, through headphones, with the paper in front of the student and the clock running. Standard Level listening runs about 45 minutes and Higher Level about an hour, and the listening and reading sections together carry half of the final grade.

faqs.question: What are the five themes in the IB Mandarin B course?
faqs.answer: Language B is built on five prescribed themes: identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation, and sharing the planet. They frame the texts studied, the written tasks and the oral discussion, and the individual oral is expected to range beyond the theme attached to the stimulus. That is why preparing one theme thoroughly is a poor strategy. We rotate all five through DP2 so that each has produced at least one genuine unscripted conversation before the recording date, rather than one set of notes. Your child's teacher will have mapped the school's units onto these themes, and that map is worth asking for.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the two literary works in Mandarin B HL?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the component where a specialist matters most. Higher Level Mandarin B requires two literary works, and the Higher Level individual oral starts from an extract from one of them followed by discussion. Supporting that means reading the works in Mandarin, discussing them in Mandarin, and rehearsing the extract-based presentation under conditions. The pool of tutors who can do all three at Diploma level is small in any single Dubai community, which is the main practical reason families here use online matching for Higher Level rather than Standard Level. A tutor teaches and questions; the student's own responses stay their own.

faqs.question: How much of the Mandarin B grade is decided by the individual oral?
faqs.answer: Twenty-five per cent, at both Standard and Higher Level. It is marked by the class teacher against three criteria — language, message, and interactive skills — and then moderated by the IB. Because it is internally assessed, its date varies between Dubai schools by several months, so ask for your child's recording date in the first week of DP2. Interactive skills is where cohorts here typically lose marks: a long memorised presentation followed by short answers scores lower than a shorter presentation followed by a real exchange. Rehearsing that exchange with someone willing to ask an awkward second question is the work that moves the mark.

faqs.question: Simplified or traditional characters — which should my child write in the exam?
faqs.answer: Whichever set their school teaches, used consistently throughout the paper. Candidates write in either simplified or traditional characters, and mixing them within a response is a problem. Dubai schools serving mainland Chinese families generally teach simplified; schools with a Taiwanese or Hong Kong intake may teach traditional. This matters when choosing a tutor, because being drilled in the other set makes a student slower rather than faster. We confirm the character set in the first session and record it on the match, so a replacement tutor later in the course inherits the same convention.

faqs.question: How many Mandarin sessions a week does a Dubai Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session plus a daily ten-minute routine is the pattern that works for most students through DP1 and the first half of DP2. Mandarin rewards frequency over length, because character recall decays between contacts and a single long weekly block does not interrupt that decay. Two periods justify more: the four to six weeks before the individual oral, where a concentrated sprint block earns its cost, and the final term before the May session, where timed paper practice needs marking turnaround. A student who starts in March of DP2 can still improve Paper 2, which is the fastest-moving component.

faqs.question: Does an HSK level tell us where my child sits in Mandarin B?
faqs.answer: It gives a rough reference point and nothing more. HSK is a separate proficiency examination with its own level structure, and no official mapping to IB Mandarin B exists — anyone publishing a precise equivalence is inferring it. In practice an HSK result is useful as evidence of vocabulary breadth and reading comfort, which helps a tutor place a new student quickly. What it does not tell you is how a student performs against the Language B criteria, where register, message development and interactive skills carry marks that HSK does not test. The school's own phase or level assessment remains the better guide.

faqs.question: Can Mandarin sessions run after the Dubai school day and the evening traffic?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the timing is the main scheduling question rather than an afterthought. Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and the window every Dubai family wants is 5pm to 7.30pm, which is also when the school run and the first wave of homework land. Families in Dubai Marina, Mirdif and Festival City often do better with a 7.30pm start or a weekend morning, because the slot survives the term instead of being cancelled twice a month. Online delivery removes a tutor's travel from the equation, which is what makes a late slot practical at all.

faqs.question: Does a private Mandarin tutor in Dubai need a UAE work permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Official guidance states the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure as unverified. You can ask any tutor whether they hold the permit, and the application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: Will Mandarin B count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency rules are set by the Ministry of Education, not by a tutoring provider, and they are curriculum-specific. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No IB points threshold has been verified from the Ministry's own pages, so we do not publish one. Check your child's position with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority directly; it is a regulatory process, and no tutoring is required for it.

faqs.question: How do Dubai's shortened Ramadan school hours affect a weekly Mandarin session?
faqs.answer: Most families move the slot later, and it is worth arranging in advance. Dubai school hours shorten during Ramadan and evening routines shift around Iftar, which makes the usual 5pm to 7.30pm window unusable for several weeks. Because sessions are delivered online, moving a weekly slot to a later evening start or to a different day costs nothing in travel and can be arranged with the tutor directly. Character routines are the part to protect during that period: shortening the daily ten minutes to five is better than pausing it, because recall decay is what the routine exists to interrupt. Confirm the revised slot before the month begins rather than week by week.

dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the component that is costing the marks
dubai/ib-dp-mandarin-b-tutor.closingBody: If you can name the component — slow characters in Paper 1, listening speed in Paper 2, a flat individual oral, or a placement that does not look right — we can usually shortlist a Mandarin specialist within a day or two. Send the level, the character set, the school's oral date if you have it, and one recent piece of written work. The trial lesson is free, one per family, with no card details taken, and it ends with a plain view of what the gap is and how long it should take to close. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the Dubai school day.

intro.heading: What changes when an AA HL student in Dubai starts being shown the marks
paragraphs: A search for an IB DP Math AA HL home tutor in Dubai almost always starts with a number that arrived without explanation. A mock grade of 4 for a child who left IGCSE with a grade 8. A predicted 5 where the university offer needs a 6. A report comment that says "needs to show more working" and nothing else. The number is real, and the frustration is that nobody has shown the family what produced it. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is examined across three papers and one piece of coursework, and each of those four components fails in a different way. Until someone separates them, every hour of extra study is a guess.

That separation is the whole of our method on this page. In the first week a tutor works through a complete past Paper 1 under timed conditions, marks it against the published mark scheme, and produces a per-question breakdown: marks earned, marks available, and the reason for each gap. Reasons are not vague. A lost mark is either a topic that was never secure, a method mark forfeited because the working stopped early, an accuracy slip in the final line, or a command term misread. Those four causes need four different responses, and a tutor who cannot tell them apart will spend ten weeks reteaching content the student already knows.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and a document camera on the student's working. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Dubai address; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate trade, and the gain is specific. A family in Emirates Hills or Arabian Ranches is no longer choosing from the AA HL teachers who happen to live within a twenty-minute drive at six in the evening. The pool becomes everybody who teaches the course, and on a Higher Level maths page that difference is not cosmetic: Paper 3 is a specialism, and plenty of capable general maths tutors have never taught it.

The second thing that changes is what a parent receives. Most tutoring in this market is invisible from the outside. You pay, the session happens behind a closed door, and you learn how it went in June. Our tutors keep a running file for each student: the marked scripts with dates, the topic log showing which syllabus sub-topics have been tested and retested, the exploration drafts in sequence with feedback attached, and a single line each fortnight that says what the current working mark is and which component it came from. You can read it without being a mathematician, because it is written in marks rather than adjectives.

Dubai gives this work a particular shape. KHDA counted 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the IB accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment. That is a large absolute number of Diploma candidates spread thinly across many schools, which is why a child can be the only AA HL student in their year group who needs help with the Maclaurin series. Online delivery is what makes a genuine subject match possible for that child, and the evidence file is what makes the match accountable.

dubai/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: AA HL does not begin in Year 12. The habits that decide a Higher Level maths grade are formed in MYP mathematics and in the IGCSE or MYP year that precedes the Diploma. Here is how each programme feeds the course, and what a Dubai family should watch for at each stage.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL is one of six Diploma subjects, taken alongside Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The guide recommends 240 teaching hours, against 150 at Standard Level. The extra ninety hours are not spread evenly: calculus, geometry and trigonometry, and number and algebra absorb most of them, and that is where Higher Level students who were comfortable at IGCSE most often come unstuck.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma candidates sit the May session, in common with most Northern Hemisphere IB schools, though a small number of UAE schools enter candidates in November. Exact session windows and results dates change and are published by the IB rather than by us, so confirm them with your child's Diploma coordinator before you plan a revision calendar around them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students who score well on criterion A and poorly on criterion B arrive in AA HL able to execute a method but unable to start an unfamiliar problem. Paper 3 punishes that profile more than any other component in the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the full IB continuum, so a child may move from MYP straight into AA HL inside the same building with no external examination in between. The absence of an IGCSE-style terminal paper means the first timed, externally styled mark many of these students ever see is a DP1 mock, which is a hard place to discover a technique problem.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP teaches mathematics through inquiry rather than through a published syllabus of topics, so attainment is reported against transdisciplinary strands rather than against a grade. Number sense and fluency with fractions, indices and algebraic manipulation are what later turn into AA HL Paper 1 marks, because Paper 1 removes the calculator and leaves nothing to hide behind.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools are inspected annually by KHDA and the inspection report comments on attainment and progress in mathematics separately. A report showing good attainment but only acceptable progress is the most useful early signal a parent gets, and it is worth reading before a child picks a Higher Level maths route five years later.

dubai/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: A Higher Level maths student rarely needs help with maths alone. The subjects below are the ones Dubai Diploma families most often pair with AA HL, with what each actually assesses and where the marks tend to go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Three papers plus the exploration. Paper 1 is 110 marks in two hours with no calculator, so algebraic fluency is examined directly. Proof, complex numbers, Maclaurin series, vectors and the full calculus toolkit sit in the HL-only content. Marks are lost most often in the final accuracy line and in abandoned method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two papers of 80 marks each plus the exploration, with no Paper 3. SL shares the structure of HL but stops short of proof by induction, implicit differentiation and the harder integration techniques. A student sliding at HL is sometimes better served by a considered move to SL than by more hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The other Diploma maths route, with a calculator permitted in every paper and a far heavier statistics load. AI HL carries its own Paper 3, built from two extended data investigations. Students who switch routes mid-course need the modelling and statistics content rebuilt, not revised.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The most common pairing with AA HL. The 2023 syllabus assesses Paper 1A multiple choice, Paper 1B data analysis and Paper 2, with the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. Students who can do AA HL calculus often still lose physics marks on uncertainties and on graph gradients with units.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Equilibrium, energetics and organic mechanisms carry the HL weight. The overlap with AA HL is in logarithms for pH and in rate equations, so a student strong in maths should not be losing those marks. Where they do, the cause is usually chemical notation rather than algebra.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: HL economics adds a quantitative paper, and AA HL students usually find the calculation questions straightforward while losing marks on definition and diagram labelling. The internal assessment is three commentaries on published news articles, each with its own word limit.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 and Paper 2 plus a solution-development internal assessment. AA HL students take to the algorithmic thinking and the pseudocode, and tend to lose marks on the written paper's extended-response questions about system design and ethics rather than on the code.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects. Mathematics is one of TOK's areas of knowledge, so an AA HL student has usable material. The grade combines with the Extended Essay to contribute up to three points towards the Diploma total.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece. A mathematics Extended Essay needs a question that can be answered with mathematics the student actually commands, which for an AA HL candidate is a real advantage and also a trap: ambition outruns the available technique more often than the reverse.

dubai/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Dubai's Diploma families are not evenly spread, and neither are the schools that offer Higher Level maths. These are the communities our AA HL enquiries come from, with the detail that changes when a session can start.

regions.note: Feeds Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Emirates International School Meadows, both offering the full Diploma. Sessions here commonly start at 17:00 or later because of after-school commitments on the same campus.

regions.note: The densest cluster of IB continuum schools in the city. A 16:30 start is realistic for students who walk or take a short bus, and these families more often ask for twin sessions covering AA HL and Physics HL in one week.

regions.note: Villa communities served by Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches. The drive to Al Barsha or Emirates Hills in evening traffic is the single reason most Ranches families we speak to abandoned the idea of a tutor travelling to them.

regions.note: A newer community whose Diploma candidates are often split across several schools in different districts. Online delivery matters more here than almost anywhere, because the nearest AA HL teacher is rarely the right AA HL teacher.
