sections.heading: What a search for an AA HL home tutor in Dubai is actually asking for
paragraphs: An IB DP Math AA HL home tutor in Dubai costs roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour at the specialist end of this market, and the thing a parent is buying is not proximity. It is a person who has taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level often enough to recognise a Paper 3 problem on sight. IB Gram delivers that as one-to-one tuition over live video to any community in Dubai. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and we say so before anybody pays.

The phrase "home tutor" carries a specific expectation in this city, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is widely available, generally priced between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour depending on level and on how far the tutor travels, and it solves a genuine problem for younger children who need an adult physically present to keep them at the table. A seventeen-year-old working through implicit differentiation is not that child. What they need is a specialist, and the specialist in this market is a scarcer thing than a car.

There is a second cost to the in-home model that rarely appears in a quote. Travel compresses the available hours into a narrow evening window, which means a tutor can serve perhaps three or four students a night in one geographic cluster. That constraint is what produces the familiar outcome: a competent generalist who teaches everything from Year 7 maths to A Level, covering AA HL as the hardest thing on their list rather than their subject. The scarcity is not of tutors. It is of Higher Level specialists willing to lose ninety minutes a day to Sheikh Zayed Road.

Online changes the arithmetic. A tutor who teaches from 15:00 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time without moving can hold a timetable deep enough to specialise, which is why our AA HL tutors teach AA HL rather than maths in general. For the student the practical difference shows up in week one, when the marked Paper 1 comes back with the examiner's own wording in the margin instead of a tick and a score out of 110.

sections.heading: The AA HL assessment model, component by component
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is examined through three written papers and one internally assessed piece of coursework. Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 110 marks over two hours and each contributes 30 per cent of the final grade. Paper 3 is one hour, 55 marks, and 20 per cent. The mathematical exploration is marked out of 20 and contributes the remaining 20 per cent. That spread is the reason a single mock percentage tells a parent almost nothing: the same overall mark can come from four completely different profiles.

The calculator divide is the structural fact most families miss. Paper 1 is sat with no calculator of any kind, so every mark on it depends on algebraic fluency the student can produce by hand. Papers 2 and 3 assume a graphic display calculator and are written on that assumption, which means they reward a different set of skills: knowing which calculator routine answers the question, reading a graph screen correctly, and recording enough working that method marks survive even when the final value is wrong. A student who revises by doing calculator-permitted questions and then sits Paper 1 is practising the wrong paper.

Paper 3 deserves separate attention because it is unlike anything else in Diploma mathematics. It contains two extended problem-solving questions that develop an unfamiliar idea in stages, each part building on the last. There is no content on Paper 3 that is not elsewhere in the syllabus, and that is precisely why content revision does not raise a Paper 3 mark. What raises it is practice at being led through unfamiliar territory without panicking at part (c), and the discipline of answering part (a) fully enough that part (b) is reachable.

The exploration is the only component where the student controls the timetable, and the only one where a tutor's role is narrow and must be stated plainly. The work must be the student's own throughout. A tutor reads a submitted draft, comments against the published criteria, flags where the mathematics is not yet at Higher Level depth, and asks the questions a moderator would ask. The tutor adds nothing to the document.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Paper 1 script: the diagnosis that starts the work
paragraphs: The first session with a new AA HL student produces a document, not a feeling. The student sits a complete past Paper 1 under timed conditions, with no calculator, and the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme rather than impressionistically. The output is a per-question table: marks earned, marks available, and a single coded reason for each gap. Four codes cover almost everything. Content not secure. Method abandoned before the method mark was earned. Accuracy slip in the final line. Command term misread.

Those four causes have nothing in common as teaching problems. Content gaps need reteaching, which is slow and takes weeks. Abandoned method needs a habit change, which can be fixed inside three sessions because the mathematics is already there. Accuracy slips respond to a checking routine and to writing one more line than feels necessary. Misread command terms are a reading problem, and the fix is a short drill on what "hence", "show that", "find the exact value" and "justify" each require, because each of those carries a different obligation in the mark scheme.

A worked example from this market. A DP1 student arrives with 54 out of 110 on Paper 1 and a school prediction of 4. The breakdown shows 11 marks lost to incomplete working on questions where the final answer was right, 9 to sign errors in integration, 14 to genuinely unlearned HL content in complex numbers, and the remainder spread thinly. That is not a child who needs the course retaught. Twenty of those marks are available within a month, and the complex numbers block is a defined piece of work with an end date. The prediction is wrong in a way that is demonstrable, which is a different conversation to have with a school than a vague appeal.

The marked script also settles the HL-or-SL question honestly. A student losing marks to technique and habit at HL will usually stay at HL and gain. A student whose breakdown is almost entirely unlearned content eighteen months before the examinations is being asked to carry 240 hours of mathematics on a foundation that is not there, and the conversation about Standard Level should happen early, while the school can still act on it, rather than in the term before the papers.

sections.heading: The mathematical exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is worth 20 per cent of the AA HL grade and is marked out of 20 against five criteria. The IB recommends a length of twelve to twenty pages. Students lose marks here with remarkable consistency, and almost never for the reason they expect. The mathematics in a weak exploration is often perfectly correct; what is missing is the reflection, the personal engagement and the mathematical communication that three of the five criteria exist to reward.

Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six of the twenty marks and is where Higher Level candidates are judged against Higher Level expectations. An exploration that applies only material from the Standard Level syllabus cannot reach the top band however neatly it is presented. This is the single most useful thing a specialist can tell a student in week one of the exploration, because it is a decision about topic choice, and topic choice cannot be repaired in the final fortnight.

Criterion D, reflection, is worth three marks and is the cheapest to improve. Reflection means commenting on what the mathematics showed, what its limitations were, and what a different approach would have produced. Students treat it as a concluding paragraph; examiners expect it throughout. Criterion C, personal engagement, also carries three marks and is earned by independent thought rather than by writing that the topic is interesting. The two presentation and communication criteria, A and B, carry four marks each and reward a coherent structure, defined notation and consistent use of symbols.

What a tutor may and may not do here is not a matter of house style. Under IB academic-honesty rules the exploration must be entirely the student's own work. A tutor may discuss the choice of topic, comment on a submitted draft, point out where a claim is unsupported, and explain what a criterion rewards. A tutor may not supply text, rework the student's paragraphs, or hand over mathematics for insertion. Several providers in this market sell finished coursework. That is malpractice for the student and the consequence falls on the candidate, not on the seller.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks of evidence: what progress actually looks like
paragraphs: The brief for this page is evidence, so here is the shape of a first block in practice. Twelve weeks is long enough for content to be rebuilt and short enough that a family can judge whether the arrangement is working before committing to a year. Each fortnight produces one artefact a parent can read, and each artefact triggers a decision rather than a comment.

Weeks one and two establish the baseline: a full timed Paper 1, marked, with the per-question breakdown. Weeks three and four take the largest single cause of lost marks and address only that. If the diagnosis was abandoned method, the work is rewriting old answers to mark-scheme standard, which feels unglamorous and moves marks faster than anything else available. Weeks five and six introduce Paper 2 under timed conditions, because calculator technique is a separate skill and a student can be fluent on paper and clumsy on the screen.

Weeks seven and eight are the first Paper 3 attempt. Almost every student scores badly on their first Paper 3 and the mark is not the point; what the tutor is looking for is where the student stopped, and whether they stopped because they could not do the mathematics or because they did not believe they could. Weeks nine and ten return to the weakest topic for a retest, comparing like with like against the week-one script. Weeks eleven and twelve produce a second full Paper 1 under the same conditions as the first, and the comparison of those two scripts is the only honest measure of whether the block worked.

No tutor can promise a particular grade and no honest provider in this market will. What can be promised is that the evidence will be in front of you, dated, and that a block which is not working will be visible by week six rather than in the summer. If the second Paper 1 has not moved and the topic retests have not moved, the right response is to change something: the tutor, the format, or the level. That decision is easier to make with two marked scripts on the table than with a reassuring message.

sections.heading: What AA HL tuition costs in Dubai, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages we examined for this market publish no price at all, and two of those that do quote in US dollars, a currency Dubai families do not transact in. The table below sets out what the market charges in AED per hour by provider model, with the source of each figure. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. Our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, because the right number depends on the level, the number of components in play and how many weeks remain.

Four things move an AA HL quote upwards. Higher Level rather than Standard Level is the first, and it is justified: the tutor pool that can teach Paper 3 confidently is genuinely smaller. The second is proximity to the examination session, since specialist availability tightens through the spring. The third is in-home delivery, where the travel is embedded in the hourly rate whether or not anybody itemises it. The fourth is exploration supervision, which is marking-heavy work done between sessions rather than inside them.

Two things move it down without reducing quality. Ninety-minute sessions usually cost less per hour than sixty-minute ones, because the tutor's scheduling overhead is spread further, and ninety minutes is the right length for Paper 3 work in any case. Booking a defined block rather than paying week to week also tends to reduce the rate, though no family should commit to a long block before a trial lesson has happened and a first script has been marked.

Context helps. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Against a school fee that is holding flat, a tutoring decision is easier to size: one weekly session at mid-market specialist rates sits in the same monthly band Bestimate describes for exam-year support, roughly AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and upwards.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor in the room, for a Higher Level maths student
paragraphs: This comparison is the reason the page exists, so it is set out with the costs and the trade-offs visible rather than argued. In-home tuition buys presence. A tutor in the room can see a student's body language, intervene before frustration sets in, and remove the option of a quiet refusal to engage. For a nine-year-old that is worth a great deal. For a Diploma candidate working on Paper 3, the deciding variable is whether the adult in the room has taught Paper 3.

Online one-to-one buys match quality and recoverable time. A family in Arabian Ranches or Dubai Hills is no longer constrained to tutors who can reach them by 17:30; the shortlist becomes everyone who teaches AA HL at the hour required. The travel hour disappears from both sides of the arrangement, which in practice means a session can run at 20:00 on a school night without anybody driving home afterwards, and a Ramadan timetable can move to post-Iftar slots without renegotiating anything.

The honest limitations of online delivery are worth naming. A student who will not sit down without an adult physically present will not be rescued by better software. Handwritten mathematics needs either a document camera or a graphics tablet, and a laptop camera pointed at a desk is not enough for marking algebra line by line. Household internet in older Dubai buildings occasionally cannot sustain two video streams at once. Each of those is solvable, and each should be tested in the free trial rather than discovered in week three.

IB Gram's position is settled and consistent with every other country page on this site: tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not operate home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates, and in-home tutoring is something we offer only in India. If a family in the UAE decides a tutor in the room is the right answer, the sensible next step is to verify that the person holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is issued free of charge and can be asked for directly.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the timetable a Dubai tutor has to fit into
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a judgement on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, with attainment and progress reported separately by subject. For a maths parent the useful reading is not the headline band but the mathematics line, and particularly a report showing acceptable progress alongside good attainment, which describes a cohort coasting.

The emirate's school sector is unusually large and still growing. KHDA recorded 387,441 pupils in 227 private schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with UK programmes at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the IB at 7. Seven new private schools are opening for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places after a year in which enrolment rose six per cent. More Diploma places means more Higher Level maths candidates spread across more schools, each with a thinner subject cohort than the city's size suggests.

The timetable a tutor fits into is also shaped by KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Those lessons sit inside the same week as six Diploma subjects, so an AA HL student's free evenings are fewer than a parent assumes.

None of this makes KHDA a party to private tutoring. The authority licenses schools and, separately, issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises. IB Gram holds neither, and no honest page should imply otherwise. Marketing that pairs the regulator's initials with the word "approved" and attaches it to a tutor is common in this market and almost always meaningless; a parent should treat it as a reason to ask harder questions rather than as a credential.

process.title: Tell us the course, not just the subject
process.description: Analysis and Approaches HL, the school, the year group and the current mark if there is one. Naming the exact course matters: a request for a maths tutor and a request for an AA HL tutor reach different people. If there is a recent marked paper or a report comment, send it with the enquiry.

process.title: A free trial lesson with a named specialist
process.description: You see who will teach, and the tutor sees the student work. The trial is a working session rather than a sales call: the student attempts questions and the tutor forms a view on where the marks are going. If the match is wrong, say so and we introduce someone else before any payment is made.

process.title: A marked baseline paper in week one
process.description: A complete past Paper 1 under timed conditions, marked against the published mark scheme, returned with a per-question breakdown. This is the document everything afterwards is measured against, which is why it is sat properly rather than informally. It also tends to settle the question of whether a prediction is fair.

process.title: A dated plan, then fortnightly evidence
process.description: The plan names which component is being worked on, in what order, and what will be retested when. Every fortnight you receive the marked work and one line stating the current working mark and where it came from. The plan changes when the evidence says so, not on a schedule.

process.title: A review before the next block
process.description: At the end of a block the second baseline paper is compared with the first, under the same conditions. If the marks have moved, the next block is built on what worked. If they have not, we change the tutor, the format or the level, and we say which. No family should be asked to extend a block on the strength of encouragement alone.

whyPoints.title: One specialist, named before you pay
whyPoints.description: You know who is teaching your child before the first paid session, and that person stays for the block. A rota of interchangeable tutors cannot hold the thread of a diagnosis across twelve weeks, and the per-question breakdown from week one is worthless if the person who wrote it has moved on by week five.

whyPoints.title: Marking against the published mark scheme
whyPoints.description: Work comes back with the examiner's wording, not a tick and a score. A student who can see that two marks were available for a line they omitted will write that line next time. This is the slowest part of a tutor's week and the part most providers quietly skip, which is why it is written into the arrangement here.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own subject
whyPoints.description: Twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade sits in one hour and two questions, and it rewards a skill the other papers do not examine. Our AA HL tutors work on it as a distinct strand from the first term rather than as a revision afterthought, because confidence with unfamiliar stems is built slowly.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on exploration support
whyPoints.description: The exploration must be the student's own work and our tutors hold that line in writing. Feedback is keyed to criteria A to E, questions are asked, nothing is inserted. Providers in this market sell finished coursework; the consequence of that falls on the candidate, and no family should be exposed to it by a tutor.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly, before the money
whyPoints.description: Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram runs no home visits in the UAE and does not keep a Dubai office. Two providers in this market route Emirates enquiries to overseas phone numbers without saying so; stating the model up front is the cheapest form of trust available.

whyPoints.title: A visible fallback when nobody is free
whyPoints.description: AA HL Paper 3 specialists are not infinite, and the evening slots either side of 18:00 fill first. If nobody suitable is available at the hour you need, you are told that, with the alternatives: a different slot, a different week, or a tutor outside the UAE time zone whose availability is stated before you decide.

faqs.question: Does an AA HL home tutor in Dubai come to our villa, or is this online?
faqs.answer: This is online. IB Gram matches your child to an Analysis and Approaches HL specialist and the sessions run live over video, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase "home tutor" is what parents search for in this city, so the page uses it, but the delivery is stated before anybody pays. For a Higher Level maths candidate the trade is usually favourable: the shortlist stops being whoever can reach your community by 17:30 and becomes everybody who teaches the course.

faqs.question: What is in AA HL Paper 3 and why does it cost so many marks?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is one hour, 55 marks and twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade, and it contains only two questions. Each develops an unfamiliar idea in stages, with later parts depending on earlier ones. No content appears on Paper 3 that is not already in the syllabus, which is why revising topics does not raise the mark. What raises it is practice at being led somewhere unfamiliar without stalling, and answering part (a) completely enough that part (b) remains reachable. Most students score poorly on their first attempt, and the useful information is where they stopped rather than the total.

faqs.question: My son got a grade 8 in IGCSE maths and is on a 4 in AA HL. What happened?
faqs.answer: Usually three things at once. IGCSE rewarded answers; Paper 1 at Higher Level rewards working, and students who skipped lines profitably for two years lose method marks immediately. The calculator was permitted throughout IGCSE, while AA HL Paper 1 removes it entirely, so weak algebraic fluency that was hidden becomes visible. And the HL-only content, including proof, complex numbers and the harder calculus, is genuinely new. A marked Paper 1 separates these causes within a week, and the mix matters: abandoned method can be fixed in three sessions, unlearned content takes a term.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to pay for Analysis and Approaches HL tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates for specialist IB tuition in Dubai run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour, with Unitors advertising IB from AED 200, TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table reaching AED 450 and above for exam-year specialists. In-home visits are priced higher, generally AED 180 to AED 500, because travel is embedded in the rate. Those are market figures, not ours. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, since the number depends on level, how many components are in play and how many weeks remain before the session.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the mathematical exploration without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. The exploration must be entirely the student's own work. A tutor may discuss topic choice, read a submitted draft, comment against criteria A to E, point out where a claim is unsupported, and say plainly when the mathematics sits below Higher Level depth. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite paragraphs or hand over mathematics for insertion. Criterion E carries six of the twenty marks and is where HL expectations bite, so the most valuable advice usually arrives at the topic-choice stage rather than during the final fortnight.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark my daughter's algebra if the lesson is over video?
faqs.answer: Two ways, and both should be tested in the free trial rather than assumed. During the session the student writes on paper under a document camera or a phone on a stand, or writes directly on a graphics tablet shared to the screen, so the tutor watches the working appear line by line rather than seeing a finished answer. Between sessions the student photographs completed questions and sends them, and the tutor marks them against the mark scheme and returns annotated pages. A laptop camera pointed vaguely at a desk is not sufficient for marking algebra.

faqs.question: Should my child move from AA HL to AA SL, and when is it too late?
faqs.answer: The marked evidence usually answers this better than a conversation does. A student losing marks to technique, pacing and abandoned method at Higher Level will generally stay and gain. A student whose breakdown is mostly unlearned HL content, eighteen months out, is carrying 240 hours of mathematics on a foundation that is not there. Standard Level drops Paper 3 and the harder calculus and proof content while keeping the same exploration. Timing is set by your school and by IB registration rather than by us, so raise it with the Diploma coordinator early, while a change is still administratively possible.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 1 sat without a calculator, and how should revision change for it?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 is written to examine algebraic fluency directly, so no calculator of any kind is permitted. Papers 2 and 3 assume a graphic display calculator and are written on that assumption. The practical consequence is that a student who revises using calculator-permitted questions is rehearsing the wrong paper. Revision needs splitting: non-calculator work for exact values, surds, logarithms and integration by hand, and separate calculator sessions for the screen routines, graph reading and recording enough working that method marks survive a wrong final value.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and how do I check one has it?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any in-person tutor to show the permit directly.

faqs.question: What evidence will we actually see, and how often?
faqs.answer: Every fortnight, three things. The marked work from that period, annotated question by question in mark-scheme wording. The topic log, showing which syllabus sub-topics have been tested, retested and closed. And one line naming the current working mark and which component it came from, so you can tell a Paper 1 problem from an exploration problem. At the end of a twelve-week block a second full Paper 1 is sat under the same conditions as the first, and those two scripts side by side are the honest measure of whether the block worked.

faqs.question: We have ten weeks before the examinations. Is it worth starting AA HL tuition now?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but the plan has to change. Ten weeks is not enough to rebuild unlearned Higher Level content across five topics, and pretending otherwise wastes the time. It is enough to recover marks that are already nearly earned: completing working so method marks register, a checking routine for accuracy, command-term reading, and pacing so the last twenty minutes of Paper 1 stop collapsing. A marked baseline paper in week one shows how many of those marks exist. If the answer is twenty or more, the block is worth running. If it is five, we will say so.

faqs.question: Will five IGCSE passes plus AA HL satisfy UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: The British-track rule is published and specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the IB there is no points threshold we are willing to publish, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site, and one ranking competitor already states a wrong IGCSE subject count. Check the IB position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a Ministry process; no tutor performs it.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor take AA HL and Physics HL, or do we need two people?
faqs.answer: Both arrangements exist and the choice should follow the diagnosis. One tutor covering both subjects keeps the scheduling simple and lets the calculus in AA HL be used deliberately in physics, which helps students who treat the two as unrelated. The argument for two specialists is sharper at Higher Level: physics under the 2023 syllabus examines data analysis, uncertainties and a scientific investigation marked against four criteria, and that is a different expertise from Paper 3 problem-solving in mathematics. We will say honestly which of the two a particular tutor can carry.

faqs.question: What happens if no AA HL specialist is free in our evening slot?
faqs.answer: You are told, before you pay. Higher Level maths specialists who are confident with Paper 3 are a smaller group than general maths tutors, and the slots either side of 18:00 Gulf Standard Time fill first. The options are then stated plainly: a different hour in the same week, a wait for a named tutor to free up, or a specialist in another time zone whose availability is given to you before you decide. No competitor page in the research we did discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why this one does.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or while the family is travelling?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the practical advantages of online delivery. Ramadan timetables in Dubai shorten the school day and shift family routines, so sessions commonly move to post-Iftar slots for that period and then return. Travel is handled the same way: the lesson follows the student rather than the address, so a fortnight in another time zone becomes a scheduling conversation rather than a gap. Study leave and examination weeks are usually the right time to pause, and that pause should be agreed in advance rather than cancelled session by session.

intro.heading: Judge AA HL progress on marked papers, not on how sessions felt
paragraphs: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at higher level is a 240-hour course assessed through three written papers and an exploration. Paper 1 runs two hours with no technology for 110 marks. Paper 2 runs two hours with a graphic display calculator for another 110. Paper 3 runs one hour for 55 marks across two extended problem-solving questions. The exploration carries the remaining share. That structure is the whole reason AA HL behaves differently from any other course a Dubai DP student takes: there are four separate skills, and a student can be strong at two of them and still land well below where their classwork suggests.

Which is why the first question to ask an IB DP Math AA HL online tutor in Dubai is what they will show you. Not what the plan is, what the artefacts are. After four to six weeks you should be holding marked questions with the method and answer marks separated, a topic-level error log built from those papers, a record of the time each question took against the marks available, and - if the exploration has started - a draft with comments against the published criteria. All of that is inspectable by a parent who has not done calculus in twenty years.

The reason the evidence matters more here than elsewhere is that AA HL failure is specific rather than general. A student who loses marks in Paper 1 almost always loses them in a small number of recurring ways: an integral attempted without rearranging first, a proof by induction where the inductive step assumes what it should derive, a trigonometric identity applied in the wrong direction, a complex number left in the wrong form for the question asked. None of those is a shortage of ability and none is fixed by doing more past papers. They are fixed by naming the error, drilling the specific move, and checking a fortnight later whether it recurred.

The same applies to time. Paper 1 gives two hours for 110 marks, which is roughly a mark a minute with nothing spare, and a sizeable share of Dubai students we see are not short of mathematics but short of pace, having spent twenty minutes on a six-mark part because they would not abandon an approach that was not working. That shows up immediately in a timed, marked paper and never shows up in homework. It is also one of the fastest things to improve, which is why we measure it from the first week.

This page sets out the course as it is actually assessed rather than as it is advertised: the three papers with their marks and weights, the five topics plus the additional HL content and the errors each one generates, why Paper 1 without a calculator is a separate exam, why Paper 3 is where HL grades are decided, how the AA and AI routes genuinely differ, what the exploration needs from an HL student, and how a marked paper becomes a weekly plan. It also carries the market rates for this work in AED with every figure attributed, because almost nobody in this search publishes a price at all.

Delivery is straightforward on this page: lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own script on screen. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India. For AA HL the online format is the better one anyway, because a student is matched with someone who teaches the course at higher level rather than with whoever lives nearby, and because working through a mark scheme is a screen task.

dubai/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-online-tutor.programmesIntro: AA HL is the end of a long mathematical build, and students arrive at it from several different starting points. Below is what each route gives them and what it leaves them to catch up.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Analysis and Approaches at higher level runs across both DP years for 240 teaching hours, covering number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, each with additional higher level content. Assessment is three written papers plus an internally assessed exploration. Students take it alongside five other subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, which is why pacing rather than ability decides most outcomes.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP timetables also carry the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons KHDA requires of every private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. For a 240-hour course that competes with five others, the practical effect is that AHL content is often taught quickly late in DP1, which is exactly where the Paper 3 material sits.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics at extended level is the natural feed into AA HL, and its criterion on investigating patterns is the single best preparation for Paper 3 available anywhere in the IB. What MYP does not build is examination pace under non-calculator conditions, because its assessment is criterion-based rather than timed and technique-heavy.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP to Year 11 then move straight into DP1. Those students usually handle the exploration and Paper 3 style comfortably and struggle initially with Paper 1 speed. IGCSE-trained students arrive with the opposite profile: fast, accurate, and unused to an open investigation with no stated method.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE routes
programmes.description: Extended IGCSE mathematics, and particularly Additional Mathematics where a school offers it, is the strongest pre-DP preparation for AA HL. The gap it leaves is calculus beyond introductory differentiation, formal proof, and complex numbers, all of which arrive early in DP1 and all of which generate the first wave of HL difficulty.
programmes.countryNote: UK-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment, and most run IGCSE at sixteen before splitting into A Level or the IB Diploma. Students coming from Extended IGCSE without Additional Mathematics typically need focused work on algebraic fluency in the first term of DP1, because AA HL assumes manipulation speed that IGCSE does not require.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Listed for continuity. PYP builds number sense and inquiry habits rather than technique, and the connection to AA HL is indirect: students who learned to explain their reasoning in primary school find the exploration and the Paper 3 structure more natural than students who learned to produce answers.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a large PYP population with considerable movement at Year 7, so many AA HL students here began in a different system entirely. It makes no difference to the examination; it does mean the mathematical vocabulary they were taught first may not match the course's.

dubai/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: AA HL is five syllabus topics plus additional higher level content, and the errors it generates are topic-specific. Below is the map with what actually costs marks in each, which is also how the weekly error log is organised.

subjects.name: Number and algebra: proof
subjects.description: Proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample. The recurring failure in the inductive step is assuming the result for n plus one rather than deriving it from the assumption for n. Examiners award method marks for the structure, so a student who writes the framework correctly scores even when the algebra stalls.

subjects.name: Number and algebra: complex numbers
subjects.description: Cartesian, modulus-argument and Euler forms, De Moivre's theorem, roots of unity and polynomial roots. Marks go missing by staying in the wrong form: a question asking for powers or roots wants polar or exponential form, and students who force Cartesian algebra run out of time rather than ability.

subjects.name: Number and algebra: sequences, series and binomial
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric work, sigma notation, the binomial theorem extended at HL to negative and fractional indices, and partial fractions. Convergence conditions are the quiet mark-loser, because students apply an infinite sum formula without checking the common ratio.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions, the factor and remainder theorems, rational functions, odd and even functions, and inequalities. Domain and range cost more marks than any other single idea here, particularly on inverse functions and on the modulus graphs in the HL content.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry: identities and equations
subjects.description: Compound and double angle work, reciprocal and inverse trigonometric functions, and equations over a stated interval. The two standard losses are missing solutions inside the interval and applying an identity in the less useful direction, which turns a four-line question into a page.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry: vectors
subjects.description: Vector equations of lines and planes, scalar and vector products, intersections and angles. Marks come from setting the problem up correctly rather than from the arithmetic, and students who sketch before calculating consistently outperform those who do not.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Discrete and continuous random variables, the normal distribution, and at HL conditional probability with Bayes' theorem, probability density functions, expectation and variance of transformed variables, and the central limit theorem. Interpretation in context is where the final mark of a part usually sits.

subjects.name: Calculus: differentiation
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules, implicit differentiation, related rates and optimisation. The HL step that catches students is recognising when implicit differentiation is required rather than rearranging first, and related-rates questions where the variable being differentiated is not the obvious one.

subjects.name: Calculus: integration
subjects.description: Substitution, integration by parts, partial fractions, improper integrals and volumes of revolution. More Paper 1 marks are lost here than anywhere else, almost always by starting to integrate before choosing a method. Thirty seconds spent identifying the technique saves ten minutes.

subjects.name: Calculus: series and differential equations
subjects.description: Maclaurin series, limits and L'Hopital's rule, separation of variables, homogeneous equations, the integrating factor and Euler's method. This block is taught late, appears heavily in Paper 3, and is the most common reason a strong DP1 student stalls in DP2.

subjects.name: Paper 3 problem solving
subjects.description: Two compulsory extended questions over one hour, each building from accessible early parts to an unfamiliar conclusion. It is a technique in itself: read the whole question first, use the structure the examiner has provided, and never abandon a later part because an earlier one failed.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An independent piece marked on five published criteria. For an HL student the binding issue is mathematics commensurate with the course: an exploration that stays inside SL content cannot reach the top band of that criterion, however well presented it is.

sections.heading: The evidence an AA HL tutor should produce in the first month
paragraphs: Within four to six weeks of starting, a Dubai family paying for higher level mathematics support should be able to look at four things and form their own view without understanding the mathematics. None of them is hard to produce, and a tutor who cannot produce them is asking to be judged on atmosphere.

The first is marked work with the marks separated. A mark scheme awards method marks and answer marks differently, and the distinction is the single most useful diagnostic in the course. A student scoring the method and dropping the answer has an accuracy problem that drills fix quickly. A student scoring neither has a technique gap in a named topic. A student scoring the answer with no working is losing marks they have already earned, which is a presentation habit and the fastest repair available.

The second is a topic-level error log. Not a list of chapters covered, a list of errors with their topic and their recurrence: integration method chosen before rearranging, four occurrences; inductive step assumed rather than derived, three; interval solutions missed in trigonometric equations, five. Within a month that log is specific enough to drive a weekly plan, and within a term it should be visibly shrinking in the categories that were worked on.

The third is time against marks. Every timed question set should record the minutes spent against the marks available, because Paper 1 and Paper 2 allow roughly a mark a minute and Paper 3 is tighter in a different way. A student who understands everything and finishes nothing has a pacing problem, and it is invisible in homework and obvious in a log.

The fourth, once it exists, is the exploration draft with comments against the published criteria. For an HL student the question that matters most is whether the mathematics is commensurate with the course, because an exploration built on SL content has a ceiling no amount of presentation will raise. A draft with comments and a version history also establishes beyond argument that the work is the student's own, which matters in a component that is internally assessed.

sections.heading: How AA HL is actually assessed
paragraphs: Four components, four different demands. Paper 1 is two hours with no technology for 110 marks, divided into a section of shorter questions and a section of extended ones. Paper 2 is two hours with a graphic display calculator for another 110 marks in the same shape. Paper 3 is one hour for 55 marks across two compulsory extended problem-solving questions and exists only at higher level. The exploration is internally assessed against five published criteria.

The weightings mean the written papers carry the overwhelming majority of the grade, and that Paper 3, despite being the shortest by far, carries a substantial share for the hour it occupies. Per minute of examination time, Paper 3 is the most valuable paper in the course. It is also the one that receives the least practice in most schools, because the AHL content it leans on is taught late and the mock calendar in Dubai often arrives before it has been covered properly.

A formula booklet is supplied in all papers, which changes what is worth memorising. Students who spend revision time learning what is printed for them are spending it badly; the value is in knowing which formula applies and being fast at the manipulation the booklet does not do for you. The graphic display calculator is required for Papers 2 and 3, and calculator fluency is a genuine assessable skill - the student who can find an intersection, a definite integral or a distribution value in fifteen seconds has several extra minutes across a paper.

Marks are awarded by scheme, and the scheme is generous to visible method. This is the most actionable fact in the whole course. An unfinished question with clear working scores; a wrong answer with no working scores nothing. Students who erase their failed attempts are deleting marks. We teach the opposite habit from the first session, and it shows up in the next school assessment.

One caution on boundaries. Grade boundaries move session by session and are published by the IB after each series, so no page should be quoting a mark total for a particular grade. If a provider tells you how many marks a seven requires, treat that as a sales claim rather than information, and ask your child's teacher what the school has seen across recent cohorts instead.

sections.heading: Paper 1 without a calculator is a separate examination
paragraphs: Dubai students who are comfortable in class and uncomfortable in Paper 1 are not usually short of understanding. They are short of the specific fluency that a non-calculator paper demands, and it is a trainable skill rather than a talent. Two hours and 110 marks means roughly a mark a minute, and every second spent reconstructing an exact value or grinding through algebra that should be automatic is a second removed from the questions that need thought.

The first fluency is exact values and surds. Trigonometric exact values, rationalising, simplifying nested radicals, and handling logarithms and exponentials by their laws rather than by estimation. These appear constantly in Section A and should take no deliberate thought at all. Students who hesitate here lose five to ten marks on a paper simply by running out of time at the end.

The second is method selection before execution. Integration is the clearest case: substitution, by parts, partial fractions and recognising a standard form are different routes, and starting down the wrong one costs several minutes. The discipline we teach is thirty seconds of deliberate choice before the pen moves, and the effect on Paper 1 scores is larger than any content teaching we could do in the same time.

The third is algebraic resilience on long questions. Section B asks for sustained work where part three depends on part one, and a sign error early is expensive. Writing in a way that allows checking - one manipulation per line, stated intermediate results - is not neatness for its own sake; it is how a student finds their own error in forty seconds instead of restarting.

The fourth is the decision to abandon. A student who refuses to leave a question is making a scoring error, not showing determination. The honest rule is that if a part has resisted two genuine approaches and more than its share of minutes, it gets marked and left, with whatever working exists on the page for method marks, and revisited if time allows. Teaching that single habit routinely moves a Paper 1 score more than teaching a new topic does.
bullets: Exact values, surds and log laws automatic rather than reconstructed
Thirty seconds of method selection before any integration
One manipulation per line, so errors are findable without restarting
A rule for abandoning a part, agreed in advance and practised
Every failed attempt left on the page for method marks

sections.heading: Paper 3 is where higher level grades are decided
paragraphs: Paper 3 exists only at higher level. One hour, 55 marks, two compulsory questions, each starting from something accessible and ending somewhere the student has not been before. It rewards a different thing from the other papers: not recall of technique but willingness to follow a structure into unfamiliar mathematics. Students who have never practised it under time conditions usually underperform their ability on it, and in Dubai that is common because the AHL content it leans on is taught late.

The structure is the help, and most students do not use it. A Paper 3 question is built in parts deliberately, so that part (a) produces a result part (c) needs, and a definition in part (b) is the tool for part (d). Reading the entire question before starting takes ninety seconds and changes what the early parts are for. Students who work part by part without looking ahead repeatedly do unnecessary work and then run out of time at exactly the point the marks get heavy.

The second habit is continuing past a failure. In a paper where parts depend on each other, a student who cannot complete part (b) often stops, when the correct move is to state the result part (b) should have produced, say so explicitly, and use it in part (c). Examiners can award the subsequent work. Abandoning the rest of a question because of one part is the most expensive single mistake available on this paper.

The third is writing enough. Paper 3's extended parts carry substantial method marks, and a student who has set up a differential equation correctly, separated the variables and then stalled on the integration has earned real marks if the work is visible. The same student who scribbles and erases has earned nothing. We drill this with marked past questions until the habit is automatic.

The content Paper 3 draws on most heavily is the AHL material taught last: proof by induction, complex numbers in polar and Euler form, vectors and planes, Maclaurin series, differential equations by separation, integrating factor and Euler's method. That is the DP2 block in most Dubai schools, which is why a Paper 3 intensive usually belongs in the second half of DP2 rather than earlier - after the content exists, with enough weeks left to practise it.

sections.heading: AA against AI at higher level: the honest comparison
paragraphs: The Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation routes are genuinely different courses rather than a harder and an easier version of one. AA is algebra, proof and calculus with a strong emphasis on exact and analytic methods. AI is modelling, data, and the use of technology to handle situations that have no neat closed form. Both exist at higher level and both are demanding; they are demanding in different directions.

The decision that matters is the degree route, and it has to be read from the programmes themselves rather than from general advice. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics programmes specify a calculus-heavy mathematics course or a particular HL subject at a particular grade, and the exact wording differs between universities and between countries. Read the published entry requirements for the specific programmes a student is considering, and ask the school's university counsellor to confirm the reading in writing. Nothing on this page should be treated as a university's requirement.

The second consideration is fit, and a marked paper answers it better than a conversation. A student who enjoys a proof, tolerates long algebra and likes an exact answer belongs in AA. A student who thinks well about a real situation, handles data confidently and finds extended symbolic manipulation a grind may do significantly better in AI HL, which is not a step down and will not be read as one by an admissions reader who understands the IB.

The third is timing. Changing route is an administrative decision with deadlines held by the DP coordinator, and it gets harder as DP1 progresses. The right moment to test the question is the first term of DP1, with a timed HL paper marked against the scheme and the student's intended degree requirements on the table. A decision made then is a decision; one made in DP2 is usually damage control.

sections.heading: Turning a marked paper into next week's plan
paragraphs: A marked paper is only useful if something changes because of it, and most students treat marking as a verdict rather than as data. The routine we use is mechanical, which is the point: every marked script is converted into categorised errors, every category gets a drill, and every drill gets checked a fortnight later. Progress is then visible as a falling recurrence count in named categories rather than as a feeling.

The categories are deliberately narrow. Not weak at calculus, but chose an integration method before rearranging. Not careless, but dropped the constant of integration in definite work. Not weak at trigonometry, but lost solutions inside the stated interval. Narrow categories produce specific drills; broad categories produce more past papers, which is what students do by default and why six weeks can pass with no measurable change.

The drill then has to be short and repeated. Ten integrals where the only task is to name the method and not to evaluate. Fifteen trigonometric equations where the only task is to list every solution in the interval. Five inductive steps written out as structure with the algebra provided. Each takes a few minutes, each targets one error, and each gets repeated until the recurrence count falls. This is unglamorous and it is the part that moves marks.

The fortnightly check is what makes the log honest. A category that was drilled and still recurs means the drill was wrong or the understanding beneath it is missing, and that is a content conversation rather than a practice one. A category that stops recurring comes off the active list. Over a term the log should be visibly different, and a parent can see that without reading a single line of mathematics.

Timing data sits beside the error log and is treated the same way. Minutes against marks, question by question, with a target of roughly a mark a minute for Papers 1 and 2. A student consistently over on Section A and short of time in Section B has a fluency problem, not a comprehension problem, and the drill block is the answer. That diagnosis takes one timed paper and is almost never made in school, because school marking does not record time.

sections.heading: The exploration, for an HL student specifically
paragraphs: The exploration is marked on five published criteria worth twenty marks between them, and for an AA HL student one of those criteria does most of the damage. Use of mathematics asks for work commensurate with the course, correct and thorough. An HL student whose exploration stays inside standard level content has placed a ceiling on it that no amount of presentation or structure will lift.

What commensurate means in practice is mathematics from the higher level part of the syllabus, used correctly, with the student understanding what they are doing. Reaching for something exotic from outside the course and applying it incorrectly scores worse than a correct, thorough piece of genuine HL work. We steer students towards the AHL content they have actually met - differential equations, series, complex numbers, vectors - applied to a question they chose themselves.

Topic choice is where HL students most often go wrong, and it goes wrong in two directions. Some pick something they care about that has no mathematics above SL level in it; some pick something mathematically impressive that they cannot explain. The test we apply is whether the student can describe, in their own words, what the mathematics is doing and why it suits the question. If they cannot, the topic is wrong regardless of how it looks.

The other criteria are gettable and frequently abandoned. Personal engagement asks for evidence of the student's own choices, which means a decision recorded somewhere - their own data, their own question, an approach they tried and dropped. Reflection asks for evaluation as the work develops rather than a concluding paragraph. Presentation and mathematical communication reward defined variables, consistent notation and labelled graphs, which are rules rather than skills.

Our boundary here is the same as everywhere in the DP. We teach the mathematics, explain what each criterion requires, read a draft and say which criterion is underserved, and ask the questions that make the student's own thinking visible. We do not supply a topic, write any section, or produce a model to be adapted. The exploration is internally assessed by a teacher who knows what the student's own work looks like, and a version history is the simplest protection there is.

sections.heading: What AA HL tuition costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all and the others quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. Below are the AED bands actually visible in this market as of October 2026, with the provider that published each figure named, organised by the stage of the course. These are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list; our own rate follows the free trial, once the match is known.

Higher level mathematics sits at the specialist end of the market and should. A tutor at the budget rate is rarely teaching AA HL, because the pool of people who can teach Maclaurin series and Paper 3 technique is small and those people have other options. A family quoted a general maths rate for AA HL is usually being quoted for general maths, and the first three sessions tend to demonstrate it.

For market context: EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase publishes AED 270; Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table shows in-home visits at AED 180-350 and specialist support at AED 200-450 or more; BartyED publishes AED 650. Monthly packages visible in this market run about AED 799 for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Three questions to ask before comparing two quotes. Whether VAT is included, because providers here are inconsistent about it. Whether the tutor teaches Analysis and Approaches at higher level specifically, and how that was verified - teaching A Level Further Mathematics is not the same thing and neither is teaching AA SL. And what any examiner claim rests on, because examiner status confers no access to marking decisions or grade boundaries, and a rate justified on it is a claim about a specific person you are entitled to test.

For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Against a flat fee bill, a weekly specialist hour across the two DP years is a visible commitment, which is an argument for measuring it: an error log that is not shrinking after a term is a reason to change something rather than to continue paying.

sections.heading: Scheduling AA HL against the Dubai school year
paragraphs: A weekly hour only works if it survives the year, and in Dubai the year has known hazards. School mock examinations, internal assessment deadlines in five other subjects, the Extended Essay submission, a long summer when many families are abroad, and in some years Ramadan. Planning around those at the start is the difference between thirty useful sessions and twenty useful sessions with ten wasted ones.

The sequencing that works for this course has a clear shape. DP1 first term goes on algebraic fluency, because AA HL assumes manipulation speed that neither IGCSE nor MYP requires. DP1 second and third terms consolidate the content as the school teaches it, always a fortnight behind rather than ahead. The DP1 summer is for the exploration, which needs thinking time rather than teaching time and is the one piece of work that can genuinely progress while a family is away. DP2 is content completion, then Paper 3, then timed papers, then non-calculator drilling into the final weeks.

Two Dubai-specific adjustments matter. Sessions pause during school mock weeks rather than competing with them: a student revising for mocks does not need new content, and the marked mock scripts are the most valuable diagnostic of the entire year. And during Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar slots, with heavy timed work scheduled either side of the month rather than through it, because a two-hour timed paper at 4pm in Ramadan tells nobody anything useful.

On the calendar itself, this page publishes no IB examination or results dates. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date here would be second-hand, and a wrong date on a page like this costs a family real planning time. Your child's DP coordinator holds the session calendar and the internal deadlines, and one email produces a list worth more than any generic timeline. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own International GCSE and A Level timetables, which matters for siblings on the British route but not for AA HL.

Two context points about the Dubai school market worth knowing while planning. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 with seventeen different curricula, the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26, US 14 and the International Baccalaureate 7. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. Growing IB provision means more AA HL sets and, in the short term, more small sets with a shared teacher - which is precisely the situation where an external specialist hour earns its cost.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a description
process.description: The most useful thing you can send is your child's most recent marked school assessment, however it went. Add the DP year, the school, which AHL topics have been taught, and whether the exploration has started. One marked script is worth more than a paragraph of history.

process.title: Free trial with the script on screen
process.description: Sixty minutes on the actual paper. The tutor works through where method marks were earned and lost, identifies the two or three error categories driving the score, and sets one drill. You keep the written summary. No card is taken to arrange it.

process.title: Agree the plan against the school's sequence
process.description: We ask for the school's scheme of work and mock dates, then plan to sit a fortnight behind the teaching rather than ahead of it. The plan names which weeks are mock weeks, which are travel weeks and where the Paper 3 block will sit.

process.title: Weekly session, timed set, error log
process.description: Each session opens with the error log and closes with a timed question set to be completed before the next one. Marking separates method from answer marks, minutes are recorded against marks, and the log is updated in front of the student.

process.title: Fortnightly check on the drilled categories
process.description: Categories that were drilled get retested two weeks later. Recurrence that has not fallen means the drill or the underlying understanding was wrong, and we change it. Categories that stop recurring leave the active list. That is what the parent report shows.

process.title: Review at week six against the first script
process.description: A short written comparison of the current timed paper against the first one: marks, pace, and which error categories have gone. If nothing has moved, we say so and change the tutor or the approach rather than asking for more time.

whyPoints.title: Everything is on paper
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts with method and answer marks separated, an error log by topic with recurrence counts, minutes against marks, and exploration drafts with criterion comments. A parent can read all of it without doing any mathematics, and compare it month to month.

whyPoints.title: Taught by someone who teaches this course
whyPoints.description: AA HL is not general maths with harder questions. Maclaurin series, the integrating factor, Bayes' theorem and Paper 3 technique are specific, and online matching means the tutor is chosen for the course rather than for the distance to your community.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: One hour, 55 marks, two extended questions, and almost no explicit teaching of how to attack it in most schools. We drill reading to the end first, using earlier parts as tools, and continuing past a failed part - the three habits that decide the paper.

whyPoints.title: Non-calculator fluency measured, not assumed
whyPoints.description: A two-hour paper with no technology at roughly a mark a minute exposes algebraic speed. We measure minutes against marks from the first timed set, because the gap between understanding and finishing is where most Dubai AA HL marks are lost.

whyPoints.title: Honest about course fit
whyPoints.description: Sometimes the right answer in DP1 is to move to AA SL or AI HL, and we will say so with a marked paper to support it. That conversation belongs with your DP coordinator while a change is still possible, not in DP2 when it is not.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can check and a plan you can audit
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the provider that published it with October 2026 as the as-of date. Our rate follows the free trial. The error log is the audit: if it is not shrinking after a term, that is a reason to change something.

faqs.question: How is Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL assessed?
faqs.answer: Four components. Paper 1 is two hours with no technology for 110 marks, split between shorter and extended questions. Paper 2 is two hours with a graphic display calculator for another 110 marks in the same shape. Paper 3 is one hour for 55 marks across two compulsory extended problem-solving questions and exists only at higher level. The mathematical exploration is internally assessed against five published criteria. A formula booklet is supplied in the examinations. Confirm the current weightings in the mathematics guide your school holds, because the IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle.

faqs.question: Why is my son fine in Paper 2 and losing marks in Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Almost always fluency and pace rather than understanding. Paper 1 allows two hours for 110 marks, roughly a mark a minute, with no calculator to fall back on. Students who reconstruct exact trigonometric values, hesitate over surds or start integrating before choosing a method spend minutes they then do not have for Section B. The diagnosis takes one timed paper with minutes recorded against marks. The fix is drill-shaped and fast: short repeated sets where the only task is to name an integration method, or to list every solution in an interval, until those decisions stop costing time.

faqs.question: What exactly does Paper 3 ask for and how should my daughter prepare?
faqs.answer: Two compulsory extended questions in one hour, each starting accessibly and ending in unfamiliar territory, together worth 55 marks. It rewards following a structure rather than recalling a technique. Three habits decide it: read the whole question before starting, because early parts produce tools later parts need; keep going after a part that fails, stating the result it should have produced and using it; and write enough working that method marks are available even when the answer does not arrive. Practise whole past questions under the real hour, marked against the scheme, rather than isolated parts.

faqs.question: Which AA HL topics cause the most trouble for Dubai students?
faqs.answer: The additional higher level content taught late in the course: proof by induction, complex numbers in polar and Euler form, vectors and planes, Maclaurin series, and differential equations by separation, integrating factor and Euler's method. Two things combine to make this block difficult. It is mathematically harder than what came before, and in a crowded Dubai DP timetable it is often taught quickly in DP2 alongside internal assessment deadlines in five other subjects. It is also precisely the material Paper 3 leans on, which is why a Paper 3 block usually belongs in the second half of DP2.

faqs.question: Should my child take AA HL or AI HL?
faqs.answer: Decide on the degree route and on fit, and test both with a marked paper rather than a conversation. AA is algebra, proof and analytic calculus; AI is modelling, data and technology-led problem solving. Neither is a soft option. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics programmes specify a calculus-heavy course, but the exact wording differs by university and country, so read the published entry requirements for the specific programmes and have the school's counsellor confirm it in writing. On fit: a student who enjoys proof and exact answers belongs in AA; one who thinks well with data may score considerably higher in AI HL.

faqs.question: Is it too late to switch from AA HL to AA SL in DP1?
faqs.answer: Usually possible early in DP1 and progressively harder after that, and it is an administrative decision with deadlines your DP coordinator holds rather than something a tutor can advise on alone. What we can contribute is evidence: a timed higher level paper marked against the scheme, a clear view of which errors are fluency and which are conceptual, and an honest account of the DP2 content load still ahead. Some students who look borderline in the first term are simply short of algebraic speed and improve rapidly. Others are genuinely better suited to standard level, and a term of marked papers shows which.

faqs.question: How many AA HL sessions a week does a Dubai DP student usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly hour is the common pattern and it is enough for most students, provided the work between sessions actually happens. The structure that makes a single hour effective is the timed set: the session ends with questions to complete before the next one, and the next one starts with the marked results. Two sessions a week makes sense in two situations - a student catching up a whole AHL topic the school has already moved past, and the final weeks before examinations when timed papers need marking and discussing quickly. More than two is usually a sign the plan is wrong.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the mathematical exploration without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is specific. A tutor may teach the mathematics, explain each of the five criteria and what they reward, read a draft and say which criterion is underserved, and ask the questions that make the student's own reasoning visible. A tutor may not supply the topic, write any section, restructure the student's text for them, or hand over a model to be adapted. The internally assessed nature of the component makes this important: a teacher who marks the class knows what each student's own work looks like, and a shared document with version history removes any ambiguity.

faqs.question: Why is my daughter's exploration scoring low when it looks excellent?
faqs.answer: The most likely reason for a higher level student is the use of mathematics criterion, which asks for work commensurate with the course, correct and thorough. An exploration built on standard level content has a ceiling regardless of how well it is presented or structured. The second likely reason is personal engagement, which requires evidence of the student's own choices - their own data, their own question, something they tried and dropped - and a topic taken from a list of ideas shows none. Both are diagnosable from one reading against the criteria, and both are fixable while the draft is still open.

faqs.question: How important is the graphic display calculator for Papers 2 and 3?
faqs.answer: It is required, and fluency with it is a genuine assessable advantage. A student who can find an intersection, evaluate a definite integral, solve an equation numerically or read a distribution value in seconds has several extra minutes across a two-hour paper, and those minutes land on the extended questions where the marks are heavy. Conversely a student who navigates menus slowly loses time they cannot recover. Calculator work is worth deliberate practice in its own right, including knowing which tasks are faster by hand - which is a judgement, and one worth drilling.

faqs.question: How many marks does a 7 in AA HL need?
faqs.answer: Nobody can tell you, because grade boundaries are set by the IB after each examination series and move between sessions according to how the papers performed. Any provider quoting you a fixed mark total for a grade is making a sales claim rather than giving you information. What is useful instead is a mark out of 110 on a timed past paper, marked against that paper's own scheme, tracked across several attempts. Your child's teacher will also have a sense of what recent cohorts in that school have needed, which is better guidance than any general figure.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around school mocks and Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and both should be planned for rather than worked through. We pause sessions during mock weeks, because a student revising does not need new content and the marked mock scripts are the single most valuable diagnostic of the year. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar slots and heavy timed work is scheduled either side of the month, since a two-hour timed paper in the late afternoon during Ramadan tells nobody anything useful. Because lessons are online on Gulf Standard Time, moving a standing slot for a month is an administrative change rather than a problem.

faqs.question: What should AA HL tuition cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Higher level mathematics sits at the specialist end of this market. Published figures as of October 2026: budget providers advertise from AED 33-65; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase publishes AED 270; Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table shows specialist support at AED 200-450 or more and in-home visits at AED 180-350; BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are market rates and not our prices; ours follows the free trial. Ask whether VAT is included, and ask specifically whether the tutor teaches Analysis and Approaches at higher level, because AA SL and A Level Further Mathematics are different jobs.

faqs.question: My child has six weeks until exams and is well short in AA HL. What actually helps?
faqs.answer: Triage, not teaching. Six weeks is enough to change a grade and not enough to cover missing content broadly, so the work is picking targets. Start with a full timed Paper 1 and Paper 2, marked with method and answer marks separated and minutes recorded. That identifies the three or four error categories costing the most marks, which are usually fluency and pace rather than topics. Then drill those specifically, add Paper 3 technique because it is learnable quickly, and make sure every failed attempt stays on the page for method marks. Nobody can promise an outcome, and anyone who does is best avoided.

faqs.question: Do you teach AA HL online only, or do tutors come to the house in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Online only. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Dubai students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own marked scripts on screen. For higher level mathematics that is the better arrangement rather than a compromise: the pool of people who teach Analysis and Approaches at higher level is small, so matching on the course rather than on the drive genuinely changes who teaches your child, and working through a mark scheme is a screen task anyway.

You will keep the written summary whether or not you continue. If the honest conclusion is that the problem is pace rather than mathematics and six weeks of drilling will do it, we will tell you that.
